Furthermore — since the knowability of knowledge itself is accepted, the fault of infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>) follows. For knowledge cannot be cognized by another knowledge functioning as an instrument — because that [knowledge] too [would require] another, and that another — leading to an undesired consequence.
If, to avoid the infinite regress, going however far, one [posits] some primary knowledge that is not grasped by another knowledge but is grasped by itself alone — then, like knowledge, even the object would be self-apprehended [which is absurd].
If [one argues:] 'Like a lamp, [knowledge] both self-illuminates and illuminates [others], because of its luminous nature; and because the object is not of luminous nature, there is no fault' — even so, there would be the absurd consequence that luminous objects are not apprehended by cognition.
If [one argues:] 'Knowledge grasps itself through its two [aspects of] inherence in the Self and luminous nature, but external luminous [objects] differ in character from knowledge, so there is no fault' — this too [is wrong]: if inherence in the Self and luminous nature were the reasons for self-apprehension of knowledge, then all [selves] would become omniscient.
If [one argues:] 'Being of the form of the object to be grasped (<s>grāhyākāratva</s>) is also a cause' — this too [is wrong]: just as another knowledge, being of another form, becomes the instrument [of apprehension], so too for knowledge that is to be grasped, some other [cognition] of another form would be its instrument — and thus the infinite regress is indeed irresolvable.
Furthermore — there is no example whatsoever that could establish something being both the grasped and the grasper of itself. Even a lamp is grasped by the eye and other [senses]. Nor does knowledge have two parts, because it is partless. And even if there were two parts, because both would be of luminous nature, there would be no mutual grasped-grasper relationship — like two lamps [which do not illuminate each other].
Furthermore — if knowledge is accepted as both grasped and grasper, even the existence of the Self would be difficult to establish. Therefore: knowledge of object-forms, memory, recognition, effort, desire, etc. are not properties of the Self — because they are graspable, like form (<s>rūpa</s>) and the like. And because they serve another's purpose, they reside in an aggregate — as demonstrated by the example of form and the like. Likewise, from having a substrate, from being impermanent, from being preceded by effort — through such [reasons], their being non-Self properties is established.
'[Like a] lodestone': like a lodestone. Just as a lodestone assists iron in pervading its own nature merely through proximity, so too the <s>citta</s> assists the Self — whose nature is consciousness (<s>cit</s>) — in pervading its own nature, by virtue of its visibility (<s>dṛśyatva</s>).
'Like a dancer — because of having shown the object, [this is done] by the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>)' — so it was stated. Therein: what makes the <s>citta</s> the shower and the <s>Puruṣa</s> the seer? The property-owner relationship (<s>sva-svāmitva</s>). How does the property-owner relationship arise? From the nature of things (<s>vastu-svabhāva</s>). How? It has been said: '[The citta is] like a lodestone.' Now, what is the cause of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s awareness of <s>cittavṛttis</s>? It is said: Because the <s>citta</s> thus 'assists merely through proximity' 'by virtue of its visibility,' therefore this [beginningless connection] 'becomes the cause' of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s 'awareness of <s>cittavṛttis</s>' — namely, that which is the 'beginningless connection.' || 4 ||

body.text: tāḥ punarniroddhavyā bahutve sati cittasya –
body.translated_text: Those [modifications] are to be restrained — although they are many in the <s>citta</s> —

body.text: vṛttayaḥ pañcatayyaḥ kliṣṭākliṣṭāḥ ॥ 5 ॥
body.translated_text: The <s>vṛttis</s> (modifications) are fivefold, [either] <s>kliṣṭa</s> (afflicted) or <s>akliṣṭa</s> (non-afflicted). || 5 ||

body.text: kleśahetukāḥ karmāśayapracaye kṣetrībhūtāḥ kliṣṭāḥ। khyātiviṣayā guṇādhikāravirodhinyo'kliṣṭāḥ। kliṣṭapravāhapatitā apyakliṣṭāḥ। kliṣṭacchidreṣvapyakliṣṭā bhavanti। akliṣṭacchidreṣu kliṣṭā iti। tathājātīyakāḥ saṁskārā vṛttibhireva kriyante। saṁskāraiśca vṛttaya iti। evaṁ vṛttisaṁskāracakramaniśamāvartate। tadevaṁbhūtaṁ cittamavasitādhikāramātmakalpena vyavatiṣṭhate pralayaṁ vā gacchatīti। tāḥ kliṣṭāścākliṣṭāśca pañcadhā vṛttayaḥ ॥ 5 ॥
body.translated_text: Those caused by <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), which have become the field (<s>kṣetra</s>) for the accumulation of <s>karmāśaya</s> (latent impressions of actions) — [these are] <s>kliṣṭa</s> (afflicted). Those whose object is <s>khyāti</s> (discriminative cognition), which oppose the sovereignty of the <s>guṇas</s> (constituents of nature) — [these are] <s>akliṣṭa</s> (non-afflicted). Even those fallen in the stream of the <s>kliṣṭa</s> are [still] <s>akliṣṭa</s>. In the gaps of the <s>kliṣṭa</s>, the <s>akliṣṭa</s> occur. In the gaps of the <s>akliṣṭa</s>, the <s>kliṣṭa</s> [occur]. Likewise, impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>) of the same kind are produced by the <s>vṛttis</s> themselves. And by the <s>saṃskāras</s>, the <s>vṛttis</s> [are produced]. Thus the wheel of <s>vṛttis</s> and <s>saṃskāras</s> revolves incessantly. Such a <s>citta</s>, [when its] function is complete, persists — like the Self (<s>ātmakalpa</s>) — or goes to dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>). Those — afflicted and non-afflicted — are the fivefold <s>vṛttis</s>. || 5 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tāḥ punarniroddhavyāḥ bahutve] 'pi [sati cittasya] yābhirvṛttibhiḥ vyutthāne sārūpyamuktaṁ puruṣasya । kasmāt punaḥ niroddhavyā ityāha-yato [vṛttayaḥ] kliṣṭākliṣṭāḥ ॥
nanu ca bahutve sati na śakyā nirodghumityata āha- [pañcatayya] iti । yadyapi kliṣṭākliṣṭā vṛttayo'nantāḥ, tathāpi [pañcatayyaḥ] pañcavidhāḥ, pañcakulā eva । tataśca pañcaprakāravṛttipratipakṣabhūtābhyāsavairāgyaprayogādeva nirodhopapatteḥ, pratyavayavanirodhasādhanāprayojakatvādvṛttīnāṁ, tadbahutve na nirodhāśakyatvaprasaṅgaḥ । [kleśahetukāḥ] -kleśanimittāḥ । avidyādipañcakleśaprayuktaṁ hi cittaṁ vṛttibhirātmānaṁ punaḥ punarāvedayati । [karmāśayapracaye] karmāṇi kuśalākuśalavimiśrāṇi tānyevā''phalapradānāccherata iti karmāśayaśabdavācyāni, teṣāṁ pracaya itaretaraguṇapradhānabhāvena saṁhananaṁ, tasmin karmāśayapracaye nimitte, avidyādi [kṣetrībhūtāḥ] kliṣṭāśrayāṁ ityarthaḥ । satīṣu hi tāsu karmāśayo vipākābhimukhībhavati ॥
[khyātiviṣayāḥ] -khyātyāspadāḥ । [guṇānāṁ] sattvādīnām [adhikāraḥ] saṁskārapravṛttiḥ [tadvirodhinyaḥ ।] khyātiviṣayatvādeva tā [akliṣṭāḥ,] apavargahetutvāt ॥
atha kliṣṭapaṅkimadhya(mānu)janmāno'kliṣṭā vṛttayaḥ kiṁ kliṣṭā eva kṣīrakumbhaprakṣiptāmbubinduvat ? evamakliṣṭapravāhapatitā api kliṣṭāḥ kimakliṣṭā eva ? kiṁ cātaḥ ; yadi kliṣṭapravāhagatā akliṣṭāḥ kliṣṭāḥ syuḥ, tadā vṛttisaṁskārānuvidhāyinī smṛtiḥ, tadanurūpa eva vyavahāraḥ । sa cāpi na sidhyati svarūpavyabhicāre । tasmādāha- [kliṣṭacchidreṣvapyakliṣṭāḥ] akliṣṭā eva [bhavanti । aklichidreṣu] api [kliṣṭāḥ] kliṣṭā eva । yasmādevaṁ tasmāt [tathājātīyakāḥ saṁskārā vṛttibhireva kriyante ॥]
yadyapi leśādayo'pi saṁskāramārabhante, tathāpi vṛtidvāraiva teṣāmapi saṁskāra iti vṛttibhirevetyevakārārthaḥ । tathā [saṁskarai] rapi [vṛttayaḥ] svānurūpaṁ kriyanta ityevaṁ- [vṛttisaṁskāracakramaniśamanavaratamāvartate । tadevaṁbhūtaṁ cittaṁ] - evaṁ hetuhetumadvṛttisaṁskāradharmakam । avasitādhikāraṁ-nivṛttāvidyāhetupravṛttikaṁ hetumātrāvasthatvāt । [ātmakalpena] -puruṣakalpena khyātimātreṇaiva kañcitkāla [mavatiṣṭhate] -prārabdhasaṁskāraśeṣānuvṛttyā । [pralayaṁ vā gacchati] - saṁskārāvasānāditi ॥ 5 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇa</s> (Elucidation):
'Those are to be restrained, although many' in the <s>citta</s> — namely, those <s>vṛttis</s> by which conformity with <s>Puruṣa</s> in emergence was stated. Why are they to be restrained? Because the '<s>vṛttis</s>' are <s>kliṣṭa</s> (afflicted) and <s>akliṣṭa</s> (non-afflicted).
But [one might object:] since they are many, they cannot be restrained — therefore he says 'fivefold.' Although the afflicted and non-afflicted <s>vṛttis</s> are infinite, still they are 'fivefold' — of five kinds, of five families only. Therefore, since cessation is possible through the application of <s>abhyāsa</s> (practice) and <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion) — which are the antidotes to [just] five types of modifications — and since it is not necessary to accomplish the means of cessation for each individual [modification], there is no problem of impossibility of cessation due to their multiplicity.
'Caused by <s>kleśas</s>' — occasioned by afflictions. For the <s>citta</s>, impelled by the five <s>kleśas</s> beginning with <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), reveals itself again and again through the <s>vṛttis</s>. 'In the accumulation of <s>karmāśaya</s>' — actions, whether wholesome, unwholesome, or mixed — those same [actions], because they rest (<s>śerate</s>) until they yield their fruit, are denoted by the term <s>karmāśaya</s>; their 'accumulation' (<s>pracaya</s>) is their consolidation through mutual relationship of subordination and predominance. In that accumulation of <s>karmāśaya</s> as the occasion, <s>avidyā</s> and the like have 'become the field (<s>kṣetra</s>)' — meaning they are the substrate of the afflicted [modifications]. For when those [afflicted modifications] exist, the <s>karmāśaya</s> faces toward fruition.
'Whose object is <s>khyāti</s>' — whose basis is [discriminative] cognition. 'The sovereignty (<s>adhikāra</s>) of the <s>guṇas</s>' — namely <s>sattva</s> and the rest — [means] the operation of [their] impressions; [the non-afflicted modifications are] 'opposed to that.' Because of having <s>khyāti</s> as their object, they are 'non-afflicted,' since they are causes of liberation.
Now, are the non-afflicted <s>vṛttis</s> born in the midst of the afflicted stream actually afflicted — like a drop of water thrown into a pot of milk? Likewise, are those fallen in the non-afflicted stream actually non-afflicted? What follows from this? If non-afflicted [modifications] in the afflicted stream were to become afflicted, then memory — which follows the <s>vṛttis</s> and <s>saṃskāras</s> — and behavior conforming to it [would be disrupted]. And that behavior too would fail if there were deviation from [their] essential nature. Therefore he says: 'In the gaps of the <s>kliṣṭa</s>, the <s>akliṣṭa</s>' remain non-afflicted. 'In the gaps of the <s>akliṣṭa</s>, the <s>kliṣṭa</s>' remain afflicted. Because this is so, therefore 'impressions of the same kind are produced by the <s>vṛttis</s> themselves.'
Although the <s>kleśas</s> and the like also initiate <s>saṃskāras</s>, still even their <s>saṃskāras</s> [operate] only through the doorway of <s>vṛttis</s> — hence 'by <s>vṛttis</s> alone' [with the particle 'eva']. Likewise, 'by <s>saṃskāras</s> too, <s>vṛttis</s>' of their own kind are produced — thus 'the wheel of <s>vṛttis</s> and <s>saṃskāras</s> revolves without ceasing.' 'Such a <s>citta</s>' — one whose character is [these] <s>vṛttis</s> and <s>saṃskāras</s> standing in cause-effect relationship. 'Whose function is complete' — whose operation motivated by <s>avidyā</s> has ceased, [remaining] in the state of mere cause. '[Persists] like the Self' (<s>ātmakalpa</s>) — by mere <s>khyāti</s> (cognition) alone for some time — through the continuance of the residual activated <s>saṃskāras</s>. 'Or goes to dissolution' — due to the exhaustion of <s>saṃskāras</s>. || 5 ||

body.text: pramāṇaviparyayavikalpanidrāsmṛtaya ॥ 6 ॥
body.translated_text: [The five vṛttis are:] <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition), <s>viparyaya</s> (error), <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction), <s>nidrā</s> (sleep), and <s>smṛti</s> (memory). || 6 ||

body.text: tatra
body.translated_text: Among those —

body.text: pratyakṣānumānāgamāḥ pramāṇāni ॥ 7 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>Pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception), <s>anumāna</s> (inference), and <s>āgama</s> (verbal testimony) are the <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid cognition). || 7 ||

body.text: indriyapraṇālikayā cittasya bāhyavastūparāgāttadviṣayā sāmānyaviśeṣātmano'rthasya viśeṣāvadhāraṇapradhānā vṛttiḥ pratyakṣaṁ pramāṇam। phalamaviśiṣṭaḥ pauruṣeyaścittavṛttibodhaḥ। pratisaṁvedī puruṣa ityupariṣṭādupapādayiṣyāmaḥ।
body.translated_text: Through the channel of the sense organs, from the <s>citta</s>'s coloring by external objects, the <s>vṛtti</s> whose object is that [external thing] — predominant in ascertaining the particular (<s>viśeṣa</s>) of an object consisting of universal and particular — is the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition) [called] <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception). The fruit [of perception] is the undifferentiated, personal (<s>pauruṣeya</s>) awareness of the <s>cittavṛtti</s>. That the <s>Puruṣa</s> is the experiencer (<s>pratisaṃvedī</s>) — this we shall establish later.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
kāḥ punastāḥ kliṣṭākliṣṭāḥ pañcaprakārā vṛttaya ityāha – [pramāṇaviparyayavikalpanidrāsmṛtaya iti ॥]
etāvatya eva vṛttayaḥ । tatra- [pratyakṣānumānāgamāḥ pramāṇāni ॥] pramāṇākhyā vṛttistridhaiva bhidyate । tatra pramāṇākhyāyāścittavṛtteḥ prathamo bhedaḥ pratyakṣam । atastallakṣaṇamevābhidhīyate । tatpūrvakatvāt bhedadvayasya ॥ [indriyapranāḍikayā ॥] indriyamiti śrotrādipañcakaṁ na karmendriyaṁ, tasya cittavṛttyahetutvāt । kriyārthaṁ hi tat । tasmādindriyaśabdasya sāmānyārthatve'pi cittavṛtterupavyācikhyāsitatvācchrotrādiviṣayataiva । vṛttyarthatvācca śrotrādīnām । indriyameva pranāḍikā dvāraṁ śabdādyākāravṛttirūpeṇa pariṇāmamānasya cittasya । atastat tenendriyadvāreṇa sāmānyaviśeṣātmakabāhyavastvākāratayā pariṇamamānamuparajyate । tasya taduparāgāddhetoḥ [cittasya] yā mudrāpratimudrāvat [vṛttiḥ] sāmānyaviśeṣātmakavastūparāge'pi [viśeṣāvadhāraṇapradhānā] saiva [pratyakṣaṁ pramāṇam ॥]
atha svaviṣayasāmānyaviśeṣāvabhāsanasāmarthye śrotrādīnāṁ cittasya ca kiṁkṛtaṁ viśeṣāvadhāraṇaprādhānyamiti ?
ucyate-viśeṣapratibandhatvāt hānopādānādīnāṁ viśeṣāvadhāraṇapradhānanateti (tetyāha) । na sāmānyaṁ nāvadhāryate, guṇabhūtaṁ tu gṛhyata eva । yathā nīlaṁ rūpamiti nīlāvadhāraṇaprādhānye satyapi rūpameva nīlamiti guṇabhūtamavadhārayati । tathā du:khaśabdaḥ sukhaśabdo mūḍhaḥ śabda iti । tathā ca viśeṣāvadhāraṇapradhānā vṛttiriti hyupapadyate ॥
kiṁ ca-saṁśayaviparyayanimittatvācca sāmānyopalabdhe: । sāmānye hyupalabdhe bubhutsitaviśeṣasya saṁśayo jāyate, samupalabdhasāmānyānyasmṛtervā viparyayaḥ, samadhigataviśeṣasya tu saṁśayaviparyayau na sthitimupāśnuvāte, iti viśeṣāvadhāraṇapradhānatecyate ॥
yatrāpi sāmānyamevāvādidhārayiṣitaṁ gairiti vā aśva iti vā, tatrāpyanyataraparityāgenānyatarāvadhāraṇeti viśeṣāvadhāraṇapradhānataiva । sarvameva hi vastu vastvantarāpekṣayā sāmānyaṁ viśeṣaśca ॥
yasya punaḥ sāmānyamavastvadhyāropitamevoṣarāmbuvat, nendriyaviṣayāmiti, tasya pratiniyatasāmānyādhyāropaṇānupapattiḥ । na hyanupalabdhapūrvamukhye saṁbhavatyadhyāropaṇā, smṛtyasaṁbhavāt । na kadācidadṛṣṭamukhyodakasya salilādhyāropaṇamūṣareṣu vidyate । athāsmaranpyadhyāropayet rūpasvalakṣaṇe śabdatvādyāpyadhyasyet । athendriyāntaraviṣayavādrūpasvalakṣaṇe śavdatvādyadhyāso viruddha iti cet-na - avastutve satyaviśeṣāt । viśeṣābhyupagame ca vastutvaprasaṅgaḥ । śabdasvalakṣaṇādiva rūpasvalakṣaṇasya ॥
kiṁ cānyat-deśakālānyaviśiṣṭapratyakṣā [na] bhyupagame samastalokavyavahāravilepaḥ syāt । na hīdamahamamuṣminnavakāśe kāle cāsminnādrākṣametasmānnimittādevaṁviśeṣaṇamiti ca smṛtyupapattiḥ । na ca pratyakṣādṛṣṭeṣu viśeṣyavadviśeṣaṇeṣu smṛti: saṁbhavati । na ca kalpanāpoḍhena vyavahāragocarātītena vyavaharamāṇo dṛśyate । tasmāllokaprasiddhapratyakṣānusaraṇameva nyāyyam ॥
nanu ca yogināṁ nirvikalpasamādhijaṁ darśanaṁ, tasyānevaṁlakṣaṇatvāt, tathā sukharāgādivijñānasya cānindriyapranāḍī*pūrvatvāt pramāṇāntaratvamabhyupetavyaṁ, pratyakṣatvaṁ vā vaktavyam । ucyate । pratyakṣasya (na pramāṇasya) puruṣapratyayāpekṣatvena parihṛtatvāt । na hyapratyayā vṛttiḥ pratyakṣam । caitanyodayahetoreva sapratyayāyāḥ pratyakṣatvam । tathā cāha-‘ [phalaṁ tadaviśiṣṭaḥ pauruṣeyaścittavṛttibodha] ' iti ॥ evaṁ ca sati sukharāgādijñānasya kliṣṭākliṣṭarūpasya tadaviśiṣṭapuruṣapratyayaphalāvasānatvāt pratyakṣatā siddhaiva ॥
*atredamavadheyam---
ādarśakaśe 20 “pranāḍī” ityetadupari 25 ‘napekṣya sambandhaḥ sambandhatāmiyāt । yadasau prasiddhavaccocyate ya’ iti ityupakramya 34 ‘smṛtyavasānā hi sā, yataḥ pramā ityantagranthaṁ daśābhiḥ puṭairvilikhya, tadupari 20 ‘‘pūrvatvāt pramāṇāntaratvamabhyupetavyaṁ, pratyakṣatvaṁ vā vaktavyam” ityupakramya 25 ‘‘tasmāt pramāṇaphalānabhijñānām abhimānamātrameva kevalaṁ paṇḍitaṁmanyānāmityupekṣaṇīyamiti” ityantaṁ ṣaḍbhiḥ puṭairvilikhya, tataḥ 25 ‘‘anumānamathocyate” ityādi 25 ‘‘kaḥ sambandhaḥ, kayorvā, na hi sambandhināva” ityantaṁ vilikhya paṅkticatuṣṭayena, tataḥ 34 ‘‘rṇena prabādhyate, abhūtārthādiviṣayatvāt” ityādivākyaṁ likhitaṁ dṛśyate । kośāntarañca na labhyate । yathāmātṛkaṁ mudraṇe ca vākyānāmananvayaḥ-na hi 20 ‘‘pranāḍī” ityanena 25 ‘‘napekṣya sambandhaḥ sambandhatāmiyāt ?” ityanveti । na ca 25 ‘‘kaḥ sambandhaḥ kayorvā, na hi sambandhināva?? ityanena 34 ‘‘rṇena prabādhyate” iti cānveti । evaṁ pratyakṣapramāṇānarūpaṇamupakramya tadaparisamāpyaiva madhye'numānāgamapramāṇayornirūpaṇaṁ, tato viparyayanirūpaṇaṁ, punaḥ pratyakṣapramāṇanirūpaṇaśeṣaḥ, tataḥ anumānanirūpaṇopakramaḥ, tato viparyayanirūpaṇaśeṣaśca iti kramaḥ ādarśakośe dṛśyate । na cāyaṁ kramaḥ śobhate ॥ ‘‘anindriyapranāḍī pūrvatvāt pramāṇāntaratvamabhyupetavyam” iti; daśapuṭavyavāhitavākyadvayasya mitho yojane, ‘‘na hi sambandhināvanapekṣya sambandhaḥ sambandhatāmiyāt” iti, ṣoḍaśapuṣṭavyavahitavākyadvayasya mitho yojane, ‘‘smaryamāṇātadvastupratiṣṭhatvānna pramāṇaṁ, smṛtyavasānā hi sā, yataḥ pramāṇena prabādhyate । abhūtārthādāviṣayatvāt” iti ca ṣaṭpuṭavyavahitavākyadvayasya mithe yojane cānveti । yathākramaṁ pramāṇatrayanirūpaṇaṁ, tato viparyayānarūpaṇamiti ca sūtrānusārī bhāṣyānusārī ca kramo'nusṛto bhavati, iti paryālocya mahatā prayāsena mātṛkāgranthavākyānāṁ sanniveśaviparyāsaḥ kṛtaḥ । tatra sūkṣmekṣikayā guṇadoṣau pariśīlanīyau । “pranāḍī” ityāderadhaḥ aṅkitāḥ (20-25-34) iti puṭasaṅkhayāḥ mudritaitatkośānusāriṇyaḥ ॥
indriyapranāḍikāgrahaṇaṁ laukikapratyakṣodbhavānuvāda eva । anyathā hīndriyanirapekṣasya yogīśvarayorjñānasyāpratyakṣatā syāt । asti hi kleśādipratibandhābhāve sarvārthana cittasattvena sarvaviṣayeṇa yugapatsūkṣmavyavahitādigrahaṇam । tathā cāha- [tārakaṁ sarvaviṣayaṁ sarvathāviṣayamakramaṁ ceti vivekajaṁ jñānam’] iti । tasmānnāvadhāryate indriyapranāḍikayaiveti ॥
[bāhyavastūparāgāditi] viparyayanivṛtyartham । viśeṣāvadhāraṇapradhānatvena saṁśayanivṛttiriti ।
tatra keṣāṁcit phalaṁ tadeva pramāṇam । apareṣāṁ tu pramāṇādanyat(tra) pramāṇavyaktyantaram (re) । yathā ghaṭavijñānasya pramāṇasya hānopādānepekṣābuddhayaḥ phalamiti । guṇade.oṣatadubhaya(vadabhava)śūnyatvaviṣayatvādupādānādibuddhīnāṁ pramāṇabhūtaghaṭa- vijñānādatyantabhedaḥ । tataścānyaviṣayasya pramāṇasya anya(prameyasya)viṣayapramāṇa(ṇe)vyaktyantaraṁ (re)phalamiti ॥
na hi khadiracchedanasya khadiropādānaṁ tatparityāgo vā phale bhavituṁ yuktam । vi(api)yogasaṁbandhaphalatvāt tyāgopādānayoḥ । na ca phalasya phalaṁ sambhavati । dvaidhībhāvaphalavyavahitatvāca ॥
kiṁ ca-phalasya cet phalaṁ kriyānapekṣāprasaṅgaḥ । phalārthaṁ hi kriyāpekṣyate । taccetphalaṁ vināpi kriyayā phalādapi sidhyati, (atohya) tato na hyanekāyāsāpekṣitaniṣpattikriyāmanutiṣṭhet । sādhanānveṣaṇānupapattiśca । kriyāyā abhāvāt ॥
nāpi kriyaiva phalaṁ, kriyānuparamaprasaṅgāt । phalāvasānā hi (pi) kriyā । kriyāyāśca phalatve phalānabhilāṣitvaprasaṅgaḥ । tasyā duḥkhatvāt ॥
tasmānna pramāṇasvarūpameva phalam, nāpi tadvyatiriktapramāṇāntaramityāha - [phalaṁ tadaviśiṣṭa ityādi । tadaviśiṣṭaḥ] tayā pramāṇākhyayā vṛttyā aviśiṣṭa: tulyaḥ tadākāratvena, [pauruṣeyaḥ] puruṣasyāyaṁ bodha iti । puruṣasya hi vṛttyākāratā । tasmānnākriyājaṁ dravyasvarūpamātraṁ phalam । kiṁ tarhi ? dravyasyaivāvasthāntaraviśeṣaḥ (ṣa)kriyājaḥ(ja)kriyāparyavasānakālaḥ kriyoparamopapatteḥ phalam । phalaniṣpattāveva hi kriyoparama upapadyate । evaṁbhūtasya mukhyaphalatve pradhānakriyāvyavahita(viprakṛṣṭāyāḥ)kriyāyā dravyaṁ dravyasya vā kriyā phalamityanyonyapratyupasthāpakatvena pradhānaphalābhimukhīkaraṇāt phalatvopacāro na virotsyate ॥
nanu ca bhavato'pyupacaritameva phalam vṛttyaviśiṣṭatāyāḥ phalatvenābhyupagamāt , puruṣasya ca śuddhatvāt, tadākāratāyā anṛtatvam । na hi sphaṭikamaṇeralatakopadhānākāratā satyā ॥
bāḍham-tathāpi tvetadeva phalaṁ mukhyam, dṛṣṭatvāt । mukhyaphalāntarādarśanāt । sarvasyaiva kriyākārakajātasyaitatphalārthatvāt । etadavasānaṁ hi tatsarvam । tathā ca pradarśitam ॥
nanu ca mithyābhūtasyaiva mukhyaphalatvaṁ vṛttyākārasya, tathā ca tadabhilāṣānupapatiḥ । bāḍham-mithyābhūta eva vṛtyanugato bhogaḥ । tathā cāha- “ [satvapuruṣayoratyantāsekīrṇayoḥ pratyayāviśeṣo bhogaḥ” iti ॥] bhāṣyamapi – [“tayoḥ svarūpopalambhe sati kuto bhoga” iti ॥] ata eva ca samyagdarśanādātyantikī nivṛttirupapadyate ॥
yeṣāmamithyā phalaṁ, teṣāṁ vairāgyakāraṇābhāvāt samyagdarśanānveṣaṇānupapattermokṣābhāvaḥ । na ca kriyāpariniṣpādyo mokṣaḥ, anityatvaprasaṅgāt ॥
atha buddhiboddhṛtvaṁ puruṣasya sattvaṁ cāsiddhamiti cet aha- [pratisaṁvedī buddheḥ puruṣa ityupariṣṭāt pravedayiṣyāma iti ॥]
ye cāpīndriyārthasannikarṣasya pratyakṣatvamabhyupayanti, na teṣāmapi samyagabhyupetaṁ, sannikarṣasya kriyāphalatvāt । sannikarṣaśca saṁyogaḥ । sa ca kriyājastairiṣyate । yato yadupajāyate tattasya pramāṇam । tacca tasya phalaṁ yadupajāyate ॥
phalamapi sannikarṣe jñānaṁ prati pramāṇamiti cet-tacca na-jñāpakapramāṇaprastāve kārakapramāṇopanyāsasyāyuktatvāt । sannikarṣe hi jñānasyotpādako na tasya jñāpakaḥ । prameyādhigamāya hi pratyakṣādīnyupanyastāni, na jñānotpattikāraṇam । tatprakriyāyāma(yānya)prakṛtaṁ prakriyata ॥
athāpi syāt-jñānasyāpi prameyatvāttaccāpyutpadyamānaṁ pramīyata iti, tadutpattikāraṇasya sannikarṣasya jñāpakatvameveti-tacca na-jñānaṁ jñānenaiva jñāyeta, teṣāṁ tathābhyupagamāt । na ca sannikarṣo jñānam । jñānotpādakatvenābhyupagamāt ॥
atha jñānasya jñāne sannikarṣo nimittatvāt pramāṇamiti cedadṛṣṭeśvarecchāviṣayanimeṣonmeṣādīnāmapi nimittatvāt pramāṇatve kaḥ pradveṣaḥ ? na ca jñānasya jñeyatve ātmanaśca svabhāvacidrūpatvānabhyupagama śakyā anavasthā parihartum ॥
atha ātmasamavetamātratayaiva jñānasya jñeyatā, na jñānāntaramapekṣyate yenātiprasajyeteti cet-asyāpyanyat pratyakṣalakṣaṇaṁ vācyam anindriyasannikarṣādilakṣaṇatvādātmani jñānasamavāyatvasya । sannikarṣasya ca jñānotpattiphalatvāttadutpattivyavadhāne sati tasya jñānena nānantaryam ॥
tasmāttadānantaryeṇāpi na sannikarṣaphalatvaṁ jñānasya । tathā hānādibuddhīnāmapi rūpādijñānaphalatvānupapattiruktā ॥
vyabhicārācca । yathaikasminnaṅganādipiṇḍaviṣaye jñāne samāne bahūnāmutpane kasyacidupādānabuddhiḥ, anyasya heyabuddhiḥ, kasyacidubhayābhāvaḥ, tatra hānopādānabuddhivyabhicarati । anyataranaikameva jñānaṁ tadevībhayaṁ vyabhicaralyupe । kṣakasya । yacca yadyabhicarati na tattasya phalam ॥
kiṁ ca-hānepādānābhāvamātratvādabhāva evopekṣā । na cābhāvaḥ pramāṇasya vastunaḥ phalaṁ bhavitumarhati । rāgadveṣābhyāṁ copādānaparityāgabuddhī । tadabhāvāt kāraṇābhāve kāryābhāva iti pramāṇavijñāne satyapi hānopādānabuddhyabhāva evopekṣeti vyabhicārānna hānādibuddhiphalatvam ।
kiṁ ca-rāgadveṣatadabhāvanāmabhyupādānādibuddhiphalatve pramāṇatvaprasaṅgaḥ । pauruṣeyacittavṛttibodhaphalatve tu na kiñcidvirudhyata iti ॥
nanu ca cittavṛtteḥ sevedyatvamasiddham । na hi karaṇameva karma bhavati । na hi dātrameva lūyate । naiṣa doṣaḥ । kriyākārakayorbhinnadharmatvāt । kriyānirvṛttiṁ prati sambhūya kārakāṇi vyāpriyante parasparaṁ viṣayaviṣayibhāvena । kriyā tu sattāmātreṇaiva phalaheturiti karaṇatvamasyāmupacaryate, na kārakavat । kurvaddhi kārayediti kriyādhikārakaṁ syānna bhūtaṁ bhavyāyopadiśyeta ॥
kiṁ ca-anavasthāprasaṅgaśca । kriyā cet । karaṇaṁ syāt , tannirvartyayā cānyayā kriyayā bhavitavyam । na hyanyāṁ kriyāmantareṇa tasyāḥ kāraṇatvaṁ ghaṭate । yāpi cānyā sāpi kāraṇaṁ syādanyasyāḥ kriyāyāḥ । sāpyanyasyā ityanavasthā । tataśca kriyāsantānānuparamāt phalānabhinirvṛttiḥ । tatrāntyā cet । kriyāntareṇa vinā phalaheturbhavet, prathamasya tathātve kaḥ pradveṣaḥ ? cittavṛttestvabhivyañjakatvāt saṁvedyatetyadoṣaḥ ।
dṛśyate cābhivyañjakānāṁ svarūpasaṁvedyatayaiva karaṇatvaṁ pradīpādīnām । tathā cittavṛtterapi । cakṣurādiṣvabhivyañjakatve'pi agrahaṇādvyabhicāra iti cet, samāna (cetanasamāna) jātīyasaṁkarāt katham ॥
yeṣāṁ tāvadbhautikānīndriyāṇi, teṣāṁ cakṣuṣastaijasatvāt bāhyenālokena tulyajātīyena vyatibhedāt gṛhyamāṇasyaivāvivekaḥ । yathā pradīpānāṁ bahūnāṁ prabhāvyatibhedāt kasya kā prabheti na vivicyate । tathā śrotrādiṣvapi ॥
yeṣāmapyabhautikāni, teṣāmapyabhivyañjakatvena samānajātīyatā vṛtterabhivyañjakatvādagrahaṇamiti । tanna-prāptacaitanyopagrahatayā'vibhāvyatvādavyavahitatvācca । sarvagatatve'pyātmanaḥ sūkṣmatvena svacchataratvena ca citenāvyavadhānācca grahaṇaṁ cittavṛttestasmāccittavṛttipramāṇenaiva tadākāratayā pauruṣeyo'pi bodhaḥ sevedyamāna eva phalamiti siddham ॥
yeṣāṁ puna: pratyakṣeṇāsaṁvedyā cittavṛttisteṣāṁ phalagrahaṇapramāṇābhāva: ! phale ca gṛhīte jñānāsiddhatvasyārthāpattiḥ । na ca phalaṁ gṛhyate pramāṇavyāpārānabhyupagamāt । tadabhyupagame cānavasthāprasaṅgaḥ ! yatphalāvagrahaṇāya pramāṇamabhyupagamyate tasyāpyanyat phalaṁ tatpramāṇasyāpyanyaditi na kvacidavatiṣṭheta ॥
atha na pramāṇavyāpārastasya tadā pramāṇābhāvāt phalasyāsattvaṁ prasaktam । yatra hi sadupalambhakāni pramāṇāni na vyāpāraṁ gacchanti, tannāstītyabhyupagacchāmaḥ ( teṣām) [॥]
atha agṛhyamāṇamapi tadeva jñānaṁ pramāṇaṁ phalasyāpīti cet-na- abhivyañjakadharmavyatikramāt । na hyabhivyañjakaṁ gṛhyamāṇamabhivyañjayaddṛṣṭam । na hyulkā giriśikhare'pi nijaṁ dharmamatikrāmati ॥
athābhivyañjayadeva phalaṁ pratyapi pramāṇamiti cet-siddhaṁ tarhīpsitamasmākam । rāgādīnāṁ vṛttiviśeṣaṇatvena grahaṇopapatteḥ । rakto'haṁ dviṣṭo'hamiti yadyahaṁpratyayaviśeṣaṇaṁ, tadapi vṛttibhāvābhāvitvenaiva grahaṇādvṛttiviśaṣaṇānāṁ rāgādīnāṁ grahaṇamupapadyate । a(tenā)nyathā rūpādivanmānāntarāpekṣatvaprasaṅgāt । tataścānavastheti । tasmātpramāṇaphalānabhijñānāmabhimānamātrameva kevalaṁ paṇḍitaṁmanyānā mityupekṣaṇīyamiti ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
What then are those afflicted and unafflicted <s>vṛttis</s> (mental modifications) of five kinds? To this he says — [<s>Pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition), <s>viparyaya</s> (error), <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction), <s>nidrā</s> (sleep), and <s>smṛti</s> (memory).]
These alone are the <s>vṛttis</s>. Among them — [<s>Pratyakṣa</s> (perception), <s>anumāna</s> (inference), and <s>āgama</s> (testimony) are the <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid cognition).] The <s>vṛtti</s> called <s>pramāṇa</s> is divided into just three types. Of these, the first division of the <s>cittavṛtti</s> (mental modification) called <s>pramāṇa</s> is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception). Therefore, its definition alone is stated, since the other two divisions presuppose it.
[Through the channel of the sense organ (<s>indriya-pranāḍikā</s>)] — '<s>Indriya</s>' (sense organ) refers to the five beginning with <s>śrotra</s> (hearing), not the motor organs (<s>karmendriya</s>), since those are not causes of <s>cittavṛtti</s>. For those serve the purpose of action. Therefore, even though the word '<s>indriya</s>' has a general meaning, because what is intended to be explained is <s>cittavṛtti</s>, it refers only to <s>śrotra</s> and the rest. And because <s>śrotra</s> and the rest serve the purpose of <s>vṛtti</s>. The sense organ itself is the channel (<s>pranāḍikā</s>), the doorway, for <s>citta</s> (mind) as it undergoes transformation in the form of <s>vṛtti</s> having the appearance of sound and so forth. Therefore, through that doorway of the sense organ, <s>citta</s>, transforming into the form of the external object consisting of both universal and particular, is colored by it. From that coloring of [the mind], the [<s>vṛtti</s> (modification)] which is like an impression and counter-impression of [<s>citta</s> (the mind)], even when colored by an object consisting of both universal and particular, [that which is predominantly the discrimination of particulars (<s>viśeṣāvadhāraṇa-pradhānā</s>)] — that alone [is the <s>pramāṇa</s> called <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception).]
Now, given that <s>śrotra</s> and the rest and <s>citta</s> have the capacity to manifest both the universal and the particular of their respective objects, what makes the discrimination of the particular predominant?
It is said — because <s>hāna</s> (avoidance), <s>upādāna</s> (acceptance) and so forth are bound to particulars, the discrimination of the particular is predominant (thus he says). It is not that the universal is not ascertained; rather, it is apprehended as a subordinate element. Just as in 'blue color,' even though the ascertainment of blue is predominant, one ascertains 'the color that is blue' — the universal as subordinate. Similarly, 'a painful sound,' 'a pleasant sound,' 'a dull sound.' And thus it is established that the <s>vṛtti</s> is predominantly the discrimination of the particular.
Moreover — because the apprehension of the universal is the cause of doubt and error. For when the universal is apprehended, doubt arises regarding the particular one wishes to know, or error arises from the memory of another thing whose universal has been apprehended; but when the particular has been ascertained, doubt and error do not persist. Thus it is said that the discrimination of the particular is predominant.
Even where one wishes to ascertain only the universal, as in 'cow' or 'horse,' even there, the ascertainment of one involves the exclusion of another, so the predominance of particular-discrimination holds. For every entity is both universal and particular in relation to other entities.
As for one who holds that the universal is unreal, merely superimposed like water in a desert — that it is not an object of the senses — for such a person, the consistent superimposition of specific universals cannot be explained. For superimposition is not possible where the primary referent has never been apprehended, since memory would be impossible. One who has never seen real water cannot superimpose water on a desert. If one were to superimpose even without remembering, then one could also superimpose sound-nature and the like on the particular form of color. If it be said that superimposing sound-nature on the particular of color is contradictory, like an object of a different sense — no, because when something is unreal, there is no distinction. And if distinction is admitted, then reality would follow — just as with the particular of sound, so with the particular of color.
Furthermore — if perception unqualified by place, time, and other distinctions is [not] accepted, then the entire conduct of worldly life would be disrupted. For there would be no justification for memory of the form 'I perceived this thing in that place at that time, having such-and-such qualities.' And memory cannot occur regarding qualifiers that have not been perceived through direct perception along with the qualified. And no one is seen conducting transactions through something that is devoid of conceptual construction and beyond the scope of practical activity. Therefore, it is proper to follow perception as commonly known in the world.
But the <s>yogins</s>' vision born of <s>nirvikalpa-samādhi</s> (thought-free absorption) — since its definition is not of this kind — and similarly, since cognition of pleasure, attachment and so forth is not preceded by the channel of a sense organ* — must either be accepted as a different <s>pramāṇa</s>, or must be called <s>pratyakṣa</s>. It is said: because <s>pratyakṣa</s> (not <s>pramāṇa</s> in general) has been resolved by its dependence on <s>puruṣa-pratyaya</s> (the cognition of the Self). For a <s>vṛtti</s> without <s>pratyaya</s> (cognition) is not <s>pratyakṣa</s>. <s>Pratyakṣa</s>-hood belongs only to that which has <s>pratyaya</s>, because it causes the arising of consciousness. And thus he says — '[The fruit (<s>phala</s>) is the cognition of <s>Puruṣa</s> (<s>pauruṣeya bodha</s>) which is indistinguishable from that (<s>tadaviśiṣṭa</s>)].' And this being so, the <s>pratyakṣa</s>-hood of the cognition of pleasure, attachment and so forth — whether afflicted or unafflicted — is established, since it culminates in the fruit that is the <s>Puruṣa</s>'s cognition indistinguishable from that.
*A note must be made here —
In the manuscript, above 'pranāḍī' on page 20, on page 25 beginning with 'without depending on the relation, the relation would become a relation — that which is stated as well-known,' and up to page 34 'it ends in memory, since it is a <s>pramāṇa</s>' — a text of ten folios was written; and above that, from page 20 beginning with 'not being preceded [by sense-channel], a different <s>pramāṇa</s> must be accepted, or it must be called <s>pratyakṣa</s>' up to page 25 ending with 'therefore, the mere conceit of those ignorant of the fruit of <s>pramāṇa</s>, who consider themselves learned, should be disregarded' — six folios were written; then from page 25 'inference is now stated' up to page 25 'what is the relation, and between what two? For the related things themselves' — four lines were written; then from page 34 the sentence beginning 'is contradicted by that, because of having unreal objects as its domain' is written. And no other manuscript is available. In both the original manuscript and the printed edition, the sentences do not connect — for page 20 'pranāḍī' does not connect with page 25 'without depending on the relation, the relation would become a relation.' Nor does page 25 'what is the relation, between what two? For the related things themselves' connect with page 34 'is contradicted by that.' Thus, having begun the exposition of <s>pratyakṣa-pramāṇa</s>, without completing it, in the middle the exposition of <s>anumāna</s> and <s>āgama-pramāṇa</s> appears, then the exposition of <s>viparyaya</s>, then the remainder of the exposition of <s>pratyakṣa-pramāṇa</s>, then the beginning of the exposition of <s>anumāna</s>, then the remainder of the exposition of <s>viparyaya</s> — this is the order seen in the manuscript. And this order is not coherent. When joining 'not being preceded by sense-channel, a different <s>pramāṇa</s> must be accepted' — the two sentences separated by ten folios; when joining 'for the related things themselves, without depending on the relation, the relation would become a relation' — the two sentences separated by sixteen folios; and when joining 'being not established in reality because it is recalled, it is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>, for it ends in memory, since it is contradicted by a <s>pramāṇa</s>; because of having unreal objects as its domain' — the two sentences separated by six folios — they connect. The exposition of the three <s>pramāṇas</s> in order, then the exposition of <s>viparyaya</s> — an order following the <s>sūtra</s> and following the <s>bhāṣya</s> is maintained. Having considered this, with great effort, the rearrangement of the sentences of the original text has been made. Therein, the merits and faults should be examined with careful scrutiny. The numbers marked below 'pranāḍī' and so forth (20-25-34) are page numbers following the printed edition.
The mention of '<s>indriya-pranāḍikā</s>' (sense-channel) is merely a restatement of the origin of ordinary perception. Otherwise, the knowledge of <s>yogins</s> and <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), which is independent of the senses, would not be <s>pratyakṣa</s>. For in the absence of obstructions such as <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), the <s>citta-sattva</s> (pure mind), having all objects as its domain, simultaneously grasps the subtle, the concealed, and the like. And thus he says — ['The knowledge born of discrimination (<s>vivekaja jñāna</s>) is <s>tāraka</s> (liberating), has all objects as its domain, has all modes as its domain, and is without sequence.'] Therefore, it is not established that perception occurs only through the channel of the sense organ.
['From the coloring by an external object'] — this is to exclude <s>viparyaya</s> (error). The exclusion of doubt is by virtue of the predominance of particular-discrimination.
Regarding this, some hold that the fruit (<s>phala</s>) is identical with the <s>pramāṇa</s> itself. But others hold that the fruit is different from the <s>pramāṇa</s> — another instance of <s>pramāṇa</s>. For example, they say that the cognitions of avoidance and acceptance that follow from the <s>pramāṇa</s>-cognition of a pot are the fruit. Since the cognitions of acceptance and so forth have entirely different objects — being directed at qualities, defects, both, or the absence of both — they are completely different from the <s>pramāṇa</s>-cognition of the pot. Therefore, the fruit is another instance of <s>pramāṇa</s> whose object differs from the object of the original <s>pramāṇa</s>.
For it is not reasonable that the acceptance or rejection of <s>khadira</s> (acacia wood) should be the fruit of cutting <s>khadira</s>. Because acceptance and rejection have as their fruit the connection and disconnection respectively. And there cannot be a fruit of a fruit. And because it is separated by the intermediate fruit of bifurcation.
Moreover — if there were a fruit of the fruit, then action would become unnecessary. For action is required for the sake of the fruit. If that fruit could be obtained from another fruit even without action, then one would not undertake action whose accomplishment requires much effort. And the search for means would be unjustified, due to the absence of action.
Nor is action itself the fruit, because that would lead to the non-cessation of action. For action terminates in its fruit. And if action were the fruit, there would be no desire for the fruit, since action is painful.
Therefore, neither is the nature of <s>pramāṇa</s> itself the fruit, nor is it a different <s>pramāṇa</s> distinct from it — thus he says: ['The fruit is the cognition of <s>Puruṣa</s> which is indistinguishable from that,' and so forth. 'Indistinguishable from that'] — indistinguishable from, i.e. identical in form with, that <s>vṛtti</s> called <s>pramāṇa</s>; ['of <s>Puruṣa</s>' (<s>pauruṣeya</s>)] — this is the cognition belonging to <s>Puruṣa</s>. For <s>Puruṣa</s> assumes the form of the <s>vṛtti</s>. Therefore, the fruit is not merely the nature of an inactive substance. Rather, it is a particular state of the substance itself — produced by action, being the moment when action concludes — since the cessation of action is justified. For the cessation of action is justified only upon the accomplishment of the fruit. When such is the primary fruit, since the subsidiary action connected to the primary action presents substance as the fruit of action or action as the fruit of substance — through their mutual indication leading toward the primary fruit — the figurative designation as 'fruit' is not objectionable.
But even for you, the fruit is only figurative, since you accept the indistinguishability from the <s>vṛtti</s> as the fruit, and since <s>Puruṣa</s> is pure, the assumption of that form is unreal. For the appearance of a red flower placed near a crystal gem is not real in the crystal.
Indeed so — nevertheless, this alone is the primary fruit, because it is directly experienced, because no other primary fruit is seen, and because the entire assemblage of actions and agents exists for the purpose of this fruit. For all of that terminates in this. And thus it has been demonstrated.
But the primary fruit is the form of the <s>vṛtti</s>, which is itself unreal, and therefore the desire for it would be unjustified. Indeed — the experience (<s>bhoga</s>) that follows the <s>vṛtti</s> is itself of an unreal nature. And thus he says — ['Experience (<s>bhoga</s>) is the cognition that does not distinguish between <s>Sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, which are absolutely distinct.'] The <s>bhāṣya</s> also states — ['When their true natures are recognized, how can there be experience?'] And for this very reason, from right knowledge (<s>samyag-darśana</s>), absolute cessation is justified.
For those who hold that the fruit is not unreal, since they lack the cause of <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), the search for right knowledge is unjustified, and therefore liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) would be impossible. And liberation is not something produced by action, because that would entail impermanence.
If it be objected that <s>Puruṣa</s>'s nature as knower of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) and <s>sattva</s> are unestablished — he says: ['<s>Puruṣa</s> is the experiencer of <s>buddhi</s>' — this we shall explain later.]
Even those who accept that <s>pratyakṣa</s> consists in the contact of sense organ and object — even for them it is not properly maintained, because contact is the fruit of action. And contact is conjunction (<s>saṁyoga</s>). And they accept that it is produced by action. That from which something arises is its <s>pramāṇa</s>. And that which arises from it is its fruit.
If it be said that the fruit, namely contact, is also a <s>pramāṇa</s> with respect to cognition — that is not so, because in the context of <s>pramāṇa</s> as that which makes known (<s>jñāpaka</s>), it is improper to introduce <s>pramāṇa</s> as a causal factor (<s>kāraka</s>). For contact is a producer of cognition, not that which makes it known. <s>Pratyakṣa</s> and the other <s>pramāṇas</s> are presented for the ascertainment of the knowable (<s>prameya</s>), not as causes of the production of cognition. In that procedure, what is relevant to the topic is being discussed.
Even if one were to argue that since cognition too is knowable (<s>prameya</s>), and since it is being known as it arises, the contact that causes its arising is indeed that which makes it known — that is not so, because cognition is known by cognition itself, as they themselves accept. And contact is not cognition, since it is accepted as the producer of cognition.
If it be said that contact is a <s>pramāṇa</s> for the cognition of cognition because it is a causal condition (<s>nimitta</s>) — then why should there be any objection to <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit), the will of <s>Īśvara</s>, the blinking of eyes, and the like also being <s>pramāṇas</s>, since they too are causal conditions? And if cognition is knowable, then without accepting that the self is by nature pure consciousness, an infinite regress cannot be avoided.
If it be said that cognition is knowable merely by virtue of inhering in the self, and no other cognition is required so that no over-extension occurs — even so, a different definition of <s>pratyakṣa</s> must be stated for this, since the inherence of cognition in the self is not characterized by sense-contact and the like. And since contact has the production of cognition as its fruit, when there is an interval before that production, there is no immediacy between contact and cognition.
Therefore, even by virtue of that immediacy, cognition is not the fruit of contact. Likewise, it has been stated that the cognitions of avoidance and the like cannot be the fruit of the cognition of form and the like.
And because of deviation. Just as when many people have the same cognition regarding a single object such as a woman, one person has a cognition of acceptance, another of rejection, and another has neither — there the cognitions of avoidance and acceptance deviate. One and the same cognition deviates from both for someone. And that which deviates from something is not the fruit of that thing.
Moreover — since indifference is merely the absence of avoidance and acceptance, it is just an absence. And an absence cannot be the fruit of a <s>pramāṇa</s>, which is a real entity. And the cognitions of acceptance and rejection arise from <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion). In the absence of those causes, the absence of the effect follows — thus even when <s>pramāṇa</s>-cognition is present, the absence of cognitions of avoidance and acceptance constitutes indifference — therefore, due to this deviation, the cognitions of avoidance and the like are not the fruit.
Moreover — if <s>rāga</s>, <s>dveṣa</s>, and their absence were accepted as having the cognitions of acceptance and so forth as their fruit, then they would have to be accepted as <s>pramāṇas</s>. But if the fruit is the cognition of <s>Puruṣa</s> in the form of <s>cittavṛtti</s>, nothing is contradicted.
But it may be objected that the knowability of <s>cittavṛtti</s> is unestablished — for an instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) cannot itself be the object of action (<s>karma</s>). A sickle does not reap itself. This is not a fault. Because action and agent have different properties. The various causal factors (<s>kārakas</s>) cooperate for the accomplishment of action, mutually serving as object and subject. But action, merely by its existence, is the cause of the fruit — hence instrument-hood is figuratively attributed to it, not in the same way as to a causal factor proper. For if what is acting were also to be acted upon, the agent would become subordinate to action, and what is past could not be taught for the sake of the future.
Moreover — there would be the problem of infinite regress. If action were an instrument, then another action would be needed to accomplish it. For its causality cannot work without another action. And that other action would also be an instrument for yet another action, and so on — infinite regress. And therefore, because the series of actions would never cease, the fruit would never be accomplished. If the final action in the series could be the cause of the fruit without another action, then why object to the first one being so? But <s>cittavṛtti</s> is known because it is a manifestor (<s>abhivyañjaka</s>) — there is no fault.
And it is observed that manifestors such as a lamp serve as instruments precisely by being known in their own nature. So too with <s>cittavṛtti</s>. If it be objected that even though the sense organs are manifestors, they are not apprehended, and hence there is deviation — how so, given the commingling with things of the same class as consciousness?
For those who hold that the sense organs are material (<s>bhautika</s>) — since the eye is of the nature of fire (<s>taijasa</s>), due to the interpenetration with external light of the same class, there is non-discrimination even though it is being apprehended. Just as when the lights of many lamps interpenetrate, one cannot distinguish which radiance belongs to which lamp. So too with <s>śrotra</s> (hearing) and the rest.
Even for those who hold that the sense organs are non-material — since <s>vṛtti</s> is also a manifestor, there is sameness of class, and hence non-apprehension due to its being a manifestor. That is not so — because it is not manifest, since it has already been grasped by consciousness, and because it is not separated by an intervening medium. Even though the self is omnipresent, due to its subtlety and greater transparency, and because consciousness is not obstructed, <s>cittavṛtti</s> is apprehended. Therefore, through <s>cittavṛtti</s> as the <s>pramāṇa</s>, the cognition of <s>Puruṣa</s> too, having the form of that <s>vṛtti</s>, being experienced, is established as the fruit.
But for those who hold that <s>cittavṛtti</s> is not knowable through <s>pratyakṣa</s> — they lack a <s>pramāṇa</s> for apprehending the fruit! And if the fruit is apprehended, the implication is that cognition is established. But the fruit is not apprehended, since they do not accept the operation of <s>pramāṇa</s> in that regard. And if such operation is accepted, there is the problem of infinite regress! For the <s>pramāṇa</s> accepted for apprehending the fruit would itself have another fruit, and the <s>pramāṇa</s> for that would have yet another — and one would never reach a stopping point.
If no <s>pramāṇa</s> operates there, then since <s>pramāṇa</s> is absent, the non-existence of the fruit would follow. For where <s>pramāṇas</s>, which apprehend what exists, do not operate, we conclude that thing does not exist.
If it be said that even though not apprehended, that very cognition is the <s>pramāṇa</s> even for the fruit — no, because that would violate the nature of a manifestor. For a manifestor has never been seen to manifest while itself being apprehended. A torch does not transcend its own nature even on a mountain peak.
If it be said that while manifesting, it is also a <s>pramāṇa</s> even for the fruit — then what we desire is established! For <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and the like are apprehended as qualifiers of the <s>vṛtti</s>. 'I am attached,' 'I am averse' — even though this qualifies the I-cognition, it is apprehended precisely as something that exists or does not exist as a <s>vṛtti</s>, and thus the apprehension of <s>rāga</s> and the like as qualifiers of <s>vṛtti</s> is justified. Otherwise, there would be the problem of requiring another <s>pramāṇa</s> as with form and the like, and then infinite regress. Therefore, the mere conceit of those ignorant of the fruit of <s>pramāṇa</s>, who consider themselves learned, should be disregarded.

body.text: anumeyasya tulyajātīyeṣvanuvṛtto bhinnajātīyebhyo vyāvṛttaḥ saṁbandho yastadviṣayā sāmānyāvadhāraṇapradhānā vṛttiranumānam। yathā deśāntaraprāptergatimaccandratārakaṁ caitravat, vindhyaścāprāptiragatiḥ। āptena dṛṣṭo'numito vā'rthaparatrasvabodhasaṁkrāntaye śabdenopadiśyate, śabdāttadarthaviṣayā vṛttiḥ śroturāgamaḥ। yasyāśraddheyārtho vaktā na dṛṣṭānumitārthaḥ sa āgamaḥ plavate। mūlavaktari tu dṛṣṭānumitārthe nirviplavaḥ syāt ॥ 7 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>Anumāna</s> (inference) is the cognitive activity whose primary content is the ascertainment of a universal (<s>sāmānya</s>), directed toward that relation which persists among things of the same class (<s>tulyajātīya</s>) with respect to the inferendum (<s>anumeya</s>) and is excluded from things of different classes (<s>bhinnajātīya</s>). For example: the moon and stars possess movement because they reach different places, like <s>Caitra</s>; whereas the <s>Vindhya</s> mountain, because it does not reach [other places], is without movement. A thing seen or inferred by a trustworthy person (<s>āpta</s>) is taught through words (<s>śabda</s>) for the purpose of conveying one's own understanding to others; the cognitive activity of the listener directed toward the meaning of that thing, arising from the word, is <s>āgama</s> (verbal testimony). When the speaker's content is not credible—not based on what is directly perceived or inferred—that <s>āgama</s> is unstable. But when the original speaker's [teaching] is based on what is perceived or inferred, it would be unshakable. // 7 //

body.text:
vivaraṇam
anumānamathocyate- [anumeyasya tulyajātīyeṣvanuvṛtta iti । anumeyasya] [jijñāsita]dharmaviśiṣṭasya । taddharmavattayā [tulyajātīyeṣvanuvṛttaḥ] sadbhāvamātreṇa, [ [bhinnajātīyebhyaḥ] ] tadviruddhadharmakebhyo [vyāvṛttaḥ] -teṣvasan ityarthaḥ । [sambandha] iti । kaḥ sambandhaḥ ? kayorvā ? na hi sambandhināvanapekṣya sambandhaḥ sambandhatāmiyāt, yadasau prasiddhavaccocyate ‘ [ya] ’ iti ॥ nanu ca anumānasya prakṛtatvāt, liṅgaliṅginoḥ sambandhaḥ prasiddha eva-na-agamakatvāt । na kevalaḥ sambandho gamakaḥ । ucyate liṅgasyaiva sambandho vyāvṛttyanuvṛttyoḥ । kaḥ punarasau ? liṅgameva । na hi liṅgādanyadanuvṛttaṁ vyāvṛttaṁ ca । tacca gamakam । nanu liṅgamapi naiva gamakaṁ liṅgisambandhānapekṣaṁ, yadi cānapekṣitaliṅkaliṅgisambandhaṁ gamakaṁ, yatkiñcidgamakaṁ syāt, tasmāt liṅgaliṅgisambandho vaktavyaḥ ॥
na-uktatvāt ॥ ['anumeyasya tulyajātīyeṣvanuvṛttaḥ'] ityādinaivoktatvāt । na hyanumeyenāsaṁbaddhaṁ liṅginā tatsadṛśajātīyeṣvanuvartate, bhinnajātīyebhyo vā nivartate । tasmāt ya iti ca prasiddhameva saṁbandhamanuvadati ॥
[tadviṣayā] -evamanvayavyatirekaviśiṣṭasaṁbandhasaṁbandhiviṣayā [vṛttiḥ sāmānyāvadhāraṇapradhānā] -liṅgisāmānyāvadhāraṇapradhānā, [anumānam ॥]
[yathā deśāntaraprāptergatimaccandratārakaṁ caitravaditi ॥] yadyapi lakṣaṇābhidhānamātreṇa tadabhivyaktiḥ, tathāpyudāharaṇapratyudāharaṇapradarśanādatitarāmityudāharaṇapratipādanam । tatra gatimaccandratārakamiti candratārakasya gatimattvamanumeyam । tatsamānajātīyeṣvanuvṛttā deśāntaraprāptirgatimatsu caitrādiṣu, bhinnajātīyebhyaścāgatebhyo vindhyādibhyo vyāvṛtteti avyabhicarantī । nityaṁ gatimatā saṁbandhāt ।
tasmāditthaṁjātīyakamavinābhāvena saṁbaddhaṁ saṁbandhyantaraṁ gamayati । yathā vadhyaghātaka(kṛdi)kāryakāraṇādi ॥
bhavatu tāvadaviruddhānāṁ nityasaṁbandhāddeśāntaraprātaptyādīnāṁ gamyagamakatā, vadhyaghātakodīnāṁ tu saṁbandhābhāve kathamityucyate gamyagamakabhāvaḥ (bhāvena) ?
tatrāpi nityasaṁbandhādadoṣaḥ । na hyanyatrāpi prāptilakṣaṇaḥ saṁbandho'bhipreyate । sāmānyato dṛṣṭā(nu)bhāvaprasaṅgāt । na hi candratārakādiṣu deśāntaraprāpte: prāptilakṣaṇasaṁbandhaḥ pratyakṣeṇa gṛhyate । agṛhyamāṇaścedgamakaḥ sarvaṁ sarvasya gamakaṁ syāt । na hi kiṁcitkenacidasaṁbaddham, ākāśādīnāṁ sarvatra bhāvāt ॥
tasmādgamyagamakabuddhyutpattihetureva saṁbandho'numānaviṣaye । tathā ca vadhyaghātakayorapi anyatara(rā)bhāvadarśane'nyatarābhāvo gamyata ityanumānameva । yasyāpyucite deśe abhāvadarśanādanyatra bhāvo gamyate । yathā ghātakadarśanena vadhyābhāvo'numīyate । caitrasya jīvato gṛhe , abhāva(gṛhyabhāva)darśane bahirbhāvaśvati ।
nanu cābhāvārthāpattī ete, nānumāne, (na) lakṣaṇāsaṅgateḥ, gavādivat ॥ na-yathoktalakṣaṇopapatteḥ- vadhyaghātakayorvirodhalakṣaṇaḥ saṁbandhaḥ । yatra yatra ghātakabhāvastatra tatra vadhyābhāva evetyavinābhāvaḥ । na hi vadhyasyābhāvaṁ ghātaka(ka)bhāvo vyabhicarati । vadhyasya vā bhāve ghātaka(ka)bhāvam, agnibhāvamiva dhūmabhāvaḥ ॥
kathaṁ punaravagamyate ghātakabhāvadarśanādeva tadgocare vadhyasyābhāvabuddhiriti ? na punaḥ sadupalambhakapramāṇānāṁ ghātaka iva vadhye vyāpārābhāvāditi ॥
ucyate-ghātakabhāve vyāpṛ(pyāvṛ)tapramāṇasyeva vadhyābhāvabudhyutpati:, dhūmabhāve vyāpṛ(vṛ)tapramāṇasyevāgnibhāvabuddhyutpatti:, tathā ghātakaviśeṣavyāpṛ(vṛ)tapramāṇasya vadhyaviśeṣābhāvabuddhyutpattiḥ, dhūmaviśeṣavyāpṛ(vṛ)tapramāṇasyevāgniviśeṣabuddhiriti । abhāvapramāṇavādinastu sarvatra pramāṇābhāvasyāviśiṣṭatvādvirodhiviśeṣa darśanānuvidhānaṁ virodhyantarābhāvadarśanasyānupapannaṁ, liṅgaviśeṣānuvidhānamiva liṅgiviśeṣadarśanasya । na hi sadupalambhakapramāṇavyāpārābhāvasya kaścidviśeṣaḥ, yena viśeṣabuddhistadviśeṣamanuvidhīyate ॥
atha jijñāsite viśeṣe sadupalambhakapramāṇābhāvāditi cet-tanna-asataḥ smṛtīcchādisahabhāvāpekṣānupapatte: । na hyasat sahāyāpekṣayā kāryaṁ nirvartayaddṛṣṭaṁ śaśaviṣāṇādi । dṛṣṭamiheti cet-na-vipratipattisthānatve dṛṣṭāntābhāvāt । tulyamiti cet-na-ghaṭādeḥ sato'pekṣādarśanāt ॥
na cāpi nirvyāpārasyāvastutvādabhāvasya pramāṇabhāvo yuktaḥ । na hi nirastavyāpārakaṁ kiṁcit kāryārambhakaṁ dṛśyate loke । tasmādvyāpārarūpapramāṇajanitā prameyābhāvabuddhiḥ, prameyaviṣayatvāt ghaṭādibuddhivat । tathā ca vastutvāt pravṛttinivṛttihetutvāt । vipakṣaḥ śaśaviṣāṇādiḥ । tathā abhāva[pramā]pramāṇā(ṇa)bhāvajanitā na bhavati, yathā'bhihitahetudṛṣṭāntadarśanāt । (nena) ॥
ghātakadarśanaṁ vadhyābhāvabuddherliṅgaṁ tadbhāvabhāvitvādagnyādibuddhinimittadhūmādibuddhivat saṁśayanivartakatvācca । vadhyābhāvabuddhirvā liṅgajanitā niścayarūpatvādagnibuddhibaditi ॥
iha ghaṭo nāstīti kila nānumānaṁ liṅgaliṅgisaṁbandhāgrahaṇāt । na hi yathā'gnyādibuddherdhūmādiliṅgānveṣaṇaṁ tatheha nāsti ghaṭa ityatra liṅgānveṣaṇamasti । progava liṅgānveṣaṇāt budhyutpatteḥ ॥
naiṣa doṣaḥ । ihapratyayākārasyaiva liṅgatvāt । na hi prathamameva liṅgabudhyupajanane sati liṅgānveṣaṇaṁ bhavati । ihetyākāroparañjitā buddhirliṅgam । umuparañjakavyatiriktaghaṭādyabhāvabuddherghātakabuddhivadeva । virodhalakṣaṇa eva cātrāpi sambandhaḥ ॥
yatra punaraviruddhānyuparañjakāni tatrāstitvabuddheḥ । etenaivārthāpatteranumānatvaṁ vyākhyātamavinābhāvena saṁbandhena । tatrāpi jīvato hi devadattasya gṛhābhāve bahirbhāvaḥ, yadā gṛhe bhāvaḥ na tadā bahirbhāva ityanyatareṇānumānam । sākṣāt dṛśyamānabahirbhāvābhyantarābhāvatvaṁ dṛṣṭāntaḥ । vṛttyuparañjakānuparañjakatvena hyabhāvagrahaṇasyābhihito hetuḥ ॥
agnyādāvapi dahanādiśaktigrahaṇamanumānameva । kāryanirvarttakayoravinābhāvasaṁbandhasyātmani dṛṣṭatvādbhujyādau । dṛśyate hi pratyagātmāni śakto'hamidaṁ kāryaṁ kartumaśakto'hamityātmavadātmaviśeṣaṇasya śaktergrahaṇam । śaktinirvartyameva dahanādikāryamapīlyanumānasiddhiḥ ।
nanu cābhāvasya pratyakṣatāmupagāyati kecit । yathā kilādarśakena pradīpādinā sati gṛhyamāṇe vastuni na tadavayavini yadupalabhyate tannāstītyevaṁ sata: prakāśakaṁ pramāṇamasadapi prakāśayati । tathā codāharanti-anaṅkitaṁ vāsa ānayetyuktaḥ praviśya bhāṇḍāgāram aṅkitānaṅkitavāsassannidhāvaṅkitavāsograhaṇenaiva pratyakṣeṇāṅgābhāvaviśiṣṭaṁ vāsa upalabhyānayati । tasmāt pratyakṣa evābhāvo lakṣaṇāntarānupapatteriti ॥
tanna-buddhyākāreṇārthāvadhāraṇānṛtatvaprasaṅgāt । yadākārā hi buddhistasya pratyakṣāvadhriyamāṇātmatābhyupagamyate । yathā nīlaṁ vastu pītamityatrāpi viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyasaṁbandhapratyayo mithyāṁ prāpnoti । tadyatheha ghaṭo nāstīti ihapradeśasya ghaṭābhāvenāsati saṁbandhe saṁbandhapratyayaḥ ; na hi ghaṭābhāvasyehapradeśasya cā [prāpta]prāptilakṣaṇaḥ samavāyābhidhāno vā saṁbandhastairabhyupeyate । yatheha devadatta iti । tasmādabhāva(ve)pratyayava(yā)nnīlaṁ vastviti viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyasaṁbandhapratyayo'pi saṁbandhapratyayatvānmithyā prasajyeta ॥
yathā cāsatyapīhadeśaghaṭābhāvasaṁbandhe sabandhapratītistathaivānīle'pi vastunyasatyeva nīlatvasaṁbandhe nīlatvasaṁbandhapratyayaḥ prāpnoti, tathā saṁbandhiṣvapi । athāstyeva saṁbandhaḥ, dviṣṭhatā virudhyeta saṁbandhasya । abhāvasyāvastutvābhyupagamāt ।
athāpyekaśataṁ ṣaṣṭhyarthā iti yāvat ṣaṣṭhyarthaḥ saṁbandha iṣyeta, tadā dvividha eva saṁbandhaḥ samavāyākhyaḥ saṁyogākhyaśceti na yujyate ॥
athai(tatha)kaśatasyapi ṣaṣṭhyarthanāmubhayānta:pātitvamucyeta-na-abhāve'nyatarasyāpyasambhavāt ।
kiñca(ntva)nyat । iha nabhasi kusumaṁ nāstīti saṁbandhino nabhaso'pyapratyakṣatvāt gaganakusumābhāvasyāpratyakṣatvaṁ prāpnoti । athāpratyakṣatvameveti cedāpatitaṁ gaganakusumābhāvavadapratyakṣatvamiha bhūpradeśe ghaṭābhāvasyāpi । viśeṣo vaktavyaḥ ॥
atha vyomno'pratyakṣatvāditi-tanna-puṣpasya patato nabhasyastitvadarśanādvyomāpratyakṣatvamahetuḥ । yathaiva nipatatkusumasadbhāve vyomāpratyakṣatvamahetustathā sadbhāvaviruddhagrahaṇe'pyahetuḥ syāt । athākāśāpratyakṣatvādeveti cet, asaṁbandhamapi yatkiñcidvyavahitāpratyakṣatvādi so'pi hetuḥ syāt । atha nabhaḥkusumābhāvaḥ pratyakṣa iti cet-indriyārthasannikarṣānarthakyaṁ sarvatra prasajyeta । tathā ca satyasannikṛṣṭopalabdheḥ sarveṣāṁ sarvajñatvaṁ prasaktam ॥
athānumeyaṁ tatreti cet-nabha:kusumābhāvavadiha ghaṭābhāvasyāviśeṣādānumānikatva(kīya)meva siddham । evaṁ ca satyabhāvapramāṇavādino'pi vyavahitaviprakṛṣṭodakādāvanalādyabhāvasyānumeyatvādiha ghaṭabhāvo'pi tatsāmānyādanumānagrāhya eveti niścetuṁ yuktam ॥
[vindhyaścāprāptaragati] riti ca prayogāntaram । agatirvindhya iti pratijñānam । aprāpteriti hetuḥ । caitravaditi kākalocanavadubhayatra saṁbadhyate । [gatimaccandratāraka] mityanena sādhardhyeṇa, [vindhyaścāprāpte] rityanena vaidharmyeṇa saṁbandhaḥ । evaṁ ca satyanvayavyatirekā(ka)darśanakṛto na doṣaḥ ॥
athavaitasminprayoge vyatirekaviparyayadarśanena doṣābhāva ityupanyastam । lakṣaṇasya ca lakṣyaviśeṣeṇohyatvādadoṣaḥ ॥
āptaḥ parānujighṛkṣāprayukto doṣarahito dṛṣṭānumitārtha: । [tena dṛṣṭo vā anumito vārthaḥ paratra] śrotṛviśeṣe [svabodhasaṅkrāntaye] svādhigamasaṁkramaṇāya [śabdena] śabda iti vākyaṁ tato viśiṣṭārthapratipatteḥ । tasmāttadupadiṣṭādvākyāt । { [tadarthaviṣayā] ] vākyārthaviṣayā yā [cittavṛttiḥ] sā anumānavadeva sāmānyāvadhāraṇapradhānā ॥
itthamāptyādidharmagrahaṇapūrvikā [śroturāgamaḥ] , na vaktuḥ । dṛṣṭānumitārtho hi vaktā, tasya laiṅgikamaindriyakaṁ vā tajjñānam । śrotureva tu śravaṇapūrvakaṁ niścitaṁ vijñānaṁ laiṅgikaindriyakavyatiriktam । sa [āgamaḥ] [na] pratyakṣamindriyā[viṣaya]- viṣayatvāt yathābhihitaliṅgaliṅgasaṁbandhanirapekṣatvācca nānumānam । na hi svargāpūrvadevatādiśabda(bde')rthānvitaṁ jñānamāsāditaliṅgāliṅgisaṁbandhapurassaramupajāyate । phalaṁ tu sarvatra pauruṣeyo vṛttibedha eva ॥
[yasya] āgamasya [vaktā] āgamākhyavṛttyutpattinimite śabdoccāraṇāt āgamasya praye.āgopanyāsena pratipāditaṁ phalaṁ tu pūrvavadeva । yadapyeka eva praye.āgasta(thā)dāpi sādhyasādhanābhavamātrasya vivakṣitatvānna viparītavyatirekadarśanādityucyate ॥
aśraddheyārthavaktrabhihitatvenāgama eva viśeṣyate । kathamasāvaśraddheyārtho vaktetyata āha- [na dṛṣṭo'numito vārthaḥ] tena vaktrā । śiṣṭalokaprasiddhānyathāpratipādanāt buddhārhatādiḥ । na hi rāgādidoṣānupahatānta:karaṇa: prasiddhamanyathā nirvarṇayati । [sa āgamaḥ plavate] ābhāsībhavati ॥
yadyapi pratyakṣānumānaviṣayābhāsadarśanaṁ svaśabdena na kṛtaṁ, tathāpyāgamābhāsopapradarśanenaiva pūrvatrāpi yathābhihitalakṣaṇaviparītatvena pratyakṣānumānābhāsādi draṣṭavyamarthāduktam ॥
[mūlavaktari tu] ādyavaktarīśvare tannimitte ya āgamaḥ sa viplavanimittābhāvānnirviplavaḥ syāt । yathārtha(ya)vaktṛvat ॥
upamānaṁ (mānaṁ) śabdapūrvakam । tadāgamāntaḥpatitvānna pramāṇāntaram । yathā gauriva gavaya iti vanecarābhihitādeva vākyādavadhṛtasādṛśyasya punarvane gavayadarśane'pi pūrvaśrutavākyopasthāpitasādṛśyasmaraṇamātrameva nādhikam । sādṛśyaṁ tu vākyādeva pūrvapratipannam ॥
nāpi saṁjñāsaṁjñisaṁbandhapratipattita eva mānaṁ, tasyā api tadvākyādevāvagatatvāt । na hi gaurityetāvatānavagatagavayanāmakasya vanagatagavayadarśino'pi gavayo'yamiti saṁjñāsaṁjñisaṁbandhāvabodho bhavati ॥
tasmādgauriva gavaya iti gavayaśabdo'pi tadvākye'pekṣitavyaḥ । tathā ca sati pūrvaśrutādeva vākyāt sarvaṁ pratītam । athāpi syādayaṁ(dasya)gavaya iti na pūrvabuddhaviṣayamiti-tadapi tatrabhavatāmapi paricodanaparihāramavapaśyatāmapi pīḍitakaivale[kaule]yakavṛttikoṇe'vasthānamiva lakṣyate ॥
tathā hi-deśakālasannikarṣaviprakarṣadibhedanānekopamānabheda: prasajyeta । tathāstviti cet-tatpūrvadhiyaivātatvamantarnihitasamastaviśeṣameva hi vā neyau pūrvamupapāditam । nahi gauriyukta deśakālādiviśeṣābhāve na gośabdādarthapratipati: ॥
kiṁ cānyat-na hi saṁjñāsaṁjñisaṁbandhapratipattirupamānaṁ, yena hyupamīyate tadupamānaṁ, sādṛśyajñānaṁ hi tat । na hi nāmināmasaṁbandhapratipattyā kiṁcidupamīyate uttarakālatvāt । avadhṛtasādṛśyasya hi paśvāda(sya)yaṁ gavaya ityevaṁ so'pi nipatati ॥
evaṁ tarhi syādaśabdapūrvakaṁ pramāṇāntaraṁ, yathā gavayadarśanādetatsadṛśo gauriti grāmīṇasya buddhiḥ-tadapi na-prameyābhāvāt । sati hi prameye sadupalambhakatvābhimatasya pramāṇasya vyāpāraḥ, na hi gogavayayorvyāvṛttamanuvṛttaṁ ca vastutaḥ sādṛśyaṁ nāmaikamasti ॥
nanu ca sādṛśyabuddhirasyeva, nāsau nirālambanā bhavitumahati । satyamevaṁ tatraiva vicāraṇā-kimasau vanayūthādipratyayavat ? atha ghaṭādibuddhivaditi । kiṁ cātaḥ ? yadi vanapratyayavadbhavettadā yathaiva viśiṣṭasanniveśānugatā mahīruhā evātmavyatirekeṇāvidyamānavanapratyayahetavastathaiva gogavayāvayavā eva dvayadarśanasmṛtyapekṣayā svātmavyatirekeṇāsataḥ sādṛśyasya pratītau kāraṇamiti prāptamavastutvam ॥
atha punarghaṭādipratyayavadvastutvaṁ pramāṇatvaṁ ca, tadā syāditi ॥
tatra kīdṛśaṁ vastviti vicāryate - kiṁ gogavayayoranuvṛttamekaṁ sādṛśyaṁ gotvagavayatvābhyāmanyat ? te eva vānyonyaviśiṣṭe, yadi vā tābhyāṁ bhinne gogavayādhāre dve sādṛśye parasparānapekṣe, sāpekṣe vā ?
kiṁ vyaktireva sā'nyatarajātiviśiṣṭā vā, kiṁ jātiḥ, sā cānyataravyaktiviśiṣṭā, vyaktidvayaviśiṣṭā vā, saṁbandho vaiteṣāṁ yathāvikalpayogamityekaikānyonyaviśiṣṭaviśeṣaṇatvādinā bhūyāṁso'nye'pi vikalpā udbhāvayitavyāḥ । tatra yadyekaṁ sādṛśyamubhayagataṁ, tadā nopameyatvamekatvāt, yathā gauriva gairiti ।
atha tenānyataravyaktirupamīyeta-naitadapi-svātmagatatvāt gauriva gotvena । atha tadvatyā vyaktyā vyaktyantaramupamīyeta-naitadapi-na hi gotvaṁ khaṇḍamuṇḍopameyatvakāraṇam । atha dharmāntarāpekṣayā sādṛśyaṁ tadbuddheḥ kāraṇamiti, naṣṭaṁ tarhi sādṛśyaṁ, sa evāstu dharmaḥ tadbuddheḥ kiṁ te sādṛśyahatakena kalpitena ॥
kiṁ ca-sa cāpyapekṣyamāṇo dharmaḥ kimekaḥ sādṛśyavadubhayatra, atha bhinna ityevamādivikalpāḥ syurityasambhavaḥ pūrvavadeva । atha bhinnaṁ sādṛśyamucyeta-tacca na-bhedādeva, na hi bhavati gaurivāśva iti । yathaivaikaikatvādaghaṭamānatā tathā bahubhirapekṣyamāṇaiḥ । etena jātivyaktisambandhādayaḥ pūrvavikalpitāḥ pratyuktāḥ ॥
atha buddhyutpatyanyathānupapatyā sādṛśyakalpanā, satyevaṁ vanavivarapūrvadakṣiṇottarādibuddhiyogānyathānubhavāt [nyathānupapatyā]vastutvaṁ kiṁ na kalpyate । syādeṣā tava buddhirvṛkṣādaya eva tatra tadbuddhijanmahetava iti । yadyevaṁ mithyāpratyayo gavayena sadṛśī gauriti vanabuddhivat । atha ye vyāvṛttāḥ ka ihopamārtha: gaurivāśva iti । athobhaye'pi te'vayavā vyāvṛttānuvṛttātmānastaduddhihetavaḥ, tathāpi vanapratyayavadeva prāptam ॥
tasmāt parīkṣyamāṇaṁ nātivimardanakṣamamiti ta evāvayavā ubhayatre.opalabhyamānā bhūyāṁsaḥ sādṛśyabuddheḥ kāraṇaṁ vanabuddheriva pādapāḥ [iti] nopamānaṁ nāma pramāṇāntaramiti siddham ॥
nāpi prameyadvitvāt pramāṇadvitvakalpanam । kutaḥ ? pramāṇavaśādarthapratīteḥ । na hyarthavaśāt pramāṇakalpanā । yadi cārthavaśāt pramāṇakalpanā syāt, adhunā tanna śakyam, janānāmasarvajñatvāt । caityavandanāt svargo bhavatītyatra caityavandanasya svargahetutvabuddheḥ pratyakṣānumānāviṣayatvānmithyātvaṁ syāt । tadarthaṁ vā pramāṇāntarakalpanam ॥
atha sā buddhiranumānaphalamiti cet-pramāṇādanyatra phalaprasaṅgaḥ, evaṁ śa(ka)raṇatrayādivākyārthaviṣayabuddhirapīti ॥
nāpi cātra pramāṇalakṣaṇanirūpaṇatātparyaṁ, prasiddhapramāṇādivṛttinirodhābhyupāyābhipradarśanaparatvāt । ata eva na sūtrakāraḥ sūtrayāñcakāra । bhāṣyakāreṇa tu kiñciprasiddhānuvādamātramavalambitamiti tadanusaraṇena kimapi jalpitamiti ॥ 6 - 7 ॥
body.translated_text:
Commentary (<s>Vivaraṇa</s>)

Inference is now discussed. ['That which is present in similar instances of what is to be inferred' means:] of what is to be inferred (<s>anumeya</s>)—that is, what is characterized by the property under investigation (<s>jijñāsita-dharma</s>). ['Present in similar instances'] means present merely in terms of existence in things that possess that property. ['Excluded from dissimilar instances']—that is, absent from those possessing the contrary property. ['Relation' (<s>sambandha</s>)]—what is this relation? And between what two things? For a relation cannot attain the status of being a relation without reference to the relata. It is stated as something well-known by the word 'which' (<s>ya</s>).

Objection: Since inference is the topic, the relation between the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) and what possesses the mark (<s>liṅgin</s>) is well-known—why state it? Because the relation alone is not indicative (<s>gamaka</s>). Reply: The relation of the inferential mark itself consists in positive and negative concomitance (<s>anuvṛtti</s> and <s>vyāvṛtti</s>). What then is that? It is the inferential mark itself. For nothing other than the mark is what is positively and negatively concomitant. And that is what is indicative. Objection: But even the inferential mark is not indicative without reference to the relation with the thing possessing the mark. And if it were indicative without reference to the mark-marked relation, anything would be indicative of anything. Therefore the relation between mark and marked must be stated.

Because it has already been stated. By the statement 'present in similar instances of what is to be inferred' etc., it is already stated. For that which is unrelated to what is to be inferred, to the thing possessing the mark, does not occur in instances similar to it, nor does it exclude itself from dissimilar instances. Therefore the word 'which' merely restates the well-known relation.

['The cognitive activity whose object is that']—thus, the cognitive activity whose object is the relation qualified by positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>) and the relata, ['predominantly characterized by the ascertainment of the universal']—predominantly characterized by the ascertainment of the universal of the thing possessing the mark, ['is inference' (<s>anumāna</s>)].

['For example: the moon and stars possess motion, because they reach different locations, like <s>Caitra</s>.'] Although the mere statement of the definition makes it manifest, nevertheless, through the presentation of examples and counter-examples it becomes even clearer—hence the presentation of examples. Therein, 'the moon and stars possess motion'—the motion of the moon and stars is what is to be inferred. 'Reaching different locations' is present in similar instances—i.e., in moving things like <s>Caitra</s> etc.—and excluded from dissimilar instances, namely from non-moving things like the <s>Vindhya</s> mountains etc.—thus it is non-deviating (<s>avyabhicārin</s>). Because of its invariable relation with what possesses motion.

Therefore, something of this kind, related by invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>), indicates another relatum. Just as in the case of the killed and the killer, effect and cause, etc.

Granted that for non-contradictory things like reaching different locations, the relation of indicated and indicator exists through permanent connection. But for the killed and the killer, in the absence of a relation, how can the relation of indicated and indicator be asserted?

Even there, there is no fault due to permanent connection. For elsewhere too, a relation characterized by physical contact is not what is intended, because of the unwanted consequence of inference based on mere general observation. For in the case of the moon and stars, the contact-characterized relation of reaching different locations is not grasped by perception. And if what is not grasped were indicative, everything would be indicative of everything. For nothing is unrelated to anything, since space etc. exist everywhere.

Therefore, in the domain of inference, the relation is merely the cause of the arising of the cognition of indicated and indicator. And thus, even for the killed and the killer, when the absence of one is observed, the absence of the other is inferred—this itself is inference. And for one whose absence is inferred from the observation of absence in an appropriate place, its existence elsewhere is inferred. Just as from the sight of the killer, the absence of the victim is inferred. When <s>Caitra</s> is alive, from observing his absence in the house, his existence outside is inferred.

Objection: These are cases of <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), not inference, since they do not fit the definition—like a cow etc. Reply: No—because they fit the stated definition. The relation between killed and killer is characterized by contradiction (<s>virodha</s>). Wherever there is the existence of the killer, there is the absence of the killed—this is invariable concomitance. For the existence of the killer does not deviate from the absence of the killed. Nor does the existence of the killed from the existence of the killer, just as the existence of smoke does not deviate from the existence of fire.

How then is it ascertained that merely from seeing the existence of the killer, the cognition of the absence of the killed in that domain arises? Not because, like perception, means of valid knowledge that apprehend what exists have no operation regarding the killed, as they do regarding the killer?

Reply: Just as the cognition of the absence of the killed arises for one whose means of knowledge is engaged with the existence of the killer, and just as the cognition of the existence of fire arises for one whose means of knowledge is engaged with the existence of smoke—similarly, for one whose means of knowledge is engaged with a particular killer, there arises the cognition of the absence of a particular victim, just as for one whose means of knowledge is engaged with a particular smoke, there arises the cognition of a particular fire. But for those who maintain that absence is a means of valid knowledge, since the absence of a means of knowledge that apprehends what exists is undifferentiated everywhere, the cognition of the absence of a particular contrary thing following upon the observation of a particular contrary thing is untenable—just as the perception of a particular thing possessing a mark following upon a particular mark. For the absence of the operation of a means of knowledge that apprehends what exists has no distinguishing feature by which a particular cognition would follow that particular feature.

If one objects: 'Because of the absence of a means of knowledge apprehending what exists regarding a particular thing under investigation'—this is not so, because the dependence on co-existing factors like memory, desire, etc., of what is non-existent is untenable. For nothing non-existent, like a hare's horn, is seen to accomplish an effect through dependence on auxiliary factors. If one says 'it is seen here'—no, because in a case that is a matter of dispute, there is no example. If one says 'it is the same'—no, because dependence is observed even in the case of existing things like pots.

Nor is it proper that absence, being without action and without substance, should have the status of a means of valid knowledge. For nothing devoid of causal operation is seen in the world to initiate an effect. Therefore, the cognition of the absence of the object of knowledge is produced by a means of valid knowledge in the form of an operation, because it has an object of knowledge as its content, like the cognition of a pot etc. And this is so because, being a real thing, it is the cause of engagement and disengagement. The counter-example is a hare's horn etc. Furthermore, the cognition of absence is not produced by the absence of a means of valid knowledge, as can be seen from the stated reasons and examples.

The seeing of the killer is the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) for the cognition of the absence of the killed, because it is present when that cognition is present, like the cognition of smoke being the cause of the cognition of fire; and because it removes doubt. Or, the cognition of the killed's absence, being produced by an inferential mark, has the form of certainty, like the cognition of fire.

'There is no pot here'—this indeed is not inference, because of the non-apprehension of the relation between mark and marked. For just as in the cognition of fire etc. one searches for marks like smoke etc., so here in 'there is no pot' there is no search for a mark. Because the cognition arises prior to the search for a mark.

This is not a fault. Because the very form of the cognition 'here' serves as the mark. For the search for a mark does not occur when the cognition of the mark has already arisen first. The cognition tinged with the form 'here' is the mark. The cognition of the absence of a pot etc., distinct from the coloring factor, is just like the cognition of the killer. And here too the relation is characterized precisely by contradiction.

But where the coloring factors are non-contradictory, there is a cognition of existence. By this very reasoning, <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) is explained as being inference, through the relation of invariable concomitance. There too: if <s>Devadatta</s> is alive and absent from the house, his existence outside follows. When he is in the house, he is not outside—this is inference through one of the pair. The instance of directly observed external existence and internal absence is the example. For the reason for the apprehension of absence has been stated as the presence or absence of the coloring factor of the cognition.

Even in the case of fire etc., the apprehension of the capacity for burning etc. is inference itself. Because the invariable relation between an effect and what produces it is observed in oneself, as in the arm etc. For one observes in one's own self the apprehension of capacity as a qualification of the self: 'I am able to do this act, I am unable'—just as the self, so the capacity as a qualifier of the self. And burning etc. is precisely the effect produced by that capacity—thus the establishment through inference.

Now, some maintain that absence is perceptible. They claim: when, in the presence of a revealer like a lamp, a thing is being perceived, that which is not perceived among its parts 'does not exist'—thus the means of knowledge that illuminates what exists also illuminates what does not exist. And they give this example: one who is told 'bring an unmarked garment' enters the storehouse, and in the presence of both marked and unmarked garments, merely by perceiving the marked garments through perception, apprehends a garment characterized by the absence of marks, and brings it. Therefore, absence is perceptible, since no other definition is tenable.

This is not so—because the unwanted consequence that the determination of objects by the form of cognition would be false would follow. For whatever form the cognition has, that is accepted as its perceptually determined nature. Just as 'the object is blue,' even in the case of 'it is yellow,' the relational cognition of qualifier and qualified would become false. Similarly, 'there is no pot here'—in this case, when there is no relation between 'this place' and 'the absence of a pot,' the relational cognition would be false. For those thinkers do not accept a relation characterized by contact or called 'inherence' (<s>samavāya</s>) between the absence of a pot and this place. Just as in 'here is <s>Devadatta</s>.' Therefore, from the cognition of absence, even the relational cognition of qualifier and qualified such as 'the object is blue' would become false, because it is a relational cognition.

And just as the relational cognition arises even when the relation between this place and the absence of a pot does not exist, so too even when the object is not blue, the relational cognition of blueness would arise when the relation of blueness does not exist; and similarly regarding the relata. But if the relation does exist, the two-place nature of the relation would be contradicted, since absence is accepted as non-substantial.

Even if the genitive case is taken to express the relation, and thus the genitive-meaning is accepted as the relation—even then, since relation is of only two kinds, called 'inherence' (<s>samavāya</s>) and 'conjunction' (<s>saṃyoga</s>), this is not tenable.

Even if the genitive-meaning is said to fall between both—this is not so, because in the case of absence, neither of the two is possible.

Furthermore, in the statement 'there is no flower in the sky,' since the sky too is imperceptible as a relatum, the absence of a sky-flower would become imperceptible. If one says 'let it be imperceptible'—then the same imperceptibility, like that of the absence of a sky-flower, would follow for the absence of a pot in this piece of ground. A distinguishing feature must be stated.

If one says 'because the sky is imperceptible'—this is not so, because the perception of the sky's existence through a falling flower shows that the sky's imperceptibility is not the reason. Just as the imperceptibility of the sky is not the reason when there is the existence of a falling flower, so too it should not be the reason when there is the apprehension of what contradicts existence. If one says 'precisely because the sky is imperceptible'—then even something unrelated, such as the imperceptibility of something spatially separated, would also be a reason. If one says 'the absence of a sky-flower is perceptible'—then the purposelessness of sense-object contact would follow everywhere. And if that were so, since the cognition of what is not in contact would obtain, the omniscience of all would follow.

If one says 'it is to be inferred there'—then, since there is no difference between the absence of a sky-flower and the absence of a pot here, its character as being inferential is established. And this being so, even for those who maintain that absence is a means of valid knowledge, since the absence of fire etc. in concealed, distant water etc. is to be inferred, the absence of a pot here, being of the same kind, should properly be determined as graspable only by inference.

['And the <s>Vindhya</s> has not reached, hence it lacks motion'] is another formulation. 'The <s>Vindhya</s> lacks motion' is the thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>).
