Therefore, "for the mind whose activities have been restrained by the twofold means of practice and detachment described above, how is it described"—how is its definition stated? "By the accompaniment of <s>vitarka</s>, <s>vicāra</s>, <s>ānanda</s>, and the form of <s>asmitā</s>, it is <s>saṃprajñāta</s>." The word 'accompaniment' (<s>anugama</s>) should be connected with each: by the accompaniment of <s>vitarka</s>, by the accompaniment of <s>vicāra</s>, by the accompaniment of <s>ānanda</s>, by the accompaniment of the form of <s>asmitā</s>. The word 'form' (<s>rūpa</s>) means 'merely,' serving to indicate the exclusion of the three preceding properties from the fourth.
"<s>Vitarka</s> is the mind's gross engagement with its object." The gross intermixture—the first interaction of the mind with its object as it transforms into the form of the object—that is <s>vitarka</s>. "The subtle is <s>vicāra</s>"—the connection is: the engagement is subtle. "<s>Ānanda</s> is joy"—<s>vicāra</s> is a still more subtle engagement, the third. Being blissful is the distinguishing feature. "The unified awareness is <s>asmitā</s>"—for one who has attained the state of his own ground-nature, <s>asmitā</s>, <s>asmitā</s> is mere cognition-ness, being of a single form. And he will illustrate: 'He knows that atomic self; he is aware only of "I am" this much.'
Objection: <s>Asmitā</s> will be listed among the <s>kleśas</s>: '<s>Asmitā</s> is the seeming identity of the powers of seeing and the instrument of seeing' (YS 2.6). How then can <s>samādhi</s> be accompanied by a <s>kleśa</s> in the form of <s>asmitā</s>? Reply: Even so, because <s>asmitā</s> manifests the form of its own deeper cause excellently and because it involves the withdrawal from all other objects, there is no fault in its being a form of <s>samādhi</s>.
Alternatively, even if the object in the form of <s>asmitā</s> is <s>avidyā</s>, the <s>yogin</s>'s cognition is not itself <s>avidyā</s>. For in the desire to know another's mind, the other's <s>avidyā</s>-nature [does not transfer]. One who grasps a cognition of another's mind does not become infected with <s>avidyā</s> through the defect of an object that has the form of another's ignorance.
As for the <s>kleśa</s>—it is specifically conjoined with erroneous cognition (<s>viparyaya</s>), as in 'I go' or 'I am thin.' Since <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> are subordinated in the <s>yogin</s>'s mind, it is not so [for the <s>yogin</s>].
Thereof, each former [<s>samādhi</s>] is accompanied by the properties of its own subsequent [stages]. Each latter is devoid of the properties of its former [stages]. Since this <s>saṃprajñāta samādhi</s> is accompanied by this fourfold set of properties, this is its definition—the <s>sūtra</s> is for the purpose of definition. In common usage too, whatever is accompanied by a distinctive property is defined by that—as a cow is defined by a dewlap and the like.
Lest anyone suspect that these <s>samādhis</s> are without support, from the statement of '<s>asmitā</s> alone,' he says: "All of these have a support." As for one who thinks that <s>asmitā</s> means 'being without conceptual construction'—that is wrong, because the word <s>asmitā</s> is well-established in the sense of ego-sense. Thus he says: 'The sense of being is <s>asmitā</s>.' // 17 //

body.text: athāsaṁprajñātaḥ samādhiḥ kimupāyaḥ kiṁsvabhāvo veti –
body.translated_text: Then, what is the means and what is the nature of <s>asaṃprajñāta samādhi</s>?

body.text: virāmapratyayābhyāsapūrvaḥ saṁskāraśeṣo'nyaḥ ॥ 18 ॥
body.translated_text: The other [<s>samādhi</s>] is preceded by the practice of the cessation-cognition, and has only latent impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>) remaining. // 18 //

body.text: sarvavṛttipratyastamaye saṁskāraśeṣo nirodhaścittasya samādhirasaṁprajñātaḥ। tasya paraṁ vairāgyamupāyaḥ। sālambano hyabhyāsastatsādhanāya na kalpata iti virāmapratyayo nirvastuka ālambanī kriyate। sa cārthaśūnyaḥ। tadabhyāsapūrvakaṁ hi cittaṁ nirālambanamabhāvaprāptamiva bhavatītyeṣa nirbījaḥ sabhādhirasaṁprajñātaḥ ॥ 18 ॥
body.translated_text: When all activities have subsided, the cessation of the mind with only latent impressions remaining is the <s>asaṃprajñāta samādhi</s>. Its means is the supreme detachment. For practice with a support is not sufficient to accomplish that; therefore the cessation-cognition, which is without an object, is made the support. And that is devoid of content. The mind preceded by the practice of that [cessation-cognition] becomes, as it were, having reached non-existence, without support—this is the seedless (<s>nirbīja</s>) <s>asaṃprajñāta samādhi</s>. // 18 //

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[atha asamprajñātaḥ 'yogaścittavṛttinirodha’] ityupapāditalakṣaṇaḥ [kimupāyaḥ] kiṁsādhanaḥ kenopāyenopetya ityarthaḥ । [kiṁsvabhāvaḥ] kiṁsvarūpaḥ kimavastha iti svabhāvaviśiṣṭasādhanasaṁbandhapradarśanārthamāha- [virāmapratyayābhyāsa pūrvaḥ saṁskāraśeṣo'nyaḥ ॥]
[virāmapratyayābhyāsapūrva] ityetāvatā sādhanasambandhamācaṣṭe । [saṁskāraśeṣa] iti tu svabhāvavyākhyānam । [anya iti] anantaroktalakṣaṇāt samprajñātādavanyo'yaṁ nirbījaḥ asamprajñātaḥ ॥
anya ityubhābhyāṁ saṁbadhyate --virāmapratyayābhyāsapūrveśva saṁskāraśeṣaśca । ko'sāvubhayaviśiṣṭa ityāha- [anya iti ॥]
viramaṇaṁ virāmaḥ । virāmaśvāsau pratyayaśca virāmapratyaya: । virāmarūpatvāt sa eva pratyayo virāma ityucyate । sarvaviṣayebhyo vinivartamānasya vinivartanakāle prāgapratyayāpatteḥ pratyayarūpatvam । etadyathā-pāvakasya jvalataḥ prakṣīyamāṇendhanasya śanaiśśanairupaśāmyataḥ prāgaṅgāratāpatterjvalātmakatā ॥
tasmādvirāmarūpaḥ pratyayo [virāmapratyayaḥ] tasya [abhyāsaḥ pūrvo] mukhaṁ yasya saḥ [virāmapratyayābhyāsapūrvaḥ ।] saṁskāra eva śeṣo yasya sa [saṁskāraśeṣaḥ ।] pratyayoparame tu pratyayasaṁskāra evāvaśiṣyate । viṣayapratyayebhya uparataṁ cittaṁ saṁskāraśeṣamevetyarthaḥ । [tasya paraṁ vairāgyamupāyaḥ] tasya samādheḥ paramuttaram ॥
nanu ca paraṁ vairāgyaṁ ceti vaktavyam, abhyāsavairāgyābhyāṁ vṛttinirodhasyābhipretatvāt । naiṣa doṣaḥ । virāmapratyayābhyāsasya sūtropāttatvādanāśaṅkayastadabhyāsaḥ । vairāgyaṁ punaranupāttatvādāśaṅkayeta । tasmāttadeva prāpayatā na cā [caḥ] paṭhitaḥ ॥
yadyevaṁ kasmānna sūtra eva vairāgyagrahaṇaṁ kṛtam ? pūrvatra paṭhitatvāt । tatra kimarthaṁ paṭhitamiti cet--vairāgyaprasaṅgāt । pūrvavairāgyaviśeṣa evottaraṁ vairāgyamiti prasaṅgāduttaram[duktam] । pūrvasya ca vairāgyasya samprajñātaviṣaye('pi)viniyogādavaśiṣṭatya parasya sādhanatvādanyaviṣayatvācca nirbījenaiva sambandha iti na sūtre vairāgyagrahaṇaṁ kṛtam । sāmarthyaprāptaṁ tu bhāṣyakāro darśeyati ॥
“abhyāsavairāgyābhyāṁ tannirodha' iti hi pratipāditam । [sālambane.o hyābhyāso] viruddhatvānnirālambanasya samādheḥ [sādhanatvāya na kalpata] iti [nirvastuko'pi virāmapratyayo] nirālambanasamādhyanurūpatvā [dālambanīkriyate ।] tasmā [ttadabhyāsavairāgyopāyapūrvakaṁ cittaṁ] nirālambana [mabhāprāptamiva bhavati sa eṣa nirbījaḥ] saṁskāraśeṣasvabhāvaḥ [samādhirasamprajñāta iti ॥ 18 ॥]
body.translated_text:
[Vivaraṇa]
"Then, <s>asaṃprajñāta</s> [samādhi], whose definition was established by 'yoga is the cessation of the activities of the mind'—what is its means?" What instrument, by what means is it approached—that is the meaning. "What is its nature?" What is its form, what is its state—to demonstrate its relation to a means qualified by a specific nature, he says: "Preceded by the practice of the cessation-cognition, with only latent impressions remaining, the other."
"Preceded by the practice of the cessation-cognition"—by this much he states the relation to the means. "With only latent impressions remaining"—this is the explanation of its nature. "The other"—this seedless <s>asaṃprajñāta</s> is different from <s>saṃprajñāta</s>, whose definition was stated just before.
"The other" is connected with both—preceded by the practice of the cessation-cognition, and with only latent impressions remaining. Who is this entity qualified by both? He says: "the other."
Cessation is <s>virāma</s>. It is both cessation and cognition, hence cessation-cognition (<s>virāma-pratyaya</s>). Being of the nature of cessation, that very cognition is called 'cessation.' At the time of withdrawing from all objects, before the attainment of the absence of cognition, it has the nature of cognition. This is like a blazing fire whose fuel is gradually being consumed: before reaching the state of embers, it has the nature of flame.
Therefore, a cognition whose nature is cessation is the cessation-cognition; the practice of that is the "preceding" (i.e., that which has as its face/beginning)—hence "preceded by the practice of the cessation-cognition." That whose remainder is only latent impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>) is "with only <s>saṃskāras</s> remaining." When cognition ceases, only the <s>saṃskāra</s> of that cognition remains. The mind withdrawn from object-cognitions has only <s>saṃskāras</s> as its remainder—that is the meaning. "Its means is the supreme detachment"—the supreme, the highest, of that <s>samādhi</s>.
Objection: It should say 'the supreme detachment and [practice],' since cessation of activities was intended through both practice and detachment. Reply: This is not a fault. Since the practice of the cessation-cognition is derived from the <s>sūtra</s> itself, that practice is not in question. But since detachment is not derived [from the <s>sūtra</s>], it might be doubted. Therefore, in presenting that, the conjunction 'and' was not read.
If so, why was detachment not mentioned in the <s>sūtra</s> itself? Because it was mentioned earlier. And why was it mentioned there? Because of the occasion for detachment. The supreme detachment was stated in that context because it is a specific form of the prior detachment. And since the prior detachment is applied to the domain of <s>saṃprajñāta</s> too, and the remaining supreme [detachment] is the means [for <s>asaṃprajñāta</s>] and has a different object, its connection is with the seedless alone—hence detachment was not mentioned in the <s>sūtra</s>. But the <s>Bhāṣya</s>-author shows what is obtained by implication.
"By practice and detachment, the cessation of that"—this has been established. "Since practice with a support," being incompatible, "is not sufficient as a means for" the unsupported <s>samādhi</s>, "the cessation-cognition, though without an object, is made the support" because it conforms to unsupported <s>samādhi</s>. "Therefore, the mind, preceded by the means of that practice and detachment, becomes as if without support, as if having reached non-existence—this is the seedless" <s>samādhi</s>, whose nature is having only <s>saṃskāras</s> remaining—"the <s>asaṃprajñāta samādhi</s>." // 18 //

body.text: sa khalvayaṁ dvividhaḥ - upāyapratyayo bhavapratyayaśca। tatropāyapratyayo yogināṁ bhavati –
body.translated_text: Now, this [<s>asaṃprajñāta samādhi</s>] is indeed twofold: that which has means as its occasion (<s>upāya-pratyaya</s>), and that which has existence as its occasion (<s>bhava-pratyaya</s>). Of these, the means-occasioned belongs to <s>yogins</s>—

body.text: bhavaprayayo videhaprakṛtilayānām ॥ 19 ॥
body.translated_text: The existence-occasioned belongs to the bodiless and those absorbed in <s>Prakṛti</s>. // 19 //

body.text: videhānāṁ devānāṁ bhavapratyayaḥ। te hi svasaṁskāramātropayogena cittena kaivalyapadamivānubhavantaḥ svasaṁskāravipākaṁ tathājātīyakamativāhayanti। tathā prakṛtilayāḥ sādhikāre cetasi prakṛtilīne kaivalyapadamivānubhavanti, yāvanna punarāvartate'dhikāravaśāccittamiti ॥ 19 ॥
body.translated_text: For the bodiless gods, it is existence-occasioned. They, experiencing as it were the state of <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation) through the mind's utilization of their own latent impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>) alone, pass through the maturation of their <s>saṃskāras</s> of that very kind. Likewise those absorbed in <s>Prakṛti</s>, when the mind still bearing its task (<s>adhikāra</s>) has dissolved into <s>Prakṛti</s>, experience as it were the state of <s>kaivalya</s>, until the mind returns again by force of its remaining task. // 19 //

body.text:
vivaraṇam
﻿ [sa khalvayaṁ dvividhaḥ ।] saḥ nirbījaḥ samādhiḥ [upāyapratyayo bhavapratyayaśca ।] upāyena pratīyate prāpyata ityupāyapratyayo [yogināṁ bhavati ।] yadyapi videhā api yogina eva । tathāpi yamādiyogasādhanānuṣṭhāyino'bhipretāḥ । teṣāṁ śraddhāvīryādyupāyalabhyaḥ samādhiḥ ॥
videhaprakṛtilayānāṁ tu janmanaiva labhyaḥ । tehi tanutarapratibandhāvaśeṣāḥ । sa tu pratibandhāvaśeṣasteṣāṁ sakṛdāsāditapunarjanmanāṁ samādhivyāghātāya na paryāpnoti । sa tu janmapratilambhamātranimittam । (tvāt)jñānavairāgyādyanuṣṭhānakāryatvādvidehaprakṛtilayatvasya tadanuṣṭhānastutyarthaṁ sūtram । idṛśaṁ hi tadanuṣṭhānamāhātmyam । yaduta sāmarthyādivaikalyādabhīpsitaphalānavātāvapi mahanīyataraṁ videhaprakṛtilayatvaṁ prāpyate ।
videhā nāma devāḥ puryaṣṭakaśarīropabandhāḥ । [te svasaṁskāramātropabhogena] vairāgyābhyāsāhitaḥ saṁskāraśeṣastanmātropabhogena [cittena kaivalyamihānubhavanta iti ।] sattvaguṇavinirmoṁkā [ttathājātīyakaṁ svasaṁskāraparipākaṁ] kṣapayanti ॥
prakṛtilayāḥ--sādhikāre aparyavasitā[dhi]kare । yāvaddhi na kṛtā guṇapuruṣāntarakhyātiḥ, tāvadaparisamāptādhikārameva cittaṁ tasmin prakṛtilayāpanne [kaivalyamivānubhavantīti ।] pūrvavat । [yāvanna punarāvartate'dhikāravaśāt] vidyākartavyatāvaśāt tāvadanubhavanti kaivalyamiva ॥ 19 ॥
body.translated_text:
[Vivaraṇa]
"Now, this is twofold." This seedless <s>samādhi</s> is "means-occasioned and existence-occasioned." That which is attained by means—approached through means—is means-occasioned. "It belongs to <s>yogins</s>." Although the bodiless too are indeed <s>yogins</s>, what is intended here are those who practice the means of <s>yoga</s> such as <s>yama</s> and the rest. Their <s>samādhi</s> is obtained through means such as faith, vigor, and the rest.
But for the bodiless and those absorbed in <s>Prakṛti</s>, it is obtained by birth alone. For their obstructions have been reduced to a very thin remainder. But that thin remainder of obstruction, for those who have once acquired rebirth, is not sufficient to obstruct <s>samādhi</s>. It is merely the occasion for attaining a birth. Since the state of bodilessness and absorption in <s>Prakṛti</s> is the result of prior practice of knowledge, detachment, and the rest, the <s>sūtra</s> serves to praise that practice. For such is the greatness of that practice: that even when the desired fruit is not attained due to deficiency of capacity and the rest, one attains the highly exalted state of bodilessness or absorption in <s>Prakṛti</s>.
The 'bodiless' are gods bound only to the subtle body (<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>). They, "through the enjoyment of their own <s>saṃskāras</s> alone"—the remainder of <s>saṃskāras</s> devoid of the practice of detachment—"experience as it were <s>kaivalya</s> through the mind." Being liberated from the <s>sattva-guṇa</s>, they "exhaust the maturation of their <s>saṃskāras</s> of that very kind."
Those absorbed in <s>Prakṛti</s>—"still bearing their task"—whose task is not yet completed. For as long as the discriminative knowledge between <s>guṇas</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> has not been achieved, the mind's task is not yet finished. When that [mind] has been absorbed into <s>Prakṛti</s>, "they experience as it were <s>kaivalya</s>"—as before. "Until it returns again by force of its task"—by force of the obligation of knowledge still to be completed—until then they experience something resembling <s>kaivalya</s>. // 19 //

body.text: śraddhāvīryasmṛtisamādhiprajñāpūrvaka itareṣām ॥ 20 ॥
body.translated_text: For the others, [<s>samādhi</s>] is preceded by faith, vigor, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom. // 20 //

body.text: upāyapratyayo yogināṁ bhavati। śraddhā cetasaḥ saṁprasādaḥ। sā hi jananīva kalyāṇī yoginaṁ pāti। tasya hi śraddadhānasya vivekārthino vīryamupajāyate। samupajātavīryasya smṛtirupatiṣṭhate। smṛtyupasthāne ca cittamanākulaṁ samādhīyate। samāhitacittasya prajñāviveka upāvartate। yena yathārthaṁ vastu jānāti। tadabhyāsāttattadviṣayācca vairāgyādasaṁprajñātaḥ samādhirbhavati ॥ 20 ॥
body.translated_text: The means-occasioned [<s>samādhi</s>] belongs to <s>yogins</s>. Faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) is the serenity of the mind. Like a benevolent mother, she protects the <s>yogin</s>. For the one who has faith and seeks discrimination, vigor (<s>vīrya</s>) arises. When vigor has arisen, mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>) becomes established. When mindfulness is established, the mind, free from disturbance, becomes concentrated (<s>samādhīyate</s>). For one whose mind is concentrated, discriminative wisdom (<s>prajñā-viveka</s>) manifests. By this he knows things as they truly are. Through the practice of that, and through detachment from those very objects, <s>asaṃprajñāta samādhi</s> arises. // 20 //

body.text:
vivaraṇam
yeṣāmupāyapratyayo yogināṁ, teṣāṁ [śraddhāvīryasmṛtisamādhiprajñāpūrvakaḥ] samādhiḥ, [śraddhā] nāmāpavargaprāptau tatsādhanaśravaṇe ca kautakaphalasaṁparka iva salilasya [cetasaḥ] [samprasādaḥ] [saṁprasattiḥ । sā hi jananīva kalyāṇī yoginaṁ pāti] rakṣatyaśubhebhyaḥ । [tasya hi vivekārthinaḥ] samyagdarśanārthino [vīryam] utsāha [upajāyate] yogasādhanānuṣṭhānaṁ prati । sañjātavīryasyāgamajñānādiviṣayā dṛḍha़tarā smṛtirupatiṣṭhate । [vivekārthina] iti sarvatrānuṣajyate ॥
dṛḍha [smṛtyupasthāne ca cittamanākulaṁ samādhīyate । samāhitacittasya] prajñāyā buddheḥ [viviktatā] sarvārthaprakāśanasāmathryam । ta(thā)t viśinaṣṭi - yena yathābhūtam ātmādi vastu jānāti iti ॥
[tadabhyāsāt] etaduktaṁ bhavati – ārmadarśanavirāmapratyayābhyāsāditi । [tadviṣayācca vairāgyā] (khyādviṣayā)t parasmādvairāgyāditi । [asamprajñātaḥ samādhiḥ] iti ॥ 20 ॥
body.translated_text:
[Vivaraṇa]
For those <s>yogins</s> whose [<s>samādhi</s>] is means-occasioned, "the <s>samādhi</s> is preceded by faith, vigor, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom." "Faith" is the serene clarity of mind arising upon hearing about the attainment of liberation and its means—like the natural affinity of water [for flowing downward]. "Like a benevolent mother, she protects the <s>yogin</s>"—protects from inauspicious things. "For one who seeks discrimination"—who seeks right vision—"vigor," enthusiasm, "arises" toward the practice of the means of <s>yoga</s>. When vigor has arisen, "mindfulness" regarding scriptural knowledge and the rest becomes more firmly "established." "Who seeks discrimination" is to be connected throughout.
When firm "mindfulness is established, the mind, free from disturbance, becomes concentrated. For one whose mind is concentrated," "discriminativeness" of wisdom (<s>buddhi</s>)—the power to illuminate all things. He specifies: "by which he knows things as they truly are"—the self and so forth.
"Through the practice of that"—this amounts to saying: through the practice of the cessation-cognition [which involves] the seeing of the Self. "And through detachment from that very object"—from the supreme detachment. "<s>Asaṃprajñāta samādhi</s> [arises]." // 20 //

body.text: te khalu nava yogino mṛdumadhyādhimātropāyā bhavanti। tadyathā - mṛdūpāyo madhyopāyo'dhimātropāya iti। tatra mṛdūpāyastrividhaḥ – mṛdusaṁvego madhyasaṁvegastīvrasaṁvega iti। tathā madhyopāyastathā'dhimātropāya iti। tatrādhimātropāyānāṁ –
body.translated_text: Now, these nine [types of] <s>yogins</s> have mild, moderate, and intense means. Namely: one of mild means, one of moderate means, and one of intense means. Of these, the one of mild means is threefold: of mild intensity, moderate intensity, and keen intensity. Likewise the one of moderate means, and likewise the one of intense means. Among those of intense means—

body.text: tīvrasaṁvegānāmāsannaḥ ॥ 21 ॥
body.translated_text: For those of keen intensity, [<s>samādhi</s>] is near at hand. // 21 //

body.text: samādhilābhaḥ samādhiphalaṁ ca bhavatīti ॥ 21 ॥
body.translated_text: The attainment of <s>samādhi</s> and the fruit of <s>samādhi</s> are near at hand. // 21 //

body.text:
vivaraṇam
te'pi śraddhādimādhinā nava(nupa)yogino bhavanti । taddarśayati- [tadyathā mṛdūpāyo madhyopāyo'dhimātropāya iti ।] teṣāmekaikastridhā bhidyate-tatra [mṛdūpāya iti ।] sādhanānuṣṭhānaṁ prati mandopakramo madhyopakramaḥ tī(vrasaṁvego)vropakrama iti । evamitaratrāpīti । nātra tirobhūtam(t) ॥
[॥ tatrādhimātropāyānāṁ tīvrasaṁvegānāmāsannaḥ samādhilābhaḥ samādhiphalaṁ ca] ॥ 21 ॥
body.translated_text:
[Vivaraṇa]
They too, by means of faith and the rest, become nine [types of] <s>yogins</s>. He shows this: "Namely: one of mild means, one of moderate means, one of intense means." Each of these is divided threefold: "of these, the one of mild means"—mild in undertaking the practice of means, moderate in undertaking, keen in undertaking. Likewise for the others too. Nothing is hidden here.
"Among those of intense means, for those of keen intensity, the attainment of <s>samādhi</s> and the fruit of <s>samādhi</s> are near at hand." // 21 //

body.text: mṛdumadhyādhimātratvāttato'pi viśeṣaḥ ॥ 22 ॥
body.translated_text: There is further distinction due to mild, moderate, and intense [degrees]. // 22 //

body.text: mṛdutīvro madhyatīvro'dhimātratīvra iti। tato'pi viśeṣaḥ। tadviśeṣādapi mṛdutīvrasaṁvegasyā''sannaḥ, tato madhyatīvrasaṁvegasyā''sannataraḥ, tasmādadhimātratīvrasaṁvegasyādhimātropāyasyāpyāsannatamaḥ samādhilābhaḥ samādhiphalaṁ ceti ॥ 22 ॥
body.translated_text: Mildly keen, moderately keen, intensely keen—there is further distinction. Due to that distinction, for one of mildly keen intensity, [<s>samādhi</s>] is near; for one of moderately keen intensity, nearer; for one of intensely keen intensity with intense means, nearest is the attainment of <s>samādhi</s> and the fruit of <s>samādhi</s>. // 22 //

body.text:
vivaraṇam
teṣāmapi mṛdumadhyatīvropakramatayā viśiṣyamāṇatvā [ttato'pi viśeṣaḥ] sādhanānuṣṭhānasaṁskārasya । [tadviśeṣāda] pyuttamasya [samādhilābhaḥ] pratyāsīdatitarām ॥ etadasya sūtrasya prayojanam-yogasādhanānuṣṭhānaṁ prati yoginaḥ kathamupabṛṁhitotsāhā bhaveyuriti । yathā loke drutataraṁ sīmāntaṁ pari[prati]dhāvatāmetatphale bhavatīti tadvat । athavā-mandamandetaropakramāṇāmapi yogināmabhimataphalāvāptiprakāśanādanavasanna- cetasaḥ pravarteranniti । itarathā tīvratarāyāsajanitabhītaye'vasīdeyuriti ॥ 22 ॥
body.translated_text:
[Vivaraṇa]
Since even among them there is distinction by mild, moderate, and keen undertaking, "there is further distinction"—of the <s>saṃskāras</s> of the practice of means. "Due to that distinction," for the highest, "the attainment of <s>samādhi</s>" is most proximate.
The purpose of this <s>sūtra</s> is this: how may <s>yogins</s> have their enthusiasm strengthened toward the practice of the means of <s>yoga</s>? Just as in the world this fruit accrues to those who run most swiftly to the boundary—so too here. Alternatively, by making manifest the attainment of the desired fruit even for those whose undertaking is mild or less, they may proceed with undespairing minds. Otherwise, they might lose heart from fear generated by the most intense exertion. // 22 //

body.text: kimetasmādevā''sannatamaḥ samādhirbhavati। athāsya lābhe bhavatyanyo'pi kaścidupāyo na veti –
body.translated_text: Is <s>samādhi</s> most proximate only through this [graduated practice]? Or is there also some other means for its attainment?

body.text: īśvarapraṇidhānādvā ॥ 23 ॥
body.translated_text: Or, through devotion to <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord). // 23 //

body.text: praṇidhānādbhaktiviśeṣādāvarjita īśvarastamanugṛhṇātyabhidhyānamātreṇa। tadabhidhyānamātrādapi yogina āsannatamaḥ samādhilābhaḥ samādhiphalaṁ ca bhavatīti ॥ 23 ॥
body.translated_text: Through <s>praṇidhāna</s> (devotion), through a special kind of <s>bhakti</s> (devotion), <s>Īśvara</s>, won over, favors that [<s>yogin</s>] by mere contemplation. Through that mere contemplation too, the attainment of <s>samādhi</s> and the fruit of <s>samādhi</s> become most proximate for the <s>yogin</s>. // 23 //

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[kimetasmādevāsannataro bhavati ? atha (tasya) asya lābhe bhavatya nyo'pi kaścidupāyo] na veti । upāyāntaramastītyāha- [īśvarapraṇidhānādvā ।] īśvaraśabdārthamuttaratra vyākhyāsyati । praṇidhānamiha vyācaṣṭe- [bhaktiviśeṣādāvarjita] iti । anugrahaṁ pratyabhimukhībhāvamāpāditaḥ taṁ bhaktyātiśayayoginaṁ yoginam [abhidhyānamātreṇa] parameśvaratvādeva nirāyāsatayā satyasaṁkalpatvāt [anugṛhvāti ।] tadanugrahādapi [pratyāsannataraḥ samādhilābhaḥ phalaṁ ca] iti ॥ 23 ॥
body.translated_text:
[Vivaraṇa]
"Is it most proximate only through this? Or is there also some other means for its attainment?" There is another means—he says: "Or, through devotion to <s>Īśvara</s>." The meaning of the word '<s>Īśvara</s>' he will explain later. <s>Praṇidhāna</s> (devotion) is here explained: "Won over through a special kind of <s>bhakti</s>"—brought into a favorable disposition for granting grace. That <s>yogin</s> devoted with an excess of <s>bhakti</s>—"by mere contemplation," by the very nature of being the Supreme Lord, effortlessly, because His will is always true, "He favors" him. "Through that grace too, the attainment of <s>samādhi</s> and its fruit" are most proximate. // 23 //

body.text: atha pradhānapuruṣavyatiriktaḥ ko'yamīśvaro nāmeti –
body.translated_text: Then, who is this <s>Īśvara</s>, distinct from <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial nature) and <s>Puruṣa</s>?

body.text: kleśakarmavipākāśayairaparāmṛṣṭaḥ puruṣaviśeṣa īśvaraḥ ॥ 24 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>Īśvara</s> is a special <s>Puruṣa</s>, untouched by afflictions, actions, their fruitions, and their residual impressions. // 24 //

body.text: avidyādaya kleśāḥ। kuśalākuśalāni karmāṇi। tatphalaṁ vipākaḥ। tadanuguṇā vāsanā āśayāḥ। te ca manasi vartamānāḥ puruṣe vyapadiśyante, sa hi tatphalasya bhokteti। yathā jayaḥ parājayo vā yoddhṛṣu vartamānaḥ svāmini vyapadiśyate। yo hyanena bhogenāparāmṛṣṭaḥ sa puruṣaviśeṣa īśvaraḥ।
body.translated_text: <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance) and the rest are the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). Meritorious and demeritorious are the actions. Their fruit is the fruition (<s>vipāka</s>). The impressions conforming to these are the residual stores (<s>āśayas</s>). And these, though existing in the mind, are attributed to <s>Puruṣa</s>, for he is the experiencer of their fruit—just as victory or defeat, though taking place among warriors, is attributed to the lord. He who is untouched by this experience is a special <s>Puruṣa</s>—that is <s>Īśvara</s>.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[atha pradhānapuruṣavyatiriktaḥ ko'yamīśvara] iti sāṁkhyaśāsre prasiddhyabhāvādīśvarasadbhāve copapattimavaśyamanavagateśvaraviśeṣo vā pṛcchati । tatra tāvat pratijānīte- [kleśakarmavipākāśayairaparāmṛṣṭaḥ puruṣaviśeṣa īśvaraḥ ॥]
[kleśā] iti । [avidyādayaḥ] kleśayantīti [kleśāḥ ।] tatpūrvānuṣṭhitāni [kuśalākuśalāni] karmāṇi । kuśalāni cākuśalāni [ca kuśalākuśalāni] cetyekaśeṣaḥ । kuśalākuśalānīti kuśalākuśalavimiśrāṇīti yāvat । [tatphalaṁ vipākaḥ] jātyāyurbhogalakṣaṇaḥ । ta eva kleśādaya ā nirvāṇāccherata iti kleśakarmavipākā āśayā: । yadi vā kleśādīnāṁ rāśayaḥ kleśakarmavipākāśayā: ॥
te [manasi vartamānā] manovṛtiprabhavatvāt [puruṣe vyapadiśyante ।] kasmāt ? [sa hi tatphalasya bhokteti ।] yathā rājani jayaparājayau yodheṣu vartamānāvapadiśyete tatphalaṁ rājasaṁbandhi iti ।
[yā hmanena bhogenāparāsṛṣṭa] iti ucyate । na kālavivakṣā, upalakṣaṇārthatvaṁ-na parāmṛśyate, nāpi parāmṛkṣyate, nāpi parāmṛṣṭa iti । kleśakarmavipākāśayāsaṁbandhī(ndhayegī)tyarthaḥ ॥
body.translated_text:
[Vivaraṇa]
"Then, who is this <s>Īśvara</s>, distinct from <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>?" Since <s>Īśvara</s> is not well-established in the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> teaching, and since evidence for the existence of <s>Īśvara</s> must necessarily be provided, he asks about the specific nature of <s>Īśvara</s>. To begin, he asserts: "<s>Īśvara</s> is a special <s>Puruṣa</s>, untouched by afflictions, actions, their fruitions, and their residual impressions."
"<s>Kleśas</s>"—"<s>avidyā</s> and the rest"—they torment, hence <s>kleśas</s>. The actions previously performed from those [<s>kleśas</s>]—"meritorious and demeritorious"—meritorious and demeritorious, that is, including mixed ones. "Their fruit is the fruition"—characterized by birth, lifespan, and experience. These very <s>kleśas</s> and the rest are the 'stores' (<s>āśayas</s>), resting until liberation. Alternatively, the 'stores' are the accumulated heaps of <s>kleśas</s>, actions, and their fruitions.
These, "existing in the mind," because they arise from mental activities, "are attributed to <s>Puruṣa</s>." Why? "For he is the experiencer of their fruit." Just as victory and defeat, though taking place among warriors, are attributed to the king, because the fruit belongs to the king.
"He who is untouched by this experience"—it is said. There is no reference to a particular time—the expression is illustrative: he is not touched, nor will he be touched, nor has he ever been touched. The meaning is: one who has no connection with <s>kleśas</s>, actions, fruitions, and residual impressions.

body.text: kaivalyaṁ prāptāstarhi santi ca bahavaḥ kevalinaḥ। te hi trīṇi bandhanāni cchittvā kaivalyaṁ prāptā īśvarasya ca tatsaṁbandho na bhūto na bhāvī। yathā muktasya pūrvā bandhakoṭiḥ prajñāyate naivamīśvarasya। yathā vā prakṛtilīnasyottarā bandhakoṭiḥ saṁbhāvyate naivamīśvarasya। sa tu sadaiva muktaḥ sadaiveśvara iti।
body.translated_text: Then there are many who have attained <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation). They, having cut the three bonds, have attained <s>kaivalya</s>. But <s>Īśvara</s>'s connection with those [bonds] was neither past nor will it be future. Just as the prior limit of bondage is recognized for one who is liberated, it is not so for <s>Īśvara</s>. Or just as a future limit of bondage is conceivable for one who has merged into <s>Prakṛti</s>, it is not so for <s>Īśvara</s>. He, however, is forever liberated, forever the Lord.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
sūtrārthaviśuddhiṁ kurvannāha- [kaivalyaṁ prāptastarhīti ।] kleśādyaparāmarśasya kādācitkatayā'pi saṁbhavāt । [santi bahavaḥ kevalinaḥ] kiṁ tadī[te'pī]śvarā iti ? । parāmarśasyāpi saṁbhavānna ta ekāntena kleśādibhiraparāmṛṣṭāḥ । parāmarśāparāmarśī hi staḥ teṣām । īśvaratvaparāmṛṣṭa eva । na hyanavadhṛtaḥ śabdārtho lakṣaṇatvenopādeya: aparāmṛṣṭa iti । tasmādya ekāntenāparāmṛṣṭaḥ evāparāmṛṣṭa ityucyate ॥
[te hi trīṇi bandhanāni] prākṛtavaikṛtadākṣiṇāni samyagdarśanena hitvā [kaivalyaṁ prāptāḥ । īścarasya tu tatsaṁbandhaḥ] kleśādisaṁbandho na [bhūto yathā muktasya bhāvī bandha koṭi] rmuktatvopapattereva jñāyate । bandhapūrvakā hi muktiḥ । [nāpi bhāvī ।] yathā [prakṛtilīnasya ।] tasya hyanārabdhasaṁsārasya [uttarā bandhakoṭiḥ sambhāvyate ।] pravṛttasaṁsārasya cāprakṛtilīnacittasya sā(samā)dhikāratvāt pūrvottarabandhakoṭī saṁbhavataḥ । tadidaṁ sarvamatrāparāmṛṣṭa iti kālāvivakṣāpradarśanārtham । [sa tu sadaiva muktaḥ sadaiveścaraḥ ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇa</s> (Elucidation):
Purifying the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>, he says: ["Then those who have attained <s>kaivalya</s>..."]. Because non-contact with <s>kleśas</s> and the rest is possible even occasionally. ["There are many <s>kevalins</s>"]—are they then also <s>Īśvaras</s>? Because contact is also possible, they are not absolutely unaffected by <s>kleśas</s> and the rest. For they have [states of] both contact and non-contact. Only [<s>Īśvara</s>] is one whose [nature is defined as] unaffected. For a word-meaning that is not ascertained should not be adopted as a definition—[merely] 'unaffected.' Therefore, only one who is absolutely unaffected is said to be 'unaffected.'
["They, having [cut] the three bonds"]—the <s>prākṛta</s> (natural), <s>vaikṛta</s> (derivative), and <s>dākṣiṇa</s> (ritual) [bonds], having abandoned through right vision, [attained <s>kaivalya</s>. But <s>Īśvara</s>'s] connection with <s>kleśas</s> and the rest [was not] past. Just as the future limit of bondage of a liberated being is known from the very fact of liberation—for liberation is preceded by bondage. [Nor future.] As for [one merged into <s>Prakṛti</s>]—for one whose <s>saṃsāra</s> has not begun, [the future limit of bondage is conceivable.] And for one whose <s>saṃsāra</s> has begun, whose mind has not merged into <s>Prakṛti</s>, since both conditions apply, the prior and future limits of bondage are possible. All this here under 'unaffected' is for the purpose of showing that no specification of time is intended. ["He, however, is forever liberated, forever the Lord."]

body.text: yo'sau prakṛṣṭasattvopādānādīśvarasya śāśvatika utkarṣaḥ sa kiṁ sanimitta āhosvinnirnimitta iti। tasya śāstraṁ nimittam। śāstraṁ punaḥ kiṁnimittaṁ, prakṛṣṭasattvanimittam।
body.translated_text: That eternal excellence of <s>Īśvara</s>, which results from the adoption of supreme <s>sattva</s>—is it caused (<s>sanimitta</s>) or uncaused (<s>nirnimitta</s>)? Its cause is <s>śāstra</s> (scripture/knowledge). And what is the cause of <s>śāstra</s>? Supreme <s>sattva</s> is its cause.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
tatra puruṣaviśeṣa īśvara ityuktatvāt, īśvarasya puruṣasyānaiścaryadharmatvāt, cittasya caiścaryadharmatvāt, nirātiśayaiśvaryasya ca prakṛṣṭacittasaṁbandhāpekṣatvāt prāptamevottarārthamanuvadati- [yo'sau prakṛṣṭasattvopādānādīśvarasya śāśvatika utkarṣa iti ।] nityaniratiśayasarvajñānaiśvaryaśaktisampattirutkarṣaḥ ॥
tatra pratijñāviśuddhayarthaṁ praśnapūrvamupakramate-- [sa kiṁ sanimitta ahosvinnirnimitta iti ।] nimittaśabdaḥ kāraṇaparyāyaḥ । sa kiṁ sakāraṇa āhettvinniṣkāraṇa iti । kiñcātaḥ ? yadi tāvat sakāraṇastadā sadaiveśvara ityayuktam, anityatvāt । atha niṣkāraṇaḥ, tathā cotkarṣasya kāryatvādasattvaprasaṅgaḥ । na hi niṣkāraṇaṁ kāryai dṛśyate loke ॥
atrocyate-na niṣkāraṇaḥ [śāstranimittatvāt । śāsraṁ] jñānam । śāstrasya hetutvāt । yataḥ sarvaviṣayaṁ jñānaṁ nityaṁ dravyasvabhāvasādhyasādhanavyavahitaviprakṛṣṭāspadam ॥
yadyevaṁ jñānasyānyato'dhigamapūrvatvātprāganutkarṣaḥ prāpta ityata āha- [śāstraṁ punaḥ kiṁnnimittamiti ।] yadi svābhāvikaṁ jñānaṁ, mattonmattajñānavadanutkarṣahetutvam । atha punaḥ sanimittakaṁ, nimittāt prāganutkarṣa iti manyate ॥
na tāvannirnimittam । yataḥ [prakṛṣṭasattvanimittaṁ] prakṛṣṭasattvāśrayamiti yāvat । ata eva svabhāvajñānadoṣābhāvaḥ ॥
kiñca - svābhāvikajñānatve'pi na mattādijñānavadapakarṣahetutvam । nityamuktakleśādisattvāśrayatvāt । tatra yathaiva jñānasaṁskārasmṛtiprabandhānāmanyonyanimittanaimittikabhāvena bījāṅkuravadanādisaṁbandhaḥ, tathaiva śāstraprakarṣayorīśvaracetasi nityapravṛttaprabandharūpeṇa pravartamānayoranādyantaḥ saṁbandhaḥ । tatrotkarṣo jñānasya kāryemeva । jñānamapi tasya kāraṇameva ॥
anyeṣāṁ vyākhyānam-nimittaśabdaḥ pramāṇavācī । [tasya śāstraṁ nimittaṁ] pramāṇam , tena hi tadutkarṣaḥ pramīyate । śāstraṁ punaḥ kiṁpramāṇakam ? īśvaranirmalasattvapramāṇam । viśuddhasattvapraṇītatvāddhi śāstrasya prāmāṇyam ? yathā manvādīnām । tathā ca śrutiḥ-‘yakiṁcinmanurabhyavadattadbheṣajam' iti । yathā ca loke guruṇā'bhihitamiti ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇa</s> (Elucidation):
Since it has been stated that <s>Īśvara</s> is a special <s>Puruṣa</s>, and since <s>Īśvara</s> as <s>Puruṣa</s> does not possess the property of sovereignty [by nature], and since it is the mind (<s>citta</s>) that possesses the property of sovereignty, and since unsurpassed sovereignty depends on a connection with a supreme mind—he restates what has already been established for the following purpose: ["That eternal excellence of <s>Īśvara</s> which results from the adoption of supreme <s>sattva</s>..."]. The excellence is the endowment of eternal, unsurpassed omniscience and sovereign power.
Therein, in order to purify the thesis, he begins with a question: ["Is it caused or uncaused?"]. The word <s>nimitta</s> (cause) is a synonym for <s>kāraṇa</s> (cause). Is it with a cause or without one? And what follows from this? If it is caused, then the statement 'He is forever the Lord' would be unjustified, because of its being impermanent. If it is uncaused, then, since excellence would be an effect, the absurd consequence follows that it would not exist—for in the world, no effect is seen to be without a cause.
To this it is replied—it is not uncaused, [because it has <s>śāstra</s> (knowledge) as its cause. <s>Śāstra</s>] is knowledge. Because knowledge is its cause. For all-encompassing knowledge is eternal, having as its domain the nature of substances, means of accomplishment, objects, the remote and the hidden.
If so, since knowledge presupposes prior acquisition from another, the objection arises that there was no excellence before—therefore he says: ["And what is the cause of <s>śāstra</s>?"]. If knowledge is innate, it would not be a cause of excellence, like the knowledge of an intoxicated or a mad person. But if knowledge has a cause, one would think there was no excellence before its cause.
It is certainly not without a cause, because [it has] supreme <s>sattva</s> as its cause—that is, it depends on supreme <s>sattva</s> as its substrate. Hence the absence of the faults of innate knowledge.
Moreover, even if knowledge is innate, it is not a cause of inferiority like the knowledge of an intoxicated person and the like, because it rests on <s>sattva</s> that is eternally free from <s>kleśas</s> and the rest. Just as the series of knowledge, impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>), and memory are in a beginningless relation of mutual cause and effect like seeds and sprouts, so too <s>śāstra</s> (knowledge) and excellence in <s>Īśvara</s>'s mind, operating in the form of an eternally active series, are in a beginningless and endless relation. There, excellence is indeed the effect of knowledge, and knowledge is indeed its cause.
Other commentators explain: The word <s>nimitta</s> means 'means of valid knowledge' (<s>pramāṇa</s>). ["Its cause is <s>śāstra</s>"]—that is, <s>pramāṇa</s>; for by that, its excellence is established. And what is the <s>pramāṇa</s> for <s>śāstra</s>? It is established by <s>Īśvara</s>'s pure <s>sattva</s>. For the authority of scripture rests on its being composed by one of pure <s>sattva</s>, as in the case of <s>Manu</s> and others. And thus the Vedic text says: 'Whatever <s>Manu</s> pronounced, that is medicine.' And as in the world [one says]: 'It has been stated by the teacher.'

body.text: etayoḥ śāstrotkarṣayorīśvarasattve vartamānayoranādiḥ saṁbandhaḥ। etasmādetadbhavati sadaiveśvaraḥ sadaiva mukta iti। tacca tasyaiśvaryaṁ sāmyātiśayavinirmuktam। na tāvadaiśvaryāntareṇa tadatiśayate। yadevātiśayi syāttadeva tatsyāt। tasmādyatra kāṣṭhāprāptiraiśvaryasya sa īśvara iti। na ca tatsamānamaiśvaryamasti। kasmāt, dvayostulyayorekasminyugapatkāmite'rthe navamidamastu purāṇamidamastvityekasya siddhāvitarasya prākāmyavighātādūnatvaṁ prasaktam। dvayośca tulyayoryugapatkāmitārthaprāptirnāsti। arthasya viruddhatvāt। tasmādyasya sāmyātiśayairvinirmuktamaiśvaryaṁ sa eveśvaraḥ। sa ca puruṣaviśeṣa iti ॥ 24 ॥
body.translated_text: The relation between these two—<s>śāstra</s> (knowledge) and excellence—existing in <s>Īśvara</s>'s being, is beginningless. From this follows the statement: 'He is forever the Lord, forever liberated.' And His sovereignty is free from both equality and superiority. First, it is not surpassed by any other sovereignty—for whatever would surpass it would itself be that [supreme sovereignty]. Therefore, He in whom sovereignty reaches its ultimate limit is <s>Īśvara</s>. Nor does any sovereignty equal to His exist. Why? Because when two equal [beings] simultaneously desire a [mutually contradictory] object, and one [desires] 'let this be new' while the other [desires] 'let this be old'—the accomplishment of one would obstruct the free will of the other, resulting in inferiority. And for two equals simultaneously desiring the same object, there is no attainment of [their contradictory] purpose, because of the mutual contradiction of the objects. Therefore, He whose sovereignty is free from both equals and superiors—He alone is <s>Īśvara</s>. And He is a special <s>Puruṣa</s>. // 24 //

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[etayoḥ śāsrotkarṣayoḥ] pramāṇaprameyatayā [nirādyantaḥ sambandhaḥ ॥]
nanu ca naiveśvarasatva[a]vartamānena śākheṇa tadutkarṣaḥ pramīyate । naiṣa doṣaḥ । tatprabhavatvāttatra vartamānam । varta(māna)ta eva tatprabhavamapi śāsraṁ tasmin sarvajñatvādeva । loke'pi yato yatprabhavati vartate tattasmin, yathā tantvādiṣu paṭādi । tatprabhavatvamanumānāgamābhyāmavagamyate । śāstrapramāṇakaḥ utkarṣaḥ, īśvarabhramāṇakaṁ śāstramiti bhinnāśrayatvācchāsrotkarṣayornetaretarāśrayatvam ॥
nanu ca śāstrādīśvaraprāmāṇyaṁ, tatprāmāṇyācca śāstraprāmāṇyamiti syādanyonyāśrayatvam-ucyate-īśvaraprāmāṇyasyānumānena siddhatvādadoṣaḥ ॥
[etasmādetadbhavati ।] kasmāt ? īśvaraprakṛṣṭasattvāśrayayorniratiśayajñānotkarṣayoḥ kāryakāraṇarūpe prabandhanityatayā nityatvādetadbhavati- [sa tu sadaiva muktaḥ sadaiveśvara iti ।] (ityatrāha) [tacca tasyaiścaryaṁ sāmyātiśayavimuktamiti] vakṣyamāṇapramāṇaphalam । etatsūtrapiṇḍārtho vā ॥
atiśayavimuktatāṁ vyācaṣṭe - [na tāvadaiśvaryāntareṇa tadatiśayyate ।] kutaḥ? [yadevaiśvaryāntaraṁ tadatiśayānaṁ] manyase [tadeva tat] aiśvaryaṁ mayā'bhihitam । yatraivaiśvaryantarātiśāyi bhavatyaiśvaryaṁ sa eveśvara iti yāvat । [na ca tatsamānamaiśvaryamasti ।] samānadharmaprakarṣāsaṁbhavāt ॥
na hyekasmin rājye dvayoḥ saṁbhavo rājñoḥ । ekasya vā dve rājye । tathā pratipādayati-taddvayostutyatvaṁ prasaktam । na hyekasyānyataratra prākāmyamabādhitvā anyatarasmin pravṛttirupapadyate । dvayośca yugapadekārthayorekasya prākāmyeṇa pravṛttireva nāsti । prakāmite vastuni samānaprakarṣasyārthasya viruddhatvāt ॥ yena ca samānaprakarṣatā tasya tenaiva sa bādhyate । (te ca) tava na vācā bādhanamitarasya rūpātiśayā āvṛttyatiśayāśca virudhyante । sāmānyāni tvatiśayaiḥ saha vartanta iti vakṣyāmaḥ ॥
tasmādyasya sāmyātiśayaviproṣitamaiśvaryaṁ sa īśvara iti pradhānapuruṣavyatiriktaḥ puruṣaviśeṣa īśvaraḥ siddhaḥ ॥ 24 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇa</s> (Elucidation):
["Of these two—<s>śāstra</s> (knowledge) and excellence—"] in the relation of means of knowledge and object of knowledge, [the relation is beginningless and endless."]
Objection: <s>Īśvara</s>'s excellence is not established by a scripture existing in <s>Īśvara</s>'s being. This is not a fault. Because it originates from Him, it exists in Him. And even though existing [in Him], the scripture too originates from Him, precisely because of His omniscience. In the world too, that which originates from something exists in that thing, as cloth and the like [exist] in threads and the like. That it originates from Him is understood through inference and scripture. The excellence is established by scripture; scripture is established by <s>Īśvara</s>—thus, because they have different substrates, there is no mutual dependence between scripture and excellence.
Objection: <s>Īśvara</s>'s authority is [known] from scripture, and scripture's authority from His authority—would this not be mutual dependence? Reply: There is no fault, because <s>Īśvara</s>'s authority is established through inference.
["From this follows..."] Why? Because the unsurpassed excellence of knowledge, resting on <s>Īśvara</s>'s supreme <s>sattva</s>, being in the form of cause and effect, is eternal by virtue of the eternity of the [causal] series—from this it follows: ["He is forever liberated, forever the Lord."] (And here he says) ["And His sovereignty is free from equality and superiority"]—this is the result of the forthcoming proof. Or this is the summary meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>.
He explains the freedom from superiority: ["It is not surpassed by any other sovereignty."]. Why? ["Whatever other sovereignty you consider to surpass it"]—["that itself is that"] sovereignty spoken of by me. That sovereignty which surpasses all other sovereignty—the one who possesses it is <s>Īśvara</s>. ["Nor is there any sovereignty equal to His."] Because the utmost degree of identical properties is impossible.
For in one kingdom, two kings are not possible, nor two kingdoms for one. He demonstrates this: the equality of two is an absurd consequence. For the activity of one in one [domain] is not possible without obstructing his free will in the other. And for two [equals] simultaneously [desiring] one object, there is simply no activity with full free will for one—because of the contradiction of the object in [a domain] where free will is exercised. And whatever [property] constitutes the equality—by that very thing, it is obstructed. And it is not by your mere words that the other is obstructed—[rather] superiorities of form and superiorities of occurrence are contradicted. But general [properties] coexist with superiorities—this we shall explain.
Therefore, He whose sovereignty is utterly free from both equality and superiority—that special <s>Puruṣa</s>, distinct from <s>Pradhāna</s> and [ordinary] <s>Puruṣa</s>, is established as <s>Īśvara</s>. // 24 //

body.text: kiṁ ca –
body.translated_text: Moreover—

body.text: tatra niratiśayaṁ sarvajñabījam ॥ 25 ॥
body.translated_text: In Him, the seed of omniscience is unsurpassed (<s>niratiśaya</s>). // 25 //

body.text: yadidamatītānāgatapratyutpannapratyekasamuccayātīndriyagrahaṇamalpaṁ bahviti sarvajñabījametadvivardhamānaṁ yatra niratiśayaṁ sa sarvajñaḥ। asti kāṣṭhāprāptiḥ sarvajñabījasya sātiśayatvātparimāṇavaditi। yatra kāṣṭhāprāptirjñānasya su sarvajñaḥ। sa ca puruṣaviśeṣa iti।
body.translated_text: This [seed of omniscience] which is the apprehension—individually and collectively—of things past, future, and present, and of things beyond the senses, whether few or many—this seed of omniscience, progressively increasing, where it is unsurpassed, He is omniscient. There is an ultimate limit to the seed of omniscience, because it admits of degrees, like magnitude. He in whom knowledge reaches its ultimate limit is omniscient. And He is a special <s>Puruṣa</s>.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
yathāpratijñātasyeśvarasya siddhau pramāṇamupanyasyate- [tatra niratiśayaṁ sarvajñabījam । tatra] tasmin yathāpratijñātalakṣaṇa [īśvare niratiśayaṁ] bhavitumarhati । kiṁ taditi ? [yadidam] avyabhicāri pratyakṣānumānajñānam [atīta] viṣayam [anāgata] viṣayaṁ (vartamānakāla) [pratyutpanna] [viṣaya]matītādi [samuccaya] viṣayam [atīndri] yaviṣayaṁ ca । atīndriyayoratītānāgatayoḥ saṁbhavādatīndriya[grahaṇa]mityucyate ॥
taccātīndriyagrahaṇaṁ trividham-sūkṣmaviṣayaṁ vyavahitaviṣayaṁ viprakṛṣṭaviṣayañca । [alpaṁ bahniti ।] yathāprasiddha [metadvivardhamānaṁ] sātiśayatvena [sarvajñabījaṁ] yathā । dhūmavijñānamagnivijñānasya । katham ? yatra prakarṣakāṣṭhāṁ pratipadyate । jñānasya jñātrāśrayatvāt [yatre] ti jñātocyate-yasmin jñātarīti । [sa savaijñaḥ] siddhaḥ ॥
tathā śaktirapi sātiśayatvena vivardhamānā yatra kāṣṭhāṁ prāpnoti, sa sarvaśaktiḥ । tena jagannirmāṇasthāpanopasaṁhādikartṛtvasiddhiḥ । tathaiśvaryasyāpi vardhamānasya yatra kāṣṭhāprāptiḥ, sa parameśvaraḥ । tataśca aśaktyādiviparyayadoṣābhāvasiddhiḥ ॥
athāpi syāt-ajñānasyāpi vivardhamānasya svabhāvasiddhasya kāṣṭhāprāptasya tasminnīśvare siddhiriti-na-jñānāvirodhāt । na hi jñānājñānayorviruddhayorekasminnabhisaṁyogo'sti । na hi jñāne prakarṣavati tatrājñānaṁ saṁbhavati ॥
yatra hi jyotirvivardhate tatra tamo'pakṛṣyata eva । viparyayo'pīti cet- tacca na-sati jyotiṣi tamaso'nupalambhāt । vidyamānaṁ hi tamo jyotiṣā tiraskriyate, na kadācidvidyamānaṁ jyotistamasā'bhibhūyate ।
yadapi jaladharoparodhāt prāvṛṣi raveradarśanam, tadapi dṛṣṭivyavadhānamātram । na punaḥ prakāśa eva tirodhīyate tamovat । tasmānna, yatra jñānavivṛddhistatrājñānasya bhāvaḥ savitarīva tamasaḥ । nityātyantatirohitarajastame.oguṇasattvopādānāt ॥
kiñca- nājñānasyāvastuviṣayatvādvivṛddhiḥ saṁbhavati । jñānasya jñeyavastuviṣayatvādabhivṛddhayupapattiḥ । ajñānasya hi vastuviṣayatve jñānatvaprāptiḥ ॥
yaścāpi sthāvarādiṣvajñānaprakarṣa iti, nāsau prakarṣaḥ । atyantajñānābhāvāpekṣayā hi sa ucyate । ajñānasya prakarṣe hi satyajñānasahasrasya na jñānenaikena bādhaḥ syāt । tathā[dā]hi pratyajñānaṁ jñānenotpannenānekena bādhanaṁ syāt । tasmānnājñānasya prakarṣaḥ svarūpeṇa ॥
yasya hi sātiśayatvaṁ tasya kāṣṭhāpraptirdṛśyate । yathā phalādiparimāṇānāmākāśaparyantatā । tathā sarvajñabījamapi parāṁ kāṣṭhāṁ prātumarhati ॥
samastaṁ vyastaṁ ca sarvaṁ vastujātamekasya pratyakṣaṁ, jñeyatvāt, ghaṭādivat ॥
jñānāviṣayatvena puruṣārthatvāt, ghaṭādivadeva ॥
utpattimatī ca pṛthivī, sāvayavatvāt, ghaṭādivat ॥
prāṇikarmatatsādhanaphalavibhāgavideka(gadhaika)niṣpāditaṁ jagat, tadupabhogyasthānādiracanā-viśeṣavatvāta prāsādādivat ॥
anekaprāṇyupabhogavijñānavadekanirvartitā pṛthivī, anekaprāṇavadupabhogyatvāt vrīhiyavādivat ॥
anekaprayojanārthinā ekena nirmitā pṛthivī, gṛhādivadeva ॥
sarvaprāṇyāśrayo girinadīsamudāyaḥ tannivāsiparibhogayogyavijñānavadekakuśalotpāditaḥ, prakṛtahetunidarśanābhyāmeva ॥
anekaprāṇabhākprakāśādisāmarthyajñānavatā ekena nirvartitaḥ savitā, prakāśātmakatvāt pradīpādivat ॥
niyatakālamādityodayāstamayādisañcaraṇam etatprayojanajñānavadekaprayuktaṁ, pratiniyatakālatvāt, kṛṣyādivat ॥
buddhimadekeśvaraprayuktā sūryagrahacandranakṣatrādipravṛttiḥ, pravṛtterduḥkhātmakatve sati niyatasamayatvāt, dharmajñaśiṣyabhṛtyādipravṛttivat ॥
candramaso vṛddhikṣayau tithyādikālajñānavataikena prayuktau, kālaparicchedakatvāt, ghaṭikā[harā]divat । kālaparicchedajñānavataikena nirvartitaścandramā:, vṛddhikṣayayuktatvāt, ghaṭikādivadeva ॥
buddhimadekasvāmikaṁ jagat, anyonyaviruddhasaṁhatānekaprāṇināyakādhiṣṭhitabahumaṇḍalatvāt, itthaṁjātīyakaikarājyavat ॥
sarvametatsādhanasādhyavyāpārāvasthaṁ pratyakṣaṁ kasyacidekasya, avāntaravirodhānugrahavattayaikaprayojanatvāt, sāṁgrāmavastuvat ॥
saṁhatatvāt, kulālādivastuvat । saiva pratijñā ॥
yugapacca sarvaṁ pratyakṣameka(ta)sya, anekatve (tva)sakṣyanyonyasaṁbandhāt, prasiddhasambandhānekārthavat ॥
agnihotrādisādhanasādhanīye kasyacitpratyakṣe, sādhyasādhanarūpatvāt , bhujitṛptivat ॥
sarvāḥ śaktayaḥ kasyacit pratyakṣāḥ, vastutvāt, ghaṭādivat ॥
a[vā]ntarapratibandhābhāve sarvaṁ vastujātaṁ nairantaryeṇa kasyacit pratyakṣaṁ, śabdādimattvena sambandhāt, drāghīyasīmiva śaṣkulīṁ bhakṣayataḥ śabdādayaḥ ॥
svatantratayā kenacidekena sarvaṁ pratyakṣata upalabhyate, jñeyatvenābhimatatvāt, nāṭyavastuvat ॥
apratibandhena kasyacit pratyakṣopalabhyaṁ sarvam, aneka(satve)tve satyanyonyasaṁbandhāt, nāṭyasaṁbandhinartakādivat ॥
saṁsārarahitaḥ sarvajñaḥ, ajñānābhāvāt, muktātmavat । kleśādirahita īśvaraḥ, apratibandhajñānatvāt, siddhayogivat ॥
etena kleśādipratibandhājñānarahitatvena cakṣurādīndriyagrāmanirapekṣasarvaviṣayajñānatvaṁ siddham । sarvārthagrahaṇasamarthasya parameśvaracittasya sarvavyāpino yugapatsarvaviṣayayogitvāt । evaṁ sati samastavastugrahaṇābhāve kāraṇābhā(vānu)vopapatiḥ ॥
nāpi mūrtimatpratibandho'pyākāśavadeva sarvaviṣayayogino'pi cittasya । viṣayānavasthānādāvirbhāvatirobhāvasmṛtisaṁkalpānavasthitatvopapattiḥ । viṣayākāratayā vṛttilābhādarkaprabhāvat ॥
na hi kleśādyāvaraṇāvacchannaṁ cittasatvam, tasyādharmādiyogāt । sarvagatasya sarvārthasyāpi satvasyādharmādipratibandhakaniruddhasvakīyapravṛttimārgatvādindriyādidvārāpekṣitvamupapadyate । yathā apavarakādyāvaraṇāvṛtaḥ pradīpastadāvaraṇagatacchidradvāreṇa bahiḥ prakāśayati । sa eva tu pradīpaḥ prabhinnāpavarakāvaraṇaḥ sannanapekṣya tattacchidramārgaṁ samantataḥ prakāśayati ॥
tathaiveśvarasatvaṁ kleśādyāvaraṇayogābhāvādasati viṣayaviśeṣānirodhikāraṇe yugapadaśeṣārthagrahaṇam । tataśca svātilaṅghanānatilaṅghanādidoṣābhāvaḥ ॥
sarvasya viṣayatvāt sarvamekeśvaraṁ jagat, paripālakāpekṣasthānādyanekavastuviśeṣatvāt, prasiddhevaṁbhūtaikarājyavat ॥
tathā, niyatasthitihetvanekopakaraṇavattvāt, anyonyābhibhavanīyaprabhūtataradurgayuktānekadeśatvāt, abhaṅguravyavasthaśarīrabhedavatvācca, pratītaivaṁvidhaikarājyavat ॥
anekakartṛbhoktṛkriyāsādhanaphalasaṁbandhaviśeṣajñānavadupadiṣṭāni varṇāśramādyanuṣṭhānāni, phalārthibhiḥ pratyavāyabhīrubhistaiścānuṣṭhīyamānatvāt, bhaiṣajyarasāyanādyanuṣṭhānavat ।
tathā tadupadeśāḥ, parārthatvāt, upadetvāt, vidvacchraddheyatvāt, upadeśādṛte manuṣyānavagamyārthatvācca, bhaiṣajyādyupadeśavat ॥
śarīrendriyāṇi sarvatatprayojanavidekanimittakāraṇābhinirvartitāni, niyatakriyāsthitihetusādhanavatvāt, prāsādagṛhadāruyantrādivat ॥
atrābhidhīyate-svābhāvikī tāvanna bhavati pṛthivyādiracanā । dṛṣṭānto naiva tatsādhanasya vidyate । kaṇṭakādīnāṁ ca taikṣṇyaṁ na svābhāvikamabhyupeyate ॥
agnyādīnāmivauṣṇyādi svabhāvo vastudharmatvāddhetoḥ pṛthivyādiracaneti cet-prāsādādiracanāyā vastudharmatvāt syādānaikāntikatvam ॥
atha svābhāvikatvāditi cet-asiddhatvam, jagadracanāyā dharmādharmaphalopabhegārthaprayuktatvābhyupagamāt । kartṛdharmādharmastitvamupariṣṭāt sādhayiṣyate ॥
tasmāt pṛthivyādiracanā svābhāvikī na bhavati, prāṇyupabhegārthatvāt , prāsādādiracanāvat । candrādipravṛtirna svābhāvikī, pravṛtitvāt, asmadādipravṛttivat ॥
asmadādipravṛtirapi svābhāvikīti cet-na-agnyuṣṇatvavānityatvaprasaṅgāt । na hyagnyuṣṇatvaṁ svābhāvikaṁ sanniyataṁ nimittamātmalābhāya kāṅkṣati dharmisattāvyatirekeṇa । kriyāphalaracanādīnāṁ tu viśiṣṭanimittākāṅkṣaṇamātmapratilambhāyati na svābhāvikatvam ॥
niyatanimittākāṅkṣaṇamapi prāsādādiracanānāṁ svabhāva iti vet— astu tathāvidhasvabhāvatvam । tathā'pi pṛthivyādiracanāyā niyatanimittākāṅkṣaṇasvabhāvatvaṁ prāsādādivadeva । tataśva nāmni vipratipatirna doṣāya, kārakāntarāpekṣatvāditi pratijñā pratirūpakāriṇī ca ॥
bhavadbhiruktani [anumānāni] lokānumāgamavirodhāt [apramāṇāni] । anumānavirodhaṁ tāvat sātiśayatvādibhyo brūmaḥ ॥
āgamavirodhaṁ ca [“yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavit” “eko vaśī”] ityevamādibhyaḥ samācakṣmahe ॥
samastale.okavirodhaṁ cāpi । sarva evānārīge.opālaṁ saṁvyavaharamāṇāḥ satataṁ śivanārāyaṇādināmnā praṇihitacetasaḥ pratiṣedhatsvapi saṁbhinnabuddhiṣu akarṇīkṛtatatpratiṣedhaviṣayapallavāḥ parameśvaraṁ praṇatamūrdhānaḥ kusumāñjaliprabhṛtibhirarcayanti । phalaṁ cāpi tata eva prārthayante ॥
atha cedbrūyāt - sarvajñābhāvapratipādibhirasmadanumānairitarapratijñānāṁ virodha iti - atrocyate –
naitānyanumānāni । katham ? prathamaṁ tāvat pratijñaiva duṣṭā । yadi tāvadīśvaraśabdārthaḥ sarvajño na bhavatīti yuṣmadabhipreta īśvara ucyeta, tathā ca siddhasādhyatā syāt ॥
athāsmadabhipretaḥ, tathāpi yuṣmākamasiddhaviśeṣyatā bhavet ॥
atheśvaratvasyāsarvajñatvamucyate, tathāpi siddhaṁ sādhyate ॥
tathaivābhyupagamavirodho'pi । katham ? aiśvaryasarvajñabījatvayorvivardhamānatvāt kāṣṭhāprāpti: parimāṇavadevābhyupagamanīyā । tathā kāṣṭhāprāptaiśvaryasarvajñatvavācināvapīśvarasarvajñaśabdāveṣitavyau । kāṣṭhāpraptiśca niravadhikatvam । yathā parimāṇādīnāmātmākāśādyanantaparimāṇāntatvam । tathā cānumānābhyupagamasvavacanavirodhāḥ syuḥ ॥
kiñcānyat-kāṣṭhāprāteśvaratvasya ca śabdārthasya parityāge śabdārthavādaḥ prāpnoti । na hi śabdaḥ parityaktābhidheyaikadeśa uccaritaḥ ॥
atha parimāṇāderapi niravadhikaniṣṭhatvaṁ neṣyate-siddhāntavirodhaḥ । ātmākāśādīnāṁ hi sarvagatatvābhāve, madhyamaparimāṇatvānityatvādidoṣaprasaṅgaśca । athāpyātmanaḥ sarvatra kāryadarśanāt sarvagatatvam, tatrāpi śakunyādyātmanāṁ manuṣyagocarākāśādigatatvaṁ sāmānyato dṛṣṭādevānumānāt syāt । tathā cehāpi sāmānyato dṛṣṭānumānatvaṁ kena vāryate ॥
athānumānavirodhānnāvadhāryata iti cet-ātmādīnāmapi prameyatvavastutvādibhyaḥ pṛthivyādivadityanumānavirodhodbhāvanā śakyate [kartum] vaktum । na ca tāvatā'trānumānavirodhitvam, anumānābhāvaprasaṅgāt ॥
tathā anumānābhāva iṣyata iti cet---pratyakṣe'pyanāśvāsaḥ syāt । atha niścīyamānabuddhyutpatteḥ pratyakṣapramāṇatvam, anumānasyāpi tarhi niścitabuddhisamudbhavādastu prāmāṇyam । atha dṛṣṭasambandhadhūmādiviṣayamevānumānamiti cet-tatrāpyanumānābhāva eva - anagniḥ dhūmavān predaśaḥ, pratyakṣānupalabhyamānāgnisambandhe sati pradeśatvāt, agniśūnyopalabhyamānapradeśavaditi ॥
atha pramāṇāntarasaṁvādādadṛṣṭasambandhaviṣaye'numānasyānumānatvamucyate, pratyakṣamapi pramāṇāntarasaṁvādāt pramāṇaṁ bhavet, pramāṇatvāt, anumānavadeva । apramāṇaṁ syāt । pramāṇāntarasaṁvādābhāvāt, sāmānyato dṛṣṭādivaditi । tasmānna sāmānyato dṛṣṭasya pramāṇatvaṁ niścitabuddhitvādbādhituṁ śakyam ॥
kiṁ ca – sāmānyato dṛṣṭasya mānatvamanabhyupagacchataḥ svaśarīramaraṇasambandhalakṣaṇasyānupalabdhapūrvatvāt sarpādibhyo bhayānupapattiḥ । vyādhipratīkārāya cikitsādiprayogo na ghaṭeta । maraṇaśaṅkākāraṇābhāvāt । tathā janmanopyupalambhābhāvādātmaśarīrasyājatvaṁ cintyeta । hānopādānaniyogābhāvaśca syāt ॥
tasmāt sāmānyato dṛṣṭaparimāṇatvādisātiśayatvasāmānyādīśvarajñānaniravadhikatvasiddhiḥ ॥
kiṁ cānyat-īśvarasarvajñatvasya pratiṣiddhyamānatvāt sattvābhyupagamaḥ, a(nupa)padārthasya pratiṣedhāsambhavāt । na hi kevalo neti (na) prayujyate । īśvaraḥ sarvajño na bhavatītyucyate । tatra kvacit sarvajñatvamabhyupagataṁ bhavati ॥
tadyathā-śaśasya viṣāṇaṁ nāsti, vandhyāyāḥ suto nāsti, kusumamākāśasya nāstīti kvacidvidyamānānameva viṣāṇasutakusumādīnāṁ śaśādisaṁbanvena pratiṣedhaḥ, tadvadihāpi syāt ॥
kiṁ ca-īśvaraḥ sarvajño na bhavatīti, īśvaraśabdārthasarvajñatvasambandhapratiṣedhādinā īśvarādanyasya sarvajñatvābhyupagamaḥ । sambandhināvanabhyupagamya sambandhapratiṣedho hi na śakyaḥ kartum ॥
sa eṣa yuktaḥ sambandhaḥ pratiṣidhyate, ayuktaścābhyupagamyate । tatpariśramamātram । īśvarasarvajñayoḥ prasiddhapadārthayorapratiṣedhāt । na hyanantaparimāṇamākāśaṁ na bhavatītyākāśasya prasiddhamanantaparimāṇatvaṁ pratiṣidhyāprasiddhānantaparimāṇatveṣu ghaṭādiṣu tat vyavasthāpayituṁ yuktam ॥
atha sanbandhināveveśvarasarvajñatve pratiṣidhyete, svavacanavirodhinī pratijñā syāt । īśvarasarvajñatvayorīśvarasarvajñaśabdārthatvābhyupagamāt । na bhavatyagniragniśabdārtho na bhavatīti ॥
athāprasiddhapadārthāvīśvarasarvajñaśabdau, tathā'pi tadarthapratiṣedhānupapattiḥ । aprasiddhasyārthasya prāptyabhāvāt । na hi kiṁcidaprasiddhametacchikhare meṣakuṭumbinīṁ pratiṣeddhumarhati । kiṁ ca śabdopādānānarthakyaṁ ca । aprasiddhapadārthatvāt ॥
atha prasiddhārthayorīśvarasarvajñaśabdayorniravadhikeśvarasarvajñatvābhyāmaprasiddhābhyāṁ gaganasyeva kusumaiḥ saṁbandhaḥ kaiścit kalpitaḥ, sa pratiṣidhyeta-tathā'pyabhyupetārthapratiṣedhāt svavacanavirodhinyeva pratijñā syāt । sātiśayaniratiśayānekeśvarasarvajñavyaktimatsāmānyayorīśvarasarvajñaśabdārthavenābhyupagamāt ॥
prasiddhaṁ hi loke īśvarasarvajñaśabdayorutkarṣopakarṣayuktānekavyaktiviṣayabuddhyutpādakatvam । na hi grāmādhipatirīśvara iti dvitrigrāmaviṣayādhipataya uttarottareśvarā na bhavanti । yo vā kuṭumbādhipatirīśvaro na bhavati sarvaiścāsāvarthavānīśvaraśabdaḥ ॥
tathā vaiyākaraṇaḥ sarvajña ityukte nādhikavijñānayukto na bhavati । niravadhikau sāvadhikau veśvarasarvajñāvīśvarasarvajñaśabdayorarthāvabhyupagamyeyātām । atastatpratiṣedhādabhyupagamavirodhinī pratijñā syāt, ātmākāśādīnāṁ mahattvasya mahacchabdārthatvapratiṣedhavat ॥
atheśvarasarvajñau niravadhikau na sta:, anupalabhyamānatvāt, anīśvaradvitīyaśirovadityucyeta, tathā'pi śabdārthābhyupagamādabhyupagamāvirodhinī pratijñā ॥
sātiśayatvādibhiraiśvaryasarvajñatvabījādiliṅgairniravadhikeśvarasarvajñatvayorupalabhyamānatvaniravadhikaparimāṇatvavadityasiddhiranupalabdheḥ ॥
atha aviśeṣyaiveśvaraśabdārthaḥ sarvaijño na bhavatītyucyeta vastutvādihetubhirasmadādivaditi, tadā sarvapramāṇavirodhinī pratijñā syāt । prasiddheśvaraśabdārthasya prākṛtasarvajñatvasya sarvapramāṇasiddhatvāt । yathā īśvaraśabdārthaḥ [sarvajño na bhavati] prameyatvādibhirhetubhirghaṭādivadityukte yat brūyāttadevāhaṁ vakṣyāmi ॥
iha sarvajñaśūnyaṁ jagat । kālī vā diśa ākāśaṁ vā prāṇimaddeśo vā prāṇino vā sarve sarvajñaśūnyāḥ । pramāṇāni vā sarvāṇi sarvajñāviṣayāṇi । pramātāro vā sarvajñasyāpratipattāra:, ityevaṁjātīyāsu pratijñāsu niravadhikeśvare sarvajñe vā pratiṣidhyamāne, prasiddheśvarasarvajñaśabdārthābhyupagamavirodhāḥ pratijñādoṣā vacanīyāḥ ॥
nanu ca vandhyāsuto nāstīti, tacchūnyaṁ jagat kālo veti, pratijñāyamāne yathoktapratijñādoṣaprāptirbhavet - naiṣa doṣaḥ- vandhyāsutasattālakṣaṇasya pratiṣeddhavyasya vākyārthasyeśvarasarvajñaśabdārthavadaprasiddhatvāt kevalaśabdaprāpitasannidhānabuddhimātrapratipanne padārtha [padārtha pratiṣedha] vyāpāro'stīti vandhyāsutastitvasya (vā nāstitvasya) nābhyupagamo'sti । tato nābhyupagatapratiṣedhadoṣaḥ ॥
nanu ceśvaraḥ sarvajño na bhavatītyatrāpi buddhimātraṁ prāpyamāṇaṁ pratiṣidhyate, na kacidapi prāpnuvadvastu (na) pratiṣeddhuṁ śakyate pratihastineva hastī । yadi ca nañā vastu nirākariṣyate, nañmātreṇaiśvaravādipakṣatvamapi[pakṣo'pi]nirākariṣyate, (ataḥ) tasmādihāpi buddhimātrapratiṣedha iti nābhyupagatapratiṣedhaḥ pratijñādoṣaḥ ॥
satyamevam । kiṁ tvasti viśeṣaḥ । pramāṇasiddhavastuviṣayā buddhirvastvantare kālaviśeṣe vā pratiṣidhyate vastusāmānyāt prāpnuvatī yathā ghaṭo nāstīti । kvacidvināpyarthena buddhireva śabdapratyupanītasannidhānā kalpitavastvantarā pratiṣidhyate । yathā vandhyāsutī nāstīti ॥
yatra tu pramāṇāntarasiddhasadvastupratiṣedhastatrāpi[sti]abhyupagatārthapratiṣedhadoṣaḥ । yathā īśvaraśabdārthaḥ sarvajño na bhavatīti । īśvarasarvajñaśabdayorabhivardhamāneśvarasarvajñavyaktyanugatasāmānyavacanatvena liṅgena niravadhikeśvarasarvajñasattāvadyotitvaṁ siddhameva । mahadbahusarvānantaparimāṇādiśabdavat ॥
yathaivaite mahadādiśabdāḥ prasiddhasātiśayamahadādyanugatasāmānyārthābhidhāyinaḥ santo niravadhikamahadvahusarvānantaparimāṇavyaktīnāmastitvāvadyotanaliṅgā bhavanti । mahadādisāmānyānāṁ sātiśayavyaktyanugatānāṁ niravadhikamahadādivyaktivyāpana(ravyākṣīṇa)śaktitvāt । na hi santaṁ vyāpyamarthaṁ tadvaddhyāpakaḥ sannartho na vyāpnotīti । niravadhikāttu paro vyāpyo nāstīti vyāpakasya sāmānyasya kṣayaḥ vyāpyaviṣayatvenaiva prasiddhatvāttatra । tasmāt pramāṇasiddhatvādīśvarasarvajñaśabdāthayorabhāvaṁ sādhayato'bhyupagatārthapratiṣedha eveti duṣṭā pratijñā ॥
na ceśvarasarvajñaśabdayoratadarthavamanyārthatvaṁ vā karta viktuṁ śakyate । tathā śatijñānaiśvayaṇāṁ pratipururṣa samucitānāṁ sātiśayānāṁ niravadhika tatrva ataḥ[nānunmattaḥjpratiṣeddhumutsahetetyanumānavirodhitvaṁ pratijñāyāḥ ॥
kiṁ cānyat- pari[para]kalpitasyeśvarasya pratiṣedhaṁ kurvantaḥ pratyakṣaparacittāniṣṭāḥ prāpnuvanti । paravākyāditi cenna - sātiśayatvādisarvajñasādhakaliṅgapratipādakavadaviśiṣṭatvāt paravākyasya । tādṛśavākyārthapratiṣedhe cābhyupagatapratiṣedhaḥ, pūrvavadevānumānavirodhaśca ॥
kiṁ ca - prameyatvādihetūnāmapi asiddhatvam । kutaḥ ? asmābhirniratiśayajñānaiśvaryaviśiṣṭatvasyābhyupagatatvāt । atha svayamapi tādṛśamabhyupagacchettadā । sarvajñasiddhiḥ, abhyupagatatvāt ॥
kiṁ cānyat-abhyupagatatādṛkpratiṣedhe, yathā ghaṭo ghaṭo na bhavati, vastutvāt, paṭavāditi, evamihāpi syāt ॥
kiṁ ca-niravadhikasyānabhyupagame, prameyavādīnām [a]pakṣadharmatvamāśrayāsiddhatvaṁ ca । tadabhyupagame hi kiṁ sādhyaṁ bhavet ? yo hi tṛptavantaṁ brūyāt mā'trātsīriti, kiṁ tena kṛtaṁ syāt ॥
athāpi syāt--niravadhikamīśvaramabhisandhāya tasya sarvajñatvaṁ niṣedhāmīti । naidatapi yuktam -sarvajñatvasyapi niravadhikatvāt ॥
api ca sātiśayaiśvaryasarvajñatvayorutkarṣānutkarṣaviṣayatvena vyabhicārānneśvarasarvajñaśabdamukhyābhidheyatvam । yathā mahadādayaḥ śabdā vyabhicaritamahattvādiṣu ghaṭādiṣvamukhyāḥ, nākāśādiṣu, tathaivātrāpi niratiśayamaiśvaryaṁ sarvajñatvaṁ cāvyabhicārīti sa eva mukhyaḥ śabdārthaḥ । na ca mukhyanirākaraṇaṁ sādhimānamṛcchati ॥
kiṁ ca-yathā bhavatā anumānāgamaprasiddheśvarasya prameyatvādidharmavikalpatayā sarvajñatvaṁ nirākriyate, tathaiva prameyatvādibhiracetanatvamapi ghaṭādivadeva prāpnuyāt । avirodhāt । yathā prameyatvaṁ[a]sarvajñatvena vyāptamevamacetanatvādibhirapi ॥
pratyakṣavirodha iti cet-ihāpi anumānāgamavirodhaṁ kiṁ kaṭākṣeṇāpi nekṣase ॥
nāpi ca prameyatvādidharmasāmānyena sapakṣe vipakṣe vā kiñcit । kvacidadhyāropayituṁ śakyam । vastuviṣaye sarvatra prameyatvādīnāmāstitvāt । na matimohanārthaḥ prameyatvādyupanyāsaḥ ॥ atha ātmatvāditi cet, muktātmavadajñatvaprasaṅgaḥ syādbhavadīśvarāṇām । pratyakṣādivirodha iti cet-atrāpyanumānādivirodhaḥ pūrvavadeva ॥
bhūtabhaviṣyatkālayorapi īśvarasyānupalabdhāra itīdānīntaneśvarāṇāmupailabdhṛbhiranaikāntike prāṇitvādityādi । kiṁ ca atītānāgatakālayorapi sātiśayatvādiliṅgairupalabdhavanta upalapsyamānāśca prāṇinaḥ pramāṇakuśalāḥ, pramāṇakuśalatvāt, asmadādivat । atha aśarīratvādasarvajñaḥ, muktākāśādivat iti cet-na-saśarīratvāt । vyaktāvyaktaṁ hi sarvamaśarīraṁ saśarīratvādanityeśvaratvaṁ dharmādyapekṣatvādityuktatvāditi cet – na – śarīratvāt । saśarīrāśarīratvavirodha iti cet – na – muktamucyamānaikātmano'śarīratvasaśarīratvadarśanāt । tatra bhinnakālatvādavirodha iti cet-na- atrāpi bhinnakālābhyupagamāt ॥
kiṁ ca-yugapadīśvaratvādeva dvayasambhavaḥ । sakaraṇatā akaraṇatā'pi īśvaratvādeva yuktā । tathā ca śrutayaḥ- [“aśarīraṁ śarīreṣu”] iti । tathā [“yaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu tiṣṭhan”] iti । tathā [“yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavit”] ityādayaḥ ॥
śrutīnāṁ vipratiṣedhārthavādīśvarāpratyāyakatvam iti cet-na-ananyaśeṣatvāt । na hi karmaśeṣatve śrutiliṅgādīnāmanyatamadapi pramāṇamasti ॥
svādhyāyavidhiparigrahāddarśapūrṇamāsādiśeṣa iti cet-na-jyetiṣṭomādivadvidhyantarasya bhāvāt । yathaiva jyotiṣṭomādīnāṁ (prathamapraṁ,pṛthakprakaraṇādikāraṇādanyonyaśeṣaśeṣibhāvo nāsti । tathaiva [‘mantavyo nididhyāsitavyaḥ'] ityādiviṣayatvānnāgnihotrādiśeṣatvaṁ yuktam ॥
phalābhāva iti cet-na- [“sarvāṁśca lekānāpnoti sarvāṁśca kāmānyastamātmānamanuvidya vijānāti'] ityādiphalamuddiśya vidhānāt ॥
athaivamapyupāsanāvidhiśeṣatvāt stutireveti cet-nātyantamasatā stutirasti । na hi [“vāyurvai kṣepiṣṭhā devatā”] iti vāyorakṣepiṣṭhatvam । kvacidasatā'pi stutyadisambhava iti cet-na-anumānasiddhasyehopadānāt ॥
atha sarvakāryakaraṇayogādīśvarasya sarvaprāṇisukhaduḥkhādisaṁbandha iti cet-na-nimittabhedāt । dharmādinimittaḥ saṁsāriṇāṁ śarīrādisambandhaḥ । dharmādinimi(ktānāṁ)tto duḥkhādiyogaḥ । neśvarasya dharmādayaḥ । niratiśayaiśvaryādihetutvāccharīrādikāryakaraṇasaṁbandhasya । yathā grahatadāviṣṭayoḥ ॥
atha cakṣurādikaraṇatvādasmadādivat sarvānupalabdhariti cet-na- sarvaviṣayagrahaṇasamarthānāṁ pratibandhakaraṇābhāvāt । sarvagatānāṁ hi karaṇānāṁ [a]dharmādisaṁvaraṇena svaviṣayasaṅkocaḥ kriyate । yasya punarāvaraṇaṁ pratibandhaka[maṁ]- dharmādi na vidyate, tasya tadabhāvādaśeṣasvaviṣayagrahaṇāni karaṇānīti na duṣyati ॥
atha vā sarvaprāṇikaraṇaiḥ [īśvaraḥ] pṛthagātmanaḥ karaṇābhāve'pyāveśagraha iva sarvamanubhavati । na ca prāṇiśūnyo viṣayaḥ kaścidvidyate, ‘yaḥ pṛthivyāṁ tiṣṭhan’ ‘yo'psu tiṣṭhan’ ityevamādiśruterantaryāminānna īśvarasya sarveṣvavasthitatvaśravaṇāt ॥
api vā prakṛṣṭameva sa(rva)ttvaṁ nilyānatiśāyitaśaktijñāneśvaratvadharmakam, sarvagatatvādākāśavat sarvayogi, sarvārthatvātsarvaviṣayaprakāśakam, dharmādhamīdiviprayogādapratibandhaśaktikaṁ ca iti akāyānindriyatvapakṣe'pīśvarasarvajñatvasiddhiḥ ॥
cakṣurādyapekṣameva cittasya rūpādipratilambhasāmarthyamiti cet – na - aiśvaryadharmādyabhāvābhyāṁ parihṛtatvāt ॥
api ca cakṣurgrāhyasyāpi cakṣuṣā agrahaṇaṁ loke dṛśyate । cakṣurgrāhyaṁ sat sarvaṁ tamaḥ sannimīlitalocanairapi svasthāntaḥkaraṇairupalabhyate । tadeva cāndhatamasaṁ viṣphāritanayanairapyanyagatacittairnaiva gṛhyate । yathā gṛhyamāṇa evākāśe prakāśaḥ ॥
athāpi prakāśābhāvamātrameva tame na vasviti brayāt - tacca na - abhāvasya vastutirodhānasāmarthyābhāvāt ॥
atha grahaṇanimittasya prakāśasyābhāvādeva ghaṭādyagrahaṇaṁ, na vastutirodhāyakaṁ tama iti bruvīta-na-cakṣuṣaḥ prakāśakatvāt prakāśasāhāyakāpekṣānupapattiḥ । asati bhinnajātīye vastuni vastūnāṁ tirodhātṛṇi tatra yā ca yāvatī ca । mātrā prakāśakatvāccakṣuṣā prakāśyeta । na hi pradīpaḥ pradīpāntaradvaitīyakāpekṣaḥ prakāśayati ॥
kiṁ cānyat-cakṣuṣaḥ prakāśāntarasahāyatvāpekṣatāyāṁ ca niśāyāmapi tārādhipatiprakāśadvitīyena cakṣuṣā divasa iva rūpādigrahaṇaprasaṅgastirodhānasyāsati nimitte ॥
kiṁ cānyat-abhāvaścettamaḥ, candramāsu niśāyāṁ bhā(bhava)ntīṣu tamasā mandena na pravartitavyam । sarvātmanaiva hi tena vinaśanīyam । bhāsāṁ bhāvāt । bhāsāṁ tu vastutvānmandatvapāṭavādiviśeṣo ghaṭate, na(bhāvasya)abhāvasya nirviśeṣatvāt ॥
kiṁ ca-sahāyābhāvāccakṣuṣa upalabdhasāmarthyābhāvādagrahaṇamityetadapi vyabhicarati । yathā satyapi vidyullatāprakāśe tīvratare vidyullatavilāse ca kiṁ taddṛṣṭirnopalabhate । na hi vidyutaḥ sahāyake dṛṣṭacakitatvenāgrahaṇaṁ virodhābhāvādyuttam ॥
kiñca - cikitsāśāstre chāyā madhuraśītaletyucyate । na hyavastuno madhuraśītalatvam । tathā cākṣipati pathyatvam । nābhāvasya pathyāpathyatvaṁ brūyuḥ ॥
pradīpācchāyopalabdheśca । abhāvaścettamaḥ, pradīpaprabhāmaṇḍale pradīpācchāyā kathaṁ bhavet । vastutve'pi virodhādayuktamiti cet-na-viṣasarpayoriva saṁbhavāt । yathā prāṇaviyogakaramapi viṣaṁ pannagaprāṇaviyogāya na paryāpnoti, tathā pradīpatacchāyayorapi ॥
tasmādvastu tamaḥ, prakarṣāpakarṣavattvāt , prabhāvat । virodhidravyāpaneyatvācca, ghaṭavat । upalabdhṛvyavadhānakaratvācca, bhittivaditi ॥
itaśvendriyanirapekṣamapyantaḥkaraṇamindriyaviṣayagrahaṇāya samartham । pihitakarṇavivarasya ghoṣopalaṁbhāt । na ca pihitakarṇasaṁpuṭasya śrotrāntaramanumātuṁ śakyam । badhirasyāpi pihitaśrotrapuṭasya tadagrahaṇāt ॥
kiñca-pratijñājñānenāpi rūpādigrahaṇamindrayanirapekṣaṁ dṛśyate ॥
kiñcānyat-smṛteścānupapattiḥ syāt indriyanirapekṣasya cittasya sātiśayagrahaṇasāmartharye'pi । spaṣṭāśca smṛtayaḥ svāpnā rūpādiviṣayāḥ ॥
yadi cakṣurādyantaḥkaraṇābhyāṁ samanvitābhyāṁ rūpagrahaṇaṁ pūrvamapi nirvartiṣyate, svapnādāvapi samucitābhyāmeva paryagrahīṣyata । na caivamasti । sukhādigrahaṇe svātantryaṁ cittasya sarvaprasiddham ॥
tasmādālokasthānīyānīndriyāṇi cittasya, viṣayagrahaṇe svatantrasyaiva svataḥ । taduktam [“indriyapranāḍikayā’] iti । tathā śrutirapi- [‘manasā° hyeva paśyati manasā śṛṇoti’] iti ॥
athocyeta - indriyāṇāmālekāpekṣāvat antaḥkaraṇamapīndriyasāhāyakāpekṣameva grāhakamiti –tanna - vyabhicārāt । rātriñcarāṇāṁ vibhinnavyālokadvaitīyakena divasa iva rūpagrahaṇam । satyapi prakāśe na rūpasya grahaṇamulūkādibhirdine ॥
kiñca-sādhanāpekṣasya vijñānasādhanādṛte'pi tulādau । darśanamātreṇaiva suvarṇādiparimāṇajñānaṁ dṛśyate ॥
atha cedbrūyādānarthakyaṁ cakṣurādīnāmiti-sa vaktavyaḥ-tulādivadevānyatrārthavattvamindriyāṇāmiti । yathaiva tulādiviṣayavaimatyaprakarṣāt puruṣasya vināpi tulādisādhanena darśanamātrādeva kanakadivastuparicchedakauśalaṁ, tathaivāntaḥkaraṇasyānapekṣitacakṣurādisāhāyakasyāpi vaimatyaprakarṣādrūpādigrahaṇasāmarthyaṁ na vihanyate ॥
nāpi hyanekanirvartanīyaṁ kriyājātamekena nābhinirvartyate । dṛśyante ca bahubhiruttotyamānaṁ śilādikamadvitīyā hastipuruṣādayaḥ keciduttolayantaḥ ॥
tathaivendriyasahāyenānyeṣāmanta:karaṇena gṛhyumāṇā rūpādayaḥ parameśvaracittasatvenānākalita(vakarṇita)cakṣurādiparispandena kevalenaiva gṛhyante । kāṣṭhāgatatvādvematyaśakyaiśvaryaprakarṣasya ॥
saṁsāriṇāṁ tato nikṛṣṭatvādavidyādimalenaiśvaryaśaktijñānādīnāmindriyasahakāritvāpekṣitvamanta: karaṇasya । śilādisamuttolana iva hīnabalānām ॥
ye(ṣāṁ) punaḥ saṁsāriṇa eva santa īśvarībhavanti buddharṣabhādayaḥ, teṣāṁ niratiśayaśaktijñānaiśvaryanupapattiḥ । kālaparicchedyatvāt । abhyupagacchanti ca taddarśanaślāghinaḥ kālaparicchedanīyake teṣām ॥
nāsmadīśvarasya kālaparicchedyatā । tatkālaistadādyakālaiśva buddhādibhiraparijñātaiśvaryādisātiśayatvādiliṅgairanumeya evāsau । nāmuṣmin kāla utpanna utpadyata utpatsyamāna iti tridhā kaiścidanumīyate । niratiśayatvavirodhī hi tathā[dā]syāt ॥
tasmāt buddhādīnāṁ siddhyapekṣatvāt, pūrvabuddhānāṁ kālādhikyaprāpteruttarakālabuddhasyāpi na niratiśaktyaiśvaryajñānatvaṁ viruddham । atha tutyaśaktijñānaiśvaryāṇāmeva teṣāṁ samānarājyarājānāmivāsamānakālatvamiti brūyāt, tathāpi buddhāntarakālasya vyāptyabhilāṣavighātānniratiśayaiśvaryādyabhāvaḥ ॥
abhilaṣati hi kaścit buddhāntaraṁ vaśīkartum , tadviṣayaṁ ca vyāptum । aniyatatvādicchāyāḥ । buddhāntarāvaśīkaraṇe ca sarvavaśitvaṁ hī(nī)yeta ॥
atha ceducyeta, buddhāntarasyānanugrāhyatvādrāgādyabhāvācca tadviṣayavyāptāvanabhilāṣa iti-atrocyate-yathaiva prāptabuddhatvasya kaṁcitkālamavasthānamabhilāṣapūrvakam, tathā buddhāntarakālāvasthānābhilāṣeṇāvaśyaṁ bhavitavyam ॥
anugrāhyaprāṇyantarabhāvācca kālāntarāvasthānābhilāṣeṇa yukta bhavitum । na ca bhaviṣyatā buddhena sarve prāṇabhṛto'nugrahīṣyante ॥
buddhatvasya ca duḥkhādyātmakatve'pi prāṇyanugrahārthatvādbuddhasthiteḥ kālāntarāvasthānecchayā bhavitavyameva । siddheśca prāgavidyādiparāmaśat, buddhasvarūpasya ca duḥkhaśūnyādyātmakatvasya tairabhyupetatvāt, buddharṣabhādyanyatīrthakaraṇāt[karāt]niratiśayaśaktijñānaiścaryānupapattiḥ ॥
kālānavacchedātu naite doṣā asmadīśvare kramante । śaktijñānaiśvaryāṇāṁ tu niravadhikatvānumānāt sātiśayatvānavasthitatvādidoṣaḥ nātmākāśādīnāmivātiśaṅkanīyaḥ ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇa (Elucidation):
A proof is presented for establishing <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) as previously declared— [Therein is the unsurpassed seed of omniscience. 'Therein'] means in that <s>Īśvara</s> of the previously declared definition, [unsurpassedness] is appropriate. What is that? [That which is] the unerring knowledge of perception and inference [having as its objects] the past, future, present, the aggregate [of all three times], and the supersensory. Since the supersensory includes the past and future, the term 'supersensory grasp' is used.
That supersensory grasp is threefold: having subtle objects, having obscured objects, and having remote objects. ['From small to many.'] As is well known, [this knowledge] increasing through degrees of surpassability [is] the seed of omniscience—just as the knowledge of smoke is [the seed] of the knowledge of fire. How? Where it reaches its ultimate limit. Since knowledge resides in a knower, [the text says] 'in whom'—meaning 'in which knower.' [He is the omniscient one]—established.
Likewise, power (<s>śakti</s>) too, increasing through degrees of surpassability, where it reaches its limit—he is the all-powerful one. Thereby is established his agency in the creation, maintenance, and dissolution of the world. Likewise, sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>) too, increasing, where it reaches its limit—he is the supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>). And thereby is established the absence of defects such as the opposite of power, etc.
One might object: even ignorance, increasing, being naturally established and reaching its limit, could be established in that <s>Īśvara</s>—no, because of incompatibility with knowledge. For there cannot be a conjunction of knowledge and ignorance, which are mutually contradictory, in one subject. For where knowledge is supreme, ignorance cannot exist there.
For where light increases, darkness is necessarily diminished. If one says 'the reverse too'—that is not so, because darkness is not perceived when light is present. Existing darkness is concealed by light; but existing light is never overpowered by darkness.
As for the invisibility of the sun during the rainy season due to the obstruction of clouds—that too is merely an obstruction of vision, not the concealment of light itself as by darkness. Therefore, where knowledge increases, ignorance does not exist, just as darkness does not exist in the sun—because [<s>Īśvara</s>'s] <s>sattva</s> has <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> permanently and completely concealed.
Moreover, ignorance, not having real objects as its domain, cannot increase. Knowledge, having knowable real objects as its domain, can reasonably increase. For if ignorance had real objects as its domain, it would become knowledge.
As for the alleged 'increase of ignorance' in plants and the like—that is not truly an increase. It is spoken of only in relation to the absolute absence of knowledge. For if ignorance truly increased, then a thousandfold ignorance would not be removable by a single [act of] knowledge. Rather, each ignorance would have to be removed by a separately arisen knowledge. Therefore ignorance does not increase in its own nature.
For that which has degrees of surpassability is seen to reach its ultimate limit—just as the magnitudes of fruits etc. reach their maximum in the infinity of space. Likewise, the seed of omniscience too should reach its ultimate limit.
The entirety of all objects, both collectively and individually, is perceptible to some one being, because of being knowable, like a pot etc.
Because of serving the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Self), as objects of knowledge, like a pot etc.
And the earth has an origin, because of having parts, like a pot.
The world has been produced by a single being who knows the distinction between the <s>karmas</s> (actions) of living beings, their means, and their fruits—because of possessing specific arrangements of places for enjoyment etc., like a palace.
The earth, made for the enjoyment of many beings, has been produced by a single intelligent being—because of being enjoyable by many living beings, like rice and barley.
The earth has been produced by a single being desiring multiple purposes—like a house etc.
The aggregate of mountains, rivers, etc., which is the abode of all beings, has been produced by a single skilled being possessing the knowledge appropriate for the enjoyment of its inhabitants—from the very cause and example already stated.
The sun, possessing the power of illumination etc. for many beings, has been produced by a single being possessing knowledge of its capacities—because of being luminous in nature, like a lamp.
The regulated movement of the sun's rising, setting, etc. at fixed times has been set in motion by a single being possessing knowledge of its purpose—because of being at fixed times, like agriculture etc.
The activity of the sun, planets, moon, stars, etc., set in motion by a single intelligent lord (<s>Īśvara</s>)—because, though the activity is of the nature of suffering, it occurs at regulated times—like the activity of disciples, servants, etc. of one who knows <s>dharma</s>.
The waxing and waning of the moon have been set in motion by a single being possessing knowledge of time-measurement such as <s>tithis</s> (lunar days)—because of serving to demarcate time, like a water-clock etc. The moon has been produced by a single being possessing knowledge of time-measurement—because of possessing waxing and waning, like a water-clock.
The world has a single intelligent sovereign—because of consisting of many domains governed by mutually opposed leaders of many beings, like a kingdom of this kind.
All of this—the entire complex of means, ends, and states of activity—is perceptible to some single being, because of having a single purpose through the mutual opposition and support of its parts, like a military operation.
Because of being composite—like the products of a potter. That itself is the thesis.
And all [objects] are simultaneously perceptible to a single being—because, if there were many [knowers], their mutual relation would require a witness—like one who knows multiple objects with established connections.
When the rituals such as <s>agnihotra</s> are perceptible to someone [through their means and ends]—because of being of the nature of means and ends, like eating and satisfaction.
All powers are perceptible to someone—because of being real, like a pot.
In the absence of intervening obstruction, all objects are perceptible to someone in unbroken succession—because of their connection through possessing sound etc., like one eating a long pastry perceives sounds etc.
By a single being, independently, everything is perceived directly—because of being intended as knowable, like the subject matter of a drama.
All things are perceivable by someone without obstruction—because, being manifold, they have mutual connection, like dancers etc. connected with a drama.
The omniscient one is free from <s>saṃsāra</s>—because of the absence of ignorance, like a liberated soul. <s>Īśvara</s> is free from <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) etc.—because of having unobstructed knowledge, like an accomplished <s>yogin</s>.
By this, it is established that through freedom from the obstruction of <s>kleśas</s> etc., [<s>Īśvara</s>] has knowledge of all objects independent of the sense organs such as the eye etc. For the mind (<s>citta</s>) of the supreme Lord, capable of grasping all objects, being all-pervading, is simultaneously connected with all objects. This being so, the absence of grasping all objects [by ordinary beings] is explained by the absence of the cause.
Nor is there any material obstruction for the mind that is connected with all objects—for it is like space itself. Because of the non-fixity of objects, the arising and disappearing, memory and intention, are established as unstable. Through assuming the form of objects, it obtains its modifications, like the radiance of the sun.
For the <s>sattva</s> (pure being) of the mind is not veiled by obstructions such as <s>kleśas</s>, when it is [<s>Īśvara</s>'s], because of the absence of connection with <s>adharma</s> (demerit) etc. Even though <s>sattva</s> is all-pervading and of the nature of all objects, when its own channel of activity is blocked by obstructions such as <s>adharma</s>, dependence on doors such as the sense organs is established.
