body.translated_text: <s>tasyāpi nirodhe sarvanirodhān nirbījaḥ samādhiḥ</s> — Upon the cessation of even that, from the cessation of all, arises <s>nirbīja samādhi</s> (seedless concentration). (Sūtra 51)

body.text: sa na kevalaṁ samādhiprajñāvirodhī prajñākṛtānāmapi saṁskārāṇāṁ pratibandhī bhavati। kasmāt, nirodhajaḥ saṁskāraḥ samādhijānsaṁskārānbādhata iti।
body.translated_text: That [impression born of truth-bearing wisdom] is not merely opposed to the wisdom of <s>samādhi</s>; it also obstructs the impressions produced by wisdom. Why? Because the impression born of cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) suppresses the impressions born of <s>samādhi</s>.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
kiñca— [tasyāpi nirodhe sarvanirodhānnirbījassamādhiriti । iti] śabdaḥ parisamāptyarthaḥ । [tasyāpi] samādhiprajñāprabhavasya saṁskārasyābhinavasya [nirodhe api] śabdātsaṁskārakāraṇasya samādhiprajñāyā api nirodhe, [sarvanirodho] bhavati । uktamevopāyadvayaṁ paravairāgyavirāmapratyayābhyāsākhyaṁ tannirodhasya ॥
kiṁ punastatsarvaṁ ? yannirotsyate । vyutthānasamādhiprajñātatsaṁskārāḥ । tasmāt [sarvanirodhānnirbījaḥ samādhiḥ ॥]
[sa na kevalaṁ] ṛtambharaprajñājanitasaṁskāraḥ [samādhiprajñānirodhī,] yathaiva tāṁ samādhiprajñāmṛtambharāṁ niruṇaddhi, tathaivātmanā sahātmasajātīyānāṁ svakāraṇa [prajñākṛtānāṁ saṁskārāṇāmapi pratibandhī] nirodhā [dbhavati ॥]
kasmāt ? [nirodhajaḥ saṁskāraḥ] yasmātsamādhiprajñāyāstajjanmanaśca saṁskārasya nirodhe, nirodhakaḥ samādhiprajñājānitasaṁskārādanyo jāyate, sa cāpi yataḥ samādhiprajñāṁ tajjanitasaṁskārāṁścātiraskṛtya na janma pratipadyate, tasmātsa [nirodhajaḥ saṁskāraḥ samādhijānsaṁskārānbādhata iti ॥]
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇa (Elucidation):
Moreover— [Upon the cessation of even that, from the cessation of all, arises <s>nirbīja samādhi</s> (seedless concentration).] The word '<s>iti</s>' is for the sense of completion. [Of even that]—of the impression born of the wisdom of <s>samādhi</s>, which is fresh, [upon the cessation]—and by the word '<s>api</s>' (even), upon the cessation of the wisdom of <s>samādhi</s> which is the cause of that impression—[the cessation of all] occurs. The twofold means already stated—namely, supreme dispassion (<s>paravairāgya</s>) and the practice of the cessation-cognition (<s>virāmapratyayābhyāsa</s>)—is the means of that cessation.
What then is that 'all' which is to be ceased? The cognitions of distraction, of <s>samādhi</s>-wisdom, and their impressions. Therefore, [from the cessation of all, <s>nirbīja samādhi</s> arises.]
[That impression born of truth-bearing wisdom] is [not merely opposed to the wisdom of <s>samādhi</s>]—just as it suppresses that <s>ṛtambharā</s> wisdom of <s>samādhi</s>, so too [it obstructs] its own kind, together with itself, and the impressions produced by its cause, the wisdom—[it becomes the obstructor of the impressions produced by wisdom, due to cessation.]
Why? [The impression born of cessation]—because, when the wisdom of <s>samādhi</s> and the impression born of it are ceased, another [impression] born of the ceasing agent arises distinct from the impression born of the wisdom of <s>samādhi</s>; and since it does not arise without first having surpassed the wisdom of <s>samādhi</s> and its produced impressions—therefore [the impression born of cessation suppresses the impressions born of <s>samādhi</s>.]

body.text: nirodhasthitikālakramānubhavena nirodhacittakṛtasaṁskārāstitvamanumeyam। vyutthānanirodha-samādhiprabhavaiḥ saha kaivalyabhāgīyaiḥ saṁskāraiścittaṁ svasyāṁ prakṛtāvavasthitāyāṁ pravilīyate। tasmātte saṁskārāścittasyādhikāravirodhino na sthitihetavo bhavantīti।
body.translated_text: From the experience of the gradual duration of the cessation-state, the existence of impressions produced by the mind in the cessation-state is to be inferred. Together with the impressions conducive to <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation)—born of distraction, of cessation, and of <s>samādhi</s>—the mind dissolves into its own primal nature (<s>prakṛti</s>), which remains as it is. Therefore those impressions, being opposed to the mind's further activity, do not serve as causes of its continuance.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
kathaṁ punarasau nirodhajaḥ saṁskāro'stīti gamyate ? vidyamāne'pi sa bādhako bhavatīti ? āha- [nirodhasthitikālakramānubhaveneti ।] nirodhasya sthitistasyāḥ kālaḥ sa ca kālaḥ krameṇānubhūyate, yataḥ pratyabhyāsamabhivardhate, tasmāttena [nirodhasthitikālakramānubhavena] nirodha [cittakṛtaṁ] nirodhāvasthacittakṛtaṁ [saṁskārāstitvamanumeyam ॥]
[vyutthānanirodhasamādhiprabhavaiḥ] vyutthānasamādhiprabhavaiḥ nirodhasamādhiprabhavaiśca [saha kaivalyabhāgīyaiḥ saṁskaraiścittaṁ] avasitādhikāratvāt [svasyāṁ prakṛtau] svakāraṇe'smitāyāmahaṅkāre [pravilīyate] pratyastameti । [tasmātte] khyātinirodhajanmānaḥ [saṁskārā] yasmāt [cittasyādhikārāvirodhinaḥ na sthitihetavo bhavantīti ॥]
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇa (Elucidation):
But how is it known that this impression born of cessation exists? That it is an obstructor even while existing? He says— [From the experience of the gradual duration of the cessation-state.] The stability of cessation, its duration, and the gradual experience of that duration—because it increases with each successive practice—therefore [from the experience of the gradual duration of the cessation-state], the [existence of an impression produced by the mind in the cessation-state is to be inferred.]
[Together with the impressions born of distraction, cessation, and <s>samādhi</s>]—born of distraction and <s>samādhi</s>, and born of cessation and <s>samādhi</s>—[together with the impressions conducive to <s>kaivalya</s>, the mind,] because its function is complete, [dissolves into its own nature (<s>prakṛti</s>)]—into its own cause, the <s>asmitā</s> (I-am-ness), the <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle)—[it subsides.] [Therefore those] impressions born of discriminative knowledge and cessation [are not causes of the mind's continuance, because they are opposed to the mind's further activity.]

body.text: yasmādavasitādhikāraṁ saha kaivalyabhāgīyaiḥ saṁskāraiścittaṁ nivartate, tasminnivṛtte puruṣaḥ svarūpamātrapratiṣṭho'taḥ śuddhaḥ kevalo mukta ityucyata iti ॥ 51 ॥
body.translated_text: Since the mind, its function complete, ceases together with the impressions conducive to <s>kaivalya</s>—when it has ceased, <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Self), established solely in its own nature, is therefore said to be pure, isolated (<s>kevala</s>), and liberated.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[yasmādavasitādhikāraṁ saha kevalyabhāgīyaiḥ saṁskaraiścittaṁ] yaṁ puruṣaṁ prati caritaprayojanaṁ tasmāt [nivartate । tasminvinivṛtte puruṣaḥ svarūpamātrapratiṣṭhaḥ kevalo mukta ityucyate,] cittavṛttinivṛttireva muktiḥ iti ॥ 51 ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇa (Elucidation):
[Since the mind, its function complete, together with the impressions conducive to <s>kaivalya</s>,] ceases with respect to that <s>Puruṣa</s> for whom its purpose has been fulfilled. [When it has ceased, <s>Puruṣa</s>, established solely in its own nature, is isolated and said to be liberated]—the cessation of the modifications of the mind is itself liberation.

body.text: sādhanapādaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Sādhanapādaḥ</s> — Chapter on the Means of Practice.

body.text: uddiṣṭaḥ samāhitacittasya yogaḥ। kathaṁ vyutthitacitto'pi yogayuktaḥ syādityetadārabhyate –
body.translated_text: The <s>yoga</s> of one whose mind is concentrated has been described. How one whose mind is in the state of distraction may also become united with <s>yoga</s>—this is now undertaken:

body.text: tapaḥsvādhyāyeśvarapraṇidhānāni kriyāyogaḥ ॥ 1 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>tapaḥsvādhyāyeśvarapraṇidhānāni kriyāyogaḥ</s> — <s>Tapas</s> (austerity), <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study), and <s>Īśvarapraṇidhāna</s> (devotion to the Lord) constitute <s>kriyāyoga</s> (the yoga of action). (Sūtra 2.1)

body.text: nātapasvino yogaḥ sidhyati। anādikarmakleśavāsanācitrā pratyupasthitaviṣayajālā cāśuddhirnāntareṇa tapaḥ saṁbhedamāpadyata iti tapasa upādānam। tacca cittaprasādanamabādhamānamanenā''sevyamiti manyate। svādhyāyaḥ praṇavādipavitrāṇāṁ japo mokṣaśāstrādhyayanaṁ vā। īśvarapraṇidhānaṁ sarvakriyāṇāṁ paramagurāvarpaṇaṁ tatphalasaṁnyāso vā ॥ 1 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>Yoga</s> does not succeed for one who is not an ascetic (<s>atapasvī</s>). The impurity—variegated by <s>karmas</s>, <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), and <s>vāsanās</s> (latent tendencies) accumulated since beginningless time, with the net of sense-objects arrayed before it—does not undergo dissolution without <s>tapas</s>; hence the adoption of <s>tapas</s>. And he considers that [<s>tapas</s>] purifies the mind and does not cause harm when thus practiced. <s>Svādhyāya</s> (self-study) is the repetition of sacred syllables such as <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ) etc., or the study of the scriptures on liberation (<s>mokṣaśāstra</s>). <s>Īśvarapraṇidhāna</s> (devotion to the Lord) is the offering of all actions to the supreme teacher (<s>paramaguru</s>), or the renunciation of their fruits.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
athedānīṁ dvitīyaḥ sādhanapāda ārabhyate । kaivalyasya sādhanaṁ samyagdarśanam । yogasādhanāni ca yogadvāreṇa samyagdarśanasādhanānyeva । tāni ca prādhānyenāsminpāde pratipādyanta iti sādhanapāda ityucyate ॥
tathā, yogasādhanānuṣṭhānapravṛttasyānuṣaṅgikavibhūteḥ prādhānyena pratipādanādvibhūtipāda ityucyate tṛtīyaḥ ॥
tathā, sakalayogaiśvaryavibhūtibhyo viraktasya sarvopasaṁhāradvāreṇa kaivalyasya prādhānyena pradarśanāt kaivalpāda ityucyate caturthaḥ ॥
tathā, samādhiḥ prādhānyenādāvupākhyāta iti prathamaḥ samādhipāda ityucyate ॥
tadetadāha- [uddiṣṭaḥ samāhitacittasya yoga iti] -karmaṇyacittasyetyarthaḥ । maitrīkaruṇādibhāvanādyupā(khyā)yalabdhasthitipadasya yoginaḥ paravairāgyavirāmapratyayasādhano nirbījaḥ samādhiruddiṣṭaḥ । [kathaṁ vyutthitacitto'pi yogayuktaḥ syāditi ।] vikṣiptacitto'pi kathaṁ nāma samādhiyogyo bhavedityata idamārabhyate ।
tapa ādisādhanamanukramyate- [tapassvādhyāyeśvarapraṇidhānāni kriyāyogaḥ ।]
nanu ca tapassvādhyāyeśvarapraṇidhānāni niyameṣu vadiṣyamāṇāni kimarthamihocyante ॥
nanu caitadeva prayojanaṁ--yaduktaṁ vyutthitacitto'pi yogayuktaḥ syāditi ॥
nai tadasti-yatra niyamāḥ paṭhyante tatraivedaṁ prayojanaṁ sidhyati ।
atha kleśatanūkaraṇārthamiti cenna-tasyāpi tatraivābhidhānāt । yathā [“ yogāṅgānuṣṭhānādaśuddhikṣaye”] iti । aśuddhiśca kleśādi: । samādhibhāvanārthañca yogāṅgānuṣṭhānamāmnāyiṣyata eva । yathā [“ samādhisiddhirīśvarapraṇidhānāt”] iti । tasmādiha tapa ādisamāmnānamanarthakam ॥
na-yogāṅgānuṣṭhānasya samyagdarśanopāyasya samyagdarśanapūrvatvapratipādanārthatvāt । sarvāṇi ca yogāṅgāni samyagdarśanopāyatvātsamyagdarśanaprākkālāni । teṣāṁ ca niyamaikadeśa iha paṭhita: sarvopāyaprākkālatve nidarśanāya । yadyapyupāyatvādeva prākālatvamarthātsiddham , tathā'pi spaṣṭatvamevaṁ sati syāditi ॥
nanu caivamapi prāk samyagdarśanādanantaraṁ paṭhitavyam-ucyate-na-samyagdarśanasyaiva sākṣātkleśadipratipakṣatvāt । avidyā hi samastānarthamūlam । sā ca sākṣātpratyanīkabhūtasamyagdarśanena nivartyate । tapa ādestadanantaraṁ pāṭhe satyavidyāsamyagdarśanayorvyavadhānaṁ bhavet । tato'bhiśaṁketa-kiṁ avidyāyāstapaādiḥ sākṣātpratipakṣaḥ ? kiṁ vā samyagdarśanameveti ॥
kiñca---viṣayaśca prathamaṁ darśanīyaḥ samyagdarśanaśāsrasya । sa ca kleśakarmavipākāśayābhibhūtaḥ puruṣaḥ । yathā rogārtaḥ cikitsāśākhasya viṣayaḥ । tapaādestadanantaraṁ samāmnāne viṣayaviṣayiṇau vyavadhīyeyātāṁ, tataścāyaṁ viṣayo'yañca viṣayīti na vivicyeta ॥
pādādau ca pāṭhe samyagdarśanopāyatvaṁ ca pratipāditaṁ bhavati, prathamapādasambandhaśca vyākhyātaḥ syāt-samāhitacittasya yoga uddiṣṭaḥ, vyutthitacitto'pi tapaādisādhanaḥ kathaṁ yogayuktaḥ syāditi ॥
kiñca-samādhibhāvanakleśatanūkaraṇārthatvañca tapaādīnāṁ darśayitavyam ॥
nanu parastādevaitadvakṣyati- ["samādhisiddhirīścarapraṇidhānāt " "kāyendriyasiddhiraśuddhikṣayāttapasaḥ"] ityevam । pratyekasādhanānāṁ siddhiṁ ca vakṣyati ॥
naitadasti-siddhānāmiha tatra sādhanastutyarthamanuvādāt । atra hi tādarthyamucyate । tathā cāha- ["samādhibhāvanārthaḥ kleśatanūkaraṇārthaśca"] iti । tatra hyanūdyante sādhanastutaye । samprati sūtrākṣarāṇi vyākhyāyante-tapaśca svādhyāyaśceśvarapraṇidhānañca tapassvādhyāyeśvarapraṇidhānāni । tānyava kriyārūpo yoga: kriyāyogaḥ । tapaādikriyā ca yogārthavādyoga ityucyate । citatdharmo hi samādhiryogaḥ । tadarthaścāyaṁ kriyāyogaḥ । tasmādanena kriyāyogena yogīti ॥
[tapa iti] kṛcchracāndrāyaṇādi, śītoṣṇādidvandvasahatvam । [svādhyāyaḥ] -praṇavasya mokṣaśāstrāṇāṁ copaniṣatprabhṛtīnāṁ pavitrāṇāṁ japaḥ । [īśvarapraṇidhānaṁ] -kriyāṇāṁ paramagurāvīśvare samarpaṇam । tāsāṁ vā phalasanyāsa: parameśvare saṁnyasanam ॥
kathaṁ punaścittasamādhānaṁ prati viprakṛṣṭasya kāyakleśadirūpasya tapaso yogatvam ? svādhyāyeśvarapraṇidhānayostu yuktamantaraṅgatvādyogatvamiti, tadarthamāha - [nātapasvino yogaḥ sidhyatīti ॥]
śarīrādipoṣaṇābhiratacittasya kāyendriyamanaḥkhedaparihāraparāyaṇasyātyantaśarīrādyātmatvadarśinaḥ sukumārataraṁmanyasya na yogaḥ sidhyatīti tapasa upādānam ॥
kiñca- [anādivāsanācitrā] -viṣayagrahaṇavāsanābhiranadikālabhiruparacitavicitrabhāvā । tathā [pratyupasthitaviṣayajālā] -vartamānakālā viṣayā eva jāle, tena ca vartamānaviṣayākhyena jālena ānāyena jhaṣāniva cita aśuddhiḥ pāśayati yā sā pratyupasthitaviṣayajālā satī yasmāt [nāntareṇa tapaḥ] tapasā vinā [sambhedaṁ] vināśam [āpadyate,] asambhinnāśuddheścittasya kutaḥ samādhiḥ [iti] tatsambhedanāya ca [tapasa upādānam । tacca] tapaḥ [cittaprasādanaṁ] samādhyantaraṅgaṁ [abādhamānamanenāsevyamiti] yogā [manyante ।] cittaprasādārthatvāttapasastameva cedvādheta tādarthyameva hīyeta ॥ 1 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
Now the second chapter, the <s>Sādhanapāda</s> (Chapter on Means), begins. The means to <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation) is <s>samyag-darśana</s> (right knowledge). And the means of <s>yoga</s> are themselves means to right knowledge through yoga. Since these are predominantly taught in this chapter, it is called the <s>Sādhanapāda</s>.
Likewise, since the incidental <s>vibhūtis</s> (powers) that arise for one engaged in the practice of the means of yoga are predominantly taught, the third chapter is called the <s>Vibhūtipāda</s> (Chapter on Powers).
Likewise, since for one who has become dispassionate toward all yogic powers and supernatural attainments, <s>kaivalya</s> is predominantly demonstrated through the withdrawal of everything, the fourth chapter is called the <s>Kaivalyapāda</s> (Chapter on Liberation).
Likewise, since <s>samādhi</s> (absorption) is predominantly explained at the beginning, the first chapter is called the <s>Samādhipāda</s> (Chapter on Absorption).
This is what he states — ['Yoga has been described for one whose mind is concentrated'] — meaning, for one whose mind is fit for work. For the <s>yogin</s> who has attained a stable state through the cultivation of <s>maitrī</s> (friendliness), <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) and the like, the seedless <s>samādhi</s> (absorption) accomplished through the practice of supreme <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion) has been described. ['How can one whose mind is in the ordinary state also be united with yoga?'] How indeed can one whose mind is distracted become fit for <s>samādhi</s>? Therefore this chapter is begun.
The means beginning with <s>tapas</s> (austerity) are enumerated — [<s>Tapas</s> (austerity), <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study), and <s>Īśvara-praṇidhāna</s> (devotion to the Lord) constitute <s>Kriyāyoga</s> (yoga of action).]
But if <s>tapas</s>, <s>svādhyāya</s>, and <s>Īśvara-praṇidhāna</s> will be stated among the <s>niyamas</s> (observances), for what purpose are they mentioned here?
But is not the purpose precisely this — what was stated, namely that one whose mind is in the ordinary state may also be united with yoga?
No, that is not so — this purpose can be accomplished right there where the <s>niyamas</s> are taught.
If it be said that it is for the purpose of attenuating the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) — no, because that too is stated right there. As in ['From the practice of the limbs of yoga, upon the destruction of impurity'] — and impurity refers to <s>kleśas</s> and the like. And the practice of the limbs of yoga for the cultivation of <s>samādhi</s> will be taught as well, as in ['The perfection of <s>samādhi</s> comes from devotion to <s>Īśvara</s>']. Therefore, the enumeration of <s>tapas</s> and the rest here is purposeless.
No — because the purpose is to teach that the practice of the limbs of yoga, which is the means to right knowledge, is preceded by right knowledge itself. All the limbs of yoga, being means to right knowledge, precede right knowledge temporally. And a portion of the <s>niyamas</s> is mentioned here as an illustration that all means precede it temporally. Although the temporal precedence is implicitly established from the very fact of being a means, nevertheless, stating it explicitly makes it clearer.
But even so, it should be taught immediately before right knowledge — it is said: No — because right knowledge itself is the direct counteragent to <s>kleśas</s> and the like,

body.text: sa hi kriyāyogaḥ –
body.translated_text: For that <s>Kriyāyoga</s> (yoga of action) —

body.text: samādhibhāvanārthaḥ kleśatanūkaraṇārthaśca ॥ 2 ॥
body.translated_text: is for the purpose of cultivating <s>samādhi</s> (absorption) and for the purpose of attenuating the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). || 2 ||

body.text: sa hyāsevyamānaḥ samādhiṁ bhāvayati kleśāṁśca pratanū karoti। pratanūkṛtānkleśānprasaṁkhyānāgninā dagdhabījakalpānaprasavadharmiṇaḥ kariṣyatīti। teṣāṁ tanūkaraṇātpunaḥ kleśairaparāmṛṣṭā sattvapuruṣānyatāmātrakhyātiḥ sūkṣmā prajñā samāptādhikārā pratiprasavāya kalpiṣyata iti ॥ 2 ॥
body.translated_text: For when practiced, it cultivates <s>samādhi</s> and attenuates the <s>kleśas</s>. Having attenuated them, it will render the <s>kleśas</s> like seeds burnt by the fire of <s>prasaṁkhyāna</s> (discriminative knowledge), deprived of the capacity to germinate. From their attenuation, the subtle <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) — the mere discernment of the distinction between <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, untouched by the <s>kleśas</s> — having completed its function, will be fit for <s>pratiprasava</s> (involution). || 2 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[sa hi kriyāyogaḥ] kimartha iti tasya pārārthyapratipādanārthamāha- [samādhibhāvanārthaḥ kleśatanūkaraṇārthaśca ॥]
kathaṁ punarubhayāthaitvamityāha- [sa hi āsevyamānaḥ samādhiṁ bhāvayati ।] itarayogāṅgasahitaḥ samādhiṁ bhāvayati [kleśāṁśca tanūkaroti ।] vakṣyati ca ["yogāṅgānuṣṭhānādaśuddhikṣaye jñānadīptirāvivekakhyāte:”] iti । tadetadāha- [tanūkṛtānkleśānprasaṁkhyānena] kleśatanūkaraṇāt sañjātasamyagdarśanaśīlanena, [dagdhabījakalpān] bījānīva dagdhaprasavaśaktīn , ata eva [aprasavadharmiṇaḥ] avidyamānaḥ prasavo yeṣāṁ te aprasavāḥ, aprasavāśca te dharmiṇaścetyaprasavadharmiṇaḥ, (sarvabījādiṣu vā draṣṭavyam) tānaprasavadharmiṇaḥ [kariṣyati] prasavaśaktirahitān kariṣyati ॥
[teṣāṁ tanūkaraṇānujanmā punaḥ kleśairaparāmṛṣṭā satvapuruṣānyatāmātrakhyātiḥ samāsādhikārā prajñā pratiprasavāya [kalpiṣyate]] saṁsārābhimukhatāyai punarna kalpiṣyata ॥
yadyapi śāstrācāryopadeśena yogāṅgānuṣṭhānādṛte'pi satvapuruṣānyatāmātrakhyātirupajāyate, tathā'pi na kleśādharmādīnatīvātiraskṛtya sā jāyeteti punaḥ punaḥ kleśādibhiḥ parāmṛśyata ityetaddarśayati [punaḥ kleśairaparāmṛṣṭe] tyanena ॥ 2 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['For that <s>Kriyāyoga</s>'] — to teach its purpose, i.e. its serving another end, he says — ['is for the purpose of cultivating <s>samādhi</s> and for the purpose of attenuating the <s>kleśas</s>.']
How then does it serve both purposes? To this he says — ['For when practiced, it cultivates <s>samādhi</s>.'] Together with the other limbs of yoga, it cultivates <s>samādhi</s>. ['And attenuates the <s>kleśas</s>.'] And he will state ['From the practice of the limbs of yoga, upon the destruction of impurity'],

body.text: atha ke kleśāḥ kiyanto veti –
body.translated_text: Now, what are the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), and how many are they? —

body.text: avidyāsmitārāgadveṣābhiniveśāḥ kleśāḥ ॥ 3 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>asmitā</s> (egoism), <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), and <s>abhiniveśa</s> (clinging to life) are the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). || 3 ||

body.text: kleśā iti pañca viparyayā ityarthaḥ। te spandamānā guṇādhikāraṁ draḍhayanti, pariṇāmamavasthāpayanti, kāryakāraṇasrota unnamayanti, parasparānugrahatantrī bhūtvā karmavipākaṁ cābhinirharantīti ॥ 3 ॥
body.translated_text: The <s>kleśas</s> — meaning the five <s>viparyayas</s> (errors). When active, they strengthen the dominion of the <s>guṇas</s>, stabilize the process of transformation, cause the stream of cause and effect to swell, and being dependent on mutual support, they bring about the fruition of <s>karma</s> (action). || 3 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[ke te kleśāḥ] svarūpeṇa, [kiyanto vā] saṁkhyayā [iti] saṁkhyāsvarūpapratipādanārthaṁ sūtraṁ praṇīyate- [avidyāsmitārāgadveṣā bhiniveśāḥ kleśāḥ] eṣāmekaikasya lakṣaṇaṁ sūtraireva vyākhyāyiṣyata iti [na] vyākhyeyatve yatnaḥ kriyate, vyākhyeyaṁ vetāvadeva ॥
yathā pramāṇaviparyayavikalpādayaḥ parasparabhinnāḥ, na tathā kleśānā viparyayādvedaḥ । kintarhi? viparyaṁyasyaivaite bhedā iti । kasmātū? viparyayabhāvabhāvitvādityetadāha- [pañca viparyaṁyā ityarthaḥ ॥]
nanu ca yathā vṛttibhedavyākhyāne pramāṇavṛtte: [“ pratyakṣānumānāgamāḥ pramāṇāni”] iti tridhā bhedastatraiva vyākhyātaḥ, tathā kasmāttatraivāsya viparyayasyāpi bhedaḥ pañcadhā nopavyākhyātaḥ ? cittavṛttireva ca viparyaya ityuktam । tathā codāhataṁ, [“sadviṣayeṇaikacandradarśanena dvicandradarśanaṁ bādhyate”] iti ॥
naiṣa doṣaḥ--kleśānāmavṛttitvāt । na hi kleśāḥ pratyayamātrāḥ, pratyayamātrā hi vṛttayaḥ । kleśāstu cittasya malaṁ, yathā cakṣuṣastimiram । kleśamalaviyoge cittasya viparyayapratyayābhāvāt ॥
yadi hi pratyaya eva viparyayaḥ, tadā yathā kleśanirodhe'pi yoginaḥ smṛtipramāṇapratyayo bhavanti, tathā viparyayo'pi bhavet । na tu viparyayaḥ kṣīṇakleśānām । tasmāccākṣuṣa iva ayathārthagrahaṇanimittaṁ pratyayasya malaṁ viparyaya ityucyate ॥
tatpunaḥ pratyayavyatirekeṇa pratipattumākhyātuṁ cāśakyamita pratyayenaivākhyāyate ['viparyayo vṛttiḥ'] iti । tathā ca vṛttayaḥ [kliṣṭākliṣṭaśceti] kleśena viśeṣitāḥ । na ca vṛttibhireva vṛttīnāṁ viśeṣaṇaṁ yuktam । tathā ['kleśahetukā'] iti ca vyākhyātam । na ca vṛttaya eva vṛttihetukā iti yuktam ॥
tasmāccāvṛttitvādvṛtibhedatvena na tatra kleśā vyākhyātāḥ । tathā coktam- [''cittamalaprasaṅgenabhidhāyiṣyante''] iti kleśānāṁ na vṛttitvaṁ, malatvamevetyabhiprāyeṇa । abhedopacāreṇa tu pratyayena sāmānādhikaraṇyaṁ, yathā dhūmo malairagniṁ garbhādaśāntavṛttāstathā jñānameteneti, (?) tathaivātrāpi ॥
pratyayaviparītatvamāha- [te spandamānā] ityādinā । spandamānāḥ pratyayadvāreṇodbhāsamānāḥ, na hi svatasteṣāñcalanamasti, vastrādirāgavat । [guṇādhikāraṁ dṛḍhayanti] guṇānāmadhikāraṁ pravṛttiṁ (saṁ)kartavyatvaṁ sthirīkurvānti । na hi teṣu parispandamāneṣu kartavyatāśūnyaṁ cittaṁ bhavati ॥
[parīṇāmamavasthāpayānti] punaḥ punaḥ pariṇamayantīti yāvat । [kāryakaraṇasrota unnamayanti] śarīrasya karaṇādīnāṁ cakṣurādīnāṁ pravṛttisrota ucchrā(va)yayanti । kathamityāha- [parasparānugrahatantrībhūtvā] avidyādaya itaretaranimittanaimittikabhāveneti ॥
kiñca – [karmavipākāṁścābhinirvartayanti ।] karma trividhaṁ, tadvipākāṁśca jātyāyurbhogāniti ॥ 3 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['What are those <s>kleśas</s>'] — in their essential nature; ['and how many'] — in number. ['Thus'] — the <s>sūtra</s> is composed for the purpose of teaching their number and essential nature — [<s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>asmitā</s> (egoism), <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), and <s>abhiniveśa</s> (clinging to life) are the <s>kleśas</s>]. Since the definition of each of these will be explained by the <s>sūtras</s> themselves, [no] effort is made to explain them here; only this much needs to be explained.
Just as <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition), <s>viparyaya</s> (error), <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction) and the rest

body.text: avidyā kṣetramuttareṣāṁ prasuptatanuvicchinnodārāṇām ॥ 4 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance) is the field for the others, whether dormant, attenuated, interrupted, or fully active. || 4 ||

body.text: atrāvidyā kṣetraṁ prasavabhūmiruttareṣāmasmitādīnāṁ caturvidhavikalpānāṁ prasuptatanuvicchinnodārāṇām। tatra kā prasuptiḥ। cetasi śaktimātrapratiṣṭhānāṁ bījabhāvopagamaḥ। tasya prabodha ālambane saṁmukhībhāvaḥ। prasaṁkhyānavato dagdhakleśabījasya saṁmukhībhūte'pyālambane nāsau punarasti, dagdhabījasya kutaḥ praroha iti। ataḥ kṣīṇakleśaḥ kuśalaścaramadeha ityucyate। tatraiva sā dagdhabījabhāvā pañcamī kleśāvasthā nānyatreti। satāṁ kleśānāṁ tadā bījasāmarthyaṁ dagdhamiti viṣayasya saṁmukhībhāve'pi sati na bhavatyeṣāṁ prabodha ityuktā prasuptirdagdhabījānāmaprarohaśca।
body.translated_text: Here, <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is the field, the breeding ground, of the subsequent [afflictions]—<s>asmitā</s> (egoism) and the rest—in their four varieties: dormant (<s>prasupta</s>), attenuated (<s>tanu</s>), interrupted (<s>vicchinna</s>), and active (<s>udāra</s>). What is the dormant state? It is the assumption of the seed-condition by those [afflictions] that are established in the mind as mere potency (<s>śakti</s>). Their awakening is the coming face-to-face with a [supporting] object. For one who possesses <s>prasaṃkhyāna</s> (discriminative discernment), whose <s>kleśa</s>-seeds are burnt—even when the object comes face-to-face, that [affliction] no longer exists. How can there be sprouting from a burnt seed? Therefore he is called 'one whose <s>kleśas</s> are destroyed, skillful, [wearing] his last body.' That fifth state of the <s>kleśas</s>—the burnt-seed state—exists only there [in such a person], not elsewhere. The seed-potency of the existing <s>kleśas</s> is then burnt, so even when the object comes face-to-face, their awakening does not occur. Thus the dormant state and the non-sprouting of burnt seeds have been described.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[avidyā kṣetramuttareṣāṁ prasuptatanuvicchinnodārāṇām ।] kathamasmitādayo viparyayā iti, tatpradarśyate sūtreṇaiva । [avidyā kṣetraṁ prasavabhūmiḥ] ātmalābhakṣetraṁ yathā pṛthivī tṛṇalatāgulmavīrudhāṁ svātmano'natiriktānāṁ, evamavidyāto viparyayādavyatiriktānāṁ [asmitādīnāṁ] caturṇamekaikaśaḥ [prasuptatanuvicchinnodāratayā caturvikalpānāṁ prasavabhūmiravidyā ॥]
viparyayapratyayā hi tāmāśrityātmānaṁ pratilabhante । tasmādavidyaivāsmitādicatuṣṭayarūpeṇa vipariṇamate ॥
[tatra kā prasuptiriti ।] asmitādīnāṁ prasutirnāma dharme ucyate, nāvidyāyāḥ । kāraṇatvāt । sarvāsmitādivikalpeṣvanugamātsarvadā prabuddhaiva sā, na prasuptā । prasvapane vyavahārābhāvāt । asmitādīnāmanyatamasya prasuptāvanyatamasyāvasthānamavaśyameva । anyathā kleśāntarasyodbhava eva na syāt । tasmādasmitādīnāmeva caturṇāṁ prasuptādicaturvikalpatvam ॥
[cetasi śaktimātrapratiṣṭhānami] tyasya vyākhyānaṁ karoti- [bījabhāvopagama] iti । yathā bījaṁ sadevānaṅkurībhavadapi bhūmigataṁ tiṣṭhati, tathā cetasyasmitādayaḥ śaktirūpeṇānabhivyaktasvarūpāṅkurā vyavatiṣṭhante ॥
[tasya prabodha] iti- [tasya] kleśasyāsmitādeḥ [prabodha] udbhavaḥ ālambane viṣaye [sammukhībhāvaḥ] svavyañjakāñjanasya ॥
tatraitat syāt, sarvadaiva kleśasya bījabhāvopagamaḥ prabodhaśca niyamena syāditi । tata āha- [prasaṁkhyānavataḥ] samyagdarśanābhyāsavataḥ [adagdhakleśabījasya] yoginaḥ [saṁmukhībhūte'pyālambane nāsau] bījabhāvopagamaḥ । [dagdhasya] dagdhatvādeva [kutaḥ punaḥ prabodhaḥ] udbhavaḥ । vidyamānasya hi bījasya kṣitijalādisaṁyoganimittaprāptāvaṅkurībhāvo na dagdhabījaśakteḥ, tathā kleśasyāpi ॥
yadyevam , eṣā pañcamī kasmādavasthā noktā dagdhaprasuptatanuvicchinno dārāṇāmiti-na-asādhāraṇatvāt । na hi sarvadehināṁ sādhāraṇī pañcamī kleśāvasthā । yogina eva hi sā, tato nāmnāyate ॥
kathaṁ vā asādhāraṇīti? tata āha- [tatraiva sā] samyagdarśanābhyāsavatyeva [dagdhā nānyatra । kṣīṇakleśaḥ kuśalaścaramadeha] iti samyagdarśana ucyate yogī । [tatraiva sā dagdhabījabhāvā pañcamī kleśāvasthā । satāṁ kleśānāṁ tadānīṁ dagdhaṁ bījasāmarthyam ।] yathā vidyamānānāṁ yavādibījānāṁ bharjitānāṁ bījasāmarthyaṁ dagdham । [viṣayasya sammukhībhāve'pi na bhavatyeṣāṁ prabodhaḥ,] samyagdarśinaḥ saṁskāraśeṣāvasthatvādiṣoriva lakṣyavimuktasya ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇa</s> (Elucidation):
["<s>Avidyā</s> is the field of the subsequent [afflictions] in their dormant, attenuated, interrupted, and active [states]."]. How are <s>asmitā</s> and the rest forms of <s>viparyaya</s> (error)? This is shown by the <s>sūtra</s> itself. ["<s>Avidyā</s> is the field, the breeding ground"]—the field for obtaining their existence. Just as the earth is [the field] for grasses, creepers, shrubs, and herbs that are not distinct from its own nature, so <s>avidyā</s>, as <s>viparyaya</s>, is the breeding ground of the four [afflictions] beginning with <s>asmitā</s>, which are not distinct from it, each having four varieties as ["dormant, attenuated, interrupted, and active."].
For the cognitions of <s>viparyaya</s>, depending on it [<s>avidyā</s>], obtain their existence. Therefore, <s>avidyā</s> itself transforms into the fourfold form of <s>asmitā</s> and the rest.
["What is the dormant state?"] Dormancy is predicated of <s>asmitā</s> and the rest, not of <s>avidyā</s>—because [<s>avidyā</s>] is the cause. Since it accompanies all varieties of <s>asmitā</s> and the rest, it is always awake, never dormant—because in sleep there would be no [functional] activity. When one of the [afflictions] <s>asmitā</s> and the rest is dormant, another necessarily persists; otherwise, the arising of another <s>kleśa</s> would be impossible. Therefore, only the four [afflictions] beginning with <s>asmitā</s> have the fourfold variety of dormant and so forth.
["Established in the mind as mere potency"]—he explains this: ["the assumption of the seed-condition."]. Just as a seed, even while not sprouting, remains in the ground, so too <s>asmitā</s> and the rest persist in the mind in the form of potency, their essential sprouts unmanifested.
["Their awakening"]—the awakening, that is, the arising of the <s>kleśa</s> beginning with <s>asmitā</s>, [means] the coming face-to-face of the object with its own manifesting agent.
Here one might think that the seed-condition and the awakening of the <s>kleśa</s> would invariably always occur. Therefore he says: ["For one who possesses <s>prasaṃkhyāna</s>"]—one who practices right vision—[for that] <s>yogin</s> ["whose <s>kleśa</s>-seeds are burnt, even when the object comes face-to-face,"] there is no [longer] the seed-condition. ["How can there be"] arising ["from a burnt"] seed? For a seed that exists, when it encounters conditions such as earth and water, sprouts—but not one whose potency is burnt. So too with the <s>kleśa</s>.
If this is so, why is this not mentioned as a fifth state—'burnt, dormant, attenuated, interrupted, and active'? No—because it is not common [to all beings]. For the fifth state of the <s>kleśas</s> does not belong to all embodied beings. It belongs only to the <s>yogin</s>, and therefore it is [merely] mentioned [rather than enumerated].
How is it uncommon? Therefore he says: ["Only there"]—only in one who practices right vision—["is it burnt, not elsewhere."] ["One whose <s>kleśas</s> are destroyed, skillful, [wearing] his last body"]—is called a <s>yogin</s> of right vision. ["Only there is that fifth state of the <s>kleśas</s>, the burnt-seed condition. The seed-potency of the existing <s>kleśas</s> is then burnt."]. Just as the seed-potency of parched barley-seeds and the like is burnt, ["even when the object comes face-to-face, their awakening does not occur"]—like an arrow released [from the target], for one who is in the state of remaining impressions, who has right vision.

body.text: tanutvamucyate – pratipakṣabhāvanopahatāḥ kleśāstanavo bhavanti। tathā vicchidya vicchidya tena tenā''tmanā punaḥ punaḥ samudācarantīti vicchinnāḥ। kathaṁ, rāgakāle krodhasyādarśanāt। na hi rāgakāle krodhaḥ samudācarati। rāgaśca kvacidṛśyamāno na viṣayāntare nāsti। naikasyāṁ striyāṁ caitro rakta ityanyāsu strīṣu viraktaḥ kiṁtu tatra rāgo labdhavṛttiranyatra tu bhaviṣyadvṛttiriti। sa hi tadā prasuptatanuvicchinno bhavati।
body.translated_text: Attenuation (<s>tanutva</s>) is described: <s>kleśas</s> that have been weakened by the cultivation of their antidote become attenuated (<s>tanu</s>). And being interrupted again and again, they recur again and again in one form or another—these are the interrupted (<s>vicchinna</s>) [afflictions]. How? Because anger is not seen at the time of passion. For anger does not arise at the time of passion. And passion, though seen toward one object, is not absent toward other objects. It is not that because <s>Caitra</s> is enamored of one woman, he is dispassionate toward other women; rather, his passion has found active expression toward one, while toward others it is of future expression. Thus [the affliction] is then dormant, attenuated, or interrupted.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
uktā prasuptiḥ । kiñca dagdhabījānāṁ ca kleśānāmaprabodho yogina ukta iti । [tanutvaṁ] idānīṁ [ucyate] - [pratipakṣabhāvanopahatāḥ] pratipakṣasya śarīrādyavadyadarśanādeḥ [bhāvanayopahatāḥ] abalīkṛtā mandaprabhāvāḥ [kleśāstanava] ucyante ॥
[tathā vicchidya] vicchidyārthāntaropajanakālāntarāleṣu svātmānamapradarśayantaḥ [tena tenātmanā] yena rūpeṇa pūrvamupalabdhāstenaivātmanā [samudācaranti] punarudbhavantīti [vicchinnāḥ ॥]
yadi vā [vicchidya vicchidya] vicchedakāle [te vyaktenātmanā] svarūpeṇa pūrvottarakālavat [na samudācaranti ॥]
tatrodāharaṇamū- [kathaṁ ? rāgakāle krodhasyādarśanāt । na hi rāgakāle krodhaḥ samudācarati ।] kuta: rūpātiśayānāṁ vṛtyatiśayānāṁ ca virodhāt । sa hi rāgodayāttirobhūto'nyenāvyaktenātmanā vartata iti vicchinnaḥ ॥
tathā [rāgaśca kvaciddṛśyamāno na viṣayāntare nāsti ।] kutaḥ? viṣayavirodhādatra । pūrvatra rāgeṇa virodhādasamudācaraṇaṁ krodhasya । atra tu viṣayāṇāmanyonyavirodhāt । na hi viṣaya ekasminnupajanayati rāgaṁ viṣayāntaramapi tasyaiva rāgasyotpādakam ॥
tadyathā- [naikasyāṁ striyāṁ caitro rakta ityanyāsu viraktaḥ । kintu tatra rāgo labdhavṛttiḥ] yasyāṁ raktaḥ । [anyatra bhaviṣyadvṛttiḥ] anyāsu strīṣu sa hi bhaviṣyadrāgavyaktiviśeṣaḥ [tadā prasuptastanurveti ॥]
nanu ca ‘ [rāgaśca kacit dṛśyamāna’] ityādi bhāṣyaṁ kimarthaṁ? nanu rāgasvabhāvākhyānaṁ, itthaṁ viṣayabhedāllabdhabhaviṣyadvṛttisvabhāvo rāga iti-satyam tathā'pi prakrāntānupayogaḥ । prakrānta hi vicchedavyākhyānaṁ । na caitadvicchedavyākhyānam । nāpi vakṣyamāṇodāravyākhyānena sambandhaḥ । tasya nirākāṅkatvāt ॥
evaṁ tarhi pūrvaśeṣa evāyam । katham ? evaṁ manyate, prasuptatanūdāratvavyatirekeṇa vicchittirnāma dharma eva nāsti । katham ? yāvanna labdhavṛttistāvatprasupta ityuktam । pratipakṣabhāvanopahato mandapravṛttistanurityucyate ॥
yaścāpi labdhavṛttiḥ sa udāra ityākhyāyate । vicchinno nāma sa bhavati, yaḥ kvacidupalabdhaḥ punarupalabhyate । yathā sarasvatīsrotaḥ । na hi rāgodaye krodhaḥ kvacidapi dṛśyate । tasmānna vicchittirnāma dharmo'sti । adarśanāt ॥
atrocyate-yadyadarśanādvicchedo nāsti, tadā rāgasya kvaciddṛśyamānasyānyatrādarśanādabhāvo'stu । nanvastvevābhāvaḥ, anyatrādarśanāt । na hi । kasmāt ? kvacit dṛśyamānasvādeva । na hi viṣayāntarābhimukho na bhavatīti dharmiṇyapi cetasi nāsti । na hi cakṣuḥ kadācidgajābhimukhaṁ na bhavatīti ghaṭābhimukhapravṛttaṁ sannāsti । ghaṭābhimukhadarśanādeva । tadetadāha- [kacit dṛśyamāno na viṣayāntare nāstī] tyādi ॥
tathā krodho'pi rāgeṇodbhūtenābhibhūtatvādvicchinnadarśano bhaviṣyati, sarasvatīsrotovadeva । sa hi rāgo viṣayāntare prasuptaḥ tanurvā । tadābhimukhyenādṛśyamānaviśeṣatvāt ॥
kaḥ punaḥ prasuptivicchedayorviśeṣaḥ ? yāvatobhayatrādarśanamaviśiṣṭam । ucyate-pravṛttadarśanaprabandhasyāntarāvirodhinā'nubaddhatvādadarśanaṁ vicchittiradagdhasya ॥
prasuptiḥ punarnimitteṣu satsvapyadagdhabījasyaivāsatyapi virodhinā'bhibhave nyagbhūtatayā bījarūpeṇāvasthānam ॥
nanu caivaṁ sati “sa(na)hi tadā prasuptastanurve”ti viruddhaṁ, pravṛtteradarśanaprabandho hi viṣayāntareṇa dṛśyate-na-viṣayāntarābhimukhyasya vivakṣitatvāt । viṣayāntarābhimukhyaṁ nāma yo rāgasya dharmaḥ sa hi tadā prasuptaḥ tanurvā । na rāgaḥ sarvedā āmanaiva prasuptastanurvā । kvacit dṛśyamānatvādeva । krodhaḥ prasuptastanurvā ātmanaiva rāgakāle sarvaviṣayeṣu na dṛśyate ॥
athavā vichinnodāharaṇāntarapratipādanārthameva ['rāgaśca kvaci'] dityādi bhāṣyam । kathaṁ ? dviprakāro vicchedaḥ pradarśayiṣya(ti)te । ekastāvatpravṛttadarśanaprabandhasya virodhinā'bhibhavātsarvatrādarśanam । yathā darśitaṁ [‘rāgakāle krodhasyādarśanā'diti ॥]
tathā'yamanyo viṣayaviśeṣe dṛśyamānasyaiva viṣayāntare prātinimittasyādarśanam । yathā caitrasya ekasyāṁ striyāṁ raktasya anyāsu satīṣvapi rāgasyādarśanaṁ [tatra labdhavṛtti] riti kvacidviṣaye dṛśyamānasyaiva yatra [bhaviṣyadvṛtti] viṣaye yadadarśanaṁ, sa cāpi viccheda iti ॥
kasmātpunaranyatra na dṛśyata ityāha- [sa hi tadā prasuptastanurvā ।] na hi prasuptistānavaṁ vā vivakṣyate । yathā tathā vā bhavatu । tatrādarśanaṁ vicchedatvena vivakṣitam ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇa</s> (Elucidation):
Dormancy has been described. And it has been stated that for the <s>yogin</s>, the <s>kleśas</s> with burnt seeds do not awaken. ["Attenuation"] is now ["described"]: ["Weakened by the cultivation of the antidote"]—that is, the antidote being the vision of the body's defects and the like—["weakened by its cultivation"], meaning enfeebled, of diminished power—["the <s>kleśas</s> are called attenuated (<s>tanu</s>)."]
["And being interrupted"]—not manifesting themselves in the intervening periods when other [states] arise—["in that very form"] in which they were previously perceived, ["they recur"]—arise again—["these are the interrupted (<s>vicchinna</s>)."]
Or alternatively, ["being interrupted"]—at the time of interruption, ["they do not recur in their manifest form"] as they do in the previous and subsequent periods.
The example for this: ["How? Because anger is not seen at the time of passion. For anger does not arise at the time of passion."]. Why? Because of the opposition between the superior aspects of their forms and activities. For anger, having disappeared at the arising of passion, persists in another, unmanifest form—thus it is interrupted.
Likewise, ["passion, though seen toward one object, is not absent toward other objects."]. Why? Because of the opposition of objects in this case. In the former case, it was the non-arising of anger due to opposition with passion. But here, it is due to the mutual opposition of objects. For the object that arouses passion toward one [thing] does not arouse passion toward another.
For example: ["It is not that because <s>Caitra</s> is enamored of one woman, he is dispassionate toward other women. Rather, his passion has found active expression"] toward the one he desires. ["Toward others it is of future expression"]—that is, the specific manifestation of future passion toward other women. ["Thus it is then dormant or attenuated."]
Now, what is the purpose of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> passage ['passion, though seen toward one object...']? Is it an explanation of the nature of passion—that passion has the nature of being of active and future expression depending on differences of objects? True, but even so, it is not relevant to the topic at hand. For what is being explained is interruption. And this is not an explanation of interruption, nor is it connected to the forthcoming explanation of the active state, since that is self-sufficient.
Then this is a continuation of the previous [discussion]. How? One thinks thus: apart from the dormant, attenuated, and active states, there is no property called 'interruption' at all. How? As long as [the <s>kleśa</s>] has not found expression, it is called 'dormant.' When weakened by the cultivation of the antidote, its expression being feeble, it is called 'attenuated.'
And when it has found active expression, it is called 'active.' The 'interrupted' is one that, having been perceived somewhere, is perceived again—like the stream of the <s>Sarasvatī</s>. But anger is nowhere seen at the time of passion. Therefore there is no property called 'interruption'—because of non-observation.
To this we reply: if interruption does not exist because of non-observation, then let passion too, though seen toward one object, be non-existent elsewhere because of non-observation. Well, let it indeed be non-existent, because of non-observation elsewhere. No, it cannot be. Why? Because of being seen somewhere. For just because it is not directed toward another object does not mean it does not exist in the mind as substrate. Just as the eye, because it is sometimes not directed toward an elephant, does not thereby cease to exist when engaged in seeing a pot—it exists, as evidenced by its seeing the pot. Thus he says: ["Passion, though seen toward one object, is not absent toward other objects,"] and so forth.
Similarly, anger too, being overpowered by the arising of passion, will have its perception interrupted—just like the stream of the <s>Sarasvatī</s>. For that passion is dormant or attenuated toward other objects—because the specific [manifestation] is not seen when directed toward that [particular object].
But what is the distinction between dormancy and interruption? For in both cases, the non-observation is the same. Reply: interruption is the non-observation of an unburnt [affliction] that occurs in the midst of an ongoing stream of manifest perception, being obstructed by something that is not ultimately opposed.
Dormancy, on the other hand, is the subsistence in seed-form, in a subordinate state, of an unburnt-seed [affliction] even when conditions are present and even without being overpowered by an opposing [state].
Objection: If so, then the statement 'thus it is then dormant or attenuated' is contradictory, for the interruption of the stream of manifest expression is seen with reference to another object. Reply: No—because what is intended is the directedness toward another object. 'Directedness toward another object' is a property of passion—that is then dormant or attenuated. Passion is not itself always dormant or attenuated—precisely because it is seen somewhere. Anger is dormant or attenuated by its own nature at the time of passion, since it is not seen in any object.
Alternatively, the <s>Bhāṣya</s> passage ['passion, though seen toward one object...'] is for the purpose of presenting another example of interruption. How? Two kinds of interruption are to be shown. The first is the non-observation everywhere due to overpowering by an opponent when the stream of manifest expression is ongoing—as was shown: ['Because anger is not seen at the time of passion.'] The second is the non-observation toward another object of something that is actually seen toward a specific object. Just as when <s>Caitra</s> is enamored of one woman, his passion is not seen toward other women even though they exist—['there having found expression'] in one object, the non-observation toward the object where ['it is of future expression']—that too is interruption.
Why then is it not seen elsewhere? He says: ["Thus it is then dormant or attenuated."]. For it is not dormancy or attenuation that is intended to be expressed. Let it be however it may—the non-observation there is what is intended as interruption.

body.text: viṣaye yo labdhavṛttiḥ sa udāraḥ। sarva evaite kleśaviṣayatvaṁ nātikrāmanti। kastarhi vicchinnaḥ prasuptastanurudāro vā kleśa iti, ucyate – satyamevaitat, kiṁtu viśiṣṭānāmevaiteṣāṁ vicchinnāditvam। yathaiva pratipakṣabhāvanāto nivṛttastathaiva svavyañjakāñjanenābhivyakta iti। sarva evāmī kleśā avidyābhedāḥ। kasmāt, sarveṣvavidyaivābhiplavate। yadavidyayā vastvākāryate tadevānuśerate kleśā viparyāsapratyayakāla upalabhyante kṣīyamāṇāṁ cāvidyāmanu kṣīyanta iti ॥ 4 ॥
body.translated_text: That which has found active expression toward [its] object is 'active' (<s>udāra</s>). All of these do not transcend the condition of being objects of the <s>kleśas</s>. Then who is the <s>kleśa</s> that is interrupted, dormant, attenuated, or active? It is replied: this is certainly so, but the conditions of being interrupted and so forth belong only to these specific [afflictions]. Just as a [<s>kleśa</s>] ceases through the cultivation of its antidote, so it is manifested through its own manifesting agent. All these <s>kleśas</s> are divisions of <s>avidyā</s>. Why? Because <s>avidyā</s> pervades them all. That which is obscured by <s>avidyā</s>—that very thing the <s>kleśas</s> follow, being perceived at the time of erroneous cognition; and when <s>avidyā</s> diminishes, they diminish accordingly. // 4 //

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[viṣaye yo labdhavṛttiḥ sa udāraḥ ।] nanu ca prasuptatanuvicchinnānāṁ kāryāsamarthānāṁ na kleśatā । na hi prasuptastanuvicchinne vā prasuptivicchittitanniyamāvasthāyāṁ kāryaṁ kartuṁ kṣamate । na hyajātaśśatrurupaghātāyālam । vicchinne vā pradeśe srotasi snātuṁ śakyam । tasmādavidyā kṣetramuttareṣāmityetāvadevāstu । kintairakāryakṣamaiḥ prasuptatanuvicchinairupadiṣṭai: । etadāśaṁkyāha- [sarve caite kleśaviṣayatvannātikrāmantīti ।] na hi śatruḥ prasupto janiṣyamāṇo vā nāpakariṣyati ॥
[kastarhi vicchinnaḥ prasutastanurudāro vā kleśaḥ ।] na yuktamevaṁ bhedena vacanam । ekamevodāharaṇamastu । na codārāvasthāyā anyatra kāryaṁ kariṣyati ॥
[satyamevametat ।] tathā'pi parihāra ucyate, [kiṁ tu viśiṣṭānāmevaiteṣāṁ] aparityaktakleśatvadharmakāṇamiva [vicchinnāditvam ।] vicchinnādyavasthāyāmapi nāpāgamadapakartṛtvaśaktirityadoṣaḥ ॥
tatkāle kāryākṣamatvamiti cet-na-pratipakṣavidhānārthavādvacanasya । na hi śatroradṛśyamānasya prasuptasya janiṣyamāṇasya vā na pratividhātavyam ॥
śrūyate cendraḥ pratipakṣabhayena saptadhā ditergarbhamabhinaditi । tatra kāraṇaṁ svayameva prakaṭayati- [yathaiva pratipakṣabhāvanāto nivṛttastathaiva svavyañjakāñjanena] viṣayādinā [abhivyakta iti ॥]
yasmātte punarabhivyaktāḥ punaśca tirohitāḥ punarapyabhivyañjiṣyante ca, tasmātprasuptādyavasthā api pratipakṣavidhānāya vaktavyā eva, hreśatvānatikrāntatvāt ॥
idānīmupasaṁharati- [sarva evāmī kleśā avidyābhedāḥ । kasmāt?] yasmāt [sarveṣu] asmitādiṣu [avidyaivābhiplavate] pratarati, udbhūtā dṛśyate ॥
kiñca- [yadavidyayā vastvākāryate] prakalpyate [tadanuśerate] tadviṣayā upajāyante [kleśāḥ] rāgādayaḥ । yathā stryādipiṇḍe heye'pi bhogyo'yamityavidyayā parikalpyātmābhimānaṁ kṛtvā rajyate । dharmajñāne viparītaṁ parikalpya dveṣṭi ॥
kathaṁ punastadevānuśerate iti-yasmāt [viparyāsapratyayakāla evopalabhyante ।] itaścāvidyābhedā:, yasmā [tkṣīyamāṇāmavidyāmanu kṣīyanta iti ।] avidyāpraṇāśānupraṇāśino hi kleśā । asmitādayaḥ । na hyasatyāmavidyāyāṁ kaścidapi kleśaḥ sambhavati ॥ 4 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['One who has obtained activity in its object is the fully active (<s>udāra</s>).'] But surely the dormant, attenuated, and interrupted states, being incapable of producing effects, do not constitute affliction-hood. For one who is dormant, attenuated, or interrupted — in the state determined by dormancy, interruption, and the like — is not capable of producing an effect. For an unborn enemy is not capable of causing harm. Nor can one bathe in a stream that is interrupted at a certain place. Therefore, let it simply be that '<s>avidyā</s> is the field for the others' — what is the point of mentioning the dormant, attenuated, and interrupted states, which are incapable of producing effects? Anticipating this objection, he says —

body.text: tatrāvidyāsvarūpamucyate –
body.translated_text: Now the essential nature of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is stated —

body.text: anityāśuciduḥkhānātmasu nityaśucisukhātmakhyātiravidyā ॥ 5 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance) is the cognition of the eternal, pure, pleasurable, and self in what is non-eternal, impure, painful, and non-self. || 5 ||

body.text: anitye kārye nityakhyātiḥ। tadyathā - dhruvā pṛthivī, dhruvā sacandratārakā dyauḥ, amṛtā divaukasa iti। tathā'śucau paramabībhatse kāye – sthānādbījādupaṣṭambhānniḥsyandānnidhanādapi। kāyamādheyaśaucatvātpaṇḍitā hyaśuciṁ viduḥ ॥ iti aśucau śucikhyātirdṛśyate। naveva śaśāṅkalekhā kamanīyeyaṁ kanyā madhvamṛtāvayavanirmitevacandraṁ bhittvā niḥsṛteva jñāyate, nīlotpalapatrāyatākṣī hāvagarbhābhyāṁ locanābhyāṁ jīvalokamāśvāsayantīveti kasya kenābhisaṁbandhaḥ। bhavati caivamaśucau śuciviparyāsapratyaya iti। etenāpuṇye puṇyapratyayastathaivānarthe cārthapratyayo vyākhyātaḥ।
body.translated_text: The cognition of permanence in the impermanent effect — for example: 'The earth is eternal,' 'The sky with its moon and stars is eternal,' 'The celestials are immortal.' Likewise, the cognition of purity in the supremely revolting body — 'By reason of its location, its origin, its sustenance, its excretions, and its death, the learned know the body to be impure, since it is of adventitious cleanliness' — such a cognition of purity in what is impure is seen. 'This maiden is as lovely as the new crescent moon, as if fashioned from honey and nectar, as if she emerged from the moon itself, with eyes long like blue lotus petals, with glances pregnant with coquetry,'

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tatrāvidyāsvarūpamucyate ।] kiṁ punaravidyāsvarūpākhyāne prayojanaṁ ? tatsvayameva bhāṣyakṛdākhyāsyate ['avidyā mūlamasya kleśasantānasya'] ityādinā । ajñāte ca kleśasantānamūlasvarūpe tanmūlonmūlanaṁ na śakyaṁ kartumiti tatsvarūpamākhyāyate ॥
[anityāśuciduḥkhānātmasu nityaśucisukhātmakhyātiravidyā ।] katham? [anitye kārye nityakhyātiḥ] nityamiti viparyayabuddhiḥ [yathā dhruvā pṛthivī, dhuvā sacandratārakā dyau:, amṛtā divaॅ.aukasa iti ॥]
nanu caitasmānmantrātpṛthivyādīnāṁ dhruvatvaṁ pratīyate । tatra kathameṣāṁ kāryatvamucyate ? āpekṣikatvādadoṣaḥ । manuṣyādyapekṣayā pṛthivyādayo dhruvāḥ । kāryatvamanityatvaṁ ca sarvapramāṇasiddhaṁ śrutiṣu vacanāt [‘dyaurāsīnna pṛthivī nāntarikṣa'] mityādiṣu siddham ॥
[tathā aśucau paramabībhatse] paramodvegakare'tyantaghṛṇāspade kārātmasadmanīvāśucau kāye । kathama(pi)sya bībhatsakatvamityāha- [sthānādaśuciḥ] garbhāśayasthānatvādaśuciḥ । [bījādaśuciḥ] -śuklaśoṇitabījo hi kāyaḥ । [upaṣṭambhāt] -vātapittaśleṣmopaṣṭambhāt । teṣāṁ cāśucitvaṁ prasiddham । [niṣyandāt] -prasvedamūtrapurīṣādimalājasraniṣyandāt । [nidhanādapi] -- maraṇāt । mṛtasaṁbandhināṁ daśāhādyāśaucasmaraṇam ॥
nanu ca svabhāvato yadyaśuciḥ kāyastasya śaucavidhānamanarthakaṁ prāpnotītyata āha- [kāyamādheyaśaucatvāditi ।] śāsrata ādhātavyameva śai.aucamasminna svato'stīti yāvat ॥
yadvā, karaṇani buddhisatvādīni satvātmakatayā śucīnyādheyānyasminniti, tacchrucitvādasyāpi śaucam । buddhisatvādyādheyaviprayoge cātyantāśucitvadarśanāt ॥
[tasmātpaṇḍitā hyaśuciṁ viduḥ ।] paṇḍitagrahaṇaṁ viparyastadhiyāṁ śucitvagrahaṇakhyāpanārtham ॥ [aśucau śucikhyātirdṛśyate] viparītacetasām ॥
na [veva śaśāṅkalekhā kamanīyeyaṁ kanyā amṛtāvayavanirmiteva candra bhitveva nissṛtā jñāyate nīlotpalapatrākṣī bhāvagarbhābhyāṁ locanābhyāṁ jīvalokaṁ samāśvāsayantīti kasya kenābhisaṁbandho bhavatīti ।] kva śarīrādiyāthātmyaṁ, kva [bhavatyevamaśucau] (kvacidvi)śuciviparyāsa iti ॥
[etenāpuṇye puṇyapratyayaḥ,] yathā saṁsāramocakānāṁ, [tathaivānarthe cārthapratyayo vyākhyātaḥ,] yathā taskarāṇām ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['Now the essential nature of <s>avidyā</s> is stated.'] What then is the purpose of explaining the essential nature of <s>avidyā</s>? The author of the <s>bhāṣya</s> himself will explain it with the passage beginning '<s>avidyā</s> is the root of this stream of <s>kleśas</s>' and so forth. And since the uprooting of that root is not possible without knowing the essential nature of the root of the stream of <s>kleśas</s>, its essential nature is explained.
['The cognition of the eternal, pure, pleasurable, and self in what is non-eternal, impure, painful, and non-self is <s>avidyā</s>.'] How? ['The cognition of permanence in the impermanent effect'] — the erroneous cognition 'permanent' — ['for example, the earth is eternal,']

body.text: tathā duḥkhe sukhakhyātiṁ vakṣyati - pariṇāmatāpasaṁskāraduḥkhairguṇavṛttivirodhācca duḥkhameva sarvaṁ vivekinaḥ iti। tatrasukhakhyātiravidyā। tathā'nātmanyātmakhyātirbāhyopakaraṇeṣu cetanācetaneṣu bhogādhiṣṭhāne vā śarīre puruṣopakaraṇe vā manasyanātmanyātmakhyātiriti। tathaitadatroktam - vyaktamavyaktaṁ vā sattvamātmatvenābhipratītya tasya saṁpadamanu nandatyātmasaṁpadaṁ manvānastasya vyāpadamanu śocatyātmavyāpadaṁ manvānaḥ sa sarvo'pratibuddhaḥ iti। eṣā catuṣpadā bhavatyavidyā mūlamasya kleśasaṁtānasya karmāśayasya ca savipākasyeti।
body.translated_text: Likewise, he will state the cognition of pleasure in what is painful — 'Due to the pains of transformation, burning, and <s>saṁskāra</s> (latent impressions), and due to the conflict of the activities of the <s>guṇas</s>, everything is indeed painful for the discerning one.' Therein, the cognition of pleasure is <s>avidyā</s>. Likewise, the cognition of self in what is non-self — in external instruments, whether sentient or insentient, or in the body which is the seat of experience, or in the mind which is the instrument of <s>Puruṣa</s> — the cognition of self in what is non-self. And thus it is stated here: 'Having identified <s>sattva</s>, whether manifest or unmanifest, as the self, one rejoices in its prosperity thinking it is the prosperity of the self, and grieves at its adversity',

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tathā duḥkhe sukhakhyātiṁ] vakṣyati । ['pariṇāma tāpasaṁskāraduḥkhairguṇavṛttivirodhācca duḥkhameva sarvaṁ vivekinaḥ'] iti । [tatra] sarvasmin saṁsāre duḥkhe [sukhakhyātiravidyā ॥]
[tathā anātmanyātmakhyātibodhyopakaraṇeṣu cetanācetaneṣu] gavādighaṭādiṣu [bhogādhiṣṭhāne vā śarīre puruṣopakaraṇe vā manasyanātmanyātmakhyātireti ॥]
atrocyate-kasya punarmanasyanātmanyātmakhyātiriti ? nanu manasa eva khyātiḥ, kiṁ codyate-yāvatā avidyā viparyayaścittavṛttiriti hyuktam । cittameva prāptacaitanyopagrahaṇarūpatvādātmānaṁ cetanamabhimanyate ‘ahaṁ draṣṭṛ śrotṛ vā ahamidaṁ mame'ti cāviśeṣeṇa ।
[tathaitadatra] etasminnarthe [uktaṁ vyaktamavyaktaṁ vā] pradhānādikaṁ śarīrendriyādi viṣayaviśeṣaparyantaṁ kiṁcit [vyaktaṁ] ānubhavikaṁ, kiṁcidānumānikamāgamikaṁ [avyaktaṁ vā satvamātmatvenābhipratītaḥ] pratipannaḥ [tasya sampadamanu nandati] tasya vyaktāvyattātmakasyātmatvenāvagatasya sampadaṁ samṛddhiṁ vibhūtimanu nandati anu hṛṣyati, [ātmasampadaṁ manvānaḥ] ‘sampanne'hamanayā sampadā, mamaiṣā sampadi”ti manyamānaḥ । [tasya vyāpadaṁ] tasya kṣayaṁ [anu śocati] ‘mamaiṣā vyāpadahameva vyāpanna' iti । [sa sarva] evābhimānī [apratibuddhaḥ] ajña [iti ॥]
[eṣā catuṣpadī bhavatyavidyā ।] nanu cāpuṇye puṇyakhyātiḥ puṇye apuṇyakhyātiḥ ityābhyāṁ ṣaṭpadītvam-na-caturṣveva padeṣu yathāsaṁbhavamantarbhāvāt । [avidyā mūlaṁ] prabhavabījam [asya kleśasantānasya] abhiniveśāntakleśānāmanavaratapravartanasya । kiṁ ca- [karmāśayasya] ca trividhasya jātyāyurbhogalakṣaṇa [vipākatrayasahitasya] sakalasya saṁsārasyetyarthaḥ ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['Likewise, the cognition of pleasure in what is painful'] he will state. ['Due to the pains of transformation, burning, and <s>saṁskāra</s>, and due to the conflict of the activities of the <s>guṇas</s>, everything is indeed painful for the discerning one.'] [Therein] — in all of <s>saṁsāra</s> (worldly existence) which is painful — [the cognition of pleasure is <s>avidyā</s>.]
['Likewise, the cognition of self in what is non-self — in external instruments, whether sentient or insentient'] — such as cows, pots, and the like — ['or in the body which is the seat of experience, or in the mind which is the instrument of <s>Puruṣa</s> — the cognition of self in what is non-self.']
Here it is asked — in whose mind does the cognition of self in what is non-self, namely the mind, arise? Surely the mind

body.text: tasyāścāmitrāgoṣpadavadvastusatattvaṁ vijñeyam। yathā nāmitro mitrābhāvo na mitramātraṁ kiṁ tu tadviruddhaḥ sapatnaḥ। yathā vā'goṣpadaṁ na goṣpadābhāvo na goṣpadamātraṁ kiṁtu deśa eva tābhyāmanyadvastvantaram, evamavidyā na pramāṇaṁ na pramāṇābhāvaḥ kiṁtu vidyāviparītaṁ jñānāntaramavidyeti ॥ 5 ॥
body.translated_text: And the real nature of that [<s>avidyā</s>] should be understood as being like an enemy or a hoof-print: just as an enemy (<s>amitra</s>) is not the mere absence of a friend, nor is it simply a friend, but rather an adversary who is the opposite of a friend; and just as a hoof-print (<s>agoṣpada</s>) is not the absence of a hoof-print, nor is it merely a hoof-print, but rather a particular place that is something altogether different from both — so too <s>avidyā</s> is not <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition), nor is it the absence of <s>pramāṇa</s>, but rather a different cognition that is the opposite of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) — that is <s>avidyā</s>. || 5 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tasyā] śca avidyāyāḥ [amitrāgoṣpadavadvastusatatvaṁ] vastvantaratvaṁ [vijñeyam ।] kimarthamidamucyate ! yāvatā viparītakhyātiriti vastusatatvamuktameva ॥
ayamabhiprāyaḥ-avidyā iti nañsamāso'yaṁ tatpuruṣaḥ, sa cottarapadārthapradhāno vā syāt , yathā rājapuruṣa iti । yadvā, pūrvapadārthapradhānaḥ, ardhapippalīti ॥
tatra yadi pūrvapadārthapradhānastadānīṁ vidyāyāḥ pramāṇasyābhāva (vādi) iti, yatraiva vidyāprasaṅgo vṛttisāmānyāttatraiva (smṛtya)vṛttyantarādau pratītiriti, anirdhāritaviśeṣatatvo'rthaḥ prajñāyeta । yā tu viparītākhyātiḥ pūrvoktā avidyeti sā pāribhāṣikī syāt ॥
tataḥ ko doṣaḥ syāt ? avidyāśabdaśravaṇe sandehaḥ syāt । kiṁ prasiddha eva śabdārtha: paribhāṣita: śākhasaṁvyavahārārthaṁ, yathā [loke yeṣvarthaṣu prasiddhāni padāni tāni sati sambhave tadarthānyeva sūtreṣvityavagantavyaṁ] iti । athāśabdārtha eva, yathā [‘iko guṇavṛddhī'] iti । tataścāniścite padārthe nāvidyāśabdena vyavahāra: kriyeta ॥
athottarapadārthaprādhānyaṁ samānādhikaraṇatvānnīlotpalavat, tatrāpi nīlotpalaśabdārthayoravirodhādviśeṣyaviśeṣaṇabhāvena saṁbandho yuktaḥ ॥
iha nañā nivṛttirucyate । vidyāśabdenāpi vidyā । tatra yadyuttarapadasyārthaṁ pradhānaṁ prati guṇabhūto nañ tasyaivottarapadārthasyābhāvaṁ kuryāt, tadā tadguṇatvameva hīyeta । nāpītarasya prādhānyam ॥
yo hi kañcinnirvartayituṁ anuprasthito nirvartyameva vyāpādayet, na tasya nirvartyaṁ prati guṇatvam । nāpi nirvartyasya pradhānatā, tadvat । tasmāt pradhānavaśavartinā guṇena bhavitavyamiti vidyāyāmanyasyābhāva eveti kevalo nañ nityānuvādīti vidyāmātraṁ pratīyeta ॥
tadetadevaṁ kṛtvocyate । [‘tasyāścāmitrāgoṣpadavadvastusatatvaṁ vijñeyam’] iti । [yathā amitro na mitrābhāvaḥ] yathā pūrvapadārtheprādhānye ardhapippalīti । [na mitramātram ।] yathoktaṁ uttarapadārthaprādhānye pradhānavaśavartinā guṇena bhavitavyaṁ, na pradhānavināśeneti । tathā coktam-- [“abrāhmaṇamānayetyukte brāhmaṇamātrasyānayanaṁ prāpnotī'ti] nañvārtike । uttarapadārthaprādhānyapakṣe naño nityānuvādatvāt । evamamitra iti । evamavidyādi ॥
[yathā vā agoṣpadaṁ na goṣpadābhāvo na goṣpadamātraṁ, kintu deśa eva tābhyāṁ] goṣpadābhāvagoṣpadamātrābhyām [anyadvastvantaram । [kathamevam?]] dhyavasāyasvarūpayā: [ekātmateva] ekaśvāsāvātmā ca tasya bhāva ekātmatā । ivaśabdenātyantaviviktatāmācaṣṭe । [ekasvarūpāpattirivāsmitā kleśa ucyate ॥]
tataścāgoṣpadamiti goṣpadaprasakto'rthaḥ , goṣpadamātraṁ, goṣpadaviruddhaśceti trayo'rthāḥ pratibhānti । tatra yadi goṣpadamātraṁ bhavettadā nañaḥ prayogo'narthaka eva । anyābhāvānuvādī cedgoṣpade nañ syādevamapyanarthaka eva ।
atha goṣpadaprasaṅgayukte'rthe, tathāpi nañamukhye'rthe pravṛttassyāt , gobhiratyantāsevitatvasyānuktatvāt । yataḥ sevitattve bhaviṣyatyapi triṣvapi kāleṣu śabdaprayogo yuktassyāt । mukhyaścārtho nāma sa bhavati, yatra gobhiḥ sevitaṁ na bhūtaṁ na vartate nāpi bhaviṣyati । tasmāt, sati sambhave nañarthaḥ sa eva yukta iti na sevitaprasaṅgo nāpi sevitamātra iṣyate । gosevitaviruddha eva deśo'goṣpadaśabdenābhidhīyate ।
kathaṁ punarnīlotpalavadviśeṣyaviśeṣaṇabhāvaḥ ekasya, bhāvābhāvayorvirodhāt । tadabhāvapratipādanamātreṇa saṁvyavahārānupapatteḥ yasmin vastuni tadabhāva ucyate tadeva vastvantaraṁ pratīyate । taduktam - "goṣpadaṁ sevitāsevitapramāṇeṣu iti" ।
atrāsevitagrahaṇe punaḥ kriyamāṇe ca bahuvrīhirayaṁ vijñāyate, avidyamānasevitāsevita iti । (tasmāt) avidyā na pramāṇaṁ na ca pramāṇābhāvaḥ । [kintu viparītaṁ jñānāntaramiti] ॥ 5 ॥
body.translated_text:
[Vivaraṇa]
[And of that] <s>avidyā</s>, [its real nature is to be known as a positive entity, like an enemy or an unfrequented place.] 'A positive entity' means 'something other [than mere absence].' For what purpose is this said? Since 'erroneous cognition' (<s>viparītakhyāti</s>) already stated its real nature.
The intention is this: the compound '<s>avidyā</s>' is a <s>nañ-samāsa</s> (negative compound), a <s>tatpuruṣa</s>. It could be either one in which the latter member's meaning predominates, as in '<s>rājapuruṣa</s>' (king's man); or one in which the former member's meaning predominates, as in '<s>ardhapippalī</s>' (half a long pepper).
Therein, if the former member's meaning predominates, then [<s>avidyā</s> would mean] 'the absence of <s>vidyā</s>, of valid knowledge'—and wherever there is occasion for knowledge, by the generic nature of mental activity, the cognition through memory or other [non-valid] mental activities [would arise]—and thus the object would be apprehended without its specific nature being determined. But the 'erroneous cognition' (<s>viparītākhyāti</s>) described earlier as <s>avidyā</s>—that would then be merely a technical term.
What fault would follow from that? Upon hearing the word '<s>avidyā</s>,' there would be doubt: is it the well-known word-meaning, or a technical one for the purposes of the treatise's discourse—as [the principle states]: ['In the world, those words that are well-known in certain meanings—when possible, they are to be understood in those very meanings in the <s>sūtras</s>']? Or is it a non-standard meaning, as in ['<s>iko guṇavṛddhī</s>'] (where <s>guṇa</s> and <s>vṛddhi</s> are technical terms)? And thus, with the word-meaning uncertain, one would not be able to employ the word '<s>avidyā</s>' [with precision].
Now, if the latter member's meaning predominates, being a co-referential compound like '<s>nīlotpala</s>' (blue lotus)—even there, since there is no contradiction between the meanings of '<s>nīla</s>' and '<s>utpala</s>,' their relation as qualifier and qualified is justified.
But here, the <s>nañ</s> (negative particle) expresses negation, and the word '<s>vidyā</s>' expresses knowledge. If the <s>nañ</s>, being subordinate to the latter member's meaning as predominant, were to negate the very meaning of that latter member—then its subordinate status would itself be undermined. Nor would there be predominance of the other [member].
For one who, having set out to produce something, were to destroy the very thing to be produced—for such a one there is no subordination to the thing to be produced. Nor is there predominance of the thing produced—likewise here. Therefore, since the subordinate element must follow the predominant one, [and if <s>nañ</s> merely negates knowledge,] then only the absence of everything other than knowledge would be understood—the <s>nañ</s> being a mere constant qualifier—and only knowledge itself (<s>vidyāmātra</s>) would be understood.
Having established this, he says: ['And its real nature is to be known as a positive entity, like an enemy or an unfrequented place.'] [Just as an enemy (<s>amitra</s>) is not the mere absence of a friend]—as when the former member's meaning predominates, like '<s>ardhapippalī</s>.' [Nor is it merely a friend]—as stated, when the latter member's meaning predominates, the subordinate must follow the predominant, not by destroying the predominant. And thus it has been said: ['When told "Bring a non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>," it results in not bringing merely a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>']—in the <s>Nañ-vārtika</s>. Since on the view that the latter member's meaning predominates, the <s>nañ</s> is merely a constant qualifier. Thus '<s>amitra</s>' (enemy). Thus '<s>avidyā</s>' and the rest.
[Or, just as '<s>agoṣpada</s>' (a place unfrequented by cows) is neither the mere absence of a cow-trodden place nor merely a cow-trodden place, but rather a place—a positive entity different from both] the absence of a cow-trodden place and a merely cow-trodden place. [How so?] Through the nature of determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>), [there is a seeming identity]—'one' and 'self' (<s>ātman</s>)—the state of being one self (<s>ekātmatā</s>). The word '<s>iva</s>' (as if) indicates that they are in reality utterly distinct. [The seeming attainment of a single form is the <s>kleśa</s> called <s>asmitā</s>.]
And thus '<s>agoṣpada</s>' presents three possible meanings: (1) something connected with a cow-trodden place, (2) merely a cow-trodden place, or (3) something contrary to a cow-trodden place. If it were merely a cow-trodden place, the use of <s>nañ</s> would be pointless. If the <s>nañ</s> in '<s>goṣpada</s>' merely qualifies by negating something else—even so, it would be pointless.
Now, if [<s>agoṣpada</s> refers to] something that is connected with the possibility of being cow-trodden—even then, the <s>nañ</s> would be employed in its primary sense, since it has not been stated that cows have always frequented it. For even if it will be frequented [by cows] at all three times, the use of the word would still be justified. And the primary meaning is that in which cows have not frequented, do not frequent, and will not frequent the place. Therefore, when possible, the meaning of <s>nañ</s> is precisely that—neither the possibility of being frequented nor merely being frequented is intended. What is denoted by the word '<s>agoṣpada</s>' is a place that is contrary to being frequented by cows.
But how can there be a qualifier-qualified relation, as with '<s>nīlotpala</s>' (blue lotus), for one [compound], given the contradiction between being and non-being? Since communication is impossible through the mere statement of something's absence, when one says 'the absence of X exists in Y,' the positive entity Y itself is understood. As stated: 'A cow-trodden place is [understood] in relation to the standards of frequented and unfrequented.'
When the mention of 'unfrequented' is made again here, this is understood as a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound: 'that in which frequented and unfrequented are not present.' Therefore, <s>avidyā</s> is neither a valid means of knowledge nor the mere absence of a valid means of knowledge. [But rather, it is a different cognition that is erroneous.] // 5 //

body.text: dṛgdarśanaśaktyorekātmatevāsmitā ॥ 6 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>Asmitā</s> (egoism) is the seeming identity (<s>ekātmatā iva</s>) of the power of seeing (<s>dṛk</s>) and the power of sight (<s>darśana</s>). // 6 //

body.text: puruṣo dṛkśaktirbuddhirdarśanaśaktirityetayorekasvarūpāpattirivāsmitā kleśa ucyate। bhoktṛbhogyaśaktyoratyantavibhaktayoratyantāsaṁkīrṇayoravibhāgaprāptāviva satyāṁ bhogaḥ kalpate। svarūpapratilambhe tu tayoḥ kaivalyameva bhavati kuto bhoga iti। tathā coktam – ‘buddhitaḥ paraṁ puruṣamākāraśīlavidyādibhirvibhaktamapaśyankuryāttatrā''tmabuddhiṁ mohena’ iti ॥ 6 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>Puruṣa</s> is the power of seeing (<s>dṛkśakti</s>); <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) is the power of sight (<s>darśanaśakti</s>). The seeming attainment of a single form by these two is the <s>kleśa</s> called <s>asmitā</s>. When the powers of the experiencer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>) and the experienceable (<s>bhogya</s>), which are utterly distinct and utterly unmixed, appear as if having attained non-differentiation—then enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) is constructed. But when their own natures are recovered, there is only <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation) for them both—whence then enjoyment? And thus it has been said: 'One who, through delusion, not seeing <s>Puruṣa</s> as distinct from <s>buddhi</s> by form, nature, and knowledge, would impose the notion of self upon it [<s>buddhi</s>].' // 6 //

body.text:
vivaraṇam
adhunāsmitākhyaṁ viparyayamācaṣṭe - dṛk darśanam upalabdhiḥ puruṣaḥ sa eva śaktiḥ । dṛśyate'neneti darśanam । saiva śaktiḥ antaḥkaraṇādhyavasāyarūpā । tayoḥ dṛgdarśanaśaktyoḥ upalabdhyadhyavasayasvarūpayoḥ ekātmateva ekaścāsāvātmā ca tasya bhāva ekātmatā । ivaśabdenātyantaviviktatāmācaṣṭe । ekasvarūpāpattirivāsmitā kleśa ucyate ॥
yasminnahaṁpratyaye cittapuruṣayorviveko nopalabhyate so'yamahaṁpratyayo'smitākhyaḥ kleśa ucyate ।
pūrvatra tu puruṣopakaraṇe'ntaḥkaraṇe'nātmanyātmakhyatiriti viparītadarśanamevāvidyetyuktama । iha tu punarbuddhipuruṣayoraviśeṣadarśanamekasvarūpāpattiriva darśanamasmiteti viśeṣaḥ ॥
tadetaduktaṁ bhavati - [bhoktṛbhogyaśaktyoratyantāviviktayoḥ] atyantāsaṅkīrṇayoḥ [avibhāgaprāptāviva satyāṁ bhogaḥ kalpate ।] bhogaheturasmitābhidhānakleśa ityarthaḥ । sati hyahaṁpratyaye sukhito'haṁ du:khito'hamati sukhadu:khādisambandho bhavati । tasmādetadevamiti ॥
[svarūpapratilambhe tu tayoḥ] viveke nāhaṁ mameti svarūpopalabdhau satyāṁ buddhipuruṣayoḥ kaivalyameva avimiśrataiva bhavati । [kuto bhoga iti ।] kāraṇe hyaviśeṣāhaṁpratyayātmani sati kāryaṁ bhogaḥ, tasminnasati kāraṇe na bhoga iti ॥
na hi manasi cetanāvatvamanadhyāropya sukhitvaṁ duḥkhitvaṁ vā śakyaṁ pratyetum । ahaṁpratyayaviṣayo hi sukhaduḥkhapralyayādhikaraṇam । 'ahaṁ sukhī duḥkhī cāham' iti sāmānādhikaraṇyāt । tasmādasmitākhyo'haṅkāro bhogahetuḥ ॥
[tathā coktaṁ-buddhitaḥ paraṁ puruṣaṁ] buddhitaḥ sakāśāt [vibhaktaṁ] vilakṣaṇamanyam । kairguṇairvibhāga ityāha- [ākāraśīlavidyābhiḥ ākāreṇa] vṛtisārūmyeṇa, [śīlena] buddhipratisaṁveditathā । [vidyayā] caitanyasvarūpatayā । athavā [ākāreṇa] śuddhānantasvarūpatvena, [śīlena] apariṇāmitvādapratisaṁkramatvena, [vidyayā] citiśaktisvarūpatayā । tadetairdharmarbuddhito vibhāgaḥ ॥
tathā buddherapi [ākāreṇa] sukhaduḥkhamohātmakatvena, [śīlena] prakhyāpravṛttisthityātmanā, [vidyayā] sarvārthīdhyavasāyātmakatvena puruṣāt [vibhāgaḥ ।] itthamanyonyamākāraśīlavidyābhirvibhaktaṁ puruṣaṁ [apaśyan kuryāttatra] tasyāṁ buddhau [ātmabuddhim] ātmapratyayaṁ [mohena] loka iti । vidyāśīlākārairatyantavibhaktayorbuddhipuruṣaye.oravibhāga iva taddarśanamityanenāṁśenodāharaṇam ॥
yattu [vibhaktamapaśyan kuryāttatrātmabuddhim] iti । sā pūrvoktaivāvidyā । yadvā asmitāyā avidyābhedatvāt sarvamudāharaṇamiti । apaśyan kuryāditi puruṣasvarūpādarśanamavidyāyāḥ, asmitāyāśca hetuḥ kāraṇaṁ cittasya draṣṭṛdṛśyoparaktatā । puruṣasya tvadarśanaṁ draṣṭṛtvādeva ॥ 6 ॥
body.translated_text:
[Vivaraṇa]
Now he describes the error (<s>viparyaya</s>) called <s>asmitā</s>. '<s>Dṛk</s>' is seeing (<s>darśana</s>), apprehension (<s>upalabdhi</s>)—that is <s>Puruṣa</s>; that itself is 'power' (<s>śakti</s>). '<s>Darśana</s>' means 'that by which one sees'—that very [instrument of seeing] is the 'power' in the form of the inner organ's determination (<s>antaḥkaraṇādhyavasāya</s>). Of these two—the power of seeing and the power of sight—apprehension and determination in their own natures—'seeming identity' (<s>ekātmatā iva</s>): 'one' and 'self'—the state of being one self is <s>ekātmatā</s>. The word '<s>iva</s>' (as if) indicates that they are in reality utterly distinct. The seeming attainment of a single form is the <s>kleśa</s> called <s>asmitā</s>.
The I-cognition (<s>ahaṃpratyaya</s>) in which the distinction between <s>citta</s> (mind) and <s>Puruṣa</s> is not perceived—that I-cognition is the <s>kleśa</s> called <s>asmitā</s>.
Previously, <s>avidyā</s> was described as erroneous seeing—the superimposition of selfhood upon the non-self, the inner organ that is an instrument of <s>Puruṣa</s>. But here, the non-differentiated seeing of <s>buddhi</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>—the seeing that is like an attainment of a single form—that is <s>asmitā</s>. This is the distinction.
What has been stated amounts to this: [When the powers of the experiencer and the experienceable, utterly] unmixed, [appear as if having attained non-differentiation—then enjoyment is constructed.] The meaning is: the <s>kleśa</s> called <s>asmitā</s> is the cause of enjoyment. For when the I-cognition is present, the connection 'I am happy,' 'I am unhappy' with pleasure, pain, and the like occurs. Therefore, this is so.
[But when their own natures are recovered]—when there is discrimination, when there is the realization 'I am not [this], this is not mine,' when the own nature of both <s>buddhi</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> is apprehended—then there is only <s>kaivalya</s>, nothing but non-admixture. [Whence then enjoyment?] For when the cause—the I-cognition of non-differentiation—is present, enjoyment is the effect; when that cause is absent, there is no enjoyment.
For without superimposing the nature of consciousness upon the mind, one cannot cognize happiness or unhappiness. For the object of the I-cognition is the locus of the cognitions of pleasure and pain. 'I am happy, I am unhappy'—because of their co-referentiality. Therefore, the ego (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>) called <s>asmitā</s> is the cause of enjoyment.
[And thus it has been said: '<s>Puruṣa</s>, beyond <s>buddhi</s>']—from <s>buddhi</s>, [distinct]—different in character. By what qualities is the distinction? He says: [by form, nature, and knowledge. 'By form']—by the conformity of modifications, ['by nature']—by the manner of <s>buddhi</s>'s experiencing, ['by knowledge']—by the nature of being consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>). Alternatively: ['by form']—by the nature of being pure and infinite, ['by nature']—by being unchanging and non-transferring, ['by knowledge']—by the nature of being the power of consciousness (<s>citiśakti</s>). By these properties, the distinction from <s>buddhi</s>.
Likewise for <s>buddhi</s> too: ['by form']—by being constituted of pleasure, pain, and delusion; ['by nature']—by having the nature of luminosity (<s>prakhyā</s>), activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>), and inertia (<s>sthiti</s>); ['by knowledge']—by being of the nature of determination regarding all objects—the distinction from <s>Puruṣa</s>. [One who, not seeing] <s>Puruṣa</s>, mutually distinct from <s>buddhi</s> by form, nature, and knowledge, [would impose the notion of self upon] <s>buddhi</s> [through delusion]—so does the world. The illustration pertains to this aspect: the seeing of non-differentiation, as it were, between <s>buddhi</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, which are utterly distinct by knowledge, nature, and form.
As for [one who, not seeing the distinct, would impose the notion of self upon it]—that is the very <s>avidyā</s> described earlier. Or, since <s>asmitā</s> is a subdivision of <s>avidyā</s>, the entire illustration applies. 'Not seeing'—the non-seeing of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s own nature is <s>avidyā</s>'s [function]; and <s>asmitā</s>'s cause is the mind's being colored by both seer and seen. But <s>Puruṣa</s>'s non-seeing is precisely because of its nature as the seer. // 6 //

body.text: sukhānuśayī rāgaḥ ॥ 7 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>Rāga</s> (attachment) is that which dwells on (<s>anuśayin</s>) pleasure. // 7 //

body.text: sukhābhijñasya sukhānusmṛtipūrvaḥ sukhe tatsādhane vā yo gardhastṛṣṇā lobhaḥ sa rāga iti ॥ 7 ॥
body.translated_text: For one who has known pleasure, preceded by the memory of pleasure, the craving, thirst, greed toward pleasure or toward its means—that is <s>rāga</s> (attachment). // 7 //

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[sukhānujanmā] sukhānuśayī [rāgaḥ ।] anu janma, anu utpattiryasya saḥ । [sukhānuśayī] tathā [duḥkhānuśayīti] anyeṣāṁ pāṭhaḥ । [sukhānuśayī rāgaḥ duḥkhānuśayī dveṣa] iti te vyācakṣate, sukhamanubhavituṁ śīlamasya sa sukhānuśayī, tathā duḥkhānuśayīti । ubhayadhā'pyanujanmataiva । tadeva tācchīlyam । tathā ca vakṣyati- ['dharmātsukhaṁ sukhādraga:'] iti ॥
kathaṁ sukhānuśayitvamiti tadāha - [sukhābhijñasya] sukhe ābhijñānamābhijñā yasya sa sukhābhijñaḥ sukhaṁ ya upalabdhavāṁstasya, sukhābhijñasya [sukhānusmṛtipūrvaḥ] sukhaṁ pūrvānubhūtamanusmaran [sukhe] hlāde [tatsādhane vā] agarucandanādāvanurajyate । tatra [yo'sau gardhaḥ sa] ucyate [tṛṣṇā lobho rāga iti ॥ 7 ॥]
body.translated_text:
[Vivaraṇa]
[Born after pleasure] '<s>Sukhānuśayī</s>' (dwelling on pleasure) is <s>rāga</s>. '<s>Anu janma</s>'—born after, arising after. [<s>Sukhānuśayī</s>] likewise [<s>duḥkhānuśayī</s>]—this is the reading of others. [<s>Sukhānuśayī</s> is <s>rāga</s>; <s>duḥkhānuśayī</s> is <s>dveṣa</s>]—thus they explain: one whose habit (<s>śīla</s>) it is to experience pleasure is '<s>sukhānuśayī</s>'; likewise '<s>duḥkhānuśayī</s>.' In both ways, it is through being born after. That very thing is the habitual tendency. And thus he will say: ['From <s>dharma</s> comes pleasure; from pleasure, attachment.'] 
How is the 'dwelling on pleasure' [explained]? He says: [For one who has known pleasure]—<s>ābhijñā</s> is recognition of pleasure; one who possesses that is '<s>sukhābhijña</s>'—one who has experienced pleasure. [Preceded by the memory of pleasure]—remembering previously experienced pleasure, [toward pleasure]—toward delight, [or toward its means]—toward sandalwood paste, etc.—one becomes attached. Therein, [that which is craving]—[that] is called [thirst, greed, <s>rāga</s>.] // 7 //

body.text: duḥkhānuśayī dveṣaḥ ॥ 8 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>Dveṣa</s> (aversion) is that which dwells on (<s>anuśayin</s>) suffering. // 8 //

body.text: duḥkhābhijñasya duḥkhānusmṛtipūrvo duḥkhe tatsādhane vā yaḥ pratigho manyurjighāṁsā krodhaḥ sa dveṣaḥ ॥ 8 ॥
body.translated_text: For one who has known suffering, preceded by the memory of suffering, the hostility, anger, desire to harm, wrath toward suffering or toward its means—that is <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion). // 8 //

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[duḥkhānujanmā] duḥkhānuśayī dveṣaḥ । duḥkhamuktam [‘yenābhihatāḥ prāṇinastadapaghātāya prayatante'] iti । [duḥkhābhijñasyeti] pūrvavadvyākhyānam । [duḥkhānusmṛtipūrvo duḥkhe tatsādhane vā] sataskarārdau [yo manyurujjihāsā] uddhātumicchā [krodhaḥ sa dveṣaḥ ।] rāgeṇa tulyaṁ vyākhyānaṁ sarvam ॥ 8 ॥
body.translated_text:
[Vivaraṇa]
[Born after suffering] '<s>Duḥkhānuśayī</s>' (dwelling on suffering) is <s>dveṣa</s>. Suffering has been described [as 'that by which afflicted beings strive to remove it']. [For one who has known suffering]—the explanation is as before. [Preceded by the memory of suffering, toward suffering or toward its means]—toward robbers and the like—[the anger, the desire to cast out]—the wish to eject—[wrath—that is <s>dveṣa</s>.] The entire explanation is parallel to that of <s>rāga</s>. // 8 //

body.text: svarasavāhī viduṣo'pi tathā rūḍho'bhiniveśaḥ ॥ 9 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>Abhiniveśa</s> (clinging to life) flows by its own momentum (<s>svarasavāhī</s>), being firmly established even in the wise. // 9 //

body.text: sarvasya prāṇina iyamātmāśīrnityā bhavati mā na bhūvaṁ bhūyāsamiti। na cānanubhūtamaraṇadharmakasyaiṣā bhavatyātmāśīḥ। etayā ca pūrvajanmānubhavaḥ pratīyate। sa cāyamabhiniveśaḥ kleśaḥ svarasavāhī kṛmerapi jātamātrasya pratyakṣānumānāgamairasaṁbhāvito maraṇatrāsa ucchedadṛṣṭyātmakaḥ pūrvajanmānubhū'taṁ maraṇaduḥkhamanumāpayati।
body.translated_text: Every living being has this eternal self-blessing: 'May I not cease to be! May I continue to exist!' And this self-blessing could not belong to one who has not experienced the nature of death. And by this, experience from previous births is inferred. And this <s>abhiniveśa</s>, the <s>kleśa</s>, flowing by its own momentum—the terror of death even in a worm just born, unexplainable by perception, inference, or scripture—being of the nature of the view of annihilation (<s>ucchedadṛṣṭi</s>)—causes the inference of suffering from death experienced in previous births.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[svarasavāhī viduṣo'pi tathā rūḍho'bhiniveśaḥ svarasena] svabhāvena cittasyavidyāmātraṇa [voḍhuṁ] pravartirnu [śīlamasya ।] vahaterakarmakasyāpi darśanāt yathā nadī vahatīti । athavā [svarasaṁ] svabhāvaṁ [voḍhuṁ śīlamasya svarasavāhī viduṣo'pi] samyagdarśanasyāpi । apiśabdādaviduṣa eva yukto maraṇatrāsa ātmocchedamānina ityabhiprāyaḥ । samyagdarśanasyātmānucchedamānino'yukta iti । tathā vimūḍhatarabuddhiṣvātmocchedadarśiṣvayamabhiprāyo maraṇatrāso rūḍho'bhiniviṣṭaḥ sthiro yathā tathaiva viduṣe'pyātmānucchedadarśitvādayukto'pi rūḍhaḥ ॥
kasmāt punarayaṁ maraṇatrāsaḥ svarasenaiva rūḍha iti ? yataḥ [sarvasya prāṇinaḥ iyamātmāśīrnityā bhavati,] yadasau [maraṇaṁ mānvabhūvam] ucchedaṁ mā prāpam । iyamāśīrvā, [bhūyāsaṁ] guṇaiḥ śubhātmabhiḥ sampatsīyeti na tairviyogo bhūyāditi । mūḍheṣu bhogasampadāmātmanaścānucchedaḥ prārthanīyaḥ ॥
