kimetayā''śiṣā avagamyata ityāha- [na cānanubhūtamaraṇadharmakasya bhavatyeṣā ā.ātmāśī] riti । [etayā ca] ātmāśiṣā [pūrvajanmānubhavaḥ pratīyate ।] tadetaduktaṁ bhavati-na hyananubhūte sukhe bhavati prārthanā, nāpyananubhūte duḥkhe tatparihāravāñchā bhavatīti । yenāpi pratyakṣānumānābhyāmananubhūtaṁ maraṇaduḥkhaṁ tasyāpyanayātmāśiṣā pūrvo maraṇānubhavaḥ pratīyate, so'pi nāntareṇa janmeti janmānubhavaḥ । tayā pūrvaḥ pūrvo janmamaraṇānubhavo'nādiriti mataḥ । [sa cāyamabhiniveśaḥ leśaḥ kṛmerapi jātamātrasyeti ॥]
maraṇānubhavakāraṇamācaṣṭe- [pratyakṣānumānāgamairasambhāvito maraṇātrāsa ucchedadṛṣṭadyātmaka] ātmabhogocchedapratipattihetuḥ [pūrvajanmānubhūtaṁ maraṇadu:khamanumāpayati ।]
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇa (Elucidation):
[Flowing by its own momentum, <s>abhiniveśa</s> (clinging to life) is firmly established even in the wise.] 'By its own momentum' (<s>svarasena</s>) means by the mind's own nature, through the impulsion of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) alone, [it carries along]—this is its disposition. For the verb 'to carry' (<s>vahati</s>) is seen even without an object, as in 'the river flows.' Alternatively, ['flowing by its own momentum'] means [<s>abhiniveśa</s>] whose disposition is to carry along its own nature—[established] even in the wise, even in one who has right vision. The word '<s>api</s>' (even) implies that the fear of death is fitting only for the ignorant who consider the self to be annihilated. For one who has right vision and does not consider the self to be annihilated, it is unfitting. The idea is: just as in those of extremely deluded intelligence who hold the view of self-annihilation, this fear of death is firmly established and entrenched—so too in the wise one, though unfitting because of not holding the view of self-annihilation, it is nevertheless firmly established.
Why then is this fear of death established by its own momentum? Because [every living being has this eternal self-wish:] that 'May I not have died'—meaning 'may I not have been annihilated.' Or this wish: [May I continue to be]—'may I be enriched with auspicious qualities, and may there be no separation from them.' Among the deluded, the non-annihilation of enjoyments, possessions, and the self is what is desired.
What is understood from this wish? He says— [This self-wish does not arise in one who has not experienced the nature of death.] [And from this] self-wish, [the experience of previous births is inferred.] This amounts to saying: there is no desire for happiness that has not been experienced, nor is there a wish to avoid suffering that has not been experienced. Even for one who has not experienced the suffering of death through perception or inference, a prior experience of death is inferred from this self-wish; and that [prior experience] is not without a birth, so there is an experience of birth. Through this, the prior and prior experience of birth and death is beginningless—such is the view. [And this <s>abhiniveśa</s> as an affliction is found even in a newly born worm.]
He states the cause of the experience of death— [The fear of death, though not established by perception, inference, or scripture—being of the nature of the view of annihilation etc.]—being a cause for the apprehension of the annihilation of self and enjoyments—[leads to the inference of death-suffering experienced in a former birth.]

body.text: yathā cāyamatyantamūḍheṣu dṛśyate kleśastathā viduṣo'pi vijñātapūrvāparāntasya rūḍhaḥ। kasmāt। samānā hi tayoḥ kuśalākuśalayormaraṇaduḥkhānubhavādiyaṁ vāsaneti ॥ 9 ॥
body.translated_text: And just as this <s>kleśa</s> (affliction) is seen in the extremely deluded, so too it is firmly established even in the wise one who has understood the prior and posterior limits [of existence]. Why? Because this <s>vāsanā</s> (latent tendency) arising from the experience of death-suffering is the same in both the virtuous and the non-virtuous.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[yathā cāyamatyantamūḍheṣu dṛśyate] kṛmiprabhṛtiṣu [kleśastathā viduṣo'pi vijñātapūrvāparāntikasyāpi] pūrvāntikaṁ bandhaḥ aparāntikaṁ muktiḥ । jñātajanmamaraṇāntikasya vā [rūḍhaḥ । kasmāt] punarmūḍhasyeva viduṣo [rūḍha] iti, tata āha- [samānā hi kuśalākuśalayorvidvadaviduṣormaraṇānubhavādiyaṁ vāsanā] maraṇabhayavāsanā ॥ 9 ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇa (Elucidation):
[Just as this <s>kleśa</s> is seen in the extremely deluded]—in worms and the like—[so too in the wise one who has known the prior and posterior limits], it is [firmly established]. The 'prior limit' is bondage; the 'posterior limit' is liberation. Or it means one who has known the limits of birth and death. [Why] is it firmly established even in the wise, as in the deluded? To this he says— [Because this <s>vāsanā</s> (latent tendency) arising from the experience of death is the same in both the virtuous and the non-virtuous]—the <s>vāsanā</s> of the fear of death [is common to both the wise and the unwise].

body.text: te pratiprasavaheyāḥ sūkṣmāḥ ॥ 10 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>te pratiprasavaheyāḥ sūkṣmāḥ</s> — Those [<s>kleśas</s>], when subtle, are to be destroyed by involution (<s>pratiprasava</s>). (Sūtra 2.10)

body.text: te pañca kleśā dagdhabījakalpā yoginaścaritādhikāre cetasi pralīne saha tenaivāstaṁ gacchanti ॥ 10 ॥
body.translated_text: Those five <s>kleśas</s>, like burnt seeds, when the mind of the <s>yogin</s> whose function is complete dissolves, come to an end together with it.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[‘kleśamūlaḥ karmāśayaḥ’, ‘sati mūle tadvipākaḥ’] iti vakṣyate । tasmātte kleśā hātavyāḥ । hānārthaśca te pradarśaitāḥ । tadavahānau copāyaṁ vakṣyati – [‘dhyānaheyāstadvṛttayaḥ?] iti । tatra na jñāyate kiṁviṣayo dhyānaprayogaḥ, kiṁ dagdhabījakarmakleśaviṣayaḥ ? kiṁ sarvaviṣayaḥ ? iti । tadviṣayavibhajanārthamidaṁ sūtramārabhyate-- [te pratiprasavaheyāḥ sūkṣmā iti ॥]
[te pañca kleśāḥ dagdhabījakalpāḥ yoginaśvaritādhikāre cetāsi pralīne saha tenāstaṁ gacchanti ।] etaduktaṁ bhavati--samyagdarśanābhyāsānaladagdhabījasāmarthyānāṁ kleśānāṁ kṛtāśeṣapuruṣaprayojanasya cetasaḥ pratiprasavenaiva pralayenaiva pralayotpatterna dhyānasādhanāpekṣā । na hi dagdhaṁ dāhamapekṣate, piṣṭaṁ vā peṣaṇamiti । cetastu sādhitapuruṣārthatvāt sthitiprayojanābhāvācca svayameva nivartate ॥ 10 ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇa (Elucidation):
It will be stated: ['The reservoir of <s>karma</s> is rooted in the <s>kleśas</s>'; 'When the root exists, its fruition follows.'] Therefore those <s>kleśas</s> are to be destroyed. And the purpose of their destruction has been shown. The means for their destruction will be stated: ['Their active modifications are to be destroyed by meditation.'] In this regard, it is not known what is the object of the application of meditation—is it directed toward <s>kleśas</s> whose seeds are burnt? Or toward all [<s>kleśas</s>]? For the purpose of distinguishing their objects, this <s>sūtra</s> is introduced— [Those, when subtle, are to be destroyed by involution.]
[Those five <s>kleśas</s>, like burnt seeds, when the mind of the <s>yogin</s> whose function is complete dissolves, come to an end together with it.] This amounts to saying: for <s>kleśas</s> whose seed-capacity has been burnt by the fire of the practice of right vision, when the mind that has fulfilled all purposes of <s>Puruṣa</s> dissolves through involution (<s>pratiprasava</s>) alone—dissolution being its natural end—there is no need for the means of meditation. For what is already burnt does not need burning, nor does what is already ground need grinding. And the mind, having accomplished the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> and having no reason for continued existence, ceases of its own accord.

body.text: sthitānāṁ tu bījabhāvopagatānām –
body.translated_text: But for those that remain, having reached the state of seeds—

body.text: dhyānaheyāstadvṛttayaḥ ॥ 11 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>dhyānaheyās tadvṛttayaḥ</s> — Their active modifications are to be destroyed by meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>). (Sūtra 2.11)

body.text: kleśānāṁ yā vṛttayaḥ sthūlāstāḥ kriyāyogena tatkṛtāḥ satyaḥ prasaṁkhyānena dhyānena hātavyā yāvatsūkṣmīkṛtā yāvaddagdhabījakalpā iti। yathā vastrāṇāṁ sthūlo malaḥ pūrvaṁ nirdhūyate paścātsūkṣmo yatnenopāyena cāpanīyate tathā svalpapratipakṣāḥ sthūlā vṛttayaḥ kleśānāṁ, sūkṣmāstu mahāpratipakṣā iti ॥ 11 ॥
body.translated_text: The gross active modifications of the <s>kleśas</s>, having been attenuated by <s>kriyāyoga</s> (the yoga of action), are to be destroyed by the meditation of discriminative knowledge (<s>prasaṃkhyāna</s>)—until they are made subtle, until they become like burnt seeds. Just as the gross dirt of garments is first shaken off, and then the subtle [dirt] is removed with effort and means, so too the gross modifications of the <s>kleśas</s> have a mild antidote, while the subtle ones have a great antidote.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
kīdṛśānāṁ punardhyānādisādhanāpekṣetyata ucyate- [sthitānāṁ tu bījabhāvopagatānāmiti ॥]
[dhyānaheyāstadvṛttayaḥ । kleśānāṁ yā vṛttayaḥ sthūlāstāḥ kriyāyogena] tapassvādhyāyeśvarapraṇidhānākhyena sthūlapratipakṣeṇa [tanūkṛtāḥ] pūrvam । tata idānīṁ tanūkaraṇādbījaśaktyavasthāḥ [prasaṁkhyānena] samyagdarśanaśīlanato naipuṇaviśeṣeṇa [dhyānena] mahatā balīyasā pratipakṣeṇa [hātavyāḥ,] tato'pi [yāvatsūkṣmīkṛtāḥ ।] kimuktam bhavati ! [yāvaddagdhabījakalpāḥ] yāvanirbājīkṛtā iti ॥
tat kimiveti ? [yathā vastrāṇāṁ sthūlo malaḥ pūrvaṁ nirdhūyate, paścātsūkṣmo] malaḥ khenehanādinimitto [yatnena copāyena] kṣārādiviśiṣṭopāyena [apanīyate, tathā svalpapratipakṣāḥ] tapassvādhyāyeśvaraprāṇidhānayamānayamādiyogāṅgānuṣṭhānādipratipakṣāḥ [sthūlā vṛttayaḥ kleśānām । sūkṣmāstu mahāpratipakṣā iti ।] tapassvādhyāyādyanuṣṭhānapratilabdhadīptiprakarṣāviplavasamyagdarśanamahāpratipakṣā: sūkṣmā bījaśaktyapekṣā iti ॥ 11 ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇa (Elucidation):
What kind of [<s>kleśas</s>] require the means of meditation etc.? To this it is said— [But for those that remain, having reached the state of seeds.]
[Their active modifications are to be destroyed by meditation. The gross active modifications of the <s>kleśas</s>] are first [attenuated by <s>kriyāyoga</s>]—namely, the gross antidote consisting of <s>tapas</s> (austerity), <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study), and <s>Īśvarapraṇidhāna</s> (devotion to the Lord). Then, now that they have been attenuated, being in the state of seed-potency, [they are to be destroyed by the meditation of <s>prasaṃkhyāna</s>]—through the practice of right vision, through a particular excellence of skill—[by meditation,] a great and powerful antidote, [to be destroyed,] further [until they are made subtle.] What is being said? [Until they become like burnt seeds]—until they are rendered seedless.
In what way? [Just as the gross dirt of garments is first shaken off, and then the subtle] dirt, caused by perspiration etc., [is removed with effort and a specific means]—a special means such as alkali—[so too, the gross modifications of the <s>kleśas</s> have a mild antidote]—the antidotes consisting of the practice of <s>tapas</s>, <s>svādhyāya</s>, <s>Īśvarapraṇidhāna</s>, <s>yama</s> (restraints), <s>niyama</s> (observances), and other limbs of <s>yoga</s>. [The subtle ones, however, have a great antidote]—the great antidote of right vision whose brilliance and excellence have been attained through the practice of <s>tapas</s>, <s>svādhyāya</s>, etc., [and which is] unwavering—these are the subtle ones in their seed-potency state.

body.text: kleśamūlaḥ karmāśayo dṛṣṭādṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaḥ ॥ 12 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>kleśamūlaḥ karmāśayo dṛṣṭādṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaḥ</s> — The reservoir of <s>karma</s>, rooted in the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), is to be experienced in a seen (present) or unseen (future) birth. (Sūtra 2.12)

body.text: tatra puṇyāpuṇyakarmāśayaḥ kāmalobhamohakrodhaprabhavaḥ। sa dṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaścādṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaśca। tatra tīvrasaṁvegena mantratapaḥsamādhibhirnirvartita īśvaradevatāmaharṣimahānubhāvānāmārādhanādvā yaḥ pariniṣpannaḥ sa sadyaḥ paripacyate puṇyakarmāśaya iti। tathā tīvrakleśena bhītavyādhitakṛpaṇeṣu viśvāsopagateṣu vā mahānubhāveṣu vā tapasviṣu kṛtaḥ punaḥ punarapakāraḥ sa cāpi pāpakarmāśayaḥ sadya eva paripacyate। yathā nandīśvaraḥ kumāro manuṣyapariṇāmaṁ hitvā devatvena pariṇataḥ। tathā nahuṣo'pi devānāmindraḥ svakaṁ pariṇāmaṁ hitvā tiryaktvena pariṇata iti। tatra nārakāṇāṁ nāsti dṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaḥ karmāśayaḥ। kṣīṇakleśānāmapi nāstyadṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaḥ karmāśaya iti ॥ 12 ॥
body.translated_text: Therein, the reservoir of meritorious and demeritorious <s>karma</s> arises from desire, greed, delusion, and anger. It is either to be experienced in this present life or in a future unseen life. When brought to fruition with intense urgency through <s>mantras</s>, <s>tapas</s>, and <s>samādhi</s>, or through the worship of <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), deities, great sages, and exalted beings—such a meritorious <s>karmāśaya</s> (reservoir of <s>karma</s>) ripens immediately. Likewise, a demeritorious <s>karmāśaya</s>—offense committed again and again against the frightened, the sick, the wretched, those who have sought refuge in trust, or against exalted beings and ascetics—that too ripens immediately. Just as <s>Nandīśvara</s>, the youth, abandoning the human state, was transformed into a divine state; so too <s>Nahuṣa</s>, though lord of the gods (<s>Indra</s>), abandoning his own state, was transformed into an animal state. In this regard, for those in hell there is no <s>karmāśaya</s> to be experienced in this present life. And for those whose <s>kleśas</s> are exhausted, there is no <s>karmāśaya</s> to be experienced in a future unseen life.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
kimarthaṁ punaḥ kleśahānāya prayatata ityāha--yataḥ [kleśamūlaḥ karmāśayo dṛṣṭādṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaḥ ॥ kleśā] avidyādayo [mūlaṁ] janmakāraṇaṁ yasya karmāśayasya sa [kleśamūla: karmāśaya] iti । ākarmaphalapradānādantaḥkaraṇe śeta iti karmāśayaḥ śuklakṛṣṇātmakaḥ । dṛṣṭaṁ cādṛṣṭaṁ ca dṛṣṭādṛṣṭe janmanī tayorvedanīyamanubhavanīyaṁ phalaṁ yasya [sa dṛṣṭādṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaḥ karmāśayaḥ ।] yo dṛṣṭādṛṣṭakarmānubhavitavyaṁphalaḥ karmāśayaḥ sa kleśamūla iti sūtrārthaḥ ।
yasya puṇyāpuṇyarūpasya karmāśayasya yasmin janmani niṣpattistasya tasminneva janmani vedanīyaṁ phalaṁ sa dṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaḥ । yasya tu janmāntare vedanīyaṁ phalaṁ so'dṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaḥ karmāśaya iti ॥
bhāṣyamidānīṁ vyākhyāyate- [tatra puṇyāpuṇyakarmāśayo lobhakrodhamohaprabhava iti,] kleśamūlatvaṁ tasyācaṣṭe । puṇyakarmāśayo lobhaprabhavo yathā-svarge vā atra vā śubhaṁ phalamanubhaviṣyāmīti svargakāmaputrakāmayāgādiḥ । krodhaprabhavo yathāviśvāmitrasyāmbāyāśca । mohaprabhavo yathā-draupadyāḥ kumbhakarṇasya ca ॥
apuṇyakarmāśayo'pi lobhaprabhavo yathā---carmaṇi dvīpinaṁ hanti kuñjaraṁ hanti dantayoḥ । karṇasya cāsrajñānalobhādanṛtavacane ॥ krodhaprabhavo yathā-brahmahatyā । bhārate(bhāve)'pyaśvatthāmnaśca । mohaprabhavo yathā-saṁsāramocakādīnāṁ nahuṣasya ca ।
asmitāvidyayorlobhakrodhamohaiḥ pratyekaṁ sambandhaḥ । katham ? ahamadhikṣipto'smīti krudhyati । ahaṁ sukhamanubhaviṣyāmīti lubhyati । ahaṁ muhyāmīti muhmati ॥
avidyā'pi sarvatraiva viparītadarśanalakṣaṇā sambadhyate । nahyasātyāmavidyāyāmasmitādīnāṁ sambhavo'sti । rāgastu lobha eva । dveṣastu krodhaḥ । abhiniveśe vimoha evāntarbhavati ॥
yattu mohaḥ punaravidyeti, tadavivekasāmānyāduktam । lobhakrodhamohāstu parasparanirapekṣā dharmādharmotpatidvāram । tathā ca vakṣyati--lobhakrodhamohapūrvikā iti ॥
[sa dṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaśca] sa lobhakrodhamohaprabhavaḥ karmāśayo [dṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaśca adṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaśca ।]
kathaṁ punaḥ karmaṇāṁ svarūpanimittatulyatve kasyaciddṛṣṭajanmavedanayitvaṁ kasyacidadṛṣṭajanmavedanīyatvañcetyāha--- [yathā tīvrasaṁyogena] tīvrodyamena [mantratapassamādhibhi] ryathāprasiddharūpaistīvrasaṁvegānuṣṭhitai [rnirvartitaḥ, īśvaradevatāmaharṣimahānubhāvānāmārādhanādvā ।] īśvara uktaḥ, devatā adityādayaḥ, maharṣayo bhṛgvādayaḥ, mahānubhāvā dharmajñānaniratamatayaḥ, eta eva vā (tadeṣāṁ vā) । tīvratarā [rādhanapariniṣpannaḥ sadyaḥ paripacyate] sa tasminneva janmani । yathā nandīśvarakumārasya ॥
[tathā tīvrakleśena] lobhādiprakarṣeṇa [bhītavyādhitakṛpaṇeṣu visrambhopagateṣu mahānubhāveṣu vā tapasviṣu] jñānadharmeniratamatiṣu tapasviṣu [punaḥ punaḥ] ābhīkṣṇyena [kṛto'pakāra:, sa cāpi pāpakarmāśayaḥ sadya eva paripacyate] phalati । yathā nahuṣasya ॥
loke'pi kṣetrabījasaṁskāraviśeṣeṇa vṛkṣādiphalasannikarṣaḥ prasiddhaḥ vṛkṣāyurvedaprasiddhyā । tathā kriyāsu phalasannikarṣaviprakarṣadarśanaṁ gamipacyādiṣu tīvramandānuṣṭhānaviśeṣataḥ ।
tatra puṇyakarmāśayasyodāharaṇamāha--- [yathā nandīśvaraḥ kumāro manuṣyapariṇāmaṁ svakaṁ hitvā] maheśvarārādhanapariniṣpannena tīvratarakleśānuṣṭhānena janmanā [devatātvena pariṇataḥ ॥]
[tathā nahuṣo'] puṇyakarmāśayasyodāharaṇam । sa [devānāmindraḥ ।] sa [svakaṁ pariṇāmaṁ hitvā] tīvrataramohānuṣṭhānajena karmāśayena [tiryaktvena pariṇata iti ॥]
krodhādīnāṁ tu yathāsaṁkhyaṁ dṛṣṭādṛṣṭajanmavedanīyatvenodāharaṇāni vyākhyātāni pūrvameva । etena ca mandamandataralobhādikkeśānuṣṭhānajanmānau puṇyapāpakarmāśayāvadṛṣṭajanmavedanīyau vyākhyātau lokavadeva । tatrāpi tāvaducyate ॥
[tatra nārakāṇāṁ nāsti] -yairnarakaprāptyarthameva karmānuṣṭhitaṁ brahmahatyāgurudāragamanādilakṣaṇaṁ, teṣāṁ nārakāṇāṁ nārakatvasyāśubhāvitvamāśritya [teṣāṁ nārakāṇāṁ nāsti dṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaphalaḥ karmāśayaḥ] [yena phalaṁ] ā.ārabhyate ॥
kathaṁ punarnārakāṇāṁ karmārambhastiryagādīnāṁ devatānāṁ ca ? manuṣyāṇāṁ hi karmādhikāraḥ । eṣā ca karmabhūmirna narakādirityucyate---na-nahuṣārdanāṁ karmadarśanāt । śrūyate ca śatakratorapi vṛtrādivadhena brahmahatyāprāptiryogādyanuṣṭhānaśravaṇaṁ ca ॥
yanmanuṣyāṇāṁ karmādhikāra: iyaṁ ca karmabhūmiriti, tatkṣipraphalasiddhyapekṣam । taduktama- ['kṣipraṁ hi mānuṣe loke siddhirbhavati karmajā”] iti । vyāsena kīṭopākhyāna(śrava)smaraṇāca tiraśvāmipi karmopapattiḥ ॥
kiñca-dehendriyādimataḥ kriyopapatteḥ । kriyāṇāṁ ca kāyavāṅmanaḥprabhavānāṁ phalārambhakatvaṁ, kleśapūrvakavāt ॥
[kṣīṇakleśānāmapi] samyagdarśināmapi [nāstyadṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaḥ karmāśayaḥ] kleśābhāvādeva । na hi vītarāge jāto dṛśyate । kleśānāṁ kamīrambha iva karmaphalārambhe'pi hetutvāt । kṣīṇakleśasyāpi jñānaprāpteḥ prāgārabdho dṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaḥ sambhavati karmāśayaḥ pravṛttaphalatvānmuktaśaravaditi ॥ 12 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
Why then does one strive for the removal of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions)? To this he says — Because [the store of <s>karma</s> (<s>karmāśaya</s>), rooted in <s>kleśas</s>, is to be experienced in seen and unseen births.] The <s>kleśas</s> — <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and the rest — are the [root], i.e. the cause of birth, of the store of <s>karma</s>; hence it is called [the <s>karmāśaya</s> rooted in <s>kleśas</s>]. Because it rests (<s>śete</s>) within the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) until the delivery of the fruit of action, it is called <s>karmāśaya</s> (store of <s>karma</s>), consisting of white and black. The seen and the unseen are the two births — seen and unseen; that whose fruit (<s>phala</s>) is to be experienced in those two births [is the <s>karmāśaya</s> to be experienced in seen and unseen births.] That which is to be experienced in the seen birth,

body.text: sati mūle tadvipāko jātyāyurbhogāḥ ॥ 13 ॥
body.translated_text: When the root exists, the fruition of that is birth, lifespan, and experience. || 13 ||

body.text: satsu kleśeṣu karmāśayo vipākārambhī bhavati nocchinnakleśamūlaḥ। yathā tuṣāvanaddhāḥ śālitaṇḍulā adagdhabījabhāvāḥ prarohasamarthā bhavanti nāpanītatuṣā dagdhabījabhāvā vā, tathā kleśāvanaddhaḥ karmāśayo vipākaprarohī bhavati nāpanītakleśo na prasaṁkhyānadagdhakleśabījabhāvo veti। sa ca vipākastrividho jātirāyurbhoga iti।
body.translated_text: When the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) exist, the store of <s>karma</s> (<s>karmāśaya</s>) begins to fructify, but not when its root in <s>kleśas</s> has been severed. Just as rice grains enclosed in husks, with their seed-nature unburnt, are capable of sprouting, but not when the husks are removed or the seed-nature is burnt — so too the store of <s>karma</s>, enveloped by <s>kleśas</s>, is capable of sprouting into fruition, but not when the <s>kleśas</s> are removed or the seed-nature of the <s>kleśas</s> is burnt by <s>prasaṁkhyāna</s> (discriminative meditation). And that fruition is threefold: birth (<s>jāti</s>), lifespan (<s>āyus</s>), and experience (<s>bhoga</s>).

body.text:
vivaraṇam
kiśva- [sati mūle tadvipāko jātyāyubhoṁgāḥ । mūlaṁ hi] karmaṇāṁ kleśaḥ । asmin [sati mūle] kleśeṣu satsvityarthaḥ । [tasya] lobhakrodhaprabhavasya puṇyāpuṇyakarmāśayasya [vipākaḥ] phalaniṣpattiḥ [tadvipākaḥ ।] kiṁ punastatphalamityāha-- [jātyāyubhoṁgāḥ ॥]
bhāṣyaṁ [“satsu kleśeṣu karmāśayo vipākārambhī bhavati nocchinnakleśamūla”] iti, mūlasya vyākhyānam । tatra satsu kleśeṣu karmaśayo vipākārambhītyisya dṛṣṭāntamāha- [yathā tuṣāvanaddhāḥ śālitaṇḍulā adagdhabījabhāvāḥ ॥]
tuṣāvanaddhā api kadāciddagdhabījabhāvā na prarohasamarthā bhavanti । adagdhabījabhāvā api vyapanītatuṣā na prarohāyālaṁ bhavanti । ubhayathā ca dārṣṭāntikapratipādanārthaṁ dṛṣṭhāntavikalpa: ॥
katham ? [tathā kleśāvanaddhaḥ karmāśayo vipākaprarohī bhavati] kleśopabandhaḥ tuṣāvanaddhaśālitaṇḍulavat । [nāpanītakleśo] [na prasaṁkhyāna] [dagdhakleśabījabhāvo veti ।] apanītatuṣaśālitaṇḍulavadapanītakleśo na vipākaprarohī ॥
yogāṅgānuṣṭhānakleśakṣayapūrvasamyagdarśanānāṁ yogināma[na]panītakleśo'pya [na] panītatuṣadagdhabījaśaktiśālivadyogāṅgānuṣṭhānapraṇālikevalasamyagdarśanānaladagdhabījasāmarthyo na vipākaprarohī bhavati ॥
tathā ca vyāsaḥ sāṁkhyānāṁ yogināṁ ca pṛthaṅmokṣaṁ darśayati ॥
[“bījānyagnyupadagdhāni na rohanti yathā punaḥ ।]
[jñānadagdhaistathā leśainātmā sampadyate punaḥ ॥ ”] iti ॥
tathā [“yogaiśvaryamatikrānto yogī mucyeta”] ityādi । vakṣyati cātrāpi prāptāprāptaiśvaryayogayoḥ kaivalyam ॥
katiprakāro'sau vipāka ityāha- [sa ca vipākastrividhaḥ jātirāyurbhoga] iti ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
And moreover — ['When the root exists, the fruition of that is birth, lifespan, and experience. For the root'] of <s>karmas</s> is the <s>kleśa</s>. ['When this root exists'] — meaning, when the <s>kleśas</s> exist. ['Of that'] — of the store of meritorious and demeritorious <s>karma</s> born of greed and anger — ['the fruition'] — the accomplishment of the fruit — is ['that fruition.'] What then is that fruit? He says — ['Birth, lifespan, and experience.']
The <s>bhāṣya</s> ['When the <s>kleśas</s> exist, the store of <s>karma</s> begins to fructify, but not when its root in <s>kleśas</s> has been severed'] — this is the explanation of the root. Therein, when the <s>kleśas</s> exist, the store of <s>karma</s>

body.text: tatredaṁ vicāryate – kimekaṁ karmaikasya janmanaḥ kāraṇamathaikaṁ karmānekaṁ janmā''kṣipatīti। dvitīyā vicāraṇā – kimanekaṁ karmānekaṁ janma nirvartayati athānekaṁ karmaikaṁ janma nirvartayatīti। na tāvadekaṁ karmaikasya janmanaḥ kāraṇam। kasmāt, anādikālapracitasyāsaṁkhyeyasyāvaśiṣṭasya karmaṇaḥ sāṁpratikasya ca phalakramāniyamādanāśvāso lokasya prasaktaḥ, sa cāniṣṭa iti। na caikaṁ karmānekasya janmanaḥ kāraṇam। kasmāt, anekeṣu karmasu ekaikameva karmānekasya janmanaḥ kāraṇamityavaśiṣṭasya vipākakālābhāvaḥ prasaktaḥ, sa cāpyaniṣṭa iti। na cānekaṁ karmānekasya janmanaḥ kāraṇam। kasmāt, tadanekaṁ janma yugapanna saṁbhavatīti krameṇaiva vācyam। tathā ca pūrvadoṣānuṣaṅgaḥ।
body.translated_text: Here the following is examined — Does a single <s>karma</s> cause a single birth, or does a single <s>karma</s> project multiple births? The second inquiry is — Do multiple <s>karmas</s> produce multiple births, or do multiple <s>karmas</s> produce a single birth? First, a single <s>karma</s> is not the cause of a single birth. Why? Because if the innumerable <s>karma</s> accumulated since beginningless time, both remaining and current, had no fixed order of fruition, there would be no assurance for the world, and that is undesirable. Nor does a single <s>karma</s> cause multiple births,

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tatredaṁ vicāryate ।] kiṁ punarvicāraphalam ? ucyate-ekaikena prāṇinā viruddhaphalāni bhūyiṣṭhānyekasminneva janmani karmaṇi kriyante । tadyathā –
[śarīrajaiḥ karmadoṣairyāti sthāvaratāṁ naraḥ ।]
[vācikaiḥ pakṣimṛgatāṁ mānasairantyajātitām ॥ “]
svargārthāni ca tāvadanutiṣṭhati । narakaprāpīṇi ca karmāṇi । tatraikasya brahmahatyādikarmaṇo'nekajanmakārakatvaṁ śrūyate [śvasūkarakharoṭrāṇāmi] tyādasmṛteḥ ॥
tatra viruddhadeśakālanimittavipākānāṁ karmaṇāmekajanmārambhe viruddhavipākatādarthyaṁ hīyeta । tataśca tādarthyacodanāḥ karmeṇāṁ bādhyeran ॥
atha paryoyeṇa janmārambhitvaṁ, karmaṇāmasaṁkhyeyatvāt kenacideva phalamārabdhaṁ nānyairiti, tatra niyamānupapattiḥ, kenārabdhaḥ kena vā neti । tathā । ca kartṝṇāṁ karmaphalaṁ pratya(pya)visrambhādutsāhavibhaṅgaḥ syāt abhyudayāniśreyasapravṛttiṣu ॥
athānyatamenārambhe vināśa evānyeṣāmiti, tathā'pi sa eva doṣaḥ, kiṁ vinaṣṭa kimārambhakamityaniyamāt ॥
athāvināśa eva, tathāpyavaśiṣṭasyārambhakālābhāvo mokṣābhāvaśveti । tasmātpravṛttinivṛttiśāstrārthavatvapratipādanārthamidaṁ vicāryate ॥
[kimekaṁ karma ekasya janmanaḥ kāraṇaṁ] svargādiprāptinimitteṣu bahuṣu karmasu satsu । [athaikaṁ karmānekaṁ janmākṣipatī] ti prathama vicāraṇā । viruddhapakṣadvayālambinī hi vicāraṇā ekaiva syāt ॥
[dvitīyā vicāraṇā - kimanekaṁ karmānekaṁ janma nirvartayati] viruddhaphalamaviruddhaphalaṁ vā । [athānekaṁ karmaikaṁ janma nirvartayati] viruddhaphalamaviruddhaphalaṁ vā ॥
kiñcāta: ? [na tāvadekaṁ karmaikasya janmanaḥ kāraṇam । kasmāt?] bahuṣu karmasu satsvekameva karma janmaikaṁ nārabhata iti ॥
yadyekasyaiva janmārambhitvaṁ, tadā [anādikālapracitasya] saṁsārānāditvādekaikena puruṣeṇāsaṁkhyeyamekaikasmin janmani karma pracīyate viruddhaphalamaviruddhaphalaṁ ca ॥
tatra [avaśiṣṭasya] janmārambhikarmavyatiriktasya [asaṅkhyeyasya] anekajanbhāntarapracitasya [karmaṇaḥ] karmakalāpasya [sāmpratasya ca] vartamānajanmapracitasyānārabdhakāryasya [phalakramāniyamāt] kiṁ pūrvajanmepacitakarmarāśigatasya kasyacideva bhaviṣyajjanmārambhitvam, āhotvididānīntanajanmakarmarāśigatasya kasyaciditi phalakramo na niyamyeteti [anāścāso lokasya ॥]
kiṁ pūrvajanmakarmaṇā duṣṭenāduṣṭena vā phalamārabdhavyam ? athedānāntanakarmaṇā duṣṭenāduṣṭena vā? ityavisrambhāt na kaścidagnihotrādi kurvīta । nāpi mokṣāya samīhetetyanāścāsaḥ [prasaktaḥ, sa cāgniṣṭaḥ ॥]
idānīṁ prathamavicāraṇāyāṁ dvitīyaṁ pakṣaṁ nirākaroti- [na caikaṁ karmānekasya janmanaḥ kāraṇam । kasmāt ?] ekaikasmiṁstāvajanmāna [anekaṁ karmā] nuṣṭhīyate, [tatraikaikameva cetkarmānekasya janmavipākasya] janmapariṇāmasya [nimittaṁ bhavet , tato'vaśiṣṭasya] ārabdhakāryādanyasya [vipākakālābhāvaḥ] prasaktaḥ, [sa cāpyaniṣṭaḥ ।] phalakramāniyamaśceti pūrvadoṣo'pi । naivaṁbhūtamaniṣṭamabhyupagantavyam । yattu brahmahatyādikarmaṇāmekaikasyānekajanmārambhitvaṁ, tasya śāstragocaratvāt brahmahatyādiviṣayatvamevābhyupagamyate ॥
dvitīyavicāraṇāyāmidānīṁ prathamaḥ pakṣo nirākriyate – [na cānekaṁ karmānekasya janmanaḥ kāraṇam । kasmā] devaṁ nābhyupagamyate? taducyate, [tadevānekaṁ janma yugapanna sambhavati] ekasyānīśvarasya । tataśca [krameṇa vācyamāne] kimekamanekaṁ janmārabhata iti । [tathā ca pūrvadoṣānuṣaṅgaḥ] sarvatra prathamadoṣānuṣaṅgaḥ phalakramāniyamādanāśvāsa iti ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['Here the following is examined.'] What then is the result of the inquiry? It is said — each individual living being performs in a single lifetime many actions with contradictory results. For example —
'Through bodily transgressions, a person attains the state of a plant;
through verbal transgressions, the state of a bird or animal; through mental transgressions, the state of an outcaste.'
And one performs actions aimed at heaven, and also actions leading to hell. Among these, it is heard that a single action such as killing a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (<s>brahmahatyā</s>) produces multiple births — in the bodies of dogs, pigs, donkeys, and camels,

body.text: tasmājjanmaprāyaṇāntare kṛtaḥ puṇyāpuṇyakarmāśayapracayo vicitraḥ pradhānopasarjanabhāvenāvasthitaḥ prāyaṇābhivyakta ekapraghaṭṭakena maraṇaṁ prasādhya saṁmūrchita ekameva janma karoti। tacca janma tenaiva karmaṇā labdhāyuṣkaṁ bhavati। tasminnāyuṣi tenaiva karmaṇā bhogaḥ saṁpadyata iti। asau karmāśayo janmāyurbhogahetutvāttrivipāko'bhidhīyata iti। ata ekabhavikaḥ karmāśaya ukta iti।
body.translated_text: Therefore, the accumulated store of meritorious and demeritorious <s>karma</s> (<s>karmāśaya</s>) created between birth and death, being diverse, arranged in a hierarchy of principal and subordinate, becoming manifest at the time of death, accomplishing death in a single impetus, and coalescing, produces a single birth. And that birth, by virtue of that very <s>karma</s>, has a determined lifespan. Within that lifespan, experience (<s>bhoga</s>) is accomplished by that very <s>karma</s>. Since this store of <s>karma</s> is the cause of birth, lifespan, and experience, it is said to have a threefold fruition. Therefore, the <s>karmāśaya</s> is said to be 'pertaining to a single existence' (<s>ekabhavika</s>).

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tasmāt] evaṁ pakṣatrayānupapattāvidānī siddhāntamupasaṁharati-— [janmaprāyaṇāntare] janmamaraṇayorantare madhye kṛtaḥ [puṇyapāpakarmāśayaḥ] aviruddhajanmadeśanimitta iti vākyaśeṣaḥ । viruddhajanmadeśanimittaḥ punaḥ adṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaḥ apratiniyatavipākaḥ । tasya tridhā viniyogaṁ vakṣyati । tasmādaviruddhaphalasyaiva puṇyāpuṇyakarmāśayasyāyaṁ niyama ucyate ॥
[pracayavicitraḥ] tulyātulyānekakarmapracitatvā [tpracayena vicitraḥ । pradhānopasarjanabhāvenāvasthitaḥ] kiñcitkarma kasyacitkarmaṇaḥ pradhānamapi kasya cidanyasyopasarjanamupasarjanamapi pradhānamityevamanekakarmaśabalimnā'vasthitaḥ ॥
[prāyaṇābhivyaktaḥ] yathā bījakṣetrasaṁskārasaṁyogo'ṅkurabhāvābhivyaktikāraṇaṁ, tathā prāyaṇamapyaviruddhānāṁ karmaṇāmabhivyaktinimittam । [ekapraghadṛkena] ekalolībhāvena [samuccitaḥ] ekībhūtaḥ [ekameva janma karoti ॥]
[tacca janma tenaiva] prāyaṇābhivyaktātmanā [karmaṇā labdhāyuṣkaṁ bhavati । tasminnāyuṣi tenaiva karmaṇā bhogaḥ sampadyate,] yena janmāyuṣī kṛte । yathā yena bījenāṅkuro nirvṛttastenaiva phalapuṣpādayo'pi ॥
tena ca karmaṇā bhogāyurnivṛttirbhavatyeyavetyavadhāryate । na punaranyasyāyurbhegādinimitasya putrapaśukāmādiyāgādeḥ putrāyurādiprāterhetutvaṁ nirākriyate । itarathā hi sarvaśrutismṛtiviprakopaḥ syāt । tasmā [ttenaiva karmaṇeti] janmamātramārabhya kṛtakāryatvādvinivṛttyāśaṅkaniṣedhamātraṁ kriyate ॥
[asau karmāśayo janmāyurbhogahetutvāt] trayo vipākā janmādayo yasya sa [trivipāko'bhidhīyate । ayamaikabhavikaḥ karmāśaya uktaḥ] eka (eva) janmaprayojana ekabhavikaḥ ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['Therefore'] — since the three alternative views are untenable, he now presents the established conclusion — ['Between birth and death (<s>janma-prāyaṇāntare</s>)'] — in the interval between birth and death, the accumulated ['store of meritorious and demeritorious <s>karma</s>'] — the remainder of the sentence being: 'having non-contradictory birth, place, and cause.' The store of <s>karma</s> with contradictory birth, place, and cause, however, is to be experienced in an unseen birth, and its fruition is undetermined. Its threefold application will be stated. Therefore, this rule applies only to the store of meritorious and demeritorious <s>karma</s> with non-contradictory fruits.
['Diverse in accumulation (<s>pracaya-vicitra</s>)'] — equal and unequal,

body.text: dṛṣṭajanmavedanīyastvekavipākārambhī bhogahetutvāddvivipākārambhī vā āyurbhogahetutvāt nandīśvaravannadvuṣavadveti। kleśakarmavipākānubhavanirvartitābhistu vāsanābhiranādikālasaṁmūrchitamidaṁ cittaṁ vicitrīkṛtamiva sarvato matsyajālaṁ granthibhirivā''tatamityetā anekabhavapūrvikā vāsanāḥ। yastvayaṁ karmāśaya eṣa evaikabhavika ukta iti। ye saṁskārāḥ smṛtihetavastā vāsanāstāścānādikālīnā iti।
body.translated_text: The <s>karma</s> to be experienced in the present birth initiates either a single fruition, being the cause of experience alone; or a twofold fruition, being the cause of both lifespan and experience — like <s>Nandīśvara</s> or like <s>Nahuṣa</s>. But through <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions) produced by the experience of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), <s>karma</s>, and their fruition, this <s>citta</s> (mind), saturated since beginningless time, is rendered variegated like a fishing net stretched out with knots everywhere — these <s>vāsanās</s> pertain to multiple existences. But the <s>karmāśaya</s> described here is said to pertain to a single existence only. And the <s>saṁskāras</s> (impressions) that are the causes of memory are <s>vāsanās</s>, and those are beginningless.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[dṛṣṭajanmavedanīyastvekavipākārambhī] yathā – putrāgrāmādikāmayāgaḥ । [dvivipākārambhī] vā [bhogāyurhetutvāt ।] yathā āyurādikāmayāgaḥ । [trivipākārambhī vā nandīśvaranahuṣavat ॥]
nanu ca nandīśvaranahuṣayordṛṣṭajanmavedanīyatvaṁ trivipākāsmbhitvaṁ ca viruddham । dṛṣṭaṁ hi janma nandīśvarasya manuṣyatvam । yatpunarnandīśvarasya devatvaṁ, nahuṣasya cājagaratvaṁ tat dvayamapyadṛṣṭaṁ, na hi manuṣyatva eva devatvaṁ saṁvedyaṁ nandīśvarasya, nāpi devatva eva nahuṣasyājagarasvaṁ sevadyamiti, kathaṁ trivipākārambhitvaṁ dṛṣṭajanmavedanīyatvaṁ ceti ॥
naiṣa doṣaḥ । dṛśyamānajātiviśiṣṭameva śarīraṁ tayorjātyantaratvena pariṇatam । na ca yathā'nyeṣāṁ dṛṣṭajātiviśiṣṭaśarīropamardena jātyantaropādānaniṣekādinimittāpekṣayā jātyantaraprāptiḥ, tathā nandīścaranahuṣayoḥ । tasmāt trivipākārambhitvaṁ dṛṣṭajanmavedanīyatvaṁ cetyudāhṛtam ॥
tatra trividhaḥ karmarāśirdṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaścādṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaśca । dṛṣṭajanmavedanīyatavipākaniyatavipāraḥ kadācidbhogaheturityekavipākaḥ । kadācidbhogāyurhetutvāt dvivipākaḥ । kadācit jātyāyurbhegahetutvāt trivipāko nandīśvaranahuṣayoriva ॥ ।
adṛṣṭajanmavedanīyastu dvividho niyatavipākaścāniyatavipākaśca । niyatavipākastu pradarśitaḥ [tasmājjanmaprāyaṇāntare kṛta] ityādinā । yastvaniyatavipākaḥ sa trividho vakṣyate ॥
idānīṁ tu karmavipākajanito vāsanārāśirapara ākhyāyate – [kleśakarmavipākānubhavanirvartitābhaiḥ] kleśānubhavaśca karmānubhavaśca vipākānubhavaśca kleśakarmavipākānubhavāḥ, tairnirvartitābhiḥ [vāsanābhiḥ] saṁskaraiḥ [anādikālasaṁmūrchitamidaṁ cittaṁ citrīkṛtamiva] paṭakuḍyādivat [sarvato matsyajālaṁ granthibhirivātataṁ] vyāptam ॥
athaikaikasmin janmāni [anekabhavapūrvakā vāsanāḥ] karmaṇi vipāke ca tadaṅgībhāvena vyāpriyante । na hi vāsanāyāḥ karmavipākānajñabhāve sati jātamātrasya pṛṣadaṁśadārakasya vṛṣabuvānaṁ prati sphuritaparikopasyāvaskandanaṁ jāghaṭīti । na ca sakṛdanubhavavāsanāmāttratayā tena śakyaṁ bhavitum ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['The <s>karma</s> to be experienced in the present birth initiates a single fruition'] — for example, a sacrifice performed with the desire for a son, village, and the like. ['Or a twofold fruition'] ['being the cause of experience and lifespan.'] For example, a sacrifice performed with the desire for longevity and the like. ['Or a threefold fruition, like <s>Nandīśvara</s> and <s>Nahuṣa</s>.']
But the assertion that the <s>karmas</s> of <s>Nandīśvara</s> and <s>Nahuṣa</s> are both to be experienced in the present birth and have threefold fruition is contradictory. For the seen birth of <s>Nandīśvara</s> is his human state. But <s>Nandīśvara</s>'s attainment of divinity and <s>Nahuṣa</s>'s becoming a serpent — both of these are unseen, for

body.text: yastvasāvekabhavikaḥ karmāśayaḥ sa niyatavipākaścāniyatavipākaśca। tatra dṛṣṭajanmavedanīyasya niyatavipākasyaivāyaṁ niyamo na tvadṛṣṭajanmavedanīyasyāniyatavipākasya। kasmāt। yo hyadṛṣṭajanmavedanīyo'niyatavipākastasya trayī gatiḥ – kṛtasyāvipakvasya nāśaḥ, pradhānakarmaṇyāvāpagamanaṁ vā, niyatavipākapradhānakarmaṇā'bhibhūtasya vā ciramavasthānamiti।
body.translated_text: But the store of <s>karma</s> pertaining to a single existence (<s>ekabhavika</s>) is either of determined fruition (<s>niyata-vipāka</s>) or of undetermined fruition (<s>aniyata-vipāka</s>). Among these, this rule applies only to that which is to be experienced in the present birth and has determined fruition, not to that which is to be experienced in an unseen birth and has undetermined fruition. Why? Because the <s>karma</s> to be experienced in an unseen birth with undetermined fruition has three possible destinies — destruction without having ripened, merging into the principal <s>karma</s>, or remaining for a long time while being overpowered by the principal <s>karma</s> of determined fruition.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[yastvayaṁ karmāśayaḥ] yastvayaṁ janmaprāyaṇāntare kṛto'viruddhajanmadeśanimittaḥ pradhānopasarjanībhāvena trivipākārambhī [eṣa evaikabhavika uktaḥ ।] na dṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaḥ, nāpyaniyatavipaktiradṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaḥ, nāpi ca vāsanāḥ ॥
tāsāṁ tāvat svarūpamāha – [ye saṁskārāḥ smṛtihetavastā vāsanāstāścānādikālīnāḥ,] saṁsārasya kleśararmavipākānubhavarūpasyānāditvātū ॥
[yastvasāvekabhavikaḥ karmāśayaḥ] pūrvottastasyāpavāda ucyate ekadeśasya । kathaṁ ? [sa niyatavipākaścāniyatavipākaśca ।] ko'sau niyatavipākaḥ ? yaḥ prāyaṇābhivyaktaḥ kāryamārabhate । sa eva caikabhavikaḥ ॥
yastu viruddhajanmadeśakālanimittaḥ so'dṛṣṭajanmavedanīyatvasāmānye satyapyaniyatavipākaḥ । kasmāt? niyatavipākena virodhāt । nacāyamekabhavikaḥ, virodhādeva । yatvasyaikabhavikatvamuktaṁ, [yastvasāvekabhavika: karmāśaya] iti, tadadṛṣṭajanmavedanīyatvasāmānyena ॥
nanu ca yadyevaṁ [janmaprāyaṇāntare kṛtaḥ puṇyapāpakarmāśayaḥ pracayavicitraḥ pradhānopasarjanabhāvenāvasthitaḥ prāyaṇābhivyaktaḥ ekapraghaṭṭena sammūrchita ekajanma karotī] tyevamādirniyamo virudhyeta । kutaḥ ? prāyaṇasya sarvapūrvakarmābhivyañjakatvāt, āśayādhāropamardena cāśayāntarotpatteḥ, mānuṣyakāśayādhāre pūrvaṁ daivatairyagyonāśayānāṁ samavatthānaṁ, tadādhāropamardanakāle ca prāyaṇe sādhāraṇe sarvakarmabhivyaktikāraṇe daivatairyagyonāśayānāṁ kasyacidevābhivyaktirnetareṣāmiti nāsti hetuḥ । na hi svagecarāpannaṁ vyaṅgyamekadeśaparityāgenābhivyanakti pradīpaḥ ॥
atrecyate – naitadyuktaṁ, karmānarthakyaprasaṅgāt । bahuprakārāṇi hi karmaṇi parasparaviruddhāni kriyante । yo hi svargārtha karma kṛtavān sa eva paśugrāmādyarthaṁ karmānuṣṭhāya punarbahmahatyāṁ vā sthāvarādiprāptyarthaṁ vā balavakarmānutiṣṭhet । tatra narakasyāvarādiprāptasya na hi paśugrāmādilābhasaṁbhavaḥ । tataśca tatkarmaṇāmānarthakyaṁ prasajyeta ॥
atha tatrāpi grāmādilābhasukhaṁ bhavatīti cet – na hi grāmakāma ityukte grāmasukhatvamabhipretam । na hi grāmasukhaṁ prāpto grāmaṁ prāptavān ॥
kiñca – sarvaśāstraviprakopaśca syāt । adṛṣṭānāṁ ca svarganarakādīnāṁ sukhaduḥkhamātraprasaṅgaḥ । [‘tataḥ śeṣeṇa'] iti śeṣasadbhāvajñāpanaśrutismṛtayo bādhyeran । tasmānna sarvaṁ karma prāyaṇe'bhivyajyate । atyantaviruddhānāṁ karmaṇāmānarthakyaprāpteḥ । karmaśākhānarthakye ca mokṣaśāstre'pyanāśvāsaprasaṅgaḥ ॥
abhivyañjakānāmapi kasyacidabhivyañjakatvaṁ kasyacinneti dṛśyate vyabhicāraḥ । yathā cakṣuṣo rūpābhivyañjakatve'pi caitroळ.ūkacakṣuṣorahorātrayoritaretaravyabhicāraḥ । ālokasya ca samāne sarvacakṣussahakāritve, nolūkacakṣussahakāritvam । ekasmiśva stryādipiṇḍe sukhaduḥkhamehānāṁ sarveṣāmabhivyaktinimitte'pi kasyacidevābhivyaktiḥ ॥
tatra karmādyapekṣayā virodhādadoṣa iti cet – ihāpi virodhādanabhavyaktiḥ sarvakarmaṇām । na cāpi bījādhāre kṣetre upamardyamāne jalādinimittasaṁyoge satyapi tadgatānāṁ bījānāṁ viruddhajātīyānāmaṅkurādikāryārambhitvam । evaṁ mānuṣyakālīnāśayādhāre'pyupamardyamāne, na viruddhajātīyadevatairyagyonāśayānāṁ sarveṣāṁ yugapadvṛttilābhaḥ ॥
na ca prāyaṇameva karmaṇāmabhivyañjakam । dṛṣṭajanmavedanīyānāṁ bhogārthānāṁ darśanāt । yeṣāṁ prāyaṇamevābhivyañjakaṁ teṣāṁ sarveṣāṁ bhavatvabhivyaktiriti cet – na – virodhāddaivatairyagyonamānuṣyakāśyānām ॥
prāyaṇānāṁ ca bhūtabhaviṣyatkālaviśeṣervi(ṣāvi)śeṣopapatterna sarvakarmābhivyañjakatvam । prāyaṇaviśeṣaśravaṇācca prāyaṇabhedaḥ yathā – [‘yaṁ yaṁ vāpi smaranbhāvaṁ tyajatyante kaळ.ebaram’] iti smaraṇaviśeṣabhedāt prāyaṇabhedaḥ । tasmānna sarvakarmabhivyañjakatvaṁ prāyaṇasya । anyathā viśeṣaṇānarthakyaprasaṅgāt ॥
na ca smaraṇādiviśeṣaṇena prakṛtasyānyathātvaṁ nāśo vā syāt । tannāśanyathātvakaraṇe hi smaraṇasya prakṛtakarmasahakāritvaṁ na syāt । svatantraṁ hi smaraṇaṁ syāt । tathā cānuṣṭhitakarmanairarthakyaṁ bhavet ॥
kiñca – kalalādyavasthāsu mṛtānāṁ mokṣaprasaṅgaḥ । karmārambhāt । tāsāṁ phalatravatkarmatvamapīti cet – na – karaṇāvyūhāt । karaṇeṣu hi vyūhiteṣu karmaṇāṁ vṛttilābhaḥ phalatvaṁ ca । na tadā tadvyūha upapadyate ॥
svapnavaditi cenna । tatrāpi karmānabhyupagamāt । śrutiśca [‘sa yattatra kiñcitpaśyatyananvāyatastena bhavati’] iti karmaṇā svapnadarśanajenāsambandhaṁ darśayati । na kaścitsvapnairaparādhavānasti । brahmahatyādikaraṇadarśanāt । atha skannaprāyaścittādidarśanānneti cenna, retasskandananimittatvātprāyaścittasya ॥
tasamādyadyapi svapnādyavasthāyāmiva kalalādyavasthāsu phalamabhyupagamyate, tathā'pi karaṇavyāpārābhāvāt svapnanāvasthāvadeva phalamātraṁ tat, na karmakartṛtvamiti mokṣaprasaṅga eva garbhaprasṛtānāmapatita iti ॥
tasmānna sarvakarmābhivyañjakatvaṁ prāyaṇānāṁ, teṣāṁ ca viśeṣopapatterityata idamucyate-- [tatrādṛṣṭajanmavedanīyasya niyatavipākasyaivāyaṁ niyamo] yo'sau [‘janmaprāyaṇāntare kṛta'] ityevamādibhāṣyeṇa trivipākārambhitvaniyama uktaḥ, [na tu addaṣṭajanmavedanīyasya aniyatavipākasya । kasmāt ? yastvadṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaḥ aniyatavipākastasya trayī gatiḥ ॥]
katham ? [kṛtasyāvipakasya vināśaḥ] nāśakālamaprāptasyaiva nāśa: । yathā---prāyāścittādinā pratiṣiddhasya kṛtasya nāśaḥ ॥
[pradhānakarmaṇyāvāpagamanaṁ] pradhānakarmaṇi niyatavedanīye ācāpāpāte: pradhānakarmaphalātiraskareṇa svayamapi mandamandaṁ phalaṁ madhyamanupraviśya prayacchati । yathā – sakaleṣu taṇḍuleṣu vipacyamānaṣu asakalā api taṇḍulakaṇā uptā alpīyāṁsamartha sādhayantyeva । [niyatavipākapradhānakarmābhibhūtasya vā'pyavasthānaṁ] niyatavipākaṁ yatpradhānakarma prārabdhaphalaṁ tenābhibhūtasya nyakkṛtasya viruddhadeśakālanimittavipākatvādavasthānamū । yathā-vijigīṣamāṇayorantareṇa pravṛttarājyenābhibhūtasyetarasyāvasthānaṁ deśakālanimittāpekṣayā ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['Now this store of <s>karma</s> (<s>karmāśaya</s>)'] — this store of <s>karma</s> performed in the interval between birth and death, having non-conflicting birth, place, and occasion, beginning the threefold fruition through the relation of principal and subordinate — ['this alone has been called <s>ekabhavika</s> (operative in a single lifetime).'] It is not that which is to be experienced in the seen birth (<s>dṛṣṭajanmavedanīya</s>), nor is it the <s>adṛṣṭajanmavedanīya</s> (to be experienced in unseen births) with indeterminate fruition (<s>aniyatavipāka</s>), nor are they <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions).
Regarding those [<s>vāsanās</s>], he first states their nature — ['Those <s>saṁskāras</s> (impressions) that are the cause of memory are <s>vāsanās</s>, and they are from beginningless time,'] because <s>saṁsāra</s> — whose nature is the experience of afflictions, <s>karma</s>, and fruition — is beginningless.
['Now this <s>ekabhavika</s> store of <s>karma</s>'] — of the previously stated [<s>karmāśaya</s>], a partial exception is stated. How? ['It is both of determinate fruition (<s>niyatavipāka</s>) and of indeterminate fruition (<s>aniyatavipāka</s>).'] What is this <s>niyatavipāka</s>? That which, manifested at the time of death (<s>prāyaṇa</s>), begins its effect. That alone is <s>ekabhavika</s>.
But that which has conflicting birth, place, time, and occasion — though sharing the general character of being <s>adṛṣṭajanmavedanīya</s> — is of indeterminate fruition (<s>aniyatavipāka</s>). Why? Because of conflict with the <s>niyatavipāka</s> (determinate fruition). And this is not <s>ekabhavika</s>, precisely because of that conflict. As for the statement that it is <s>ekabhavika</s> — ['Now this <s>ekabhavika</s> store of <s>karma</s>'] — that is by virtue of its sharing the general character of being <s>adṛṣṭajanmavedanīya</s>.
Now, if this is so, [the objection arises that] the rule — ['The store of meritorious and demeritorious <s>karma</s> performed in the interval between birth and death, varied in accumulation, arranged in the relation of principal and subordinate, manifested at death, coalescing in a single mass, produces a single birth'] — and so forth would be contradicted. Why? Because death (<s>prāyaṇa</s>) would manifest all prior <s>karmas</s>; because upon the destruction of the substratum of the [current] store, another store would arise; because in a human substratum, the stores belonging to divine and animal births would subsist from before; and because at the time of destruction of that substratum — at death, which is a common cause of manifestation for all <s>karmas</s> — there is no reason why only some particular store belonging to divine or animal births should manifest and not the others. For a lamp, when it encounters its object of illumination within its range, does not illuminate by abandoning one part.
To this it is replied — This is not correct, because it would lead to the futility of <s>karma</s>. For <s>karmas</s> of many kinds, mutually conflicting, are performed. One who has performed <s>karma</s> for heaven may also perform <s>karma</s> for the sake of cattle and villages, and then again perform powerful <s>karma</s> such as <s>brahmahatyā</s> (killing a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>) or for attaining the condition of a plant and the like. In that case, for one who has attained hell or the condition of a plant, there is no possibility of gaining cattle, villages, and so forth. Thus, the futility of those <s>karmas</s> would follow.
If it be said that even there one obtains the pleasure of villages and the like — [we reply:] when it is said 'one desiring a village,' what is intended is not the mere pleasure of a village. One who has obtained the pleasure of a village has not [thereby] obtained the village itself.
Moreover, there would be conflict with all <s>śāstras</s> (scriptures). And for the unseen [fruits] such as heaven and hell, there would be the unwanted consequence that they amount to mere pleasure and pain [in any birth]. The <s>śrutis</s> and <s>smṛtis</s> that declare the existence of a remainder, such as ['then with the remainder'], would be contradicted. Therefore, not all <s>karma</s> is manifested at death, because of the futility that would befall extremely conflicting <s>karmas</s>. And if the <s>karma</s> branch of scripture were rendered purposeless, there would be the consequence of no confidence even in the scripture teaching <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation).
Furthermore, even among manifesting agents, the deviation is observed that some manifest certain things while others do not. Just as, although the eye manifests form, there is a reciprocal deviation between the eye of <s>Caitra</s> and that of an owl with respect to day and night — and although light equally assists all eyes, it does not assist the owl's eye — and although for a single object such as a woman, the occasion for manifestation of pleasure, pain, and delusion exists for all, only some particular [reaction] manifests.
If it be said that there is no fault because of conflict dependent on <s>karma</s> and the like — here too, because of conflict, not all <s>karmas</s> manifest. Nor, when the field that is the substratum of seeds is being destroyed, even though the conditions of water and the like are present, do the seeds therein that belong to conflicting species begin to produce sprouts and other effects. Similarly, even when the substratum of stores accumulated in the human [birth] is being destroyed, not all the stores belonging to conflicting species — divine and animal births — simultaneously gain activity.
Nor is death alone the manifesting cause of <s>karmas</s>, since <s>karmas</s> to be experienced in the seen birth, whose purpose is enjoyment, are observed. If it be said that for those whose manifesting cause is death alone, let all of them manifest — [we reply:] no, because of the mutual conflict among stores belonging to divine, animal, and human births.
And because death at different past and future times admits of both particular and general application, it is not the manifesting agent of all <s>karmas</s>. And because of the scriptural teaching of a specific kind of death, there is differentiation of death, as in — ['Whatever state one remembers when abandoning the body at the end'] — because of the differentiation of specific recollection, there is differentiation of death. Therefore, death is not the manifesting agent of all <s>karmas</s>, because otherwise the qualification would be purposeless.
Nor would the qualification of recollection and the like cause the subject at hand to become otherwise or to be destroyed. For if recollection caused the destruction or alteration [of the principal <s>karma</s>], then recollection would not be a cooperating factor of the principal <s>karma</s>. Recollection would be independent. And in that case, the performed <s>karma</s> would become purposeless.
Moreover, there would be the unwanted consequence of liberation for those who die in the embryonic stages such as <s>kalala</s> (the initial stage of the embryo). [If objected:] because <s>karma</s> has begun [its work]. [And if said:] those stages themselves constitute the fruition of <s>karma</s> — [we reply:] no, because the sense organs have not yet developed. For it is when the sense organs are developed that <s>karmas</s> gain activity and bear fruit. At that stage, such development is not possible.
If it be said that it is like dream — no, because even there, <s>karma</s> [of that kind] is not accepted. And the <s>śruti</s> ['Whatever one sees there, one is not connected with it'] shows that there is no connection with <s>karma</s> arising from dream experience. No one is guilty on account of dreams, even though one may see oneself committing <s>brahmahatyā</s> and the like [in a dream]. If it be said that this is denied because of the observation of atonement for seminal discharge and the like — no, because the atonement is for the occasion of seminal discharge [as a physical event, not for the dream content].
Therefore, even if fruition is accepted in the embryonic stages such as <s>kalala</s> as in dream and similar states, nevertheless, due to the absence of activity of the sense organs, that fruition is merely like the dream state — it is only fruition, not the agency of <s>karma</s>. Thus, the unwanted consequence of liberation for those who perish in the womb remains unanswered.
Therefore, death is not the manifesting agent of all <s>karmas</s>, and because particular application is established for those [specific <s>karmas</s>] — hence this is said: ['This rule applies only to the <s>adṛṣṭajanmavedanīya</s> (to be experienced in unseen births) that has <s>niyatavipāka</s> (determinate fruition)'] — that rule which was stated in the <s>bhāṣya</s> as ['performed in the interval between birth and death'] and so forth regarding the threefold fruition — ['but not to the <s>adṛṣṭajanmavedanīya</s> with <s>aniyatavipāka</s> (indeterminate fruition). Why? Because for the <s>adṛṣṭajanmavedanīya</s> with <s>aniyatavipāka</s>, there is a threefold course.']
How? ['The destruction of what has been done but has not yet ripened'] — the destruction before it has reached its time of ripening. For example — the destruction of performed [<s>karma</s>] that has been counteracted by atonement (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) and the like.
['Merging into the principal <s>karma</s>'] — the merging into the <s>niyatavedanīya</s> (determinate) principal <s>karma</s> up to its completion: by being overshadowed by the fruit of the principal <s>karma</s>, it itself gradually yields its fruit by entering into the middle [of the principal <s>karma's</s> fruition], albeit faintly. Just as — when whole rice grains are being cooked, even fragmentary rice grains that have been put in accomplish a lesser purpose. ['Or the persistence of what has been overpowered by the principal <s>karma</s> of determinate fruition'] — the persistence of that which has been overpowered, i.e. suppressed, by the principal <s>karma</s> whose fruit has commenced and whose fruition is of determinate nature, because its fruition pertains to a conflicting place, time, and occasion. Just as — the persistence of one who has been overpowered by another who has entered into his kingdom, with reference to place, time, and occasion.

body.text: tatra kṛtasyāvipakvasya nāśo yathā śuklakarmodayādihaiva nāśaḥ kṛṣṇasya। yatredamuktam –“dve dve ha vai karmaṇī veditavye pāpakasyaiko rāśiḥ puṇyakṛto'pahanti tadicchasva karmāṇi sukṛtāni kartumihaiva te karma kavayo vedayante।”
body.translated_text: Regarding this, the destruction of what has been done but has not ripened — for example, upon the arising of white <s>karma</s>, the destruction of black <s>karma</s> occurs in this very life. As it has been said — 'Two types of <s>karma</s> indeed are to be known: one heap of sinful [<s>karma</s>], [while] meritorious action destroys [it]. Therefore, desire to perform auspicious deeds — the wise declare your welfare here in this very life.'

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tatra kṛtasyāvipakasya nāśo yathā śuklamoṁdiyādihaiva] tapasvādhyāyayogādilakṣaṇasya śuddhasyodayāt prāyaścittādilakṣaṇasya ca, [kṛṣṇasya aśuddhirūpasya] hiṁsādilakṣaṇasya prāgeva vṛttilābhāt [nāśaḥ । ihaiveti] tvavivakṣitam । janmāntare'pi prāgvṛttilābhānnāśepapatte: । yathā kaunakhyādinimittapāpaviśeṣaṇāṁ kaunakhyādicihairavagamya prāyaśvittena nāśaḥ kriyate ॥
tadetattantrāntaraprasiddhenodāharaṇena vyācaṣṭe--- [yatredamuktaṁ dve dve ha vai karmaṇī] śuklakṛṣṇe janmani janmani sādhakasya puruṣasyādhikṛtasya । [eko rāśiḥ svādhyāyādipuṇyena kṛtaḥ puṇyakṛtaḥ apahantī] taramapuṇyena kṛtaṁ rāśim । atha vā [puṇyakṛtaḥ] puruṣasya śuklakarma [rāśiḥ] kṛṣṇakarmarāśi [mapahanti । tadicchasva] tasmāt [svacchakarmaṇi svakīyāni] karmāṇi śuklāni [sukṛtāni kartum ।] kutaḥ ? yataḥ [ihaiva atraiva tava śarma sukhaṁ] śāntiṁ [kavayo vedayante] karmavipākavibhāgajñāḥ jñāpayanti ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['Regarding this, the destruction of what has been done but has not ripened — for example, upon the arising of white'] — upon the arising of pure [<s>karma</s>] characterized by austerity (<s>tapas</s>), self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), <s>yoga</s>, and the like, and also of that characterized by atonement (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) and the like — ['the destruction of black'] impure [<s>karma</s>] ['characterized by violence (<s>hiṁsā</s>) and the like, occurs'] before it gains activity. ['In this very life'] — however, this is not the intended exclusive meaning, since destruction before gaining activity is established even in another birth. Just as the destruction of specific sins occasioned by nail-biting (<s>kaunakhya</s>) and the like is effected through atonement, having ascertained [the sin] by the marks of nail-biting and the like.
This he illustrates with an example well-known in another system — ['As it has been said: two types of <s>karma</s> indeed'] — white and black, in each and every birth of the practitioner, the qualified person. ['One heap'] of meritorious [<s>karma</s>], ['that which is made of merit, destroys'] the heap made of demerit. Alternatively, ['of the meritorious one'] — the white <s>karma</s> of the person — ['destroys the heap'] of black <s>karma</s>. ['Therefore, desire'] — therefore — ['to perform one's own <s>karmas</s>'] that are white, ['auspicious deeds.'] Why? Because ['here, in this very place, your welfare, happiness,'] peace — ['the wise declare'] — those who know the classification of the ripening of <s>karma</s> make known.

body.text: pradhānakarmaṇyāvāpagamanam। yatredamuktaṁ – “syātsvalpaḥ saṁkaraḥ saparihāraḥ sapratyavamarṣaḥ kuśalasya nāpakarṣāyālam। kasmāt, kuśalaṁ hi me vahvanyadasti yatrāyamāvāpaṁ gataḥ svarge'pyapakarṣamalpaṁ kariṣyati” iti।
body.translated_text: The merging into the principal <s>karma</s>. As it has been said — 'The intermixture may be slight, accompanied by expiation, accompanied by remorse, and is not sufficient to diminish [the fruit of] the meritorious [<s>karma</s>]. Why? Because my meritorious [<s>karma</s>] is abundant and of another kind, into which this [demerit] has merged. Even in heaven it will cause only a slight diminution.'

body.text:
vivaraṇam
pradhānakarmaṇyāvāpagamanamudāharaṇena pradarśyate- [svalpasaṅkaraḥ] alpīyānū, doṣāvakaraḥ । kutaḥ ? [saparihāraḥ] parihārasahitaḥ । parihāramapekṣate, na tu parihṛtaḥ । parihāraśaktyuṇayāvijñānasamānāśraya ityarthaḥ । [sapratyavamarśaḥ] sapratyavekṣaṇaḥ । kathamakārya mayā kriyate kadā nu nistariṣyāmyetat na punaḥ kariṣyāmītyāpadi pravṛttasyākāryaṁ kurvataḥ prāṇasthityādinimittam ॥
[kuśalasya] karmaphaladoṣaparihārādivibhāgāvaśāradasya viduṣaḥ । [nāyamapakarṣāya] nāyaṁ svalpaḥ saṁkaraḥ puṇyaphalātpravṛttādvahutarādapakraṣṭum, apakṛṣya ca svakārye niyoktuṁ paryāptaḥ । atha vā, [kuśalasya] karmaṇa eva [nāyamapakarṣāya paryāptaḥ ।] kasmāt ? [kuśalaṁ hi me ।] sādhaka evaṁ manyate । śubhaṁ yasmānmama [bahvanyadasti yatrāyaṁ] yasmin bahuni śubhe [ayaṁ saṅkara avāpagataḥ svarge'pyapakarṣamalpaṁ kariṣyatīti ॥]
[niyatavipākapradhānakarmabhibhūtasya vā'pyavasthānam । katha] miti duṣṭābhiprāyaḥ praśnaḥ । kathaṁ ? pravṛttarājyenaparasyāpravṛttarājyasyābhibhave yukto nimittabhedena rājyapravṛtteḥ । iha tu nimittamābhivyañjakaṁ maraṇaṁ sarveṣāṁ karmaṇāṁ tulyaṁ tasmiṁstu nimitte sati sarveṣāṁ karmaṇāṁ vṛtilābho yukta iti pradhānakarmābhabhavo na yukta itarasyeti manyate । tataśvāvāpagamanamevāstviti ॥
atrocyate – [tatrādṛṣṭajanmavedanīyasyaiva] aviruddhadeśakālavipākadinimittasya [niyatavipākasya] puṇyāpuṇyarūpasyānekasya [karmaṇaḥ samānaṁ maraṇamabhivyaktikāraṇamuktam । na tu dṛṣṭajanmavedanīyasya] putragrāmādiviṣayasya, [aniyatavipākasya vā] adṛṣṭajanmavedanīyasya yathākṛtavyākhyānasya ॥
[yattvadṛṣṭajanmavedanīyamaniyatavipākaṁ tannaśyedāvāpaṁ vā gacchedabhibhūtaṁ vā ciramapyupāsīta] udāsīta, [yāvatsamānama] viruddhaṁ tulyajātīya [mabhivyañjakaṁ nimittaṁ] karma । samānajātīyaṁ hi karma vipacyamānameta [dabhimukhaṁ karoti ॥]
[tadvipākasyaiva] tasyāniyatavipākasya karmaṇo vipākasyaiva । [deśakālanimittānavadhāraṇā] tkasminvā deśe kasminvā nimitte kasminkāle vā tatkarma vipākābhimukhaṁ bhaviṣyatītyanavadhāraṇāt । [iyaṁ gatiścitrā durjñānā ca] bhavati । [citrā] nāśāvāpābhibhavādivaicitryāt । [durjñānā] deśakālanimittānavadhāraṇāt ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
The merging into the principal <s>karma</s> is demonstrated with an example — ['Slight intermixture'] — a small contamination of fault. Why? ['Accompanied by expiation'] — accompanied by the possibility of expiation. It requires expiation but has not yet been expiated. The meaning is that [this demerit] shares the same substratum as the deficiency of the power of expiation or as ignorance. ['Accompanied by remorse'] — accompanied by self-examination. 'How is this wrongful act being done by me? When shall I be free from this? I shall not do this again' — thus [thinks] one who, engaged in a calamity, performs a wrongful act for the sake of preserving life and the like.
['Of the wise one'] — of the learned person who is skilled in the classification of <s>karma</s>, its fruit, its faults, and its remedies. ['This is not sufficient to diminish'] — this slight intermixture is not sufficient to draw away from the abundant meritorious fruit that has commenced, nor, having drawn it away, to yoke it to its own effect. Alternatively, ['it is not sufficient to diminish the meritorious'] <s>karma</s> itself. Why? ['Because my meritorious <s>karma</s> is abundant.'] The practitioner thinks thus: 'Since my auspicious [<s>karma</s>] ['is abundant and of another kind, into which this'] intermixture ['has merged — even in heaven it will cause only a slight diminution.'']
['Or the persistence of what has been overpowered by the principal <s>karma</s> of determinate fruition. How'] — this is a question with a hostile intent. How? In the case of the one overpowered by another who has entered into his kingdom, the overpowering is justified because of the difference in occasion for the commencement of the kingdom. But here, the occasion — the manifesting agent, namely death — is common to all <s>karmas</s>; and when that occasion is present, it is reasonable that all <s>karmas</s> should gain activity, so the overpowering by the principal <s>karma</s> and not by the other is not justified — so the objector thinks. And therefore [he suggests] there should only be merging.
To this it is replied — ['Only for the <s>adṛṣṭajanmavedanīya</s>'] — that which has non-conflicting place, time, and occasion of fruition — ['having <s>niyatavipāka</s> (determinate fruition),'] consisting of both meritorious and demeritorious [<s>karma</s>], being manifold — ['death has been stated as the common manifesting cause. But not for the <s>dṛṣṭajanmavedanīya</s>'] — that pertaining to objects such as sons, villages, and the like — ['nor for the <s>aniyatavipāka</s>'] — the <s>adṛṣṭajanmavedanīya</s> as explained above.
['But the <s>adṛṣṭajanmavedanīya</s> with <s>aniyatavipāka</s> may be destroyed, or may merge, or may persist overpowered for a long time,'] may remain waiting, ['until a compatible'] non-conflicting, of the same kind, ['manifesting occasion'] — <s>karma</s> [arises]. For <s>karma</s> of the same kind, when ripening, ['turns this one toward [fruition].']
['Of the fruition of that alone'] — of the fruition of that very <s>karma</s> with <s>aniyatavipāka</s>. ['There is indeterminacy of place, time, and occasion'] — because it cannot be ascertained in what place, at what occasion, or at what time that <s>karma</s> will turn toward fruition. ['This course is variegated and difficult to know.'] ['Variegated'] — because of the variety of destruction, merging, overpowering, and the like. ['Difficult to know'] — because of the indeterminacy of place, time, and occasion.

body.text: niyatavipākapradhānakarmaṇā'bhibhūtasya vā ciramavasthānam। kathamiti, adṛṣṭajanmavedanīyasyaiva niyatavipākasya karmaṇaḥ samānaṁ maraṇamabhivyaktikāraṇamuktam na tvadṛṣṭajanmavedanīyasyāniyatavipākasya। yattvadṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaṁ karmāniyatavipākaṁ tannaśyedāvāpaṁ vā gacchedabhibhūtaṁ vā ciramapyupāsīta, yāvatsamānaṁ karmābhivyañjakaṁ nimittamasya na vipākābhimukhaṁ karotīti। tadvipākasyaiva deśakālanimittānavadhāraṇādiyaṁ karmagatiścitrā durvijñānā ceti। na cotsargasyāpavādānnivṛttirityekabhavikaḥ karmāśayo'nujñāyata iti ॥ 13 ॥
body.translated_text: Or, [the karmic residue] that has been overpowered by a <s>karma</s> of determinate fruition remains for a long time. How so? It has been stated that death is the cause of manifestation only for <s>karma</s> of determinate fruition that is to be experienced in an unseen [future] birth, but not for <s>karma</s> of indeterminate fruition that is to be experienced in an unseen birth. However, that <s>karma</s> which is to be experienced in an unseen birth and has indeterminate fruition — it may perish, or reach exhaustion, or remain overpowered for a long time, so long as no concurrent <s>karma</s> acting as a manifesting cause turns it toward fruition. Because of the impossibility of determining the place, time, and occasion of its fruition, this course of <s>karma</s> (<s>karmagati</s>) is variegated and difficult to understand. And since the general rule is not annulled by the exception, the single-life <s>karmāśaya</s> (store of karma) is acknowledged. || 13 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
nanu cādṛṣṭajanmavedanīyasya prāyaṇe'bhivyaktasya [ekameva janma karotī] tyekajanmārambhitvamuktam - tadidānīṁ nāśāvāpābhibhavāvasthānādivacanādvādhyeteti ceta – na – upapādite.ottaratvāt [adṛṣṭajanmavedanīyasya niyatavipākasyevāyaṁ niyama] iti । [na tasyotsargasya] asmādaniya [māpavādānnivṛttiriti ।] kathaṁ [na] nivṛttiḥ ? [ekabhavikaḥ karmāśayo dujñāna ityevaṁ] na nivṛttiḥ । aniyatavipākasyāpyekajanmārambhitvaṁ na pratiṣiddhamityartha: ॥
athavā, utsargasyāpavādānnivṛttiriti matvā naikabhavikaḥ karmāśayo durśana ityanena nañ saṁbadhyate । yasmādutsargasyaikadeśasyāpavādo nivartako na savaisya, tasmānniyatavipaki ekabhavika karmīśayaḥ sujñāna eva ॥
aparaḥ kalpaḥ--iha karmagatirjñātavyeti prakṛtaṁ, tasyāyamapavāda ekabhavikaḥ karmāśayo durjñāna iti । tatretiśabdo hatvarthe । yasmāddhetorautsargikasya karmagatijñānasya prakṛtasya etasmādapavādānna nivṛttiriti, tasmādyathā jñeyā karmagatistathā jñātavyaiva । durjñānā iti duḥkhena jñeyatvamucyate kleśena ॥ 13 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
Now, if one objects that it was stated that <s>karma</s> to be experienced in an unseen birth, when manifested at the time of death, 'brings about a single birth only,' and that this statement of single-birth causation is now contradicted by the mention of destruction, exhaustion, overpowering, and long remaining — no, because [what follows] is an established answer: [this restriction applies only to <s>karma</s> of determinate fruition that is to be experienced in an unseen birth.] [The general rule] is not annulled by this exception. How is it not annulled? [Because] it is not annulled [in the sense that] 'the single-life <s>karmāśaya</s> is difficult to understand' — meaning that single-birth causation for <s>karma</s> of indeterminate fruition is also not precluded.
Alternatively, thinking that the general rule is annulled by the exception, the negation connects with 'the single-life <s>karmāśaya</s> is difficult to discern' — since an exception that negates only a part of the general rule does not negate the whole, therefore the single-life <s>karmāśaya</s> of determinate fruition is indeed easy to understand.
Another interpretation: Here, the topic under discussion is that the course of <s>karma</s> is to be understood. The exception to this is that the single-life <s>karmāśaya</s> is difficult to understand. In this, the word 'iti' has a causal sense. Because there is no annulment of the general knowledge of the course of <s>karma</s> under discussion by this exception, therefore the course of <s>karma</s> must be understood just as it is to be understood. 'Difficult to understand' expresses that it is known only with difficulty, with effort. || 13 ||

body.text: te hlādaparitāpaphalāḥ puṇyāpuṇyahetutvāt ॥ 14 ॥
body.translated_text: They [i.e., birth, lifespan, and experience] have pleasure and pain as their fruits, because of merit and demerit as their cause. || 14 ||

body.text: te janmāyurbhogāḥ puṇyahetukāḥ sukhaphalā apuṇyahetukā duḥkhaphalā iti। yathā cedaṁ duḥkhaṁ pratikūlātmakamevaṁ viṣayamukhakāle'pi duḥkhamastyeva pratikūlātmakaṁ yoginaḥ ॥ 14 ॥
body.translated_text: They — birth, lifespan, and experience — have pleasure as their fruit when caused by merit, and pain as their fruit when caused by demerit. And just as this suffering is of a disagreeable nature, so too even at the time of contact with sense objects, there is indeed suffering of a disagreeable nature for the <s>yogin</s>. || 14 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
karmāṁśaya upavyākhyāto dṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaśva adṛṣṭajanmavedanīyaśca । tasyāpi trividhā vipākā jātyāyurbhogāḥ [hlādaparitāpaphalāḥ puṇyāpuṇyahetutvāt ।] hvāda: sukhaṁ, paritāpī du:khaṁ, hvādaśca paritāpaśca hvādaparitāpau, tau phalaṁ yeṣāṁ te hlādaparitāpaphalāḥ । tathā puṇyaṁ ca apuṇyañca puṇyāpuṇye, te eva hetū yeṣāṁ te puṇyāpuṇyahetavaḥ, teṣāṁ bhāvaḥ puṇyāpuṇyahetutvaṁ, tasmātpuṇyāpuṇyahetutvāt । [te jātyāyurmorgāḥ puṇyahetukā: sukhaphalāḥ । apuṇyahetukā duḥkhaphalāḥ । yathedaṁ duḥkhaṁ pratikūlātmakamevaṁ viṣayasukhakāle'pi du:khamasyeva pratikūlātmakaṁ yoginaḥ ॥ 14 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
The <s>karmāśaya</s> (store of karma) has been explained above as both that to be experienced in the present birth and that to be experienced in an unseen [future] birth. Its fruitions are also threefold: birth, lifespan, and experience. ['They have pleasure and pain as their fruits, because of merit and demerit as their cause.'] <s>Hlāda</s> (delight) is pleasure; <s>paritāpa</s> (affliction) is pain; delight and affliction together are <s>hlāda-paritāpa</s>, and those whose fruits are these are 'having delight and affliction as their fruits.' Likewise, merit and demerit are <s>puṇya-apuṇya</s>; those very two are the causes of which they are 'having merit and demerit as causes'; the state of being such is 'the condition of having merit and demerit as cause,' therefore 'because of merit and demerit as their cause.' ['They — birth, lifespan, and experience — have pleasure as their fruit when caused by merit, and pain as their fruit when caused by demerit. Just as this suffering is of a disagreeable nature, so too even at the time of sensory pleasure, there is indeed suffering of a disagreeable nature for the <s>yogin</s>.'] || 14 ||

body.text: kathaṁ, tadupapādyate –
body.translated_text: How so? This is now demonstrated —

body.text: pariṇāmatāpasaṁskāraduḥkhairguṇavṛttivirodhācca duḥkhameva sarvaṁ vivekinaḥ ॥ 15 ॥
body.translated_text: Due to the sufferings of transformation, burning, and <s>saṁskāra</s> (latent impressions), and because of the conflict among the activities of the <s>guṇas</s> (constituents of nature), all is indeed suffering for the discerning one. || 15 ||

body.text: sarvasyāyaṁ rāgānuviddhaścetanācetanasādhanādhīnaḥ sukhānubhava iti tatrāsti rāgajaḥ karmāśayaḥ। tathā ca dveṣṭi duḥkhasādhanāni muhyati ceti dveṣamohakṛto'pyasti karmāśayaḥ। tathā coktam – “nānupahatya bhūtānyupabhogaḥ saṁbhavatīti hiṁsākṛto'pyasti śārīraḥ karmāśayaḥ” iti। viṣayasukhaṁ cāvidyetyuktam।
body.translated_text: Everyone's experience of pleasure is pervaded by <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and dependent on sentient and insentient means — therefore there exists a store of <s>karma</s> (<s>karmāśaya</s>) born of attachment. Likewise, one hates the means of suffering and is deluded — therefore there also exists a <s>karmāśaya</s> produced by aversion and delusion. And thus it has been said: 'Since enjoyment is not possible without harming beings, there also exists a bodily <s>karmāśaya</s> produced by <s>hiṃsā</s> (violence).' And sensory pleasure has been called <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance).

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[kathaṁ] viṣayasukhakāle yogina: du:khamasti ? tathā pūrvatra coktaṁ [du:khe sukhakhyārti vakṣyatīti । tadupapādyate] pratipādyate । tatra caitanna pratipāditam । duḥkhasya karmakāryatvāt, karmānantaraṁ pratipādanayuktamiti, bahuvaktavyatvācca । [pariṇāmatāpasaṁskāraduḥkhairguṇavṛtivirodhācca duḥkhameva sarva vivekinaḥ ॥]
pariṇatiḥ [pariṇāmaḥ,] tapti [stāpaḥ,] saṁskṛtiḥ [saṁskāraḥ,] tāpaśca saṁskāraśca [tāpasaṁskārau,] pariṇāmaśva tāpasaṁskārau ca [pariṇāmatāpasaṁskārā:,] ta eva [duḥkhā] duḥkhanimittāni, etaiḥ [pariṇāmatāpasaṁskāraduḥkheheṁtubhiḥ sarvameva duḥkham ।] kintatsarva ? kleśa । duḥkhakāraṇatvādeva heto: । karmāṇa hlādaparitāpaphalatvāt । jātyāyubhaugāśva kleśādīnāmāśrayanimittaviṣayāśva duḥkhahetutvādityetatsarvameva duḥkham ॥
kiṁ sarvasyaiva ? netyāha- [vivekina iti ।] kleśādīnāṁ vibhāgavivekī yasya vidyate sa vivekī ; tasya kleśakarmavipākābhijñasya pariṇāmatāpasaṁskāraguṇavṛttivirodhātmaka(dhāñca)sarvaduḥkhatvopapādaka(pratipādaka)hetvabhidarśina ityartha: । netarasyānitthaṁdarśinaḥ ॥
tasya tu tatimātraṁ duḥkham । tadapi ‘ahaṁ tapya' ityātmatvena pratipadyamānaḥ tatrāpi saṁśayāno'sau mamedaṁ duḥkhamityetāvanmātramapi viviṅkte । yadi hyetāvadapyantaraṁ viviścīta, tato duḥkhasādhanamapyetadduḥkha(sādhana)miti manvīta ॥
tathā ca sarvamidaṁ duḥkhamiti titikṣediti so'pi vivekī syāt । tasmādyadyapi tāpakāle duḥkhamātraṁ paśyanti, tathā'pi na tatsādhanādi sarvaṁ du khamiti manyante nirvivekinaḥ । yasya punaḥ pariṇāmaduḥkhahetudarśarnaṁ tasya vivekinaḥ sarvameva duḥkham ॥
tatra tāvatpariṇāmaduḥkhatāṁ vyācaṣṭe-- [sarvasyāyaṁ rāgānuviddhaḥ ।] sarvasyetyanena sarvaprāṇiprasiddhatvādavyabhicāripratyakṣāvagamyatvaṁ darśayati । [cetanācetanādhīnaḥ] putrapuśuhiraṇyādisādhanāyattaḥ sukhānubhava iti । sukhānubhavakāle rāgo manovyāpāra: tadviśiṣṭo hi sukhamanubhavati । sa sarvo vyāpāra: kleśopasaṁhitatvāddharmādharmahetuḥ । tatpūrvaśca karmāśayaḥ prārabdhaphala upabhujyate, bhogakāle cāpara upacīyate । tataśva [kleśamūlaḥ karmāśayaḥ sati mūle tadvipāka] ityupapannaṁ bhavati ॥
[tathā,] sukhavelāyāṁ sukhapratyanīkabhūtāni [duḥkhasādhanāni] upalabhamāno [dveṣṭi,] tathā sukhopabhogaparipālanavyagranaramānaso [muhyati ceti dveṣamoha] pūrvavyāpārajanito'pya [sti karmāśayaḥ ।] athavā dveṣamohāveva vyāpārarūpāviti tatkṛta eva ॥
[tathā,] yaśvāsau sukho [pabhogaḥ] sa [nānupahatya] nānupahiṅsya [bhūtānyupabhogaḥ sabhbhavatīti ।] upabhoga evopaghātahetutvādupahantṛvena vivakṣita iti, samānakartṛkatvam । anyo'pi madīyamevopabhokṣyata iti manyate, tatrāpi sarvopabhogasāmarthyayuktaṁ dhanamita tasminnupādīyamāne dhruvaṁ parapīḍā syāt । kimuta pīḍayitvaiva yadupādīyate । tataśva [hiṁsākṛto'pyasti karmāśaya: śārīraḥ ।] tadupādānavyāpārasya śarīranirvartyatvāt ॥
evamekasminnupabhogakāle bahudhā karmaśayo lobhakrodhamohanimitta upacīyate । tathā ca rāgadveṣamohaviśiṣṭatvādanekamukhakarmāśayaviśiṣṭa: sukhānubhavaḥ pariṇamamānaḥ sannanubandhe duḥkhībhavatīti pariṇāmaduḥkhatetyucyate । vivekinasvevaṁ paśyataḥ sukhānubhavakāle'pi duḥkhamasyeva । tadyathā – viṣadigdhatāṁ jñātvā dadhyodanaṁ bhuñjānasya ॥
itaśva sarva duḥkhameva, avidyātvādviṣayasukhasya । avivekapratyayātmako hi viṣayasukhānubhavaḥ । tadetadāha – [viṣayasukhaṁ cāvidyetyuktamiti ।] kvoktam ? ihaiva paryāyaśabdena [“atyantavivi[bha]ktayoratyantāsaṅkīrṇayoravivekaprāptāviva satyāṁ bhogaḥ kalpate । svarūpapratilambhe tu tayoḥ kaivalyameva bhavati kuto bhoga iti”] ityanena bhāṣyeṇa ॥
yadvā, sūtrakoreṇoktamupariṣṭāt [“pratyayāviśeṣo bhogaḥ”] iti । avidyā ca pariṇamamānā sarvamanarthaṁ kareti । tataśva duḥkhabījāvādduḥkhameva viṣayasukham । yathā vyādhinimittatvāt svādutaramapi bhakṣyamāṇam ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['How'] is there suffering for the <s>yogin</s> at the time of sensory pleasure? And it was stated earlier that ['he will state the cognition of pleasure in what is painful.' This is now demonstrated,] i.e., elucidated. But it was not elucidated there, because suffering is an effect of <s>karma</s>, and it is proper to elucidate it after <s>karma</s> [has been discussed], and because there is much to be said. ['Due to the sufferings of transformation, burning, and <s>saṁskāra</s>, and because of the conflict among the activities of the <s>guṇas</s>, all is indeed suffering for the discerning one.']
Transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>) is change; burning (<s>tāpa</s>) is torment; impression (<s>saṁskāra</s>) is conditioning. Burning and <s>saṁskāra</s> together are <s>tāpa-saṁskāra</s>; transformation and <s>tāpa-saṁskāra</s> together are <s>pariṇāma-tāpa-saṁskāra</s>; these themselves are sufferings, i.e., causes of suffering. ['By means of these — the sufferings of transformation, burning, and <s>saṁskāra</s> — everything is indeed suffering.'] What is this 'everything'? The <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) — because they are causes of suffering. <s>Karmas</s> — because their fruits are pleasure and affliction. Birth, lifespan, and experience — because they are the loci, causes, and objects of <s>kleśas</s> and the rest, and thus causes of suffering. All this is indeed suffering.
Is it so for everyone? No, he says — ['for the discerning one.'] One who possesses the discriminative knowledge (<s>viveka</s>) that distinguishes <s>kleśas</s> and the rest is the discerning one (<s>vivekin</s>); for him, who knows <s>kleśas</s>, <s>karma</s>, and fruition, and who perceives the demonstrating reasons that establish the universal suffering-nature consisting of transformation, burning, <s>saṁskāra</s>, and the conflict of <s>guṇa</s>-activities — this is the meaning. Not for the other who does not see things thus.
For the latter, there is only that much suffering [which is directly felt]. But even he, experiencing it as 'I am burning,' identifying it with the self — even there, wavering, he discerns at least this much: 'This suffering is mine.' For if he were to discern even this much of a distinction, then he would recognize that even the means of suffering is itself a cause of suffering.
And thus, [thinking] 'all this is suffering,' he would endure it with forbearance — and he too would be a discerning one. Therefore, although at the time of burning people see only the suffering, still the undiscerning do not consider all its causes and means to be suffering. But for the one who sees the causes of transformation-suffering, for that discerning one, everything is indeed suffering.
Regarding this, he first explains the nature of transformation-suffering — ['Everyone's (experience of pleasure) is pervaded by attachment.'] By 'everyone's' he shows that because it is well-known to all beings, it is known through invariable direct perception. ['Dependent on sentient and insentient means'] — dependent on means such as sons, cattle, gold, and the like — is the experience of pleasure. At the time of experiencing pleasure, <s>rāga</s> (attachment) is a mental activity; qualified by that, one experiences pleasure. All that activity, being conjoined with <s>kleśas</s>, is the cause of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>. The prior <s>karmāśaya</s> whose fruit has commenced is being experienced, while at the time of enjoyment another is being accumulated. And thus [the statement] 'the <s>karmāśaya</s> rooted in <s>kleśas</s> — when the root exists, the fruition of that' becomes established.
['Likewise,'] at the time of pleasure, perceiving things opposed to that pleasure as ['means of suffering, one hates'] them; likewise, being engrossed in protecting and maintaining pleasurable enjoyment, ['one is deluded — therefore there also'] exists a <s>karmāśaya</s> born of ['aversion and delusion.'] Or rather, aversion and delusion themselves are forms of activity, so it is produced by them alone.
['Likewise,'] whatever that enjoyment of pleasure is, it ['is not possible without harming beings.'] Since enjoyment itself is the cause of harm, it is described as the harmer — hence the identity of agent. Even another thinks, 'He will enjoy what is mine alone,' and in that case too, wealth being capable of providing enjoyment to all, when it is appropriated, harm to others will certainly result — how much more so when something is appropriated through actual violence. And therefore ['there also exists a bodily <s>karmāśaya</s> produced by violence,'] because the activity of appropriation is accomplished through the body.
Thus, at a single occasion of enjoyment, the store of <s>karma</s> is accumulated in many ways through greed, anger, and delusion. And thus, because the experience of pleasure is qualified by attachment, aversion, and delusion, and qualified by a <s>karmāśaya</s> of many aspects, it is called transformation-suffering because, while being experienced, it transforms and becomes suffering in its consequence. For the discerning one who sees it thus, there is indeed suffering even at the time of experiencing pleasure — just as for one who, knowing it to be laced with poison, eats sweetened rice.
And moreover, all is indeed suffering, because sensory pleasure is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). For the experience of sensory pleasure is essentially a cognition of non-discrimination (<s>aviveka</s>). This he states — ['And sensory pleasure has been called <s>avidyā</s>.'] Where was it stated? Here itself, in a synonymous expression, by the <s>bhāṣya</s> passage: ['When these two, which are absolutely distinct and absolutely unmixed, appear as if in a state of non-discrimination, enjoyment is imagined. But when their true natures are recovered, there is only <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation) — whence enjoyment?']
Alternatively, it is stated by a <s>sūtra</s> further on: ['Experience (<s>bhoga</s>) is a cognition without discrimination (<s>pratyaya-aviśeṣa</s>).'] And <s>avidyā</s>, as it transforms, produces all misfortune. Therefore, since it is the seed of suffering, sensory pleasure is itself suffering — just as food, however delicious, is [harmful] when it is the cause of disease. || 15 ||
