Those very <s>guṇas</s> in their state of equilibrium assume the single designation of <s>pradhāna</s>. When they assume imbalance, they become designated by the word 'effect' (<s>vikāra</s>) and have [active] modifications.
[This is said to be the seen (<s>dṛśya</s>).]

body.text: tadetadbhūtendriyātmakaṁ bhūtabhāvena pṛthivyādinā sūkṣmasthūlena pariṇamate। tathendriyabhāvena śrotrādinā sūkṣmasthūlena pariṇamata iti। tattu nāprayojanamapi tu prayojanamurarīkṛtya pravartata iti bhogāpavargārthaṁ hi taddṛśyaṁ puruṣasyeti। tatreṣṭāniṣṭaguṇasvarūpāvadhāraṇamavibhāgāpannaṁ bhogo bhoktuḥ svarūpāvadhāraṇamapavarga iti। dvayoratiriktamanyaddarśanaṁ nāsti। tathā coktam – ayaṁ tu khalu triṣu guṇeṣu kartṛṣvakartari ca puruṣe tulyātulyajātīye caturthe tatkriyāsākṣiṇyupanīyamānānsarvabhāvānupapannānanupaśyannadarśanamanyacchaṅkata iti।
body.translated_text: This [seen], consisting of elements and sense organs, transforms in the form of elements—earth etc., both subtle and gross. Likewise it transforms in the form of sense organs—hearing etc., both subtle and gross. But it does not operate without purpose; rather, accepting a purpose, it proceeds. For the seen serves the purposes of experience (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) for <s>Puruṣa</s>. Therein, the ascertainment of the essential nature of the qualities—desirable and undesirable—that has become undifferentiated [from <s>Puruṣa</s>], is experience (<s>bhoga</s>) of the experiencer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>). The ascertainment of one's own essential nature is liberation (<s>apavarga</s>). There is no third form of vision beyond these two. And thus it was said: 'This [person], rightly seeing, observing the three <s>guṇas</s> that are agents and the fourth—<s>Puruṣa</s> who is a non-agent, of similar and dissimilar kind, the witness of their activities—seeing all states that are presented [to him], established as intellectual cognitions that are merely of the nature of the <s>guṇas</s>, does not suspect any other form of vision.'

body.text:
vivaraṇam
tadetaddṛśyaṁ [bhūtendriyātmakaṁ] bhūtātmakamindriyātmakaṁ ca । kathaṁ tadātmakatvamityāha – [bhūtabhāvena pṛthivyādinā sūkṣmasthūlena] sūkṣmeṇa tanmātrarūpeṇa sthūlena viśeṣarūpeṇa । dvividho hi bhūtabhāvastanmātrarūpo viśeṣarūpaśca । [vipariṇamate] sthūlasūkṣmabhāvamāpadyate । [indriyabhāvene] driyarūpeṇa [śrotrādinā sūkṣmasthūlena vipariṇamate ।] sūkṣmeṇāhaṅkārarūpeṇa sthūlena śrotrādirūpeṇa ॥
tattu dṛśyaṁ [nāprayojanam ।] sarvatraiva pravṛtteḥ prayojanadarśanāt । [api tu prayājanamūrīkṛtya] aṅgīkṛtya [pravartate ।] kiṁ purnadṛśyapravṛtiprayojanamityāha – [bhāgāpavargārthaṁ hi dṛśyaṁ puruṣasya] agnyādipratipattivat ॥
kau punastai bhogāpavargavityāha – [tatreṣṭāniṣṭaguṇasvarūpāvadhāraṇamavibhāgāpannam iṣṭānām] agarucandanasparśanādilakṣaṇānām [aniṣṭānāṁ] pratikūlātmakānāṁ kṛpāṇakaṇṭakādisparśanarūpaṇāṁ guṇānāṁ [svarūpāvadhāraṇaṁ] svarūpāvagamaḥ svarūpādhyavasānam । tasya viśeṣaṇam [avibhāgāpannaṁ] puruṣapratyaye 'nāyaṁ puruṣa idaṁ sattvam’ ityavibhāgatāṁ gatam । prāptacaitanyopagraharūpavādbauddhasya pratyayasya । sa itthaṁbhūtaḥ puruṣasya [bhoga] ityākhyāyate ॥
tasmādbhogasvarūpādbauddhātū pratyayādvivicya tatsākṣiṇo dṛśirūpasya [svarūpāvadhāraṇaṁ] bhoktṛsvarūpādavadhāryamāṇāduttarakālamapyapavṛttasya viśeṣābhāvādapavarga ityucyate । sarvadā svarūpapratiṣṭho hi (tadā) sa iti । vṛttisārūpyamitaratra viśeṣa iti ॥
[dvayo] rbhogāpavargayo [ratiriktamanya] ttṛtīyaṁ da [rśanaṁ nāsti ।] yāvadavidyā tāvadiṣṭāniṣṭe sta iti bhoga eva । puruṣasya tvaheyānupādeyasvarūpatvāt tadavadhāraṇe kuto bhoga iti bhogarūpasyāvidyālakṣaṇasya pratyayasya pratipakṣaḥ pratyayaḥ puruṣāvadhāraṇam । yasmādetadata etaddarśanadvayavyatirekeṇa tṛtīyaṁ darśanāntaraṁ na kalpayituṁ śakyate ॥
[tathā coktam – ayaṁ tu khalvevaṁ] samyagdaśī [triṣu] guṇeṣūktalakṣaṇeṣu [kartuṣu] sarvavyāpāranirvṛttikareṣvakartari ca guṇadharmavilakṣaṇe [puruṣe caturthe tatkriyāsākṣiṇi] guṇakriyāsūpadraṣṭari sandhikriyāsākṣibhūtopadraṣṭṛva [dupānīyamānān] antaḥkaraṇalakṣaṇairguṇaiḥ prāpyamāṇān darśitaviṣayatvāt [sarvabhāvān] upapannān gaiṇāneva bauddhapratyayākaraṇa pariniṣpannān paśyan upalabhamāno [nāhaṁ] na mametyevaṁ [na darśanamite'nyat] sambhavati samyagdarśanamiti [na śaṅkate ।] nāstyevānyat samyagdarśanamiti manyate ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇa (Elucidation):
This seen [consists of elements and sense organs]—having the nature of elements and having the nature of sense organs. How is it of that nature? He says: [In the form of elements—earth etc., subtle and gross]—subtle in the form of <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) and gross in the form of the gross elements (<s>viśeṣas</s>). For the elemental form is twofold: in the form of <s>tanmātras</s> and in the form of gross elements. [It transforms]—it assumes the state of gross and subtle. [In the form of sense organs]—in the form of organs, [such as hearing etc., subtle and gross, it transforms]—subtle in the form of <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle) and gross in the form of the hearing organ etc.
But the seen [does not operate without purpose]—because in all instances, a purpose is seen to motivate activity. [Rather, accepting a purpose, it proceeds.] What then is the purpose of the activity of the seen? He says: [The seen serves the purposes of experience and liberation for <s>Puruṣa</s>]—like the perception of fire etc.
What then are experience and liberation? He says: [Therein, the ascertainment of the essential nature of the qualities—desirable and undesirable—that has become undifferentiated]—of the desirable ones, characterized by the touch of sandalwood, aloe, etc., and of the undesirable ones, characterized by the touch of swords, thorns, etc.—the ascertainment of the essential nature of [these] qualities, the understanding and determination of their essential nature. Its qualification is [that has become undifferentiated]—having entered into non-distinction in the cognition of <s>Puruṣa</s>, as 'this is not <s>Puruṣa</s>, this is <s>sattva</s>'; because the intellectual cognition has the form of having received the imprint of consciousness. Such [experience], thus characterized, is called the experience (<s>bhoga</s>) of <s>Puruṣa</s>.
Therefore, distinguishing from that experience-nature—from the intellectual cognition—the [ascertainment of the essential nature] of the witness who has the nature of pure seeing (<s>dṛśi</s>); since even after the determination of the experiencer's essential nature there is no difference in the subsequent [state of] one who has thus turned away [from objects]—it is called liberation (<s>apavarga</s>). For he is always established in his own essential nature; the difference elsewhere lies in the conformity with mental modifications.
[There is no third] form of [vision] beyond these two—experience and liberation. As long as <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) persists, the desirable and undesirable exist, and therefore it is experience alone. But since <s>Puruṣa</s>'s essential nature is such that nothing is to be avoided or acquired, upon the determination of that, whence would there be experience? Therefore the cognition that is the counterpart of the cognition characterized by <s>avidyā</s>—which has the form of experience—is the determination of <s>Puruṣa</s>. Since this is so, no third form of vision can be imagined beyond these two.
[And thus it was said: 'This one, truly] seeing rightly, [the three <s>guṇas</s>] of the described characteristics [that are agents]—that accomplish all activities—and [in <s>Puruṣa</s>], the fourth, who is a non-agent, distinct from the properties of the <s>guṇas</s>, [the witness of their activities]—the observer of the activities of the <s>guṇas</s>, like a witness of a transaction—[seeing all states that are presented] to him by the <s>guṇas</s> in the form of the inner organ, that have the status of being shown their objects, [as established]—as merely intellectual cognitions accomplished by the <s>guṇas</s>—seeing and perceiving thus 'not I, not mine'—[does not suspect any other] form of right vision—he considers that there is no other form of right vision.'

body.text: tāvetau bhogāpavargau buddhikṛtau buddhāveva vartamānau kathaṁ puruṣe vyapadiśyete iti। yathā vijayaḥ parājayo vā yoddhṛṣu vartamānaḥ svāmini vyapadiśyate, sa hi tatphalasya bhokteti, evaṁ bandhamokṣau buddhāveva vartamānau puruṣe vyapadiśyete, sa hi tatphalasya bhokteti। buddhereva puruṣārthāparisamāptirbandhastadarthāvasāyo mokṣa iti। etena grahaṇadhāraṇohāpohatattvajñānābhiniveśā buddhau vartamānāḥ puruṣe'dhyāropitasadbhāvāḥ। sa hi tatphalasya bhokteti ॥ 18 ॥
body.translated_text: These two—experience (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>)—are brought about by <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) and exist in <s>buddhi</s> alone; how then are they attributed to <s>Puruṣa</s>? Just as victory or defeat, though occurring among the warriors, is attributed to the sovereign—for he is the enjoyer of their fruit—so too bondage and liberation, though occurring in <s>buddhi</s> alone, are attributed to <s>Puruṣa</s>, for he is the enjoyer of their fruit. The non-completion of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose by <s>buddhi</s> is bondage; the fulfillment of that purpose is liberation. By this, grasping, retention, reasoning, creative ideation, and the realization of truth—all occurring in <s>buddhi</s>—have their existence superimposed upon <s>Puruṣa</s>. For he is the enjoyer of their fruit.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tāvetau bhogāpavargau buddhikṛtau] budvinirvartitau [buddhāveva vartamānau ।] anyakṛtasyāpyanyatra vṛttirdṛṣṭā yathā rajakakṛto vastrarāga iti kathaṁ [puruṣe'padiśayete?] iti tau buddhāveva vartamānau puruṣe'padiyete iti kuta etat ? [sa hi tattatphalasya bhokteti] samyaṅmithyāpratyayayorupalabdheti ॥
dṛṣṭāntena vyākhyātamarthaṁ nigamayati – [yathā vijayaḥ parājayo veti । budverevārthāparisamāptirbandha iti ।] yāvat samāptau kartavyau bhogā'pavargāviti buddhirmanyate tāvadbandhaḥ । [tadarthāvasāyo mokṣaḥ ।] tasyā eva buddherarthāvasāyaḥ kartavyasamāptiḥ । yadā ātmavilakṣaṇaṁ bandhamokṣāsambandhinaṁ puruṣamīkṣate nāsya kartavyamastīti, sa kartavyāvasāyo buddhermokṣa iti ॥
[etena grahaṇadhāraṇavijñānohāpohakriyāvacanayathānyāyāvadhāraṇābhiniveśāḥ] puruṣe'vyāropitasadbhāvā iti jñeyāḥ । pratyayatvāviśeṣāt buddhidharmāḥ [buddhāveva vartamānāḥ] buddhikṛtāḥ [puruṣe'dhyāropitasadbhāvāḥ] puruṣo gṛhṇāti puruṣo dhārayatītyevameva puruṣe apyāropyante ॥
[grahaṇaṁ] śabdādīnāṁ śrotrādibhirupādānam । gṛhītānāmavismaraṇaṁ [dhāraṇam ।] dhāritasya sāmānyaviśeṣāvadhāraṇaṁ [vijñānam ।] vijñātasyaiva punastadgataviśeṣāvabubhutsayohana [mūhaḥ ।] ūhitasya viruddhānāṁ dharmāṇāṁ vyudasa [namapohaḥ] । viṣayeṣu pravṛttiḥ [kriyā ।] vākyaviṣayo vṛttiviśeṣaści tasya [vacanam ।] yo yo nyāyo yathānyāyaṁ yasya ca vastuno yathaivopapattistathaivāvadhāraṇaṁ [yathānyāyāvadhāraṇam ।] tatra punaḥ punaḥ samyakpratyayāvicalanāya yaścittasyābhiyogaḥ so ['bhiniveśaḥ ।] ta ete grahaṇādayaḥ puruṣe'dhyāropitasadbhāvāḥ । [sa hi tatphalasya bhokteti] grahaṇadiphalasyopalabdheti ॥ 18 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['These two — experience (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) — are effected by <s>buddhi</s> (intellect)'] — produced by <s>buddhi</s> — ['and exist in <s>buddhi</s> alone.'] But it is observed that what is produced by one can exist in another — as the dye applied by a washerman exists in the cloth. So how are they ['attributed to <s>Puruṣa</s>?'] That is, these two, existing in <s>buddhi</s> alone, are attributed to <s>Puruṣa</s> — how is this? ['Because he is the experiencer of the respective fruits'] — of right and wrong cognition,

body.text: dṛśyānāṁ guṇānāṁ svarūpabhedāvadhāraṇārthamidamārabhyate –
body.translated_text: For the purpose of ascertaining the divisions of the essential nature of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) which constitute the seen (<s>dṛśya</s>), the following is begun —

body.text: viśeṣāviśeṣaliṅgamātrāliṅgāni guṇaparvāṇi ॥ 19 ॥
body.translated_text: The specific (<s>viśeṣa</s>), the non-specific (<s>aviśeṣa</s>), the merely indicated (<s>liṅga-mātra</s>), and the unindicated (<s>aliṅga</s>) are the stages of the <s>guṇas</s>. || 19 ||

body.text: tatrā''kāśavāyvagnyudakabhūmayo bhūtāni śabdasparśarūparasagandhatanmātrāṇāmaviśeṣāṇāṁ viśeṣāḥ। tathā śrotratvakcakṣurjihvāghrāṇāni buddhīndriyāṇi, vākpāṇipādapāyūpasthāḥ karmendriyāṇi, ekādaśaṁ manaḥ sarvārtham, ityetānyasmitālakṣaṇasyāviśeṣasya viśeṣāḥ। guṇānāmeṣa ṣoḍaśako viśeṣapariṇāmaḥ।
body.translated_text: Among these, space, air, fire, water, and earth are the gross elements (<s>bhūtas</s>), which are the specific forms (<s>viśeṣas</s>) of the non-specific (<s>aviśeṣas</s>) — the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) of sound, touch, form, taste, and smell. Likewise, the organs of hearing, touch, sight, taste, and smell are the <s>buddhīndriyas</s> (cognitive sense organs); speech, hands, feet, excretory organ, and generative organ are the <s>karmendriyas</s> (motor organs); and the eleventh is <s>manas</s> (mind), which serves all purposes — these are the specific forms of the non-specific characterized by <s>asmitā</s> (egoism). This is the sixteenfold transformation of the <s>guṇas</s> into the specific.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[dṛśyānāṁ 'guṇānāṁ] yathāvyākhyātātmanāṁ [svarūpabhedāvadhāraṇārthaṁ] tattvāvarathābhedāvadhāraṇārthamidaṁ sūtramārabhyate – [viśeṣāviśeṣaliṅgamātrāliṅgā guṇaparvāṇaḥ ।] viśeṣāścāviśeṣāśva liṅgamātraṁ cāliṅgaśca, na liṅgati, kutaścinnāgacchati pradhānākhyo'rtha iti pacādyac sarvadhātubhya iti yaugikassanabhidheyaliṅge bhajate । yo hi cihnaparyāyo liṅgaśabda: sa napuṁsakaliṅgaḥ । sa ca karaṇasādhana iti । atha vā liṅgaṁ na vidyate, liṅgamavagamanaṁ paricchedaḥ pratyakṣeṇa pradhānākhyasyārthasyāsāvaliṅgaḥ iti bahuvrīhiḥ ॥
te ca viśeṣādayaḥ puruṣābhiprāyaṁ pālayanti bhogāpavargapradānena, pūrayanti vā vikārān svāniti piparteḥ [‘anyebhyo'pi dṛśyante'] iti kartari vanipralyayaḥ ॥ tathā ca sati yannāntamakartari tannapuṅsakam । yatu nāntaṁ kartari tatsarvaliṅgaṁ bhavati । yathā merudṛśvā merudṛśvanīti । tataśca viśeṣādayaḥ parvaṇaḥ । keṣāṁ te sambandhina iti? guṇānāṁ parvāṇo guṇaparvaṇaḥ । keṣāñcidayameva pāṭho – viśeṣāviśeṣaliṅgamātrāliṅgāni guṇaparvāṇīti ॥
[tatrākāśavāyvagnijalabhūmayo bhūtāni ।] śabdatanmātrārabdhamākāśam । sparśatanmātraṇa śabdasparśalakṣaṇenārabdho vāyu; । rūpatanmātreṇa śabdasparśarūpalakṣaṇenārabdho'gniḥ ॥ rasatanmātreṇa śabdasparśarūparasacatuṣṭayalakṣaṇenā''pa ārabdhāḥ । gandhatanmātreṇa śabdasparśarūparasagandhapañcatayalakṣaṇena bhūmirārabdhā ॥
nanu ca nityamākāśam , prāgutpattervināśakālaṁ ca viśeṣābhāvāt । yo ya utpatimāṁstasya tasya pṛthivyādeḥ prāgutpattervināśottarakālaṁ ca viśeṣo dṛṣṭaḥ । tathā ākāśaṁ yadyutpattimat syāt prāgutpattervināśottarakālaṁ ca bhavedviśeṣaḥ । na ca so'sti । tasmādākāśamanutpattikam ॥
athāvakāśadānābhāvo viśeṣa iti cenna, mūrtimato'nyasyābhāvāttulyaṁ nityatve'pi । anityalakṣaṇābhāvāca nityamākāśam, sarvagatatvādātmādivat ॥
na – āgamāvirodhāt । ["tasmādvā etasmādātmana akāśaḥ sambhūtaḥ’] ityāgamavirodhaḥ । smṛtivirodhaśca । avakāśaṁ kurvate tadupacāra iti cenna, vāyvādiṣvapyupacārapraṅgāt । [ākāśādvāyuḥ] sambhūta ityekavākyatvāt ॥
prāgutpatterviśeṣābhāvādānityo na bhavatīti ca bruvatā viśeṣābhāvānnityatvamityuktaṁ bhavati । viśeṣabhāvāccānityatvamityuktaṁ bhavati । tathā ca satyātmadīnāmapi bandhamokṣopalabdhyanupalabdhyādiviśeṣābhāvāt sato vaiśeṣikasya anityatvaprasaṅgaḥ । tathā, paramāṇvādīnāṁ cānityatvaṁ prasajyeta ॥
athāpyutpattimata eva prāgūrdhvaṁ ca viśeṣabhāvābhāvai vivakṣitāviti cet – na – ākāśasyotpatyabhyupagamaprasaṅgāt । athākāśotpativādinā viśeṣo vaktuṁ na śakyata iti cet – na – puruṣārthasādhanāsādhanatvaviśeṣāt । sarvagatatvāditi cāsiddho hetuḥ ॥
aṁsaṁrvagatāni kāladigākāśamanāṁsyanityāni ca, svārthībhāve parārthatvātū, ghaṭādivat । utpatimanti ca, pradhānapuruṣābhyāmanyatvāt, ghaṭādivat । evamākāśam [utpatimadanityaṁ ca] bāhendriyaviṣayaguṇatvāt, ghaṭādivat । bhūtatvācca, pṛthivīvat । anityadravyasaṁyogotpādyaguṇatvāt, pṛthivyādivat । cikitsānivartyaprakopakaratvāt, vāyuvat । nabhasaśca prakopaścikitsānivartanīyaścikitsakaprasiddhimupārūḍhaḥ । etenānityasādharmyaṁ vyākhyātam ॥
etāni ca [bhūtāni śabdasparśarūparasagandhatanmātrāṇāmaviśeṣāṇāṁ viśeṣāḥ ।] śāntadhoramūḍhādyanekaviśeṣavatvādviśeṣā: । śāntādyabhāvāccāviśeṣā: tanmātrāṇi ॥
[tathā śrotratvak-cakṣurjihvāghrāṇani,] śabdādiviṣayabuddhayarthavād- [buddhīndriyāṇi] svaviṣayabuddhi.ābhirevānumitāni । [vākpāṇapādapāyūpasthāni karmendriyāṇi] vacanadikriyānirvartakāni tadanumatānyeva । na vāgādīni karmandriyāṇi siddhānīti cenna, śrutiprasiddhatvāt । indriyāṇa prakṛtya [‘sarveṣāṁ vedānāṁ vāgekāyanam’] ityādiśruteḥ ॥
smṛtiṣu ca sarvatraiva vidhipratiṣedhaviṣayapravṛttinivṛttimatvācca śrotrādivadindriyatvam । [‘na vākcapalo na pāṇipādacapalaḥ’] ityādervidhipratiṣedhaviṣayapravṛttinivṛttimatvasiddhaḥ ॥
tathā, vāgādīnīdriyāṇa, kauśalayatvāt, cakṣurādivat । sarvagotraṣu cendriyaśaktiḥ karaṇavṛttyāḥ sandarśanādiṣyata eva । vāggudaprabhṛtīnāṁ sarpādīnāṁ mūkaṣaṇḍānāṁ ca mukhamevopasthendriyam । [ekādaśaṁ manaḥ sarvārtha] matītānāgatavartamānaviṣayārthaṁ buddhīndriyakarmendriyaviṣayārthaṁ ca ॥
[etānye] kādaśendriyāṇya [smitālakṣaṇasya] asmibhāvo'smitā asmīti pratyayaḥ, sa ca lakṣaṇaṁ yasya so ['smitālakṣaṇo] 'smitāpratyayena hi lakṣyate liṅgyate ṣaṣṭhamaviśeṣākhyaṁ tattvamahaṅkāraḥ । tasyā [viśeṣasya viśeṣā] etāni ॥
[guṇānāma] viśeṣākārasaṁsthitānāṁ sattvādīnā [meṣa ṣoḍaśako viśeṣapariṇāmaḥ] sattvabahulamākāśaṁ, rajobahulo vāyuḥ, satvarajobahule.o'gniḥ, [jalaṁ ca] । sattvatamobahulā pṛthivī, grāhyatvāt । tāmasatve'pyeṣāṁ guṇapradhānakṛto viśeṣaḥ । karaṇāni prakāśatvāt sattvabahulāni, mana:ṣaṣṭhāni tu buddhīdriyāṇi prakāśaprādhānyāt sattvabahulāni । karmendriyāṇi kriyāprādhānyādrajebahulāni ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['Of the seen, the <s>guṇas</s>'] — whose nature has been explained as stated — ['for the purpose of ascertaining the divisions of their essential nature'] — for the purpose of ascertaining the divisions of the categories (<s>tattvas</s>) — this <s>sūtra</s> is begun: ['The specific, the non-specific, the merely indicated, and the unindicated are the stages of the <s>guṇas</s>.'] The specific and the non-specific, the merely indicated, and the unindicated — it does not indicate, it does not come from anywhere — the entity called <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter),

body.text: ṣaḍaviśeṣāḥ। tadyathā – śabdatanmātraṁ sparśatanmātraṁ rūpatanmātraṁ rasatanmātraṁ gandhatanmātraṁ ceti ekadvitricatuḥpañcalakṣaṇāḥ śabdādayaḥ pañcāviśeṣāḥ, ṣaṣṭhaścāviśeṣo'smitāmātra iti। ete sattāmātrasyā''tmano mahataḥ ṣaḍaviśeṣapariṇāmāḥ। yattatparamaviśeṣebhyo liṅgamātraṁ mahattattvaṁ tasminnete sattāmātre mahatyātmanyavasthāya vivṛddhikāṣṭhāmanubhavanti।
body.translated_text: Six non-specific (<s>aviśeṣas</s>): namely — the <s>tanmātra</s> of sound, the <s>tanmātra</s> of touch, the <s>tanmātra</s> of form, the <s>tanmātra</s> of taste, and the <s>tanmātra</s> of smell — these are the five non-specifics characterized by one, two, three, four, and five qualities respectively, namely sound and the rest; the sixth non-specific is the mere <s>asmitā</s> (egoism). These are the six non-specific transformations of <s>mahat</s> (the great principle), whose nature is mere existence. That which is the merely indicated (<s>liṅga-mātra</s>), namely the <s>mahat-tattva</s> — in that,

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[ṣaḍaviśeṣāḥ । tadyathā śabdamātraṁ sparśamātra] miti dvilakṣaṇasyāpi pradhānena vyapadeśaḥ । tathā [rūpamātramiti] trilakṣaṇasyapi pradhānena vyapadeśaḥ । tathottarayorapi [mātra] śabdaḥ śāntaghorādiviśeṣavyāvartanārthaḥ । [ekadvitricatuḥpañcalakṣaṇabhedāḥ] śabdatattaivaikalakṣaṇaḥ śabdatanmātrabhedaḥ । śabdasparśalakṣaṇaḥ spaśatanmātrabhedaḥ, ityevamekaikādhikyenottaratrāpi draṣṭavyam । [ṣaṣṭhaścāviśeṣo'smitāmātraḥ ।] śabdāditanmātrāpekṣayā ṣaṣṭha indriyāṇāmekādaśānāmaviśeṣaḥ ॥
[ete sattvamātrasyā] stitvamātrasya [liṅgamātrasya] mūrtimātrasya, pradhānasyāmūrtasya prathamā mūrtiriyaṁ yathā bījasyāṅkurībhāvaḥ । [ātmano] vasturūpasya [mahataḥ] sarvaviśeṣāviśeṣebhyo mahattvāt [ṣaḍaviśeṣapariṇāmāḥ] ṣaḍaviśeṣā eva pariṇāmāḥ sattvādīnāṁ mahadrūpāvasthitānāmamī [aviśeṣapariṇāmāḥ ॥]
[yattatparaṁ sūkṣmamaviśeṣebhyo liṅgamātraṁ mahattattvam, tasminnete sattāmātre mahatvānmahatyavasthāya] kāraṇasvarūpe mahatyavasthāya [vivṛddhikāṣṭhāṁ] pṛthivyādiviśeṣāntatā [manubhavanti ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['Six non-specifics. Namely, the mere sound, the mere touch'] — even though it has two characteristics, it is designated by the predominant one. Likewise ['the mere form'] — even though it has three characteristics, it is designated by the predominant one. Likewise for the remaining two as well. The word ['mere' (<s>mātra</s>)] is for the purpose of excluding the specific distinctions such as tranquil (<s>śānta</s>), violent (<s>ghora</s>), and the like. ['Distinguished by one, two, three, four, and five characteristics'] — the <s>tanmātra</s> of sound has a single characteristic, the <s>tanmātra</s> of sound,

body.text: pratisaṁsṛjyamānāśca tasminneva sattāmātre mahatyātmanyavasthāya yattanniḥsattāsattaṁ niḥsadasannirasadavyaktamaliṅgaṁ pradhānaṁ tatpratiyanti। eṣa teṣāṁ liṅgamātraḥ pariṇāmo niḥsattāsattaṁ cāliṅgapariṇāma iti।
body.translated_text: And when they are being reabsorbed, they rest in that very <s>mahat</s> (great principle), whose nature is mere existence, and return to the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) — that which is beyond existence and non-existence, beyond the existent and non-existent, beyond both sat and asat, the unmanifest (<s>aliṅga</s>), <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter). This is their transformation into the merely indicated (<s>liṅga-mātra</s>), and the transformation into the unindicated (<s>aliṅga</s>) is that which is beyond existence and non-existence.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[pratisaṁsṛjyamānāśca] pratilīyamānāścāviśeṣāḥ [tasminneva sattāmātre liṅgamātre mahatyātmanyavasthāyāvyaktaṁ prati yānti ।] kiṁviśiṣṭam ? [nissattāsattaṁ] viśeṣāviśeṣadharmarahitam । [nissadasaditi] avyaktādīṣadvikṛtamiti sat, aviśeṣebhyaḥ sūkṣmataramiti cāsat, saccāsacca sadasaditi mahattattvamucyate । taddharmarahitamavyaktaṁ nissadasaditi ॥
[eṣa teṣāṁ] guṇānāṁ sattvādīnāṁ [liṅgamātraḥ pariṇāmaḥ] yasminnavasthāya vivṛddhikāṣṭhāṁ pratilayaṁ ca pratiyāntyaviśeṣāḥ । [nissattāsaktaṁ] cāvyaktaṁ [ca] yat sa teṣāmeva guṇānā [maliṅgapariṇāmaḥ ।] paraśca na sūkṣmo'vasthāntarapariṇāmo'sti guṇānām ॥ [‘sūkṣmāviṣayatvaṁ cāliṅgaparyavasānam’] iti hi vyākhyātam ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['And when being reabsorbed'] — and when the non-specifics are being dissolved — ['they rest in that very merely indicated (<s>liṅga-mātra</s>), the <s>mahat</s> whose nature is mere existence, and return to the unmanifest.'] What is its characterization? ['Beyond existence and non-existence (<s>niḥsattāsattam</s>)'] — devoid of the properties of the specific and the non-specific. ['Beyond sat and asat (<s>niḥsadasat</s>)'] — 'sat' (existent) because it is slightly modified from the unmanifest state, and 'asat' (non-existent) because it is subtler than the non-specifics — being both sat and asat, that is sadasat, namely <s>mahat</s>,

body.text: aliṅgāvasthāyāṁ na puruṣārtho heturnāliṅgāvasthāyāmādau puruṣārthatā kāraṇaṁ bhavatīti। na tasyāḥ puruṣārthatā kāraṇaṁ bhavatīti। nāsau puruṣārthakṛteti nityā''khyāyate। trayāṇāṁ tvavasthāviśeṣāṇāmādau puruṣārthatā kāraṇaṁ bhavati। sa cārtho heturnimittaṁ kāraṇaṁ bhavatītyanityā''khyāyate। guṇāstu sarvadharmānupātino na pratyastamayante nopajāyante। vyaktibhirevātītānāgatavyayāgamavatībhirguṇānvayinībhirupajananāpāyadharmakā iva pratyavabhāsante। yathā devadatto daridrāti। kasmāt। yato'sya mriyante gāva iti, gavāmeva maraṇāttasya daridrāṇaṁ na svarūpahānāditi samaḥ samādhiḥ।
body.translated_text: In the unindicated state (<s>aliṅga</s>), the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> is not the cause — in the unindicated state, at the beginning, the serving of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose does not become a cause. The serving of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose does not become a cause for that state. Therefore, that state is not brought about for <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose, and hence it is declared to be eternal. But for the three particular states, at the beginning, the serving of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose becomes the cause. And that purpose, being a cause, motive, and reason, is declared to be non-eternal. The <s>guṇas</s>, however,

body.text:
vivaraṇam
aliṅgatvādevā [liṅgāvasthāyāṁ na puruṣārtho hetuḥ ।] aliṅgāvasthānimittaṁ na puruṣārtho hetuḥ । nāliṅgāvasthā puruṣārthaprayuktetyarthaḥ । tadetat vyācaṣṭe – [nāliṅgāvasthāyāmādau puruṣārthatā kāraṇam ।] kasmāt punastadavasthā puruṣārthaprayuktā na bhavatīti ? tat āha – [yasmānnāsyāṁ puruṣārthatā kāraṇaṁ vidyate ।] svayamapi [nāsau puruṣārthatā] mahadādivadasaṁvedyatvādīśvarāṇāmapi ॥
yataścaitadevaṁ tasmā [nnityā vyākhyāyate ।] yo hi puruṣārthaprayukta: so'nityo dṛṣṭo yathā pṛthivyādiḥ । na caiṣā pradhānāvasthā puruṣārthaprayukteti nityā vyākhyāyate ॥
[trayāṇāṁ tvavasthāviśeṣāṇāṁ] viśeṣāviśeṣaliṅgamātrāṇā [mādau puruṣārthatā] mahadādyavasthā puruṣārthaprayuktā । [sa cārthaḥ] sa ca puruṣārthe [heturnirmittaṁ kāraṇamityanityā vyākhyāyante] mahadādyāstino'vasthāḥ ॥
[guṇāstu sarvadharmānupātinaḥ] sarvavikārānupātinaḥ । yathā sarpaḥ prāṁśutvasarpaṇakuṇḍalatvādiviśeṣānupātī, tathā viśeṣāditatvānupatino guṇāḥ piṇḍapratyayānupātinaśca [na pralīyante nopajāyante ।] yathā sarpaḥ kuṇḍalāditve pralīyamāne na pralīyate tadupajane ca [nopajāyate] tathaiva guṇā api । yathā ca ghaṭapiṭharādiṣu pralīyamāneṣu jāyamāneṣu ca mṛnna pralīyate nāpi jāyate ॥
[guṇā vyaktibhireva dharmairevātītānāgatavyayāgamavatībhikhrilakṣaṇābhirguṇānvayinībhirguṇopādānakāraṇabhirupajanāpāyadharmakā ivo] tpattipralayavanta iva [pratyavabhāsante] na svarūpeṇa vinaśyanti jāyante vā ॥
etasyaivārthasya dṛṣṭāntamāha – [yathā devadatto daridrāti । kasmāt ? yenāsya mriyante gāva iti । gavameva maraṇāttasya daridrāṇaṁ na svarūpahānāditi samaḥ samādhiḥ] tulyaścarco dṛṣṭāntena dārṣṭāntikasya devadattadaridrāṇavadeva guṇānugatābhivryatibhirmahadādibhirguṇavimardanavaicitryakṛtābhirvivardhamānabhirguṇānāmāḍhyatā tatpralaye ca teṣāṁ daridrāṇāṁ, na svarūpeṇāpacaya upacayo veti tulya: samādhiriti ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
Precisely because it is unindicated — ['In the unindicated state, the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s> is not the cause.'] The cause of the unindicated state is not the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>. The meaning is that the unindicated state is not motivated by <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose. He explains this — ['In the unindicated state, at the beginning, the serving of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose does not become a cause.'] But why is that state not motivated by <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose? To this he says — ['Because in this state, <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose,']

body.text: liṅgamātramaliṅgasya pratyāsannaṁ, tatra tatsaṁsṛṣṭaṁ vivicyate kramānativṛtteḥ। tathā ṣaḍaviśeṣā liṅgamātre saṁsṛṣṭā vivicyante pariṇāmakramaniyamāt। tathā teṣvaviśeṣeṣu bhūtendriyāṇi saṁsṛṣṭāni vivicyante। tathā coktaṁ purastāt। na viśeṣebhyaḥ paraṁ tattvāntaramastīti viśeṣāṇāṁ nāsti tattvāntarapariṇāmaḥ। teṣāṁ tu dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāpariṇāmā vyākhyāyiṣyante ॥ 19 ॥
body.translated_text: The merely indicated (<s>liṅga-mātra</s>) is proximate to the unindicated (<s>aliṅga</s>); therein, what is merged in it is differentiated first, because the order of evolution cannot be transgressed. Likewise, the six non-specifics, merged in the merely indicated, are differentiated according to the fixed order of transformation. Likewise, in those non-specifics, the elements and sense organs that are merged are differentiated. And thus it has been stated earlier. Since there is no further category beyond the specifics, the specifics have no further category transformation.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
sarvasya pradhānakāryatve sati viśeṣā aviśeṣā vā kasmādanantaraṁ nopajāyanta iti tadāha – [liṅgasyāliṅgaṁ pratyāsannaṁ] yathā mūlaṁ vṛkṣasya pratyāsannaṁ bīje saṁsṛṣṭaṁ mūlameva prathamataraṁ vivicyate, na vṛkṣasyottarāvasthā । evaṁ tanna pradhāne tat liṅgaṁ [saṁsṛṣṭaṁ] saṁlīnaṁ prathamaṁ [vivicyate] āvirbhavati nottare viśeṣā viprakṛṣṭatvādeva । tadevāha – [kramānatipatteḥ] kramānatikramāt । na hi loke kasyacidutpadyamānasya kramātilaṅghanamasti ॥
[tathā ṣaḍaviśeṣāḥ] pūrvottā [liṅgamātre] pratyāsannatvāt [saṁsṛṣṭatvādvivicyante ।] kasmādityāha – [pariṇāmakramaniyamāt । tathā teṣvaviśeṣeṣu bhūtendriyāṇi ।] tanmātreṣu bhūtāni saṁsṛṣṭāni vivicyante । asmitāmātre indriyāṇi manassahitāni ॥
[tathā coktaṁ purastāt । na viśeṣebhyaḥ] prāguktebhya ākāśādibhyaḥ [paraṁ tattvāntaramasti ।] na viśeṣāṇāmanyastattvāntarapariṇāma ityarthaḥ । etadevāha – [viśeṣāṇāṁ nāsti tattvāntaramiti ।] tattvaṁ hi nāma sādhāraṇaṁ sarvaprāṇadhāriṇāmāmahāpralayasthāyi । nairvilakṣaṇaṁ pṛthivyādibhya utpadyamānamanyadasti । dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāpariṇāmāstu bhavantyeveti । [teṣāṁ tu] viśeṣāṇāṁ [dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāpariṇāmā vyākhyāyiṣyante] tṛtīyapade ॥ 19 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
Given that everything is an effect of <s>Pradhāna</s>, why do the specifics or non-specifics not arise immediately? To this he says — ['The indicated (<s>liṅga</s>) is proximate to the unindicated (<s>aliṅga</s>).'] Just as the root of a tree, being proximate to the seed and merged in it, is differentiated first — not the later state of the tree — so too that indicated (<s>liṅga</s>), [merged] and dissolved in <s>Pradhāna</s>, is first

body.text: vyākhyātaṁ dṛśyamatha draṣṭuḥ svarūpāvadhāraṇārthamidamārabhyate –
body.translated_text: The seen (<s>dṛśya</s>) has been explained. Now, for the purpose of ascertaining the essential nature of the seer (<s>draṣṭṛ</s>), the following is begun —

body.text: draṣṭā dṛśimātraḥ śuddho'pi pratyayānupaśyaḥ ॥ 20 ॥
body.translated_text: The seer (<s>draṣṭṛ</s>) is mere seeing (<s>dṛśi-mātra</s>); though pure, it witnesses through cognitions (<s>pratyaya</s>). || 20 ||

body.text: dṛśimātra iti dṛkśaktireva viśeṣaṇāparāmṛṣṭetyarthaḥ। sa puruṣo buddheḥ pratisaṁvedī। sa buddherna sarūpo nātyantaṁ virūpa iti। na tāvatsarūpaḥ। kasmāt। jñātājñātaviṣayatvātpariṇāminī hi buddhiḥ। tasyāśca viṣayo gavādirghaṭādirvā jñātaścājñātaśceti pariṇāmitvaṁ darśayati। sadājñātaviṣayatvaṁ tu puruṣasyāpariṇāmitvaṁ paridīpayati। kasmāt। nahi buddhiśca nāma puruṣaviṣayaśca syādagṛhītā gṛhītā ceti siddhaṁ puruṣasya sadājñātaviṣayatvaṁ tataścāpariṇāmitvamiti।
body.translated_text: 'Mere seeing' (<s>dṛśi-mātra</s>) means the power of seeing alone, unqualified by any other attribute — that is the meaning. That <s>Puruṣa</s> is the experiencer of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect). He is neither identical in form with <s>buddhi</s> nor entirely different from it. First, he is not identical. Why? Because <s>buddhi</s> is subject to transformation, having known and unknown objects as its domain. Its object — whether a cow and the like or a pot and the like — being known or unknown, demonstrates its transformative nature. But <s>Puruṣa</s>'s having an always-known object

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[vyākhyātaṁ dṛśyam] avaghṛtaṁ dṛśyam । yadarthaṁ ca dṛśyate tasyedānīṁ [draṣṭuḥ svarūpāvadhāraṇārthamidabhārabhyate – draṣṭā dṛśimātraḥ śuddho'pi pratyayānupaśyaḥ draṣṭā] dṛśyasya yathāvyākhyātarūpasyopalabdhā puruṣaḥ । tasyedaṁ lakṣaṇaṁ [dṛśimātraḥ śuddho'pi pratyayānupaśya] śceti । purastādākhyātam – [‘tadā draṣṭuḥ svarūpe'vasthānam' 'vṛttisārūpyamitaratra’] iti ca, tadeva dvayamiha pratipādyate ॥
yaccoktaṁ [pratisaṁvedī buddheḥ puruṣa ityupapādayiṣyāma] iti, taccātropapādyate । dṛśirdarśanamupalabdhistāvanmātro [dṛśimātraḥ ।] yata evaṁ tasmācchuddhaḥ । śuddho'pi sannasau bauddhasya [pratyayasyānupaśyaḥ,] dṛśimātratvādeva । tasmāttamanupaśyan tatsvarūpo bhavati । dṛśisannidhau vṛtterdṛśisvarūpāvabhāsatā draṣṭurvṛttisārūpyam ॥
dṛśimātrasyaivāvikriyātmakasya sato'sya bauddhapratyayānudarśanaṁ yasmātasmācca svarūpapratiṣṭhatā ca siddhā । [pratyayānupaśya iti ।] etattu tadastitvānumānam । katham ? ghaṭādīnāṁ dṛśyānāṁ svarūpavyatiriktenānyena dṛśyatvadarśanāt , tatprakāśakānāṁ ca ālekādīnāṁ vyatiriktadṛśyatvāt , sarvārthāvabhāsakānāmapi pratyayānāṁ svarūpavyatiriktadṛśyatvaṁ dṛśyatvādavagamyate ghaṭāditadālokādivaditi ॥
yasmācca bauddhameva pratyayamanupaśyati, taṁ ca paśyatyeva, na kadācit svaviṣayaṁ pratyayaṁ na paśyati, tasmāddṛśimātraḥ । mātragrahaṇaṁ dharmāntaranivartanārtham । etena draṣṭurdṛśirityetannivartitamicchādisamānāśrayatvaṁ ca nivartitaṁ, dṛśereva draṣṭṛtvāt । tadetaducyate – [dṛśimātra iti । dṛkchaktireva] dṛgdarśanaṁ tadeva śaktirdṛkchaktiḥ । nāpyanyo dṛkchaktimānasti । saiva śaktirdṛgiti । tatra mātraśabdārthaṁ vyācaṣṭe – [viśeṣeṇāparāmṛṣṭetyarthaḥ ।] viśeṣeṇa kenacidicchādinā guṇairguṇadharmeśvāparāmṛṣṭaḥ ॥
[sa puruṣo buddheḥ] pratisaṁvedituṁ śīlamasyeti [pratisaṁvedī ।] bauddhapralayopalabdhisvabhāva ityarthaḥ । puruṣo buddhe: pratisaṁvedī dṛśimātraḥ śuddhaśreti kathaṁ gamyata ityāha – [sa buddherna sarūpo nātyantaṁ virūpa] iti । na samānalakṣaṇo nāpyatyantavidharmetyetat । asarūpatayā dṛśimātratrva śuddhatvaṁ cāha । nātyantavirūpa iti vṛttisārūpyatāmāha ॥
kathaṁ punaḥ na sarūpateti ? ucyate – [na tāvat sarūpaḥ ।] kasmāt ? ko hetuḥ ? । buddhestāvat svarūpaṁ vaidharmyadarśanārthamāha— [jñātājñātaviṣayatvāt pariṇāminī buddhirita ।] kaḥ punarasau buddherviṣayo yo jñātaścājñātaścetyāha – [tasyāstu viṣayo gavādirghaṭādiśca jñātaścājñātaśca ।] yena bāhyākāreṇa pariṇatā buddhiḥ sa jñātaḥ । yenākāreṇa na pariṇatā so'jñātaḥ ॥
yadi na pariṇametāpariṇamamānā cedviṣayaṁ vikhyāpayet sadaiva viṣayitvaṁ buddheḥ syāt । tasmāt jñātājñātaviṣayatā pariṇāmitvaṁ khyāpayati । pariṇāminī buddhiḥ, jñātājñātaviṣayatvāt । dīpacakṣurādi(viṣaya)vat ॥
tadvilakṣaṇaḥ puruṣaḥ sadā jñātaviṣayaḥ । sarvadā hi jñāta eva puruṣasya svo viṣayaḥ । tasmāt [sadā jñātaviṣayatvaṁ puruṣasyāpariṇāmitvaṁ paridīpayati ।] sadā jñātaviṣayatvamasiddhaṁ puruṣasyetyāśaṅkayāha – [kasmāt ?] ko hetuḥ ? [na hī] ti [hi] śabdaḥ prasiddhāvadyotanārthaḥ । [buddhiśca nāma] buddhiriti bauddhapratyayaḥ, [puruṣasya viṣayaḥ syādagṛhītā gṛhītā ceti ।] sarvadā ca gṛhīta eva bauddhaḥ pratyayaḥ । tadavyabhicāreṇaiva puruṣasya vyatiriktatvasiddhiḥ । tasmāt puruṣasya sadā jñātaviṣayatvam । tataścāpariṇāmitvaṁ siddham । apariṇāmī puruṣa iti pratijñā । sadā jñātaviṣayatvāditi hetuḥ । vaidharmyadṛṣṭānto buddhayādiḥ ॥
nanu ca buddhyā vyavasitamarthaṁ puruṣaścetayati, buddheśca sarvo viṣayo jñātaścājñātaśca puruṣasyāpi samānaḥ । jñātājñātaviṣayatvaṁ buddhyā vyavasitārthopalambhitvāt । tasmāt puruṣasyāpi pariṇāmitvaṁ jñātājñātaviṣayatvādbuddhivadeva ॥
naiṣa doṣaḥ । buddhereva puruṣaviṣayatvāt । buddhireva hi bāhyārthākārā puruṣasya viṣayo nārthaḥ kevalaḥ kharūpeṇa । tasmānna jñātājñātaviṣayaḥ puruṣaḥ । buddhistu sadaiva jñātaiveti na pariṇāmitvaṁ puruṣasya ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['The seen has been explained'] — the seen has been thoroughly examined. And now, for the purpose for which it is seen — ['for the purpose of ascertaining the essential nature of the seer, the following is begun — The seer is mere seeing; though pure, it witnesses through cognitions. The seer'] — <s>Puruṣa</s>, the perceiver of the seen whose nature has been explained as described. This is its definition: ['mere seeing, though pure, witnessing through cognitions.']

body.text: kiṁ ca parārthā buddhiḥ saṁhatyakāritvāt, svārthaḥ puruṣa iti। tathā sarvārthādhyavasāyakatvāttriguṇā buddhistriguṇatvādacetaneti। guṇānāṁ tūpadraṣṭā puruṣa ityato na sarūpaḥ।
body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) serves another's purpose because it acts in combination, while <s>Puruṣa</s> is self-purposeful. Likewise, because <s>buddhi</s> determines the meaning of all things, it consists of the three <s>guṇas</s>; and because it consists of the three <s>guṇas</s>, it is insentient. But <s>Puruṣa</s> is the witness of the <s>guṇas</s> — therefore he is not identical in form.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
nanu ca buddhayā vyavasitamarthaṁ puruṣaścetayatīti kaścidāha । tat katham ? ucyate – na – tairapyapariṇāmitvasyābhyupagamāt puruṣasya । buddhayā vyavasitamarthamityetaduktaṁ bhavati – buddhyākāraṁ cetayati buddhivyavasāyākārāpannamarthaṁ cetayatīti । anyathā hi teṣāṁ pariṇāmitvaparārthatvasaṁhatyakārivādayo buddhidharmāḥ sarva eva prasajeyuḥ ॥
athāpariṇāmitve darśanānupapattiriti cet – na – darśanasaiyaiva puruṣasvarūpatvāt । yo hi puruṣapariṇāmitvamabhimanyate, sa idaṁ praṣṭavyaḥ – kiṁ pariṇāmena kriyata iti ॥
sa cedabhidadhīta – darśanamiti । sa pratyabhidhānīyaḥ – puruṣasya darśanameva rūpam, ataḥ pariṇāmānarthakyamiti ॥
sa cet pratibrūyāt – na puruṣasyopalabdhirbhogaḥ, kastarhi ? vikriyaiva bhoga iti - sa punarvaktavyaḥ – tathāpi vikriyāvattvādanityattvamupanataṁ śarīrādivadeva ॥
athāpi pratibhāṣeta – svātmani vikriyā nānityatvakāraṇaṁ syāt , kiṁ tvavasthāntarabhāvivikriyā hi kāraṇamanityatvasyeti । sa puna: pratibhāṣitavyaḥ – vikriyāvasthāyā evāvasthāntaratvāt । pūrvamavikṛtasya vastunaḥ punarvikriyā avasthāntaram ॥
kiṁ ca – viṣayābhyupagame ca vikriyaiva, tāvatā niyamaḥ pāryete na kartum । na cāpi svātmani vikriyamāṇānāṁ vajravaidūryādīnāmanityatvaṁ nāsti । na ca vikriyājanitasyaiva darśanasya dṛśyaviṣayatvaṁ na nityasya darśanasyeti niyamaheturasti । vikriyaivopalabdhirna vikriyājaniteti cet – na – śarīrādīnāṁ vikriyāvatāmupalabdhiprasaṅgāt ॥
tasmāddṛśimātra evāpariṇāmī ca, sadā jñātaviṣayatvāt puruṣa iti siddham । tasya ca nityopalabdhisvarūpatve'pi dṛśyabauddhapratyayabhāvābhāvikṛto'yaṁ vyapadeśaḥ paśyati darśayiṣyati dadarśeti ca । savitrādiprakāśanavyapadeśavat । yathā prakāśayati savitā prakāśayiṣyati prācīkaśaditi ca prakāśyabhāvābhāvakṛto vyapadeśaḥ । śuddhatvādayo hetavo vaidharmyeṇa buddhayādayo dṛṣṭāntāḥ ॥
itaśvāsurūpaḥ । [sarvārthādhyavasāyitvādgho] raśāntādisamastārthāvasāyitvāt [triguṇā buddhiḥ] śrotrādivat । [guṇānāṁ tūpadraṣṭe] tyupadraṣṭṛtvaṁ hetuḥ । [atriguṇaḥ puruṣa] iti pratijñā । vaidharmyeṇa buddhaśyādireva dṛṣṭānto'triguṇatvāccāsarūpaḥ ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
Now, someone says that <s>Puruṣa</s> cognizes the object determined by <s>buddhi</s> (intellect). How is that? It is replied — no — because even they (the opponents) accept the non-transformability of <s>Puruṣa</s>. What is meant by 'the object determined by <s>buddhi</s>' is this — he cognizes the form of <s>buddhi</s>, he cognizes the object that has assumed the form of <s>buddhi</s>'s determination. Otherwise, all the properties of <s>buddhi</s> — transformability, existing for another's purpose, acting in conjunction, etc. — would absurdly apply to them as well.
If it be objected that seeing (<s>darśana</s>) is impossible without transformation — no — because seeing itself is the very nature of <s>Puruṣa</s>. He who maintains that <s>Puruṣa</s> undergoes transformation should be asked — what is produced by the transformation?
If he were to answer — 'seeing' — then he should be told: seeing is the very nature of <s>Puruṣa</s>, hence transformation is purposeless.
If he were to reply — 'The apprehension of <s>Puruṣa</s> is not experience; what then? Modification itself is experience' — he should again be told: even so, impermanence would follow from the fact of being subject to modification, just as with the body and so on.
Even if he were to respond — 'Modification within one's own self would not be the cause of impermanence; rather, modification that brings about a different state is the cause of impermanence' — he should be answered thus: because the state of modification itself constitutes a different state. For a thing previously unmodified, subsequent modification is a different state.
Moreover, even if one accepts modification with respect to objects, no such restriction can be established. Nor is it the case that diamonds, <s>vaidūrya</s> gems, and the like, which undergo modification within themselves, are not impermanent. Nor is there any ground for restricting that only seeing born of modification has visible objects as its domain, and not eternal seeing. If it be said that apprehension is modification itself, not born of modification — no — because that would entail that bodies and such, which undergo modification, would also have apprehension.
Therefore, it is established that <s>Puruṣa</s> is mere seeing (<s>dṛśimātra</s>), non-transforming, and always has objects of knowledge. Even though his nature is eternal apprehension, the conventional usage 'he sees,' 'he will see,' 'he saw' is occasioned by the presence or absence of the visible intellectual cognitions (<s>dṛśya-bauddha-pratyaya</s>). This is like the conventional usage of illumination regarding the sun and others — just as 'the sun illuminates,' 'it will illuminate,' 'it illuminated' is occasioned by the presence or absence of what is to be illuminated. Purity and so forth are the reasons; by dissimilarity, <s>buddhi</s> and the rest are the examples.
And thus his dissimilar nature: [Because of determining all objects] — because of determining all objects ending with the terrible (<s>ghora</s>) and the tranquil (<s>śānta</s>) — [<s>buddhi</s> is of three <s>guṇas</s>], like the ear and other sense organs. ['But the overseeing of the <s>guṇas</s>'] — the overseeing is the reason. ['<s>Puruṣa</s> is without the three <s>guṇas</s>'] — this is the proposition. By dissimilarity, <s>buddhi</s> itself serves as the example, and because of being without the three <s>guṇas</s>, he is of dissimilar nature.

body.text: astu tarhi virūpa iti। nātyantaṁ virūpaḥ। kasmāt, śuddho'pyasau pratyayānupaśyo yataḥ। pratyayaṁ bauddhamanupaśyati, tamanupaśyannatadātmā'pi tadātmaka iva pratyavabhāsate। tathā coktam - apariṇāminī hi bhoktṛśaktirapratisaṁkramā ca pariṇāminyarthe pratisaṁkrānteva tadvṛttimanupatati, tasyāśca prāptacaitanyopagraharūpāyā buddhivṛtteranukāramātratayā buddhivṛttyaviśiṣṭā hi jñānavṛttirityākhyāyate ॥ 20 ॥
body.translated_text: Let him then be of dissimilar form — [he is] not completely dissimilar. Why? Because, though pure, he perceives cognitions (<s>pratyaya</s>). He perceives the intellectual cognition (<s>bauddha pratyaya</s>), and perceiving it, though not of its nature, he appears as if of its nature. And thus it has been stated: 'The experiencer-power (<s>bhoktṛ-śakti</s>), being non-transforming and non-transmigrating, follows the modification of the transforming object as though it had transmigrated into it; and that cognitive activity (<s>jñāna-vṛtti</s>), being merely an imitation (<s>anukāra-mātratā</s>) of that <s>buddhi</s>-modification which has attained the form of receiving consciousness (<s>caitanya-upagraha</s>), is called indistinguishable from the <s>buddhi</s>-modification.' ॥ 20 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[astu tarhi virūpa] eva । tataścātyantavirūpatvādbhogānupapattiriti । atrocyate – [nātyantaṁ virūpaḥ । kasmāt ?] ke.o'tra hetuḥ ? na hi śuddhasya buddhisvarūpavirūpasyāśuddhabai.auddhapratyayādatyantāvairūpyasiddhaye heturityabhiprāyaḥ ॥
na – buddhipratyayasākṣitvasya siddhatvāt । [yataḥ śuddho'pyasau bauddhaṁ pratyayamanupaśyati] tacca bauddhapratyayānudarśanaṁ sādhitam । [anupaśyatīti] viṣayākārapariṇāme sati bauddhaṁ pratyayaṁ paśyatītyarthaḥ । [tamanupaśyannapi na tadātmā] na triguṇaḥ । [tadātmaka iva] śāntaghoramūḍhavyavasāyarūpa iva [pratyavabhāsate ।] tasmānnātyantavirūpa: pravṛttisārūpyāt । tatra yaduktaṁ buddheḥ [pratisaṁvedī puruṣa ityupapādayiṣyāmaḥ] iti, tadupapāditam । tathā ca tatsārūpyamādarśitam । tathoktaṁ tantre – [apariṇāminī bhoktṛśaktiḥ] –dṛkchaktiryathāvyākhyātarūpā [apratisaṅkramā ca pariṇāminyarthe] bauddhe pratyaye pratisaṅkrānteva pratyayaviṣayatvāt tadvṛttimanupatantīva asyā buddhervṛttimanupatantīva draṣṭratvādupalabhamānā । bauddhaḥ pratyayo jāyamāna eva dṛkchakteḥ karmatāmāpadyate । tamanupatantyupalabhamānā bhoktṛśaktiḥ [tasyāśca prāptacaitanyopagraharūpāyāḥ] prāptaṁ caitanyopagraharūpaṁ puruṣopagraharūpai yayā buddhivṛtyā āsāditaṁ pāvakopagraharūpataptalohapiṇḍavaddṛgśikarmamaitvādeva [anukāramātratayā] buddhivṛttisārūpyamātratayā [buddhivṛtyaviśiṣṭā jñavṛttiriti] jña evopalabdhireva [vṛttirityākhyāyate ॥ 20 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['Let him then be of dissimilar form'] entirely. And from being completely dissimilar, experience (<s>bhoga</s>) would be impossible. To this it is replied — ['He is not completely dissimilar. Why?'] What is the reason here? The intention is that there is no reason for establishing complete non-dissimilarity of the pure one, who is dissimilar to the nature of <s>buddhi</s>, from the impure intellectual cognition.
No — because his being the witness of intellectual cognitions is established. ['Because, though pure, he perceives the intellectual cognition (<s>bauddha pratyaya</s>)'] — and that perceiving of intellectual cognitions has been proven. ['Perceives' means] when there is transformation into the form of an object, he sees the intellectual cognition — this is the meaning. ['Though perceiving it, he is not of its nature'] — he is not of the three <s>guṇas</s>. ['As if of its nature'] — as if of the form of tranquil (<s>śānta</s>), terrible (<s>ghora</s>), and deluding (<s>mūḍha</s>) determinations, ['he appears.'] Therefore he is not completely dissimilar, due to similarity with activity. Regarding what was stated — 'We shall establish that <s>Puruṣa</s> is the experiencer (<s>pratisaṁvedī</s>) of <s>buddhi</s>' — that has been established. And thus the similarity with it has been shown. As stated in the doctrine — ['The experiencer-power (<s>bhoktṛ-śakti</s>) is non-transforming'] — the power of seeing (<s>dṛk-śakti</s>), whose nature is as already explained, ['non-transmigrating into the transforming object'] — into the intellectual cognition, as though having transmigrated, due to being the object of cognition, appearing as though it follows its modification — as though following the modification of this <s>buddhi</s>, apprehending by virtue of being the seer. The intellectual cognition, as it arises, assumes the status of being the object of the seeing-power. The experiencer-power, apprehending by following it — ['of that <s>buddhi</s>-modification which has attained the form of receiving consciousness (<s>caitanya-upagraha</s>)'] — that <s>buddhi</s>-modification which has attained the form of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s reception, like a heated iron ball attaining the form of fire's reception, due to being the object of seeing — ['by mere imitation (<s>anukāra-mātratā</s>)'] — by mere similarity to the <s>buddhi</s>-modification — ['indistinguishable from the <s>buddhi</s>-modification, the cognition of the knower (<s>jña</s>)'] — apprehension itself — ['is called activity (<s>vṛtti</s>).' ॥ 20 ॥]

body.text: tadartha eva dṛśyasyā''tmā ॥ 21 ॥
body.translated_text: The self (<s>ātman</s>) of the seen (<s>dṛśya</s>) exists for the sake of that (the seer) alone. ॥ 21 ॥

body.text: dṛśirūpasya puruṣasya karmarūpatāmāpannaṁ dṛśyamiti tadartha eva dṛśyasyā''tmā bhavati। svarūpaṁ bhavatītyarthaḥ। svarūpaṁ tu pararūpeṇa pratilabdhātmakaṁ bhogāpavargārthatāyāṁ kṛtāyāṁ puruṣeṇa na dṛśyata iti। svarūpahānādasya nāśaḥ prāpto na tu vinaśyati ॥ 21 ॥
body.translated_text: The seen (<s>dṛśya</s>), having assumed the status of being the object of <s>Puruṣa</s> who is of the nature of seeing (<s>dṛśi</s>), exists for the sake of that alone — the self (<s>ātman</s>) of the seen is its own nature (<s>svarūpa</s>). This is the meaning. But its own nature, having attained its being through the other's form, is not seen by <s>Puruṣa</s> when its purpose of providing experience (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) has been fulfilled. From the loss of its own nature, its destruction would follow — but it does not actually perish. ॥ 21 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tadartha eva dṛśyasyātmā ta] cchabdena draṣṭā dṛśimātraḥ śuddho yathādhigatātmā pratyāmnāyate । tadarthaḥ tasmai tadarthastatprayojanaḥ dṛśikarmatvārtha ityarthaḥ । bhogarūpeṇāpavargarūpeṇa ca । ko'sāvityāha – [dṛśyasyātmā] pradhānasyātmā svarūpe svarūpalābha iti ॥
nanu caturvyūhatvaṁ vyācikhyāsitaṁ kimarthametadaprakṛtamucyate । naiṣa doṣaḥ । ātyantikaduḥkhanivṛttiprayojanasya prakṛtatvāt । kathaṁ dṛśyatādarthyalābhāvadhāraṇenātyantikī duḥkhaviratiruktā bhavediti । ucyate – yadi dṛśyasvarūpapratilaibhastadartha eva, tadā aśeṣatadarthaviratau punaḥ kṛtārthatvāt kāryābhāvādātyantikadṛśyaviratiḥ syāt । tasya punaḥ pravṛttau prayojanābhāvāt । na hi kṛtameva punaḥ karaṇīyakamupāśnute । atha tu svārtho'pi dṛśyasyātmalābho'bhaviṣyadataḥ svārthasya bhāvāt punaḥ punaḥ prāvartiṣyata । tataśca nātyantikī nivṛttiḥ । tasmāttādarthyamevāvadhāryete ॥
dṛśyātmalābhasya svārthābhāvaśca dṛśyasya bhogyatvāt odanādivat siddhaḥ, acetanatvātsaṁhatyakārivācca । tadāha – [dṛśirūpasya puruṣasya karmaviṣayatāmāpannaṁ dṛśyamiti ।] itiśabdo hetvarthe । [tadartha eva dṛśyasyātmā bhavati svarūpaṁ bhavatītyarthaḥ ।] puruṣārtha eva pradhānasyātmalābho dṛśikarmatāpatterodanādivat ॥
sūtraprayojanamācaṣṭa idānīm – [tataśca] tādarthyasya niyatatvāt kāraṇāt [puruṣarūpeṇa pratilabdhātmakaṁ] prāptacaitanyopagraharūpaṁ [sadbhogāpavagīrthatāyāṁ kṛtāyāṁ puruṣeṇa na dṛśyate ।] bhogāpavargavyatirekeṇa kartavyābhāvāt ॥ 21 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['The self of the seen exists for the sake of that'] — by the word 'that,' the seer (<s>draṣṭā</s>), who is mere seeing (<s>dṛśimātra</s>), pure, whose nature has been ascertained, is referred back to. 'For the sake of that' means: for him, having him as its purpose, having the purpose of being the object of seeing — this is the meaning. In the form of experience (<s>bhoga</s>) and in the form of liberation (<s>apavarga</s>). Who is this? He says — ['the self of the seen'] — the self (<s>ātman</s>) of <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial nature), its own nature, meaning the attainment of its own form.
Now, the fourfold arrangement was intended to be explained — why is this unrelated topic being stated? This is no fault, because the cessation of ultimate suffering is the topic at hand. How can the ultimate cessation of suffering be stated through the determination of the purpose-serving nature of the seen? It is replied — if the attainment of the seen's own nature exists for that (the seer's) sake alone, then upon the complete cessation of all its purposes, there would be ultimate cessation of the seen, because there is no further function, its purpose being fulfilled. For what has already been accomplished does not require being accomplished again. But if the self-attainment of the seen were also for its own sake, then because of its own purpose remaining, it would continue to operate again and again. And then there would be no ultimate cessation. Therefore, it is precisely its purposive nature that is to be ascertained.
The absence of self-purpose in the seen's self-attainment is established because the seen is an object of enjoyment, like cooked rice and the like, and because it is insentient and acts in conjunction. Thus he says — ['The seen, having assumed the status of being the object of <s>Puruṣa</s> who is of the nature of seeing.'] The word 'thus' (<s>iti</s>) has the sense of reason. ['The self of the seen exists for the sake of that alone — its own nature exists, this is the meaning.'] The self-attainment of <s>Pradhāna</s> serves <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose alone, due to its assuming the status of being the object of seeing, like cooked rice and the like.
Now he states the purpose of the <s>sūtra</s> — ['And therefore,'] because the purposive nature is established, ['that which has attained its being through <s>Puruṣa</s>'s form'] — having attained the form of receiving <s>Puruṣa</s>'s consciousness — ['when the purpose of experience and liberation has been fulfilled, it is not seen by <s>Puruṣa</s>.'] Because there is nothing further to be done beyond experience and liberation. ॥ 21 ॥

body.text: kasmāt –
body.translated_text: Because —

body.text: kṛtārthaṁ prati naṣṭamapyanaṣṭaṁ tadanyasādhāraṇatvāt ॥ 22 ॥
body.translated_text: Though destroyed for one who has fulfilled their purpose, [the seen] is not destroyed, because of being common to others. ॥ 22 ॥

body.text: kṛtārthamekaṁ puruṣaṁ prati dṛśyaṁ naṣṭamapi nāśaṁ prāptamapyanaṣṭaṁ tadanyapuruṣasādhāraṇatvāt। kuśalaṁ puruṣaṁ prati nāśaṁ prāptamapyakuśalānpuruṣānprati na kṛtārthamiti teṣāṁ dṛśeḥ karmaviṣayatāmāpannaṁ labhata eva pararūpeṇā''tmarūpamiti। ataśca dṛgdarśanaśaktyornityatvādanādiḥ saṁyogo vyākhyāta iti। tathā coktam –rdhamiṇāmanādisaṁyogāddharmamātrāṇāmapyanādiḥ saṁyoga iti ॥ 22 ॥
body.translated_text: For one <s>Puruṣa</s> who has fulfilled his purpose (<s>kṛtārtha</s>), the seen (<s>dṛśya</s>), though having reached destruction, is not destroyed, because it is common to other <s>Puruṣas</s>. Even though it has reached destruction with respect to an accomplished <s>Puruṣa</s>, it has not fulfilled its purpose with respect to unaccomplished <s>Puruṣas</s>; therefore, having assumed the status of being the object of seeing for them, it attains its own nature through the other's form. And thus, because the powers of the seer and seeing are eternal, their beginningless conjunction has been explained. And thus it has been stated — 'From the beginningless conjunction of substances (<s>dharmin</s>), the conjunction of their qualities (<s>dharma</s>) alone with <s>Puruṣas</s> is also beginningless.' ॥ 22 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
sūtrasambandhaṁ karoti – yaṁ puruṣaṁ prati caritārthaṁ dṛśyaṁ, taṁ prati dṛśikarmatāṁ nāpatsyata iti svarūpahānam, ataśca [svarūpahānādasya vināśaḥ prāptaḥ । na tu vinaśyati] sarvātmanā । [kasmāt ?] ko hetuḥ ? pradhānānāṁ pratipuruṣaṁ bahutvāt kṛtārthaṅ prati naṣṭameveti manyate ॥
[kṛtārthaṁ prati naṣṭamapyanaṣṭaṁ tadanyasādhāraṇatvāt । kṛtārthaṁ] yaṁ puruṣaṁ prati bhogāpavarganirvartanena kṛtaprayojana [tamekaṁ puruṣaṁ prati] punaḥ kāryakaraṇarūpeṇāpravartanādbhāvābhāvayoraviśeṣā [nnaṣṭamapi ।] asya vyākhyānaṁ [nāśaprāptamapīti । anaṣṭaṁ tadanyapuruṣasādhāraṇatvāt ।] yān pratyakṛtārthaṁ tān pratyanaṣṭam ॥
kathamanaṣṭamityāha-- [kuśalapuruṣān prati nāśaprāptaṁ] bhogāpavargapradānena kuśalapuruṣānprati kṛtaprayojanam । [akuśalapuruṣān prati akṛtārthaṁ] bhogāpavargayoḥ kartavyayorakṛtatvā [tteṣāma] kuśalānāṁ [dṛśeḥ] ta eva dṛśistasyāḥ [karmatāṁ dṛśyatāmāpannaṁ labhata eva puruṣarūpeṇa] puruṣanirbhāsatayā [ātmarūpami] ti । ataśca sādhāraṇatvādekameva pradhānaṁ pṛthivyādivat । kāryakaraṇānāṁ ca bhinnatvāt puruṣāṇāṁ nānātvaṁ siddham । sukhaduḥkhanānātvācca puruṣabhedasiddhiḥ ॥
[ataśca dṛgdarśanaśaktyornityatvādanādiḥ saṁyogo vyākhyātaḥ । tathā coktaṁ tantre – dharmiṇāmanādisaṁyogāt] guṇānāṁ puruṣāṇāṁ cānādisaṁyogā [ddharmamātrāṇāṁ] mahadādikāryakaraṇāntānāmapi [puruṣairanādiḥ saṁyogo] dharmibhirdharmāṇāmabhihrutvāt ॥ 22 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
He establishes the connection with the <s>sūtra</s> — that <s>Puruṣa</s> for whom the seen has fulfilled its purpose, with respect to him it would not assume the status of being the object of seeing — this constitutes the loss of its own nature, and therefore ['from the loss of its own nature, its destruction would follow. But it does not perish'] entirely. ['Why?'] What is the reason? Because of the multiplicity of <s>Pradhānas</s> corresponding to each <s>Puruṣa</s>, one might think it is simply destroyed for one who has fulfilled his purpose.
['Though destroyed for one who has fulfilled their purpose, it is not destroyed, because of being common to others. For one who has fulfilled his purpose'] — for that <s>Puruṣa</s> whose purpose has been fulfilled through providing experience and liberation — ['for that one <s>Puruṣa</s>'] — because it does not operate again in the form of body and instruments, there being no difference between existence and non-existence — ['though destroyed.'] The explanation of this is: ['though having reached destruction. Not destroyed, because of being common to other <s>Puruṣas</s>.'] For those with respect to whom its purpose is unfulfilled, for them it is not destroyed.
How is it not destroyed? He says — ['Though having reached destruction with respect to accomplished <s>Puruṣas</s>'] — whose purpose has been fulfilled through providing experience and liberation. ['With respect to unaccomplished <s>Puruṣas</s>, its purpose is unfulfilled'] — because the tasks of experience and liberation remain to be accomplished. ['Of those'] unaccomplished ones, ['assuming the status of being the object of seeing, it attains'] indeed ['its own nature through <s>Puruṣa</s>'s form'] — through appearing as <s>Puruṣa</s>. And therefore, due to being common, <s>Pradhāna</s> is one alone, like the earth and so on. And because of the diversity of body-and-instrument complexes, the multiplicity of <s>Puruṣas</s> is established. And from the diversity of pleasure and pain, the distinction of <s>Puruṣas</s> is proven.
['And thus, because the powers of seer and seeing are eternal, their beginningless conjunction has been explained. And thus it has been stated in the doctrine — from the beginningless conjunction of substances (<s>dharmin</s>)'] — from the beginningless conjunction of the <s>guṇas</s> and <s>Puruṣas</s> — ['of the qualities (<s>dharma</s>) alone'] — of the effects ending with the great (<s>mahat</s>) and the body-instrument complex — ['with <s>Puruṣas</s>, the conjunction is also beginningless'] — because the qualities are entailed by the substances. ॥ 22 ॥

body.text: saṁyogasvarūpābhidhitsayedaṁ sūtraṁ pravavṛte-
body.translated_text: With the desire to state the nature of conjunction (<s>saṁyoga</s>), this <s>sūtra</s> is introduced —

body.text: svasvāmiśaktyoḥ svarūpopalabdhihetuḥ saṁyogaḥ ॥ 23 ॥
body.translated_text: Conjunction (<s>saṁyoga</s>) is the cause of apprehending the nature of the power of the owned (<s>sva</s>) and the owner (<s>svāmin</s>). ॥ 23 ॥

body.text: puruṣaḥ svāmī dṛśyena svena darśanārthaṁ saṁyuktaḥ। tasmātsaṁyogādṛśyasyopalabdhiryā sa bhogaḥ। yā tu draṣuḥ svarūpopalabdhiḥ so'pavargaḥ। darśanakāryāvasānaḥ saṁyoga iti darśanaṁ viyogasya kāraṇamuktam। darśanamadarśanasya pratidvaṁdvītyadarśanaṁ saṁyoganimittamuktam। nātra darśanaṁ mokṣakāraṇamadarśanābhāvādeva bandhābhāvaḥ sa mokṣa iti। darśanasya bhāve bandhakāraṇasyādarśanasya nāśa ityato darśanaṁ jñānaṁ kaivalyakāraṇamuktam।
body.translated_text: <s>Puruṣa</s>, the owner (<s>svāmin</s>), is conjoined with the seen (<s>dṛśya</s>), which is his own (<s>sva</s>), for the purpose of seeing (<s>darśana</s>). From that conjunction, the apprehension of the seen — that is experience (<s>bhoga</s>). But the apprehension of the seer's own nature — that is liberation (<s>apavarga</s>). Conjunction has seeing as the culmination of its function — thus seeing is stated as the cause of separation (<s>viyoga</s>). Seeing (<s>darśana</s>) is the counterpart of non-seeing (<s>adarśana</s>) — non-seeing is stated as the cause of conjunction. Seeing is not the cause of liberation here; rather, from the mere absence of non-seeing (<s>adarśana</s>), there is absence of bondage — that is liberation. When seeing arises, the cause of bondage, namely non-seeing, is destroyed — therefore seeing, i.e., knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), is stated as the cause of <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute freedom).

body.text:
vivaraṇam
dṛśyamavadhṛtam । draṣṭā cāvadhṛtaḥ । draṣṭṛdṛśyayoḥ saṁyogo heyaheturiti coktam । sa ca saṁyogo'vadhārayitavyaḥ kīdṛśa iti । tataśca saṁyogasvarūpāvadhāraṇārthamidaṁ sūtraṁ pravavṛte – [svasvāmiśaktyoḥ svarūpopalabdherhetuḥ saṁyogaḥ । svasvāmiśaktyoḥ] buddhipuruṣayoḥ [svarūpopalabdherhetuḥ] kāraṇam । yasmin sati tayoḥ svarūpamupalabhyate vadanadarpaṇayoriva, sa tayeḥ svarūpopalabdhahetuḥ । [saṁyogaḥ] dṛśyadṛśyatvarūpakāryānumeya ityarthaḥ ॥
pramāṇaṁ cātra svasaṁyogapūrvikā buddhipuruṣayoḥ svarūpopalabdhiḥ, viṣayaviṣayisvarūpopalabdhitvāt , īkṣaṇadarpaṇasvarūpopalabdhivat । yā kācit sukhaduḥkhopalabdhirvivādagocarāpannā sā sukhaduḥkhahetusaṁyogapūrvekā, sukhaduḥkhepalabdhitvāt, candanakaṇṭakasukhaduḥkhopalabdhivat ॥
tadāha – [puruṣaḥ svāmī dṛśyena svena] svayā buddhyā [darśanārthaṁ] bhogāpavargadarśanārthaṁ [saṁyuktaḥ ।] darśanaprayukta eva saṁyoga ityarthaḥ ॥
[tasmāt saṁyogādda] rśanaprayuktā [dṛśyasyopalabdhiḥ] aviśiṣṭā yā [sa bhogaḥ । yā tu draṣṭuḥ svarūpopalabdhi] rviviktā [so'pavargaḥ ।] yasmāddarśanakāryadvayaprayuktaḥ saṁyogastasmā [ddarśanakāryāvasānaḥ saṁyogaḥ] tena puruṣasaṁyogava [ddarśanaṁ viyogasya kāraṇamityuktam ।] guṇapuruṣāntaradarśanaṁ pradhānapuruṣaviyogasya kāraṇamityuktaṁ, kāryasya darśanena paryavasitatvāt ॥
saṁsārisaṁsārahetuyāthātmyadarśarnaṁ duḥkhaduḥkhisaṁyogahetunivartakaṁ, duḥkhiduḥkhahetuyāthātmyaviṣayatvāt , rogirogahetuyāthātmyadarśanavat ॥
avidyā draṣṭṛdṛśyayoḥ saṁyogakāraṇaṁ, duḥkhanimittasaṁyegahetutvāt, rogahetusaṁyoganimittamithyājñānavat । draṣṭṛdṛśyasaṁyogo mithyājñānapūrvaka:, duḥkhahetutvāt , rogirogahatusaṁyogavat । yasmādduḥkhiduḥkhahetuyāthātmyaviṣayaṁ [darśanaṁ,] tasmāttadanyathāviṣayasyā [darśanasya pratidvandvamityadarśanaṁ saṁyoganimittamityuktaṁ] tasya [heturavidyeti ।] duḥkhanimittatvācca saṁyogasya ॥
yasmādadarśanameva nivartayati darśanaṁ nānyatkāryaṁ karoti, tasmānnātra [darśanaṁ mokṣakāraṇam adarśanābhāvādevā] rthādadarśanakāryasya duḥkhaheto [rbandhasyābhāvaḥ, sa mokṣaḥ] । na punarbandhābhāvavyatirekeṇa bhāvayitavyo mokṣaḥ । tataśca mokṣasya nityatvasiddhiḥ ॥
[darśanasya bhāve] draṣṭṛdṛśyaviṣayasya darśanasya bhāve tadviṣayasyā [darśanasya nāśaḥ ।] darśanādarśanayorekatra virodhāt timiraravikiraṇajalayoriva । [ato darśanaṁ kaivalyakāraṇamuktam – ‘vivekakhyātiraviplavā hānopāyaḥ’] iti ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
The seen (<s>dṛśya</s>) has been ascertained. The seer (<s>draṣṭṛ</s>) too has been ascertained. And it has been said that the conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) of seer and seen is the cause of what is to be avoided (<s>heya</s>). That conjunction is to be ascertained — of what nature is it? Accordingly, for the purpose of ascertaining the essential nature of conjunction, this <s>sūtra</s> is introduced: ['The conjunction is the cause of the apprehension of the essential nature of the powers of the owned and the owner.'] Of [the powers of] <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) and <s>Puruṣa</s>, [the cause of the apprehension of their essential nature] is the reason. That in whose presence the essential nature of both is apprehended — like a face and a mirror — that is the cause of the apprehension of their essential nature. [The conjunction] is to be inferred from its effect, which has the nature of seer and seen — this is the meaning.
And the proof here is: the apprehension of the essential nature of <s>buddhi</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> is preceded by their mutual conjunction, because it is an apprehension of the essential nature of object and subject — just like the apprehension of the essential nature of a face and a mirror. Whatever apprehension of pleasure and pain falls within the domain of dispute, that is preceded by conjunction with the cause of pleasure and pain, because it is an apprehension of pleasure and pain — just like the apprehension of pleasure and pain from sandalwood and thorns.
He then states: ['<s>Puruṣa</s>, the owner, conjoined with the seen, his own'] — with his own <s>buddhi</s> — ['for the purpose of seeing'] — for the purpose of seeing enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>). ['Conjoined'] — the conjunction is impelled by seeing alone, this is the meaning.
['From that conjunction, the apprehension of the seen'] — undifferentiated — ['impelled by seeing, is experience (<s>bhoga</s>). But the apprehension of the essential nature of the seer'] — discriminated — ['is liberation (<s>apavarga</s>).'] Since the conjunction is impelled by the twofold effect of seeing, therefore ['the conjunction terminates with the fulfillment of seeing's purpose,'] hence ['seeing is the cause of separation (<s>viyoga</s>) — it has been stated.'] The seeing of the distinction between the <s>guṇas</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> is the cause of the separation of <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> — it has been stated, because seeing brings about the conclusion of its effect.
The true seeing of the nature of the transmigrating self (<s>saṃsārin</s>) and the cause of transmigration (<s>saṃsāra</s>) removes the cause of the conjunction of the sufferer with suffering, because it has as its object the true nature of the sufferer and the cause of suffering — just like the true seeing of the nature of a disease and its cause.
<s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance) is the cause of the conjunction of seer and seen, because it is the cause of conjunction that occasions suffering — just like false knowledge that occasions conjunction with the cause of disease. The conjunction of seer and seen is preceded by false knowledge, because it is the cause of suffering — just like the conjunction of a sick person with the cause of disease. Since ['seeing'] has as its object the true nature of the sufferer and the cause of suffering, therefore ['non-seeing (<s>adarśana</s>), which has a contrary object, is the cause of conjunction — it has been stated;'] its ['cause is <s>avidyā</s>.'] And because conjunction is the occasion of suffering.
Since seeing only removes non-seeing and does not produce any other effect, therefore ['seeing is not the cause of liberation; rather, from the mere absence of non-seeing'] — by implication — ['there is the absence of bondage, the cause of suffering — that is liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>).'] Liberation is not to be conceived as something positive apart from the absence of bondage. And from this, the eternality of liberation is established.
['In the presence of seeing'] — in the presence of seeing whose object is the seer and the seen — ['there is the destruction of non-seeing'] which has that as its object. Because of the mutual opposition of seeing and non-seeing, like darkness and sunlight, or fire and water. ['Therefore, seeing has been called the cause of <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation): "Discriminative knowledge (<s>vivekakhyāti</s>), unwavering, is the means of cessation."']

body.text: kiṁ cedamadarśanaṁ nāma, kiṁ guṇānāmadhikāra āhosviddṛśirūpasya svāmino darśitaviṣayasya pradhānacittasyānutpādaḥ। svasmindṛśye vidyamāne yo darśanābhāvaḥ।
body.translated_text: What is this non-seeing (<s>adarśana</s>)? Is it the purposeful activity (<s>adhikāra</s>) of the <s>guṇas</s>? Or is it the non-arising of the principal <s>citta</s> (mind) that has presented its object to the seer (<s>dṛśi</s>), the owner, whose nature is inward consciousness? That is, the absence of seeing while the seen exists within oneself.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[kiṁcedamadarśanaṁ nāma ?] nanu coktamavidyaiva । sā cā [mitrāgoṣpadavaditi] vidyāviparyayeṇa vyākhyātā । satyamevaṁ, kintu śāsragatā vikalpā darśayiṣyante svābhimatapakṣaniścicīṣayā । paraparikalpitavastukhaṇḍimānamāpādayatā hi nijābhimatanirūpitavastu draḍhimānamatitarāmānīyate ॥
[kiṁceda] miti sarvaireva vikalpairvakṣyamāṇairabhisaṁbandhanīyam । [kiṁ guṇānāmadhikāra] iti, sāmānyena paripṛṣṭasya viśeṣaparyanuyogaḥ । [adhikṛtiradhikāraḥ,] guṇānāṁ pravṛttiḥ ॥
nanu guṇānāmadhikārasya kathamadarśanāśaṅkā ? ucyate – arthadvāreṇa bhavatyevādarśanamadhikāraḥ । yāvaddhi guṇānāṁ pravṛttistāvadbandhaḥ । bandhakāraṇamavidyeti sthitisthairyamānīyate । śabdadvāreṇāpi – darśanādanyadadarśanaṁ yadā, bhavatyeva tadānīmāśaṅkā । guṇadhikāro hi darśanādanya eveti ॥
[āhosviddṛśisvarūpasya svāmino darśitaviṣayasya cittasyānutpādaḥ ।] iha tu pūrvapadārthapradhānatvamadarśanasya gṛhītvā śaṅkyate । [cittasyānutpādaḥ] prāgutpatterdarśanasyābhāvaḥ । kimuktaṁ bhavatyanutpāda ityata āha – [svasmin dṛśye citte vidyamāne yo darśanābhāvaḥ] guṇapuruṣāntaradarśanānutpattiradarśanamiti ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
['What is this non-seeing?'] Surely it has already been said that it is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) itself. And that has been explained ['as the footprint of a non-enemy'] — through the opposite of knowledge. This is indeed so; however, the various opinions found in the <s>śāstra</s> (authoritative texts) will be shown, with the desire to establish one's own preferred position. For by demonstrating the weakness of positions imagined by others, the firmness of one's own established view is all the more brought forth.
['What is this'] — is to be connected with all the alternatives about to be stated. ['Is it the purposeful activity of the <s>guṇas</s>?'] — this is a specific inquiry into what was asked in general terms. ['Activity (<s>adhikṛti</s>) is purposeful engagement (<s>adhikāra</s>)'] — the operation of the <s>guṇas</s>.
But how can the activity of the <s>guṇas</s> be suspected of being non-seeing? It is said: through the medium of meaning, activity is indeed non-seeing. For as long as there is the operation of the <s>guṇas</s>, so long is there bondage. That <s>avidyā</s> is the cause of bondage is thus firmly maintained. Through the medium of the word also — when non-seeing is something other than seeing, then indeed this suspicion arises. For the activity of the <s>guṇas</s> is indeed something other than seeing.
['Or is it the non-arising of the <s>citta</s> (mind) that has presented its object to the seer (<s>dṛśi</s>), the owner?'] Here, however, taking the primacy of the meaning of the first alternative of non-seeing, the doubt is raised. ['The non-arising of <s>citta</s>'] — the absence of seeing prior to its arising. What is meant by 'non-arising'? To this he says: ['The absence of seeing while the seen, the <s>citta</s>, exists within oneself'] — the non-arising of the seeing of the distinction between the <s>guṇas</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> is non-seeing.

body.text: kimarthavattā guṇānām। athāvidyā svacittena saha niruddhā svacittasyotpattibījam। kiṁ sthitisaṁskārakṣaye gatisaṁskārābhivyaktiḥ। yatredamuktaṁ pradhānaṁ sthityaiva vartamānaṁ vikārākaraṇādapradhānaṁ syāt।
body.translated_text: Is it the purposefulness (<s>arthavatā</s>) of the <s>guṇas</s>? Or is <s>avidyā</s>, dissolved together with one's own <s>citta</s> (mind), the seed for the arising of one's own <s>citta</s>? Is it the manifestation of the <s>saṃskāras</s> (impressions) of activity upon the destruction of the <s>saṃskāras</s> of stability? In this regard it was said: <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal nature), existing only in a state of equilibrium, would become non-<s>Pradhāna</s> by not producing modifications.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[kimarthavatā guṇānāṁ] bhogāpavargābhyāṁ yā guṇānāmarthavatā tadadarśanamiti । atra tvarthadvāreṇaivāśaṅkā । prayojanavato hi prayojanamavaśyakṛtyamiti ॥
kaḥ punareṣu pakṣeṣu doṣaḥ ? ucyate – yadyadhikāro guṇānāmadarśanaṁ vidyānarthakyaṁ prāptam । na hyāsmin pakṣe vidyā pratyanīkabhūtā syādadarśanasya । yasmādvidyādhikārayoravirodhaḥ, ataścānirmokṣaḥ prasaktaḥ । punaḥ punaḥ prayojanavattayā pravṛttisaṁbhavāt ॥
guṇārthavattā adarśanamiti pakṣe'pyeṣa eva doṣaḥ । tathā cittasyānutpādapakṣe'pyeṣa eva । anutpādo hi darśanābhāvaḥ, tasya cāvastutvādvidyayā nivṛtiranupapanneti । abhāve hi sati pratyanīkavidhānamanarthakameva ॥
[athāvidyā svacintena saha niruddheti ।] atra hyavidyāyā adarśanasya ca kenacidaṁśena bhedaṁ manyamāno vikalpayati । katham ? aniruddhā hyavidyā dṛśyamānatvāddarśanameva । yā tu niruddhā cittena saha pralīnā svakāraṇe । [svacittasyotpatibījamu] tpattikāraṇaṁ sā na dṛśyata ityadarśanamityabhimānaḥ । tataścānirodhāvasthāyā darśanatvaprasaṅga iti duṣṭa evāyaṁ pakṣaḥ syāt । atha tu nirodhānirodhāvasthayorapyadaśarnameva, tathā satyabhimatasiddhiriṣyadoṣa eva । [kiṁ sthitisaṁskārakṣaye gatisaṁskārābhivyaktiḥ । kime] tadadarśanamiti na saṁbadhyate । kathaṁ tarhi saṁbandhaḥ? ucyate – tatrāvidyā svacittasahaniruddhā cittasyotpattibījāmityuktaṁ, tata idamarthāt siddham – cittaṁ svakāraṇe nirudhyate punaścotpadyata iti । tataścedamapi siddhamarthāccittasya kāraṇamapi sthityā gatyā ca vartata iti । tataścaitadvispaṣṭīkaraṇārthaṁ pṛcchati ॥
sthityartho guṇānāṁ sāmyavasthāhetuḥ saṁskāraḥ [sthitisaṁskāraḥ ।] tasya [kṣaye sthitisaṁskārakṣaye] gatirmahadādyākāreṇa pravṛttistadarthaḥ saṁskāro [gatisaṁskāraḥ] tasyā [bhivyakti] riti ॥
yadi sthityā gatyā ca vartate, tataḥ ko doṣaḥ syāttadudāharaṇena darśayati – [yatredamu] ktaṁ pradhānaṁ [sthityaiva vartamānaṁ vikārākaraṇāt mahadādyākāreṇā] pariṇāmā [dapradhānaṁ syāt ।] yataḥ pradhatte vikārāniti pradhānam । tena vikārāṇām apradhātṛtvādapradhānaṁ syāt ।
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
['Is it the purposefulness of the <s>guṇas</s>?'] — the purposefulness of the <s>guṇas</s> through enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) — that non-seeing is the cessation of that. Here too the doubt is through the medium of meaning alone. For what is purposeful must necessarily accomplish its purpose.
What then is the defect in these positions? It is said: If the activity of the <s>guṇas</s> is non-seeing, then the purposelessness of knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) would follow. For in this position, knowledge would not be the counteragent of non-seeing. Since there is no opposition between knowledge and activity, therefore the impossibility of liberation follows — because operation could arise again and again through purposefulness.
In the position that the purposefulness of the <s>guṇas</s> is non-seeing, this same defect applies. Likewise in the position that non-seeing is the non-arising of <s>citta</s>, this same defect applies. For non-arising is the absence of seeing, and since that is a non-entity, its removal by knowledge is untenable. For when something is an absence, prescribing a counteragent is entirely pointless.
['Or is <s>avidyā</s> dissolved together with one's own <s>citta</s>?'] Here, regarding <s>avidyā</s> and non-seeing, one imagines some aspect of difference and thus proposes alternatives. How? <s>Avidyā</s>, when not dissolved, is seeing itself because it is perceived. But when dissolved, it has merged with <s>citta</s> into its own cause. ['The seed for the arising of one's own <s>citta</s>'] — the cause of arising — that is not perceived, hence it is non-seeing: this is the view. And therefore, the consequence that the undissolved state too would be seeing — thus this position is defective. If, however, non-seeing applies to both the dissolved and undissolved states, then the desired conclusion is merely a restatement of the assumption — which is itself a defect. ['Is it the manifestation of the <s>saṃskāras</s> of activity upon the destruction of the <s>saṃskāras</s> of stability?'] This does not syntactically connect with non-seeing. How then is the connection? It is said: there it was stated that <s>avidyā</s>, dissolved together with one's own <s>citta</s>, is the seed for the arising of <s>citta</s>. From that, this is implicitly established: <s>citta</s> dissolves into its own cause and arises again. And from that, this too is implicitly established: the cause of <s>citta</s> also operates through stability and activity. Therefore, for the purpose of clarifying this, he asks:
The <s>saṃskāra</s> (impression) whose purpose is stability — the cause of the state of equilibrium of the <s>guṇas</s> — is the ['<s>saṃskāra</s> of stability.'] Upon its ['destruction — upon the destruction of the <s>saṃskāra</s> of stability'] — activity (<s>gati</s>), i.e., operation in the form of <s>mahat</s> (the great principle) and so forth, the <s>saṃskāra</s> whose purpose is that is the ['<s>saṃskāra</s> of activity;'] its ['manifestation'] — thus.
If it operates through both stability and activity, then what defect would follow? He shows this through an illustration: ['In this regard it was said:'] <s>Pradhāna</s>, ['existing only in a state of equilibrium, would become non-<s>Pradhāna</s> by not producing modifications'] — i.e., by not producing modifications in the form of <s>mahat</s> and so forth. Since <s>Pradhāna</s> is so called because it 'sets forth' (<s>pradhatte</s>) modifications, therefore, by not setting forth modifications, it would become non-<s>Pradhāna</s>.

body.text: tathā gatyaiva vartamānaṁ vikāranityatvādapradhānaṁ syāt। ubhayathā cāsya vṛttiḥ pradhānavyavahāraṁ labhate nānyathā। kāraṇāntareṣvapi kalpiteṣveva samānaścarcaḥ। darśanaśaktirevādarśanamityeke, “pradhānasyā''tmakhyāpanārthā pravṛttiḥ” itiśruteḥ। sarvabodhyabodhasamarthaḥ prākpravṛtteḥ puruṣo na paśyati sarvakāryakaraṇasamarthaṁ dṛśyaṁ tadā na dṛśyata iti। ubhayasyāpyadarśanaṁ dharma ityeke। tatredaṁ dṛśyasya svātmabhūtamapi puruṣapratyayāpekṣaṁ darśanaṁ dṛśyadharmatvena bhavati। tathā puruṣasyānātmabhūtamapi dṛśyapratyayāpekṣaṁ puruṣadharmatvenevādarśanamavabhāsate। darśanaṁ jñānamevādarśanamiti kecidabhidadhati। ityete śāstragatā vikalpāḥ। tatra vikalpabahutvametatsarvapuruṣāṇāṁ guṇānāṁ saṁyoge sādhāraṇaviṣayam ॥ 23 ॥
body.translated_text: Likewise, if existing only through activity, it would become non-<s>Pradhāna</s> due to the permanence of modifications. Only when its operation is twofold does the designation <s>Pradhāna</s> apply, and not otherwise. Even when other causes are hypothesized, the same line of reasoning applies. Some say that the power of seeing itself is non-seeing, based on the <s>śruti</s> (scripture): 'The operation of <s>Pradhāna</s> is for the purpose of revealing itself.' <s>Puruṣa</s>, though capable of knowing all that is to be known, does not see prior to the operation [of <s>Pradhāna</s>]; the seen (<s>dṛśya</s>), though capable of all effects and instruments, is not seen then — thus non-seeing is a property of both, say some. In this regard: seeing, though belonging to the very nature of the seen, depends on the cognition of <s>Puruṣa</s> and thus functions as a property of the seen. Likewise, non-seeing, though not belonging to the nature of <s>Puruṣa</s>, depends on the cognition of the seen and thus appears as if it were a property of <s>Puruṣa</s>. Some declare that seeing is knowledge itself and non-seeing [is its absence]. These are the various opinions found in the <s>śāstra</s> (authoritative texts). Among these, the mere multiplicity of opinions pertains to the general topic of the conjunction of all <s>Puruṣas</s> with the <s>guṇas</s>. || 23 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tathā gatyaiva vartamānaṁ] nityaṁ vikārarūpeṇeva vartamānaṁ [vikāranityatvānna] vikārān pradhata iti kāraṇatvahāne [rapradhānaṁ syāt । ubhayathā vṛttiḥ] gatyā sthityā ca vartanaṁ vṛttiryasya pradhānasya [tadubhayathāvṛtti vyavahāraṁ pradhānatvavyavahāraṁ] kāraṇatvavyavahāraṁ [labhate । nānyathā] pradhānatvaṁ pradhānasya । [kāraṇāntareṣvapi] puruṣeśvaraparamāṇvādiṣu [parakalpiteṣu samānaścarcaḥ] tulyaviṣayaḥ nyāyaḥ । prakṛta evādhunā nirūpyate । [darśanaśaktirevādarśanamityeke । darśanasya śaktira] nabhivyaktāvasthā bīja ivānabhivyaktāṅkurāvasthā tadetadadarśanami [tyeke manyante ।] kutaḥ ? [pradhānasyātmaprakhyāpanārthā] prakhyāpanaṁ darśanamākhyāyamānarūpatā tasyai tadadarśanamiti śruteḥ ॥
asmin pakṣe tadevānābhivyaktātmakaṁ śaktirūpamadarśanaṁ tadeva cābhivyaktaṁ darśanamiti svātmani virodhānupapatterdarśanādadarśanasya nivṛttyanavaklṛptiḥ ॥
tathā darśanāntaraṁ – [sarvabodhasamarthaḥ] bodhātmakatvāt [prāk pravṛteḥ] pradhānapravṛtteḥ [prāṅna paśyati] darśanātmako'pi san puruṣa iti । [sarvakāryakaraṇa] kriyā [samarthaṁ dṛśyaṁ] pradhānaṁ [na tadā prākpravṛtteḥ] paramārthamapi [sat dṛśyata ityubhayasya] pradhānapuruṣayo [radarśanaṁ dharma ityeke manyante ॥]
atrāpyubhayorapi prāgavasthaivādarśanamuttarakālāvasthā ca darśanamiti pūrvadoṣaḥ sthita eva । [dṛśyasyātmabhūta] mavyatiriktamapi [puruṣapratyayāpekṣaṁ] puruṣākāreṇa puruṣasya na dṛśyate । puruṣākāraviśiṣṭatayā vā puruṣasya dṛśyata iti puruṣapratyayāpekṣamadarśanaṁ puruṣasya dharmatvena bhavati । tadetatspaṣṭayati – [puruṣasyānātmabhūtamapi dṛśyapratyayāpekṣaṁ] dṛśyapratyayo'jñānaṁ tadapekṣaṁ, kathaṁ puruṣākāreṇādarśanāt saṁkareṇa vā darśanādantaḥkaraṇapratyayāpekṣaṁ puruṣānā [tmabhūtamapi puruṣadharmatvenaivādarśanamābhāsate ।] tathā ca sati dṛśyadharma evāyamityadoṣaḥ ॥
sarvavikalpapakṣakhyāpanārtha upanyāsaḥ । [darśanaṁ jñānaṁ,] tadeva jñāna [madarśanamiti kecinmanyante ।] samāsasyottarapadārthaprādhānyamūrīkṛtyārya vikalpaḥ । etasya doṣo'vidyāsūtra eva vyākhyātaḥ ।
