[ete śāstragatā vikalpāḥ] darśanāntaragatā vikalpāḥ । [tatra vikalpabahutvamātrametat] na bahutvamātreṇārthīseddhirityabhiprāyaḥ । yasya tu buddhipuruṣasaṁyogahetutvaṁ tasyādarśane [natvaṁ] yuktaṁ daśainavirodhāt । tathā ca vyākhyātamiti nātra punaḥ prayatyate ॥ 23 ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
['Likewise, existing only through activity'] — constantly existing only in the form of modifications — ['due to the permanence of modifications, it does not'] set forth modifications; hence, with the loss of causality, ['it would become non-<s>Pradhāna</s>. The twofold operation'] — the existence through both activity and stability is the operation of <s>Pradhāna</s> — ['that which has twofold operation obtains the designation'] — the designation of <s>Pradhāna</s>-hood — the designation of causality. ['Not otherwise'] is there <s>Pradhāna</s>-hood of <s>Pradhāna</s>. ['Even when other causes'] — <s>Puruṣa</s>, <s>Īśvara</s> (God), atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>), and so forth — ['are hypothesized by others, the same line of reasoning'] — the principle applicable to the same subject — applies. It is now being examined only with respect to what is under discussion. ['The power of seeing itself is non-seeing, say some. The power of seeing'] — its unmanifested state, like the unmanifested state of a sprout in a seed — ['that is non-seeing, say some.'] Why? ['The operation of <s>Pradhāna</s> is for the purpose of revealing itself'] — revelation is seeing, the state of being made known; that is non-seeing — based on the <s>śruti</s>.
In this position, that very unmanifested power-form is non-seeing, and that very same thing when manifested is seeing; thus, due to the impossibility of opposition within one's own self, the cessation of non-seeing through seeing cannot be established.
Likewise, another view of seeing: ['Capable of knowing all'] — because of being of the nature of knowledge — ['prior to the operation'] of <s>Pradhāna</s> — ['does not see'] — though being of the nature of seeing, <s>Puruṣa</s> [does not see]. ['The seen (<s>dṛśya</s>), <s>Pradhāna</s>, capable of all effects and instruments'] — of action — ['though truly existing, is not seen then, prior to the operation'] — ['thus non-seeing is a property of both'] — of <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> — ['say some.']
Here too, the earlier state of both being non-seeing and the later state being seeing — the same defect as before stands. ['Though belonging to the very nature of the seen'] — though not different from it — ['depending on the cognition of <s>Puruṣa</s>'] — it is not seen by <s>Puruṣa</s> in the form of <s>Puruṣa</s>; or, being seen as qualified by the form of <s>Puruṣa</s>, non-seeing, depending on the cognition of <s>Puruṣa</s>, functions as a property of <s>Puruṣa</s>. He clarifies this: ['Though not belonging to the nature of <s>Puruṣa</s>, depending on the cognition of the seen'] — the cognition of the seen is ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>); depending on that — because of non-seeing in the form of <s>Puruṣa</s>, or because of seeing through intermixture — ['depending on the cognition of the inner instrument (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), though not belonging to the nature of <s>Puruṣa</s>, non-seeing appears as if it were a property of <s>Puruṣa</s> alone.'] And in that case, this is actually a property of the seen — thus the defect [remains].
The exposition is for the purpose of displaying all the alternative positions. ['Seeing is knowledge;'] that very knowledge ['is non-seeing, say some.'] This is an alternative that takes the primacy of the latter member of the compound. The defect of this has been explained in the <s>sūtra</s> on <s>avidyā</s> itself.
['These are the opinions found in the <s>śāstra</s>'] — the opinions found in other systems of seeing. ['Among these, it is merely a multiplicity of opinions'] — the intent is that the truth is not established by mere multiplicity. But that whose nature is being the cause of the conjunction of <s>buddhi</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> — its being non-seeing is fitting, because of the absence of contradiction with seeing. And this has been explained, hence no further effort is made here. || 23 ||

body.text: yastu pratyakcetanasya svabuddhisaṁyogaḥ –
body.translated_text: Now, the conjunction of the inward-facing consciousness (<s>pratyakcetana</s>) with its own <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) —

body.text: tasya heturavidyā ॥ 24 ॥
body.translated_text: Its cause is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). || 24 ||

body.text: viparyayajñānavāsanetyarthaḥ। viparyayajñānavāsanāvāsitā ca na kāryaniṣṭhāṁ puruṣakhyātiṁ buddhiḥ prāpnoti sādhikārā punarāvartate। sā tu puruṣakhyātiparyavasānāṁ kāryaniṣṭhāṁ prāpnoti, caritādhikārā nivṛttādarśanā bandhakāraṇābhāvānna punarāvartate।
body.translated_text: The meaning is: the latent impression (<s>vāsanā</s>) of erroneous knowledge (<s>viparyayajñāna</s>). And <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), permeated by the latent impression of erroneous knowledge, does not attain the final cognition of <s>Puruṣa</s> (<s>puruṣakhyāti</s>) that constitutes the fulfillment of its purpose; rather, having its function still remaining, it returns again. But when it attains the final cognition of <s>Puruṣa</s> that constitutes the fulfillment of its purpose, having completed its function and with non-seeing removed, it does not return again, due to the absence of the cause of bondage.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[sarvapuruṣāṇāṁ guṇasaṁyegāviśeṣaḥ ।] guṇaiḥ saṁyogaḥ sarveṣāmaviśiṣṭaḥ sādhāraṇaḥ, tathā [pyasādhāraṇaviṣayastu] pratyātmaṁ viśiṣṭastu [pratyakcetanasya] bauddhapratyayānudarśinaḥ [svabuddhisaṁyogaḥ ।] sa cāsādhāraṇaḥ svabuddhisaṁyogo yena bhavati tadevādarśanam । [tasya heturavidyā । tasya] svasvāmiśākasvarūpopalabdhihetoḥ – saṁyogasya hetuḥ kāraṇam avidyā viparyayajñānavāsanetyarthaḥ ॥
nanu ca ['viparyayo mithyājñānamatadūpapratiṣṭham’] ityuktam । tathā ['anityāśuciduḥkhānātmasu nityaśucisukhātmakhyāti] ravidyā' ityutam । atra kathaṁ viparyāyaijñānavāsanetyucyate ! naiṣa doṣaḥ-avidyākāryatvādvāsanāyāḥ saivāvidyetyucyate । pralīneṣvapi karaṇeṣu sāmyāvasthāyamapi satyāmavidyāvāsanā punaḥ punaḥ pravṛttau pradhānasya heturbhavati । na punarviparyayaḥ prāk buddhyutpatterabhāvātpravṛttikāraṇamiti, tadvāsanaiva pradhānapuruṣasaṁyogasya kāraṇamityākhyāyate ॥
tadevāha – [viparyayajñānavāsanāvāsitā na kāryaniṣṭhāṁ] kāryesamāptim । kāryaniṣṭhāmāha – [puruṣakhyāti] miti । tāṁ buddhi [rna prāpnoti ।] puruṣakhyātiparyavasānā hi buddheḥ karaṇīyavattā । [sādhikārā] karaṇīyavatī [punaḥ punarāvartate] viparyayajñānavāsanāvaśāt ॥
[sā tu] buddhiḥ [puruṣakhyātiparyavasānā kāryaniṣṭhāṁ prāpnoti ।] punarapi tadeva spaṣṭayati – [caritādhikārā nivṛttādarśanabandhanā] karmāvipākayoradarśanamūlatvādadarśanameva bandhanam । adarśananivṛttau ca bandhanivṛtte [rbandhakāraṇābhāvādba] ndhakāraṇasyādarśanasyābhāvā [nna punarāvartate ॥]
body.translated_text:
[Vivaraṇa]
[The conjunction with the <s>guṇas</s> is common to all <s>Puruṣas</s>.] The conjunction with the <s>guṇas</s> is undifferentiated, common to all. [Yet what is specific is] the conjunction of each individual's [inner consciousness (<s>pratyakcetana</s>)]—one who observes intellectual cognitions—[with its own <s>buddhi</s>.] And that specific conjunction with one's own <s>buddhi</s>, by which [bondage] exists—that itself is non-seeing (<s>adarśana</s>). [Its cause is <s>avidyā</s>. The cause of that]—of the conjunction that is the cause of the experience of the master-and-owned relationship—is <s>avidyā</s>, meaning the latent impression of erroneous knowledge (<s>viparyayajñānavāsanā</s>).
Objection: It was said: ['Error is false knowledge not based on the real form of that [object]']. And it was said: ['The cognition of the eternal, pure, joyful, and self in the non-eternal, impure, painful, and non-self] is <s>avidyā</s>.' How then can it be called 'the latent impression of erroneous knowledge'? Reply: This is not a fault—because the latent impression (<s>vāsanā</s>), being the effect of <s>avidyā</s>, is itself called <s>avidyā</s>. For even when the instruments [of knowledge] have dissolved, even in the state of equilibrium [of the <s>guṇas</s>], the latent impression of <s>avidyā</s> becomes the cause of <s>pradhāna</s>'s renewed activity again and again. But error (<s>viparyaya</s>) itself cannot be the cause of activity prior to the arising of <s>buddhi</s>, due to its non-existence [at that stage]. Therefore, it is the latent impression of that [error] that is declared to be the cause of the conjunction of <s>pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>.
This is what he says: [Imbued with the latent impression of erroneous knowledge, <s>buddhi</s> does not reach the completion of its task (<s>kāryaniṣṭhā</s>)]. He specifies the task's completion: [the knowledge of <s>Puruṣa</s> (<s>puruṣakhyāti</s>)]. <s>Buddhi</s> [does not attain] that. For <s>buddhi</s>'s having-a-task-to-do culminates in the knowledge of <s>Puruṣa</s>. [Still bearing its task (<s>sādhikārā</s>)]—still having something to do—[it revolves again and again] under the power of the latent impression of erroneous knowledge.
[But that] <s>buddhi</s>, [culminating in the knowledge of <s>Puruṣa</s>, reaches the completion of its task.] And again he clarifies: [Having fulfilled its task, the bondage of non-seeing having ceased]—since non-seeing is the root of <s>karma</s> and its fruition, non-seeing itself is bondage. And when non-seeing ceases, bondage ceases—[because of the absence of the cause of bondage]—because of the absence of non-seeing, which is the cause of bondage—[it does not revolve again.]

body.text: atra kaścitpaṇḍakopākhyānenoddhāṭayati - mugdhayā bhāryayā'bhidhīyate - paṇḍakā''ryaputra, apatyavatī me bhaginī kimarthaṁ nāma nāhamiti, sa tāmāha - mṛtaste'hamapatyamutpādayiṣyāmīti। tathedaṁ vidyamānaṁ jñānaṁ cittanivṛttiṁ na karoti, vinaṣṭaṁ kariṣyatīti kā pratyāśā। tatrā''cāryadeśīyo vakti – nanu buddhinivṛttireva mokṣo'darśanakāraṇābhāvādbuddhinivṛttiḥ।
body.translated_text: Here someone challenges with the parable of the eunuch: A naive wife says [to her husband]: 'Noble husband, my sister has children—why then do I not?' He replies: 'When I am dead, I shall beget offspring for you.' Similarly, existing knowledge does not bring about the cessation of the mind; what hope is there that destroyed [knowledge] will do so? To this, one who is like a teacher (<s>ācārya-deśīya</s>) says: But the cessation of <s>buddhi</s> itself is liberation—because of the absence of the cause of non-seeing, <s>buddhi</s> ceases.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[atra kaścitpaṇḍakopākhyānenoddhaṭṭayati ।] paṇḍakaḥ [ṣaṇḍaḥ ।] sa kila [mugdhayā bhāryayā abhidhīyate ।] katham ? [āryaputra, me bhaginyapatyavatī, kimarthaṁ nāham apatyavatyasmīti । tāmaha mṛtaste'hamapūtyamutpādayiṣyāmīti । tathadaṁ vidyamānaṁ jñānaṁ citanivṛttiṁ na karoti, naṣṭaṁ kariṣyatīti kā pratyāśā ॥]
ayamudghaṭṭayiturabhiprāyaḥ – avidyā cedbuddhipuruṣasaṁyegasya kāraṇaṁ, tasyāśca vidyā nivṛttihetuḥ, tataśca vidyamānāyāṁ vidyāyāṁ tadvirodhinyavidyā nivartate । na tu vidyotpattyanantaramapi cittanivṛttiḥ । tatra yathaiva satyāṁ vidyāyāṁ na cittanivṛtaḥ, tathā naṣṭāyāmapi vidyāyāṁ na nivartsyati tarāmidānī ṣaṇḍādiva mṛtādapatyopattiḥ । ata eva kāraṇādavidyā'pi na saṁyogakāraṇam ॥
[atrācāryadeśīyaḥ parihāraṁ vakti ।] ācāryadeśīyagrahaṇaṁ pūrvapakṣasyāsāratvaprakhyāpanārtham । uddhaṭṭanenaiva pratyuttaraṁ vadāmi iti ॥
[nanu buddhinivṛttireva mokṣaḥ ।] katham ? [adarśanakāraṇābhāvādbuddhinivṛttiḥ ।]
body.translated_text:
[Vivaraṇa]
[Here someone challenges with the parable of the eunuch.] A eunuch (<s>paṇḍaka</s>) [is a <s>ṣaṇḍa</s>]. He, it is said, [is addressed by his naive wife.] How? ['Noble husband, my sister has children—why am I not one who has children?' He replies: 'When I am dead, I shall beget offspring for you.' Similarly, existing knowledge does not bring about the cessation of the mind; what hope is there that destroyed knowledge will do so?]
The intention of the challenger is: if <s>avidyā</s> is the cause of the conjunction of <s>buddhi</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, and <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) is the cause of its cessation, then when <s>vidyā</s> is present, <s>avidyā</s>, its opposite, ceases. But even immediately after the arising of <s>vidyā</s>, the cessation of the mind does not occur. So just as when <s>vidyā</s> is present, the mind does not cease, likewise when <s>vidyā</s> has been destroyed, it will not cease either—like the begetting of offspring from a dead eunuch. For this very reason, <s>avidyā</s> too is not the cause of conjunction.
[To this, one who is like a teacher offers a reply.] The expression 'one like a teacher' (<s>ācārya-deśīya</s>) is used to indicate the insubstantiality of the objection. 'I shall reply with the very objection itself'—this is the meaning.
[But the cessation of <s>buddhi</s> itself is liberation.] How? [Because of the absence of the cause of non-seeing, <s>buddhi</s> ceases.]

body.text: taccādarśanaṁ bandhakāraṇaṁ darśanānnivartate। tatra cittanivṛttireva mokṣaḥ, kimarthamasthāna evāsya mativibhraḥ ॥ 24 ॥
body.translated_text: And that non-seeing, the cause of bondage, ceases through seeing. Therefore, the cessation of the mind itself is liberation. Why this confusion about something that has no basis? // 24 //

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[taccādarśanaṁ bandhakāraṇaṁ darśanānnivartate, tannivṛttireva mokṣaḥ । kimarthamasthāne vibhramaḥ] । pradhānapuruṣasaṁyogasya du:khahetoravidyā kāraṇamiti vistareṇa pratipāditam । tataśca darśanādadarśananivṛtyupapettaḥ pūrvapakṣamasāraṁ manyate ॥
nanu coktaṁ vidyānantarameva buddhirna nivartata iti । ucyate । vidyayā tāvadavidyā nivartata eva । nātra vibhramaḥ kāryaḥ । tasyāṁ tu nivṛttāyāṁ budvinivṛttiśca bhavatyeva । punarbuddhisaṁyogasyāvidyāvyatirekeṇa kāraṇāntarābhāvāt । tataśca buddhinivṛttireva mokṣaḥ ॥
yattu vidyānantarameva buddhirna nivartata iti, tadakāraṇam । kasmāt ? nimittanaimitikayoranekaprakāradarśanāt । yathā takṣādinimitāḥ prāsādādayastakṣādiṣūparateṣvapi na nimittaviratyā viramanti । bhagnasya ca drumasya bhaṅgānantarameva viśeṣādarśanāt । tathā cittasyapi vimuktasāyakavadārabdhasaṁskārāparikṣayāt, tatsaṁskārāpekṣayā kaṁcitkālaṁ darśanenaivāvasthānam iti । tathā ca śrutiḥ – [“tasya tāvadeva ciram”] iti ॥ 24 ॥
body.translated_text:
[Vivaraṇa]
[And that non-seeing, the cause of bondage, ceases through seeing; the cessation of that is liberation. Why this confusion about something that has no basis?] It has been demonstrated at length that <s>avidyā</s> is the cause of the conjunction of <s>pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, which is the cause of suffering. And since the cessation of non-seeing through seeing is established, [the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>] considers the objection insubstantial.
Objection: But it was said that even immediately after <s>vidyā</s>, <s>buddhi</s> does not cease. Reply: Through <s>vidyā</s>, <s>avidyā</s> certainly ceases—there should be no confusion about this. And when <s>avidyā</s> has ceased, the cessation of <s>buddhi</s> does indeed take place—because there is no other cause for the conjunction with <s>buddhi</s> apart from <s>avidyā</s>. And therefore, the cessation of <s>buddhi</s> itself is liberation.
As for the [objection] that even immediately after <s>vidyā</s>, <s>buddhi</s> does not cease—that is no reason [against the doctrine]. Why? Because multiple types of cause-effect relationships are observed. Just as a palace and such, caused by a carpenter and others, do not cease even when the carpenters have stopped—they do not cease merely because the cause ceases. And because a felled tree is not seen to differ [from its standing state] immediately after felling. Likewise, the mind too—like a released arrow—because the <s>saṃskāras</s> initiated have not yet been exhausted, it remains for some time in the state of seeing, in dependence upon those <s>saṃskāras</s>. And thus the <s>śruti</s>: ['For him there is that much delay only.'] // 24 //

body.text: heyaṁ duḥkhaṁ heyakāraṇaṁ ca saṁyogākhyaṁ sanimittamuktamataḥ paraṁ hānaṁ vaktavyam –
body.translated_text: The suffering to be avoided and the cause to be avoided—called conjunction—along with its basis, have been stated. Hereafter, cessation (<s>hāna</s>) is to be stated:

body.text: tadabhāvātsaṁyogābhāvo hānaṁ taddṛśeḥ kaivalyam ॥ 25 ॥
body.translated_text: From the absence of that [<s>avidyā</s>], the absence of conjunction—that is cessation (<s>hāna</s>). That is <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation) for the seer. // 25 //

body.text: tasyādarśanasyābhāvādbuddhipuruṣasaṁyogābhāva ātyantiko bandhanoparama ityarthaḥ। etaddhānam। taddṛśeḥ kaivalyaṁ puruṣasyāmiśrībhāvaḥ punarasaṁyogo guṇairityarthaḥ। duḥkhakāraṇanivṛttau duḥkhoparamo hānaṁ, tadā svarūpapratiṣṭhaḥ puruṣa ityuktam ॥ 25 ॥
body.translated_text: From the absence of that non-seeing (<s>adarśana</s>), the absolute cessation of the conjunction of <s>buddhi</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>—the absolute cessation of bondage—that is the meaning. This is cessation (<s>hāna</s>). 'That is <s>kaivalya</s> for the seer'—the state of non-admixture of <s>Puruṣa</s>, the non-conjunction with the <s>guṇas</s> once again—that is the meaning. When the cause of suffering ceases, the cessation of suffering is <s>hāna</s>; then <s>Puruṣa</s> is established in its own nature—as was said [earlier]. // 25 //

body.text:
vivaraṇam
catvāro vyūhāḥ prakṛtāḥ । tatra heyaṁ du:khaṁ ' [heyaṁ duḥkhamanāgatam'] ityuktam । regasthānīya eka vyūho vyākhyāta ityarthaḥ । [heyakāraṇaṁ ca sanimittaṁ saṁyogākhyamuktam ।] dvitīyo vyūho rogahetusthānīyo heyohetustvavidyānimittasāhitaḥ pradhānapuruṣasaṁyoga upavarṇitaḥ । uttaparikīrtanaṁ ca sopapattikoktestadvaṣayākāṅkṣānivṛttyartham ॥
[ataḥ paraṁ hānam] ārogyasthānīyaṁ mokṣaśāstraprayojane [vaktavyam ।] vakṣyamāṇasaṁkīrtanaṁ ca śrotṛbuddhisamādhānārtham । [tadabhāvāt saṁyogābhāvo hānaṁ tat dṛśeḥ kaivalyam ॥]
[taditi] pūrvaprakṛtāyā avidyāyāḥ pratyavamarśaḥ । [tasyādarśanasya] avidyāyā [abhāvāt buddhipuruṣasaṁyogasya] duḥkhaheto: [abhāvaḥ ālyantiko bandhanoparama ityarthaḥ । etat hānam] arerāgyasthānīyam । [tat dṛśeḥ kaivalyaṁ] tadeva hānaṁ atyantiko bandhanoparamaḥ [dṛśeḥ puruṣasya kaivalyam ।] asya vyākhyānaṁ [puruṣasyāmiśrabhāvaḥ punarasayogo guṇairityarthaḥ ॥]
padārthaṁ vyākhyāya vākyārthamidānīṁ darśayati – [duḥkhakāraṇanivṛtau duḥkhoparamo hānam । tadā svarūpapratiṣṭhaḥ puruṣa ityuktam – “svarūpapratiṣṭhā vā citiśaktiḥ” iti ॥]
nanu ca aniyatavipākasya karmaṇaḥ sadbhāve kathaṁ hānaṁ syāt ? punarāneyatavipākakarmaṇā śarīrasyārambha iti । na—abhihitapratividhānatvāt । samyagdarśanena kreśabījasya dāhāta karmaṇāmanārambhakatvamuktaṁ dagdhabījabhāvāpanītatuṣaśalitaṇḍulanidarśanena । tasmāt na viduṣaḥ kāraṇābhāvāccharīrārambhaḥ ॥ 25 ॥
body.translated_text:
[Vivaraṇa]
The four parts [of the teaching] have been commenced. Therein, the suffering to be avoided was stated—['The suffering yet to come is that which is to be avoided']. The first part, corresponding to disease, has been explained. [And the cause to be avoided, together with its basis, called conjunction, has been stated.] The second part, corresponding to the cause of disease, namely the conjunction of <s>pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> caused by <s>avidyā</s>—the cause to be avoided—has been described. And the re-stating of what follows is for the purpose of removing any further inquiry about the matter already stated with supporting reasoning.
[Hereafter, cessation (<s>hāna</s>)]—corresponding to health, the purpose of the science of liberation—[is to be stated.] The announcement of what is to follow is for the purpose of settling the listener's mind. [From the absence of that, the absence of conjunction—that is cessation. That is <s>kaivalya</s> for the seer.]
'That' (<s>tat</s>) is a reference back to the previously discussed <s>avidyā</s>. [From the absence of that non-seeing]—of <s>avidyā</s>—[the absence of the conjunction of <s>buddhi</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>]—the cause of suffering—[its absence, the absolute cessation of bondage—that is the meaning. This is cessation]—corresponding to health. ['That is <s>kaivalya</s> for the seer']—that very cessation, the absolute cessation of bondage, [is <s>kaivalya</s> for <s>Puruṣa</s>, the seer.] The explanation of this is: [the state of non-admixture of <s>Puruṣa</s>, non-conjunction with the <s>guṇas</s> once again—that is the meaning.]
Having explained the words, he now shows the meaning of the sentence: [When the cause of suffering ceases, the cessation of suffering is <s>hāna</s>. Then <s>Puruṣa</s> is established in its own nature—as was said: '<s>Citiśakti</s> (the power of consciousness) is established in its own form.']
Objection: If <s>karma</s> of undetermined fruition still exists, how can there be cessation? For through <s>karma</s> of undetermined fruition, there would be the origination of another body. Reply: No—because the remedy has been stated. Through right vision, by the burning of the seed of the <s>kleśas</s>, the inability of <s>karmas</s> to initiate [new births] has been stated with the illustration of rice-grain from which the husk has been removed through the burning of the seed. Therefore, for the wise one, because of the absence of the cause, there is no origination of a body. // 25 //

body.text: atha hānasya kaḥ prāptyupāya iti –
body.translated_text: Now, what is the means of attaining cessation (<s>hāna</s>)?

body.text: vivekakhyātiraviplavā hānopāyaḥ ॥ 26 ॥
body.translated_text: Unwavering discriminative knowledge (<s>vivekakhyāti</s>) is the means of cessation (<s>hānopāya</s>). // 26 //

body.text: sattvapuruṣānyatāpratyayo vivekakhyātiḥ। sā tvanivṛttamithyājñānā plavate। yadā mithyājñānaṁ dagdhabījabhāvaṁ vandhyaprasavaṁ saṁpadyate tadā vidhūtakleśarajasaḥ sattvasya pare vaiśāradye parasyāṁ vaśīkārasaṁjñāyāṁ vartamānasya vivekapratyayapravāho nirmalo bhavati। sā vivekakhyātiraviplavā hānopāyaḥ। tato mithyājñānasya dagdhabījabhāvopagamaḥ punaścāprasava ityeṣa mokṣasya mārgo hānasyopāya iti ॥ 26 ॥
body.translated_text: The cognition of the otherness of <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> is <s>vivekakhyāti</s> (discriminative knowledge). But as long as erroneous knowledge has not ceased, it wavers. When erroneous knowledge attains the state of a burnt seed—barren of offspring—then, for one whose <s>sattva</s> has been cleansed of the dust of the <s>kleśas</s>, abiding in the supreme mastery-stage (<s>vaśīkāra-saṃjñā</s>) of supreme clarity, the stream of discriminative cognition becomes pure. That unwavering discriminative knowledge is the means of cessation. Thereafter, the erroneous knowledge, having attained the state of a burnt seed and being barren of offspring—this is the path to liberation, the means of cessation. // 26 //

body.text:
vivaraṇam
uktastṛtīye vyūhaḥ – ārogyasthānīyo hānaṁ nāma । adhunā caturthaṁ vyūhaṁ bhaiṣajyasthānīyamupācikhyāsannāha – [hānasya kaḥ prāptyupāyaḥ?] iti ॥
nanu ca kathaṁ hānasya prāpyupāya iti ? yāvatā naiva hānamavastutvāt prāpyam । bandhanoparama eva hi hānam । naiṣa doṣaḥ । yatnasādhyatvādavidyānivṛtteḥ yathā nigalabhedaḥ । samyakūkhyātau satyāmavidyānivṛttiriti hānamavastvapi prāpyamityupacaryete ॥
[vivekakhyātiraviplavā hānopāyaḥ ।] kā punarvivekakhyātirityāha – [sattvapuruṣānyatāpratyayaḥ] sattvapuruṣayoḥ sādharmyayaivaidhamyaiyāthātmyāvabodha ityarthaḥ । [sā tu] vivekakhyātiḥ [anivṛttamithyājñānā vipluvatte] na sthirībhavati, na kāryekṣameti ॥
tathā coktam-- [‘yathā hemāvipakvaṁ na virājate ।]
[tathā'pakvakaṣāyasya vijñānaṁ na prakāśate ॥]
tathā [“kāmagrāhagṛhītasya jñānamapyasya na plavaḥ” ।] iti ॥
[yadā tu mithyājñānaṁ dagdhabījabhāvaṁ] dagdhabījatvādeva [vandhyaprasavaṁ] kāryārambhākṣamaṁ [sampadyate] , [tadā vidhūtakleśarajasaḥ] kleśā eva rajaḥ vidhūtaṁ yasya tadvidhūtakeśarajaḥ tasya [sattvasya] rāgādimalākalaṅkitasya [pararayāṁ vaśīkārasaṁjñāyāṁ vartamānasya] jñānaprasādamātre vartamānasya । tadevānuvadati – [vivekapratyayapravāhaḥ] vivekajñānanirantarabhāvaḥ [nirmalo bhavati ॥]
[sā vivekakhyātiḥ] itthaṁbhūtā satī [aviplavā bhavati ।] yadaivamaviplavā vivakakhyātiḥ [tato mithyājñānasya dagdhabījabhāvopagamo] viruddhatvāt । punaścāprasavaḥ mithyājñānasya dagdhabījabhāvopagamādeva । tathā coktam –
[“bījānyagnyupadagdhāni na rohanti yathā punaḥ ।]
[jñānadagdhaistathā kleśairnātmā sampadyate punaḥ ॥ ” iti ।]
sā ca tādṛśī vivekakhyāti [rmokṣasya mārgo hānasyopāya] ityarthaḥ ॥ 26 ॥
body.translated_text:
[Vivaraṇa]
The third part has been stated—cessation, corresponding to health. Now, wishing to teach the fourth part, corresponding to medicine, he says: [What is the means of attaining cessation?]
Objection: How can one speak of 'the means of attaining cessation'? Since cessation, being a non-entity, cannot be 'attained.' For cessation is merely the stopping of bondage. Reply: This is not a fault. Because the removal of <s>avidyā</s> is accomplished through effort—just as the breaking of chains is. When right knowledge arises, <s>avidyā</s> ceases—and thus cessation, though a non-entity, is figuratively said to be 'attained.'
[Unwavering discriminative knowledge is the means of cessation.] What then is discriminative knowledge? He says: [The cognition of the otherness of <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>]—the understanding of the true nature of the similarity and dissimilarity of <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>—that is the meaning. [But that] discriminative knowledge, [as long as erroneous knowledge has not ceased, wavers]—does not become stable, does not become capable of producing its effect.
And thus it has been said: ['Just as unpurified gold does not shine,]
[so too the knowledge of one whose impurities are unripened does not manifest.']
Likewise: ['For one seized by the crocodile of desire, even knowledge is not a raft.'] 
[When erroneous knowledge attains the state of a burnt seed]—precisely because of being a burnt seed—[barren of offspring]—incapable of initiating effects—[then, for one whose] dust of the <s>kleśas</s>—the <s>kleśas</s> themselves being the dust—[has been cleansed], for that <s>sattva</s>, unstained by the defilement of <s>rāga</s> and the rest, [abiding in the supreme mastery-stage]—abiding in the mere clarity of knowledge. He restates this: [the stream of discriminative cognition]—the uninterrupted continuity of discriminative knowledge—[becomes pure.]
[That discriminative knowledge], being of such a nature, [becomes unwavering.] When discriminative knowledge is thus unwavering, [then the erroneous knowledge attains the state of a burnt seed]—because of being opposed [to it]. And [it is] barren of offspring—precisely because erroneous knowledge has attained the state of a burnt seed. And thus it has been said:
['Just as seeds burnt by fire do not sprout again,]
[so too the self is not again bound by <s>kleśas</s> burnt by knowledge.']
And such discriminative knowledge [is the path to liberation, the means of cessation]—that is the meaning. // 26 //

body.text: tasya saptadhā prāntabhūmiḥ prajñā ॥ 27 ॥
body.translated_text: For one [whose discriminative knowledge has arisen], the sevenfold wisdom is at the final stage (<s>prāntabhūmi</s>). // 27 //

body.text: tasyeti pratyuditakhyāteḥ pratyāmnāyaḥ। saptadheti aśuddhyāvaraṇamalāpagamāccittasya pratyayāntarānutpāde sati saptaprakāraiva prajñā vivekino bhavati।
body.translated_text: 'For that one' (<s>tasya</s>) is a reference back to one whose discriminative knowledge has arisen. 'Sevenfold'—when the defilement, obstruction, and impurity have been removed, the <s>yogin</s> who discriminates has wisdom that is precisely sevenfold, there being no arising of any other cognition.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
utpakṣasamyagdarśanasya samyagdarśanotpattau svānubhavapratyayaliṅgaprakaṭīkaraṇārthamāha – [tasya saptadhā prāntabhūmiḥ prajñā । tasyeti pratyuditakhyāteḥ] pratyutpannasamyagdarśanasya [pratyāmnāyaḥ] pratyavamarśaḥ । [saptadheti aśuddhyāvaraṇamalāpagamāt ।] aśuddhirevāvaraṇaṁ kleśāḥ karmaṇi ca, tadeva malaṁ tasyāpagamāt [cittasya pratyayāntarānutpāde] mamāhamiti ca viruddhapratyayāntarāṇāmanutpattau । saptadhetyasya vivaraṇe [saptaprakāraiva prajñā] buddhiḥ [vivekino bhavati ॥]
body.translated_text:
[Vivaraṇa]
To make manifest through the mark of one's own experience-cognition that right vision has arisen for one whose right vision has been generated, he says: [For that one, the sevenfold wisdom is at the final stage. 'For that one' is a reference back to one whose] right vision has arisen in the present—[a reference back.] ['Sevenfold'—when the defilement, obstruction, and impurity have been removed.]—impurity itself is the obstruction—the <s>kleśas</s> and <s>karmas</s>—that itself is the defilement; from its removal, [when the mind has no arising of any other cognition]—when cognitions contrary [to discrimination], such as 'mine' and 'I,' do not arise. The elucidation of 'sevenfold' is: [the wisdom of the discriminating one is precisely sevenfold.]

body.text: tadyathā – parijñātaṁ heyaṁ nāsya punaḥ parijñeyamasti। kṣīṇā heyahetavo na punareteṣāṁ kṣetavyamasti। sākṣātkṛtaṁ nirodhasamādhinā hānam। bhāvito vivekakhyātirūpo hānopāya iti। eṣā catuṣṭayī kāryā vimuktiḥ prajñāyāḥ। cittavimuktistu trayī caritādhikārā buddhiḥ। guṇā giriśikharataṭacyutā iva grāvāṇo niravasthānāḥ svakāraṇe pralayābhimukhāḥ saha tenāstaṁ gacchanti। na caiṣāṁ pravilīnānāṁ punarastyutpādaḥ prayojanābhāvāditi। etasyāmavasthāyāṁ guṇasaṁbandhātītaḥ svarūpamātrajyotiramalaḥ kevalī puruṣa iti। etāṁ saptavidhāṁ prāntabhūbhiprajñāmanupaśyanpuruṣaḥ kuśala ityākhyāyate। pratiprasave'pi cittasya muktaḥ kuśala ityeva bhavati guṇātītatvāditi ॥ 27 ॥
body.translated_text: Namely: (1) 'That which is to be known has been fully known—there is nothing more to be known for him.' (2) 'The causes to be avoided have been exhausted—there is nothing more to be exhausted for them.' (3) 'Cessation has been directly realized through <s>nirodha-samādhi</s>.' (4) 'The means of cessation in the form of <s>vivekakhyāti</s> (discriminative knowledge) has been cultivated.' This is the fourfold liberation of wisdom relating to the task. But the threefold liberation of the mind is: (5) '<s>Buddhi</s>, having fulfilled its task.' (6) 'The <s>guṇas</s>, like boulders fallen from a mountain peak, without any resting place, facing dissolution into their own cause, disappear together with it.' (7) 'And for these, once dissolved, there is no further arising—because there is no further purpose.' In this state, <s>Puruṣa</s>, having transcended the connection with the <s>guṇas</s>, being mere light of its own nature, stainless, alone (<s>kevalin</s>)—thus [it is described]. One who sees this sevenfold wisdom at the final stage—that <s>Puruṣa</s> is called 'accomplished' (<s>kuśala</s>). Even at the re-dissolution of the mind, the liberated one is 'accomplished' indeed—because of having transcended the <s>guṇas</s>. // 27 //

body.text:
vivaraṇam
tān sapta prakārān kramaṇācaṣṭe – [yathā parijñātaṁ heyaṁ] sarvaṁ duḥkhaṁ heyaṁ sarvaṁ duḥkhaṁ heyaṁ jñātamupapattibhiḥ । [nāsya parijñātavyo] duḥkhaprakāraḥ ॥
[kṣīṇā heyahetava] iti bahuvacanaprayogāt kleśāḥ karmāṇi ca abhidhīyante । na punareṣāṁ kleśakarmaṇāmalpamapi samyagdarśanapāvakādagdhabījābhāvāt kṣe(dutprekṣi)tavyamasti । etenāpi prāntabhūmitvamevoktam । itthaṁ ca pratyupasthitasamīcīnapratyayasya kṣīṇakleśatvāt na kṣetavyamasti । kṛtakaraṇīyo'hamiti ca samyagdarśanaparipākaliṅgapratyaya upāvartate । yathā rogāturasya rogahetukṣaye nīrogo'haṁ na punarbhaiṣajyamastīti pratyayaḥ । evameva [ṣa] dvitīyaḥ prajñāprakāra uktaḥ ॥
[sākṣātkṛtaṁ nirodhasamāpattirhānam ।] hānapratyāsannatvāt hānatulyarūpatvācca nirodhasamādhireva hānamityākhyāyate । tacca [sākṣātkṛtam] anubhavaviṣayatāmānītam । tadidaṁ kaivalye paryavasitam kaivalyaṁ kartavyamiti ca prajñāyate । eṣo'pi prāntabhūmiprajñāprakāraḥ tṛtīya ākhyātaḥ ॥
[bhāvitaḥ] samyagabhyastataraḥ [vivekakhyātirūpo hānopāyaḥ ।] samyagdarśanaṁ yathāvadupasthitamiti niścitā cetprajñā vivekino jāyate sa eṣa caturthaḥ prajñāprakāraḥ । [ityeṣā catuṣṭayī kāryavimuktiḥ] kāryāt kartavyāt vimuktiryasyāḥ prajñāyāḥ sā kāryavimuktiḥ catūrūpā [prajñā] puruṣārthekartavyatetyarthaḥ ॥
atha vā – kāryasya vimuktiḥ nivṛttiḥ [kāryavimuktiḥ ।] sā ca [catuṣṭayī kāryavimuktiriti] samāptaṁ vākyam । [prajñā] iti pareṇa saṁbadhyate । katham ? prajñā (pra) yuktam, vivekakhyātiyuktaṁ cittaṁ [prajñācittaṁ] tasya vimuktiḥ pralayaḥ [prajñācittavimuktiḥ ।] sā trayī । tathā ca vakṣyati – [“puruṣārthaśūnyānāṁ guṇānāṁ pratiprasavaḥ kaivalyam” iti ॥]
tatra kāryavimuktiścatuṣṭayī । purūṣāthaiśśūnyatvaṁ pūrvamuktam । idānīṁ buddhiguṇānnivṛtiḥ । puruṣārthakartavyānāṁ puruṣārthaśūnyānāṁ pratiprasavaḥ prajñācittavimuktistrayī vyākhyāyate । yathā – [caritādhikārāḥ] nivṛttakartavyāḥ [buddhiguṇāḥ] sattvādayo buddhyākāravasthitāḥ [praळyābhimukhāḥ ।] kimiva ? [giriśikharakūṭacyutā iva grāvāṇo niravasthānāḥ] kartavyābhāvāt svakāraṇe ahaṁkāre [pralayābhimukhāḥ saha tena] buddhisaṁsthānena kāyeṁṇa, athavā, svakāraṇenāhaṅkāreṇa kuśalaṁ puruṣaṁ prati svakāraṇamapyavyaktabhāvaṁ pratipadyata iti [saha tenāstaṁ gacchanti] ityucyate । eṣā prathamā prajñācittavimuktiḥ ॥
[na caiṣāṁ pratipralīnānāṁ puruṣaṁ prati punarastyutpādaḥ prayojanābhāvāt ।] vimuktaṁ hi caturvidhaṁ kāryam । eṣā dvitīyā prajñācittavimuktiḥ ॥
[etasyāmavasthāyāṁ] caritārthaguṇapralayāvasthāyāṁ [guṇasambandhātītaḥ] guṇasaṁbandho draṣṭṛdṛśyalakṣaṇaḥ tamatītaḥ । svarūpamātrajyotiḥ dṛśisvarūpamātramevaṁ jyotiḥ । [puruṣaḥ kevalī śuddha] iti tṛtīyā prajñācittavimuktiriti ॥
[etāṁ saptavidhāṁ prāntabhūmiṁ] prāntāḥ pragatāvasānāḥ bhūmayaḥ avasthāḥ yasyāstāṁ [prāntabhūmiṁ prajñāmanupaśyan] samyagdarśanaliṅgaparipākabhūtāmīkṣamāṇaḥ [puruṣaḥ kuśala ityākhyāyate ।] kuśala iti saṅketaḥ । [pratiprasave'pi] pralaye'pi [cittasya muktaḥ kuśala ityeva] bhūtapūrvagatyā kuśala ityeva [bhavati ।] kutaḥ kauśalaṁ tasyetyāha – [guṇātītatvāt iti ।] guṇānatīto hi kuśalaḥ ॥ 27 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
He describes those seven types in order — ['That which is to be abandoned has been fully known'] — all suffering is to be abandoned, all suffering to be abandoned has been known through reasoning. ['There is nothing further to be known of it'] — no further aspect of suffering remains to be known. ||
['The causes of what is to be abandoned have been diminished'] — by the use of the plural, both <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and <s>karmas</s> (actions) are referred to. Moreover, not even a trace of these afflictions and actions is to be expected, since their seeds have been burnt by the fire of right vision (<s>samyag-darśana</s>). By this too, only the final stage (<s>prānta-bhūmi</s>) is indicated. And thus, for one in whom the correct cognition has arisen, there is nothing more to be diminished, since the afflictions are destroyed. And the conviction 'I have accomplished what was to be done' arises as an indication of the maturation of right vision. Just as for one afflicted with disease, when the cause of disease is destroyed, the conviction arises 'I am free from disease, there is no more need for medicine.' Thus the second type of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) has been stated. ||
['The cessation-attainment (<s>nirodha-samāpatti</s>) that has been directly realized is the abandonment.'] Because of the proximity to abandonment and because it has a form equivalent to abandonment, the <s>nirodha-samādhi</s> (cessation-absorption) itself is called abandonment. And that has been 'directly realized' — brought within the range of experience. This culminates in <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation), and the understanding arises that <s>kaivalya</s> is what must be accomplished. This too is a type of final-stage wisdom, declared as the third. ||
['The means of abandonment, which has the form of discriminative discernment (<s>viveka-khyāti</s>), has been fully cultivated'] — that is, it has been most thoroughly practiced. If the wisdom of the discerning one arises with the certainty that right vision has been properly established, this is the fourth type of <s>prajñā</s>. ['This is the fourfold liberation from duty (<s>kārya-vimukti</s>)'] — the liberation from what is to be done, that <s>prajñā</s> which is free from duty in its four forms — the meaning is that there is nothing more to be accomplished regarding <s>puruṣārtha</s> (the purpose of the Self). ||
Alternatively — the cessation of duty is 'liberation from duty' (<s>kārya-vimukti</s>). And ['this is the fourfold liberation from duty'] — this completes the sentence. ['<s>Prajñā</s>'] connects with what follows. How? The mind endowed with <s>prajñā</s>, endowed with <s>viveka-khyāti</s> (discriminative discernment), is the 'wisdom-mind' (<s>prajñā-citta</s>); its liberation, its dissolution, is the 'liberation of the wisdom-mind' (<s>prajñā-citta-vimukti</s>). That is threefold. And so it will be stated — ['The return of the <s>guṇas</s> to their source, when devoid of purpose for <s>Puruṣa</s>, is <s>kaivalya</s>' (liberation).] ||
Therein, the fourfold liberation from duty has been stated. The emptiness of purpose for <s>Puruṣa</s> was stated earlier. Now the cessation of the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) is described. The <s>pratiprasava</s> (return to source) of those devoid of purpose for <s>Puruṣa</s> is explained as the threefold liberation of the wisdom-mind. Namely — ['Having fulfilled their function'] — their duties completed — ['the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>buddhi</s>'] — <s>sattva</s> and the others established as modifications of <s>buddhi</s> — ['incline toward dissolution.'] Like what? ['Like boulders fallen from a mountain peak, without any resting place'] — due to the absence of any purpose to fulfill, they incline toward dissolution into their cause, <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego), ['together with that'] — with that constitution of <s>buddhi</s>, that body; or alternatively, together with their cause <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, they attain even the state of the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) with respect to the liberated <s>Puruṣa</s> — thus it is said ['they set together with that.'] This is the first liberation of the wisdom-mind. ||
['And for these, once dissolved, there is no further arising with respect to <s>Puruṣa</s>, due to the absence of any purpose.'] For the fourfold duty has been discharged. This is the second liberation of the wisdom-mind. ||
['In this state'] — in the state of dissolution of the <s>guṇas</s> that have fulfilled their purpose — ['having transcended connection with the <s>guṇas</s>'] — the connection with the <s>guṇas</s>, characterized as seer-seen, has been transcended. A light consisting of its own nature alone — the light of seeing (<s>dṛśi</s>) in its own form alone — ['<s>Puruṣa</s> is isolated (<s>kevalī</s>), pure'] — this is the third liberation of the wisdom-mind. ||
['This sevenfold final stage'] — the stages (<s>bhūmis</s>) that have reached their ultimate conclusion — ['one who perceives this final-stage wisdom'] — one who beholds it as having matured through the indications of right vision — ['that <s>Puruṣa</s> is called accomplished (<s>kuśala</s>).'] <s>Kuśala</s> is a conventional designation. ['Even in the dissolution (<s>pratiprasava</s>)'] — even in the dissolution ['of the mind, the liberated one is called accomplished (<s>kuśala</s>)'] — by virtue of the former designation, he is indeed called <s>kuśala</s>. Why is there accomplishment for him? He says — ['Because of having transcended the <s>guṇas</s>.'] For one who has transcended the <s>guṇas</s> is indeed accomplished. || 27 ||

body.text: siddhā bhavati vivekakhyātirhānopāya iti, na ca siddhirantareṇa sādhanamityetadārabhyate –
body.translated_text: It has been established that <s>viveka-khyāti</s> (discriminative discernment) is the means of abandonment, and that accomplishment does not occur without the means — this is now introduced —

body.text: yogāṅgānuṣṭhānādaśuddhikṣaye jñānadīptirāvivekakhyāteḥ ॥ 28 ॥
body.translated_text: From the practice of the limbs of <s>Yoga</s>, upon the destruction of impurity, the light of knowledge arises, extending up to discriminative discernment (<s>viveka-khyāti</s>). || 28 ||

body.text: yogāṅgānyaṣṭāvabhidhāyiṣyamāṇāni। teṣāmanuṣṭhānātpañcaparvaṇo viparyayasyāśuddhirūpasya kṣayo nāśaḥ। tatkṣaye samyagjñānasyābhivyaktiḥ। yathā yathā ca sādhanānyanuṣṭhīyante tathā tathā tanutvamaśuddhirāpadyate। yathā yathā ca kṣīyate tathā tathā kṣayakramānurodhinī jñānasyāpi dīptirvivardhate। sā khalveṣā vivṛddhiḥ prakarṣamanubhavatyā vivekakhyāteḥ, āguṇapuruṣasvarūpavijñānādityarthaḥ। yogāṅgānuṣṭhānamaśuddherviyogakāraṇam। yathā paraśuśchedyasya। vivekakhyātestu prāptikāraṇaṁ yathā dharmaḥ sukhasya nānyathā kāraṇam। kati caitāni kāraṇāni śāstre bhavanti। navaivetyāha।
body.translated_text: The limbs of <s>Yoga</s> are eight, which will be enumerated. From their practice, the destruction — the annihilation — of impurity in the form of the fivefold error (<s>viparyaya</s>) occurs. Upon that destruction, the manifestation of right knowledge takes place. And as the means are progressively practiced, so impurity progressively becomes attenuated. And as it diminishes, so the light of knowledge increases in accordance with the progressive order of diminution. That increase reaches its culmination up to <s>viveka-khyāti</s> (discriminative discernment) — the meaning is: up to the knowledge of the distinction between <s>guṇas</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>. The practice of the limbs of <s>Yoga</s> is the cause of separation from impurity, like an axe for what is to be cut. But for <s>viveka-khyāti</s>, it is the cause of attainment, as <s>dharma</s> (merit) is for happiness — not otherwise a cause. How many such causes are there in the science (<s>śāstra</s>)? Nine only, he says.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[siddhā vivekakhyātiḥ] samadhigatā vivekakhyātiḥ saptavidhaprāntabhūmiprajñāphalāvasānā [hānasyopāya iti । na ca siddhiḥ antareṇa sādhanam, ityata idaṁ] vivekakhyātisiddhisādhanārthamārabhyate – [yogāṅgānuṣṭhānādaśuddhikṣaye jñānadīptirāvivekakhyateḥ ॥]
yogāṅgānuṣṭhānādeva vivekakhyātiriti nāvadidhārayiṣitam, gurūpāsanadharmaprabhṛtikebhyo'pi vivekakhyāteḥ siddhiriṣyata eva ! kiṁ tarhi ? sādhanamātramantareṇa na bhavatyevetyavadhārayiṣyate । na punaryogāṅgānuṣṭhānameva sādhanaṁ, yogāṅgānuṣṭhānāttu bhavatyeva vivekakhyāti siddhiriti । tathā cācāryairuktam – [‘yogastattvajñānārthaḥ’] iti ॥
[yogāṅgānyabhidhāyiṣyamāṇāni teṣāmanuṣṭhānaṁ] yogāṅgānuṣṭhānam tasmāt । aśuddheḥ kleśākhyāyāḥ kṣayaḥ, tatkṣaye dīptiḥ prakarṣaḥ । kiyadavasānetyāha- [ā vivekakhyateḥ] bhavatītyupaskāraḥ ॥
svayameva bhāṣyakāraḥ spaṣṭataraṁ vivṛṇoti- [yogāṅgānyaṣṭāvabhidhāyiṣyamāṇāni । teṣāmanuṣṭhānāt paśvaparvaṇo viparyayasya aśuddhirūpasya kṣayaḥ nāśaḥ, tatkṣaye samyagdarśanasyābhivyaktiḥ'] dīptiḥ । kathametadbhavatītyāha - [yathā yathā ca sādhanānyanuṣṭhīyante tathā tathā tanutvamaśuddhirāpadyate ।] tathā ca manurabhāṣiṣṭa –
[“prāṇāyāmairdaheddoṣān dhāraṇābhiśca kilbiṣān ।]
[pratyāhāreṇa saṁsargān dhyānenānaiśvarān guṇān ॥ ” iti ।]
[yathā yathā cāśuddhiḥ kṣīyate tathā tathā tatkṣayakramānuredhinī] divasakarasyeva śiśirāvasāne [jñānasya dīptirvivardhate । sā khalviyaṁ vivṛddhiḥ prakarṣamanubhavati ।] kimavasānam ? tadāha- [ā vivekakhyāteḥ ।] tasya vyākhyānam - [ā guṇapuruṣasvarūpavivekajñānādityarthaḥ ।] sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātiparyavasānaiva śuddhiḥ ॥
[yogāṅgānuṣṭhānamaśuddheḥ kṣayakāraṇaṁ vivekakhyāteśca prāptikāraṇamiti,] dvidhaiva kāraṇam, dharmaparaśudvayasthānīyamekamubhayakāraṇaṁ, [nānyathā] bhavatīti । tatra kāraṇaprasaṅgena śāstraprasiddhāni kāraṇāni vyācaṣṭe – [kati caitāni kāraṇāni śāstre bhavanti ? navaivetyāha ।]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['<s>Viveka-khyāti</s> is established'] — <s>viveka-khyāti</s> (discriminative discernment), which has been attained, culminating in the fruit of the sevenfold final-stage wisdom, ['is the means of abandonment. And accomplishment does not occur without the means — therefore this'] is begun for the purpose of establishing the means of accomplishing <s>viveka-khyāti</s> — ['From the practice of the limbs of <s>Yoga</s>, upon the destruction of impurity, the light of knowledge extends up to <s>viveka-khyāti</s>.'] ||
It is not intended to establish that <s>viveka-khyāti</s> arises from the practice of the limbs of <s>Yoga</s> alone, for the accomplishment of <s>viveka-khyāti</s> is indeed accepted as arising also from attending upon a teacher (<s>guru-upāsana</s>), <s>dharma</s>, and other means. What then? It is to be determined that without some means it simply does not arise. But it is not that the practice of the limbs of <s>Yoga</s> alone is the means — rather, from the practice of the limbs of <s>Yoga</s>, the accomplishment of <s>viveka-khyāti</s> certainly does occur. And so the teachers have said — ['<s>Yoga</s> is for the purpose of knowledge of reality (<s>tattva-jñāna</s>).'] ||
['The limbs of <s>Yoga</s>, which will be enumerated — their practice'] constitutes the practice of the limbs of <s>Yoga</s>. From that, the destruction of impurity known as <s>kleśa</s> (affliction) occurs; upon that destruction, the light — the excellence — of knowledge arises. How far does it extend? He says — ['up to <s>viveka-khyāti</s>'] — the supplement is 'it arises.' ||
The commentator (<s>Bhāṣyakāra</s>) himself elucidates more clearly — ['The limbs of <s>Yoga</s> are eight, which will be enumerated. From their practice, the destruction — the annihilation — of impurity in the form of the fivefold error (<s>viparyaya</s>) occurs; upon that destruction, the manifestation of right vision'] — that is, its light. How does this happen? He says — ['As the means are progressively practiced, so impurity progressively becomes attenuated.'] And so <s>Manu</s> has declared —
['Through <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control), one burns away faults; through <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), sins;]
[through <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal of senses), impure associations; through <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), qualities that are not divine.'] ||
['And as impurity diminishes, so in accordance with the progressive order of that diminution'] — like the sun at the end of winter — ['the light of knowledge increases. That increase reaches its culmination.'] To what end? He states — ['up to <s>viveka-khyāti</s>.'] Its explanation — ['the meaning is: up to the knowledge of the distinction between the essential natures of <s>guṇas</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>.'] Purity culminates in the discernment of the difference between <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> (<s>sattva-puruṣa-anyatā-khyāti</s>). ||
['The practice of the limbs of <s>Yoga</s> is the cause of the destruction of impurity and the cause of the attainment of <s>viveka-khyāti</s>'] — the causality is twofold only, standing in the place of both <s>dharma</s> and the axe; one single means is the cause of both — ['it is not otherwise.'] In that connection, by way of discussing causation, he explains the causes well-known in the science (<s>śāstra</s>) — ['How many such causes are there in the science? Nine only, he says.']

body.text: tadyathā – utpattisthityabhivyaktivikārapratyayāptayaḥ। viyogānyatvadhṛtayaḥ kāraṇaṁ navadhā smṛtam ॥ iti। tatrotpattikāraṇaṁ mano bhavati vijñānasya, sthitikāraṇaṁ manasaḥ puruṣārthatā, śarīrasyevā''hāra iti। abhivyaktikāraṇaṁ yathā rūpasyā''lokastathā rūpajñānaṁ, vikārakāraṇaṁ manaso viṣayāntaram। yathā'gniḥ pākasya। pratyayakāraṇaṁ dhūmajñānamagnijñānasya। prāptikāraṇaṁ yogāṅgānuṣṭhānaṁ vivekakhyāteḥ।
body.translated_text:
Namely — arising, persistence, manifestation, modification, cognition, attainment,
separation, alteration, and sustenance — causation is remembered as ninefold. ||
Therein, the cause of arising: the mind is the cause of arising for cognition (<s>vijñāna</s>). The cause of persistence: the purpose of serving <s>Puruṣa</s> is the cause of persistence for the mind, as food is for the body. The cause of manifestation: as light is for form, so too for the knowledge of form. The cause of modification: another object is the cause of modification for the mind, as fire is for cooking. The cause of cognition: knowledge of smoke is the cause of the knowledge of fire. The cause of attainment: the practice of the limbs of <s>Yoga</s> is the cause of attainment of <s>viveka-khyāti</s> (discriminative discernment).

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tadyathā] – tāni ślokenaiva kathayati [utpattisthityabhivyaktivikārapratyayāptayaḥ ।]
[viyogānyatvadhṛtayaḥ kāraṇaṁ navadhā smṛtam ॥] iti ।
tatpravivekārthamudāharaṇāni prastāviṣyante । [tatrotpattikāraṇaṁ mano bhavati [vijñānasya]] , manaso hi vṛttiḥ [jñānaṁ,] yathā jalamūrbhīṇām ॥
[sthitikāraṇaṁ] sthiteḥ kāraṇam [manasaḥ puruṣārthatā ।] bhogāpavargārthavena hi manasaḥ sthitiḥ । [śarīrasya] yathā sthitikāraṇa [māhāraḥ ॥]
[abhivyakteḥ kāraṇaṁ rūpasyālokaḥ । tadā rūpajñānam ।] na hyālokenānabhivyakte rūpe'vabodhaḥ ॥
[vikārasya] kāraṇaṁ [manaso viṣayāntaram ।] viṣayāntarasannidhānena hi mano vikriyāmāsīdati । [yathā agniḥ pākasya ।] yaḥ pākākhyo vikārastasya pākasya vikārarūpasyāgniḥ kāraṇaṁ yathā ॥
[pratyayakāraṇaṁ dhūmajñānamagnijñānasya ।] pratyayasya phalavataḥ pramāṇasya kāraṇamityarthaḥ । pūrvatra tu [‘bhavati vijñānasya’] iti jñānasyopādānakāraṇaṁ vivakṣitam ॥
[prāptikāraṇaṁ yogāṅgānuṣṭhāne vivekakhyāteḥ] dharma iva sukhasya ।
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['Namely'] — he states them through a verse itself: ['Arising, persistence, manifestation, modification, cognition, attainment,]
[separation, alteration, and sustenance — causation is remembered as ninefold.'] ||
For the purpose of distinguishing among these, examples are presented. ['Therein, the cause of arising: the mind is the cause of arising for cognition (<s>vijñāna</s>)'] — for the activity (<s>vṛtti</s>) of the mind is knowledge, just as water is for aquatic creatures. ||
['The cause of persistence'] — the cause of persistence ['for the mind is the purpose of serving <s>Puruṣa</s>.'] For the mind persists by virtue of serving the purposes of experience (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>). ['As food is the cause of persistence for the body.'] ||
['The cause of manifestation: light is the cause of manifestation of form. Then arises the knowledge of form.'] For there is no apprehension of form when it has not been manifested by light. ||
['The cause of modification for the mind is another object.'] For the mind undergoes modification due to the proximity of a different object. ['As fire is for cooking.'] Just as fire is the cause of the modification known as cooking — the cause of that modification in the form of cooking. ||
['The cause of cognition: knowledge of smoke is the cause of the knowledge of fire.'] The meaning is: it is the cause of a fruitful means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>). But in the earlier case, ['the cause of arising for cognition'] — there the material cause (<s>upādāna-kāraṇa</s>) of knowledge was intended. ||
['The cause of attainment: the practice of the limbs of <s>Yoga</s> for <s>viveka-khyāti</s>'] — as <s>dharma</s> is for happiness.

body.text: viyogakāraṇaṁ tadevāśuddheḥ। anyatvakāraṇaṁ yathā suvarṇasya suvarṇakāraḥ। evamekasya strīpratyayasyāvidyā mūḍhatve dveṣo duḥkhatve rāgaḥ sukhatve tattvajñānaṁ mādhyasthye। dhṛtikāraṇaṁ śarīramindriyāṇām। tāni ca tasya। mahābhūtāni śarīrāṇāṁ, tāni ca parasparaṁ sarveṣāṁ tairyagyaunamānuṣadaivatāni ca parasparārthatvādityevaṁ nava kāraṇāni। tāni ca yathāsaṁbhavaṁ padārthāntareṣvapi yojyāni। yogāṅgānuṣṭhānaṁ tu dvidhaiva kāraṇatvaṁ labhata iti ॥ 28 ॥
body.translated_text: That same [practice of the limbs of <s>Yoga</s>] is the cause of separation from impurity. The cause of alteration: as a goldsmith is for gold. Thus, of a single cognition of 'woman,' <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is the cause of delusion, <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion) is the cause of its being painful, <s>rāga</s> (attachment) is the cause of its being pleasurable, and knowledge of reality (<s>tattva-jñāna</s>) is the cause of equanimity (<s>mādhyasthya</s>). The cause of sustenance: the body is the cause of sustenance for the sense organs, and they in turn for it. The great elements (<s>mahābhūtas</s>) are the cause of sustenance for bodies, and they mutually sustain one another. The animal, human, and divine realms mutually sustain each other because they serve one another's purposes. Thus there are nine causes, and they should be applied to other categories as appropriate. The practice of the limbs of <s>Yoga</s>, however, obtains only a twofold causality. || 28 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tadevāśuddherviyogakāraṇaṁ] paraśuriva chedyasya ॥
[anyatvakāraṇaṁ yathā suvarṇakāraḥ suvarṇasya ।] suvarṇaṁ hi bhittvā vardhamānakamanyaṁ karoti । tathā vardhamānakaṁ bhitvā anyadābharaṇāntaraṁ karoti । tathā'nyaditi ॥
[evamekasya 'strī' iti pratyayasyāpi avidyā kāraṇaṁ mūḍhatve । dveṣa] stasyaiva strīpratyayasya [duḥkhatve kāraṇam ।] tathā [rāgaḥ sukhatve ।] tathā tasyaiva [mādhyasthye] heyopādeyaśūnyatāyāṁ [vivekayuktaṁ jñānaṁ] kāraṇam । evamekaḥ strīpratyayaḥ suvarṇavadanekadhā mūḍhatvaduḥkhatvasukhatvamādhyasthyādibhedairbhidyate ॥
[dhṛteḥ kāraṇam ।] dhāraṇe dhṛtiḥ, tasyāḥ kāraṇaṁ [śarīramindriyāṇām ।] na hi śarīramaprāpyendriyāṇi dhṛtiṁ labhante । [tāni] cendriyāṇi [tasya] śarīrasya [dhṛtikāraṇaṁ] bhavanti । indriyavṛttidvāreṇa hi śariraṁ dhriyate ॥
tathā [mahābhūtānyā] kāśādīni [śarīrāṇāṁ] dhṛtikāraṇam । mahābhūtārabdhāni hi śarīrāṇi brahmādistambāvasānāni [[tāni ca] parasparam] upakāryopakārakatvadvāreṇa dhṛtikāraṇam ॥
tathā [sarveṣāṁ] padārthānāṁ [tairyagyaunamānuṣadaivatāni] dhṛtikāraṇam । kutaḥ? [parasparārthatvāt ।] tairyagyaunaṁ mānuṣadaivatayorvāhanadohanahavirādibhirupakurvat dhṛtikāraṇam ॥
tathā mānuṣaṁ ijyārakṣaṇādibhirdaivatairyagyaunayoḥ dhṛtikāraṇam । tathā daivamitarayoḥ śītoṣṇapravarṣaṇārdanā dhṛtikāraṇam ॥
evaṁ varṇāśramāṇāmapyanyonyopakāreṇa dhṛtikāraṇatvam । parasparopāśrayeṇa hi jagadakhilamapi dhriyate । [evaṁ navaiva kāraṇāni] iti kāraṇāntaraṁ pratiṣedhati । [tāni ca yathā'rthasaṁbhavaṁ] yo yo'rthasaṁbhavaḥ [padārthāntareṣvapya] nudāhṛteṣu [tathā ye.ājyāni । yogāṅgānuṣṭhānaṁ tu dvidhaiva kāraṇatvaṁ labhate ।] tathā ca vyākhyātam ॥ 28 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['That same is the cause of separation from impurity'] — like an axe for what is to be cut. ||
['The cause of alteration: as a goldsmith is for gold.'] For the goldsmith breaks gold and makes a <s>vardhamānaka</s> (ornamental design) or another form. Likewise, breaking the <s>vardhamānaka</s>, he makes yet another ornament. And so on. ||
['Thus, of a single cognition of "woman," <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is the cause of delusion. <s>Dveṣa</s>'] (aversion) ['is the cause of that very cognition of "woman" being painful.'] Likewise, ['<s>rāga</s> (attachment) is the cause of its being pleasurable.'] Likewise, ['knowledge endowed with discrimination (<s>viveka</s>) is the cause of equanimity (<s>mādhyasthya</s>)'] — of the state of being free from what is to be rejected or accepted. Thus a single cognition of 'woman' is divided in multiple ways — like gold — into the distinctions of delusion, painfulness, pleasurableness, equanimity, and so forth. ||
['The cause of sustenance'] — <s>dhṛti</s> means sustaining; its cause is ['the body for the sense organs.'] For the sense organs do not obtain sustenance without reaching the body. ['And they'] — the sense organs — ['are the cause of sustenance for that'] — the body. For the body is sustained through the activity of the sense organs. ||
Likewise, ['the great elements (<s>mahābhūtas</s>)'] — space and the rest — ['are the cause of sustenance for bodies.'] For bodies from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass are constituted of the great elements. ['And they'] are ['the cause of sustenance for one another'] — through the relationship of mutually supporting and being supported. ||
Likewise, ['the animal, human, and divine realms are the cause of sustenance for all'] categories. Why? ['Because they serve one another's purposes.'] The animal realm serves as a cause of sustenance for the human and divine realms through being mounts, being milked, providing oblations, and so forth. ||
Likewise, the human realm is the cause of sustenance for the divine and animal realms through sacrifice, protection, and the like. Likewise, the divine realm is the cause of sustenance for the other two through cold, heat, rain, and nourishment. ||
Thus, the <s>varṇas</s> (social orders) and <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life) too are causes of sustenance for one another through mutual assistance. For the entire world is sustained through mutual dependence. ['Thus there are nine causes only'] — he negates any additional cause. ['And they, as appropriate to the meaning'] — whatever the relevant application — ['should be applied to other categories as well'] — those not exemplified. ['The practice of the limbs of <s>Yoga</s>, however, obtains only a twofold causality.'] And that has been explained. || 28 ||

body.text: tatra yogāṅgānyavadhāryante –
body.translated_text: Now the limbs of <s>Yoga</s> are to be ascertained —

body.text: yamaniyamāsana​prāṇāyāmapratyāhāra​dhāraṇādhyāna​samādhayo'ṣṭāvaṅgāni ॥ 29 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>Yama</s> (restraint), <s>niyama</s> (observance), <s>āsana</s> (posture), <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control), <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal of the senses), <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and <s>samādhi</s> (absorption) are the eight limbs. || 29 ||

body.text: yathākramameṣāmanuṣṭhānaṁ svarūpaṁ ca vakṣyāmaḥ ॥ 29 ॥
body.translated_text: We shall describe the practice and the essential nature of these in order. || 29 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
kāni punastāni yogāṅgāni? yeṣāmanuṣṭhānaṁ dvidhā kāraṇatvaṁ labhata iti । [tatra yogāṅgānyavadhāryante – yamaniyamāsanaprāṇāyāmapratyāhāradhāraṇādhyānasamādhayo'ṣṭāvaṅgāni ॥]
nanu ca yogaśāstrāntareṣvāsanādīnyeva ṣaḍaṅgāni । tadyathā - [‘ṣaḍaṅgo yoga ucyata'] ityādi ।
kiñca – sākṣādāsanādīnyeva samādherupakurvanti, na yamaniyamau ॥
naiṣa doṣaḥ । yamaniyamavatoryogādhikāropapatteḥ । na hi yathākāmacāriṇāṁ yogādhikāraḥ । [‘nāvirato duścaritānnāśanāntaḥ’] iti śruteḥ । tathā – [‘yeṣāṁ tapo brahmacaryaṁ yeṣu satyaṁ pratiṣṭhitam’] ityādi cātharvaṇe । tathā gītāyām [‘brahmacārivrate sthitaḥ’] iti । tasmādyamaniyamayorapyaṅgatvam ॥
yamaniyamayośca yamasya prathamopādānaṁ prādhānyakhyāpanārtham । yamasya hi prādhānyaṁ sarvatra siddham । yamaniyamayuktasyādhikṛtasya yogina āsanādyaṅgānāṁ pūrvapūrve sthirapadaprāptasyottarottarānuṣṭhānaṁ prāptam । na hi prathamaṁ sopānamanāruhyottaramāroḍhuṁ śakyam ॥
yadanyatrācyate –
[“sthānāsanavidhānāni yogasya vidhayo'pi vā ।]
[vyākṣepajanākāḥ sarve na te yogasya hetavaḥ ॥]
[sarvadoṣaparityāgaḥ samādhiśceti taddvayam ॥]
[nirṇaya[yāt] yogahetuḥ syādbhavati vānyanna vā [bhavatvanyanna vā bhavet] ॥ ”] iti ॥
tatsamādhisarvadoṣaparityāgayoḥ prādhānyāt tatstutyartham, nāsanādyaṅgapratiṣedhārtham । [yathākramameṣāṁ] yamādīnā [manuṣṭhānaṁ svarūpaṁ ca vakṣyāmaḥ] - svarūpe hi anavagate nānuṣṭhātuṁ śakyamiti ॥ 29 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
What then are those limbs of yoga, whose practice obtains causality in two ways? [Therein, the limbs of yoga are ascertained — <s>Yama</s>, <s>niyama</s>, <s>āsana</s>, <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, <s>pratyāhāra</s>, <s>dhāraṇā</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, and <s>samādhi</s> are the eight limbs.]
But in other yoga treatises, only six limbs beginning with <s>āsana</s> are taught — as in ['Yoga is said to have six limbs'] and so forth.
Moreover — directly, <s>āsana</s> and the rest

body.text: tatra –
body.translated_text: Among these —

body.text: ahiṁsāsatyasteyabrahmacaryāparigrahā yamāḥ ॥ 30 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>Ahiṁsā</s> (non-violence), <s>satya</s> (truthfulness), <s>asteya</s> (non-stealing), <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy), and <s>aparigraha</s> (non-possessiveness) are the <s>yamas</s> (restraints). || 30 ||

body.text: tatrāhiṁsā sarvathā sarvadā sarvabhūtānāmanabhidrohaḥ। uttare ca yamaniyamāstanmūlāstatsiddhiparatayaiva tatpratipādanāya pratipādyante। tadavadātarūpakaraṇāyevopādīyante। tathā coktam – sa khalvayaṁ brāhmaṇo yathā yathā vratāni bahūni samāditsate tathā tathā pramādakṛtebhyo hiṁsānidānebhyo nivartamānastāmevāvadātarūpāmahiṁsāṁ karoti।
body.translated_text: Among these, <s>ahiṁsā</s> (non-violence) is the non-harming of all beings in every way and at all times. The subsequent <s>yamas</s> and <s>niyamas</s> are rooted in it, and are taught for the purpose of establishing and perfecting it. They are adopted for the purpose of purifying its form. And thus it has been stated: 'Indeed, the more vows this <s>brāhmaṇa</s> undertakes, the more he turns away from occasions of harm caused by negligence,'

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tatra] teṣu yamādiṣu prathamaṁ yamā vyākhyāyante- [ahiṁsāsatyāsteyabrahmacaryāparigrahā yamāḥ । tatrāhiṁsā sarvathā] sarvātmanā sarvaprakāreṇa, [sarvabhūtānāmanabhidrohaḥ] sarvabhūtānāṁ sthāvarajaṅgamānāṁ anabhidroho'pīḍanam ॥
yamaniyamānāmahiṁsā pradhānabhūtā kāyavāṅmanasaiḥ sarvātmanā karaṇīyeti darśayati – [uttare ca yamāḥ] satyādayaḥ [tanmūlāḥ] ahiṁsāprayojanāḥ ahiṁsārthāḥ [tatsiddhiparatayaiva] ahiṁsāsiddhitatparatvena [pratipādyante ।] kimukaṁ bhavatītyāha - [tadavadāta[rūpa]karaṇāyopādīyante] ahiṁsāśuddhipratipādānāyopādayante ॥
tathā hyuktam – sa khalvayaṁ [brāhmaṇo yathā yathā bahūni vratāni samāditsate tathā tathā pramādakṛtebhyo hiṁsānidānebhyaḥ] hiṁsāmūlebhyaḥ hiṁsākāraṇebhyaḥ [nivartamānastāmevāvadātarūpāmahiṁsāṁ karoti iti ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['Among these'] — among the <s>yamas</s> and the rest, first the <s>yamas</s> are explained — ['<s>Ahiṁsā</s>, <s>satya</s>, <s>asteya</s>, <s>brahmacarya</s>, and <s>aparigraha</s> are the <s>yamas</s>. Among these, <s>ahiṁsā</s> is, in every way'] — in all respects, in every manner — ['the non-harming of all beings'] — the non-injury, the non-affliction, of all beings, whether stationary or moving.
<s>Ahiṁsā</s> is the principal among the <s>yamas</s> and <s>niyamas</s>, to be practiced in all respects through body, speech, and mind,

body.text: satyaṁ yathārthe vāṅmanase। yathā dṛṣṭaṁ yathā'numitaṁ tathā vāṅmanaśceti। paratra svabodhasaṁkrāntaye vāguktā, sā yadi na vañcitā bhrāntā vā pratipattivandhyā vā bhavediti। eṣā sarvabhūtopakārārthaṁ pravṛttā na bhūtopaghātāya। yadi caivamapyabhidhīyamānā bhūtopaghātaparaiva syānna satyaṁ bhavetpāpameva bhavettena puṇyābhāsena puṇyapratirūpakeṇa kaṣṭaṁ tamaḥ prāpnuyāt। tasmātparīkṣya sarvabhūtahitaṁ satyaṁ brūyāt।
body.translated_text: <s>Satya</s> (truthfulness) is speech and mind being in accordance with reality. As it is seen and as it is inferred, so are speech and mind. Speech is employed for the purpose of communicating one's own understanding to another, and it should be neither deceptive, nor erroneous, nor barren of comprehension. It is undertaken for the benefit of all beings, not for their harm. And if even when thus spoken it would result only in harm to beings, it would not be <s>satya</s> but rather sin,

body.text:
vivaraṇam
uktaṁ ca – satyaṁ brūyāt priyaṁ brūyānna brūyāt satyamapriyam । priyaṁ ca nānṛtaṁ brūyādeṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ ॥ ” iti ।
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
And it has been said: 'One should speak the truth, one should speak what is pleasant; one should not speak truth that is unpleasant. One should not speak a pleasant untruth — this is the eternal <s>dharma</s>.'

body.text: steyamaśāstrapūrvakaṁ dravyāṇāṁ parataḥ svīkaraṇaṁ, tatpratiṣedhaḥ punaraspṛhārūpamasteyamiti। brahmacaryaṁ guptendriyasyopasthasya saṁyamaḥ। viṣayāṇāmarjanarakṣaṇakṣayasaṅgahiṁsādoṣadarśanādasvīkaraṇamaparigraha ityete yamāḥ ॥ 30 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>Steya</s> (stealing) is the appropriation of another's property without scriptural authorization; its negation, in the form of the absence of covetousness, is <s>asteya</s> (non-stealing). <s>Brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) is the restraint of the concealed organ of generation. <s>Aparigraha</s> (non-possessiveness) is the non-acceptance of objects, having seen the faults of acquisition, preservation, loss, attachment, and harm — these are the <s>yamas</s>. || 30 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[steyaṁ aśāsrapūrvaṁ dravyāṇāṁ parataḥ svīkaraṇaṁ] spṛhānimittam । yat steyaṁ [tatpratiṣedhastu] na spṛhālūnāṁ sambhavatīti tasyaiva steyasya pratiṣedhastu । saḥ aspṛhārūpamasteyamucyate ॥
[brahmacaryaṁ guptendriyasya] guptānyendriyasya puruṣasya abrahmacaryārthavāṅmanasādivṛttiśūnyasya [upasthendriyasaṁyama] iti ॥
[viṣayāṇāmārjanarakṣaṇakṣayasaṅgahiṁsādoṣadarśanādasvīkaraṇam] anupādānaṁ [aparigrahaḥ ।] na punarasāmarthyenāsvīkaraṇam । ityete yamāḥ ॥ 30 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['<s>Steya</s> is the appropriation of another's property without scriptural authorization'] — motivated by covetousness. That which is stealing — ['its negation, however,'] is not possible for those who are not covetous, so the negation is of that very stealing. That ['which has the form of absence of covetousness is called <s>asteya</s>.'].
['<s>Brahmacarya</s> is'] the restraint of ['the concealed organ'] — of a person whose organs are controlled, who is free from mental and verbal activity directed toward unchastity,

body.text: te tu –
body.translated_text: But these —

body.text: jātideśakālasamayānavacchinnāḥ sārvabhaumā mahāvratam ॥ 31 ॥
body.translated_text: When not limited by birth, place, time, and circumstance, and extending to all, they constitute the great vow (<s>mahāvrata</s>). || 31 ||

body.text: tatrāhiṁsā jātyavacchinnā matsyavadhakasya matsyeṣveva nānyatra hiṁsā। saiva deśāvacchinnā na tīrthe haniṣyāmīti। saiva kālāvacchinnā na caturdaśyāṁ na puṇye'hani haniṣyāmīti। saiva tribhiruparatasya samayāvacchinnā devabrāhmaṇārthe nānyathā haniṣyāmīti। yathā ca kṣatriyāṇāṁ yuddha eva hiṁsā nānyatreti। ebhirjāti deśakālasamayairanavacchinnā ahiṁsādayaḥ sarvathaiva paripālanīyāḥ। sarvabhūmiṣu sarvaviṣayeṣu sarvathaivāviditavyabhicārāḥ sārvabhaumā mahāvratamityucyante ॥ 31 ॥
body.translated_text: Among these, <s>ahiṁsā</s> limited by birth — the fisherman kills only fish and not otherwise. The same limited by place — 'I shall not kill at a sacred site.' The same limited by time — 'I shall not kill on the fourteenth day of the lunar fortnight, nor on an auspicious day.' The same, when the three limitations are removed, limited by circumstance — 'I shall kill only for the sake of gods and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, not otherwise.' And just as for <s>kṣatriyas</s> (warriors), violence is permitted only in battle and not elsewhere,

body.text:
vivaraṇam
anyadharmāṇāṁ jātideśakālādyavacchedenānuṣṭhānādihāpi tathā prasaṅga iti tatpratiṣedhāyāha- [ete tviti । ete] tvahiṁsādayo mahāvratasaṁjñāḥ saṁnyāsavatāmanuṣṭhānīyāḥ । kīdṛśāste mahāvratanāmāna iti- [jātideśakālasamayānavacchinnāḥ sārvabhaumā mahāvratam ।] mahacca tat vrataṁ ca mahāvratam । mahattvaṁ ca sārvabhaumatvam ॥
kathaṁ punarjātyādyanavacchinnatvameṣāmiti anavacchedapratipādanāya vyatirekeṇa ahiṁsāmudāharati- [tatra ahiṁsā jātyavacchinnā matsyabandhakasya matsyeṣveva nānyatra matsyajāterhiṁsā ।] sā ca matsyajātyavacchinnā matsyabhūmemanaśnuvānā vartata iti asārvabhaumyeva ॥
[saivāhiṁsā deśāvacchinnā] katham? [na tīrthe] prayāgādau [haniṣyāmīti ।] tīrtheṣvahiṁsā ca tīrthādanyaṁ deśaṁ na vyaśnuta iti asārvabhaumī ॥
[saiva ca kālāvacchinnā] yathā – [na caturdaśyāṁ na puṇye'hanīti ।] caturdaśyādikālādanyaṁ kālaṁ na vyaśnuta iti sāpyasārvamaimī ॥
[tribhiḥ] api jātideśakālaiḥ [uparatasya tasyaiva] matsyabandhakasya [samayāvacchinnā] samayaḥ kartavyatāniyamaḥ, katham ? [devabrāhmaṇārthaṁ] haniṣyāmi [nānyatheti] , śrāddhādisamayabhūmimanaśnuvānā vartata iti sā'pi na sārvabhaumī । [yathā ca kṣatriyasya yuddha eva hiṁsā nānyatreti] samayāvacchinnasyaivodāharaṇam ॥
ye punarete yamāḥ [jātideśakālasamayairanavacchinnā ahiṁsādayaḥ, te sarvathaiva paripālanīyāḥ sarvabhūmiṣu] jātyādiṣu [sarvaviṣayeṣu] sarvaprāṇiṣu [sarvathaivāviditavyabhicārāḥ] vinā vyabhicāreṇa, te cetthaṁ viśiṣṭāḥ [sārvabhaumā mahāvratamityucyante ॥ 31 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
Since other virtues are practiced with limitations of birth, place, time, and the like, and there might be a similar presumption here, to preclude that he says — ['But these. These'] — <s>ahiṁsā</s> and the rest, designated as the great vow (<s>mahāvrata</s>), are to be practiced by those who have taken up <s>saṁnyāsa</s> (renunciation). What are these that bear the name 'great vow'? — ['When not limited by birth, place, time, and circumstance, and extending to all, they constitute the great vow.'] It is great and it is a vow, hence the great vow (<s>mahāvrata</s>).

body.text: śaucasaṁtoṣatapaḥsvādhyāyeśvarapraṇidhānāni niyamāḥ ॥ 32 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>Śauca</s> (purity), <s>saṁtoṣa</s> (contentment), <s>tapas</s> (austerity), <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study), and <s>Īśvara-praṇidhāna</s> (devotion to the Lord) are the <s>niyamas</s> (observances). || 32 ||

body.text: tatra śaucaṁ mṛjjalādijanitaṁ medhyābhyavaharaṇādi ca bāhyam। ābhyantaraṁ cittamalānāmākṣālanam। saṁtoṣaḥ saṁnihitasādhanādadhikasyānupāditsā। tapo dvaṁdvasahanam। dvaṁdvāśca jighatsāpipāse śītoṣṇe sthānāsane kāṣṭhamaunākāramaune ca। vratāni caiṣāṁ yathāyogaṁ kṛcchracāndrāyaṇasāṁtapanādīni। svādhyāyo mokṣaśāstrāṇāmadhyayanaṁ praṇavajapo vā। īśvarapraṇidhānaṁ tasminparamagurau sarvakarmārpaṇam। śayyāsanastho'tha pathi vrajanvā svasthaḥ parikṣīṇavitarkajālaḥ। saṁsārabījakṣayamīkṣamāṇaḥ syānnityayukto'mṛtabhogabhāgī ॥ yatredamuktaṁ tataḥ pratyakcetanādhigamo'pyantarāyābhāvaśceti ॥ 32 ॥
body.translated_text: Among these, <s>śauca</s> (purity) is of two kinds: external, produced by earth, water, and the like, and by the consumption of pure food; and internal, the cleansing of the impurities of the mind. <s>Saṁtoṣa</s> (contentment) is the absence of desire to acquire more than the means at hand. <s>Tapas</s> (austerity) is the endurance of the pairs of opposites — the pairs being hunger and thirst, cold and heat, standing and sitting, and the silences of the log and the mute. And the observances of these, as appropriate, include <s>kṛcchra</s>, <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>, <s>sāṁtapana</s>, and the like. <s>Svādhyāya</s> (self-study),

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[śaucasantoṣatapassvādhyāyeśvaraprāṇadhānāni niyamāḥ । tatra śaucaṁ mṛdādijanitam] ādiśabdādudakaṁ ca । [medhyābhyavaharaṇāni ca] dhṛtapayaādīni bhakṣaṇāni । caśabdāt medhyadarśanaśravaṇādīni ca । bāhyametacchaucam ॥
[ābhyantarama] dhunocyate - [cittamalānāṁ] kāmakrodhādīnāṁ tatpratipakṣabhāvanāsalilaiḥ [ākṣālanam ॥]
[santoṣaḥ sanni.āhatasādhanāśvāsāt] sannihitādāśvāsīnamittāt [adhikasādhanānupāditsā] sannihitamātrādatṛptau satyāmapyalaṁpratyayaḥ ॥
[tapo dvandvasahanam । dvandvaśca jighatsāpipāse ।] jighatsā attumicchā । pātumicchā pipāsā । jighatsāpipāsāsahanaṁ tapaḥ । [svarūpeṇaiva [vā] te jighatsāpipāse] alpīyaḥ pānāśananimitte tapaḥ । [śītoṣṇe] apratikriyamāṇe alpapratikriye vā tapaḥ । [sthānāsane 'tiṣṭhadahani rātrāvāsīta'] iti smṛtiprasthānam । [kāṣṭhamaunākāṣṭhamaune ।] kāṣṭhamaunaṁ hastaprayogādirahitam । akāṣṭhamaunaṁ hastādiprayogayuktaṁ sambhāṣaṇādirahitam ॥
[vratāni caiṣāṁ] yogināṁ [yathāyogaṁ] yathāsambhavam । homādiviruddhadharmaviruddhapratiṣedhārthaṁ yathāyogamityāha । kāni tāni? kṛcchrādīni । kṛcchraṁ prājāpatyādi । [tryahaṁ prātaḥ tryahaṁ sāyaṁ tryamadyādayācitam । upoṣaṇaṁ tryaham'] iti । [cāndrāyaṇaṁ] yavamadhyapipīlikāmadhyādi । [‘ekaikaṁ vardhayet grāsam’] ityādismṛtiḥ । [sāntapanam—]
[‘gomūtraṁ gomayaṁ kṣīraṁ dadhi sarpiḥ kuśodakam ।]
[ekarātropavāsaśca kṛcchraḥ sāntapanaḥ smṛtaḥ ॥]
etānyeva dravyāṇi trirabhyastāni mahāsāntapanam । ādigrahaṇaṁ parākādi pratyupādānārtham । [svādhyāyo mokṣaśāstrādhyayanam] upaniṣadādyadhyayanaṁ praṇavajapo vā । [pratyakcetanādhigamo'pyantarāyābhāvaśceti ॥ 32 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['<s>Śauca</s>, <s>saṁtoṣa</s>, <s>tapas</s>, <s>svādhyāya</s>, and <s>Īśvara-praṇidhāna</s> are the <s>niyamas</s>. Among these, <s>śauca</s> is produced by earth and the like'] — the word 'and the like' includes water. ['And by the consumption of pure food'] — eating purified substances such as ghee and milk. By the word 'and,' also pure seeing, hearing, and the like. This is external <s>śauca</s>.
['Internal'] — is now stated: ['the cleansing of the impurities of the mind'] — of desire, anger, and the like, through their counteragents,

body.text: eteṣāṁ yamaniyamānām –
body.translated_text: Of these <s>yamas</s> and <s>niyamas</s> —

body.text: vitarkabādhane pratipakṣabhāvanam ॥ 33 ॥
body.translated_text: When disturbed by perverse thoughts, one should cultivate their opposites (<s>pratipakṣa-bhāvana</s>). || 33 ||

body.text: yadā'sya brāhmaṇasya hiṁsādayo vitarkā jāyeranhaniṣyāmyahamapakāriṇamanṛtamapi vakṣyāmi krayamapyasya svīkariṣyāmi dāreṣu cāsya vyavāyī bhaviṣyāmi parigraheṣu cāsya svāmī bhaviṣyāmīti। evamunmārgapravaṇavitarkajvareṇātidīptena bādhyamānastatpratipakṣānbhāvayet। ghoreṣu saṁsārāṅgāreṣu pacyamānena mayā śaraṇamupāgataḥ sarvabhūtābhayapradānena yogadharmaḥ। sa khalvahaṁ tyaktvā vitarkānpunastānādadānastulyaḥ śvavṛtteneti bhāvayet।
body.translated_text: When perverse thoughts such as violence arise in this <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — 'I shall kill my offender,' 'I shall speak untruth too,' 'I shall appropriate his property,' 'I shall have relations with his wife,' 'I shall become master of his possessions' — when thus tormented by the blazing fever of thoughts inclining toward the wrong path, one should cultivate their opposites: 'Being cooked in the terrible embers of <s>saṁsāra</s>, by me'

body.text:
vivaraṇam
tatra [yamaniyamānāṁ] viruddhāstarkāḥ [vitarkāḥ, taiḥ bādhane] sati [pratipakṣān bhāvayet] abhidhāsyamānena prakāreṇa । apratibhāvyamānā hi vitarkā yoginaṁ । hiṁsādiṣu praṇidhāpayeyuḥ ॥
[yadā asya brāhmaṇasya vitarkā hiṁsādayo jāyeran ।] tatrāhiṁsādivitarkā ye vā hiṁsādayaste vitarkāḥ kīdṛśā iti ? tatrāhiṁsāyā vitarkaḥ hiṁsā [haniṣyāmyapakāriṇamiti ।] tathā satyasya [anṛtaṁ vadiṣyāmīti] viruddhaḥ pratyayo vitarkaḥ । tathaivāsteyasya vitarkaḥ [dravyamasya svīkariṣyāmīti ।] tathā brahmacaryasya vitarkaḥ [dāreṣu cāsya garmiṣyāmīti ।] tathaivāparigrahasya vitarkaḥ [parigraheṣu cāsya svāmī bhaviṣyāmīti ॥]
asyetyetat sarvatra hiṁsādiṣu anugamapratipādanārtham । [dravyamasya svīkariṣyāmīti] paradravyasyātmasaṁbandhakaraṇam । [parigraheṣu cāsya svāmīti] parasaṁbandhiṣveva dravyeṣu svayaṁ svāmīti । yathā kumāranarapatisacivādīnām ॥
[itthamunmārgahāriṇā vitarkajvareṇa dīptena bādhyamānastatpratipakṣān bhāvayet ॥]
kathaṁ bhāvayediti ? [ghoreṣu saṁsārāṅgāreṣu pacyamānena mayā । śaraṇamabhyupagataḥ sarvabhūtābhayapradānena yogadharmaḥ । sa khalvahaṁ tyaktvā vitarkān hiṁsādīn punastānādadānastulyaḥ śvavṛtteneti ।] śuna iva vṛttaṁ yasya saḥ śvavṛttaḥ । śvavadvā vṛttaḥ śvavṛttaḥ । tena tulya iti [bhāvayet ।]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
Therein, the thoughts (<s>tarkāḥ</s>) contrary [to the <s>yamas</s> and <s>niyamas</s>] are [<s>vitarkāḥ</s>; when there is disturbance] by them, [one should cultivate the opposites] in the manner to be described. For <s>vitarkāḥ</s> that are not counteracted would lead the <s>yogin</s> toward <s>hiṁsā</s> (violence) and the like.
[When thoughts of <s>hiṁsā</s> and so forth arise in this <s>brāhmaṇa</s> —] What are the <s>vitarkāḥ</s> pertaining to non-violence and the rest, or rather, what kind of <s>vitarkāḥ</s> are those of <s>hiṁsā</s> and so forth? The <s>vitarka</s> opposing <s>ahiṁsā</s> (non-violence) is <s>hiṁsā</s> — ['I shall kill the wrongdoer.'] Likewise, the <s>vitarka</s> opposing <s>satya</s> (truthfulness) is the contrary thought ['I shall speak falsehood.'] Similarly, the <s>vitarka</s> opposing <s>asteya</s> (non-stealing) is ['I shall appropriate this person's property.'] The <s>vitarka</s> opposing <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) is ['I shall enjoy this person's wives.'] And the <s>vitarka</s> opposing <s>aparigraha</s> (non-possessiveness) is ['I shall become the master of this person's possessions.']
The word 'this person's' (<s>asya</s>) applies throughout with respect to <s>hiṁsā</s> and the rest, for the purpose of illustrating the pattern. ['I shall appropriate this person's property'] means establishing a connection between another's property and oneself. ['I shall be the master of this person's possessions'] means claiming ownership over things belonging to another — as in the case of princes, kings, ministers, and so forth.
['When afflicted by the blazing fever of <s>vitarkāḥ</s> that lead one astray, one should cultivate their opposites.']
How should one cultivate them? ['While being cooked in the terrible embers of <s>saṁsāra</s>, I took refuge in the <s>dharma</s> of <s>yoga</s> through granting fearlessness to all beings. If I now abandon that and take up again the <s>vitarkāḥ</s> of <s>hiṁsā</s> and the rest, I am equal to one who follows the conduct of a dog.'] One whose conduct (<s>vṛtta</s>) is like that of a dog (<s>śvan</s>) is called <s>śva-vṛtta</s>. Or, one who behaves like a dog is <s>śva-vṛtta</s>. Equal to such a one — [one should so contemplate.]

body.text: yathā śvā vāntāvalehī tathā tyaktasya punarādadāna iti mādi sūtrāntareṣvapi yojyam ॥ 33 ॥
body.translated_text: Just as a dog licks up its own vomit, so is the taking up again of what was abandoned — this should be applied to the other <s>sūtras</s> as well. || 33 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[yathā śvā vāntāvalehī tathā tyaktasya punarādānaṁ kurvan] ityupaskāraḥ । tena puruṣeṇa tulyo'hamiti । tathā kathamahaṁ bhaveyaṁ, na yuktametaditi bhāvayet ॥
[ityevamādi sūtrāntare'pi] niyamasūtre'pi [yojyam ।] śaucādīnāṁ pratyekaṁ vitarkī draṣṭavyāḥ śaucaṁ na kariṣyāmītyādayaḥ । bhāṣye tu yamānameva pradarśanam, teṣāmavaśyakartavyatvāt, akaraṇe ca doṣagauravāt, atyādarārtham ॥ 33 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['Just as a dog licks up its own vomit, so one who again takes up what was abandoned'] — this is the explanatory supplement. I am equal to such a person — thus one should contemplate: 'How could I become like that? This is not proper.'
['This and so forth should be applied to the other <s>sūtras</s> as well'] — to the <s>niyama</s> <s>sūtras</s> also [it should be applied.] The <s>vitarkāḥ</s> opposing each of the <s>niyamas</s> such as <s>śauca</s> (purity) should be understood — 'I shall not practice purity,' and so forth. But in the <s>bhāṣya</s>, only the <s>yamas</s> are illustrated, because they are absolutely obligatory and because of the gravity of the fault in not performing them — this is for the sake of emphasizing their importance. || 33 ||

body.text: vitarkā hiṁsādayaḥ kṛtakāritānumoditā lobhakrodhamohapūrvakā mṛdumadhyādhimātrā duḥkhājñānānantaphalā iti pratipakṣabhāvanam ॥ 34 ॥
body.translated_text: The <s>vitarkāḥ</s> — <s>hiṁsā</s> (violence) and the rest — whether done, caused to be done, or approved; preceded by greed, anger, or delusion; mild, moderate, or intense; have as their fruit endless suffering and ignorance — such is the cultivation of the opposite (<s>pratipakṣa-bhāvanam</s>). || 34 ||

body.text: tatra hiṁsā tāvat – kṛtā kāritā'numoditeti tridhā। ekaikā punastridhā lobhena māṁsacarmārthena krodhenāpakṛtamaneneti mohena dharmo me bhaviṣyatīti। lobhakrodhamohāḥ punastrividhā mṛdumadhyādhimātrā iti। evaṁ saptaviṁśatirbhedā bhavanti hiṁsāyāḥ। mṛdumadhyādhimātrāḥ punastridhā - mṛdumṛdurmadhyamṛdustīvramṛduriti। tathā mṛdumadhyo madhyamadhyastīvramadhya iti। tathā mṛdutīvro madhyatīvro'dhimātratīvra iti। evamekāśītibhedā hiṁsā bhavati। sā punarniyamavikalpasamuccayabhedādasaṁkhyeyā, prāṇabhṛdbhedasyāparisaṁkhyeyatvāditi। evamanṛtādiṣvapi yojyam।
body.translated_text: Therein, <s>hiṁsā</s> (violence) first — it is threefold: done, caused to be done, and approved. Each of these is again threefold: through greed — for the sake of flesh, skin, or bone; through anger — because of harm done to oneself; through delusion — thinking 'this will be meritorious for me.' Greed, anger, and delusion are each again threefold: mild, moderate, and intense. Thus there are twenty-seven varieties of <s>hiṁsā</s>.
