The mild, moderate, and intense are each again threefold — mild-mild, moderate-mild, intense-mild; likewise mild-moderate, moderate-moderate, intense-moderate; and mild-intense, moderate-intense, intense-intense. Thus <s>hiṁsā</s> has eighty-one varieties. And through the distinctions of injunction, option, and combination, it becomes innumerable, because the varieties of living beings are uncountable. This should be applied to falsehood and the rest as well.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
vitarkāṇāṁ svarūpaṁ bhedaḥ prabhavahetuḥ phalaṁ ca sūtreṇaiva pradarśyate – [vitarkā hiṁsādaya] iti svarūpam । [kṛtakāritānumoditā iti bhedaḥ । lobhakrodhamohapūrvakā iti] prabhavahetuḥ । [mṛdumadhyādhimātrā iti] mandamadhyottamadoṣatvam । [duḥkhājñānānantaphalā] iti pratipakṣabhāvanam । phalaṁ vā tenaiva vyākhyāyate ॥
[tatra hiṁsaiva] ekā udāhriyate sarveṣāṁ pradarśanāya । sā [kṛtā kāritā anumoditeti trividhā ।] kṛtā svavyāpāreṇa । kāritā prayojyavyāpāreṇa । anumoditā pareṣāṁ vyāpāreṇa manasā anujñātā ॥
[ekaikā punastridhā ।] katham ? [lobhena, māṁsacarmā(sthi)rthī] mṛgaṁ hinasti । [krodhena, apakṛtamaneneti । mohena, dharmo me bhaviṣyatīti ।] evamete nava bhedāḥ । ekai(tvena)sya punastridhā bhedaḥ । katham ? [lobhakrodhamohāḥ punāstridhā] - [mṛdumadhyādhimātrā] iti । [[ekaikaṁ punaḥ] tridhā bhavati - mṛdumṛdurmadhyamṛdustīvramṛduriti । tathā mṛdumadhyo madhyamadhyastīvramadhya iti । tathā mṛdutīvro madhyatīvrastīvratīvra iti । evaṁ ekāśītibhedā hiṁsā bhavati ॥]
sā ca punaḥ ekāśītibhedā'pi satī [niyogāvikalpasamucayabhedāt] asaṅkhyeyā । yathā niyogabhedaḥ kaścinniyuktaḥ sannanyaṁ niyuṅke ; yathā rājñaḥ । sa cāpi niyuktaḥ param, sa cāpi paramiti । te ca sarve niyuktāḥ samuccayena vikalpena vā hiṁsanti । tathā mūlaniyoktāpi niyojyaiḥ saṁhatya vikalpaya ca hiṁsāmanutiṣṭhatīti । vadhyaghātakādi [prāṇibhedasyāsaṅkhyeyatvāditi । evamanṛtādiṣvapi yojyam ।] kṛtakāritānumoditādi yojyam ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
The essential nature, varieties, originating cause, and fruit of the <s>vitarkāḥ</s> are shown by the <s>sūtra</s> itself — ['<s>vitarkāḥ</s> such as <s>hiṁsā</s>'] indicates the essential nature. ['Done, caused to be done, or approved'] indicates the varieties. ['Preceded by greed, anger, or delusion'] indicates the originating cause. ['Mild, moderate, or intense'] indicates the degree of fault — low, medium, or high. ['Having endless suffering and ignorance as their fruit'] is the cultivation of the opposite; or, the fruit is thereby explained.
[Therein, <s>hiṁsā</s> alone] is taken as an example to illustrate all of them. It is [threefold: done, caused to be done, and approved.] 'Done' means through one's own action. 'Caused to be done' means through the action of one who is directed. 'Approved' means mentally sanctioned through the action of others.
[Each of these is again threefold.] How? [Through greed — one who desires flesh, skin, or bone] kills an animal. [Through anger — because of harm done to oneself. Through delusion — thinking 'this will be meritorious for me.'] Thus there are nine varieties. Each of these is again threefold. How? [Greed, anger, and delusion are each again threefold] — [mild, moderate, and intense.] [Each is again] threefold — mild-mild, moderate-mild, intense-mild; likewise mild-moderate, moderate-moderate, intense-moderate; and mild-intense, moderate-intense, intense-intense. Thus <s>hiṁsā</s> has eighty-one varieties.
And though having eighty-one varieties, [through the distinctions of injunction, option, and combination] it becomes innumerable. The distinction of injunction is as follows: someone who is directed then directs another, as in the case of a king; and that one, being directed, directs yet another, and so on. All those who are directed commit <s>hiṁsā</s> in combination and in various options. Likewise, the original director also carries out <s>hiṁsā</s> jointly with those directed and through their various options — as in the case of the condemned and the executioner. [Because the varieties of living beings are uncountable — this should be applied to falsehood and the rest as well.] The classification of done, caused to be done, and approved should be applied. || 34 ||

body.text: te khalvamī vitarkā duḥkhājñānānantaphalā iti pratipakṣabhāvanam। duḥkhamajñānaṁ cānantaṁ phalaṁ yeṣāmiti pratipakṣabhāvanam। tathā ca hiṁsakastāvatprathamaṁ vadhyasya vīryamākṣipati। tataśca śastrādinipātena duḥkhayati। tato jīvitādapi mocayati। tato vīryākṣepādasya cetanācetanamupakaraṇaṁ kṣīṇavīryaṁ bhavati। duḥkhotpādānnarakatiryakpretādiṣu duḥkhamanubhavati, jīvitavyaparopaṇātpratikṣaṇaṁ ca jīvitātyaye vartamāno maraṇamicchannapi duḥkhavipākasya niyatavipākavedanīyatvātkathaṁcidevocchvasiti। yadi ca kathaṁcitpuṇyāvāpagatā hiṁsā bhavettatra sukhaprāptau bhavedalpāyuriti। evamanṛtādiṣvapi yojyaṁ yathāsaṁbhavam। evaṁ vitarkāṇāṁ cāmumevānugataṁ vipākamaniṣṭaṁ bhāvayanna vitarkeṣu manaḥ praṇidadhīta ॥ 34 ॥
body.translated_text: These <s>vitarkāḥ</s> indeed have endless suffering and ignorance as their fruit — such is the cultivation of the opposite. That of which suffering and ignorance are the endless fruit — such is the cultivation of the opposite. Thus, a person committing <s>hiṁsā</s> first seizes the strength of the victim; then causes suffering through the striking of weapons and such; then separates the victim from life itself. From the seizure of strength, the animate and inanimate means belonging to the perpetrator become depleted of strength. From producing suffering, one experiences suffering in the hells, among animals, among the departed, and so forth. From the destruction of life, existing at every moment in mortal danger, even though desiring death, one barely manages to breathe because the suffering-ripening (<s>duḥkha-vipāka</s>) must inevitably be experienced. And if, through some merit, the <s>hiṁsā</s> were slight, then even upon attaining happiness one would have a short lifespan. This should be applied to falsehood and the rest as appropriate. Thus, contemplating this invariable undesirable ripening of the <s>vitarkāḥ</s> that follows them like a shadow, one should not direct the mind toward the <s>vitarkāḥ</s>. || 34 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[te khalvamī vitarkā duḥkhājñānānantaphalāḥ ।] duḥkhaṁ cājñānaṁ ca duḥkhājñāne, te evānantaṁ [phalaṁ yeṣāṁ] te [duḥkhājñānānantaphalāḥ । duḥkhameṣāmanantaṁ phalam । ajñānaṁ caiṣāmanantaṁ phalam ।] tasmādetān vitarkān manasā'pi nopekṣayediti [pratipakṣaṁ bhāvayet ॥]
tatra hiṁsyasya triprakārā pīḍā pratipādyate tadbhedadvāreṇa phalabhedapradarśanārtham । [tathā ca hiṁsako vadhyasya vīryamākṣipati ।] ghātakarūpāvalokanabhatsainādinā trastasya vīryamākṣipya [śastrādinipātanena duḥkhayati । tato jīvitādapi mocayati ।] prāṇebhyo viyojayati ॥
[tasya vīryākṣepādasya] hiṁsituḥ [cetanācetanaṁ] paśukṣetrādikaṁ [upakaraṇaṁ kṣīṇavīryaṁ bhavati ॥]
śastrādinipātana [duḥkhotpādāt] hiṁsāviśeṣāt [narakatiryakpretādiṣu duḥkhamanubhavati ॥]
tathā [jīvitavyaparopaṇāt pratikṣaṇaṁ ca jīvitātyaye vartamāno] janmamaraṇāntare vartmani pratikṣaṇaṁ [maraṇamicchannapi duḥkhavipākasya niyatavedanīyatvāt] avaśyānubhavitavyatvāt [kathaṁcidevocchvāsiti ॥]
[yadi ca kathaṁcitpuṇyāvagamāt prabhūtapuṇyāvāpagatā] alpīyasī [hiṁsā bhavet, tatra] puṇyabhūmnā [sukhaprāptaḥ] sannapi [bhavedalpāyuḥ] āvāpagatahiṁsādoṣeṇa ॥
[itthamanṛtādiṣvapi yathāsaṁbhavaṁ] hiṁsāyāmuktaṁ [yojyam । evaṁ vitarkāṇāṁ] hiṁsādīnāṁ [chāyāmivānugataṁ vipākamaniṣṭaṁ bhāvayet, na vitarkeṣu manaḥ praṇidadhīta ॥ 34 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['These <s>vitarkāḥ</s> indeed have endless suffering and ignorance as their fruit.'] Suffering and ignorance together form a compound (<s>duḥkha-ajñāne</s>); these themselves are the endless [fruit of which] they are [called] 'having endless suffering and ignorance as their fruit.' ['Suffering is their endless fruit. Ignorance too is their endless fruit.'] Therefore one should not disregard these <s>vitarkāḥ</s> even mentally — [one should cultivate the opposite.]
Therein, the threefold affliction of the victim is set forth, for the purpose of showing the variety of fruits through the variety of harm. ['Thus the one committing <s>hiṁsā</s> seizes the victim's strength'] — by terrifying the victim through the appearance of the executioner and such, having seized the strength, ['causes suffering through striking with weapons and the like. Then separates from life itself'] — disconnects from the vital breaths.
['From the seizure of strength, the perpetrator's] animate and inanimate [instruments] — cattle, fields, and such — [become depleted of strength.]
From the particular <s>hiṁsā</s> of [producing suffering through striking with weapons, one experiences suffering in the hells, among animals, among the departed, and so forth.]
Furthermore, ['from the destruction of life, existing at every moment in mortal danger'] — being on the path between birth and death, at every moment ['even though desiring death, because the suffering-ripening must inevitably be experienced,'] because it must be necessarily undergone, ['one barely manages to breathe.']
['And if, through the attainment of some merit, through the abundance of merit,'] the [<s>hiṁsā</s> were] slight, ['then upon attaining happiness'] through the abundance of merit, ['one would have a short lifespan'] due to the fault of the slight <s>hiṁsā</s>.
['Thus this should be applied to falsehood and the rest as appropriate'] — what was said regarding <s>hiṁsā</s> [should be applied. Thus,] contemplating [the undesirable ripening that follows the <s>vitarkāḥ</s>] of <s>hiṁsā</s> and the rest [like a shadow, one should not direct the mind toward the <s>vitarkāḥ</s>.] || 34 ||

body.text: pratipakṣabhāvanāddhetorheyā vitarkā yadā'sya syuraprasavadharmāṇastadā tatkṛtamaiśvaryaṁ yoginaḥ siddhisūcakaṁ bhavati। tadyathā –
body.translated_text: Through the cultivation of the opposite as a cause, when the <s>vitarkāḥ</s> are to be abandoned and become incapable of arising again, then the mastery produced thereby becomes an indicator of the <s>yogin</s>'s <s>siddhi</s> (attainment). That is as follows —

body.text: ahiṁsāpratiṣṭhāyāṁ tatsannidhā vairatyāgaḥ ॥ 35 ॥
body.translated_text: When established in <s>ahiṁsā</s> (non-violence), there is the abandonment of hostility in the presence of that one. || 35 ||

body.text: sarvaprāṇināṁ bhavati ॥ 35 ॥
body.translated_text: Of all living beings. || 35 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[pratipakṣabhāvanāheyā vitarkāḥ yadā ca syuraprasavadharmiṇaḥ] aprasavāśca te dharmiṇaścetya [prasavadharmiṇaḥ ।] yadā yogino manasi notpadyante nikṛtamūlāḥ santaḥ, [tadā tatkṛtaṁ] yamaniyamasthairyekṛtam [aiśvaryaṁ yoginaḥ siddhisūcakam] ahiṁsādiphalasiddhijñāpakaṁ jāyata iti yogasiddhiphalamavasthitameva । anyadapi yogāṅgastutaye aiśvaryamanuṣaṅgajātamucyate । katham ? ekaikasyāpyahiṁsādīnāṁ sthiratvaliṅgamīdṛśaṁ yajñādidharmaphalairapyasamānaṁ pratyakṣata upalabhyate, kimaṅga saṁhatānāṁ yogasiddhikaratvamiti । tadetatpratidarśayati – [tadyathā – ahiṁsāpratiṣṭhāyām] ahiṁsāsthiratve avitarkaprādurbhāve । [tatsannidhau vairatyāgaḥ ।] śāśvatikavidveṣaṇāmapi sarpanakulādīnāṁ tasya ahiṁsakasya sannidhau vairatyāgo bhavati ॥ 35 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['Through the cultivation of the opposite, the <s>vitarkāḥ</s> are to be abandoned; when they become incapable of arising'] — incapable of arising and possessing that quality, hence ['incapable of arising.'] When they do not arise in the <s>yogin</s>'s mind, their roots having been cut — ['then the mastery produced by that'] — produced by the firmness in <s>yamas</s> and <s>niyamas</s> — ['becomes an indicator of the <s>yogin</s>'s <s>siddhi</s>'] — it becomes the sign of the attainment of the fruits of <s>ahiṁsā</s> and the rest, and thus the fruit of <s>yoga</s>-attainment is firmly established. Moreover, additional mastery that arises incidentally is mentioned in praise of the <s>yoga</s> limbs. How? The sign of firmness in each of the <s>ahiṁsā</s> and the rest is of such a nature that it is perceived directly as unequalled even by the fruits of <s>dharma</s> such as sacrifice and the like — how much more so their collective power to bring about <s>yoga</s>-attainment! This is illustrated — ['That is as follows — when established in <s>ahiṁsā</s>'] — when there is firmness in <s>ahiṁsā</s>, when <s>vitarkāḥ</s> no longer arise. ['In that one's presence, there is the abandonment of hostility.'] Even among those with perpetual enmity, such as serpents and mongooses, in the presence of that practitioner of <s>ahiṁsā</s>, hostility is abandoned. || 35 ||

body.text: satyapratiṣṭhāyāṁ kriyāphalāśrayatvam ॥ 36 ॥
body.translated_text: When established in <s>satya</s> (truthfulness), actions and their fruits become dependent on that one's speech. || 36 ||

body.text: dhārmiko bhūyā iti bhavati dhārmikaḥ, svargaṁ prāpnuhīti svargaṁ prāpnoti। amoghā'sya vāgbhavati ॥ 36 ॥
body.translated_text: 'May you become righteous' — and one becomes righteous. 'May you attain heaven' — and one attains heaven. That one's speech becomes infallible. || 36 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[satyapratiṣṭhāyāṁ] satyasthairye [kriyāphalāśrayatvaṁ] yajñādikriyāphalānāmāgamanaṁ prāptirbhavati । satyavādivākyāditi śeṣaḥ । katham ? adhārmiko'pi [dhārmiko bhūyā] ityukte tadvacanā [ddhārmiko bhavati ।] yathā [dharme'sya ramatāṁ mana] iti devairuktaḥ kuṇḍadhārārādhī brāhmaṇo dhārmiko babhūva । tathā [svargaṁ prāpnuhī] tyuktaḥ [svargaṁ prāpnoti ।] yathā viśvāmitreṇoktaḥ svargaṁ prāpnuhīti triśaṅkuḥ svargaṁ prāpa । kiṁ bahunā । [amoghā'sya vāk bhavati ॥ 36 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['When established in <s>satya</s>'] — when there is firmness in truthfulness — ['actions and their fruits become dependent on that one's speech'] — the fruits of actions such as sacrifice and the like come to depend on the speech of the truth-speaker. This is the completion of the meaning. How? Even one who is unrighteous, ['when told "may you become righteous,"'] through the power of that one's words ['becomes righteous.'] Just as a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who was a worshipper of the fire-pit's edge, when told by the gods ['may your mind delight in <s>dharma</s>,'] became righteous. Likewise, ['when told "may you attain heaven,"'] one ['attains heaven.'] Just as <s>Triśaṅku</s>, told by <s>Viśvāmitra</s> 'may you attain heaven,' attained heaven. In short — ['that one's speech becomes infallible.'] || 36 ||

body.text: asteyapratiṣṭhāyāṁ sarvaratnopasthānam ॥ 37 ॥
body.translated_text: When established in <s>asteya</s> (non-stealing), all jewels present themselves. || 37 ||

body.text: sarvadiksthānyasyopatiṣṭhanti ratnāni ॥ 37 ॥
body.translated_text: Jewels from all directions approach that one. || 37 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[asteyapratiṣṭhāyāṁ] aspṛhāyām । tataḥ kimasya bhavati ? [ratnopasthānaṁ] bhavati [sarvadiksthānyasyopatiṣṭhante ratnāni ātmānaṁ] darśayanti ॥ 37 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['When established in <s>asteya</s>'] — when there is freedom from craving. Then what happens? ['Jewels present themselves'] — ['jewels from all directions approach that one,'] revealing themselves. || 37 ||

body.text: brahmacaryapratiṣṭhāyāṁ vīryalābhaḥ ॥ 38 ॥
body.translated_text: When established in <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy), vigor is obtained. || 38 ||

body.text: yasya lābhādapratighānguṇānutkarṣayati। siddhaśca vineyeṣu jñānamādhātuṁ samartho bhavatīti ॥ 38 ॥
body.translated_text: Through that attainment, one brings forth unobstructed qualities; and having attained <s>siddhi</s> (perfection), one becomes capable of imparting knowledge to disciples. || 38 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[brahmacaryapratiṣṭhāyāṁ vīryalābhaḥ । brahmacaryalābhādapratighān guṇānutkarṣayati ।] apratibandhānātmana upapādayati । sarvaśubhārthapravṛttiṣvapratibaddhavīryo bhavati । na kenacit pratighātena vivadhyata ityarthaḥ ॥
kiñca – [vinayeṣu] śiṣyeṣu yogyeṣu vā sādhuṣu [jñānamādhātuṁ samartho bhavati] yathā bhagavān vyāsaḥ saṁ( [jñaye] )jajñe ॥ 38 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['When established in <s>brahmacarya</s>, vigor is obtained. Through the attainment of <s>brahmacarya</s>, one brings forth unobstructed qualities'] — one produces them in oneself without impediment. One becomes of unobstructed vigor in all endeavors toward auspicious ends. One is not weakened by any obstruction — this is the meaning.
Furthermore — ['one becomes capable of imparting knowledge to worthy disciples'] or to those who are virtuous — just as the blessed <s>Vyāsa</s> produced knowledge [in <s>Sañjaya</s>]. || 38 ||

body.text: aparigrahasthairye janmakathaṁtāsaṁbodhaḥ ॥ 39 ॥
body.translated_text: When there is steadiness in <s>aparigraha</s> (non-possessiveness), there arises the understanding of the how and wherefore of births. || 39 ||

body.text: asya bhavati। ko'hamāsaṁ kathamahamāsaṁ kiṁsvididaṁ kathaṁ svidadaṁ ke vā bhaviṣyāmaḥ kathaṁ vā bhaviṣyāma ityevamasya pūrvāntaparāntamadhyeṣvātmabhāvajijñāsā svarūpeṇopāvartate। etā yamasthairye siddhayaḥ ॥ 39 ॥
body.translated_text: This arises in the <s>yogin</s>: 'Who was I? How was I? What indeed is this? How indeed is this? Who shall we become? How shall we become?' — thus, regarding the prior limit, the posterior limit, and the middle, the inquiry into one's own existence presents itself in its true form. These are the <s>siddhis</s> (attainments) from steadiness in the <s>yamas</s>. || 39 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[aparigrahasthairye janmakathantāsambodhaḥ ।] janmanaḥ kathaṁbhāvabodho'sya [bhavati ।]
[kiṁsvididaṁ] (sama)mama janmanaḥ kiṁ satattvam, [kathaṁ sthididaṁ] kena prakāreṇa svit, [kiṁ bhaviṣyāmaḥ] prāṇo [prāyaṇo]ttarakālaṁ kiṁ vā na bhaviṣyāmaḥ, bhaviṣyanto vā [ke bhaviṣyāmaḥ, kathaṁ bhaviṣyāmaḥ, ityevam asya pūrvāparāntamadhyeṣu] bhūtabhaviṣyadvartamāneṣu [ātmajijñāsā] samyagdarśanasya pūrvarūpaṁ [svarūpeṇopāvartate ।] bāhyaparigrahāsaṅgābhāvāt svātmaviṣayālocanamayatvena pravartate । nānyeṣāṁ parigrahasantāpavitānitatṛṣāṁ yatnenāpi jāyate ॥ 39 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['When there is steadiness in <s>aparigraha</s>, there arises the understanding of the how and wherefore of births.'] The understanding of the how and why of birth [arises in the <s>yogin</s>.]
['What indeed is this'] — what is the real nature of my birth? ['How indeed is this'] — by what manner? ['What shall we become'] — after the time of death, what shall we become or shall we not become? And if we shall become, ['who shall we become? How shall we become?'] — ['thus, regarding the prior limit, the posterior limit, and the middle'] — regarding the past, future, and present — ['the inquiry into the self'] — which is a preliminary form of right vision — ['presents itself in its true form.'] Due to the absence of attachment to external possessions, it operates in the form of self-directed contemplation. It does not arise, even with effort, in others who are scorched by the fever of craving for possessions. || 39 ||

body.text: niyameṣu vakṣyāmaḥ –
body.translated_text: Among the <s>niyamas</s>, we shall now explain —

body.text: śaucātsvāṅgajugupsā parairasaṁsargaḥ ॥ 40 ॥
body.translated_text: From <s>śauca</s> (purity), there arises disgust toward one's own body and non-contact with others. || 40 ||

body.text: svāṅge jugupsāyāṁ śaucamārabhamāṇaḥ kāyāvadyadarśī kāyānabhiṣvaṅgī yatirbhavati। kiṁ ca parairasaṁsargaḥ kāyasvabhāvāvalokī svamapi kāyaṁ jihāsurmṛjjalādibhirākṣālayannapi kāyaśuddhimapaśyankathaṁ parakāyairatyantamevāprayataiḥ saṁsṛjyeta ॥ 40 ॥
body.translated_text: Through disgust with one's own body, one who undertakes <s>śauca</s> (purity), seeing the faults of the body, becomes a renunciant (<s>yati</s>) who is unattached to the body. Moreover, non-contact with others [follows]: observing the nature of one's own body, wishing to discard even one's own body, and though washing it with earth, water, etc., not seeing any purity of the body—how then could one come into contact with the bodies of others, which are utterly impure?

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[yameṣu siddhaya uktāḥ । idānīṁ niyameṣu vakṣyāmaḥ – śaucāt svāṅgajugupsā parairasaṁsargaḥ । svāṅgajugupsayā śaucamārabhamāṇaḥ kāyāvadyadarśī] śarīragarhyatvadarśī [kāyānabhiṣvaṅgī yatirbhavati । kiñca – parairasaṁsargo] bhavati । [kāyasvabhāvāvalokī svamapi kāyaṁ jihāsurmṛjjalādibhirākṣālayannapi kāyaśuddhimapaśyan kathaṁ parakāyairatyantamevāprayataiḥ saṁsṛjyata iti ॥ 40 ॥]
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇa (Elucidation):
[The accomplishments in the <s>yamas</s> (restraints) have been stated. Now we shall state those in the <s>niyamas</s> (observances): From <s>śauca</s> (purity) arise disgust with one's own body and non-contact with others. Through disgust with one's own body, one who undertakes purity, seeing the faults of the body]—seeing the contemptible nature of the body—[becomes a renunciant unattached to the body. Moreover, non-contact with others] arises. [Observing the nature of one's own body, wishing to discard even one's own body, though washing it with earth, water, etc., and not seeing any purity of the body—how could one come into contact with the bodies of others, which are utterly impure?]

body.text: kiṁ ca –
body.translated_text: Moreover—

body.text: sattvaśuddhisaumanasyai​kāgryendriyajayātma​darśanayogyatvāni ca ॥ 41 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>sattvaśuddhisaumanasyaikāgryendriyajayātmadarśanayogyatvāni ca</s> — And [from <s>śauca</s> arise] purity of <s>sattva</s>, cheerfulness, one-pointedness, mastery over the senses, and fitness for the vision of the Self. (Sūtra 2.41)

body.text: bhavantīti vākyaśeṣaḥ। śuceḥ sattvaśuddhistataḥ saumanasyaṁ tata aikāgryaṁ tata indriyajayastataścā''tmadarśanayogyatvaṁ buddhisattvasya bhavatītyetacchaucasthairyādadhigamyata iti ॥ 41 ॥
body.translated_text: 'Arise'—this is the completion of the sentence. From purity, purity of <s>sattva</s>; from that, cheerfulness; from that, one-pointedness; from that, mastery over the senses; and from that, fitness for the vision of the Self—of the <s>sattva</s> of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect)—this is understood from the steadiness of <s>śauca</s>.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[kiṁ cā] nyadbhavati । [sattvaśuddhisaumanasyaikāgryendriyajayātmadarśanayogyatvāni cāsya bhavanti ।] pūrvasya pūrvasya sthairyāduttarasyāvirbhāvaḥ । katham ? [śuceḥ] sattvaśuddhiḥ । [tataḥ saumanasyam, tata aikāgryam, tataścendriyajayaḥ, tataścātmadarśanayogyatvaṁ buddhisattvasya bhavatī] tyataḥ [śaucasthairyādādhigamyata etat] sarvam । tataśceyaṁ śaucasiddhireva ॥ 41 ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇa (Elucidation):
[Moreover,] something else arises. [Purity of <s>sattva</s>, cheerfulness, one-pointedness, mastery over the senses, and fitness for the vision of the Self arise for him.] Through the steadiness of each preceding [quality], the subsequent one manifests. How? [From purity,] purity of <s>sattva</s>. [From that, cheerfulness; from that, one-pointedness; from that, mastery over the senses; and from that, fitness for the vision of the Self of <s>buddhi</s>'s <s>sattva</s> arises.] Therefore, [from the steadiness of <s>śauca</s>, all] this [is attained.] And this is indeed the accomplishment of <s>śauca</s>.

body.text: saṁtoṣādanuttamaḥ sukhalābhaḥ ॥ 42 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>saṃtoṣād anuttamaḥ sukhalābhaḥ</s> — From <s>saṃtoṣa</s> (contentment), unsurpassed happiness is gained. (Sūtra 2.42)

body.text: tathā coktam – yacca kāmasukhaṁ loke yacca divyaṁ mahatsukham। tṛṣṇākṣayasukhasyaite nārhataḥ ṣoḍaśīṁ kalām ॥ iti ॥ 42 ॥
body.translated_text: And thus it has been said: 'Whatever happiness of desire exists in the world, and whatever great celestial happiness—these do not amount to one-sixteenth of the happiness of the destruction of craving.'

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[santoṣādanuttamaḥ sukhalābhaḥ ।] santoṣavitarkānutpattau [anuttamaḥ] na vidyate'smādanya uttamaḥ ।
[tathā coktam – ''yacca kāmasukhaṁ loke,] yaccaihikam । [yacca divyaṁ mahatsukham ।] devādisambandhi । [tṛṣṇākṣayasukhasyaite nārhataḥ ṣoḍaśīṁ kalām'' ॥ 42 ॥]
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇa (Elucidation):
[From <s>saṃtoṣa</s> (contentment), unsurpassed happiness is gained.] When the counter-thoughts to contentment do not arise, [unsurpassed] means: there exists no other happiness superior to it.
[And thus it has been said: 'Whatever happiness of desire exists in the world']—that is, in this life. ['And whatever great celestial happiness']—that pertaining to the gods and such. ['These do not amount to one-sixteenth of the happiness of the destruction of craving.']

body.text: kāyendriyasiddhiraśuddhikṣayāttapasaḥ ॥ 43 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>kāyendriyasiddhir aśuddhikṣayāt tapasaḥ</s> — From <s>tapas</s> (austerity), with the destruction of impurity, perfection of the body and senses [arises]. (Sūtra 2.43)

body.text: nirvartyamānameva tapo hinastyaśuddhyāvaraṇamalaṁ tadāvaraṇamalāpagamātkāyasiddhiraṇimādyā। tathendriyasiddhirdūrācchravaṇadarśanādyeti ॥ 43 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>Tapas</s>, even while being performed, destroys the covering of impurity. From the removal of that covering of impurity, bodily perfection—such as <s>aṇimā</s> (becoming minute) and the like—[arises].

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[kāyendriyasiddhiraśuddhikṣayāttapasaḥ । nirvartyamānameva tapo hinastyaśuddhyāvaraṇam] kimaṅga nirvartitamityabhi(mānaḥ)prāyaḥ ॥
[tadāvaraṇamalāpagamāt kāyasiddhiraṇimādyā ।] mātāpitrādisaṁbandhajaṁ kāyamalaṁ baijaṁ gārbhaṁ cāhārādijaṁ ca sarvaṁ tapasā nighātayiṣyate । tataścāṇimādikāyasiddhiḥ ॥
tathā viṣayādisamparkajamindriyāṇāmadharmādyāvaraṇaṁ malaṁ tapassnotasvinīsrotasā kṣālyate । [tathā indriyasiddhirdūrācchravaṇādyā ॥ 43 ॥]
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇa (Elucidation):
[From <s>tapas</s>, with the destruction of impurity, perfection of the body and senses arises. <s>Tapas</s>, even while being performed, destroys the covering of impurity]—how much more so when it is completed!—such is the intended meaning.
[From the removal of that covering of impurity, bodily perfection such as <s>aṇimā</s> (becoming minute) and the like arises.] The impurity of the body—born of the connection with parents, seminal, gestational, and arising from food etc.—all of it is destroyed by <s>tapas</s>. And from that, bodily perfection such as <s>aṇimā</s> etc.
Likewise, the impurity of the senses—the covering of <s>adharma</s> (demerit) etc. arising from contact with sense-objects—is washed away by the flowing stream of <s>tapas</s>. [Likewise, perfection of the senses—such as hearing from afar and the like—arises.]

body.text: svādhyāyādiṣṭadevatāsaṁprayogaḥ ॥ 44 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>svādhyāyād iṣṭadevatāsaṃprayogaḥ</s> — From <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study), union with the desired deity [arises]. (Sūtra 2.44)

body.text: devā ṛṣayaḥ siddhāśca svādhyāyaśīlasya darśanaṁ gacchanti,kārye cāsya vartanta iti ॥ 44 ॥
body.translated_text: Gods, sages, and perfected beings come into the vision of one devoted to <s>svādhyāya</s>, and they assist in his undertakings.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[svādhyāyādiṣṭadevatāsamprayogaḥ । devāḥ ṛṣayaḥ siddhāśca ya iṣṭāste svādhyāyaśīlasya darśanaṁ gacchanti kāryeṣu cāsya upadeśādiṣu vartante ॥ 44 ॥]
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇa (Elucidation):
[From <s>svādhyāya</s>, union with the desired deity arises. The gods, sages, and perfected beings]—whichever are desired by him, those are his desired deities. [They come into vision] of one devoted to <s>svādhyāya</s>, [and they assist in his undertakings.]

body.text: samādhisidvirīśvarapraṇidhānāt ॥ 45 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>samādhisiddhir Īśvarapraṇidhānāt</s> — From devotion to <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), the perfection of <s>samādhi</s> [arises]. (Sūtra 2.45)

body.text: īśvarārpitasarvabhāvasya samādhisiddhiryayā sarvamīpsitamavitathaṁ jānāti deśāntare dehāntare kālāntare ca। tato'sya prajñā yathābhūtaṁ prajānātīti ॥ 45 ॥
body.translated_text: For one who has offered all his states of being to <s>Īśvara</s>, the perfection of <s>samādhi</s> [arises]—by which he knows everything desired without error, [perceives things in] distant places and times, [and attains] subtle [perception].

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[samādhisiddhirīśvarapraṇidhānāt । īśvarārpitasarvabhāvasya samādhiḥ sidhyati । yayā] samādhisiddhyā [sarvamīpsitamavitathaṁ jānāti । tathā deśāntare kālāntare cāsya prajñā yathābhūtaṁ jānāti ॥ 45 ॥]
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇa (Elucidation):
[From devotion to <s>Īśvara</s>, the perfection of <s>samādhi</s> arises. For one who has offered all his states of being to <s>Īśvara</s>, <s>samādhi</s> is perfected.] [By which one knows everything desired without error] etc.—the fruit of <s>samādhi</s> attained through <s>Īśvarapraṇidhāna</s> (devotion to the Lord) is stated.

body.text: uktāḥ saha siddhibhiryamaniyamāḥ। āsanādīni vakṣyāmaḥ। tatra –
body.translated_text: The <s>yamas</s> (restraints) and <s>niyamas</s> (observances) have been stated together with their accomplishments. Now we shall describe <s>āsana</s> (posture) and the rest. In this regard—

body.text: sthirasukhamāsanam ॥ 46 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>sthirasukham āsanam</s> — <s>Āsana</s> (posture) is that which is steady and comfortable. (Sūtra 2.46)

body.text: tadyathā padmāsanaṁ bhadrāsanaṁ svastikaṁ daṇḍāsanaṁ sopāśrayaṁ paryaṅkaṁ krauñcaniṣadanaṁ hastiniṣadanamuṣṭraniṣadanaṁ samasaṁsthānaṁ sthirasukhaṁ yathāsukhaṁ cetyevamādīni ॥ 46 ॥
body.translated_text: Such as <s>padmāsana</s> (lotus posture), <s>bhadrāsana</s> (gracious posture), <s>svastika</s> (auspicious posture), <s>daṇḍāsana</s> (staff posture), <s>sopāśraya</s> (supported posture), <s>paryaṅka</s> (couch posture), <s>krauñcaniṣadana</s> (heron-sitting), <s>hastiniṣadana</s> (elephant-sitting), <s>uṣṭraniṣadana</s> (camel-sitting), <s>samasaṃsthita</s> (evenly-established), <s>sthiraprasrabdhi</s> (steady-and-relaxed), <s>yathāsukha</s> (as-comfortable), and the like.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[uktāḥ saha siddhibhiryamānayamāḥ ।] idānīṁ [āsanādīni vakṣyāmaḥ] - [tatra sthirasukhamāsanam ।] sthiraṁ sukhaṁ cāsanam । yasminnāsane, sthitasya manogātrāṇāmupajāyate sthiratvam, duḥkhaṁ ca yena na bhavati tadabhyasyet । [tadyathā] – śāstrāntaraprasiddhāni nāmāni [padmāsanādīni] pradarśyante ॥
tatra śucau devanilayagiriguhānadīpulinādau jvalanasalilāsamīpe jantuvivarjite nira(ṅga)śmake śuciḥ samyagācamya, parameśvaramakhilabhuvanaikanāthaṁ abhivandyāṁśca yogeśvarānātmagurūśca praṇipatya, cailājinakuśottaramaduḥkhakaraṁ prāṅmukha udaṅmukho vā viṣṭaramadhiṣṭhāya, anyatamadeṣāmāsanaṁ nirbadhnīyāt ॥
tatra padmāsanaṁ nāma – savyaṁ pādamupasaṁhṛtya dakṣiṇopari nidadhīta । tathaiva dakṣiṇaṁ savyasyopariṣṭāt । kaṭyurogrīvaṁ ca viṣṭabhya, mṛ(ga)tasuptavannāsikāgranihitadṛṣṭiḥ, samudgakavadapihitoṣṭhasampuṭaḥ, dantairdantāgramaparāmṛśan , muṣṭimātrāntaraviprakṛṣṭācibukorassthalaḥ, rājaddantāntaranihitarasanāgraḥ, hastau pārṣṇyorupari kacchapakaṁ brahmāñjaliṁ vā kṛtvā, sakṛdāsthāpitetthaṁsaṁsthāna:, punaḥ punaḥ śarīrāvayavaśarīravinyāsaviśeṣaparityaktaprayatnaḥ san yenāsīta, tat [padmāsanam ॥]
etacca sarvamanyeṣāmāsanānāmapi tulyam । kaścideva viśeṣaḥ ॥
tathā dakṣiṇaṁ pādaṁ savyasyopari kṛtvā, hastaṁ ca dakṣiṇaṁ savyahastasyopari nidhāya, yenāste, tat [bhadrāsanam] । anyat samānam ॥
tathā kuñcitānyatarapādamavanivinyastāparajānukaṁ [vīrāsanam ।] ucyamāna eva viśeṣaḥ sarvatra ॥
dakṣiṇaṁ pādāṅguṣṭhaṁ savyenorujaṅghena parigṛhyādṛśyaṁ kṛtvā, tathā savyaṁ pādāṅguṣṭhaṁ dakṣiṇenorujaṅghenādṛśyaṁ parigṛhya, yathā ca pārṣiṇibhyāṁ vṛṣaṇayorapīḍanaṁ tathā yenāste, tat [svastikamāsanam ॥]
samagulphau samāṅguṣṭhau prasārayan samajānū pādau daṇḍavadyenopaviśet, tat [daṇḍāsanam ॥]
(na)yogapaṭṭasaṁ[sthaṁ]stambhādyāśrayaṁ vā [sopāśrayam ॥]
ājānuprasāritabāhuśayanaṁ [paryaṅkāsanam ॥]
[krauñcaniṣadanaṁ hastiniṣadanaṁ uṣṭraniṣadanaṁ ca] kauñcādiniṣadanasaṁsthānasādṛśyādeva draṣṭavyam ॥
bhūmau nyastorujaṅghaṁ [samasaṁsthitam ॥]
[sthitaprasrabdhiḥ ।] anyenāpi prakāreṇa svayamutprekṣya [sthitaprasrabdhiḥ ।] anāyāse yena bhavati tadapyāsanaṁ sthita [prasrabdhi] rnāma ॥
[yathāsukhaṁ ca] - yena rūpeṇāsīnasya sukhaṁ bhavati tat [yathāsukham ।] ādiśabdādanyadapi yathācāryopadiṣṭamāsanaṁ draṣṭavyam ॥ 46 ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇa (Elucidation):
[The <s>yamas</s> and <s>niyamas</s> have been stated together with their accomplishments.] Now [we shall describe <s>āsana</s> and the rest]— [In this regard, <s>āsana</s> is that which is steady and comfortable.] Steady and comfortable is the <s>āsana</s>. That posture in which, when one is established, steadiness of mind and limbs arises, and by which no suffering occurs—that one should practice. ['Such as']—the names well-known in other treatises, [<s>padmāsana</s> etc.], are displayed.
In a clean place—a temple of the gods, a mountain cave, a sandbank of a river, etc.—not near fire or water, free from insects, not stony, clean—having properly sipped water, having bowed to <s>Parameśvara</s> (the supreme Lord), the sole master of all worlds, and having prostrated before the masters of <s>yoga</s> and one's own <s>gurus</s>—upon a seat consisting of cloth, deerskin, and <s>kuśa</s> grass spread one upon another, not causing discomfort, facing east or north—one should assume one of these postures.
Of these, <s>padmāsana</s> (lotus posture) is: drawing in the left foot, place it upon the right [thigh]; likewise the right upon the left. Keeping the waist, neck, and [head] erect, with gaze fixed on the tip of the nose like a sleeping deer, with the lips closed like a casket, with the teeth not touching the tips of the teeth, with the chest separated from the chin by the distance of a fist, with the tip of the tongue placed between the shining rows of teeth, having formed either the tortoise-mudrā or the <s>brahmāñjali</s> (gesture of Brahmā) with the hands upon the heels—having once established the body in this arrangement, then repeatedly practicing without effort regarding the particular placement of the bodily parts—thus one should sit. That is <s>padmāsana</s>.
And all this is common to the other postures as well. Only a specific difference [distinguishes each].
Likewise, placing the right foot upon the left and the right hand upon the left hand, and thus sitting—that is <s>bhadrāsana</s> (gracious posture). The rest is the same.
Likewise, with one foot bent and the other knee placed on the ground—that is <s>vīrāsana</s> (hero posture). Only the specific difference being described [varies] in each case.
Grasping the right big toe with the left thigh and calf so as to conceal it, and likewise grasping the left big toe with the right thigh and calf so as to conceal it, and sitting so that the heels do not press upon the testicles—that is <s>svastikāsana</s> (auspicious posture).
Extending both ankles, both big toes, and both knees evenly, and sitting with the feet like a staff—that is <s>daṇḍāsana</s> (staff posture).
[Supported posture (<s>sopāśraya</s>)] is [sitting] supported by a yoga-strap or a pillar etc.
[Couch posture (<s>paryaṅkāsana</s>)] is reclining with arms extended to the knees.
[Heron-sitting, elephant-sitting, and camel-sitting] are to be understood from their resemblance to the sitting postures of the heron etc.
[Evenly-established (<s>samasaṃsthita</s>)] is with thighs and calves placed upon the ground.
[Steady-and-relaxed (<s>sthiraprasrabdhi</s>)]—or by any other manner, devised by oneself, [that is steady and relaxed]—whatever posture affords ease, that too is a posture called 'steady-and-relaxed.'
[And as-comfortable (<s>yathāsukha</s>)]—whatever form of sitting produces comfort, that is '<s>yathāsukha</s>.' The word 'and the like' indicates that other postures as instructed by one's teacher should also be considered.

body.text: prayatnaśaithilyānantasamāpattibhyām ॥ 47 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>prayatnaśaithilyānantasamāpattibhyām</s> — [<s>Āsana</s> is perfected] by relaxation of effort and by absorption in the infinite. (Sūtra 2.47)

body.text: bhavatīti vākyaśeṣaḥ। prayatnoparamātsidhyatyāsanaṁ yena nāṅgamejayo bhavati। anante vā samāpannaṁ cittamāsanaṁ nirvartayatīti ॥ 47 ॥
body.translated_text: 'Is perfected'—this is the completion of the sentence. By the cessation of effort, <s>āsana</s> is perfected—by which there is no trembling of the limbs. Or by absorption in the infinite (<s>ananta</s>) the mind accomplishes the <s>āsana</s>, making it firm.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
tadāsanajayābhyupāya idānīmupapādyata – [prayatnaśaiśilyānantyasamāpattibhyām । bhavatīti vākyaśeṣaḥ ।] āsanaṁ dṛḍhaniṣpannaṁ bhavatītyupaskāraḥ । [prayatnoparamādā] sanabandhottarakālaṁ prayatnākaraṇādvā sidhyati । [yena nāṅgamejayo bhavati । yena] prayatnoparameṇa । prayatnena hyaṅgaṁ kampayati । yena acalitāsano bhavatītyarthaḥ । [anantye vā samāpannam ।] anantaṁ viśvam , anantabhāva anantyam , tasmin samāpannaṁ, vyāpya viśvabhāvaṁ sthitaṁ [cittamāsanaṁ nirvartayati] draḍhayati ॥ 47 ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇa (Elucidation):
The means for mastery of <s>āsana</s> is now set forth— [By relaxation of effort and by absorption in the infinite. 'Is perfected'—this is the completion of the sentence.] The supplement is: <s>āsana</s> becomes firmly accomplished. [By the cessation of effort]—after the initial time of assuming the posture, by not making effort—or it is perfected [by not making effort]. [By which there is no trembling of the limbs. By which]—by this relaxation of effort. For through effort one makes the limbs tremble. The meaning is: by which one becomes motionless in the posture. [Or by absorption in the infinite.] The infinite (<s>ananta</s>) is the universe; the state of being infinite is infinity; having become absorbed in that—pervading, established in the state of the universe—[the mind accomplishes the <s>āsana</s>], makes it firm.

body.text: tato dvandvānabhighātaḥ ॥ 48 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>tato dvandvānabhighātaḥ</s> — From that [mastery of <s>āsana</s>], non-affliction by the pairs of opposites [arises]. (Sūtra 2.48)

body.text: śītoṣṇādibhirdvaṁdvairāsanajayānnābhibhūyate ॥ 48 ॥
body.translated_text: One is not overcome by the pairs of opposites (<s>dvandvas</s>) such as cold and heat etc., through mastery of <s>āsana</s>.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tato dvandvānabhighātaḥ । tataḥ] āsanasthirībhāvāt । idaṁ dṛṣṭamānuṣāṅgikam । yat [śītoṣṇādibhirdvandvairnābhibhūyeta ॥ 48 ॥]
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇa (Elucidation):
[From that, non-affliction by the pairs of opposites. 'From that']—from the steadiness of <s>āsana</s>. This is a visible, human accomplishment. Through the settled establishment of the posture, the pairs of opposites such as cold and heat etc. do not agitate [the <s>yogin</s>].

body.text: tasminsati śvāsapraśvāsayorgativicchedaḥ prāṇāyāmaḥ ॥ 49 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>tasmin sati śvāsapraśvāsayor gativiccheda prāṇāyāmaḥ</s> — When that [<s>āsana</s>] has been [mastered], <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control) is the cessation of the movement of inhalation and exhalation. (Sūtra 2.49)

body.text: satyāsanajaye bāhyasya vāyorācamanaṁ śvāsaḥ, kauṣṭhyasya vāyorniḥsāraṇaṁ praśvāsaḥ, tayorgativiccheda ubhayābhāvaḥ prāṇāyāmaḥ ॥ 49 ॥
body.translated_text: When mastery of <s>āsana</s> has been achieved, inhalation (<s>śvāsa</s>) is the drawing in of external air; exhalation (<s>praśvāsa</s>) is the expulsion of the abdominal air. The cessation of the movement of both is <s>prāṇāyāma</s>—that is, the absence of both.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[kiñca] – prāṇāyāmādiyogyatā ca bhavati । katham ? tasmin sati [śvāsapraśvāsayorgativicchedaḥ prāṇāyamaḥ । satyāsane dṛḍhe bāhyasya vāyorācamanaṁ śvāsaḥ ।] yathā santatatvādudakaṁ nālenākṛṣyate, tathā santatatvāt nāsikāpuṭanālābhyāmapānavāyusaṁbandho bahirvāyurākṛṣyate, tadākarṣaṇaṁ śvāsaḥ । tathā [kauṣṭhyavāyorniścāraṇam ।] prāṇavṛttisambandhī hi kauṣṭhyo vāyuḥ । tasya bahirnissāraṇaṁ [praśvāsaḥ । tayorgativicchedaḥ ।] kimuktaṁ bhavatyata āha - [ubhayābhāvaḥ prāṇāyāma iti ॥ 49 ॥]
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇa (Elucidation):
[Moreover]—fitness for <s>prāṇāyāma</s> etc. also arises [from mastery of <s>āsana</s>]. How? When that [<s>āsana</s>] has been [mastered]: [<s>Prāṇāyāma</s> is the cessation of the movement of inhalation and exhalation. When the <s>āsana</s> is firm, inhalation is the drawing in of external air.] Just as water is drawn up through a tube due to its continuity, so too, due to continuity, the external air connected with the <s>apāna</s> (downward) breath is drawn in through the nostrils' tubes—that drawing in is inhalation (<s>śvāsa</s>). Likewise, [the expulsion of abdominal air]—for the abdominal air is connected with the function of <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath). Its expulsion outward [is exhalation]. [The cessation of the movement of both]—what is being said? To this he says: [The absence of both is <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.]

body.text: sa tu –
body.translated_text: That, however—

body.text: bāhyābhyantarastambhavṛttirdeśakālasaṁkhyābhiḥ paridṛṣṭo dīrghasūkṣmaḥ ॥ 50 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>bāhyābhyantarastambhavṛttir deśakālasaṃkhyābhiḥ paridṛṣṭo dīrghasūkṣmaḥ</s> — [<s>Prāṇāyāma</s>], having external, internal, and suspended modes, regulated by place, time, and number, becomes long and subtle. (Sūtra 2.50)

body.text: yatra praśvāsapūrvako gatyabhāvaḥ sa bāhyaḥ। yatra śvāsapūrvako gatyabhāvaḥ sa ābhyantaraḥ। tṛtīyaḥ stambhavṛttiryatrobhayābhāvaḥ sakṛtprayatnādbhavati। yathā tapte nyastamupale jalaṁ sarvataḥ saṁkocamāpadyate tathā dvayoryugapadgatyabhāva iti। trayo'pyete deśena paridṛṣṭā iyānasya viṣayo deśa iti। kālena paridṛṣṭāḥ kṣaṇānāmiyattāvadhāraṇenāvacchinnā ityarthaḥ। saṁkhyābhiḥ paridṛṣṭā etāvadbhiḥ śvāsapraśvāsaiḥ prathama uddhātastadvannigṛhītasyaitāvadbhirdvitīya uddhāta evaṁ tṛtīyaḥ। evaṁ mṛdurevaṁ madhya evaṁ tīvra iti saṁkhyāparidṛṣṭaḥ। sa khalvayamevamabhyasto dīrghasūkṣmaḥ ॥ 50 ॥
body.translated_text: Where the absence of movement is preceded by exhalation—that is the external [mode]. Where the absence of movement is preceded by inhalation—that is the internal [mode]. The third is the suspended mode, where both are absent, arising from a single effort. Just as water placed on a heated stone contracts in all directions, so too there is simultaneous absence of movement of both. All three are regulated by place—'this is the extent of its domain' in terms of place. Regulated by time—delimited by the determination of the measure of moments—that is the meaning. Regulated by number—with this many inhalations and exhalations, the first stage; with this many when restrained, the second stage; likewise the third. Thus mild, thus moderate, thus intense—regulated by number. This [<s>prāṇāyāma</s>], thus practiced, becomes long and subtle.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[sa tu] trividhaḥ [bāhyābhyantarastambhavṛttirdeśakālasaṁkhyābhiḥ paridṛṣṭo dīrghasūkṣmaḥ ।] sa bāhyavṛttirabhyantaravṛttiḥ stambhavṛttiśca । [yatra śvāsapūrvako gatyabhāvaḥ sa bāhyavṛttiḥ ।] bāhyasya vāyorantaḥ praveśanaṁ prati vṛttiḥ yasya sa bāhyavṛttiḥ । tasmāt sa [bāhyaḥ ।] bāhyamanye pūraka ityācakṣate ॥
[yatra praśvāsapūrvako gatyabhāvaḥ sa ābhyantaravṛttiḥ ।] ābhyantarasya vāyorbahirnissāraṇaṁ prati vṛttiryasya sa abhyantaravṛttiḥ । [tasmāt sa ābhyantaraḥ ।] taṁ recaka ityācakṣate ॥
[tṛtīyastu stambhavṛttiḥ । tatrobhayābhāvaḥ] ācamananiścāraṇayorabhāvaḥ sa tu [sakṛtprayatnāt prabhavati । yathā tapte nyastaṁ upale jalaṁ sarvataḥ saṁkocamāpadyate, tathā] sakṛtprayatnāt prāṇadivṛttayaḥ saṁkocamupayāntītyāha - [dvayoryugapat gatyabhāva iti ॥]
[trayo'pyate deśena paridṛṣṭhāḥ iyānasya deśa iti ।] yathā bahirvṛtterantarācamyamānasya nāsikāgraprabhṛtyapādāṅguṣṭhaṁ deśavyāptiḥ । evamantarvṛtterbahirniścāryamāṇasya vāyoḥ pādāṅguṣṭhaprabhṛtyanāsikāgraṁ deśavyāptiḥ । stambhavṛtterāmastakāpādatalavyāptiḥ । athavā bahirapi vitastyādikrameṇa deśavyāptirastyeva ॥
[kālena paridṛṣṭāḥ, kṣaṇānāmiyattāvadhāraṇena] iyantaḥ kṣaṇāḥ prāṇāyāmenātivāhitā iti ॥
[tathā saṅkhyābhiḥ paridṛṣṭāḥ, etāvadbhiḥ śvāsapraśvāsaiḥ] atītaiḥ paridṛṣṭaḥ [prathama udghātaḥ ।] yathā nirodhakṣubhitānāṁ vāyūnāṁ sakṛt mūrdhānamuddhatya nivṛttiḥ prathama uddhātaḥ । [sa eva mṛduḥ ॥]
punaśca sakṛduddhata [nigṛhītasya vāyoḥ tāvadbhiḥ] praśvāsairatītaiḥ paridṛṣṭo [dvitīya uddhātaḥ] prāṇāyāmo [madhyama] ityucyate ॥
tathā [tṛtīyaḥ,] etāvadbhiḥ śvāsapraśvāsaiḥ paridṛṣṭaḥ [tṛtīya udghātaḥ ।] sa eva ca triruddhātaḥ [tīvra] iti ॥
[sa khalvayamevaṁ] deśakālasaṅkhyāparidṛṣṭo'bhyasto dīrghakālavyāpī bhavati bhūmijayāt । tathā carṣīṇāmanekavarṣavyāpī śrūyate । tataśva [dīrghaḥ ॥]
tathā vāyūnāṁ dīrghatvamandatvāpatteḥ [sūkṣmaṁ] ca bhavati ॥ 50 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
[That <s>prāṇāyāma</s>] is of three kinds: [having external, internal, and suspension as its operations, it is observed by place, time, and number, and becomes long and subtle.] It has external operation, internal operation, and suspension operation. [Where there is cessation of movement preceded by inhalation, that is the external operation.] The operation of the external air toward entering inward — that whose operation is thus is the external operation. Therefore it [is external.] Others call it <s>pūraka</s> (filling).
[Where there is cessation of movement preceded by exhalation, that is the internal operation.] The operation of the internal air toward expulsion outward — that whose operation is thus is the internal operation. [Therefore it is internal.] They call it <s>recaka</s> (emptying).
[The third, however, is the suspension operation. In that, there is absence of both] — absence of drawing in and expelling — and it [arises from a single effort. Just as water placed on a heated stone contracts from all sides, so] from a single effort the activities of <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest undergo contraction — thus he says: [cessation of movement of both simultaneously.]
[All three are observed by place — 'such is the extent of its place.'] For example, in the case of the external operation, when the air is being drawn inward, the spatial extent ranges from the tip of the nose down to the toes. Similarly, for the internal operation, when the air is being expelled outward, the spatial extent ranges from the toes up to the tip of the nose. For the suspension operation, the extent covers from the crown of the head to the soles of the feet. Alternatively, externally too there is spatial extent measured progressively by spans and so forth.
[Observed by time, through determining the measure of moments] — 'this many moments have been passed through in <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.'
[Likewise observed by number — 'by this many inhalations and exhalations'] having passed, it is observed as [the first <s>udghāta</s> (impulse).] Just as when the breath-energies disturbed by restraint rise to the crown once and then subside — that is the first <s>udghāta</s>. [That itself is mild.]
And again, when the air once raised [and restrained, observed by that many] exhalations having passed, [the second <s>udghāta</s>] — the <s>prāṇāyāma</s> [is called medium.]
Likewise [the third] — observed by this many inhalations and exhalations, [is the third <s>udghāta</s>.] And that same threefold <s>udghāta</s> [is intense.]
[This very <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, thus] observed by place, time, and number, when practiced, becomes long in duration through mastery of stages. And indeed, for the <s>ṛṣis</s> (seers) it is heard to span many years. Hence it is [long.]
Likewise, due to the breath becoming gentle and subtle, it [becomes subtle] as well. (YS 2.50)

body.text: bāhyābhyantaraviṣayākṣepī caturthaḥ ॥ 51 ॥
body.translated_text: The fourth <s>prāṇāyāma</s> transcends the spheres of external and internal operations. (YS 2.51)

body.text: deśakālasaṁkhyābhirbāhyaviṣayaparidṛṣṭa ākṣiptaḥ। tathā''bhyantaraviṣayaparidṛṣṭa ākṣiptaḥ। ubhayathā dīrghasūkṣmaḥ। tatpūrvako bhūmijayātkrameṇobhayorgatyabhāvaścaturthaḥ prāṇāyāmaḥ। tṛtīyastu viṣayānālocito gatyabhāvaḥ sakṛdārabdha eva deśakālasaṁkhyābhiḥ paridṛṣṭo dīrghasūkṣmaḥ। caturthastu śvāsapraśvāsayorviṣayāvadhāraṇātkrameṇa bhūmijayādubhayākṣepapūrvako gatyabhāvaścaturthaḥ prāṇāyāma ityayaṁ viśeṣa iti ॥ 51 ॥
body.translated_text: That which is observed by place, time, and number in the sphere of external operation is transcended. Likewise, that which is observed in the sphere of internal operation is transcended. In both ways it becomes long and subtle. Preceded by that, through progressive mastery of both stages, the cessation of movement of both is the fourth <s>prāṇāyāma</s>. The third, however, is cessation of movement without reference to those spheres, commenced all at once and observed by place, time, and number, becoming long and subtle. But the fourth, through determination of the spheres of inhalation and exhalation, progressively through mastery of the stages of those operations, preceded by the transcending of both — that cessation of movement is the fourth <s>prāṇāyāma</s>. This is the distinction. (YS 2.51)

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[bāhyābhyantaraviṣayākṣepī caturthaḥ] – bāhyasya viṣayāḥ pādāṅguṣṭhādayaḥ । bāhyo hi vāyurācamyamāno'ntardeśān vyāpnoti, ākṣipati । ābhyantarasya viṣayā bhūmyādayaḥ । sa ca bahirniścāryamāṇe bhūmyādīn deśakālasaṅkhyāparidṛṣṭān vyāpnoti, ākṣipati । [sa bāhyābhyantaraviṣayākṣepī caturthaḥ] prāṇāyāmaḥ ॥
[deśakālasaṅkhyābhirbāhyavastuviṣayaḥ paridṛṣṭa ākṣipto] vyāptaḥ । [tathā ābhyantaraviṣayaḥ paridṛṣṭo] deśakālasaṅkhyābhiḥ ākṣipto vyāptaḥ । [ubhayathā dīrghasūkṣmaḥ ।] bāhyābhyantaraviṣayākṣepeṇobhayathā dīrghasūkṣmatvāpannaḥ ॥
kimuktaṁ bhavatītyāha - [tatpūrvakaḥ] ubhayaviṣayākṣepapūrvakaḥ । [bhūmijayāt] ubhayavṛttivāyubhūmijaya [krameṇobhayoḥ] prāṇāpānavṛttyorbāhyābhyantarayoḥ gatyabhāvaścaturtheḥ ॥
tṛtīyacaturthayorubhayavṛttisāmānyādaviśeṣatvamāśaṅkyāha – [tṛtīyastadviṣayānālocitaḥ sakṛdārabdha eva] gatyabhāvo [deśakālasaṅkhyābhiḥ paridṛṣṭo dīrghasūkṣmaḥ । caturthastu śvāsapraśvāsayoḥ] ātamitoḥ [viṣayāvadhāraṇāt krameṇa vā yadvṛttibhūmijayakrameṇobhayākṣepapūrvako gatyabhāvaścaturthaḥ prāṇāyāma ityayaṁ viśeṣaḥ tṛtīyacaturthayoḥ ॥ 51 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
[The fourth transcends the spheres of external and internal operations] — the spheres of the external are the toes and so forth. For the external air, when being drawn inward, pervades and reaches the internal regions. The spheres of the internal are the earth and so forth. And that, when being expelled outward, pervades and reaches the earth and other regions observed by place, time, and number. [That which transcends the spheres of external and internal operations is the fourth] <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.
[Observed by place, time, and number, the external sphere is transcended] — pervaded. [Likewise the internal sphere is observed] by place, time, and number — transcended, pervaded. [In both ways it becomes long and subtle.] Through the transcending of the spheres of external and internal operations, in both ways it attains length and subtlety.
What is being said? He states: [preceded by that] — preceded by the transcending of both spheres. [Through mastery of the stages] of the breath-energies of both operations, [progressively, of both] the <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> activities, external and internal, the cessation of movement is the fourth.
Anticipating the objection of no distinction between the third and fourth due to the commonality of both having cessation of operation, he says: [The third is cessation of movement without reference to those spheres, commenced all at once,] observed [by place, time, and number, becoming long and subtle. But the fourth, through determination of the spheres of inhalation and exhalation,] which are measured, [progressively, or through mastery of stages of those operations, preceded by the transcending of both — that cessation of movement is the fourth <s>prāṇāyāma</s>. This is the distinction between the third and fourth.] (YS 2.51)

body.text: tataḥ kṣīyate prakāśāvaraṇam ॥ 52 ॥
body.translated_text: From that, the covering of light is destroyed. (YS 2.52)

body.text: prāṇāyāmānabhyasyato'sya yoginaḥ kṣīyate vivekajñānāvaraṇīyaṁ karma। yattadācakṣate – mahāmohamayenendrajālena prakāśaśīlaṁ sattvamāvṛtya tadevākārye niyuṅkta iti। tadasya prakāśāvaraṇaṁ karma saṁsāranibandhanaṁ prāṇāyāmābhyāsāddurbalaṁ bhavati pratikṣaṇaṁ ca kṣīyate। tathā coktam – “tapo na paraṁ prāṇāyāmāttato viśuddhirmalānāṁ dīptiśca jñānasya” iti ॥ 52 ॥
body.translated_text: For this <s>yogin</s> who practices <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, the <s>karma</s> that covers discriminative knowledge is destroyed. As they declare: 'By the great delusion-laden magical illusion, having covered <s>sattva</s> whose nature is luminosity, that very same illusion engages it in improper action.' That <s>karma</s> which covers his light, which binds him to <s>saṁsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth), becomes weakened through the practice of <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, and is destroyed moment by moment. And thus it has been said: 'There is no <s>tapas</s> (austerity) higher than <s>prāṇāyāma</s>; from it comes purification of impurities and the radiance of knowledge.' (YS 2.52)

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tataḥ kṣīyate prakāśāvaraṇam ।] prakāśa āvriyate yena tat prakāśāvaraṇaṁ karma । [prāṇāyāmānabhyasyato yogino] vivekajñānamāvriyate yena tat [vivekajñānāvaraṇīyaṁ karma । yattu ācakṣate] śāstrāntare [‘mahāmohamayenendrajālena prakāśaśīlaṁ satvamāvṛtya tadevākārye viniyuṅkte”] iti ॥
yadāvriyate viparyayajñānamahendrajālena tadeva satvamāvaraṇakarmaṇā sarvākārye viniyujyate । [tat prāṇāyāmābhyāsādasya prakāśāvaraṇaṁ karma saṁsāranibandhanaṁ durbalaṁ bhavati ।] na kevalaṁ durbalabhāva eva, [pratikṣaṇaṁ ca kṣīyate ॥]
tathā coktam – [‘na paraṁ prāṇāyāmāttapaḥ’] iti । tasmāt [tataḥ prāṇāyāmāt] rajastamaḥkāryāṇāṁ [viśuddhirmalānāṁ, dīptiśca jñānasyeti ॥ 52 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
[From that, the covering of light is destroyed.] The <s>karma</s> by which light is covered — that is the covering of light. [For the <s>yogin</s> who practices <s>prāṇāyāma</s>,] the <s>karma</s> [that covers discriminative knowledge — as they declare] in other scriptures: ['By the great delusion-laden magical illusion, having covered <s>sattva</s> whose nature is luminosity, that very same illusion engages it in improper action.']
That which is covered by the great magical illusion of erroneous knowledge — that very <s>sattva</s> is engaged in all improper action by the covering <s>karma</s>. [Through the practice of <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, this <s>karma</s> that covers his light and binds him to <s>saṁsāra</s> becomes weakened.] Not only does it become weak, [but it is destroyed moment by moment.]
And thus it has been said: ['There is no <s>tapas</s> higher than <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.'] Therefore [from that <s>prāṇāyāma</s>] comes [purification of impurities] that are the effects of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, [and the radiance of knowledge.] (YS 2.52)

body.text: kiṁ ca –
body.translated_text: Moreover —

body.text: dhāraṇāsu ca yogyatā manasaḥ ॥ 53 ॥
body.translated_text: And fitness of the mind for <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration). (YS 2.53)

body.text: prāṇāyāmābhyāsādeva। pracchardanavidhāraṇābhyāṁ vā prāṇasya iti vacanāt ॥ 53 ॥
body.translated_text: From the practice of <s>prāṇāyāma</s> alone. As stated in the scripture: 'Or by exhalation and retention of <s>prāṇa</s>.' (YS 2.53)

body.text:
vivaraṇam
kiṁ ca – bhavatyanyadapi prāṇāyāmābhyāsāt । [dhāraṇāsu] vakṣyamāṇāsu [yogyatā manasaḥ prāṇāyāmādeva । 'pracchardanavidhāraṇābhyāṁ vā prāṇasya’ iti vacanāt] tābhyāṁ hi manasaḥ sthitisampattiruktā ॥ 53 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
Moreover — there is yet another result from the practice of <s>prāṇāyāma</s>. [Fitness of the mind for <s>dhāraṇā</s>] — the <s>dhāraṇās</s> that will be described — [comes from <s>prāṇāyāma</s> alone. As stated: 'Or by exhalation and retention of <s>prāṇa</s>'] — for by these two, stability and excellence of the mind have been declared. (YS 2.53)

body.text: atha kaḥ pratyāhāraḥ –
body.translated_text: Now, what is <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal of the senses)?

body.text: svaviṣayāsaṁprayoge citasvarūpānukāra ivendriyāṇāṁ pratyāhāraḥ ॥ 54 ॥
body.translated_text: When there is non-contact with their respective objects, the senses follow, as it were, the nature of the mind — this is <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal). (YS 2.54)

body.text: svaviṣayasaṁprayogābhāve cittasvarūpānukāra iveti, cittanirodhe cittavanniruddhānīndriyāṇi netarendriyajayavadupāyāntaramapekṣante। yathā madhukararājaṁ makṣikā utpatantamanūtpatanti niviśamānamanu niviśante tathendriyāṇi cittanirodhe nītyeṣa pratyāhāraḥ ॥ 54 ॥
body.translated_text: In the absence of contact with their respective objects, the senses follow the nature of the mind, as it were — meaning that when the mind is restrained, the senses are restrained like the mind and do not require any separate means as in other forms of sense-mastery. Just as when the queen bee flies up, the bees fly up after her, and when she settles down, they settle down after her — so too the senses, when the mind is restrained — this is <s>pratyāhāra</s>. (YS 2.54)

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[atha kaḥ pratyāhāraḥ ?] pratyāhāraviśeṣamabhidhitsamānaḥ praśnenopakramate । svaviṣayādindriyāṇāṁ pratyāharaṇamātraṁ pareṣāṁ pratyāhāraḥ । atra punarviśeṣavānucyate [svaviṣayāsamprayoge cittasya svarūpānukāra ivendriyāṇāṁ pratyāhāra iti ॥]
[svaiḥ svaiśśabdādibhirviṣayaiḥ] indriyāṇāṁ śrotrādīnāṁ [saṁyogābhāve] viṣayadoṣadarśanāt dhyāyināṁ svaviṣayāt nivartitānāṁ [cittasvarūpānukārateva ।] yoginaścittaṁ yadākāratāṁ bhajata tat cittasvarūpānukārateveti ॥
etaduktaṁ bhavati – [cittanirodhe cittavanniruddhāni nopāyāntaramapekṣante] jayārtham । cittanirodhādeva tāni nirudhyante । [yathā madhukararājānam] śrutyakṣarametat । madhukararājāmityarthaḥ । [makṣikā utpatantamanūtpatanti, niviśamānamanu niviśante । tathaivendriyāṇi cittanirodhe niruddhānītyeṣa pratyāhāraḥ ॥ 54 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
[Now, what is <s>pratyāhāra</s>?] Wishing to describe the specific nature of <s>pratyāhāra</s>, he begins with a question. For others, <s>pratyāhāra</s> is merely the withdrawal of the senses from their respective objects. But here a distinctive definition is given: [When there is non-contact with their respective objects, the senses follow, as it were, the nature of the mind — this is <s>pratyāhāra</s>.]
[In the absence of contact] of the senses — hearing and the rest — [with their respective objects] such as sound and so forth, [due to seeing the defects in sense objects,] for the meditators whose senses have been turned away from their objects, [there is, as it were, conformity to the nature of the mind.] Whatever form the <s>yogin</s>'s mind assumes, the senses conform to that very form, as it were.
What has been said amounts to this: [When the mind is restrained, the senses are restrained like the mind and do not require any separate means] for their mastery. They are restrained simply through the restraint of the mind. [Just as the queen bee] — this is a Vedic expression, meaning the king of bees — [when the bees fly up after her as she flies up, and settle down after her as she settles down — so too the senses are restrained when the mind is restrained. This is <s>pratyāhāra</s>.] (YS 2.54)

body.text: tataḥ paramā vaśyatendriyāṇām ॥ 55 ॥
body.translated_text: From that comes supreme mastery over the senses. (YS 2.55)

body.text: śabdādiṣvavyasanamindriyajaya iti kecit। saktirvyasanaṁ vyasyatyenaṁ śreyasa iti। aviruddhā pratipattirnyāyyā। śabdādisaṁprayogaḥ svecchayetyanye। rāgadveṣābhāve sukhaduḥkhaśūnyaṁ śabdādijñānamindriyajaya iti kecit। cittaikāgryādapratipattireveti jaigīṣavyaḥ। tataśca paramā tviyaṁ vaśyatā yaccittanirodhe niruddhānīndriyāṇi netarendriyajayavatprayatnakṛtamupāyāntaramapekṣante yogina iti ॥ 55 ॥
body.translated_text: Some say sense-mastery is freedom from craving toward sounds and other objects. Craving is attachment — it leads one astray from the good. A consistent understanding is appropriate. Some say it is contact with sounds and other objects at one's own will. Others say sense-mastery is knowledge of sounds and other objects devoid of pleasure and pain, in the absence of attraction and aversion. <s>Jaigīṣavya</s> holds that through one-pointedness of mind, there is simply non-apprehension of sense objects. And this is the supreme mastery — that when the mind is restrained, the senses are restrained and do not require any other effort-based means as in other forms of sense-mastery for the <s>yogin</s>. (YS 2.55)

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tataḥ] pratyāhārasthairyāt [paramā vaśyatendriyāṇāṁ] bhavati । [iti] śabdaḥ samāpyarthaḥ । yāsāṁ ca vaśyatānāṁ madhye pratyāhārasthairthāt paramā vaśyatā jāyate tā ucyante - [śabdādiṣvindriyajayaḥ avyasanaṁ] punaḥ punarapravṛttiranāsaktirveti [kecidāhuḥ ।] vyasanamiti nirbravīti – [saktirvyasanam ।] katham ? [vyasyati] kṣipati [enaṁ] pratipattāraṁ [śreyasaḥ] sakāśāditi vyasanam ॥
[aviruddhā pratipattirvā ।] viruddhānāṁ vā śabdādīnāmapratipattirvaśyateti । tasyaiva vyākhyānaṁ – [nyāyyaḥ] śāstrānujñātaḥ [śabdādiṣu saṁyogaḥ svecchayā ।] teṣvaviruddheṣu yadīcchati pravartate na vā itye [vamanye manvate ॥]
[rāgadveṣābhāve sukhaduḥkhaśūnyaṁ] heyopādeyatvavarjitaṁ [śabdādijñānaṁ] vaśyatetyeke । madhyamāyāṁ tu rāgadveṣasadbhāvamātramapi na vāryata iti viśeṣaḥ ॥
svābhipretā ākhyāyate – [aikāgryāt] cittaikāgratvānuvidhānādindriyāṇāṁ [apratipattireva] śabdādīnāmiti [jaigīṣavyo manyate ॥]
[paramā tviyaṁ] sarvāsāmuktānāmiyaṁ paramā [vaśyatendriyāṇāṁ, yat] yasmin [cittaniruddhānīndriyāṇi na itarendriyajayavat] pūrvoktāsvindriyavaśyatāsu [upāyāntaramapekṣante] jayārthaṁ, asyāṁ [punarna prayatnakṛtamupāyāntaramapekṣante yoginaḥ ॥ 55 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
[From that] — from steadiness in <s>pratyāhāra</s> — [comes supreme mastery over the senses.] The word 'thus' (<s>iti</s>) indicates conclusion. Among the various types of mastery over the senses, the supreme mastery that arises from steadiness in <s>pratyāhāra</s> is now described:
[Some say] sense-mastery is [non-craving] — non-recurrence again and again, non-attachment — [toward sounds and other objects.] He explains 'craving' (<s>vyasana</s>): [Attachment is craving.] How? [It casts] the practitioner [away from the good] — hence it is called <s>vyasana</s>.
[Or, consistent understanding] — that is, non-apprehension of conflicting sense objects is mastery. As an explanation of that: contact with sounds and other objects that is [proper] — sanctioned by scripture — [at one's own will.] Whether one engages with those non-conflicting objects or not — [this is what others hold.]
[In the absence of attraction and aversion, knowledge of sounds and other objects] devoid of what is to be rejected or grasped, [empty of pleasure and pain] — this is mastery, say some. In the intermediate type, however, even the mere presence of attraction and aversion is not prevented — that is the distinction.
The preferred view is stated: [Through one-pointedness] — through conformity of the senses to the one-pointedness of the mind — [there is simply non-apprehension] of sounds and other objects — thus [<s>Jaigīṣavya</s> holds.]
[But this is the supreme] — among all the types mentioned, this is the supreme [mastery over the senses, in which] when [the mind is restrained, the senses are restrained and do not, as in other forms of sense-mastery] mentioned previously, [require any separate means] for mastery; in this type, [however, the <s>yogins</s> do not require any effort-based separate means.] (YS 2.55)

body.text: vibhūtipādaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Vibhūti Pāda</s> (Chapter on Supernatural Powers)

body.text: uktāni pañca bahiraṅgāni sādhanāni। dhāraṇāvaktavyā –
body.translated_text: The five external limbs of practice have been described. Now <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) is to be explained —

body.text: deśabandhaścittasya dhāraṇā ॥ 1 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>Dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) is the binding of the mind to a place. (YS 3.1)

body.text: nābhicakre hṛdayapuṇḍarīke mūrdhni jyotiṣi nāsikāgre jihvāgra ityevamādiṣu deśeṣu bāhye vā viṣaye cittasya vṛttimātreṇa bandha iti dhāraṇā ॥ 1 ॥
body.translated_text: On the navel center, on the lotus of the heart, on the light in the crown of the head, on the tip of the nose, on the tip of the tongue — in such places, or on an external object, the binding of the mind through mere mental activity — this is <s>dhāraṇā</s>. (YS 3.1)

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[uktāni pañca bahiraṅgāni sādhanāni] samprajñātasya yogasya । adhunā antaraṅgaṁ dhāraṇādhyānasamādhisamākhyaṁ sādhanatrayaṁ tasyaivābhidhīyate । bahiraṅgāntaraṅgatvabhedādeva hi bahiraṅgasādhanavyākhyānenaiva pādaḥ parisamāpitaḥ । saṁhatyakāritvācca sādhanatrayasya pṛthagvacanam । bahiraṅgasādhanābhidhānānantaraparyupasthāpitāntaraṅgasādhanapratipādanena pādasambandho vyākhyātaḥ । asmiṁśca pāde vibhūtayaḥ prādhānyena pradarśyanta iti ca pṛthak(ktvādā)pādārambhaḥ । etadeva hi samākhyālābhe kāraṇamavādiṣma ॥
[dhāraṇā vaktavyā ।] pratyāhārānantaraṁ kramopanītasānnidhānā dhāraṇā abhidhānīyā । [deśabandhacittasya dhāraṇā ।] deśabandhanaṁ [deśabandhaḥ ।] kasya ? [cittasya ॥]
svayameva ca sarvaṁ vyācaṣṭe – [nābhicakre] nābhipradeśaścakramiva । sarve (vāyava)avayavāstatra cakrībhūtā iti nābhicakram । [hṛdayaṁ puṇḍarīkākāram । mūrdhajyotiṣi ।] mūrdhanāḍīdvāraṁ prabhāsvaratvājyotirityākhyāyate । [nāsikāgre jihvāgre ityevamādiṣu deśeṣu bāhyeṣu ca viṣayeṣu] candrādityādiṣu cittaṁ badhyate ॥
tasya [cittasya] ityevamadiṣvapracalitarūpeṇa yā [vṛttiḥ] sādhāraṇetyucyate । [vṛttimātreṇeti ।] taddeśapratyayamātreṇa vikṣepaśūnyatayā vartata iti ॥ 1 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
[The five external limbs of practice have been described] — of <s>samprajñāta yoga</s> (cognitive meditation). Now the three internal limbs of practice — designated as <s>dhāraṇā</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, and <s>samādhi</s> — of that very yoga are explained. It is precisely because of the distinction between external and internal limbs that the chapter was concluded with the exposition of the external limbs. And because the three internal limbs function collectively, they are stated separately. The connection of this chapter is explained by the presentation of the internal limbs, which follows immediately after the exposition of the external limbs. Moreover, because in this chapter the <s>vibhūtis</s> (supernatural powers) are principally demonstrated, a separate chapter is begun. This indeed is the reason for the chapter title, as we have stated.
[<s>Dhāraṇā</s> is to be explained.] <s>Dhāraṇā</s>, which is brought near in sequence after <s>pratyāhāra</s>, is to be described. [<s>Dhāraṇā</s> is the binding of the mind to a place.] Binding to a place [is <s>deśabandha</s> (place-binding).] Of what? [Of the mind.]
He himself explains everything: [On the navel center] — the navel region is like a wheel; all the constituents are arranged there in a wheel-like formation, hence it is called the 'navel-wheel.' [The heart is in the shape of a lotus. On the light in the crown of the head] — the opening of the channel at the crown, being luminous, is called 'light.' [On the tip of the nose, on the tip of the tongue — in such internal places, and on external objects] such as the moon, sun, and so forth, the mind is bound.
Of that [mind] — the [mental activity] that remains in such places without wavering is called ordinary. [Through mere mental activity] — through mere cognition directed at that place, functioning free from distraction — this is <s>dhāraṇā</s>. (YS 3.1)

body.text: tatra pratyayaikatānatā dhyānam ॥ 2 ॥
body.translated_text: In that place, the uninterrupted flow of cognition is <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). (YS 3.2)

body.text: tasmindeśe dhyeyālambanasya pratyayasyaikatānatā sadṛśaḥ pravāhaḥ prattyayāntareṇāparāmṛṣṭo dhyānam ॥ 2 ॥
body.translated_text: In that place, the continuity of cognition directed toward the object of meditation — a flow of similar [cognitions] uninterrupted by any other cognition — is <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). || 2 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tatra pratyayaikatānatā dhyānam । tasmin deśe] dhāraṇāvṛttiviṣaye nābhicakrādau । [dhyeyālambanasya] dhyeyo deśādiḥ, tadālambanasya । [pratyayasya [ekatānatā] sadṛśapravāhaḥ,] tulyapratyayānāṁ pravāha ekākāraḥ pratyayasantānaḥ [pratyayāntareṇa] vijātīyena [aparāmṛṣṭaḥ] anvakīrṇaḥ । tat [dhyānam ॥]
dhāraṇā tu tasminneva dhyeye tadavasthasyaiva cittasya tadviṣayavikalpitaiḥ pratyayāntaraiḥ parāmṛṣṭā'pi । yathā sūrye dhāryamāṇasya tadgataparimaṇḍalatīvrataradīdhititvādipratyayeṣvapi dhāraṇaiva । vṛttimātreṇa tatraiva vartamānatvāccittasya । dhyānaṁ punaḥ na tu tathā । bhinnajātīyapratyayāntarāparāmṛṣṭaikapratyayapravāha eva hi dhyānam ॥ 2 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['Therein, continuity of cognition is meditation. In that place'] — in the locus of the <s>dhāraṇā</s> activity, such as the navel center (<s>nābhi-cakra</s>) and so forth. ['Of the object of meditation (<s>dhyeya</s>)'] — the <s>dhyeya</s> is the place and so forth; 'of that which has that as its support.' ['The continuity of cognition'] means a flow of similar [cognitions] — a stream of cognitions of uniform character composed of identical cognitions — ['uninterrupted by'] any heterogeneous ['other cognition'] — unmixed [with dissimilar cognitions]. That is ['meditation.']
<s>Dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), however, even when directed at that same object of meditation, even in the same state of mind, may be interrupted by other cognitions that involve conceptual elaboration (<s>vikalpa</s>) regarding that object. For instance, when one concentrates on the sun, even though cognitions of its roundness, intense radiance, and so forth arise, it remains merely <s>dhāraṇā</s> — because the mind continues to operate in that domain through mere cognitive activity alone. <s>Dhyāna</s> (meditation), however, is not like that. <s>Dhyāna</s> is indeed a flow of uniform cognition uninterrupted by any cognition of a different class. || 2 ||

body.text: tadevārthamātranirbhāsaṁ svarūpaśūnyamiva samādhiḥ ॥ 3 ॥
body.translated_text: That very [meditation], when it shines forth as the object alone, as if empty of its own form, is <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption). || 3 ||

body.text: dhyānameva dhyeyākāranirbhāsaṁ pratyayātmakena svarūpeṇa śūnyamiva yadā bhavati dhyeyasvabhāvāveśāttadā samādhirityucyate ॥ 3 ॥
body.translated_text: When that very meditation shines forth in the form of the object of meditation (<s>dhyeya</s>), as if empty of its own nature as cognition (<s>pratyaya</s>), due to complete absorption into the essential nature of the object of meditation — then it is called <s>samādhi</s>. || 3 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tadevāthaimātranirbhāsaṁ svarūpaśūnyamiva samādhiḥ । tadeva dhyānaṁ] tulyapratyaya pravāharūpaṁ svāmekapratyayasantānatāmiva hitvā [dhyeyākāranirbhāsaṁ] dhyeyākāravadavabhāsate । [pratyayātmakena] svena grahaṇātmanā [svarūpeṇa śūnyamiva ।] yathā sphaṭikadravyamupadhānāvabhāsaṁ svarūpaśūnyamiva । [yadā bhavati dhyeyasvabhāvāveśāt] kāraṇāt cittasya, [tadā] tadeva dhyānaṁ [samādhirityucyate ॥]
nanu ca yogaḥ samādhirityaṅgī pūrvamuktaḥ । ihāṅgo yogasya samādhirityākhyāyate । kaḥ punaratrāṅgāṅginorbheda iti ? ucyate – yogaḥ samādhiriti cittasthitiviśeṣo vivakṣitaḥ । iha tu pratyayasantānasyaiva dhyeyasvabhāvāveśāt dhyeyākāratvamaṅgamiti viśeṣaḥ ॥ 3 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['That very one, shining as the object alone, as if empty of its own form, is <s>samādhi</s>. That very meditation'] — having the form of a flow of similar cognitions — as if abandoning its own nature as a stream of uniform cognitions, ['shines forth in the form of the object of meditation (<s>dhyeya</s>)'] — it appears as if having the form of the <s>dhyeya</s>. ['As if empty of its own nature'] as apprehension, ['as cognition (<s>pratyaya</s>).'] Just as a crystal substance, reflecting what is placed near it, appears as if empty of its own form. ['When this happens, due to complete absorption into the essential nature of the <s>dhyeya</s>'] — this being the cause, on the part of the mind — ['then'] that very meditation ['is called <s>samādhi</s>.']
But was it not previously stated that '<s>yoga</s> is <s>samādhi</s>' as the principal [practice]? Here, <s>samādhi</s> is designated as a limb (<s>aṅga</s>) of <s>yoga</s>. What then is the distinction between the limb and the principal? It is said: 'Yoga is <s>samādhi</s>' — there a particular state of mental stability (<s>citta-sthiti-viśeṣa</s>) was intended. Here, however, the distinction is that the stream of cognitions itself, through absorption into the essential nature of the <s>dhyeya</s>, assumes the form of the <s>dhyeya</s> — this is the limb. || 3 ||

body.text: trayamekatra saṁyamaḥ ॥ 4 ॥
body.translated_text: The three [<s>dhāraṇā</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, and <s>samādhi</s>] together upon a single [object] constitute <s>saṃyama</s> (complete discipline). || 4 ||

body.text: tadetaddhāraṇādhyānasamādhitrayamekatra saṁyama। ekaviṣayāṇi trīṇi sādhanāni saṁyama ityucyate। tadasya trayasya tāntrikī paribhāṣā saṁyama iti ॥ 4 ॥
body.translated_text: This triad of <s>dhāraṇā</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, and <s>samādhi</s> upon a single [object] is <s>saṃyama</s>. When these three means of practice are directed at one object, it is called <s>saṃyama</s>. This is the technical definition (<s>paribhāṣā</s>) within the system for this triad — '<s>saṃyama</s>.' || 4 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tadetaddhāraṇādhyānasamādhitrayaṁ] yadvyākhyātaṁ tat [ekatra] ekasmin deśe pariniṣpannaṁ sat [saṁyama] ityuvyate । tadāha – [ekaviṣayāṇi trīṇi sādhanāni saṁyama ityucte । tadasya trayasya] itthaṁkrameṇābhiniṣpannasya [tāntrikī] tantraprayojanā [paribhāṣā ।] jijñāsitārthasākṣādapādanāya yatra yatra saṁyamaḥ śrūyate jetavyajayāya vā, , tatra tatra trayametat praveditavyamityevamarthametasya trayetyāsmin śāstre paribhāṣeyaṁ [saṁyama] iti ॥
vakṣyati ca - ’ [pariṇāmatrayasaṁyamādatītānāgatajñānam ‘, ‘sthūlasvarūpasūkṣmānvayārthavattvasaṁyamādbhūtajayaḥ’ iti ca ॥ 4 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['This triad of <s>dhāraṇā</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, and <s>samādhi</s>'] — that which has been explained — ['upon a single'] locus, when brought to completion, ['is called <s>saṃyama</s>.'] He then states: ['These three means of practice directed at one object are called <s>saṃyama</s>. This'] triad, accomplished in this sequential manner, has ['a technical'] — a purpose within the system — ['definition.'] Wherever <s>saṃyama</s> is mentioned for the purpose of directly realizing a desired object, or for mastery over what is to be conquered, there this entire triad should be understood — such is the meaning of the technical definition ['<s>saṃyama</s>'] in this treatise.
And he will state: ['From <s>saṃyama</s> on the three transformations (<s>pariṇāma-traya</s>), knowledge of past and future arises'; 'From <s>saṃyama</s> on the gross, essential nature, subtle, inherent connection, and purposefulness, mastery over the elements arises.' || 4 ||]

body.text: tajjayātprajñālokaḥ ॥ 5 ॥
body.translated_text: From mastery of that [<s>saṃyama</s>], the light of <s>prajñā</s> (higher wisdom) [arises]. || 5 ||

body.text: tasya saṁyamasya jayātsasamādhiprajñāyā bhavatyāloko yathā yathā saṁyamaḥ sthirapado bhavati tathā tathā samādhiprajñā viśāradī bhavati ॥ 5 ॥
body.translated_text: From mastery of that <s>saṃyama</s>, there arises the light of <s>samādhi</s>-born <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). As <s>saṃyama</s> becomes firmly established, so does the <s>samādhi</s>-born wisdom become lucid and clear. || 5 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tajjayāt prajñā''lokaḥ । tasya saṁyamasya jayāt] sthiratvāpādanāt abhīpsitārthābhivyañjanasamarthaḥ pradīpālokadeśīyaḥ [samādhiprajñāyā bhavatyālokaḥ ।]
[yathā yathā saṁyamaḥ sthirapado bhavati, tathā tathā samādhiprajñā sthirapadī bhavati ।] yena samādhiprajñā''lekena vyavahitaviprakṛṣṭādivastunirbhāsanasamarthena yoginaḥ karatalakalitamivābhimatamarthamavalokayanti ॥ 5 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['From mastery of that, the light of <s>prajñā</s>. From mastery of that <s>saṃyama</s>'] — from making it stable — there arises a ['light of <s>samādhi</s>-born wisdom,'] comparable to the light of a lamp, capable of illuminating the desired object.
['As <s>saṃyama</s> becomes firmly established, so does the <s>samādhi</s>-born wisdom become firmly established.'] By means of this light of <s>samādhi</s>-born wisdom — which is capable of illuminating things that are hidden, remote, and so forth — yogins behold their desired object as if placed in the palm of their hand. || 5 ||

body.text: tasya bhūmiṣu viniyogaḥ ॥ 6 ॥
body.translated_text: Its application is by stages (<s>bhūmi</s>). || 6 ||

body.text: tasya saṁyamasya jitabhūmeryā'nantarā bhūmistatra viniyogaḥ। na hyajitādharabhūmiranantarabhūmiṁ vilaṅghyaprāntabhūmiṣu saṁyamaṁ labhate। tadabhāvācca kutastasya prajñālokaḥ। īśvaraprasādājjitottarabhūmikasya ca nādharabhūmiṣu paracittajñānādiṣu saṁyamo yuktaḥ। kasmāt, tadarthasyānyata evāvagatatvāt। bhūmerasyā iyamanantarā bhūmirityatra yoga evopādhyāyaḥ। katham। evaṁ hyuktam – yogena yogo jñātavyo yogo yogātpravartate। yo'pramattastu yogena sa yoge ramate ciram ॥ iti ॥ 6 ॥
body.translated_text: The application of that <s>saṃyama</s> should be to the stage immediately following the one already mastered. For one who has not conquered a lower stage cannot skip the next stage and obtain <s>saṃyama</s> in the further stages. And in the absence of that [<s>saṃyama</s>], how can there be the light of <s>prajñā</s>? Moreover, for one who has mastered a higher stage through the grace of <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), <s>saṃyama</s> on lower stages such as knowledge of others' minds is not appropriate. Why? Because the meaning of those [lower stages] has already been understood by other means. 'This stage is immediately next to that stage' — in this matter, <s>yoga</s> itself is the teacher. How so? For thus it has been said: 'By <s>yoga</s>, <s>yoga</s> is to be known; <s>yoga</s> proceeds from <s>yoga</s>. One who is vigilant in <s>yoga</s> delights in <s>yoga</s> for a long time.' || 6 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tasya bhūmiṣu viniyogaḥ । tasya saṁyamasya bhūmiṣu] bāhyādhyātmikeṣu dhyānālambanabhūtāsu vakṣyamāṇāsu pariṇāmatrayādiṣu [viniyogaḥ] prayegaḥ kartavyaḥ । ।
tadbhūmijayasākṣātprayojanārthinā [tasya saṁyamasya, jitabhūmeḥ] jitāyā bhūmeḥ, yatra bhūmai yoginaḥ saṁyatāyāṁ saṁyamo labdhaḥ, tasyā jitāyā bhūmeḥ [anantarā yā bhūmistatra] saṁyamasya pūrvabhūmijayānantaraṁ [viniyogaḥ] karaṇīyaḥ । ।
tadyathā – pṛthivyādīnāṁ sthūlasvarūpasūkṣamānvayārthavattvabhūmiṣu krameṇa jetavyāsu , sthūlāyāṁ bhūmau saṁyamaṁ kṛtvā, tajayānantaraṁ svarūpa evānantare saṁyamo viniyojanīyaḥ ’ । nānantaraṁ svarūpaṁ vyatilaṅghaya sūkṣmādibhūmiṣu saṁvidadhīta ॥
kasmādevam ? [na hyajitādharabhūmiranantarāṁ bhūmiṁ vilaṅghaya prāntabhūmiṣu] uparitanīṣu bhūmiṣu [saṁyamaṁ labhate ॥]
yadi cānantarāṁ bhūmimajitvā prāntabhūmiṣu saṁyamaṁ viniyuṅkṣeta, tameva saṁyamaṁ na labhate । tataśca tadalābha eva doṣaḥ । [tadalābhācca] saṁyamābhāvācca [kutastatra] seyamaviṣaye prāntabhūmāvityarthaḥ । [prajñā''lokaḥ ।] nimittābhāvāt । na hyasati tailavartijvalanābhisannipāte pradīpālokaḥ ॥
[jitottarabhūmikasya] jitottarātmādibhūmikasya yoginaḥ [nādharabhūmiṣu paracittajñānādiṣu saṁyamo yuktaḥ । kasmāt? tadarthasya] ātmādeḥ uttarabhūmerapakṛṣṭaparacitajñānādibhūmivaiparītyena [anyathaivādhigatatvāt ।] paracittajñānādibhiḥ saṁkīrṇaṁ asamadhigatavivekātmakatvāt । tatra hi jitottarabhūmiseyamasya parakīyacitālambanatve sekīrṇacittākāratā yogicittasyāpi syāditi na yuktaḥ । tatrātmāderathaisyānyathaiva viviktatayā'dhigatatvāt ॥
anyeṣāṁ vyākhyānam – [arthasya] paracittajñānādeḥ । [anyathaivādhigatatvāt] ātmādyuttarabhūmisamadhigamanenaiva adharaparacittajñānādibhūmerarthasya adhigatatvāt iti ॥
asmin pakṣe ‘adharabhūmiṣu saṁyamo'narthaka' iti vaditavyamabhaviṣyat, na *na yuktaḥ' iti । ‘na yukta' ityetadasamīcīnamiva dṛśyate ॥
[bhūmerasyā iyamanantarā bhūmiḥ] iyamanantaraṁ jayanīyeti kathamavabhotsyata ityāha – [tatra yoga evopādhyāya । yogaḥ] pūrvabhūmau saṁyamalābhaḥ । tenaivānantaryamavagamyate ।
