[katham ? evaṁ hyuktam – yogena yogo jñātavyaḥ ।] pūrvasaṁyamalābhena yogena anantaro yogaviṣayaḥ prajñānīyaḥ । sa ca [yogaḥ saṁyamaḥ, yogāt] eva pūrvasaṁyamalābādeva [pravartate] vivicyate ॥
yathaiva januṣā andhakasya sopānapaṅktatimārurukṣataḥ prathamasopānapratilabdhapadapadasparśapratyayenānantarasopānajñānamupaploṣyate [tathā yogo yogāt pravartate ॥]
yata evaṁ tasmāt sa itthaṁ jānan [apramattastu] yogī [yogena] yuktaḥ san [yogeṣu] yogaiśvaryaphaleṣu [ramate, ciram iti ॥ 6 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['Its application is by stages. Of that <s>saṃyama</s>, by stages'] — upon the external and internal objects of meditation, namely the forthcoming stages such as the three transformations (<s>pariṇāma-traya</s>) and so forth — ['application'] — practice should be carried out.
By one who seeks the fruit of mastering those stages — ['of that <s>saṃyama</s>, from the mastered stage'] — from the stage that has been conquered, where the yogin has attained <s>saṃyama</s> on a particular stage — ['the immediately next stage, there'] <s>saṃyama</s> ['should be applied'] after conquering the preceding stage.
For example — in the stages of the gross, essential nature, subtle, inherent connection, and purposefulness of earth and the other [elements], which are to be conquered sequentially — having performed <s>saṃyama</s> on the gross stage, immediately after conquering that, <s>saṃyama</s> should be applied to the next stage, namely the essential nature. One should not skip the next stage of essential nature and undertake [<s>saṃyama</s>] on the subtle and other stages.
Why is it so? ['For one who has not conquered a lower stage cannot skip the next stage and obtain <s>saṃyama</s> in the further stages.']
And if one were to apply <s>saṃyama</s> to further stages without conquering the next stage, one would not even attain that <s>saṃyama</s>. Thus the defect is precisely the non-attainment of that [<s>saṃyama</s>]. ['And in the absence of that'] — in the absence of <s>saṃyama</s> — ['how can there be'] — the meaning is: in the further stage where there is no proper domain — ['the light of <s>prajñā</s>?'] Because the cause is absent. For without the conjunction of oil, wick, and flame, there is no lamplight.
['For one who has mastered a higher stage'] — for a yogin who has conquered the higher stage of the self (<s>ātman</s>) and so forth — ['<s>saṃyama</s> on lower stages such as knowledge of others' minds is not appropriate. Why? Because the meaning of those'] — of the self and so forth, from the higher stage — has been ['understood by other means'] — in a manner contrary to the lower stages of knowledge of others' minds and so forth. Because it has not been understood in a manner that discriminates the nature of <s>viveka</s> (discernment), since it is mixed with knowledge of others' minds and so forth. For in that case, if a yogin who has mastered a higher stage were to take others' minds as objects of meditation, even the yogin's mind would take on a mixed character of mental forms — hence it is not appropriate. There, the self and so forth have already been understood in a discriminated manner by other means.
Others explain: ['The meaning'] of knowledge of others' minds and so forth — has been ['understood by other means'] — through the very attainment of the higher stage of the self and so forth, the meaning of the lower stage of knowledge of others' minds has been understood.
In this interpretation, it should have been said '<s>saṃyama</s> on lower stages is purposeless,' not ['not appropriate.'] The expression 'not appropriate' appears somewhat unsuitable [for that reading].
['This stage is immediately next to that stage'] — how will one know what is the next stage to be conquered? To this he says: ['In that matter, <s>yoga</s> itself is the teacher. <s>Yoga</s>'] — the attainment of <s>saṃyama</s> on the prior stage — by that very means, the sequential order is understood.
['How so? For thus it has been said: By <s>yoga</s>, <s>yoga</s> is to be known.'] Through <s>yoga</s> — through the attainment of the prior <s>saṃyama</s> — the next domain of <s>yoga</s> is to be known. And that ['<s>yoga</s>'] — that <s>saṃyama</s> — ['proceeds from <s>yoga</s>'] — from the very attainment of the prior <s>saṃyama</s> — ['is discerned.']
Just as for one blind from birth, ascending a staircase, knowledge of the next step arises from the sensory experience of placing one's foot on the first step — ['so <s>yoga</s> proceeds from <s>yoga</s>.']
Since this is so, therefore the one who knows thus, ['being vigilant'] — the yogin, ['engaged in <s>yoga</s>,'] ['delights in the fruits of yogic powers (<s>yoga-aiśvarya</s>) for a long time.' || 6 ||]

body.text: trayamantaraṅgaṁ pūrvebhyaḥ ॥ 7 ॥
body.translated_text: These three [<s>dhāraṇā</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>samādhi</s>] are inner limbs (<s>antaraṅga</s>) compared to the previous [five]. || 7 ||

body.text: tadetaddhāraṇādhyānasamādhitrayamantaraṅgaṁ saṁprajñātasya samādheḥ pūrvebhyo yamādibhyaḥ pañcabhyaḥ sādhanebhya iti ॥ 7 ॥
body.translated_text: This triad of <s>dhāraṇā</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, and <s>samādhi</s> is the inner limb (<s>antaraṅga</s>) of <s>saṃprajñāta samādhi</s> (cognitive absorption), compared to the previous five means beginning with <s>yama</s>. || 7 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[trayamantaraṅgaṁ pūrvebhyaḥ । dhāraṇādhyānasamādhitrayam antaraṅgaṁ pūrvebhyaḥ pañcabhyaḥ sādhanebhyaḥ yamādibhyaḥ samprajñātasya] yogasya । tatrāntaraṅgagrahaṇaṁ pūrvasādhanāsampattāvapyatra traye ādaraḥ karaṇīya ityevamartham ॥
vināpi hi yamādisādhanapañcatayasampādanena janmāntaravihitasaṁskārāveśavaśādeva videhaprakṛtilayānāmiva dhāraṇāditrayasampatyā yoga upakalpyate । dhāraṇāditrayeṇa vinā na yogaḥ saṁbhavati kasyacit । tabdyāpāranairantarya saṁvādātmakatvāṅddhāraṇāditrayasya । yogasya cittasampattirūpatvāt ॥
yadā tu jñānavairāgyasampatiḥ, tadā na kiṁcidanyaddhāraṇādyapyapekṣyate । tathā ca maṅkipiṅgalāprabhṛtīnāmanuśrūyate vairāgyādeva samastasiddhiḥ । tathā coktam – [‘sthānāsanavidhānāni ‘] iti pūrvatra ślokadvayam ॥ 7 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['These three are inner limbs compared to the previous. The triad of <s>dhāraṇā</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, and <s>samādhi</s> is the inner limb, compared to the previous five means beginning with <s>yama</s>,'] of <s>saṃprajñāta</s> (cognitive) <s>yoga</s>. Here, the designation 'inner limb' means that even when the previous means have not been fully accomplished, earnest effort should be directed toward this triad.
For indeed, even without accomplishing the five means beginning with <s>yama</s>, through the force of impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) cultivated in previous lives — just as for the <s>videha</s>s (disembodied ones) and <s>prakṛti-laya</s>s (those merged in <s>Prakṛti</s>) — <s>yoga</s> can be attained through the accomplishment of the triad beginning with <s>dhāraṇā</s> alone. Without the triad beginning with <s>dhāraṇā</s>, <s>yoga</s> is not possible for anyone, because the triad of <s>dhāraṇā</s> and so forth is characterized by effort, continuity, and harmony [with <s>yoga</s>], and because <s>yoga</s> has the nature of a particular state of mental accomplishment (<s>citta-sampatti</s>).
However, when knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) and dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) are fully accomplished, then nothing else — not even <s>dhāraṇā</s> and the rest — is required. Thus it is heard in tradition regarding <s>Maṅki</s>, <s>Piṅgala</s>, and others that all <s>siddhi</s>s (accomplishments) [came] from dispassion alone. And thus it was stated: ['Regarding the rules of posture and place'] — the two verses mentioned earlier [apply here]. || 7 ||

body.text: tadapi bahiraṅgaṁ nirbījasya ॥ 8 ॥
body.translated_text: Even these [three] are outer limbs (<s>bahiraṅga</s>) of seedless [<s>samādhi</s>]. || 8 ||

body.text: tadapyantaraṅgaṁ sādhanatrayaṁ nirbījasya yogasya bahiraṅgaṁ bhavati। kasmāt, tadabhāve bhāvāditi ॥ 8 ॥
body.translated_text: Even this inner triad of means becomes an outer limb (<s>bahiraṅga</s>) of seedless <s>yoga</s> (<s>nirbīja yoga</s>). Why? Because [seedless <s>samādhi</s>] arises even in its absence. || 8 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tadapi bahiraṅgaṁ nirbījasya । tadapi etat antaraṅgamapi] sabījasya yogasya, [bahiraṅgaṁ bhavati nirbījasya yogasya । kasmāt ? tadabhāve bhāvāt ।] tasya sabījāntaraṅgasādhanatrayasyābhāve'pi puruṣasattvaviśeṣāpekṣayā nirbījayogasya bhāvāt bahiraṅgatvam ॥
kecidatisamīcīnadarśanā janmanaiva saṁskārādaparaktāḥ । teṣāṁ paravairāgyavirāmapratyayasaṁśīlanādisamīkṣayā nirbījaḥ samādhirupajaniṣyata eva । na hi teṣāṁ dhāraṇādisamīkṣaṇam । tathā coktam – [uktaḥ samāhitacittasya yogaḥ । vyutthitacitto'pi kathaṁ yogayuktaḥ syādityata idamārabhyate’] iti । tathā [‘bhavapratyayo videhaprakṛtilayānām] iti ॥ 8 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['Even these are outer limbs of seedless <s>samādhi</s>. Even this'] inner limb of seeded (<s>sabīja</s>) <s>yoga</s>, ['becomes an outer limb of seedless <s>yoga</s>. Why? Because it arises even in its absence.'] Even in the absence of the inner triad of means of seeded [<s>yoga</s>], seedless <s>yoga</s> arises depending on the distinctive excellence of <s>Puruṣa</s> and <s>sattva</s> — hence it is an outer limb.
Certain persons of exceedingly pure vision are, from birth itself, free from attachment due to [prior] <s>saṃskāra</s>s. For them, through the cultivation of supreme dispassion (<s>para-vairāgya</s>) and the practice of cessation-cognition (<s>virāma-pratyaya</s>), seedless <s>samādhi</s> will indeed arise. For them, there is no need for the practice of <s>dhāraṇā</s> and the rest. And thus it was stated: ['<s>Yoga</s> has been described for one whose mind is concentrated (<s>samāhita-citta</s>). How can one whose mind is in the emergent state (<s>vyutthita-citta</s>) also become endowed with <s>yoga</s>? For this reason, this [section] is commenced.'] Likewise: ['<s>Bhava-pratyaya</s> (existence-conditioned) for the <s>videha</s>s and <s>prakṛti-laya</s>s.'] || 8 ||

body.text: atha nirodhacittakṣaṇeṣu calaṁ guṇavṛttamiti kīdṛśastadā cittapariṇāmaḥ –
body.translated_text: Now, since the activity of the <s>guṇa</s>s is fluctuating during the moments of <s>nirodha</s> (cessation) of the mind, what then is the transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>) of the mind at that time?

body.text: vyutthānanirodhasaṁskārayorabhibhavaprādurbhāvau nirodhakṣaṇacitānvayo nirodhapariṇāmaḥ ॥ 9 ॥
body.translated_text: The <s>nirodha-pariṇāma</s> (cessation-transformation) is the connection of the mind with the moment of <s>nirodha</s>, wherein there is the subjugation [of <s>vyutthāna</s> impressions] and the emergence [of <s>nirodha</s> impressions] of the <s>saṃskāra</s>s of emergence (<s>vyutthāna</s>) and cessation (<s>nirodha</s>). || 9 ||

body.text: vyutthānasaṁskārāścittadharmā na te pratyayātmakā iti pratyayanirodhe na niruddhā nirodhasaṁskārā api cittadharmāstayorabhibhavaprādurbhāvau vyutthānasaṁskārā hīyante nirodhasaṁskārā ādhīyante। nirodhakṣaṇaṁ cittamanveti tadekasya cittasya pratikṣaṇamidaṁ saṁskārānyathātvaṁ nirodhapariṇāmaḥ। tadā saṁskāraśeṣaṁ cittamiti nirodhasamādhau vyākhyātam ॥ 9 ॥
body.translated_text: The <s>saṃskāra</s>s (impressions) of emergence (<s>vyutthāna</s>) are properties of the mind; they are not of the nature of cognition (<s>pratyaya</s>), hence they are not suppressed when cognition is suppressed. The <s>saṃskāra</s>s of <s>nirodha</s> (cessation) are also properties of the mind. Of these two, the subjugation and emergence [operate thus]: the <s>vyutthāna</s> impressions diminish while the <s>nirodha</s> impressions increase. The mind follows the moment of <s>nirodha</s> — this transformation of <s>saṃskāra</s>s at every moment within that single mind is the <s>nirodha-pariṇāma</s> (cessation-transformation). At that time, the mind remains as a mere residue of <s>saṃskāra</s>s — thus it was explained in the context of <s>nirodha-samādhi</s>. || 9 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[atha nirodhacittakṣaṇeṣu] nirodhayuktaṁ nirudhyamānaṁ cittaṁ yeṣu' kṣaṇeṣu nirudhyate te nirodhacittakṣaṇāḥ teṣu nirodhakāle ityarthaḥ । kṣaṇeṣviti bahuvacanaṁ atītānāgatavartamānavṛttitvapradarśanārtham ॥
nirodhasya (trikṣaṇaṁ) kṣaṇe hi nirodhadharmamanvīyamānaṁ cittaṁ nirudhyate । [calaṁ guṇavṛttaṁ] gauṇaṁ cittaṁ guṇavṛttaṁ calam [iti] avaśyaṁbhāvī tasya bāhyavṛttibhyo nirudhyamānacittasya pariṇāmaḥ । na hyapariṇamamānasya cittasya puruṣavat kauṭasthye nirodha upakalpate । tataścāha – [kīdṛśastadā nirodhapariṇāma iti ॥]
[vyuthānanirodhasaṁskārayorabhibhavaprādurbhāvau nirodhakṣaṇacittānvayo nirodhapariṇāmaḥ । vyuthānaṁ] vividhamuthānaṁ calanaṁ pratyayākāreṇa cittasya । tadupajanitaḥ [saṁskāraścittasya] dharmiṇo [dharmaḥ । na sa pratyayātmakaḥ ॥]
tathā [nirodhajanmā saṁskāraḥ] apralyayātmakaḥ [cittasyaiva dharma ।] sa ca [vyutthānasaṁskāro'pratyayātmaka iti sa pratyayanirodhe na nirudhyate ।] vyutthānapratyayānirodhe nābhibhūtaḥ ॥
pratyayanirodhācca nirodhajaḥ saṁskāraḥ sañjāyate । tayoḥ vyutthānanirodhasaṁskārayoḥ dharmiṇi citte vartamānayoḥ [abhibhavaprādurbhāvau] bhavataḥ ॥
kiṁ tāvāvibhāvatirobhāvau aniyamena bhavataḥ ? na । kathaṁ tarhi । [vyutthānasaṁskārā hīyante] svakāryakṣamatvamupāśnuvate । [nirodhasaṁskārā ādhīyante ।] tau cābhibhavaprādurbhavau [nirodhakṣaṇaṁ cittaṁ] dharmitvena [anveti ?] sa tayorabhibhavaprādurbhāvayościttenānugamo nirodhapariṇāmaścitasya ॥
[tat] etadabhihitaṁ bhavati – [ekasya cittasya pratikṣaṇamidaṁ saṁskārānyathātvaṁ] vyuthānasaṁskārābhibhavena nirodhasaṁskāraprādurbhāvena saṁskārānyathātvam । vyuthānasaṁskārāṇāmapi hīyamānatayā satyapi sambandhe prādurbhavatā nirodhenaiva balavatvāt [nirodhapariṇāma] iti samākhyātam ॥
[(tadā)] nirodhyamānaṁ bāhyebhyaḥ pratyayebhyaḥ [saṁskāraśeṣaṁ cittamiti vyākhyātam virāmapratyayābhyāsapūrvaḥ saṁskāraśeṣo'nyaḥ] iti ॥
kimetena, āha – nirodhāvasānatvāt pratyayābhāvāvasānatayā pariṇāmasya nirodhapariṇāma iti ॥
samprajñātāvasthāyāṁ santo'pi pratyayā na vivakṣitāḥ । kiṁ tu pratikṣaṇasaṁskārānyathātvameva vivakṣyate । 'yathā niruddhabhūmini cetasi vidyamāno'pi samādhiḥ na vivakṣyate । nirodhamātrasya vivakṣitatvāt । tathā sabījāvasthāyāmapi saṁskārānyathātvamāttrameva vivakṣitam । na pratyayāḥ samādhirekāgratā ceti ॥ 9 ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Sub-commentary):
[Now, in the moments of nirodha-citta (cessation-mind)] — the <s>citta</s> (mind) conjoined with <s>nirodha</s> (cessation), the moments in which the <s>citta</s> being restrained is actually restrained, those are the <s>nirodha-citta-kṣaṇas</s> (moments of the cessation-mind); "in those" means "at the time of cessation." The plural "in the moments" is used to indicate that the operation pertains to past, future, and present.
Regarding the three moments of <s>nirodha</s> (cessation): at each moment, the <s>citta</s> (mind), being pervaded by the property of <s>nirodha</s>, is restrained. ["Unstable, its activity is secondary"] — the secondary <s>citta</s> is of the nature of <s>guṇa</s>-activity, hence unstable. Therefore, transformation of that <s>citta</s> being restrained from external activities is inevitable. For <s>nirodha</s> (cessation) cannot be attributed to a <s>citta</s> that does not undergo transformation, just as it cannot be attributed to <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Self), which is immutable. Hence he says — ["What then is this <s>nirodha-pariṇāma</s> (cessation-transformation)?"]
["The suppression and manifestation of the <s>saṁskāras</s> (latent impressions) of <s>vyutthāna</s> (emergence) and <s>nirodha</s> (cessation), the connection of the <s>nirodha</s>-moment with <s>citta</s>, is <s>nirodha-pariṇāma</s> (cessation-transformation). <s>Vyutthāna</s>"] means the manifold rising up, the movement of <s>citta</s> in the form of <s>pratyaya</s> (cognition). The <s>saṁskāra</s> (latent impression) generated by that [is a property] of the <s>citta</s>, which is the <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer). ["It is not of the nature of <s>pratyaya</s> (cognition)."]
Likewise, ["the <s>saṁskāra</s> born of <s>nirodha</s>"] is not of the nature of <s>pratyaya</s> (cognition); [it is a property of <s>citta</s> alone.] And ["the <s>vyutthāna-saṁskāra</s> (emergence-impression), being not of the nature of <s>pratyaya</s>, is not restrained when <s>pratyaya</s> is restrained."] When the <s>pratyayas</s> of <s>vyutthāna</s> (emergence) are restrained, it is not suppressed.
And from the cessation of <s>pratyaya</s> (cognition), the <s>saṁskāra</s> born of <s>nirodha</s> (cessation) arises. Of those two — the <s>saṁskāras</s> of <s>vyutthāna</s> and <s>nirodha</s> — existing in the <s>citta</s> as <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer), ["suppression and manifestation"] occur.
Do these manifestation and concealment occur without any fixed order? No. How then? ["The <s>vyutthāna-saṁskāras</s> (emergence-impressions) diminish"] — they lose their capacity to produce their effects. ["The <s>nirodha-saṁskāras</s> (cessation-impressions) are deposited."] And do these suppression and manifestation ["follow the <s>citta</s> at the <s>nirodha</s>-moment"] as <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer)? That connection of <s>citta</s> with the suppression and manifestation of those two is the <s>nirodha-pariṇāma</s> (cessation-transformation) of <s>citta</s>.
["That"] means what has been stated is this — ["this alteration of <s>saṁskāras</s> of the one <s>citta</s> at every moment"] — the alteration of <s>saṁskāras</s> through the suppression of <s>vyutthāna-saṁskāras</s> (emergence-impressions) and the manifestation of <s>nirodha-saṁskāras</s> (cessation-impressions). Even though the <s>vyutthāna-saṁskāras</s> still have a connection while diminishing, because <s>nirodha</s> (cessation) alone prevails by its strength as it manifests, [it is called "<s>nirodha-pariṇāma</s>" (cessation-transformation)].
["Then"] the <s>citta</s> being restrained from external <s>pratyayas</s> (cognitions), ["the <s>citta</s> has been described as having only <s>saṁskāras</s> remaining — ‘the other, preceded by the practice of cessation-cognition, has only <s>saṁskāras</s> remaining’"] (YS I.18).
What is the point of this? He says — since at the culmination of <s>nirodha</s> (cessation), the <s>pratyayas</s> (cognitions) remain only as <s>saṁskāras</s> (latent impressions), and the <s>pratyayas</s> themselves do not persist — this is the meaning.

body.text: tasya praśāntavāhitā saṁskārāt ॥ 10 ॥
body.translated_text: Its flow of tranquility comes from <s>saṁskāra</s> (latent impression). (YS III.10)

body.text: nirodhasaṁskārābhyāsapāṭavāpekṣā praśāntavāhitā cittasya bhavati। tatsaṁskāramāndye vyutthānadharmiṇā saṁskāreṇa nirodhadharmasaṁskāro'bhibhūyata iti ॥ 10 ॥
body.translated_text: The tranquil flow of <s>citta</s> (mind) depends on the skill in the practice of <s>nirodha-saṁskāra</s> (cessation-impression). When that <s>saṁskāra</s> weakens, the <s>nirodha-dharma-saṁskāra</s> (cessation-property-impression) is overpowered by the <s>saṁskāra</s> possessing the property of <s>vyutthāna</s> (emergence). (III.10)

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tasya] cittasya nirodhapariṇāmamanugacchataḥ [praśāntavāhitā saṁskārāt । nirodhasaṁskārapāṭavāpekṣā] nirodhasaṁskārasya pāṭavaṁ draḍhimā tadapekṣā [praśāntavāhitā] prasannatā [cittasya bhavati ॥]
sā praśāntavāhitā kiyantaṁ kālamityāha – [taṁ saṁskāraṁ] nirodhasaṁskāraṁ [ārabhya yāvat vyutthānadharmiṇā] vyutthānaṁ dharmo vyutthānajanitatvādyasya tena [saṁskāreṇa nirodhadharmasasaṁskāro nābhibhūyate,] tāvantaṁ kālamasya praśāntavāhitā । nirodhasaṁskārasamudayāditi ॥ 10 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Sub-commentary):
["Of that"] <s>citta</s> (mind) which undergoes <s>nirodha-pariṇāma</s> (cessation-transformation), ["the tranquil flow comes from <s>saṁskāra</s>. Depending on the skill of <s>nirodha-saṁskāra</s>"] — the skill means firmness of the <s>nirodha-saṁskāra</s> (cessation-impression); depending on that, ["the tranquil flow"] — serenity — ["of <s>citta</s> arises."]
How long does this tranquil flow last? He says — ["beginning from that <s>saṁskāra</s>"] — the <s>nirodha-saṁskāra</s> (cessation-impression) — ["as long as the <s>nirodha-dharma-saṁskāra</s> (cessation-property-impression) is not overpowered by"] a <s>saṁskāra</s> ["possessing the property of <s>vyutthāna</s>"] — whose property is <s>vyutthāna</s> (emergence) because it is born of <s>vyutthāna</s> — for that long is its tranquil flow. This is from the accumulation of <s>nirodha-saṁskāras</s>. (III.10)

body.text: sarvārthataikāgratayoḥ kṣayodayau cittasya samādhipariṇāmaḥ ॥ 11 ॥
body.translated_text: The decline of <s>sarvārthatā</s> (all-objectness) and the rise of <s>ekāgratā</s> (one-pointedness) in <s>citta</s> (mind) is <s>samādhi-pariṇāma</s> (absorption-transformation). (YS III.11)

body.text: sarvārthatā cittadharmaḥ। ekāgratā'pi cittadharmaḥ। sarvārthatāyāḥ kṣayastirobhāva ityarthaḥ। ekāgratāyā udaya āvirbhāva ityarthaḥ। tayordhamitvenānugataṁ cittaṁ, tadidaṁ cittamapāyopajanayoḥ svātmabhūtayordharmayoranugataṁ samādhīyate sa cittasya samādhipariṇāmaḥ ॥ 11 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>Sarvārthatā</s> (all-objectness) is a <s>dharma</s> (property) of <s>citta</s> (mind). <s>Ekāgratā</s> (one-pointedness) is also a <s>dharma</s> of <s>citta</s>. The decline of <s>sarvārthatā</s> means its disappearance. The rise of <s>ekāgratā</s> means its manifestation. The <s>citta</s> follows both of these as their <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer). This <s>citta</s>, following these two properties that are its own nature — namely their decline and arising — becomes absorbed; that is the <s>samādhi-pariṇāma</s> (absorption-transformation) of <s>citta</s>. (III.11)

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[sarvārthataikāgratayoḥ kṣayodayau cittasya samādhipariṇāmaḥ । sarvārthatā] bhogāpavargārthayogyatāvicitratā [cittadharmaḥ ।] vakṣyati – [‘draṣṭṛdṛśyoparaktaṁ cittaṁ sarvārtham] ’ iti । [ekāgratā'pi cittasya dharmaḥ] śāntoditapratyayayoḥ sāmyaṁ samādhīyamānasya cittasya [sarvarthatāyāḥ kṣayaḥ] bhavati । [tirobhāvaḥ ityarthaḥ ।] na hi kiṁcidvidyamānaṁ vinaṅkṣyati । [ekāgratāyā udayaḥ] bhavati । [āvirbhāva ityarthaḥ ।] nāvidyamānamutpadyate ॥
tayoḥ kṣayodayayoḥ [dharmitvenānugataṁ] cittam । pūrvasūtrādanvayagrahaṇamihāpi sannidhīyate । sarvārthatāyāḥ kṣayamekāgratāyāścodayaṁ niyamenānvīyamānaṁ citaṁ samādhiprādhānyena pariṇamate । yo'sau cittena sarvārthataikāgratākṣayodayayoranugamaḥ sa samādhipariṇāmaḥ । samādheśca prādhānyamekāgratābhūmau vyākhyātam ['yastvekāgre cetasi sa bhūtamarthaṁ pradyotayati’] iti ॥
tadevāha – [tadidaṁ cittam, apāyopajanau svātmabhūtau] avyatiriktau [tayordharmayoḥ] sarvārthataikāgratayoḥ [anu] (bhavā) [gamāt samādhīyate । sa cittasya] samādhiprādhānyāt [samādhipariṇāmaḥ ॥ 11 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Sub-commentary):
["The decline of <s>sarvārthatā</s> (all-objectness) and the rise of <s>ekāgratā</s> (one-pointedness) in <s>citta</s> is <s>samādhi-pariṇāma</s>. <s>Sarvārthatā</s>"] — the variegated capacity suited to the purposes of enjoyment and liberation — ["is a <s>dharma</s> (property) of <s>citta</s>."] As will be stated — ["the <s>citta</s>, colored by the seer and the seen, serves all purposes"] (YS IV.23). ["<s>Ekāgratā</s> (one-pointedness) is also a <s>dharma</s> of <s>citta</s>"] — when the <s>citta</s> is being absorbed, there being equality between the subsided and arisen <s>pratyayas</s> (cognitions), ["the decline of <s>sarvārthatā</s>"] occurs. ["This means disappearance."] For nothing that exists will be destroyed. ["The rise of <s>ekāgratā</s>"] occurs. ["This means manifestation."] Nor does something non-existent come into being.
The <s>citta</s> ["follows as <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer)"] these two — decline and rise — the <s>citta</s> as property-bearer follows the decline and rise; it is not that other properties follow the decline and rise, but rather the <s>citta</s> as property-bearer is what connects with those two.
["This"] <s>citta</s>, ["following the two properties that are its own nature — their decline and arising — becomes absorbed,"] becomes concentrated; ["that"] connection ["is the <s>samādhi-pariṇāma</s> (absorption-transformation) of <s>citta</s>."] (III.11)

body.text: tataḥ punaḥ śāntoditau tulyapratyayau cittasyaikāgratāpariṇāmaḥ ॥ 12 ॥
body.translated_text: Then again, when the subsided and arisen <s>pratyayas</s> (cognitions) are similar, that is the <s>ekāgratā-pariṇāma</s> (one-pointedness-transformation) of <s>citta</s> (mind). (YS III.12)

body.text: samāhitacittasya pūrvapratyayaḥ śānta uttarastatsadṛśa uditaḥ, samādhicittamubhayoranugataṁ punastathaivā''samādhibhreṣāditi। sa khalvayaṁ dharmiṇaścittasyaikāgratāpariṇāmaḥ ॥ 12 ॥
body.translated_text: For the concentrated <s>citta</s> (mind), the prior <s>pratyaya</s> (cognition) is the subsided one and the subsequent one, similar to it, is the arisen one; the <s>samādhi-citta</s> (absorption-mind) follows both of them, and again in the same manner until the breaking of <s>samādhi</s> (absorption). This indeed is the <s>ekāgratā-pariṇāma</s> (one-pointedness-transformation) of the <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer), <s>citta</s>. (III.12)

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tatra punaḥ] samādhikāle [śāntoditau tulyapratyayau cittasyaikāgratāpariṇāmaḥ । samāhitacittasya] niruddhabāhyavṛtteḥ [pūrvaḥ pratyayaḥ śāntaḥ] tirobhūtaḥ । [uttarastatsadṛśa uditaḥ] prādurbhūtaḥ । [samādhicittaṁ] samādhānaviśiṣṭaṁ samādhyavastham । [samādhicittamubhayoḥ] śāntoditayoḥ pratyayayoḥ [anugatam ॥]
[punastathaiva] yathā pratyaya ādyaḥ śānta uttarastatsadṛśa upajātaḥ, sa ca śāntaḥ punaranya uditaḥ, sa śāntaḥ punaścānya uditaḥ, ityevaṁ [ā samādhibhreṣāt] vyutthānasaṁskāreṇa yāvat samādhiḥ vibhraṁśate ॥
[sa khalvayaṁ dharmiṇaḥ cittasya] pratikṣaṇaṁ sadṛśaśāntoditapratyayayoranugamaḥ [ekāgratāpariṇāmaḥ ॥]
tatra yāvat bāhyavṛttinirodhādārabhya cittasya saṁskārapaśeṣatā, tāvat nirodhapariṇāmaḥ ॥
tathā bāhyapratyayanirodhāt prabhṛti ā prāk aśeṣapratyayanirodhāt, aśeṣapratyayanirodhottarakālaṁ ca ekāgratodayābhāvāt, tāvat samādhipariṇāmaḥ ॥
tathā samādhipariṇāmakāla eva śāntoditayostulyayoḥ saṁbhavādekāgratāpariṇāmaḥ । pūrvapariṇā(māna)manāntarīyakatvamuttarottarapariṇāmasyeti krameṇa trayo'pi pariṇāmā vyākhyātāḥ ॥
kimanena pariṇāmānvākhyānena prayojanam ? ucyate – calaṁ guṇavṛttaṁ, gauṇaṁ ca samastaṁ pariṇāmadharmakamanavasthitamiti vairāgyabhāvanārtham । tathā pariṇāmatrayasaṁyamādatītānāgatajñānārthaṁ ca etadanvākhyānam ॥ 12 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Sub-commentary):
["Then again,"] at the time of <s>samādhi</s> (absorption), ["when the subsided and arisen <s>pratyayas</s> (cognitions) are similar, that is the <s>ekāgratā-pariṇāma</s> (one-pointedness-transformation) of <s>citta</s>. For the concentrated <s>citta</s>"] — whose external activities have been restrained — ["the prior <s>pratyaya</s> is the subsided one"] — it has disappeared. ["The subsequent one, similar to it, is the arisen one"] — it has manifested. ["The <s>samādhi-citta</s>"] — the <s>citta</s> distinguished by absorption, in the state of <s>samādhi</s>. ["The <s>samādhi-citta</s> follows both"] — the subsided and arisen <s>pratyayas</s> (cognitions).
["Again in the same manner"] — just as the first <s>pratyaya</s> subsides and the subsequent one similar to it arises, and that too subsides and another arises, and that subsides and yet another arises — thus ["until the breaking of <s>samādhi</s>"] — as long as <s>samādhi</s> is not disrupted by <s>vyutthāna-saṁskāra</s> (emergence-impression), for that long is the <s>ekāgratā-pariṇāma</s> (one-pointedness-transformation). This is the meaning.
["This indeed is the <s>ekāgratā-pariṇāma</s> of the <s>dharmin</s>, <s>citta</s>"] — though the <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer), <s>citta</s>, transforms its <s>dharma</s> (property) at every moment, this transformation is of a single form alone; hence it is called <s>ekāgratā-pariṇāma</s> (one-pointedness-transformation). (III.12)

body.text: etena bhūtendriyeṣu dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāpariṇāmā vyākhyātāḥ ॥ 13 ॥
body.translated_text: By this, the transformations of <s>dharma</s> (property), <s>lakṣaṇa</s> (time-characteristic), and <s>avasthā</s> (condition) in the <s>bhūtas</s> (elements) and <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs) are explained. (YS III.13)

body.text: etena pūrvoktena cittapariṇāmena dharmalakṣaṇāvasthārūpeṇa bhūtendriyeṣu dharmapariṇāmo lakṣaṇapariṇāmo'vasthāpariṇāmaścokto veditavyaḥ। tatra vyutthānanirodhayordharmayorabhibhavaprādurbhāvau dharmiṇi dharmapariṇāmaḥ। lakṣaṇapariṇāmaśca। nirodhastrilakṣaṇastribhiradhvabhiryuktaḥ। sa khalvanāgatalakṣaṇamadhvānaṁ prathamaṁ hitvā dharmatvamanatikrānto vartamānalakṣaṇaṁ pratipannaḥ। yatrāsya svarūpeṇābhivyaktiḥ। eṣo'sya dvitīyo'dhvā। na cātītānāgatābhyāṁ lakṣaṇābhyāṁ viyuktaḥ।
body.translated_text: By this aforementioned transformation of <s>citta</s> (mind), which takes the form of <s>dharma</s> (property), <s>lakṣaṇa</s> (time-characteristic), and <s>avasthā</s> (condition), one should understand that the <s>dharma-pariṇāma</s> (property-transformation), <s>lakṣaṇa-pariṇāma</s> (time-characteristic-transformation), and <s>avasthā-pariṇāma</s> (condition-transformation) in the <s>bhūtas</s> (elements) and <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs) have also been stated. There, the suppression and manifestation of the two properties — <s>vyutthāna</s> (emergence) and <s>nirodha</s> (cessation) — in the <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer) is the <s>dharma-pariṇāma</s> (property-transformation). And regarding the <s>lakṣaṇa-pariṇāma</s> (time-characteristic-transformation): <s>nirodha</s> (cessation) has three time-characteristics, being connected with three time-paths. That <s>nirodha</s>, having first abandoned the time-path of the future characteristic, without transgressing its nature as a <s>dharma</s> (property), has entered the present characteristic — where its manifestation in its own nature occurs. This is its second time-path. And it is not disconnected from the past and future characteristics.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[etena bhūtendriyeṣu dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāpariṇāmā vyākhyātāḥ । etena pūrvoktena cittapariṇāmena ।] kiṁviśiṣṭena ? [dharmalakṣaṇāvasthārūpeṇa] dharmarūpeṇa lakṣaṇarūpeṇa avasthārūpeṇa ca । [bhūtendriyeṣu] bhūteṣu pṛthivīprabhṛtiṣu sthūleṣu, indriyeṣu ca śrotrādiṣu, yeṣāṁ tattvāntarapariṇāmo nāsti । [dharmapariṇāmo lakṣaṇapariṇāmo'vasthāpariṇāmaścokto veditavyaḥ ॥]
cittasyānavasthitatvena gamyamānena pariṇāmena bhūtendriyāṇāṁ pariṇāmasya prakāratrayayoginaḥ cittapariṇativat asuvijñānatvāt atideśaḥ kriyate ॥
nanu ca nirodhasamādhyekāgratāpariṇāmāścittasyābhihitāḥ । na tu dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāpariṇāmāḥ । kutastatrātideśa iti, abhihitatvameṣāṁ darśayati – [tatra vyutthānanirodhayoḥ] dharmayoḥ [abhibhavaprādurbhāvau dharmiṇi] citte [dharmapariṇāmaḥ ॥]
etasmāddhi dharmabhedavacanāt dharmabhedamavādiṣma । tayośca dharmapariṇāmayayoḥ vyutthānanirodhayorabhibhavaprādurbhavavacanāt lakṣṇāvasthāpariṇāmāvapi ca avādiṣmaiva ॥
katham ? vartamānalakṣaṇādatītalakṣaṇamabhisampadyamāno dharmo'bhibhūyate । yaśca anāgatalakṣaṇāt vartamānalakṣaṇamabhisampadyamānaḥ sa prādurasti । tadabhibhavaprādurbhāvavacanācca pratikṣaṇaṁ durbalarūpo'vasthāpariṇāma ukto bhavatītyāha – [lakṣaṇapariṇāmo nirodhastrilakṣaṇa] iti ॥
citte lakṣaṇapariṇāmaḥ trilakṣaṇatvena tribhiradhvabhiḥ atītānāgatavartamānaiḥ yuktaḥ pratipādyate pariṇāmino hyekaikasya trayo'pyadhvāna ete'vaśyaṁbhāvinaḥ । yasya tvete na santi so'pariṇāmī kūṭastha ityucyate ॥
[sa khalu] nirodhaḥ [anāgatalakṣaṇamadhvānaṁ hitvā dharmatvaṁ] nirodhadharmatvaṁ [anatikrāntaḥ] asatkāryārambhābhāvāt । asatkāryārambhe hi trikālatvamekasya vastuno nopapadyata (nāpi) kālatrayaparicchedyasya trilakṣasyābhāvāt । ata ucyate – [dharmatvamanatikrāmanneva vartamānaṁ lakṣaṇaṁ pratipannaḥ yatra] yasmin vartamāne lakṣaṇe [asya svarūpeṇābhivyaktiḥ eṣo'sya] nirodhasya anāgatādhvasamīkṣayā [dvitīyo'dhvā ॥]
yadā tu vyutthānaṁ vartamānaṁ lakṣaṇamārokṣyati, tadā nirodho'tītalakṣaṇamadhvānaṁ tṛtīyaṁ prāpsyatīti sa tṛtīyo'dhvā bhaviṣyatyeva ।
syādetat – vartamānalakṣaṇapratipattau nirodhasya tryadhvatvaṁ nāstīti, ata āha – [na cātītānāgatābhyāṁ lakṣaṇābhyāṁ viyuktaḥ ।] kutaḥ ? yena sa evānāgato vartamāno'tītaśceti ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Sub-commentary):
["By this, the transformations of <s>dharma</s>, <s>lakṣaṇa</s>, and <s>avasthā</s> in the <s>bhūtas</s> and <s>indriyas</s> are explained. By this aforementioned transformation of <s>citta</s>."] Of what kind? ["Taking the form of <s>dharma</s> (property), <s>lakṣaṇa</s> (time-characteristic), and <s>avasthā</s> (condition)"] — in the form of property, in the form of time-characteristic, and in the form of condition. ["In the <s>bhūtas</s> (elements)"] — in the gross elements beginning with <s>pṛthivī</s> (earth), ["and in the <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs)"] beginning with <s>śrotra</s> (hearing) — for which there is no transformation into another <s>tattva</s> (fundamental category). ["The <s>dharma-pariṇāma</s> (property-transformation), <s>lakṣaṇa-pariṇāma</s> (time-characteristic-transformation), and <s>avasthā-pariṇāma</s> (condition-transformation) have been stated and should be understood."]
The explanation is given because the transformation of the <s>bhūtas</s> (elements) and <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs), which involves the threefold mode of transformation, is difficult to discern on its own, just like the transformation of <s>citta</s> (mind), whose transformation is inferred from its instability.
["There, the suppression and manifestation of the two properties — <s>vyutthāna</s> (emergence) and <s>nirodha</s> (cessation) — in the <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer) is the <s>dharma-pariṇāma</s> (property-transformation)."] Similarly, the suppression and manifestation of the gross and subtle characteristics of <s>vyutthāna</s>-<s>nirodha</s> pertaining to <s>pṛthivī</s> (earth) and so forth in the <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer) is the <s>dharma-pariṇāma</s> (property-transformation).
["And regarding the <s>lakṣaṇa-pariṇāma</s> (time-characteristic-transformation)"] — here it is analyzed: ["<s>Nirodha</s> (cessation) has three time-characteristics"] — characterized by past, present, and future — ["connected with three time-paths. That, having first abandoned the time-path of the future characteristic"] — when <s>nirodha</s> arises — ["without transgressing its nature as a <s>dharma</s> (property)"] — without transgressing the nature of <s>nirodha</s> as a property, because <s>nirodha</s> persists without being exceeded in the <s>dharmin</s> — ["has entered the present characteristic"] — the time-path.

body.text: tathā vyutthānaṁ trilakṣaṇaṁ tribhiradhvabhiryuktaṁ vartamānalakṣaṇaṁ hitvā dharmatvamanatikrāntamatītalakṣaṇaṁ pratipannam। eṣo'sya tṛtīyo'dhvā। na cānāgatavartamānābhyāṁ lakṣaṇābhyāṁ viyuktam। evaṁ punarvyutthānamupasaṁpadyamānamanāgatalakṣaṇaṁ hitvā dharmatvamanatikrāntaṁ vartamānalakṣaṇaṁ pratipannam। yatrāsya svarūpābhivyaktau satyāṁ vyāpāraḥ। eṣo'sya dvitīyo'dhvā। na cātītānāgatābhyāṁ lakṣaṇābhyāṁ viyuktamiti। evaṁ punarnirodha evaṁ punarvyutthānamiti। tathā'vasthāpariṇāmaḥ। tatra nirodhakṣaṇeṣu nirodhasaṁskārā balavanto bhavanti durbalā vyutthānasaṁskārā iti। eṣa dharmāṇāmavasthāpariṇāmaḥ। tatra dharmiṇo dharmaiḥ pariṇāmo dharmāṇāṁ tryadhvanāṁ lakṣaṇaiḥ pariṇāmo lakṣaṇānāmapyavasthābhiḥ pariṇāma iti। evaṁ dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāpariṇāmaiḥ śūnyaṁ na kṣaṇamapi guṇavṛttamavatiṣṭhate। calaṁ ca guṇavṛttam। guṇasvābhāvyaṁ tu pravṛttikāraṇamuktaṁ guṇānāmiti। etena bhūtendriyeṣu dharmadharmibhedāttrividhaḥ pariṇāmo veditavyaḥ।
body.translated_text: Likewise, emergence (<s>vyutthāna</s>), possessing three characteristics, is connected with the three time-phases. Having left the characteristic of the present, without having transcended its nature as a property (<s>dharmatva</s>), it assumes the characteristic of the past. This is its third time-phase. And it is not devoid of the characteristics of the future and the present. Thus,

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tathā vyutthānaṁ trilakṣaṇaṁ tribhiradhvabhiḥ] atītānāgatavartamānaiḥ [yuktaṁ vartamānalakṣaṇaṁ hitvā] dharmatvamanatikrāntaṁ yathā vyākhyātaṁ nirodhe nirodhini dharme vartamānamadhvānamabhisampadyamāne [atītalakṣaṇaṁ] adhvānaṁ [pratipannam ॥]
[eṣo'sya] vyutthānasya vartamānaṁ prathamamadhvānamabhisamīkṣya [dvitīyo'dhvā ।] dvitīye tu paryāye tṛtīya evādhvā dvitīyo bhaviṣyati । [na cānāgatavartamānābhyāṁ lakṣaṇābhyāṁ viyuktam ॥]
[punarvyutthānaṁ] nirodhasaṁskoraṇa [upasampadyamānam anāgatalakṣaṇaṁ] adhvānaṁ [hitvā dharmatvamanatikrāntaṁ vartamānalakṣaṇaṁ pratipannam । yatrāsya svarūpeṇābhivyaktau satyāṁ vyāpāraḥ] svakāryāpādanasāmarthyam । [eṣo'sya] anāgatābhisamīkṣayā [dvitīyo'dhvā । na cātītānāgatāmyāṁ lakṣaṇābhyāṁ viyuktam ॥]
yathā cittaṁ vyutthānanirodhadharmābhyāṁ na yujyate । [evaṁ punarnirodhaḥ evaṁ punaḥ vyutthānamiti] eṣa lakṣaṇapariṇāmaścittadharmayorvyutthānanirodhayoḥ ॥
[tathā avasthāpariṇāmaḥ] paridṛśyate । [katham ? nirodhakṣaṇeṣu] nirodhe vartamāne [nirodhasaṁskārā balavanto bhavanti ।] saṁskārabalavatvena nirodhabalavattvamapi । [durbalā vyutthānasaṁskārāḥ,] tata eva vyutthānadurbalatvamapi । tathā vyutthānalakṣaṇe vyutthānasaṁskārabalīyastvaṁ nirodhasaṁskāradurbalatvam, [ityevaṁ] pratikṣaṇaṁ dṛḍhadurbalāvatthābhyāṁ yujyamānānāṁ [dharmāṇāṁ avasthāpariṇāmaḥ ॥]
tatra kena rūpeṇa kasya pariṇāma iti darśayati – [dharmiṇo dharmaiḥ pariṇāmaḥ ।] yathā cittasya dharmiṇo nirodhavyutthānādidharmaiḥ । [dharmāṇāṁ tryadhvanāṁ lakṣaṇaiḥ] pariṇāmaḥ । yathā nirodhādicittadharmāṇāṁ anāgatādilakṣaṇaiḥ । [lakṣaṇānāmapyavasthābhiḥ pariṇāmaḥ ।] yathā vartamānādilakṣaṇānāṁ dṛḍhadurbalatvādyavasthābhiḥ । [ityevaṁ dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāpariṇāmaiḥ aśūnyalakṣaṇam] aśūnyarūpaṁ [guṇavṛttamavatiṣṭhate ॥]
[calaṁ guṇavṛtam ।] etadeva tu [guṇasvābhāvyaṁ pravṛttikāraṇaṁ] sakalavyāpārakāraṇaṁ [uktaṁ guṇānāṁ] sattvādīnām [iti । etena] cetasi prasiddhena dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāpārīṇāmātratayena [bhūtendriyeṣu dharmadharmibhedāt trividhaḥ pariṇāmo veditavyaḥ ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['Likewise, emergence, possessing three characteristics, connected with the three time-phases'] — past, future, and present — ['having left the characteristic of the present,'] without having transcended its nature as a property, as has been explained — in the case of <s>nirodha</s> (cessation), [existing] in the property of cessation, having attained the present time-phase,

body.text: paramārthatastveka eva pariṇāmaḥ। dharmisvarūpamātro hi dharmo dharmivikriyaivaiṣā dharmadvārā prapañcyata iti। tatra dharmasya dharmiṇi vartamānasyaivādhvasvatītānāgatavartamāneṣu bhāvānyathātvaṁ bhavati natu dravyānyathātvam। yathā suvarṇabhājanasya bhittvā'nyathākriyamāṇasya bhāvānyathātvaṁ bhavati na suvarṇānyathātvamiti।
body.translated_text: In ultimate reality, however, there is only a single transformation. For a property (<s>dharma</s>) is nothing but the essential nature of the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>); this modification of the property-bearer is elaborated through the door of properties. Therein, the existence of the property — which exists in the property-bearer in the present — undergoes alteration across the past, future, and present time-phases,

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[paramārthatastveka eva pariṇāmaḥ ।] katham ? [dharmisvarūpamātro hi dharmaḥ ।] na hi dharmiparihāreṇa dharmo nāma pṛthagasti । nāpi dharmaparityāgena lakṣaṇaṁ nāma pṛthak bhāvyate । nāpi lakṣaṇavyatirekeṇa avasthānāṁ pṛthaktvaṁ bhavati । tena [dharmivikriyaivaiṣā dharmadvārā] dharmabhedadvāreṇa tridhā [prapañcyate ॥]
kathaṁ punardharmivikriyaivaiṣā । na punaratyantāpūrvotpattivināśāviti ? tata āha – [tatra dharmasya] ghaṭādeḥ [dharmiṇi] mṛdākhye [vartamānasya adhvasvatītānāgatavartamāneṣu bhāvānyathātvameva] pratyayānyathātvam, atīto ghaṭaḥ, vartate, anāgataḥ, iti ca dharmiṇi vartamānasyaiva । sa eva dharmasyāvirbhāvatirobhāvānyathātvam । [na dravyānyathātvaṁ] tadeva mṛddravyaṁ dharmi rūpāntaraṁ ca ॥
udāharaṇaṁ paridarśayati – [yathā suvarṇabhājanasya bhittvā anyathā] kuṇḍalādibhāvena [kriyamāṇasya bhāvānyathātvaṁ] svastikakuṇḍalādisaṁsthānānyatvam । [na suvarṇadravyānyathātvamiti ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['In ultimate reality, however, there is only a single transformation.'] How? ['For a property is nothing but the essential nature of the property-bearer.'] For a property does not exist as something separate apart from the property-bearer. Nor is a characteristic something separate that can be conceived apart from the property. Nor

body.text: apara āha – dharmānabhyadhiko dharmī pūrvatattvānatikramāt। pūrvāparāvasthābhedamanupatitaḥ kauṭasthyenaiva parivarteta yadyanvayī syāditi। ayamadoṣaḥ। kasmāt। ekāntatānabhyupagamāt। tadetattrailokyaṁ vyakterapaiti nityatvapratiṣedhāt। apetamapyasti vināśapratiṣedhāt। saṁsargāccāsya saukṣmyaṁ, saukṣmyāccānupalabdhiriti।
body.translated_text: Another says — the property-bearer is not something in excess of the properties, because the prior reality is not transgressed. If it were a persistent entity (<s>anvayī</s>), it would undergo change through immutability (<s>kūṭasthatva</s>) alone, following the differences of prior and subsequent states. This is not a fault. Why? Because no absolute position is accepted. This entire threefold world

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[apara āha] asatkāryasamārambhābhimānī – [dharmābhyadhiko] dharmavyatirikto [dharmī] , dharmaścāvidyamāno'nyaścānyaśca samudāyiṣyate । na punareko dharmī dharmeṣu bhūtabhaviṣyadvartamāneṣu dharmīvyatirikto'nvayīti ॥
[yadyanvayī] dharmānabhyadhiko dharmāvyatiriktaḥ [pūrvatattvāt] pūrvapūrvadravyasvarūpāt [anatikrāman pūrvāparāvasthābhedam] atītādyavasthābhedam [anupatitaḥ] anugataḥ [syāt ,] tataśca eṣa doṣaḥ prasajati – sa dharmī tavābhimataḥ [kauṭasthyenāpi parivarteta] apariṇāmitve varteta ॥
atrāha-- [ayamadoṣaḥ । kasmāt ? ekāntānabhyupagamāt] atyantakauṭasthyavināśayoḥ dharmiṇo'nabhyupagamāt । yadyatyantaṁ kūṭastho dharmī syāt ātmavat, tataśca asmāddharmiṇo dharmāṇāmabhedāt kauṭasthyaṁ prasajyeteti doṣaḥ syāt । na tu dharmiṇāṁ guṇānāmatyantakauṭasthyamabhyupagamyate । pariṇāminityatvaṁ hi guṇānāṁ vadiṣyati ॥
atha vā, dharmadharmiṇoḥ [ekānta] bhedābhedā [nabhyupagamāt ।] ekāntena hi dharmibhyo'nvayibhyo dharmāṇāṁ [a]bhede kauṭasthyaṁ prāpnuyāt । atyantabhede vā dharmāṇāṁ atyantavināśaḥ syāt । na tvatyantabhedābhedāvabhyupāyiṣyete । tasmāt na kauṭasthyadoṣa iti ॥
kathaṁ kauṭasthyābhāva ityāha-- [tadetat trailokyaṁ vyakterapaiti,] na kūṭastham । kasmāt ? [nityatvapratiṣedhāt ।] kāryatvādeva hi nityatvaṁ pratiṣiddham । athātyantavinaṣṭamiti cedāha- [apetamapyasti, vināśapratiṣedhāt ।] kāraṇasya nityatvāt tadabhedācca kāryasya atyantavināśaḥ pratiṣiddha eva ॥
tataśca yaducyate kaiścit-viruddhahetvābhāsodāharaṇametaditi, kathaṁ ? yathā - ['asau vikāro vyakterapaiti, nityatvapratiṣedhāt , apetamapyasti, vināśapratiṣadhot'] ityatra [nityatvapratiṣedhāt] ityayaṁ hetuḥ [‘apeto'pi vikāro'sti'] ityanena siddhāntena virudhyate ॥
katham ? vyaktirātmalābhaḥ, apāyaḥ pracyutiḥ, yadyātmalābhāt pracyuto vikāro'sti, nityatvapratiṣedho nopapadyata । yattu vyakterapetasyāpi vikārasyāstitvaṁ tat khalu nityatvamiti ॥
nityatvapratiṣedho nāma vikārasyātmalābhāt pracyutiḥ । yadātmalābhāt pracyavate tadanityam । yadasti na tadātmalābhāt pracyavate । astitvaṁ ca ātmalābhāt pracyutiśceti viruddhāvetau dharmau saha na sambhavataḥ । so'yaṁ hetuḥ yaṁ siddhāntamāśritya pravartate tameva vyāhantīti viruddho heturiti ॥
nāyaṁ doṣaḥ । vastūnāṁ vyaktāvyaktadharmakatvābhyupagamāt । yathā hi ghaṭādirvidyamāno'pi san agāre nopalabhyate । na ca tāvatā asau nāstīti śakyaṁ pratijñātum । ālokopāyena hi vyajyate । tathā idaṁ trailokyaṁ kāraṇe saṁsṛṣṭaṁ vidyamānameva anabhivyaktātmakaguṇasvabhāvatayā, puruṣārthanimittenāviṣkriyate ॥
tathaiva ca gatisaṁskārakṣaye sthitisaṁskārābhivyaktau kāraṇaṁ prati saṁsṛjyamānaṁ vyakterapaiti । yathā dīpālokatirodhāne vidyamāno'pi ghaṭādiḥ santamasāvaṣṭambhāt vyatterapasarati, tathā atrāpi mahadādayo yamaḥ tryadhvānaḥ saṁsargavisargadharmāṇaḥ, na tu sattvādayo dhārmiṇaḥ ॥
tatastrailokyaṁ mahadādistambaparyavasānaṁ sattvādīnāṁ dharmabhūtama[na]bhivyaktidharmakaṁ sat atyantaniruddhasūkṣmadharmasamudayāt vyaktisthūladharmarūpeṇa na gṛhyata ityucyate – [tadetat trailokyaṁ vyakterapaiti] iti । na punaḥ dharbhisvarūpeṇāpāyaḥ । tathā ca dharmirūpeṇa nityatvāducyate – [tadapetamapyasti] iti ॥
tadevaṁ vyaktirūpaśca śaktirūpaścaiko dharmī, vyaktirūpeṇa ca tasyānityatvaṁ, śaktirūpeṇa ca nityatvamiti kathameṣa virodhaḥ syāt । na hi devadattaścalanādivyāpāreṇa sarvadā gṛhyamāṇaścalanādivirāme viraṁsyati । calanameva hi tirodhīyate । tasmādavyatāvasthāyāmapyasti dharmī, vyaktāvasthāyāmupalabhyamānatvāt, andhatamasāvasthitaghaṭādivat ॥
vyaktirapi svakīyadharmāntarasamīkṣayā dharmiṇī । sā ca dharmirūpeṇa nityā, dharmarūpeṇānityā abhyupeyate । evaṁ vikāreṣu dharmadharmibhedo'navasthita ityanavasthā'pi iṣyata eva ॥
tatra [vyakterapaiti] ityanena na virudhyate, [nityatvapratiṣedhāt] ityayaṁ hetuḥ । nāpi [apetamapyasti] ityanena virodhaḥ । ubhayorbhinnaviṣayatvāt । nāpi [vināśapratiṣedhāt] ityayaṁ [apetamapyasti] ityanena virudhyate । yathā bāhyādapeto'pyasti devadatta iti ॥
atha manvīthāḥ – asti iti nityatvamucyate, tena [nityatvapratiṣedhāt] ityayaṁ nityatvena virodhamāliṅgatīti । na – anabhyupagamāt । na hi vyakternityatvamabhyupagacchema, tasyā eva nityatvaṁ pratiṣedhema । śaktivyaktidharmakatvābhyupagamāditi hi pratipāditam ॥
tadetadanirjñāya parābhiprāyaṁ virodhodāharaṇatvāpādānam andhadarpaṇīyavṛttāntamudbhāvayati । yathā kila kaścidandhaḥ svāṁ adarśaśaktiṁ anavadhārya svārthamādarśamupārjayati tadvadetadābhāti ॥
api ca yadyapyekatraiva vyaktau śaktau vā nityatvamanityatvaṁ ca adhyāropya tvaṁ pakṣasiṣādhayiṣayā bravīthāḥ, evamapi viruddhodāharaṇatvaṁ na saṁbhavati, viparītā(ta)sādhanāt । katham ? [apeto'pyasti] iti [nityatvapratiṣedhāt] ityucyate । [nityatvapratiṣedhāt] iti anityatvādityuktaṁ bhavati । [apetasyāpyastitvaṁ] nityatvamucyate । nityatvasya viparītamanityatvam । na ca pakṣasyānityatvasya anityatvaṁ heturbhavati, yo viparītaṁ sādhayan nityatvaṁ virundhīta । na hyaniṣṭamasādhayan viruddhatāmiyāt ॥
athāpi nityatvapratiṣedho nāma ātmalābhāt pracyutiriti vika(lpasya)lpya vāvadyethāḥ – evamapi śabdabhedamātra(trāt) nārthabhedaḥ । ātmalābhāt pracyutiḥ, anityatvaṁ, ityeko'rthaḥ ॥
athāpi nityatvopapattyabhāvādityavalambethāḥ – evamapi [nityatvapratiṣedhāt] ityayaṁ śabdaḥ (ekasyāṁ śuktikāyāṁ) nityatvopapattyabhāvādityasyārthasya [a]vācakaḥ ॥
athāpi vācaka ityāropya pratibhāṣeta – evamapi śaktivyaktidharmadharmibhe(darūpeṇa)de na nityatvamanityatvaṁ(tyarūpaṁ) cetyuktameva samādhānam ॥
etena vyakteḥ [apeto'pyasti, vināśapratiṣedhāt] iti virodhodbhāvanaṁ pratyākhyātam ॥
evamavasthite vyakterapetasya pratyakṣeṇānupalabhyamānasya kathamastitvam ? yāvatā, nāsti, anupalabhyamānatvāt, nabhaḥkusumavat iti ॥
atrocyate – anupalabdhirasiddho hetuḥ । anumānāgamābhyāmupalabdheḥ । yadetat vyaktaṁ etat prāgutpatterapyasti, yata utpadyate । asaccennotpadyeta, śaśaviṣāṇavadeva ॥
kiṁ ca – asataḥ sattve sataścāsattve sarvatra na āśvasyuḥ । kiṁ ca – anupalabdheścedasattvaṁ muktātmakāraṇādīnāṁ ca prāgupalambhādūrdhvaṁ ca astitvaṁ kena labhyate ? tathā-
[“nāsato vidyate bhāvo nābhāvo vidyate sataḥ । ”]
iti agamaḥ । pratyakṣānupalabdhiśca nāsattvasya kāraṇam । atha vyaktereva vikāro vidyamānaścet, kuto nopalabhyata iti ? āha – sākṣāt kāraṇe [saṁsargādasya saukṣmyam, ato'nupalabdhiḥ ।] na asatvāt ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
[Another says] one who holds the view of asatkāryavāda (the doctrine that the effect does not pre-exist in the cause) — [the dharmī (property-bearer) is beyond the dharma (property)] — the dharmī is distinct from the dharma, and the dharma, being non-existent, being one thing and yet another, will be aggregated. But there is no single dharmī that persists as a continuous entity distinct from the dharmas — past, future, and present.
[If the persisting entity] is not beyond the dharmas, not distinct from the dharmas, [from the nature of the prior substance] from the essential nature of each preceding substance, [not transcending the distinction of prior and subsequent states] the distinction of past and other states, [following along] continuing, [would be] — then this fault arises: that dharmī accepted by you [would remain even in immutability] would remain in a state of non-transformation.
Here he responds — [This is not a fault. Why? Because of the non-acceptance of an absolute position.] Because the dharmī is not accepted as absolutely immutable or absolutely destructible. If the dharmī were absolutely immutable like the Ātman, then because of non-difference between the dharmī and its dharmas, the fault of immutability would follow. But absolute immutability of the guṇas (constituents) is not accepted. For it will be stated that the guṇas have a transforming eternality.
Alternatively, because of the non-acceptance of [absolute] difference or non-difference between dharma and dharmī. For if there were absolute non-difference between the dharmas and the persisting dharmīs, immutability would result. Or if there were absolute difference, the dharmas would be absolutely destroyed. But neither absolute difference nor absolute non-difference is accepted. Therefore, there is no fault of immutability.
How is there absence of immutability? He says — [This entire triple world departs from manifestation] — it is not immutable. Why? [Because eternality is negated.] For eternality is negated precisely because of being an effect. But if it is absolutely destroyed? He says — [Even what has departed exists, because destruction is negated.] Because of the eternality of the cause and because of non-difference from it, absolute destruction of the effect is indeed negated.
Then, as some say — this is an example of a contradictory pseudo-reason (viruddha-hetvābhāsa) — how so? As in: ['That modification departs from manifestation, because eternality is negated; even what has departed exists, because destruction is negated'] — here, the reason 'because eternality is negated' contradicts the thesis ['even the departed modification exists'].
How? Vyakti (manifestation) means attaining its own nature; apāya (departure) means falling away. If the modification that has fallen from attaining its own nature still exists, then the negation of eternality is not tenable. For the existence of the modification even after departing from manifestation — that indeed is eternality.
The negation of eternality means the falling away of the modification from its attained nature. What falls away from its attained nature is non-eternal. What exists does not fall away from its attained nature. Existence and falling away from attained nature —

body.text: lakṣaṇapariṇāmo dharmo'dhvasu vartamāno'tīto'tītalakṣaṇayukto'nāgatavartamānābhyāṁ lakṣaṇābhyāmaviyuktaḥ। tathā'nāgato'nāgatalakṣaṇayukto vartamānātītābhyāṁ lakṣaṇābhyāmaviyuktaḥ। tathā vartamāno vartamānalakṣaṇayukto'tītānāgatābhyāṁ lakṣaṇābhyāmaviyukta iti। yathā puruṣa ekasyāṁ striyāṁ rakto na śeṣāsu virakto bhavatīti।
body.translated_text: Lakṣaṇa-pariṇāma (transformation of characteristic): a dharma (property) existing in the time-paths (adhvan), when past, is endowed with the past characteristic and is not separated from the future and present characteristics. Likewise, when future, it is endowed with the future characteristic and is not separated from the present and past characteristics. Likewise, when present, it is endowed with the present characteristic and is not separated from the past and future characteristics. Just as a man attached to one woman is not unattached to the rest.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
idānīṁ bhūtendriyāṇāṁ lakṣaṇapariṇāma idamucyate – [lakṣaṇapariṇāmo dharmo] yathā mṛdo ghaṭādiḥ adhvasu atītādiṣu [vartamāno'tīto] dharmaḥ । kimuktaṁ bhavati ? [atītalakṣaṇayuktaḥ,] na punarasattvamāpannaḥ । itarābhyāṁ ca [anāgatavartamānābhyāmaviyuktaḥ ।] kāraṇasya mṛdo vartamānatvāt tatra saṁsṛṣṭasya ghaṭasya [a]vidyamānatve'pi(nasyāpi) yukto vartamānena lakṣaṇena ghaṭaḥ । tathā bhaviṣyannapi ghaṭo mṛda evānāgataḥ san bhaviṣyatītyanāgatalakṣaṇenāpyaviyuktaḥ [tathā vartamānaḥ, vartamānalakṣaṇayukta:, atītānāgatābhyāṁ lakṣaṇābhyāmaviyuktaḥ ॥]
[tathā anāgataḥ anāgatalakṣaṇayuktaḥ, vartamānātītābhyāṁ lakṣaṇābhyāmaviyuktaḥ] atītānāgatalakṣaṇayoḥ mṛdātmakatvāt ghaṭasya vyavahitenāpyatītalakṣaṇenāviyogaḥ ॥
kathamekalakṣaṇayukto dharmo lakṣaṇābhyāmaparābhyāmaviyukta ityaviyogasya dṛṣṭāntamāha – [yathā puruṣa ekasyāṁ striyāṁ rakto na śeṣāsu virakto bhavati ।] śeṣāsu tu bhūtabhaviṣyallakṣaṇayukto rāgaḥ । sataścāvinanāśādasataścānutpatteriti hi pratipāditam ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
Now the lakṣaṇa-pariṇāma (transformation of characteristic) of the bhūtendriya (elements and sense organs) is explained — [Lakṣaṇa-pariṇāma: a dharma] such as a pot from clay, [existing in the time-paths] — the past and so forth — [when past, the dharma] — what is being said? — [is endowed with the past characteristic] — but it has not entered into non-existence. And [it is not separated from the other two — future and present characteristics.] Because the cause, clay, is present, the pot that is merged therein, even when its [separate existence is] not manifest, is endowed with the present characteristic. Likewise, the pot that will come into being, being future while still in the clay, is also not separated from the future characteristic. [Likewise, when present, endowed with the present characteristic, not separated from the past and future characteristics.]
[Likewise, when future, endowed with the future characteristic, not separated from the present and past characteristics.] Because the past and future characteristics have the nature of clay, the pot is not separated from even the intervening past characteristic.
How is a dharma endowed with one characteristic not separated from the other two characteristics? He gives an illustration of this non-separation — [Just as a man attached to one woman is not unattached to the rest.] Toward the rest, the attachment is endowed with the past or future characteristic. For it has been established that what exists is not destroyed, and what does not exist is not produced.

body.text: atra lakṣaṇapariṇāme sarvasya sarvalakṣaṇayogādadhvasaṁkaraḥ prāpnotīti parairdoṣaścodyata iti। tasya parihāraḥ – dharmāṇāṁ dharmatvamaprasādhyam। sati ca dharmatve lakṣaṇabhedo'pi vācyo na vartamānasamaya evāsya dharmatvam। evaṁ, hi na cittaṁ rāgadharmakaṁ syātkrodhakāle rāgasyāsamudācārāditi।
body.translated_text: Here, regarding lakṣaṇa-pariṇāma (transformation of characteristic), since everything has connection with all characteristics, the objection is raised by others that adhva-saṅkara (confusion of time-periods) would result. The resolution of that: the dharmatva (property-nature) of properties need not be established anew. And given that dharmatva exists, the distinction of characteristics must also be stated — it is not the case that its dharmatva exists only in the present moment. For otherwise, the citta (mind) would not have rāga (attachment) as its property during the time of krodha (anger), since rāga does not manifest then.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
na hi krodhakāle rāgaḥ svakāla iva samudācarati । krodhakāle hi rāgaḥ atīto'nāgato vā । tathā krodho'pi rāgakāle । yadi hi vartamānasamaya evaikaṁ lakṣaṇaṁ abhaviṣyat, krodhakāle'pi rāgaḥ samudācariṣyat । nāpi vā । samudācariṣyat । nāpi krodhakāle nāsti ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
For during the time of krodha (anger), rāga (attachment) does not manifest as it does in its own time. During the time of anger, attachment is either past or future. Likewise, krodha too during the time of rāga. For if only the present moment had a single characteristic, rāga would manifest even during the time of krodha. Nor would it not manifest. It would manifest, yet it does not exist during the time of krodha.

body.text: kiṁca trayāṇāṁ lakṣaṇānāṁ yugapadekasyāṁ vyaktau nāsti saṁbhavaḥ। krameṇa tu svavyañjakāñjanasya bhāvo bhavediti। uktaṁ ca rūpātiśayā vṛttyatiśayāśca virudhyante, sāmānyāni tvatiśayaiḥ saha pravartante। tasmādasaṁkaraḥ। yathā rāgasyaiva kvacitsamudācāra iti na tadānīmanyatrābhāvaḥ kiṁtu kevalaṁ sāmānyena samanvāgata ityasti tadā tatra tasya bhāvaḥ। tathā lakṣaṇasyeti।
body.translated_text: Moreover, the simultaneous occurrence of the three characteristics in a single manifestation is not possible. But sequentially, through its own manifesting cause, it may come into being. And it has been said: excellences of form and excellences of function are contradictory, but generalities proceed together with excellences. Therefore, there is no confusion of time-periods. Just as rāga (attachment) itself manifests in a particular instance, its non-manifestation elsewhere at that time does not mean its non-existence there; rather, it is merely accompanied by a general nature — thus it exists there at that time. So too with the characteristics.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[kiṁ ca – trayāṇāṁ lakṣaṇānāṁ yugapadekasyāṁ] lakṣaṇasya [vṛttau] virodhāt [nāsti sambhavaḥ । krameṇa] lakṣaṇānāṁ krameṇa [svavyañjakāñjanasya] ghaṭādisvavyañjakāñjanasya anyatamasya lakṣaṇasya bhavet [sambhavaḥ ॥]
[uktaṁ ca – rūpātiśayāḥ vṛttyatiśayāśca virudhyante ।] vartamānarūpavṛttyatiśayairyukte ghaṭe ca piṇḍādivyaktirūpātiśayā virodhāt na saṁbhavanti । ata eva atītānāgatarūpā dharmisāmānyānugatatvenāvirodhāt [atiśayaiḥ saha vartante ॥]
[tasmāt] adhvanām [asaṁkaraḥ । yathā rāgasyaiva kvacit samudācāra iti na tadānīmanyatra] strīṣu [abhāvo] rāgasya । [kintu kevalaṁ sāmānyena cittarūpeṇa samanvāgataḥ] atīto'nāgato'pi san i [tyasti tadā tasya] rāgasya [bhāvaḥ । tathā lakṣaṇasyeti ॥]
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
['Moreover, the simultaneous occurrence of the three characteristics in a single'] characteristic's ['functioning'] is not possible due to contradiction. ['Sequentially,'] of the characteristics, in sequence, ['through its own manifesting cause,'] through the manifesting cause specific to pots and such, the occurrence of one or another characteristic ['may come about.']
['And it has been said: excellences of form and excellences of function are contradictory.'] When a pot is endowed with excellences of present form and function, the manifest form-excellences of the lump and such cannot occur due to contradiction. For this very reason, those having past and future form, ['because they follow the generality of the property-bearer and are therefore not contradictory, proceed together with the excellences.']
['Therefore,'] there is ['no confusion'] of the time-periods. ['Just as attachment manifests in a particular instance, its non-manifestation elsewhere'] toward other women ['does not mean the non-existence'] of attachment. ['Rather, accompanied merely by the generality in the form of mind,'] even being past or future, ['there is at that time the existence'] of that attachment. ['So too with the characteristics.']

body.text: na dharmī tryadhvā dharmāstu tryadhvānaste lakṣitā alakṣitāstatra lakṣitāstāṁ tāmavasthāṁ prāpnuvanto'nyatvena pratinirdiśyante'vasthāntarato na dravyāntarataḥ। yathaikā rekhā śatasthāne śataṁ daśasthāne daśaikā caikasthāne। yathā caikatve'pi strī mātā cocyate duhitā ca svasā ceti।
body.translated_text: The property-bearer (<s>dharmī</s>) does not exist in three time-periods; rather, the properties (<s>dharmas</s>) exist in three time-periods. They are characterized and uncharacterized. Among those, the characterized ones, as they attain one state after another, are designated as 'other' by virtue of a change of state — not by virtue of being a different substance. Just as one numeral in the hundreds place is a hundred, in the tens place is ten, and in the units place is one. And just as a single woman is called mother, daughter, and sister.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
nanu ca piṇḍakapālayoratītānāgatatvāt ghaṭāvasthāyāmabhāvācca tābhyāṁ mṛdākhyasya dharmiṇo'pi atītānāgatatvamiti dharmiṇi piṇḍakapālayorabhāva iti kṛtvā dharmāṇāṁ piṇḍakapālādīnāmadhvatrayānupapattiriti pariśaṅkamānaḥ kathayati [– na dharmī tryadhvā ।] mṛdākhyo hi dharmī piṇḍakapālātītānāgatatvena nātīto'nāgato vā । sarvadharmeṣu mṛdabhijñānānu(pra)vṛtteḥ । kiṁ tarhi ? [dharmāḥ] piṇḍādayaḥ [tryadhvānaḥ] ghaṭakāle piṇḍakapālayoradarśanāt । tasmādadhvatrayāyogo na dharmāṇāṁ pariśaṅkanīyaḥ ॥
te dharmā [lakṣitāḥ] piṇḍādayaḥ tryadhvatvenābhilakṣitāḥ [tāṁ tāmavasthāṁ] dṛḍhadurbalatvādikāṁ [prāpnuvanto'nyatvena] navo ghaṭaḥ purāṇaścetyanena [pratinirdiśyante'vasthāntarataḥ । na dravyāntarataḥ] mṛdatiritāt ॥
[yathā ekā rekhā śatasthāne] śūnyadvayena tṛtīyasthāne śataṁ bhavati । saiva ca [daśasthāne] ekena śūnyena dvitīyasthāne daśa । saiva [prathamasthāne ekā ॥]
[yathā vā ekatve'pi strī mātā cocyate duhitā ca,] saiva anyāpekṣayā [svasā ca ।] tadevam avasthāntarādeva śabdapratyayādibhedāḥ । na dharmadharmibhedena । tasmāt yaducyate paraiḥ śabdapratyayalakṣaṇadharmakālādibhedo hetuḥ kāryakāraṇabhede iti, so'nenānaikāntikīkṛtaḥ ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
Now, since the lump and the potsherd are past or future, and since they are absent in the state of the pot, the property-bearer called clay would also be past or future through them — and so the lump and potsherd would be absent in the property-bearer. Anticipating this concern that the three time-periods would be untenable for properties like the lump and potsherd, he says: ['The property-bearer does not exist in three time-periods.'] For the property-bearer called clay is not past or future by virtue of the past-or-future nature of the lump and potsherd — because the recognition of clay persists across all properties. What then? ['The properties'] — the lump and such — ['exist in three time-periods'] — since the lump and potsherd are not observed at the time of the pot. Therefore, the untenable application of three time-periods should not be a concern regarding the properties.
Those properties ['characterized'] — the lump and such, characterized as existing in three time-periods — ['as they attain one state after another,'] such as hardness and softness, ['are designated as "other"'] — 'a new pot' or 'an old one' — ['by virtue of a change of state. Not by virtue of being a different substance'] other than clay.
['Just as one numeral in the hundreds place'] — with two zeros, in the third position — becomes a hundred. That same [numeral]...

body.text: avasthāparaṇāme kauṭasthyaprasaṅgadoṣaḥ kaiściduktam। katham। adhvano vyāpāreṇa vyavahitatvāt। yadā dharmaḥ svavyāpāraṁ na karoti tadā'nāgato yadā karoti tadā vartamāno yadā kṛtvā nivṛttastadā'tīta ityevaṁ dharmadharmiṇorlakṣaṇānāmavasthānāṁ ca kauṭasthyaṁ prāpnotīti parairdoṣa ucyate।
body.translated_text: Regarding transformation of state (<s>avasthā-pariṇāma</s>), the objection of immutability (<s>kauṭasthya</s>) has been raised by some. How? Because the time-periods are differentiated by function. When a <s>dharma</s> (property) does not perform its function, it is future; when it performs it, it is present; when it has performed it and ceased, it is past. In this way, they say the fault of immutability follows for the properties, property-bearer, characteristics, and states.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[avasthāpariṇāme] tṛtīye'smin [kauṭasthyaprasaṅgadoṣaḥ [kaiścit] uktaḥ ।] kathaṁ kauṭasthyaprasaṅgaḥ ? [adhvānaḥ] vartamānādayaḥ [svavyāpāreṇa vyavahi(sthi)tāḥ ।] katham ? [yadā dharmo] ghaṭaḥ piṇḍāvasthāyāṁ [svavyāpāraṁ na karoti tadā anāgataḥ । yadā karoti tadā vartamānaḥ] ayam । [yadā kṛtvā nivṛttaḥ] [tadā atītaḥ ।] tatra sa eva dharmaḥ kṛtaḥ kriyamāṇaḥ kariṣyamāṇaḥ nijavyāpāropārūḍhaḥ dharmisvātmabhūta evāvasthāpitaḥ । na vyatiriktarūpaḥ । tena [dharmiṇāṁ] guṇānāṁ [nityatvāt] nityatvāvyatirekāt [dharmalakṣaṇāvasthanāṁ kauṭasthyaṁ prāpnotīti doṣa ucyate ॥]
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
['In the transformation of state'] — in this third [pariṇāma] — ['the objection of immutability has been raised by some.'] How does immutability follow? ['The time-periods'] — present and the rest — ['are differentiated by their own function.'] How? ['When a dharma'] — the pot, in the state of a lump — ['does not perform its function, it is future. When it performs it, it is present. When it has performed it and ceased, it is past.'] There, that very dharma — performed, being performed, to be performed — mounted upon its own function, is established as identical with the property-bearer's own nature. It has no separate form. Therefore, ['due to the eternality of the property-bearers'] — the guṇas — ['because their eternality is not different, the fault of immutability of properties, characteristics, and states follows, it is said.']

body.text: nāsau doṣaḥ। kasmāt। guṇinityatve'pi guṇānāṁ vimardavaicitryāt। yathā saṁsthānamādimaddharmamātraṁ śabdādīnāṁ guṇānāṁ vināśyavināśināmevaṁ liṅgamādimaddharmamātraṁ sattvādīnāṁ guṇānāṁ vināśyavināśināṁ tasminvikārasaṁjñeti।
body.translated_text: This is not a fault. Why? Because, even though the property-bearer is eternal, the <s>guṇas</s> (constituents) display variety through mutual friction. Just as configuration (<s>saṁsthāna</s>), having an origin, is a mere property of the qualities such as sound — destructible and destructive — so too <s>liṅga</s> (the manifest), having an origin, is a mere property of the <s>guṇas</s> such as <s>sattva</s> — destructible and destructive. In that, there is the designation 'modification' (<s>vikāra</s>).

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[nāsau doṣaḥ । kasmāt ? guṇinityatve'pi guṇānāṁ vimardavaicitryāt] udbhavābhibhavatvavicitratayā puruṣavadekāntakūṭasthatā neṣyate guṇānām । pariṇāmābhyupagamāt । na cānavaratapariṇatīnāmapi parasparavimardātirekeṇa dravyāntarabhāvāpattiriti na kauṭasthyam ॥
kathaṁ vimardavaicitryamityāha- [yathā saṁsthānaṁ] śarīrādikaṁ [ādi]mat kāraṇavat [dharmamātraṁ] kāraṇasyātmabhūtamavyatiriktaṁ [vināśi] tirobhāvadharmakaṁ dharmāntarasamudaye । keṣāṁ saṁsthānamityā(mā)ha- [śabdādīnāmavināśinām । evaṁ liṅgaṁ] mahadākhyaṁ [ādimat] kāraṇavat [dharmamātraṁ vināśe guṇānāmavināśinām] ātmabhūtam । [tasmin] mahadādidharmamātre [vikārasaṁjñā] na guṇānāṁ vimardavicitratayā vināśitvaṁ guṇasvarūpeṇa nityatvaṁ [iti ॥]
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
['This is not a fault. Why? Because, even though the property-bearer is eternal, the guṇas display variety through mutual friction.'] Through the variety of emergence and suppression, absolute immutability like that of Puruṣa is not intended for the guṇas — because transformation is accepted. And even for those that undergo unceasing transformation, there is no becoming a different substance beyond their mutual friction — hence there is no immutability.
How is there variety through mutual friction? He says: ['Just as configuration'] — of the body and such — ['having an origin'] — having a cause — ['is a mere property'] — identical with and not different from the cause — ['destructible'] — having the nature of concealment when another property arises. Of what is this configuration? He says: ['of the qualities such as sound, which are indestructible. Likewise liṅga (the manifest)'] — called mahat — ['having an origin'] — having a cause — ['is a mere property, destructible, of the guṇas, which are indestructible'] — identical with them. ['In that'] — in the mere property called mahat and the rest — ['there is the designation "modification."'] It is not that the guṇas are destroyed through the variety of mutual friction; their own nature remains eternal.

body.text: tatredamudāharaṇaṁ mṛddharmī piṇḍākārāddharmāddharmāntaramupasaṁpadyamāno dharmataḥ pariṇamate ghaṭākāra iti। ghaṭākāro'nāgataṁ lakṣaṇaṁ hitvā vartamānalakṣaṇaṁ pratipadyata iti lakṣaṇataḥ pariṇamate। ghaṭo navapurāṇatāṁ pratikṣaṇamanubhavannavasthāpariṇāmaṁ pratipadyata iti। dharbhiṇo'pi dharmāntaramavasthā dharmasyāpi lakṣaṇāntaramavasthetyeka eva dravyapariṇāmo bhedenopadarśita iti। evaṁ padārthāntareṣvapi yojyamiti। ta ete dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāpariṇāmā dharmisvarūpamanatikrāntā ityeka eva pariṇāmaḥ sarvānamūnviśeṣānabhiplavate। atha ko'yaṁ pariṇāmaḥ। avasthitasya dravyasya pūrvadharmanivṛttau dharmāntarotpattiḥ paraṇāma iti ॥ 13 ॥
body.translated_text: Here is an illustration: the property-bearer, clay (<s>mṛd</s>), transforming from the property of the lump-form to another property, undergoes property-transformation (<s>dharma-pariṇāma</s>) — becoming 'pot-form.' The pot-form, leaving behind the future characteristic and assuming the present characteristic, undergoes characteristic-transformation (<s>lakṣaṇa-pariṇāma</s>). The pot, experiencing newness and oldness moment by moment, undergoes state-transformation (<s>avasthā-pariṇāma</s>). A state is another property of the property-bearer; a state is another characteristic of the property. Thus a single transformation of substance is shown through differentiation. The same should be applied to other entities. These property-transformation, characteristic-transformation, and state-transformation, not transcending the nature of the property-bearer, are a single transformation that pervades all these distinctions. Now what is this transformation? The arising of another property upon the cessation of a prior property in an abiding substance is transformation. || 13 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tatrodāharaṇam-mṛt dharmī] piṇḍākārā [piṇḍākārāt ākārāntaraṁ] ghaṭaṁ [upasampadyamāno dharmataḥ pariṇamate ॥]
[[ghaṭākāro'nāgataṁ lakṣaṇaṁ hitvā vartamānalakṣaṇaṁ pratipadyata iti lakṣaṇataḥ pariṇamate ॥ ]]
tathā [ghaṭo navapurāṇatāṁ pratikṣaṇamanubhavan avasthāpariṇāmaṁ pratipadyata iti । dharmiṇo'pi] mṛdādeḥ [dharmāntaraṁ] piṇḍādikaṁ avasthā । dharmī piṇḍakapālādirūpāvasthāmāsīditi ॥
[dharmasyāpi] ghaṭādeḥ [lakṣaṇāntaraṁ] atītādikaṁ [avasthā ।] sa eva hi ghaṭo dharmo'tītānāgatavartamānāvasthāmupārohati ॥
tata [eka eva pariṇāmo bhedenopadarśita iti । evaṁ padārthāntareṣvapi] mṛdaḥ anyeṣaavapi śarīrendriyādiṣu [yojyam । ta ete dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāpariṇāmā dharbhisvarūpamanatikrāntā ityeka eva] dharmiṇaḥ [pariṇāmaḥ sarvān dharma] lakṣaṇāvasthāpariṇāmān [viśeṣānabhiplavate ।] kutaḥ ? [yena avasthitasya dravyasya pūrvadharmanivṛttau dharmāntarotpattiḥ pariṇāma iti] dharmī pariṇāma eveti śakyate pratipattum ॥ 13 ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
['Here is the illustration: clay is the property-bearer;'] having the lump-form, ['transforming from the lump-form into another form'] — the pot — ['it undergoes property-transformation.']
['The pot-form, leaving behind the future characteristic and assuming the present characteristic, undergoes characteristic-transformation.']
Likewise, ['the pot, experiencing newness and oldness moment by moment, undergoes state-transformation. Of the property-bearer too'] — of clay and such — ['another property'] — such as the lump — is a state. The property-bearer assumes states such as the lump-form and potsherd-form.
['Of the property too'] — the pot and such — ['another characteristic'] — past and the rest — ['is a state.'] For that very pot as a property ascends through the states of past, future, and present.
Therefore, ['a single transformation is shown through differentiation. The same should be applied to other entities too'] — other than clay, to bodies, senses, and the like. ['These property-transformation, characteristic-transformation, and state-transformation, not transcending the nature of the property-bearer — it is a single'] transformation of the property-bearer that ['pervades all these'] — the transformations of property, characteristic, and state — ['distinctions.'] From where

body.text: tatra –
body.translated_text: Therein —

body.text: śāntoditāvyapadeśyadharmānupātī dharmī ॥ 14 ॥
body.translated_text: The property-bearer (<s>dharmī</s>) follows properties that are quiescent, arisen, and indeterminable. || 14 ||

body.text: yogyatāvacchinnā dharmiṇaḥ śaktireva dharmaḥ। sa ca phalaprasavabhedānumita ekasyānyo'nyaśca paridṛṣṭaḥ। tatra vartamānaḥ svavyāpāramanubhavandharmī dharmāntarebhyaḥ śāntebhyaścāvyapadeśyebhyaśca bhidyate। yadā tu sāmānyena samanvāgato bhavati tadā dharmisvarūpamātratvātko'sau kena bhidyeta। tatra ye khalu dharmiṇo dharmāḥ śāntā uditā avyapadeśyā śceti, tatra śāntā ye kṛtvā vyāpārānuparatāḥ savyāpārā uditāste cānāgatasya lakṣaṇasya samanantarā vartamānasyānantarā atītāḥ। kimarthamatītasyānantarā na bhavanti vartamānāḥ, pūrvapaścimatāyā abhāvāt। yathā'nāgatavartamānayoḥ pūrvapaścimatā naivamatītasya। tasmānnātītasyāsti samanantaraḥ। tadanāgata eva samanantaro bhavati vartamānasyeti।
body.translated_text: A property (<s>dharma</s>) is nothing but a potency (<s>śakti</s>) of the property-bearer delimited by fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>). And its existence, though unmanifest, is inferred from the differentiation of its products in the property-bearer — just as a gold lump produces earrings and such at different places and times. The differentiation of those products allows the inference that it has the capacity to produce various other forms in that property-bearer. The property-bearer that is presently observed, experiencing its own function, differs from other properties — from those that are quiescent and from those that are indeterminable. But when it is accompanied only by the universal, then since it is merely the essential nature of the property-bearer, by what would it differ from what? Among the properties of the property-bearer that are quiescent, arisen, and indeterminable: the quiescent are those that have performed their function and ceased. The arisen are those that are engaged in function — they are subsequent to the future characteristic, contiguous to the present, and then past. Why do they not become present contiguous to the past? Because of the absence of a before-and-after [relation]. Just as there is a before-and-after relation between future and present, so it is not with the past. Therefore, the past has no contiguous successor. The contiguous successor is of the future, becoming present.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
kaḥ punarasau dharmī? yasmin avasthite dharmāntaravirāme dharmāntarodayaḥ pariṇāma iti । [tatra śāntoditāvyapadeśyadharmānupātī dharmī ।] śāntoditān avyapadaśyāṁśca dharmānanupatituṁ śīlaṁ yasya so'nvayī bhinneṣvabhinnātmā dharmīti vyapadiśyate । [dharmaḥ] nāma [yogyatāvacchinnā] śaknoti raśanākuṇḍalādibhāvamāpattumiti yā suvarṇasya [dharmiṇaḥ] kuṇḍalatvādikā [śaktiḥ] sa [eva dharmaḥ ॥]
[sa ca] avyakto'pi san dharmiṇi [phalaprasavabhedānumitasadbhāvaḥ ।] yathā deśāntare kālāntare ca tāṭaṅkādika phalaṁ kanakapiṇḍaḥ prasūyate । tatphalaprasavabhedadarśanenānyānanyānapi prakārānayaṁ prasavitu vibhavatīti tasmin dharmiṇi [phalaprasavabhedānumitasadbhāvaḥ । ekasya] dharmiṇaḥ [anyaścānyaśca] dharma ityanenaikasya dharmiṇo dharmasaṁkhyatvamāha ॥
tatra [yo dṛṣṭaḥ sa vartamānaḥ svaṁ vyāpāra] mudakāharaṇādikam [anubhavan dharmānterabhyaḥ śāntebhyaścāvyapadeśyebhyaśca bhidyate ॥]
[yadā tu sāmānyena] dharmirūpeṇa [samanvāgato bhavati,] atha [tadā dharmisvarūpamātratvāt] dharmisvarūpātmabhūtatvāt [ko'sau] viśeṣataḥ [kena vā bhidyeta ।] vyāpārādhirūḍharūpāṇāmeva bhedo, na kāraṇasamanugamanirīkṣitātmanāmityarthaḥ ॥
ke punaḥ śāntā uditā avyapadeśyā vā ? [te khalu dharmiṇo dharmāḥ śāntāḥ ye kṛtvā vyāpāramuparatāḥ । savyāpārā uditāḥ । te cānāgatalakṣaṇasya samanantarāḥ ।] tathā [vartamānasyānantarā atītāḥ । kimarthamatītasyānantarā na bhavanti ।] na santītyartha: । [pūrvapaścibhābhāvāt ।] yo yasya paścādbhavati sa tasya paścimo'nantaraḥ । itaraśca tadapekṣayā pūrvaḥ । tadiha paścimābhāvāt eṣa svayamapi pūrvo na bhavatīti pūrvapaścimābhāvādatītasyānantarā na santi । [yathā anāgatavartamānayoḥ pūrvapaścimatā naivamatītasya । tasmānna[nātī]tasyāsti samanantaraḥ ॥]
yastvayaṁ pāṭhaḥ [tadanāgata eva samanantarībhavati vartamānasya] iti, na tasya prakṛtena sambandhaḥ । tasmā [ttadanāgata eva samanantaro bhavatyatītasya] ityayameva pāṭhaḥ । arthopapatteḥ । katham? yadā vyutthānasaṁskāro nirodhasaṁskāreṇa ādyo'bhibhūyate, tadā vartamānamadhvānaṁ hitvā vyutthānasaṁskāro'tītamadhvānamupasampadya punaranāgataḥ sanvartamānībhavatītyasamanantaro'pyanāgata eva samanantarībhavatyatītasyetyucyate । atītānāgatayorlakṣaṇayordharmāṇāṁ dharmisvarūpamātrāviśeṣāt ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
What then is this property-bearer in which, while it abides, the arising of another property upon the cessation of a prior property is transformation? ['Therein, the property-bearer follows properties that are quiescent, arisen, and indeterminable.'] That whose nature it is to follow the quiescent, arisen, and indeterminable properties — that persisting entity, having an undifferentiated nature amid the differentiated, is designated as the property-bearer. ['A property'] is ['nothing but a potency of the property-bearer delimited by fitness'] — that gold, for example, has the capacity to assume the forms of necklace, bracelet, and such — ['that potency is the property.']
['And'] that [property], though unmanifest, ['has its existence inferred from the differentiation of products in the property-bearer.'] Just as a gold lump produces an earring at another place and time. From observing the differentiation of those products, it is inferred that it has the capacity to produce various other forms in that property-bearer — its ['existence is inferred from the differentiation of products. Of one'] property-bearer, ['the various'] properties — by this he states the multiplicity of properties in a single property-bearer.
Therein, ['that which is observed is the present, experiencing its own function'] —

body.text: athāvyapadeśyāḥ ke। sarvaṁ sarvātmakamiti। yatroktam – jalabhūmyoḥ pāriṇāmikaṁ rasādivaiśvarūpyaṁ sthāvareṣu dṛṣṭam। tathā sthāvarāṇāṁ jaṅgameṣu jaṅgamānāṁ sthāvareṣvityevaṁ jātyanucchedena sarvaṁ sarvātmakamiti।
body.translated_text: Now what are the indeterminable [properties]? 'Everything consists of everything' (<s>sarvaṁ sarvātmakam</s>). As it has been said: 'The transformative variety of flavors and such is observed in water and earth among the stationary [plants]. Likewise, of the stationary in the mobile, and of the mobile in the stationary — thus, without the interruption of class, everything consists of everything.'

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[atha avyapadeśyā] : ke? tadavyapadeśyābhipradarśanārthamāha – sarvaṁ sarvātmakam iti । katham? [tatroktam–jalabhūmyoḥ pāriṇāmikaṁrasādivaiśvarūpyaṁ sthāvareṣu dṛṣṭam ।] yathā rasa eka eva ikṣuśṛṅgiberakādiṣu madhurakaṭukatvādivaiśvarūpyaṁ pratipadyate । tathā, rūpasya śuklakṛṣṇatvādivicitrarūpatvam । evaṁ gandhādiṣvapi । [tathā sthāvarāṇāṁ jaṅgameṣu] rasādivaiśvarūpyam । sthāvarāṇāmupayuktānāṁ jaṅgameṣu rasalohitādiviśvabhedaḥ । [tathā jaṅgamānāṁ sthāvareṣu upayuktānām] vṛkṣāyurvedaprasiddhaṁ rasādivaiśvarūpyam ॥
evaṁ sthāvarāṇāsthāvereṣu, jaṅgamānāṁ ca jaṅgameṣu, [ityevaṁ jātyanucchedana] sattvādyavināśena [sarvaṁ sarvātmakam ।] aṅguleśikhare lokatrayamapyasti। tathā ca [‘aṅguṣṭhādasṛjat brahmā romakūpebhyaḥ’] ityādiśrutismṛtiśataprasthānam ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['Now, the undesignatable (<s>avyapadeśya</s>)'] — what are they? To illustrate the intended meaning, he says — everything contains the nature of everything (<s>sarvaṁ sarvātmakam</s>). How? ['It is stated therein — the transformative diversity of taste and the like in the water and earth elements is observed in stationary beings.'] Just as taste, though singular,

body.text: deśakālākāranimittāpabandhānna khalu samānakālamātmanāmabhivyaktiriti। ya eteṣvabhivyaktānabhivyakteṣu dharmeṣvanupātī sāmānyaviśeṣātmā so'nvayī dharmī। yasya tu dharmamātramevedaṁ niranvayaṁ tasya bhogābhāvaḥ। kasmāt, anyena vijñānena kṛtasya karmaṇo'nyatkathaṁ bhoktṛtvenādhikriyeta। tatsmṛtyabhāvaśca nānyadṛṣṭasya smaraṇamanyasyāstīti। vastupratyabhijñānācca sthito'nvayī dharmī yo dharmānyathātvamabhyupagataḥ pratyabhijñāyate। tasmānnedaṁ dharmamātraṁ niranvayamiti ॥ 14 ॥
body.translated_text: Due to the binding constraints of place, time, form, and cause, there is indeed no simultaneous manifestation of all the properties of the self.
