That which persists through these properties — whether manifest or unmanifest — consisting of both universal and particular, is the persistent property-bearer (<s>anvayī dharmin</s>). But for one for whom this is merely a property with no persistent substratum,

body.text:
vivaraṇam
yadi sarvaṁ sarvātmakaṁ, tadā sarvaṁ sarvatropalabhyeta, sammataviprayogajanmā ca śoko mā pra(ti)vartiṣṭetyāderuttaraṁ paṭhati – [deśakālākāranimittāpabandhāt] deśādīnāmapabandhaḥ avavandhaḥ tasmāt, [na samānakālam ātmanāṁ sarvavastūnām abhivyaktiḥ ।] kasyacit kvacideva deśekāle ca kenacidavākareṇa tanubhṛtāṁ ca dharmādinimittābhisamīkṣayākañcidaśvābhivyāktiḥ, yathā rāhuprabhṛtīnām । etenaiva sammataviprayoganimittaśokādyupapatiḥ । ata ekaikasmin atilaṅkitasaṁkhyāgocaratvāddharmānaśakyā vyapadeṣṭum ॥
ya eteṣu śāntoditāvyapadeśyeṣu [abhivyaktānabhivyakteṣu dharmeṣu anupātī sāmānyaviśeṣātmā] sattvādiśabdādirūpeṇa [so'nvayī dharmī । yasya tu] vādinaḥ [dharmamātramevedaṁ niranvayaṁ] bāhyamādhyāmakaṁca, yasya ca jñānamātrameva, tasya dharmāṇāṁ kṣaṇapraṇāśitvādatītānāgatavartamānapathārohiṇāṁ samānakālānāṁ ca bhoktṛbhogyatvādisaṁbandhānupapatteḥ [bhogābhāvaḥ ॥]
sambandhābhāvaṁ darśayati – [kasmāt? anyena vijñānena kṛtasya karmaṇo'nyat vijñānamakartṛ] bhaviṣyat [kathaṁ bhoktṛtvenādhikriyeta ।] kartuśca phalābhipravṛtteḥ phalena saṁbandho yujyate । anyaḥ kartā phalena cānyaḥ sambadhyata iti virudhyate ॥
[smṛtyabhāvaśca ।] kṛtakaraṇīyādiviṣayasmṛtyabhāvaśca । [anyadṛṣṭasya smaraṇamanyasyanāstīti ।] na hi caitradṛṣṭasya vasumitraḥ smarati । [[vastu] pratyabhijñānācca,] yasmāttadevedamitivastupratyabhijānīmaḥ, tasmāt [sthito'nvayī dharmī dharmānyathātvaṁ] dharmairanyathātvam [abhyupagataḥ] pratipannaḥ । na tu svarūpeṇānyathātvam । yathārucakādibhedānugatamapikanakameveti pratyabhijānīmaḥ । [tasmāt nedaṁ dharmamātraṁ niranvayamiti ॥ 14 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
If everything contains the nature of everything, then everything should be apprehended everywhere, and grief born of separation from loved ones should not occur — to answer such objections and the like, he reads: ['Due to the binding constraints of place, time, form, and cause'] — the binding, i.e. the restraint, of place and the rest,

body.text: kramānyatvaṁ pariṇāmānyatve hetuḥ ॥ 15 ॥
body.translated_text: Difference in sequence is the cause of difference in transformation. || 15 ||

body.text: ekasya dharmiṇa eka eva pariṇāma iti prasakte kramānyatvaṁ pariṇāmānyatve heturbhavatīti। tadyathā cūrṇamṛtpiṇḍamṛdghaṭamṛtkapālamṛtkaṇamṛditi ca kramaḥ। yo yasya dharmasya samanantaro dharmaḥ sa tasya kramaḥ। piṇḍaḥ pracyavate ghaṭa upajāyata iti dharmapariṇāmakramaḥ। lakṣaṇapariṇāmakramo ghaṭasyānāgatabhāvādvartamānabhāvaḥ kramaḥ। tathā piṇḍasya vartamānabhāvādatītabhāvaḥ kramaḥ। nātītasyāsti kramaḥ। kasmāt। pūrvaparatāyāṁ satyāṁ samanantaratvaṁ, sā tu nāstyatītasya। tasmāddvayoreva lakṣaṇayoḥ kramaḥ। tathā'vasthāpariṇāmakramo'pi ghaṭasyābhinavasya prānte purāṇatā dṛśyate। sā ca kṣaṇaparamparānupātinā krameṇābhivyajyamānā parāṁ vyaktimāpadyata iti। dharmalakṣaṇābhyāṁ ca viśiṣṭo'yaṁ tṛtīyaḥ pariṇāma iti।
body.translated_text: When it might be supposed that for a single property-bearer there is only a single transformation, difference in sequence becomes the cause of difference in transformation. For example: powdered clay, a lump of clay, a clay pot, a clay potsherd, clay granules — such is the sequence. That property which immediately succeeds another property is its

body.text:
vivaraṇam
idānīṁ pariṇāmabhedeheturucyate – siddhehi bhedepariṇāmatrayasaṁyamaḥ prayokturupakalpeta । yata: kaśyācilliṅgadvārā atītādiṣumatirupajanayituṁ śakyate, nānyathā iti, [kramānyatvaṁ pariṇāmānyatve hetuḥ । ekasya dharmiṇaḥ cittādeḥ eka eva pariṇāma iti prasakteḥ] dharmādīnāṁ dharmyabhedāditi, pariṇāmabhedasiddhaye hetureṣa ucyate – [kramānyatvam ।] kramaḥ anantarabhāvaḥ tasyānyatvaṁ bhedaḥ ॥
trayo hi kramā anyonyavidharmāṇa upalakṣyante । lakṣaṇāvasthākramābhyāmanyo dharmakramaḥ । dharmāvasthākramābhyāmanyo lakṣaṇakramaḥ । dharmalakṣaṇakramābhyāmanyo'vasthākramaḥ । yacca teṣāmanyatvaṁ prasiddhamārgamadhirūḍhaṁ tatkramakāryāṇāṁ pariṇāmānāmanumāpakam [anyatvehetuḥ ॥]
[tadyathā] mṛtdharmī [cūrṇamṛt] iti cūrṇādibhirdhamairayugapatkālajanmabhiḥ kramavartibhiḥ pariṇamate । sarvatra mṛdgrahaṇena dharmiṇo mṛdākhyasya parasparalakṣyamāṇabhedacūrṇapiṇḍaghaṭakapālakaṇādidharmānugamaṁ pratipādayati ॥
cūrṇasyānantaraḥ piṇḍaḥ, piṇḍasyānantaro ghaṭaḥ, ghaṭasyānantarāṇi kapālāni, kapālānāṁ kaṇā anantarā iti dharma eva [cūrṇamṛt, piṇḍamṛt, ghaṭamṛt, kapālamṛt, kaṇamṛt, iti kramaḥ,] dharmāntarasyakramaḥ । na lakṣaṇaṁ, nāpyavasthā । yathā– [yo yasya dharmasya samanantaro dharmaḥ sa tasya kramaḥ ।] katham? [piṇḍo ghaṭa upajāyata iti] piṇḍarūpāmṛtghaṭībhavatītyarthaḥ । abhedopacāreṇa [piṇḍo ghaṭa upajāyata] ityucyate । na punaḥ piṇḍo dharmo dharmontarātmatāṁ pratipadyate । piṇḍadharmavimardanena tadvirodhī tadanantaraṁ ghaṭākhyo dharma upajāyate ॥
dharmapariṇāmaśca dvividhaḥ, tulyapariṇāmaścātulyapariṇāmaśca । yathā piṇḍo ghaṭa upajāyata ityatulyapiṇḍasya, ghaṭādidharmairmṛdākhyo dharmī pariṇamate, saḥ atulyadharmapariṇāmaḥ । yāvacca ghaṭasya janmanaḥ prabhṛti ākapālāpatteḥ tāvatghaṭarūpeṇaiva pariṇamate mṛditi sa tulyadharmapariṇāmaḥ ।
tathā cittamapi niruddhavṛttikamekāgratāvasthāyāṁ tulyābhyāṁ dharmābhyāṁ śānteditapratyābhyāṁ pariṇamate, vyutthānanirodhābhyāṁ dharmābhyām atulyābhyāṁ pariṇate, tathā vyutthānavelāyāṁ śāntaghoramūḍhaiḥ pratyayairdharmairatulyaiḥ pariṇāmaṁ pratipadyate । so'yaṁ [dharmapariṇāmakrama] uktaḥ ॥
idānīṁ lakṣaṇapariṇāmakrama ucyate – [lakṣaṇapariṇāmakrama: ghaṭasyānāgatātlakṣaṇātvavartamānabhāvaḥ । tathā piṇḍasya] virodhidharmodaye [vartamānādatīta [bhāvaḥ] kramaḥ । nātītasyāsti kramaḥ ।] dharme hi vartamānalakṣaṇasya samanantaraṁ yallakṣaṇaṁ sa lakṣaṇakramaḥ । na cātītalakṣaṇasya samanantaraṁ lakṣaṇamasti ॥
[kasmāt? pūrvāparatāyāṁ hi satyāṁ samanantaratvam । sā cātītasya nāsti । tasmāt dvayoreva] anāgatavartamānayoḥ [lakṣaṇayoḥ kramaḥ ।] atītasya kramābhāvapratipādanena prayojanam [kṣaṇatatkramayoḥ saṁyamāt’] ityatra bhaviṣyati ॥
[tathā avasthāpariṇāmakramaḥ ghaṭasyābhinavasya prānte] avasānāvasthāyāṁ [purāṇātā dṛśyate । sā ca kṣaṇaparamparā'nupātinā krameṇābhyūhyamānā] pratikṣaṇamabhinavabhāvaparimardanena purāṇatā sañjaniṣyate । sā ca prānteṣu [parāṁ vyaktimāpāditā ।] madhye tu sūkṣmatayā na vibhāvyate । tena madhyāvasthāyāṁ sannapi kramo na lakṣyate । prāntakālābhivyaktiliṅgenānumāyiṣyate – yena iryapurāṇatāparāṁ vyaktamupaprāpitā so'yaṁ krama iti । na hi ghaṭe pariniṣpannamātre pratikṣaṇajanmā'pipurāṇatāgṛhyate ॥
tathā ca vadiṣyati – [“kṣaṇapratiyāgī pariṇāmāparāntaniryāhyaḥ kramaḥ”] iti । tasmāt dharmalakṣaṇakramābhyāmavasthākramasyānyatvāt [dharmalakṣaṇapariṇāmābhyāṁ viśiṣṭo'yaṁtṛtīyaḥ pariṇāmaḥ ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
Now the cause of the differentiation of transformation is stated — for when the differentiation is established, the <s>saṁyama</s> (concentrated meditation) on the three transformations becomes applicable for the practitioner. Because through certain distinguishing marks, knowledge regarding the past and the rest can be generated — and not otherwise — ['Difference in sequence is the cause of difference in transformation,']

body.text: ta ete kramā dharmadharmibhede sati pratilabdhasvarūpāḥ। dharmo'pi dharmī bhavatyanyadharmasvarūpāpekṣayeti। yadā tu paramārthato dharmiṇyabhedopacārastaddvāreṇa sa evābhidhīyate dharmastadā'yamekatvenaiva kramaḥ pratyavabhāsate।
body.translated_text: These sequences obtain their essential form when there is a distinction between property and property-bearer. A property too becomes a property-bearer in relation to the essential nature of another property. But when, in ultimate reality, non-difference with the property-bearer is figuratively adopted, and through that the same is designated as a property, then this is the unity —

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[ta ete kramādharmadharmibhede sati pratilabdhasvarūpāḥ ।] vivakṣitetudharmadharmiṇorabhede tatra kramabhedo na labhyate । [dharmo'pi dharmī bhavatyanyadharmāpekṣayā ।] guṇebhyo'nyatra dharmadharmitvaṁ nāma na vyavasthitam । mahadādīnāmapyaviśeṣāpekṣayā dharmitvam । aviśeṣāṇa ca viśeṣāpekṣayā, viśeṣāṇāṁ ca śāntoditāpekṣayeti । [yadā tu paramārthato dharmiṇyabhedopacāradvāreṇābhidhīyate dharmaḥ, tadā'yamekatvenaiva kramaḥ pratyavabhāsate ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['These sequences obtain their essential form when there is a distinction between property and property-bearer.'] When non-difference between property and property-bearer is intended, then the distinction of sequence is not obtained therein. ['A property too becomes a property-bearer in relation to another property.'] Except for the <s>guṇas</s> (fundamental qualities), elsewhere a property

body.text: cittasya dvaye dharmāḥ paridṛṣṭāścāparidṛṣṭāśca। tatra pratyayātmakāḥ paridṛṣṭā vastumātrātmakā aparidṛṣṭāḥ। te ca saptaiva bhavantyanumānena prāpitavastumātrasadbhāvāḥ । nirodhadharmasaṁskārāḥ pariṇāmo'tha jīvanam । ceṣṭā śaktiśca cittasya dharmā darśanavarjitāḥ ॥ iti ॥ 15 ॥
body.translated_text: The properties of <s>citta</s> (mind) are of two kinds: observed and unobserved. Among these, those consisting of cognitions (<s>pratyaya</s>) are the observed; those consisting of mere substance (<s>vastu-mātra</s>) are the unobserved. And these latter are only seven, their existence as mere substance being established through inference: the properties of cessation (<s>nirodha-dharma</s>), the latent impressions (<s>saṁskāras</s>), transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>),

body.text:
vivaraṇam
tatra [cittasya dvaye] dvividhāḥ [dharmāḥ paridṛṣṭāścāparidṛṣṭāśca] upalabdhāścānupalabdhāśca । ke te ityāha – [tatra pratyayātmakāḥ] rāgadveṣamohādayaḥ [paridṛṣṭāḥ । vastumātrāḥ] svarūpeṇa vidyamānāḥ kāryayoginaḥ [aparidṛṣṭāḥ । [te ca]] svaviṣayavṛttisadbhāvaiḥ [saptaiva bhavanti ।] te kathamavagamyanta iti? [anumānena prāpitavastumātrasadbhāvāḥ] kāryaliṅgenāvagatasadbhāvāḥ । svarūpeṇa tu nānīśvarairupalamyante । tataścaikaikatvenocyante ॥
[nirodhadharmasaṁskārāḥ । nirodhaḥ] uktaḥ । [dharmaḥ] iti, dharmādharmau । [saṁskārāḥ] vāsanārūpāḥ । [pariṇāmaḥ] uttamalakṣaṇaḥ । [atha jīvanam] iti, dharmādyapekṣayā sakalakaraṇavṛttiḥ prāṇalakṣaṇā yena cittadharmeṇa bhavati, sa [jīvanam] ityucyate । [ceṣṭā] vyāpāraḥ । [śaktiḥ] sāmarthyaṁ, [cittasya dharmāḥ । darśanavarjitāḥ] apratyakṣāḥ । [iti ete] sapta nirodhādayaścittadharmā aparidṛṣṭā ucyante ॥ 15 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
Therein, ['the properties of <s>citta</s> are of two kinds'] — twofold — ['properties, both observed and unobserved'] — both apprehended and unapprehended. What are they? He says — ['Among these, those consisting of cognitions'] — <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), <s>moha</s> (delusion), and the rest — ['are observed. Those consisting of mere substance'] — in their own nature,

body.text: ato yogina upāttasarvasādhanasya bubhutsitārthapratipattaye saṁyamasya viṣaya upakṣipyate –
body.translated_text: Therefore, for the <s>yogin</s> who has taken up all the means and wishes to attain the desired object, the object of <s>saṁyama</s> (concentrated meditation) is now introduced —

body.text: pariṇāmatrayasaṁyamādatītānāgatajñānam ॥ 16 ॥
body.translated_text: From <s>saṁyama</s> (concentrated meditation) on the three transformations arises knowledge of the past and future. || 16 ||

body.text: dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāpariṇāmeṣu saṁyamādyogināṁ bhavatyatītānāgatajñānam। dhāraṇādhyānasamādhitrayamekatra saṁyama uktaḥ। tena pariṇāmatrayaṁ sākṣātkriyamāṇamatītānāgatajñānaṁ teṣu saṁpādayati ॥ 16 ॥
body.translated_text: From <s>saṁyama</s> on the transformations of property (<s>dharma</s>), characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), and condition (<s>avasthā</s>), knowledge of the past and future arises for the <s>yogins</s>. Concentration (<s>dhāraṇā</s>), meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), and absorption (<s>samādhi</s>) — the triad directed at a single object — has been called <s>saṁyama</s>. Through that, the three transformations, when directly realized, produce knowledge of the past and future in those practitioners. || 16 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[ete] trayaḥ pariṇāmādharmalakṣaṇāvasthārūpāḥ [yoginaḥ upāttasarvasādhanasya] samāsāditayamādisakalasādhanasya sthiratarasaṁyamasya, atītānāgatapratyupasthita [bubhutsitārthapratipattaye saṁyamasyaviṣayaḥ upakṣipyate ।] trayo'pyeko viṣayaḥ saṁyamasya ॥
[pariṇāmatrayasaṁyamādatītānāgatajñānam ।] pariṇāmatraye tāvatsaṁyamaḥ karaṇīyaḥ, yāvatsamādhiprajñā''lokaḥ । sa cayadviṣaya upasthitaḥ, taṁ viṣayaṁ yathābhūtapratyakṣatāmāpādayati । sūkṣmaṁ vyavahitamatītamanāgataṁ viprakṛṣṭaṁ vā yamuddiśya prāpaṇābhiprāyeṇa sūkṣmādiṣu saṁyamaḥ kriyate, tadā so'rthovaśyatāṁ yogina upayāti । [dharmalakṣaṇāvasthāpariṇāmeṣu saṁyamātyogino bhavatyatītānāgatajñānam । dhāraṇādhyānasamādhitrayamekatra saṁyama uktaḥ । tena] saṁyamena [pariṇāmatrayaṁ sākṣātkriyamāṇamatītānāgatajñānaṁ teṣu] pariṇāmeṣu [sampādayati ।] sakalapadārthīnāṁ pariṇāmitvātteṣāṁ cātītādiyogātkālatrayayuktasamastapadārthaviṣayapariṇāmatrayasaṁyamena sarvaṁ pratyakṣībhavati । tathā pratikṣaṇapariṇāmadharmakamanavasthitaṁ viśvamokṣamāṇasyavairāgyaṁ jāyate ॥ 16 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
["These"] three transformations — in the forms of property (<s>dharma</s>), characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), and condition (<s>avasthā</s>) — ["for the <s>yogin</s> who has taken up all the means"] — who has acquired all the means beginning with <s>yama</s> (restraints) and who possesses a more stable <s>saṁyama</s> — ["the object of <s>saṁyama</s> is now introduced for the attainment of the desired object"] pertaining to past, future, and present. All three are a single object of <s>saṁyama</s>.
["From <s>saṁyama</s> on the three transformations arises knowledge of the past and future."] <s>Saṁyama</s> on the three transformations is to be performed to the extent of the light of <s>samādhi</s>-wisdom. That [wisdom], whatever object it has at hand, brings that object to the state of direct perception as it truly is. Whether subtle, concealed, past, future, or remote — when <s>saṁyama</s> is performed on the subtle and the like with the intention of reaching [the object] aimed at, then that object comes under the <s>yogin</s>'s control. ["From <s>saṁyama</s> on the transformations of property, characteristic, and condition, the <s>yogin</s> attains knowledge of the past and future. Concentration, meditation, and absorption — these three together on a single [object] have been called <s>saṁyama</s>. By that"] <s>saṁyama</s>, ["the three transformations, being directly realized, produce knowledge of the past and future in those"] transformations. Since all entities undergo transformation, and since they are connected with past and other [time periods], through <s>saṁyama</s> on the three transformations pertaining to all entities connected with the three times, everything becomes directly perceptible. Likewise, for one who perceives the universe as subject to transformation at every moment and as unstable, dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) arises. ॥ 16 ॥

body.text: śabdārtha​pratyayānāmitaretarādhyāsātsaṁkara​statpravibhāgasaṁyamātsarva​bhūtarutajñānam ॥ 17 ॥
body.translated_text: From the conflation (<s>saṁkara</s>) of word (<s>śabda</s>), meaning (<s>artha</s>), and cognition (<s>pratyaya</s>) due to mutual superimposition, and from <s>saṁyama</s> on their distinction, [arises] knowledge of the cries of all beings. ॥ 17 ॥

body.text: tatra vāgvarṇeṣvevārthavatī। śrotraṁ ca dhavanipariṇāmamātraviṣayam। padaṁ punarnādānusaṁhārabuddhinirgrāhyamiti।
body.translated_text: Therein, speech is meaningful only in phonemes (<s>varṇas</s>). And the ear has as its object merely the transformation of sound (<s>dhvani</s>). The word (<s>pada</s>), however, is grasped by the intellect through the synthesis of sounds (<s>nāda</s>).

body.text:
vivaraṇam
ayamanyaḥ saṁyamaviṣayaḥ upakṣipyate sarvaśabdārthapratipattyarthaḥ [śabdārthapratyayānāmitaretarādhyāsāt saṁkaraḥ tatpravibhāgasaṁyamāt sarvabhūtarutajñānaṁ] sampadyate । tatra kaḥ śabdaḥ, ko vā arthaḥ, pratyayo vā, saṁkaraśca kinnimittaḥ, kathaṁ ca teṣāṁ pravibhāgaḥ? iti ॥
[tatra] kiṁ vāguccāryaḥ śrotragrāhyaḥ (sa) śabdaḥ, utārthāntaraṁ, kiṁ vāgeva, tadvadatirito vā, iti tāvadvicāryate– vāktāvannaśabdaḥ । kasmāt? vāk [varṇeṣvevārthavatī ।] vāgiti varṇabhivyañjakamaṣṭasu sthāneṣu viṣaktamindriyaṁ varṇābhivyaktimātraprayojanopakṣayaṁ, na tāvadarthābhivyaktau śabdābhivyaktau vā vyāpāraṁ karoti ॥
tathā [śrotraṁ ca] na svayaṁ śabdaḥ, nāpi śabdaviṣayam । kasmāt? [dhvanipariṇāmamātraviṣayaṁ] hi tat । dhvaniriti sāmānyaṁ varṇāvarṇarūpam । tasya viśeṣaḥ pariṇāmaḥ akārādivarṇātmakaḥ, kākādivāśitātmakaśca mūḍhakaraṇavyaṅgyaḥ । tat dhvanipariṇāmamātraprakāśāvasānaṁ śrotraṁ nārthaśabdayorvyāpriyate ॥
nanu ca śrotragrāhya evaśabdaḥ । na—arthapratyāyakatvāt । arthaṁ yaḥ sampratyāyati sa śabdaḥ । kaḥ punarasau? [padam । tatpunarnādānusaṁhārabuddhinirgrāhyaṁ] nādānāṁ dhvanīnāṁ śrotraviṣayabhūtānāṁ pratyekaṁ pratyayinisaṁskāramādhāya nivartamānānām antyena dhvanināyāsamupasthāpitābuddhiḥ sā nādānusaṁhārabuddhiḥ prathamadhvanikramānusaṁhārāsāditasaṁskārasya pratyayinaścittasya jāyate, tayaikayā buddhyā ayaṁ nirgṛhyate । tatpadam । tacca pratyakṣatvādrūpādivannānyapramāṇāpekṣam ॥
nanu ca [“gakāraukāravisarjanīyāḥ”] itibhagavānupavarṣaḥ । tanna – avācakatvāt । katham? samudāyāsambhavāt । samudāyāsambhavaśca [ekasamayāsambhavitvāt ।] na hi gakāroccāraṇakāle aukāravisarjanīyau । nāpyaukāroccāraṇakāle gakāravisarjanīyau । nāpi visarjanīyapravṛttivelāyāmitarayoḥ samavasthānamitivarṇasamudāyāsambhavādavācakatvam ॥
yathaiva varṇānāṁ yugapatsamayānavasthānam, evaṁ saṁskārāṇāṁ smṛtīnāṁ ca tajjanitānāmayugapatkālatvādavācakatvam । smṛtyupayogārthatvācca saṁskārasyānubhūtaviṣaya evopayogāt, pratyākhyasya cāpūrvatvāt ॥
api ca saṁskārāṇāṁ vācakacābhyupagame, ['śabdādarthapratipatiḥ' 'pūrvīparībhūtaṁ bhāvamākhyātenācaṣṭe’ ‘dharmasya śabdamūlatvādaśabdamanapekṣyaṁ syāt’] iti prasiddhirapahūyeta ॥
athāpivarṇabhāvabhāvitvena smṛtisaṁskārayorapiśabdatvamupacaryeta । naitadapi—tadbhāvabhāvitvaṁ nāmatasminneva sati bhavatyasatyabhāva eva yatra, tatra syāt । (na ca) tacca varṇānāṁ śabdatve siddhe bhavet । lokastu śarīrādāvātmābhimānādavivekādatasminnapi tadbuddhiṁ karotīti na sarvatra vastunirṇaye heturbhavati ॥
api ca, vākśrotravyāpāra eva satyarthapratipattiriti tasyāvyabhicārāttadbhāvabhāvitveśabdatvaṁ prāpnoti । tasmādantyovarṇo na vācakaḥ, varṇatvāt ādyavarṇavat । tathā, tatsmṛtisaṁskārānavācakāḥ, smṛtisaṁskāratvāt, ādyavarṇasmṛtisaṁskāravat ॥
yadi cāntyo varṇaḥ pūrvavarṇajanitasaṁskārasahitaḥ vācaka ityucyate-- naitadevam । kasmāt? antyavarṇoccāraṇamātrādevārthapratyayaprasaṅgāt । katham? atītadivasoccaritagakārādivarṇāhitasaṁskāro hi samastaḥ śrotā । tatrāntyavārṇoccāraṇamātrādartha: pratīyeta । athāpi niyamārthamādyāvarṇoccāraṇamiti cet – na – pūrvavarṇānāṁ paścimavarṇenātulyakālatvātsāhāyakābhāve niyamānupapatiḥ ॥
tavāpivarṇānāṁpadavyañjakatveniyamārthaṁpūrvavarṇāucārayitavyāitidoṣaeveti, padavyañjakatvakalpanāto varṇānāmeva vācakatvaṁ yuktamiticet, na – varṇanāṁ buddhau svakīyasaṁskārādhānamātrābhyupagamāt । uccaritapradhvaṁsamānavarṇasaṁskāraparaṁ paropacitāyāṁ hi buddhau padaṁ nirbhāsate । etadeva hi varṇānāṁ padavyañjakatvam । na padaṁ prati dīpavatsākṣātpravartate ॥
na buddhau dhārmidvāreṇa saṁskārāṇāmekāśrayāvasthānādanyonyopakāryopakārakabhāvaḥ samīcīnataraḥ । iṣṭāniṣṭaviṣayopalabdhismṛtīcchādveṣādivat । na kadācidanyena varṇena pūrvavarṇānāṁ tadīyasmṛtisaṁskārāṇāṁ vā sambandha upakalpate ॥
atha mamāpiniyatakramavarṇasampādi saṅskāraparamparopacitabuddhyutpādakatyenaiva varṇānāṁ vācakatvamiti cet – na – abhyupetaparivarjanāt । yadi tāvadvarṇānekasaṁskāraviśiṣṭābuddhiḥ arthaviṣayavāpadaviṣayā vā? yadyarthaviṣayā, saiva śabdaḥ prāpnoti । arthapratyāyakatvāt । atha padaviṣayā, tathā'pi padādarthapratipattiriti bādhyeta ॥
tasmādekabuddhiviṣayo varṇavyatiriktaḥ śabdo'bhyupagantavyaḥ । tena pūrvavarṇajanitasaṁskārasahito'ntyo varṇaḥ, tatsmṛtiḥ, saṁskāro vā, na vācakaḥ । saṁskārasāhāyakāpekṣatvāt, buddhivat ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
Another object of <s>saṁyama</s> is now introduced, for the purpose of understanding the meanings of all words — ["from the conflation of word, meaning, and cognition due to mutual superimposition, and from <s>saṁyama</s> on their distinction, knowledge of the cries of all beings"] is attained. Therein: what is a word? What is a meaning? What is a cognition? What is the cause of their conflation? And how is their distinction [made]?
["Therein,"] is the word that which is uttered by the voice and grasped by the ear, or is it something different? Is it the voice itself, or something distinct from it? This is first examined. The voice, to begin with, is not the word. Why? Because speech ["is meaningful only in phonemes."] Speech (<s>vāk</s>) is the sense organ engaged at the eight places of articulation, whose function is exhausted merely in the manifestation of phonemes; it does not function in the manifestation of meaning or of the word [as a unit].
Similarly, ["the ear"] is not itself the word, nor does it have the word as its object. Why? Because ["it has as its object merely the transformation of sound."] 'Sound' (<s>dhvani</s>) is the universal, whether in the form of phonemes or non-phonemes. Its particular transformation is in the form of phonemes such as the vowel 'a' and the like, as well as in the form of inarticulate cries of crows and the like, manifested by a confused organ. The ear, whose scope ends with merely illuminating the transformation of sound, does not function with respect to meaning or the word [as a unit].
But surely the word is just what is grasped by the ear? No — because it causes the understanding of meaning. That which communicates the meaning is the word. And what is that? ["The word (<s>pada</s>). And that is grasped by the intellect through the synthesis of sounds"] — the sounds that are the objects of the ear, each depositing an impression in the cognizer and then ceasing, until the final sound produces the intellect that synthesizes the sounds. That synthesis-cognition arises in the cognizer's mind, which has acquired impressions through the sequential synthesis of sounds beginning with the first. By that single cognition, it [the meaning] is grasped. That is the word. And since it is perceptual, like form and the like, it does not depend on another means of valid knowledge.
But the venerable <s>Upavarṣa</s> said ["'the letters g, au, and <s>visarga</s> [constitute the word <s>gauḥ</s>]'"] — that is not so, because [phonemes alone] are non-significative. How? Because a composite [of phonemes] is impossible. And the impossibility of a composite is ["because they cannot occur simultaneously."] For at the time of pronouncing the phoneme 'g,' 'au' and <s>visarga</s> do not exist. Nor at the time of pronouncing 'au' do 'g' and <s>visarga</s> exist. Nor when <s>visarga</s> is being produced do the other two subsist. Thus, because a composite of phonemes is impossible, they are non-significative.
Just as phonemes do not subsist simultaneously, so too the impressions (<s>saṁskāras</s>) and the memories generated from them — being of non-simultaneous time — are non-significative. And because the impression serves only for the purpose of memory, being applicable only to what has already been experienced, while what is to be communicated (<s>pratyākhya</s>) is novel.
Moreover, if impressions were accepted as significative, well-known [principles such as] 'understanding of meaning comes from the word,' 'one expresses a present entity by a name that has previously existed,' and 'since <s>dharma</s> has its root in the word, what is not based on the word should be disregarded' — [all of these] would be undermined.
Even if wordhood were figuratively attributed to memory and impressions by virtue of their being produced by phonemes — this too is not valid. For 'being produced from that' means 'occurring when that exists but not occurring when that does not exist.' And that would be established only when the wordhood of phonemes is proven. But ordinary people, due to lack of discrimination — like the superimposition of self on the body — apply the notion [of wordhood] even where it does not belong. This does not serve as the basis for determining reality everywhere.
Moreover, the understanding of meaning occurs precisely through the operation of speech and ear — and because of the invariability of that [understanding], wordhood would follow from being produced by that. Therefore, the last phoneme is not significative, because it is a phoneme, like the first phoneme. Similarly, its memory and impressions are non-significative, because they are memory and impressions, like the memory and impressions of the first phoneme.
If it is said that the last phoneme, together with the impressions generated by the prior phonemes, is significative — this is not so. Why? Because the mere utterance of the last phoneme would then entail the cognition of meaning. How? For every hearer has impressions deposited by the phonemes 'g' and the rest uttered on a previous day, complete in their totality. Thus, from the mere utterance of the last phoneme, the meaning would be understood. If [one argues that] the prior phonemes must be uttered for the purpose of restriction — no, because since the prior phonemes are of different times from the subsequent phoneme, in the absence of cooperation [between them], the restriction is untenable.
Even on your view, the prior phonemes must be uttered for the purpose of restricting the phonemes' function of manifesting the word — if so, it is more appropriate to accept that the phonemes themselves are significative rather than postulating their word-manifesting function — [one might say]. No — because the phonemes are accepted as merely depositing their own impressions in the intellect. It is in the intellect, enriched by the impressions of the uttered and subsequently perishing phonemes, that the word appears. This alone is the phonemes' function of manifesting the word. They do not directly operate upon the word, as a lamp does [upon an object].
Rather, since the impressions reside in a single substratum — the intellect — through the property-bearer, their mutual relation of helper and helped is more correct, like the impressions [underlying] the perception of pleasant and unpleasant objects, memory, desire, aversion, and the like. At no time does one phoneme have a connection with the prior phonemes or with their memories and impressions.
If [one argues] that even on your view, the phonemes are significative precisely through the function of generating cognition in an intellect enriched by a succession of impressions produced by phonemes in a fixed sequence — no, because that would abandon what has been accepted. If the single cognition qualified by the impressions of all the phonemes has meaning as its object, or the word as its object — if it has meaning as its object, then that very [cognition] would be the word, because it causes the understanding of meaning. If it has the word as its object, then even so, [the principle that] 'the understanding of meaning comes from the word' would be violated.
Therefore, the word (<s>śabda</s>) is to be accepted as an object of a single cognition, distinct from the phonemes. Thus, the last phoneme together with the impressions generated by the prior phonemes, or its memory, or its impression, is not significative — because it depends on the assistance of impressions, like the [ordinary] cognition.

body.text: varṇā ekasamayāsaṁbhavitvātparasparaniranugrahātmānaste padamasaṁspṛśyānupasthāpyā''virbhūtā-stirobhūtāśceti pratyekamapadasvarūpā ucyante।
body.translated_text: The phonemes, because they cannot occur simultaneously, being of a nature that does not mutually support one another, without touching or presenting the word — having appeared and disappeared — are each individually said to be not of the nature of the word.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
evaṁ gate kathaṁ varṇānāmarthaviṣayaḥ padaviṣayo vāvyāpāro nāstītyāha – [varṇāḥ ekasamayāsambhavitvāt ।] ekakālāsambhavitvaṁ ca vācaḥ kramavartitvāt । ataḥ [parasparaniranugrahātmānaḥ] kasyacidabhisambandhasyābhāvāditerataranirupakārāḥ । [te padamanupasaṁspṛśyānupasthāpya] kañcana pade vyāpāramavidhāya [āvirbhutāśca tirobhūtāśca] vyastā vā samastā vā na padātmānamapāṅgavikṣepaṇāpi parāmṛśanti । [pratyekamapadasvarūpāḥ] yugapadanavasthānātasamudāyātmanā'pyapadasvarūpā eva । kimaṅgaḥ punaḥ pratyekamanarthakānāmavasthitānāmiti ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
This being so, he states why phonemes have no function with respect to meaning or the word — ["The phonemes, because they cannot occur simultaneously."] The impossibility of simultaneous occurrence is because speech proceeds sequentially. Therefore, ["being of a nature that does not mutually support one another"] — because of the absence of any connection, each is incapable of aiding the other. ["Without touching or presenting the word"] — without performing any function with respect to the word — ["having appeared and disappeared,"] whether taken individually or collectively, they do not touch the nature of the word even with a sidelong glance. ["Each individually, they are not of the nature of the word"] — since they do not subsist simultaneously, even collectively they are not of the nature of the word. How much less, then, are they [significative] individually, being each meaningless even when subsisting?

body.text: varṇaḥ punarekaikaḥ padātmā sarvābhidhānaśaktipracitaḥsahakārivarṇāntara-pratiyogitvādvaiśvarūpyamivā''pannaḥ pūrvaścottareṇottaraśca pūrveṇa viśeṣe'vasthāpita ityevaṁ bahavo varṇāḥ kramānurodhino'rthasaṁketenāvacchinnā iyanta ete sarvābhidhānaśaktiparivṛtā gakāraukāravisarjanīyāḥ sāsnādimantamarthaṁ dyotayantīti।
body.translated_text: Each individual phoneme, however, is of the nature of the word, replete with the power of all designations. Having assumed, as it were, a multiform nature because it serves as a correlate of other cooperating phonemes — the preceding being determined to a specific [word] by the succeeding, and the succeeding by the preceding — thus many phonemes, conforming to a [particular] sequence, delimited by convention with regard to meaning, being just so many, encompassed by the power of all designations — [these phonemes,] 'g,' 'au,' and <s>visarga</s>, illuminate the meaning possessing dewlap and the like [i.e., a cow].

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[varṇaḥ punarekaikaḥ sarvābhidhānaśaktipracitaḥ ।] abhidhīyateyaiḥ tānyabhidhānānipadāni, teṣāṁ sarveṣāmabhidhānānāṁ padānāmabhivyañjikābhiḥ śakti.ābhiḥ pracitaḥ, arāṇāmekaika iva nābhau । tadyathā—gakāraḥ govargāgnigaganādisarvapadābhidyotanasāmarthyapracitaḥ ॥
[sahakārivarṇāntarapratiyogitvāt ।] yathā gauriti gakaraikāravisarjanīyasahakārisavyapekṣaḥ agniritīkārapratiyogī । tasmāda [nekavarṇā] ntaropādhisambandhātpratipadaṁ [vaiśvarūpyamivāpannaḥ । uttaraśravarṇaḥ pūrveṇa viśeṣe] padaviśeṣapradyotane [avasthāpitaḥ । pūrvaiścottareṇa,] madhyamo'pi pūrvottarābhyām ॥
[evaṁ bahavo varṇāḥ kramānurodhinaḥ] viśiṣṭakramam, ānupūrvīm anurudhyamānāḥ ॥
[arthasaṅketena] amī asminnarthe etatkramāvalambinaḥ iyanta iti saṅketaḥ samayaḥ, tena athaisaṅketena [avacchinnāḥ ॥]
varṇasaṅketadvāreṇapadaṁ saṅketyate । varṇāvyabhicaritacāritram asādhāraṇavarṇakramāpekṣitasaṅketasamayaṁ hi padam । varṇasaṅketa eva tasya saṅketaḥ । [iyanta ete varṇāḥ sarvābhidhānaśaktiparicyutāḥ] viśiṣṭasāsnādimadarthapratipādakāsādhāraṇapadāvabhāsanavyāpāraparatvādeva aparapadāntarapratipādakaśaktyantarebhyaḥ paricyutā: nivṛttā: itaretaraviśeṣaviniyogaparavaśāveśādudāsīnapadāntaraprakāśanaśaktayaḥ [gakāraukāravisarjanīyāḥ sāsnādimantamathaimavadyotayanti] padamabhivyañjayantaḥ ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
["Each individual phoneme is replete with the power of all designations."] Designations (<s>abhidhāna</s>) are words (<s>pada</s>) by which [meanings] are expressed; replete with the powers that manifest all those designations — all words — like each spoke [replete with its function] in a hub. For example, the phoneme 'g' is replete with the capacity to illuminate all words such as <s>go</s> (cow), <s>varga</s> (class), <s>agni</s> (fire), <s>gagana</s> (sky), and so on.
["Because it serves as a correlate of other cooperating phonemes."] Just as in <s>gauḥ</s>, [the phoneme 'g'] requires the cooperation of 'au' and <s>visarga</s>; in <s>agniḥ</s>, 'i' serves as the correlate. Therefore, due to the connection with the limiting condition of multiple other phonemes, [it has] assumed, as it were, ["a multiform nature for each word. The subsequent phoneme is determined by the preceding to the specific"] illumination of a specific word. ["And the preceding by the subsequent;"] the middle one too by both preceding and subsequent.
["Thus many phonemes, conforming to a [particular] sequence"] — following a specific sequence, an order.
["Delimited by convention with regard to meaning"] — the convention (<s>saṅketa</s>), the agreement, is that 'these [phonemes] in this number, adhering to this sequence, [denote] this meaning.' Delimited by that convention.
The word is conventionalized through the convention of phonemes. For the word has a character inseparable from its phonemes, depending on the convention tied to a distinctive sequence of phonemes. The convention of the phonemes is itself its convention. ["These phonemes, in just so many, having departed from the power of all designations"] — because of being exclusively devoted to the function of manifesting a specific word that designates a specific meaning possessing dewlap and the like — having departed, i.e., having turned away from their powers to designate other words — their powers to illuminate other words having become dormant due to being compelled by the specific assignment of each to each — ["'g,' 'au,' and <s>visarga</s> illuminate the meaning possessing dewlap and the like,"] manifesting the word.

body.text: tadeteṣāmarthasaṁketenāvacchinnānāmupasaṁhṛtadhvanikramāṇāṁ ya eko buddhinirbhāsastatpadaṁ vācakaṁ vācyasya saṁketyate। tadekaṁ padamekabuddhiviṣaya ekaprayatnākṣiptamabhāgamakramamavarṇaṁ bauddhamantyavarṇapratyayavyāpāropasthāpitaṁ paratra pratipipādayiṣayā varṇairevābhidhīyamānaiḥ śrūyamāṇaiśca śrotṛbhiranādivāgvyavahāravāsanānuviddhayā lokabuddhyā siddhavatsaṁpratipattyā pratīyate।
body.translated_text: Of these [phonemes], delimited by convention with regard to meaning, whose sequence of sounds has been synthesized — that single appearance in the intellect is the word (<s>pada</s>), which is the significator, and which is conventionalized for the significatum. That single word, the object of a single cognition, projected by a single effort, partless, non-sequential, without phonemes, mental in nature, presented through the function of the cognition of the last phoneme — is understood by others, with the intention of communicating it, through the very phonemes being uttered and heard by the listeners, by means of a worldly cognition permeated by the latent impression of beginningless linguistic usage, as though it were directly established.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tadeṣāmarthasaṅketenāvacchinnānām] abhihitena nyāyamārgeṇa [anugṛhītadhvanikramāṇāṁ] viśiṣṭānuparipaṭisamāyoginām itthaṁkramaviśeṣakramalabdhajanmanāṁ varṇānāṁ sambandhaḥ [ya eko budvinirbhāsaḥ] buddhernirbhāsaḥ [tat padaṁ] bhūmiḥ (bhūmiṣumeva) bhūmikeva [vācakaṁ vācyasya] na varṇāḥ । varṇadvoraṇa tu [saṅketyate ॥]
[tat padamekam] ekamapi, yadvastu sāvayavaṁ ghaṭādi tadanekabuddhiviṣayaṁ dṛṣṭaṁ, na tu padaṁ tathā । tat [ekabuddhiviṣayaṁ] sarvale.okapratyakṣam । varṇāḥ punaranekatvādayugapatkālajanmānaḥ ekabuddhiviṣayatāṁ na samupāśnunuvate । yasvevamekabudvinirgrāhyamanumānena nirācikīrṣati, tasya pratyakṣāvirodhinī pratijñā syāt ॥
evam [ekaprayatnākṣiptaṁ] varṇakramajanmapratyupanītasaṁskāranimittabuddhiparipākābhisamakṣayā paścimabuddhau jhaṭiti parisphuritam, [avibhāgam] avayavaśyūnyam, ata eva [akramamavarṇātmakamantyavarṇapratyayavyāpāropasthāpitam] ādyavarṇavyāpāraparamparānugṛhītapaścimavarṇagrahaṇamāttrapratyudbhāsitam ॥
[paratra] parabuddhipratipipādayiṣayā [varṇairevābhidhīyamānaiḥ] abhidhātṛbhiḥ, [śrūyamāṇaiśca śrotṛbhiḥ, anādivāgvyavahāravāsanānuviddhayā lokabuddhayā siddhavat saṁpratipatyā pratīyate ।] (nāpi) anādisaṁsāracakramaṇḍale parivartate । śabdādevārthapratipatipūrvako vyavahāraḥ, tadvāsanāvāsitāyā lokadhiyā siddhavat pratīyata iti, laukikānāṁ sammugdhākārapravartitavyavahāramātracaritaprayojanānāṁ ātmanīva pade vipratipattiḥ ।
tasmāt [padaṁ] varṇavyatiriktam, ekabuddhinirgrāhyatve sati pratyāyakatvāt, pradīpavat । arthapratipattau ca kāraṇatvāt, pradīpavat, buddhivacca । na varṇāḥ padam, ekena kartrā krameṇa prayujyamānatvāt, karaṇatvācca, vāsīvṛkṣādānādivat ॥
atra [kaścit] āha—
[varṇā vā dhvanayo vāpi spheṭaṁ na padavākyayoḥ ।]
[vyañjanti vyañjakatvena yathā dīpaprabhādayaḥ ॥]
[sattvāt ghaṭādivacceti sādhanāni yathāruci ।]
[laukikavyatirekeṇa kalpite'rthe bhavanti hi ॥]
[nārthasya vācakaḥ sphoṭo varṇebhyo vyatirekataḥ ।]
[ghaṭādivanna dṛṣṭena virodho dharmyasiddhitaḥ ॥]
[pratiṣedhettu yo varṇāstajjñānānantarodbhavāt ।]
[dṛṣṭabādho bhavettasya śaśicandraniṣedhavat ॥]
[varṇotthā vā'rthadhīrekṣā tajjñānānantaroddhavā ।]
[yādṛśī sā tadutthā hi dhūmāderiva vahnidhīḥ ॥]
[dīpavadvā gakārādergavādeḥ pratipādaka: ।]
[dhruvaṁ pratīyamānatvāt tatpūrvapratipādanāt ॥ ”] iti ।
atrocyate—varṇā vādhvanayo vā'pispheṭaṁ na padavākyayoḥ iti, padaṁ vākyaṁ vā svatastāvanna prasiddham । tatrāsativarṇavyatirikte pade vākye vā, padavākyayoḥ sphoṭaṁ na vyañjayantīti kathaṁ cetasvināṁ vacanāvakāśaḥ syāt । evaṁ ca sati, uddiśyapadavākyayoḥ sphoṭaṁ pratiṣedhatāpadaṁ vākyaṁ cābhyupagataṁ bhavet ॥
athāpiparābhaprāyeṇocyeta, tathā'pi siddhasādhyatā । na parasya padavākyayoranyaḥ sphoṭovidyate, yaḥ pratiṣidhyeta । padavākye eva hitasya sphoṭaḥ ॥
athāpi brūyāt – arthāvacchedakāviśiṣṭakramopaniveśino varṇāḥ padaṁ vākyaṁ ca pratiṣidhyate iti । tacca na yuktam, svato virodhāt ॥
athā'pi brūyāt – varṇavyatiriktaṁ padaṁ vākyaṁ vā pratiṣidhyate iti । tathā'pi vyatiriktamuddiśya tasya vyañjanapratiṣedhādvyatiriktapadavākyābhyupagamaḥ prasaktaḥ ॥
athā'pi parakalpitapadavākyapratiṣedhaḥ, evamapi vyañjakatvādityasiddho hetuḥ । katham? svātmavyātiriktasya vā padasya vyañjakatvaṁ, avyatiriktasya vā vyañjakatvaṁ, arthasya vā vyañjakatvaṁ varṇānāmiti trayīvikalpanā । yadi vyatiriktasya vyañjakatvaṁ, tadā svato'siddhaḥsyāt ॥
athāvyātiriktasya, tathā'pi parasyāsiddhaḥ । kiṁca, vyañjakatvāccavyatiriktasyaiva vyañjakatvaṁ, nāvyātiriktasya, pradīpāderiva । anyavyañjanārthaṁ hi vyañjakaḥ pradīpādirupādīyate, na svātmavyañjanāya । svātmavyaktyartho cedupādāsyate, januṣā'ndhasyāpi vyajyeta ॥
atha vyatiriktavyañjakatve siddhe, padasya vyañjakā bhaveyuḥ, arthasya vā । tatrānekasādhyaṁ yathā śibikodvahanādi, tat anyatamena na śakyam anuṣṭhātu, evamanyatamena varṇānāmarthasya pratipādanamanekasādhyatvādaśakyamiti pratipāditam ॥
na ca kūpakhānakanyāyenāpi kaṁcitkañcidvyaṅgye saṁskāramādhāyavarṇānivartante iti śakyaṁ vaktum । abhidheyasyaikabuddhiviṣayatvāt ॥
yathā ca sugatakṛtānte pradhvaṁsamānaṁ vijñānamutpatsyamānasya vijñānasya saṁskāramādhātumaparyāptaṁ, sthitasya dharmiṇaḥ kasyacidabhāvāt । evamanyonyasaṁbandhābhāvādayugapatsamayajanmanāṁ varṇānāṁ pūrvasya pūrvasya vinaśyata uttarasyottarasya copajaniṣyamāṇasya balādhānānupapattiriti nārthasya vyañjakā varṇāḥ ॥
pariśeṣātpadasyaiva vyatiriktasyābhivyañjitāraḥ iti sthitadharmaḥ । asmākaṁ tu sthiterdharmiṇiścetasi pūrvapūrvavarṇapratyupasthitasaṁskāraparamparāparipākaviśārade paścimavarṇajanmavelāyāṁ niravayavamekabuddhinirgrāhyabuddhinirbhasātmakajhaṭitisamunmiṣatīti na saṁskārādhānāsāmarthyadoṣaprasaṅgaḥ ॥
kiṁca, yadyapi varṇāḥ svabuddhiṁ vyañjayanti । sā buddhirarthapratītiṁ prati karaṇabhūtaivābhivyajyate, na tu phalaṁ prati varṇāḥ karaṇatvena vyāpriyante । karaṇabhūtabuddhyutpādanopakṣayatvāt । buddhereva hi phalaṁ prati vyāpāraḥ । yasya hi phalaṁ prati vyāpāraḥ tatpramāṇaṁ, sa śabdaḥ । tataśca arthapratītiṁ prati kāraṇabhūtabuddhivyavahitatvānnavarṇānāṁ vācakatvam । paramparayātupadaṁpratyupāyatvaṁ na varṇānāṁ pratiṣidhyate ॥
tasmādevamayaṁ ślokaḥ paṭhitavyaḥ–
[varṇā vā dhvanayo vā'pi bhinnamevārthamātmanaḥ ॥]
[vyañjanti vyañjakatvena yathā dīpaprabhādayaḥ ॥]
tathā, ghaṭādīnāmapyarthontarapratyupasthānamātratvamabhyupagamyata eva । ghaṭādayo hi darśanamātreṇa pacanāharaṇadhāraṇādiyogyatābuddhim anyadvā kiṁcit upasthāpayantyeva । tathā varṇānāṁ pāramparyeṇa ātmavyatiriktapadapratyupasthāpakatvaṁ sattvātghaṭādivadiṣyata eveti tulyametadapi ॥
[satvādghaṭādivacceti sādhanāni yathāruci ।]
[laukikavyatirekeṇa kalpite'rthe bhavanti hi ॥]
sarvathājātirvā buddhirvā bhavatu, yato vā kutaścit uccāritapradhvastavarṇānasaṁbhavino varṇavyatiriktāt arthapratipattiḥ, sasphoṭaḥ । sa ca avaśyaṁ varṇāsaṁbhāvitvātkāryasyābhyupagamanīyaḥ । tathā ca—
[‘nārthasya vācakaḥ sphoṭo varṇebhyo vyatirekataḥ']
iti bruvato'bhyupagamavirodhaḥ syāt । api ca, [varṇebhyo vyatirekataḥ] ityanyatarā siddhaḥ । svato vyatirekesyāsiddhatvāt ॥
kiṁca, nāmākhyātopasargānipātapadajāticatuṣṭayamabhyupagacchatā jātivyañjakaṁ varṇavyatiriktam anyadabhyupagantavyam । na varṇāḥ padajātimabhivyañjitumutsahante । varṇā hi varṇajātimabhivyañjayanti । na cāvayaveṣu bhinnakālajanmavināśeṣvavayavijātivyañjanamupapadyate । vyavasthiteṣvapi nāmatāvadavayaveṣu na pāṇipādādayaḥ śarīrādṛte śarīratvamabhivyañjayanti । kiṁ punaranavasthiteṣu ॥
kiṁca, aśvaḥ ayātamayātamakṣaḥ bhavati, tena mama vāyurvāyuḥ, ityādiṣu tulyasvarūpeṣu nāmatvākhyātatve parasparaviruddhajātīyenaika eva varṇo'bhivyanakti ॥
yadi vā aśvaḥ iti nāmajātyā abhivyañjakāḥ akāraśakāravakārākāravisarjanīyāḥ ākhyātajātyabhivyañjakebhyo bhinnā bhaveyuḥ, tadā upapadyate bhinnānāṁ bhinnajātyabhivyañjakatvam । tadekatvenopapadyate ॥
yadyapi arthaprakaraṇaśabdāntarasannidhānādibhiḥ idaṁ nāma idamākhyātam itiparikalpyeta, tathā'pi nāmākhyātajātyabhivyaktim arthaprakaraṇādibhireka eva varṇo na śaknoti kartum । na hi brāhmaṇa eva brāhmaṇatvaṁ kṣatriyatvaṁ cābhivyanakti ॥
tasmāt bhinnā akārāḥ śakārāvakārādayaśca bahava eṣitavyāḥ । evaṁ gośabdādayo'pi bhinnā eva । tathā gośabdatvamaśvaśabdavaṁ ca siddham । evaṁ matvamātvamitvamītvaṁ ca siddham । evaṁ ca sati akārādayo varṇā atvādīnyeva sāmānyānyabhivyañjayanti । nāśvādīnnāmākhyātajātibhedānita ॥
tasmāt varṇavyatiriktaṁ padatvasāmānyābhivyañjakaṁ padamabhyupagantavyam । evaṁ ca satyeṣa śloka evaṁ paṭhitavya:-
[pratiṣedhettu yaḥ sphoṭaṁ varṇadhīsamanantaram ।]
[dṛṣṭabādho bhavettasya śaśicandraniṣedhavat ॥]
[vaṇotthā'varṇadhīreṣā tajjñānānantarodbhavā ॥] iti ॥
karaṇabuddhivyavahitatvādanantarodbhavatvamasiddham । pāramparyoṇa cetsiddhasādhyatā । dhūmasyāpi na vahnidhiyaṁ prati kāraṇatvam । dhūmadhiyaḥ kāraṇatvāt । dhūmādīnāṁ pāramparyavatvarṇādīnāmapi pāramparyeṇopakārakatvamiṣyata ityuktam ॥
tasmādayamapi śleka evaṁ paṭhitavyaḥ---
[varṇotthā nārthadhīreṣā tajjñānānantarodbhavā ।]
[yedṛśī sā tadutthānadhūmodariva vahnidhīḥ ॥]
na ca dīpavatsannipatyagakāraukārausāsnādimadarthavyañjakau । arthavyaktikālānavasthānādanaye.ārdṛṣṭo vyabhicāra: visarjanīyaviṣaye'pi samunnīyate niravasthānādi । varṇānārthavyaktisamānakālāvasthāyinaḥ, pradīpastu vyaṅgyakālena tulyakālāvasthānaḥ kāraṇatvaṁ pratilabhate ॥
tasmādayamapyevaṁ ślekaḥ paṭhitavyaḥ–
[dīpavadvā gakārādirgavādīnāmavācaka: ।]
[dhruvaṁ pratīyamānatvāttatpūrve pratipādanāt ॥]
pramāṇaṁ cātra bhavati – arthasya na vācakāḥ, nāpyarthaṁ pratipramāṇaṁ varṇāḥ, sākṣātsaṅketāpekṣatvāt, aṅkapratimādivat । yathā śatādyaṅkāviṣṇupratimāśca saṅketāpekṣāgamamevāvadyotayanti । na viṣṇuśatādyarthaṁ prati pramāṇatvamupayānti ॥
yattu nāpekṣate saṅketaṁ, tatpramāṇam, yathā vākyaṁ, dīpādijātyantaraṁ ca । na tathā varṇā iti pratimāvadeṣā aprāmāṇyamāpātatam । tathā, varṇā arthapratipādakamātmavyatiriktamabhivyañjayanti, sākṣātsaṅketāpekṣatvāt, aṅkaviṣṇupratimādivat । sphoṭaḥ tatsaṅketena sākṣādapekṣate ityavādiṣma ॥
tasmādevam anekayuktiparivārapratyupānītabalādhānaṁ kaḥ sphoṭam apākartuṁ śaknoti ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>vivaraṇam</s> (sub-commentary):
[Of these phonemes] delimited by conventional association with meaning, [assisted in their sequence of sounds] by the method explained above — that is, of <s>varṇas</s> (phonemes) possessing a particular sequential arrangement and whose birth is obtained through a specific order — the connection [which is a single flash in cognition] — that flash of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) — [that is the <s>pada</s> (word)], the ground (as it were, the very platform) — [it is the signifier of the signified], not the <s>varṇas</s> (phonemes). Rather, through the opening provided by phonemes, [convention is established].
[That <s>pada</s> is one] — even though it is one, whatever entity has parts, such as a pot, is seen to be the object of multiple cognitions, but the <s>pada</s> (word) is not like that. That [is the object of a single cognition], evident to all people through direct perception. The <s>varṇas</s> (phonemes), however, being multiple and born at non-simultaneous times, do not attain the status of being objects of a single cognition. One who wishes to deny through inference that which is graspable by a single cognition — his thesis would contradict direct perception.
Thus, [produced by a single effort] — through the ripening of cognition caused by the <s>saṁskāras</s> (latent impressions) brought about by the sequential birth of phonemes, in the final cognition it flashes forth instantaneously by direct apprehension — [without division], devoid of parts, and therefore [without sequence, not consisting of phonemes, brought into presence by the operation of the cognition of the final phoneme] — that is, made to shine forth merely through the apprehension of the last phoneme, which is assisted by the chain of operations beginning with the first phoneme.
[In communicating to others], with the desire to convey meaning to another's intellect, [through the very phonemes being uttered] by speakers [and heard by listeners, it is cognized as if it were an established entity, through the worldly cognition pervaded by the <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression) of beginningless verbal convention.] It revolves in the cycle of beginningless <s>saṁsāra</s> (transmigration). Practical activity is preceded by the understanding of meaning from words alone, and through worldly cognition imbued with those <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions), it is cognized as if established — thus, for ordinary people whose purposes are served merely by conduct driven by confused appearances, there is no disagreement about the <s>pada</s> (word) as there is about the self.
Therefore, [the <s>pada</s> (word)] is distinct from <s>varṇas</s> (phonemes), because it is a means of conveying meaning while being graspable by a single cognition, like a lamp. And because it is a cause in the apprehension of meaning, like a lamp, and like cognition itself. The <s>varṇas</s> (phonemes) are not the <s>pada</s> (word), because they are employed sequentially by a single agent, and because they serve as instruments, like an axe, the fetching of wood, and so forth.
Here [someone] objects —
[Neither <s>varṇas</s> (phonemes) nor <s>dhvanis</s> (sounds) manifest the <s>sphoṭa</s> (the meaning-bearing linguistic unit) of words and sentences,]
[as manifestors, just as lamplight and the like.]
[The proofs that it exists like a pot, etc., are merely according to one's fancy,]
[for they apply only to an entity fabricated in contradiction to ordinary experience.]
[<s>Sphoṭa</s> is not the signifier of meaning, being distinct from phonemes;]
[there is contradiction with what is observed, due to the unestablished nature of the subject (<s>dharmin</s>), as in the case of a pot, etc.]
[But one who would deny the phonemes — since cognition arises immediately after the cognition of them —]
[his position would be contradicted by observation, like denying the moon by calling it '<s>candra</s>'.]
[The cognition of meaning arises from phonemes — or rather, this cognition arising immediately after the knowledge of them —]
[whatever its nature, it is indeed produced from them, just as the cognition of fire arises from smoke and the like.]
[Or, like a lamp, the <s>ga</s>-sound and others are expounders of 'cow' and the like,]
[certainly, because they are invariably cognized, and because they have been previously established as conveying that meaning.]
To this we reply — As for "neither <s>varṇas</s> nor <s>dhvanis</s> manifest the <s>sphoṭa</s> of words and sentences" — the <s>pada</s> (word) or <s>vākya</s> (sentence) is not by itself well-established independently. In the absence of a <s>pada</s> or <s>vākya</s> distinct from <s>varṇas</s>, how could there be any occasion for the statement by intelligent persons that they do not manifest the <s>sphoṭa</s> of words and sentences? This being so, the one who denies the <s>sphoṭa</s> of words and sentences, having made them the subject of discourse, would have thereby accepted the <s>pada</s> and <s>vākya</s>.
Even if it were said with the opponent's own intent, even so there would be the fallacy of proving what is already established. For the opponent, no <s>sphoṭa</s> other than words and sentences exists that could be denied. The <s>sphoṭa</s> is indeed nothing other than <s>pada</s> and <s>vākya</s> themselves.
Even if one were to say — "What is denied is that phonemes arranged in a specific sequence that delimits meaning constitute a <s>pada</s> or <s>vākya</s>" — that too is not proper, because it is self-contradictory.
Even if one were to say — "What is denied is a <s>pada</s> or <s>vākya</s> distinct from <s>varṇas</s>" — even so, since the denial of manifestation is directed at something distinct, the acceptance of a distinct <s>pada</s> and <s>vākya</s> would follow.
Even if it is a denial of the <s>pada</s> and <s>vākya</s> as conceived by the opponent, even then the reason "because of being a manifestor" is unestablished. How so? There is a triple alternative: either the manifestation is of a <s>pada</s> distinct from its own nature, or of one not distinct, or of the meaning by the <s>varṇas</s>. If it is manifestation of the distinct, then it would be unestablished from the proponent's own standpoint.
If of the non-distinct, even so it would be unestablished for the opponent. Moreover, the property of being a manifestor belongs only to what is distinct, not to the non-distinct, as in the case of a lamp and the like. For a manifestor like a lamp is employed for the purpose of manifesting something other than itself, not for manifesting itself. If it were employed for the purpose of manifesting itself, then even one blind from birth would perceive it.
Now, if the manifestation of something distinct is established, then they could be manifestors of the <s>pada</s> (word), or of the meaning. Regarding this — just as a task requiring multiple agents, such as carrying a palanquin, cannot be accomplished by any single one of them, so too it has been demonstrated that the conveyance of meaning by any single <s>varṇa</s> (phoneme) is impossible because it requires multiple agents.
Nor can it be said that, as in the method of well-digging, each phoneme deposits some <s>saṁskāra</s> (impression) upon the object to be manifested and then ceases — because the object to be signified is the object of a single cognition.
Just as in the doctrine established by <s>Sugata</s> (the Buddha), a consciousness that is being destroyed is incapable of depositing a <s>saṁskāra</s> (impression) upon a consciousness yet to arise, because there is no enduring substratum — similarly, due to the absence of mutual connection among <s>varṇas</s> (phonemes) born at non-simultaneous moments, the impossibility of the earlier ones, which are perishing, depositing strength upon the later ones yet to arise follows — therefore <s>varṇas</s> are not the manifestors of meaning.
By elimination, it is the established principle that they are manifestors of the <s>pada</s> (word) alone, which is distinct from them. For us, however, since there is an enduring substratum — namely the mind — which is proficient through the ripening of the chain of <s>saṁskāras</s> (impressions) deposited by each preceding phoneme, at the moment of the birth of the final phoneme, [the <s>sphoṭa</s>] flashes forth instantaneously as partless, graspable by a single cognition, and having the nature of a flash of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) — therefore there is no occasion for the fault of inability to deposit impressions.
Moreover, even though <s>varṇas</s> (phonemes) manifest their own cognition, that cognition is manifested precisely as an instrument with respect to the apprehension of meaning — but the <s>varṇas</s> do not operate as instruments with respect to the final result. This is because they are exhausted in producing the cognition that serves as the instrument. For it is <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) alone that operates toward the final result. That which operates toward the result is the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) — that is <s>śabda</s> (the word). Therefore, because the <s>varṇas</s> are separated from meaning-apprehension by the intermediary cognition that serves as the instrument, they do not possess the status of signifiers. However, the indirect instrumental role of the <s>varṇas</s> with respect to the <s>pada</s> (word) through a chain of causation is not denied.
Therefore this verse should be read thus —
[<s>Varṇas</s> (phonemes) or <s>dhvanis</s> (sounds) manifest an object distinct from themselves,]
[as manifestors, just as lamplight and the like.]
Likewise, it is indeed accepted that even pots and the like serve merely to bring about the cognition of something else. For pots and the like, merely by being seen, bring about the cognition of suitability for cooking, carrying, holding, and so forth, or some other thing. Similarly, it is accepted that <s>varṇas</s> (phonemes), through a chain of causation, serve to bring about the cognition of the <s>pada</s> (word) which is distinct from themselves — because they exist, just like a pot and the like — this argument too is equivalent.
[The proofs that it exists like a pot, etc., are merely according to one's fancy;]
[for they apply only to an entity fabricated in contradiction to ordinary experience.]
In every case, whether it be a universal or a cognition, from whatever source the apprehension of meaning arises — from something distinct from <s>varṇas</s> (phonemes) that have been uttered and have perished, which meaning-apprehension is impossible for the phonemes themselves — that is <s>sphoṭa</s>. And it must necessarily be accepted, because the effect is impossible for the <s>varṇas</s>. Accordingly —
One who says ['<s>Sphoṭa</s> is not the signifier of meaning, being distinct from phonemes'] — there would be a contradiction with his own acceptance. Moreover, ["being distinct from phonemes"] — one of the two alternatives is itself unestablished, because the distinctness from one's own position is unestablished.
Furthermore, one who accepts the fourfold classification of word-types — <s>nāman</s> (noun), <s>ākhyāta</s> (verb), <s>upasarga</s> (prefix), and <s>nipāta</s> (particle) — must accept something distinct from <s>varṇas</s> that manifests word-class universals. <s>Varṇas</s> (phonemes) are not capable of manifesting word-class universals. For <s>varṇas</s> manifest only phoneme-universals. And the manifestation of the whole's universal by parts that are born and destroyed at different times is not logically possible. Even among stable parts — for instance, hands, feet, and the like do not manifest 'body-ness' without the body. How much less so among unstable ones?
Moreover, in cases like <s>aśvaḥ</s> ('horse', a noun) and <s>ayātam ayātam akṣaḥ</s> ('the die has not gone, has not gone' — a verbal usage), or <s>mama vāyuḥ vāyuḥ</s> ('my breath, O <s>Vāyu</s>!'), where the forms are identical, a single <s>varṇa</s> would have to manifest mutually contradictory universals — noun-ness and verb-ness.
If, alternatively, the phonemes <s>a</s>, <s>śa</s>, <s>va</s>, <s>a</s>, and <s>visarjanīya</s> in <s>aśvaḥ</s> were different as manifestors of noun-universals from the manifestors of verb-universals, then the manifestation of different universals by different entities would be logically possible. But that is possible only if they are one and the same [phonemes manifesting different universals, which leads to contradiction].
Even if one were to determine "this is a noun, this is a verb" through meaning, context, proximity of other words, and so forth, even so, a single <s>varṇa</s> cannot, with the help of meaning and context, accomplish the manifestation of both noun-universals and verb-universals. For a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> does not manifest both <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-hood and <s>kṣatriya</s>-hood.
Therefore, multiple distinct <s>a</s>-sounds, <s>śa</s>-sounds, <s>va</s>-sounds, and so forth must be posited. Likewise, words such as <s>go</s>-śabda ('cow-word') and others are also distinct from each other. Thus 'cow-word-ness' and 'horse-word-ness' are established. Similarly, <s>a</s>-ness, <s>ā</s>-ness, <s>i</s>-ness, <s>ī</s>-ness, and so on are established. This being so, phonemes like <s>a</s> and others manifest only universals such as <s>a</s>-ness and the like — not word-class distinctions like 'horse' etc., or noun and verb universals.
Therefore, a <s>pada</s> (word) distinct from <s>varṇas</s> (phonemes), which manifests the universal of word-hood, must be accepted. This being so, this verse should be read thus:
[But one who would deny <s>sphoṭa</s> — since cognition arises immediately after the cognition of phonemes —]
[his position would be contradicted by observation, like denying the moon by calling it '<s>candra</s>'.]
[This cognition arises from phonemes — a cognition not of phonemes — arising immediately after the knowledge of them.]
The claim of immediate origination is unestablished, because the cognition that serves as instrument intervenes. If it is said to be established through a chain of causation, then it proves what is already established. Even smoke is not a direct cause of the cognition of fire — because the cognition of smoke is the cause. Just as smoke and the like operate through a chain of causation, so too it is accepted that <s>varṇas</s> and the like assist through a chain — this has already been stated.
Therefore this verse too should be read thus —
[The cognition of meaning does not arise from phonemes; this cognition arising immediately after the knowledge of them —]
[whatever its nature, it does not arise from them, just as the cognition of fire does not arise directly from smoke.]
Nor do the <s>ga</s>-sound and <s>au</s>-sound, like a lamp, jointly manifest an object possessing dewlap and the like. Because they do not persist at the time of meaning-manifestation — the deviation observed in other cases is extended to the case of <s>visarjanīya</s> as well, due to the same lack of persistence. <s>Varṇas</s> (phonemes) do not persist contemporaneously with the manifestation of meaning, whereas a lamp persists contemporaneously with the object to be illuminated and thereby obtains the status of a cause.
Therefore this verse too should be read thus —
[Like a lamp, the <s>ga</s>-sound and others are not signifiers of 'cow' and the like,]
[certainly, because they are cognized and because they convey that meaning previously.]
And here there is a further proof — <s>varṇas</s> (phonemes) are not signifiers of meaning, nor are they a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) for meaning, because they depend on direct convention, like numerical figures and images. Just as numerical figures like '100' and images of <s>Viṣṇu</s> merely illuminate meaning dependent on convention and tradition — they do not attain the status of being <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) with respect to the meaning of <s>Viṣṇu</s> or the number one hundred.
That which does not depend on convention is a <s>pramāṇa</s>, such as a sentence, or a lamp, or other such things of a different kind. <s>Varṇas</s> (phonemes) are not like that — hence, like images, they have arrived at the status of non-<s>pramāṇa</s>. Similarly, <s>varṇas</s> manifest something distinct from themselves that conveys meaning, because they depend on direct convention, like numerical figures and images of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. We have stated that <s>sphoṭa</s> directly depends on that convention.
Therefore, who can set aside the <s>sphoṭa</s>, which is supported by the strength of multiple lines of reasoning marshalled in its favor?

body.text: tasya saṁketabuddhitaḥ pravibhāga etāvatāmevaṁ jātīyako'nusaṁhāra ekasyārthasya vācaka iti। saṁketastu padapadārthayoritaretarādhyāsarūpaḥ smṛtyātmako yo'yaṁ śabdaḥ so'yamartho yo'yamarthaḥ so'yaṁ śabda iti। evamitaretarādhyāsarūpaḥ saṁketo bhavatīti। evamete śabdārthapratyayā itaretarādhyāsātsaṁkīrṇā gauriti śabdo gaurityartho gauriti jñānam। ya eṣāṁ pravibhāgajñaḥ sa sarvavit।
body.translated_text: The discrimination of that [word] arises from conventional understanding (<s>saṅketa-buddhi</s>): 'the combination of this many [phonemes] of this kind is the signifier of this one meaning.' Convention (<s>saṅketa</s>) has the nature of mutual superimposition (<s>itaretarādhyāsa</s>) between word and word-meaning, having the nature of memory (<s>smṛti</s>) — 'this word is this meaning, this meaning is this word.' Thus, convention has the form of mutual superimposition. In this way, word (<s>śabda</s>), meaning (<s>artha</s>), and cognition (<s>pratyaya</s>) are conflated through mutual superimposition: 'cow' is the word, 'cow' is the meaning, 'cow' is the cognition. One who knows the discrimination among these is omniscient.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
tadevaṁgate bhāṣyamidānīmucyate – [tasya padasya saṅgītabudvitaḥ pravibhāgaḥ ।] śabdārthajñānavyatibhinnarūpā hi saṅketabuddhiḥ । tasyāḥ sakāśātpadasya [pravibhāgaḥ] karaṇīya: ॥
saṅketarūpaṁ darśayati – [etāvatāṁ] varṇānām [evaṁjātīyake'nusaṁhāra etasyāthaisya vācakaḥ] iti । yathā ayamaṅkaḥ śataṁsahasre, viṣṇureṣāpratimā iti ca ॥
[saṁketastu padapadārthayoritaretarādhyāsarūpaḥ smṛtyātmā,] na pramāṇabhūtaḥ । yathāvipṇureṣā pratimā, eṣa eva caturbhuja iti, tathā pratyaya ubhayamidam ubhayaṁ nu pratyaya ityanyonyādhyastarūpāviṣṇupratimāpratyayāḥ ॥
tathā [yo'yaṁśabdaḥ so'yamarthaḥ, yo'yamarthaḥ saśabdaḥ, yaścapratyayaḥ so'rthaḥ śabdaśceti, evamitaretarādhyāsarūpaḥ saṁketo bhavati । evameteśabdārthapratyayā itaretarādhyāsātsaṁkīrṇāḥ ।] tadyathā [gauriti śabdo, gaurityartho, gaurīti jñānam] iti ॥
[ya eṣāṁ] śabdārthapratyayānāṁ [pravibhāgajñaḥ, sa sarvajñaḥ ।] kasmāt? aśakyatvātpravibhāgajñānasya । na hyasarvajñaḥ śaknoti pravibhāgena tānavagantum ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
This being so, the <s>bhāṣya</s> is now explained — ['The discrimination of that word arises from conventional understanding.'] For conventional understanding (<s>saṅketa-buddhi</s>) has a form distinct from word, meaning, and cognition. From that [conventional understanding], the [discrimination] of the word is to be made.
He shows the nature of convention — ['of this many'] phonemes (<s>varṇa</s>) ['in such a combination, this is the signifier of this meaning.'] Just as 'this numeral stands for a hundred or a thousand,' and 'this is an image of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.'
['Convention has the nature of mutual superimposition between word and word-meaning, having the nature of memory'] — it is not a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>). Just as 'this is an image of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, this is the four-armed one himself,' so too the cognition: 'this is both, and both are indeed the cognition' — thus the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-image-cognitions have mutually superimposed forms.
Likewise, ['this word is this meaning, this meaning is this word, and the cognition is both meaning and word — thus convention has the form of mutual superimposition. Thus these — word, meaning, and cognition — are conflated through mutual superimposition.'] For example: ['"cow" is the word, "cow" is the meaning, "cow" is the cognition.']
['One who knows the discrimination among these'] — among word, meaning, and cognition — ['is omniscient.'] Why? Because the knowledge of discrimination is impossible [for anyone else]. For one who is not omniscient cannot comprehend them through discrimination.

body.text: sarvapadeṣu cāsti vākyaśaktirvṛkṣa ityukte'stīti gamyate। na sattāṁ padārtho vyabhicaratīti। tathā na hyasādhanā kriyā'stīti। tathāca pacatītyukte sarvakārakāṇāmākṣepo niyamārtho'nuvādaḥ kartṛkaraṇakarmaṇāṁ caitrāgnitaṇḍulānāmiti। dṛṣṭaṁ ca vākyārthe padaracanaṁ śrotriyaśchando'dhīte, jīvati prāṇāndhārayati। tatra vākye padārthābhivyaktistataḥ padaṁ pravibhajya vyākaraṇīyaṁ kriyāvācakaṁ vā kārakavācakaṁ vā। anyathā bhavatyaśvo'jāpaya ityevamādiṣu nāmākhyātasārūpyādanirjñātaṁ kathaṁ kriyāyāṁ kārake vā vyākriyeteti।
body.translated_text: And in all words there is the power of the sentence. When the word 'tree' (<s>vṛkṣa</s>) is spoken, 'it exists' is understood. An object does not deviate from existence. Likewise, there is no action without an instrument of accomplishment. Thus, when 'cooks' (<s>pacati</s>) is spoken, all <s>kārakas</s> (case-relations) are implied — the restrictive restatement is for the purpose of specifying the agent, instrument, and object as <s>Caitra</s>, fire, and rice. And it is observed that word-composition serves sentence-meaning: 'the learned one studies the Vedas' (<s>śrotriyaś chando'dhīte</s>), 'he lives' means 'he sustains the vital breaths.' There, in the sentence, the word-meanings are made manifest; then the word is to be analyzed grammatically as either denoting an action or denoting a case-relation. Otherwise, in cases like '<s>aśvo'jāpaya</s>' and similar constructions, due to the formal similarity of nouns and verbs, how could what is undiscriminated be analyzed as pertaining to an action or to a case-relation?

vivaraṇam
[sarvapadeṣu cāsti vākyaśaktiḥ । vṛkṣa ityukte astīti gamyate । na sattāṁ padārtho vyayabhicaratīti ॥ ]
kimarthametaducyate? iha sarvabhūtarutajñānopāyaḥ pratipipādayiṣitaḥ । sarvabhūtarutaṁ ca vākyārthaviṣayameva, na padārthaviṣayam । padānāṁ kevalānāṁ varṇānāmivānarthakatvāt, saṁvyavahārābhāvācca । yathaiva varṇanāṁ varṇāntarābhisamīkṣayāpadāvadyotanaprayojanavattvam, evaṁ padānāmapipadāntarāpekṣayāvākyopasthāpanopāyatvam । evaṁ sativākyasyaiva prāmāṇyaṁ, kevalapadaprayoge'rthāpratīteḥ ॥ kiṁca, kevalaṁ padamapramāṇaṁ, tāvatā nirṇayābhāvāt, ekaikavarṇavat । nāpi padaṁ vācakam, saṅketārthāpekṣatvāt, śatādyaṅkavat । nāmākhyāte kevalena vācake, kevalāprayogāt, upasargavat । yatrāpi kevalaṁ padaṁ prayuyukṣite tatrāpyavaśyam, asti tiṣṭhati devadatta ityādi padaṁ buddhau viparivartata iti na kevalāprayogasiddhiḥ ॥

pralambate, paryāgacchati, abhyāgacchati, ityādiṣu upasargakarmapravacanīyānāṁ na kaścidarthaḥ । tathā abhimanāyate, sumanāyate, durmanāyate, ityādiṣu ca upasargāṇāṁ dyotakatvaṁ siddham । tathā, pratiṣṭhate, adhīta ityādiṣvayupasargāṇāṁ dyotakatvameva na vācakatvamiti । [tathā na hyasāvanā kriyā asti । ] kevalakarmaprayoge kimapi sādhanaṁ dravryaṁ guṇo vāvagamyate ॥ kiṁca, prakṛtipratyayānāmanavasthitāvadhikatvātvyabhicārādavācakatvam । tadyathā-daridrātiḥkeṣāñciddravyamātra eva paṭhyate । daridraśabdastu nipātopasargasthānīyaḥ punarāgacchati, drati, nidrāti, daridrāti, iti । tatra kā prakṛtiriti vaktavyam । kiṁ (drāktridaṁ) drā, iti, kiṁvā daridreti । keṣāñcittu daridretyetāvatpaṭhyate । tathā drāśabdo'pi pṛthagāmnāyate ॥ evamasti sakāramātraṁ paṭhanti । vīticapratyayekāramāgamaṁ kurvanti ।

kecittu sahakāreṇa paṭhitvā (aviti) vīticapratyaye lopamakārasyakurvanti । tatra kā prakṛtiriti vaktavyam । na nirjñāyate । prakṛtyavadhaupratyayāvadhauvāprakṛtipratyayārthau śakyau vivektum ॥ kvacidupasargo'pi ‘asaṁgrāmayataśūra' ityādiṣuprakṛtyekadeśatāmāpannaḥ । tathā, ataternaḥ, aḥ, asyāpatyamiḥ, iyān, adhunā, ityādikaḥ prakṛtyarthabhāgam asatyāṁ prakṛtau brūyāt । agnicit, somasut, bhidā, chidā, atho, kati, amā, paca, paṭha, ityādiṣu pratyayārthamasatipratyayekībrūyāt ॥ evamādiṣu lakṣitāpacārāṇāṁ prakṛtipratyayanāṁ kaḥ śaknuyādarthavattvaṁ kalpayitum । atrabhavatu nānyatreti nārdhajaratīyaṁ labhyam । uddālakapuṣpabhañjikāpāraṁ na puṣpapracāyikā, ityatra kaḥ pūrvapadottarapadārthaḥ? prajñaḥ, saṁjña, ityādiṣu pratyanvayo'pi nāstīti kasya ko'rthaḥ? iti ॥ ṛṣabho, vṛṣabho, vṛṣaḥ, udakam, udakumbhaḥ, kṣīrodaḥ, yāvo, yāvakaḥ, kūpaḥ, sūpaḥ, yūpaḥ, ityādiṣu kasya ko'rtho iti vaktavyam ।

dadhyaśāna, madhvatra, ityādiṣu, kimavadhi kiṁ padaṁ vācakam? ॥ tasmātsarvatra dṛṣṭāpacārāṇāṁ varṇaprakṛtipratyayapadānām anarthakānāmadṛṣṭāpacāraniravayavavākyopāyatvameva । tāni niḥsandhibandhanānniravayavātmithyābhūtavarṇapadadhvaniṣkṛtacitrībhāvādvākyādapoddhṛtya vyākaraṇīyāni ॥ tāni ca vākyasyānavayavabhūtāni, upāyatvādvyākyāvayavavadavabhāsamānāni, yāvatphalam asattvātśatādyaṅkavadevamithyābhūtāni, anuccāryamāṇavākyāvadyotanārthakaraṇasannipāte viśeṣeṇopādāyaparihīyamāṇāni, svakīyakramaniṣpattivinivṛttikālādibhedavicitratayā vākyātmānaṁ kramavantamiva, niṣpadyamānamiva, nivartamānamava, drāghīyāṁsamiva, kālavantamiva,bhedavantamiva, vicitrākāratāmāpādayanti ॥ evaṁ ca sati, yaducyate śaśaviṣāṇādapoddhṛtyakharaviṣāṇasya, kiṁtaditi etadalīkaṁ, yathaiva mṛgatṛṣṇikāteyamalīkamapi satyādūṣarādapoddhiyate, yathā ca sthāṇoḥ puruṣaḥ, puruṣācca sthāṇuḥ, śuktikātaśca rajatamapoddhriyate, yathaiva ca mṛgatoyādayo yathābhūteṣu rādivastupratipattihetavaḥ, tathā varṇapadaprakṛtipratyayāyathābhūtavākyārthapratipātakāraṇetatpratipattau cāpoddhriyante ॥

kvacidarthaprāptamapoddhriyate, yathā mṛgatoyādikam । kañcittu prayojanatvena vivakṣitaṁ, yathāśatādisaṅkhyātaḥ śatādyaṅkāpoddhāraḥ kriyate, yathā ca lipyakṣarāṇi saḍretāpekṣatvātakṛtasamayarūpāṇī akārādivarṇādapoddhriyante । atha ca sarvāṇyatāniyathābhūtārthapratipādanopāyatvaṁ pratipadyante । na ca tāvatā mithyātvameṣāṁ nāsti । tathāpadādanyapi ॥ yo hi prakṛttipratyayapadavarṇānāṁ saṁketadvareṇānyopāyānāṁ mithyābhūtalipyakṣarakalpānāṁ svayamapisvasaṁketena vākyārthapratipatyupāyamanekadhānirmāyavyavaharamāṇaḥ satyatvameṣāṁ manyate, nūnamasāvabhre candrāsaṁdidṛśyamāṇaḥ candradarśanopāyabhūtamabhramapi candratvena pratipadyata iti ॥ yathā ca vākyameva satyaṁ, tathā vākyārthasyaiva satyatvaṁ, na padāni, padārthā vā kevalāḥ, satyatvamupayānti । sarvamevasāmānyāviśeṣātmakaṁ vastu । na hi sāmānyavyāvṛtto viśeṣa:, viśeṣavyāvṛttaṁ vā sāmānyamasti ।

gauriyukte astīti gamyate । tena kevalapadaprayoge'pyantarnītapadāntarārtho vākyārtha eva pratīyate, na kevalapadārtha: ॥ evaṁ ca sati
[padārthā gamayantyetaṁ pratyekaṁ saṁśaye sati ॥ ]
[sāmasye nirṇayotpadātsthāṇurmūrdhasthakākavat ॥ ]
ityasiddhamasmākam । na hi sthāṇurnāma vākyārthaḥ pṛthakpadārthavenaprasiddhaḥ । yasmātvṛkṣaḥ sansthāṇuḥ sanmūrdhā sankākaḥ sanmūrdhani sthāṇoḥ ityantarnītapratīyamānapadāntarāsthānapekṣayāṁ sthāṇumūrdhatthakākabuddhirevanasyāt । satsvapi teṣu sadbuddhisamutpateḥ satpadārthāntarabuddhiravaśyaṁbhāvinī ॥ tasmātvākyārtha eva pratyekamapi saṁśayātmaka iti kutaḥ padārthāḥ pratyekamasanto vākyārthaṁ gamayeyuḥ । tasmādevamayaṁ ślokaḥ paṭhitavyaḥ---
[vākyaṁ tu gamayatyenaṁ pratyekaṁ saṁśaye sati ॥ ]
[sāmasye nirṇayotpādātsthāṇumūrdhasthakākavat ॥ ]
evam---
[vākyenaivocyate tasmādvākyārtho'nyairarūpaṇāt ।

]
[ante cāstīti bodhācca vṛkṣeṇaiva ca vṛkṣatā ॥ ]
yattu palāśaśabdena vṛkṣatā nocyate iti, sasyamevametat । na hi palāśavākyena vṛkṣavākyārthasyābhidhānam । bhinnaviṣayatvāt । anyo hi palāśavākyārthaiḥ palāśo'sti tiṣṭhatīti vā । anyovṛkṣavākyārthaḥ । yadā ca padavaṇīnāṁ niravayavānāṁ pṛthagastitvamabhyupagamyate, tadā niravayavavarṇapadopādānaṁ vākyaṁ sāvayavaṁ kathamavakalpeta । na hi kriyākāśādibhiḥ sāvayavaṁ śakyamārabdhum । atha sāvayavatvamabhyupāyiṣyate, tatrāpi doṣa eva prasajyeta ॥ [sadbhāvepadavarṇānāṁ bhedīyaḥ paramāṇuvat । ]
[sarvā bhāvastataśceti seyaṁ bālavibhīṣikā ॥ ]
paramāṇūnāṁ satvādidharmamātratvābhyupagamatvivṛtyasuṣṭhubhāṣāmahe – seyaṁ vṛddhavibhīṣaketi ॥ atha kevalapadaprayege padārthāntarasyāpi saṁgrahātkimanekapadaprayogeṇeti cet, [niyamārtho'nuvādaḥ kartṛkaraṇakarmaṇāṁ caitrāgnitaṇḍulānāṁ] kriyāvavacanātsādhanāni vidyanta ityarthaprāptānāṁ niyamaḥ, caitra eva kartā, agninaiva karaṇena, taṇḍulāneva karma, iti ॥

api ca niyamārthamātre(mantare)ṇānuvādaḥ । [dṛṣṭaṁ ca vākyārthe kevalaṁ padam । ] yathā [śrotriyaḥ chando'dhīte] iti । sādhanavacanameva kevalaśrotriyapadaṁ chando'dhīte ityasminkriyāsādhanasamudāye vartate । tathā [jīvati iti] kriyāpadamākṣiptakriyāsādhanaviśeṣam । (chatraṁ) chando'dhīte, prāṇāndhārayati, [iti vākye] śretriyo jīvatīti ca [padārthābhivyaktiḥ । ] sarvathā sarvapadeṣu vākyaśaktirityaṅgīkṛtapadāntarārthānyeva sarvāṇi padānī ityetaducyate ॥ tasmāt kvacit kriyāpadenaiva sādhanamupakṣiptam । kvacicca nāmapadenaiva kriyā abhihitā । tasmātteṣāṁ vibhāgo duravabodha iti । [tataḥ] vākyāt [pravibhajya] [padaṁ] [vyākaraṇīyaṁ kriyāvācakaṁ vā] jīvatītyādi, [kārakavācakaṁ vā] śrotriyaḥ kṣatriyaḥ ityādi ॥ [anyathā] yadi vākyātpravibhajyanavyākriyeta, tadā tato bhavatya [śvo'jāpayaḥ ityevamādiṣu nāmākhyātasārūpyādanirjñātaṁ kathaṁ kriyāyāṁ kārake vā vyā[kri]priyeta ।

] bhavati nidhehīti sarvanāmnaḥ śatrantasya vāsaptamyāṁ rūpam । bhavati bījādaṅkura ityākhyātam ॥ aśvaścaratīti jātivācakam । aścastvaṁ grāmamityaśvayaterluṅantasya madhyamapuruṣaikavacanāntasya prayogaḥ । ajāpayaḥ pīyatāmitināmapadam । ajāpayastvaṁ rājānamiti japatorṇijantasya laṅmadhyamapuruṣaikavacanāntasya rūpam ॥

body.text: teṣāṁ śabdārthapratyayānāṁ pravibhāgaḥ। tadyathā śvetate prāsāda iti kriyārthaḥ, śvetaḥ prāsāda iti kārakārthaḥ śabdaḥ, kriyākārakātmā tadarthaḥ pratyayaśca। kasmāt। so'yamityabhisaṁbandhādekākāra eva pratyayaḥ saṁketa iti।
body.translated_text: The distinction among those — word (<s>śabda</s>), meaning (<s>artha</s>), and cognition (<s>pratyaya</s>). For example, 'the palace shines white' (<s>śvetate prāsādaḥ</s>) — the word conveys the meaning of action; 'the white palace' (<s>śvetaḥ prāsādaḥ</s>) — the word conveys the meaning of the agent. The meaning, consisting of action and agent, and the cognition [are distinct]. Why? Because through the relation 'this is that same thing,' though appearing as a single form,

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[teṣāṁ śabdārthapratyayānāṁ] saṅkaraṁ pradarśya [vibhāgaḥ] pratipādyate– [śvetate prāsāda iti kriyārthaḥ । śvetaḥ prāsāda iti kārakārthaḥ ।] kriyākārakatvādvastunaḥ śvetateśreta iti ca kriyārthe na cakārakārthena cābhidhānam ॥
yathā śabdaḥ [kriyākārakātmā,] yaḥ śvetaḥ sa śvetateyaḥ śvetatesaśvetaḥ ityevaṁ kriyākārakāvyatiriktaḥ ekaḥ śabdaḥ, tathā arthaḥ tadvācyaḥ kriyākārakātmā । tathā tadviṣayaḥ pratyayaḥ kriyākārakātmā । tathā arthaḥ śabdapratyayātmā । pratyayo'pi śabdārthātmā । kasmāt? [so'yamityabhisambandhāt ।] yo'rthaḥ sa śabdaḥ, yaḥ śabdaḥ so'rthaḥ pratyayaśca, yaḥ pratyayaḥ so'rthaḥ śabdaśca, ityevam [abhedākārapratyayaḥ] smṛtyātmā [saṅketaḥ] iti । evaṁ saṅkararūpataḥ pravibhāgaḥ kāryaḥ ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['Of those — word, meaning, and cognition'] — having demonstrated their conflation, ['their distinction'] is taught — ['"the palace shines white" conveys the meaning of action. "The white palace" conveys the meaning of the agent.'] Because the object has the nature of both action and agent, 'shines white' and 'white' — the action

body.text: yastu śveto'rthaḥ sa śabdapratyayayorālambanībhūtaḥ। sa hi svābhiravasthābhirvikriyamāṇo na śabdasahagato na buddhisahagataḥ। evaṁ śabda evaṁ pratyayo netaretarasahagata ityanyathā śabdo'nyathā'rtho'nyathā pratyaya iti vibhāgaḥ। evaṁ tatpravibhāgasaṁyamādyoginaḥ sarvabhūtarutajñānaṁ saṁpadyata iti ॥ 17 ॥
body.translated_text: But the white object (<s>artha</s>) serves as the support for both word and cognition. For that object, undergoing modification through its own states, is neither accompanied by the word nor accompanied by the cognition. Thus, the word is one thing, the meaning is another, the cognition is yet another — they do not accompany each other. Thus the word is different, the meaning is different, the

body.text:
vivaraṇam
katham? [yastu śveto'rthaḥ] śvetaguṇaḥ prāsādādirarthaḥ [sa śabdapratyayayoḥ ālambanībhūtaḥ] vācyatvenaviṣayatvena ca । [sa hi svābhiravasthābhiḥ] navapurāṇatvādibhiḥ [vikrayamāṇaḥ naśabdasahagato na] api [buddhisahagataḥ ।] śabdapratyayābhāve'pi bhāvāt । [evaṁ pratyayaḥ] naśabdasahagatonāpyarthasahagataḥ । itarābhāve'pi bhāvāt । tathāśabdaḥapi, arthapratyayavyabhicārāt [iti] evam anyathā arthaḥ anyathāśabdaḥ anyathāpratyayaḥ itipravibhāgaḥ । [evaṁ ca [tat] pravibhāgasaṁyamāt] idaṁ varṇaiḥ saṅketitaiḥ vākyātmakam ‘abhivyajyamānam’ 'ayamartha: pratyayaśvāyam' iti pravibhāgena saṁyamātpravibhaktapadapadārthapratyayānāṁ svena rūpeṇa sākṣātkaraṇāt [yoginaḥ sarvabhūtarutajñānaṁ sampadyata ॥ 17 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
How? ["But the white object"] — the object such as a palace that possesses the quality of whiteness — ["serves as the support for both word and cognition"] — by being the denotatum and the object respectively. ["For that, undergoing modification through its own states"] — such as being new or old — ["is not accompanied by the word, nor"] even ["accompanied by the cognition,"] because it exists even in the absence of word and cognition. ["Likewise, the cognition"] is not accompanied by the word nor by the object, because it exists even in the absence of the others. Similarly, the word too, because of its deviation from object and cognition. ["Thus"] — the object is one thing, the word is another, the cognition is yet another — this is the distinction. ["And thus, from <s>saṁyama</s> (concentrated meditation) on that distinction"] — this sentence-form manifested through conventionally established phonemes, [distinguished as] 'this is the meaning, this is the cognition' — from <s>saṁyama</s> through such distinction, through the direct realization of the distinguished word, meaning, and cognition in their own forms, ["knowledge of the cries of all beings arises for the <s>yogin</s>."] ॥ 17 ॥

body.text: saṁskārasākṣātkaraṇātpūrvajātijñānam ॥ 18 ॥
body.translated_text: From direct perception of <s>saṁskāras</s> (latent impressions) arises knowledge of previous births. ॥ 18 ॥

body.text: dvaye khalvamī saṁskārāḥ smṛtikleśahetavo vāsanārūpā vipākahetavo dharmādharmarūpāḥ। te pūrvabhavābhisaṁskṛtāḥ pariṇāmaceṣṭānirodhaśaktijīvanadharmavadaparidṛṣṭāścittadharmāḥ। teṣu saṁyamaḥ saṁskārasākṣātkriyāyai samarthaḥ। na ca deśakālanimittānubhavairvinā teṣāmasti sākṣātkaraṇam। taditthaṁ saṁskārasākṣātkaraṇātpūrvajātijñānaputpadyate yoginaḥ। paratrāpyevameva saṁskārasākṣātkaraṇātparajāti-saṁvedanam।
body.translated_text: These <s>saṁskāras</s> are indeed of two kinds: those in the form of <s>vāsanās</s> (latent dispositions) that cause memory and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), and those in the form of <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit) that cause fruition (<s>vipāka</s>). They are properties of the mind (<s>citta</s>), fashioned by previous existences, imperceptible like the properties of transformation, activity, cessation, capacity, and vitality. <s>Saṁyama</s> on them is capable of producing direct perception of the <s>saṁskāras</s>. And their direct perception is not possible without [knowledge of their associated] place, time, cause, and experience. Thus, from direct perception of <s>saṁskāras</s>, knowledge of previous births arises for the <s>yogin</s>. In the case of others too, similarly, from direct perception of <s>saṁskāras</s> comes knowledge of their [past] births.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
