[saṁskārasākṣātkaraṇāt pūrvajātijñānam । dvaye khalvamī saṁskārāḥ vāsanā'bhidhānāḥ] paridṛṣṭāḥ aparidṛṣṭāśca smṛtikleśahetavaḥ । paridṛṣṭāḥ (ubhaye'pi) kleśakarmavipākānubhavanirvartitāḥ [cittadharmāḥ dharmādharmarūpāḥ] dharmādharmanimittāḥ [pūrvabhavābhisaṁskṛtāḥ] (tā) atikrāntānantajanmaniṣpāditāḥ [pariṇāmaceṣṭānirodhaśaktijīvanadharmāḥ] pūrvavyākhyātāḥ [aparidṛṣṭāḥ । teṣu] dvayeṣu saṁskāreṣu [saṁyamaḥ] kriyamāṇaḥ [saṁskārasākṣātkriyāyai samarthaḥ] bhavati ॥
te ca deśakālanimittānubhavaviśiṣṭatayā nirvartitatvātsākṣātkaraṇakāle'pi deśādiviśoṣaṇāviśiṣṭā eva pratyakṣībhavanti। tasmāt [na ca] (te) [deśakālanimittānubhavairvinā teṣāmasti sākṣātkaraṇam ॥]
[taditthaṁ saṁskārasākṣātkaraṇāt pūrvajātijñānamutpadyate yoginaḥ । paratrāpi prāṇiṣu evameva] yeṣāṁ jātiṁ bubhutsate tadīyasaṁskāreṣu saṁyamāt [[saṁskārasākṣātkaraṇāt]] tatpūrvajātijñānamutpadyate ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
["From direct perception of <s>saṁskāras</s> arises knowledge of previous births. These <s>saṁskāras</s>, called <s>vāsanās</s>,"] are of two kinds — perceived and unperceived — ["causing memory and <s>kleśas</s>."] The perceived ones (both types) are produced by the experience of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), <s>karma</s> (action), and <s>vipāka</s> (fruition); ["they are properties of the mind, in the form of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>,"] caused by merit and demerit, ["fashioned by previous existences"] — produced across innumerable past births. ["Having the properties of transformation, activity, cessation, capacity, and vitality"] — as previously explained — ["they are imperceptible. On those"] two kinds of <s>saṁskāras</s>, ["<s>saṁyama</s>,"] when performed, ["is capable of producing direct perception of the <s>saṁskāras</s>."]
And since they were produced as qualified by specific place, time, cause, and experience, even at the time of direct perception they become perceptible as qualified by those very specificities of place and so on. Therefore, ["their direct perception is not possible without place, time, cause, and experience."]
["Thus, from direct perception of <s>saṁskāras</s>, knowledge of previous births arises for the <s>yogin</s>. In the case of others too"] — among other living beings — similarly, through <s>saṁyama</s> on the <s>saṁskāras</s> of those whose births one wishes to know, ["from direct perception of <s>saṁskāras</s>,"] knowledge of their previous births arises.

body.text: atredamākhyānaṁ śrūyate – bhagavato jaigīṣavyasya saṁskārasākṣātkaraṇāddaśasu mahāsargeṣu janmapariṇāmakramamanupaśyato vivekajaṁ jñānaṁ prādurabhūt। atha bhagavānāvaṭyastanudharastamuvāca – daśasu mahāsargeṣu bhavyatvādanabhibhūtabuddhisattvena tvayā narakatiryaggarbhasaṁbhavaṁ duḥkhaṁ saṁpaśyatā devamanuṣyeṣu punaḥpunarutpadyamānena sukhaduḥkhayoḥ kimadhikamupalabdhamiti। bhagavantamāvaṭyaṁ jaigīṣavya uvāca – daśasu mahāsargeṣu bhavyatvādanabhibhūtabuddhisattvena mayā narakatiryagbhavaṁ duḥkhaṁ saṁpaśyatā devamanuṣyeṣu punaḥpunarutpadyamānena yatkiṁcidanubhūtaṁ tatsarvaṁ duḥkhameva pratyavaimi। bhagavānāvaṭya uvāca - yadidamāyuṣmataḥ pradhānavaśitvamanuttamaṁ ca saṁtoṣasukhaṁ kimidamapi duḥkhapakṣe nikṣiptamiti। bhagavāñjaigīṣavya uvāca – viṣayasukhāpekṣayaivedamanuttamaṁ saṁtoṣasukhamuktam। kaivalyasukhāpekṣayā duḥkhameva। buddhisattvasyāyaṁ dharmastriguṇastriguṇaśca pratyayo heyapakṣe nyasta iti। duḥkharūpastṛṣṇātantuḥ। tṛṣṇāduḥkhasaṁtāpāpagamāttu prasannamabādhaṁ sarvānukūlaṁ sukhamidamuktamiti ॥ 18 ॥
body.translated_text: Here the following narrative is related — For the venerable <s>Jaigīṣavya</s>, from direct perception of <s>saṁskāras</s>, while observing the sequence of births and transformations across ten great cycles of creation (<s>mahāsarga</s>), knowledge born of discrimination (<s>vivekaja jñāna</s>) arose. Then the venerable <s>Āvaṭya</s>, the bearer of the tradition, said to him: "Since you have existed through ten great cycles of creation, with your <s>buddhi-sattva</s> (luminous intellect) unsubdued, observing the suffering of birth in hells and animal wombs, being born again and again among gods and humans — between pleasure and pain, which have you found to be greater?" The venerable <s>Jaigīṣavya</s> replied to the venerable <s>Āvaṭya</s>: "Since I have existed through ten great cycles of creation, with my <s>buddhi-sattva</s> unsubdued, observing the suffering of existence in hells and animal births, being born again and again among gods and humans — whatever I have experienced, all of that I recognize as nothing but suffering." The venerable <s>Āvaṭya</s> said: "This mastery over <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial nature) that you possess, and this unsurpassed happiness of contentment — is even this placed in the category of suffering?" The venerable <s>Jaigīṣavya</s> replied: "It is only in comparison with sensory pleasure that this unsurpassed happiness of contentment has been called [happiness]. In comparison with the bliss of <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation), it is nothing but suffering. This is a property of <s>buddhi-sattva</s>, which is constituted of the three <s>guṇas</s>, and a cognition constituted of the three <s>guṇas</s> is placed in the category of what is to be abandoned. The thread of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) is of the nature of suffering. But from the cessation of the torment of craving-born suffering, this happiness — serene, unafflicted, and entirely agreeable — has been spoken of." ॥ 18 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
tatra saṁskārasākṣātkaraṇaphalavyañjanārtham idamākhyānamupakṣipyate— [bhagavato jaigīṣavyasya saṁskārasākṣātkaraṇāt daśasu mahāsargeṣu janmapariṇāmam anupaśyato vivekajaṁ vairāgyānimittaṁ jñānaṁ prādurabhūt ॥]
[athabhagavān āvaṭayaḥ tantradharaḥ tamuvāca – daśasu mahāsargeṣu [bhavyatvāt] anabhibhūtabuddhisatvena tvayā narakatiryaggamanaduḥkhamanupaśyatā devamanuṣyeṣu punaḥ punaḥ utpadyamānena sukhaduḥkhayoḥ kimupalabdhamadhikamiti ॥]
[bhagavantamāvaṣṭyaṁjaigīṣavyauvāca–daśasu mahāsargeṣu bhavyatvāt anabhibhūtabuddhisatvena mayā narakatiryaggamanamanupaśyatā devamanuṣyeṣu punaḥ punaḥ utpadyamānena yatkiñcit anubhūtaṁ tatsarvaṁ duḥkhamiti [] duḥkhameva [] pratyavaimi ॥]
[bhagavānāvaṭya uvāca – yadidamāyuṣmataḥ pradhānavaśitvamanuttamaṁ ca santoṣasukhaṁ [kimidamapi du:khapakṣe nikṣitamiti । bhagavān jaigīṣavya uvāca—viṣayasukhāpekṣayaivedamanuttamaṁ santoṣasukhaṁ [pradhānavaśitvasukhaṁ ca] uttam । kaivalyasukhāpekṣayā duḥkhameva । buddhisattvasyāyaṁ dharmaḥ triguṇaḥ ॥ ] ‘triguṇaśca pratyayo heyapakṣe nyasta iti ।] kimapekṣayā punaretaddvayaṁ sukhaṁ bhavatītyāha – [duḥkharūpastṛṣṇātantuḥ । tṛṣṇāsantānaduḥkhopaśamarūpaṁ tu prasannamanābādhaṁ sarvānukūlaṁ sukhamidamuktaṁ] santoṣasukhaṁ pradhānajayasukhaṁ ca ॥ 18 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
Therein, this narrative is introduced to illustrate the fruit of direct perception of <s>saṁskāras</s> — ["For the venerable <s>Jaigīṣavya</s>, from direct perception of <s>saṁskāras</s>, while observing the sequence of births and transformations across ten great cycles of creation, knowledge born of discrimination — caused by dispassion — arose."]
["Then the venerable <s>Āvaṭya</s>, the bearer of the tradition, said to him — 'Since you have existed through ten great cycles of creation, with your <s>buddhi-sattva</s> unsubdued, observing the suffering of going to hells and animal births, being born again and again among gods and humans — between pleasure and pain, which have you found to be greater?'"]
["The venerable <s>Jaigīṣavya</s> replied to the venerable <s>Āvaṭya</s> — 'Since I have existed through ten great cycles of creation, with my <s>buddhi-sattva</s> unsubdued, observing the going to hells and animal births, being born again and again among gods and humans — whatever I have experienced, all of that I recognize as suffering — indeed, nothing but suffering.'"]
["The venerable <s>Āvaṭya</s> said — 'This mastery over <s>pradhāna</s> that you possess, and this unsurpassed happiness of contentment — is even this placed in the category of suffering?' The venerable <s>Jaigīṣavya</s> replied — 'It is only in comparison with sensory pleasure that this unsurpassed happiness of contentment and the happiness of mastery over <s>pradhāna</s> have been called [happiness]. In comparison with the bliss of <s>kaivalya</s>, it is nothing but suffering. This is a property of <s>buddhi-sattva</s>, which is constituted of the three <s>guṇas</s>.'"] 'And a cognition constituted of the three <s>guṇas</s> is placed in the category of what is to be abandoned.' In comparison with what, then, do these two become happiness? He says — ['The thread of craving is of the nature of suffering. But what is serene, unafflicted, and entirely agreeable — in the form of the cessation of the torment born of craving — this happiness has been spoken of'] as the happiness of contentment and the happiness of mastery over <s>pradhāna</s>. ॥ 18 ॥

body.text: pratyayasya paracittajñānam ॥ 19 ॥
body.translated_text: From cognition [arises] knowledge of another's mind. ॥ 19 ॥

body.text: pratyaye saṁyamātpratyayasya sākṣātkaraṇāttataḥ paracittajñānam ॥ 19 ॥
body.translated_text: From <s>saṁyama</s> on cognition, through direct perception of cognition, knowledge of another's mind [arises]. ॥ 19 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[pratyayasya parācittajñānam ।] para [pratyaye saṁyamāt] para [pratyayasya sākṣātkaraṇam ।] tatsākṣātkaraṇe tatsaṁbandhinaḥ [paracittasya jñānaṁ] bhavati ॥ 19 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
["From cognition, knowledge of another's mind."] ["From <s>saṁyama</s> on another's cognition,"] ["direct perception of another's cognition"] [arises]. Upon that direct perception, ["knowledge of another's mind,"] which is connected to that [cognition], arises. ॥ 19 ॥

body.text: na ca tatsālambanaṁ tasyāviṣayībhūtatvāt ॥ 20 ॥
body.translated_text: But not the support of that [cognition], since it has not become an object [of the <s>yogin</s>'s cognition]. ॥ 20 ॥

body.text: raktaṁ pratyaya jānātyamuṣminnālambane raktamiti na jānāti। parapratyayasya yadālambanaṁ tadyogicittena nā''lambanīkṛtaṁ parapratyayamātraṁ tu yogicittasyā''lambanībhūtamiti ॥ 20 ॥
body.translated_text: He knows the cognition as having attachment — but does not know 'it is attached to this particular object.' The support (<s>ālambana</s>) of another's cognition is not made into a support by the <s>yogin</s>'s mind; only the other's cognition itself has become the support of the <s>yogin</s>'s mind. ॥ 20 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
tatra parapratyayasākṣātkaraṇāttaddu:khe du:khitvaṁ, tatsukhe sukhitvaṁ ca prāpnotītyāśaṅkyāha- [na ca sālambanaṁ tasya aviṣayībhūtatvāt । raktaṁ pratyayaṁ jānāti] yogī । parasya amuṣmin [ālambane raktaḥ] pratyaya [iti na jānāti । parapratyayasya yadālambanaṁ] sukharūrṣaduḥkharūpaṁ vā, yenasukhī duḥkhī vā bhavet ॥
nanu cālambanamasañjānānaḥ kathamamuṣminnakta iti sañjānīta iti? ucyate – raktamamuṣminniti sāmānyaṁ vijānāti । na punaḥ sukhaviśeṣaṁ sukhinaḥ pratyayasyālambanībhūtamālambate । [parapratyayamātraṁ tu yogicittasyālambanībhūtam ॥ 20 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
Therein, lest one suspect that from direct perception of another's cognition, one would become sorrowful at that person's sorrow and happy at that person's happiness, he says — ["But not the support of that, since it has not become an object. He knows the cognition as having attachment"] — the <s>yogin</s> [knows this]. He does not know that the other's [cognition] ["is attached to this particular support"] — whether it is of the nature of pleasure or pain, by which one would become happy or sorrowful.
But if one does not cognize the support, how does one cognize 'it is attached to this [object]'? It is replied — he knows in general that 'it is attached to this.' But he does not take as his support the specific pleasure that is the support of the cognition of the one who is happy. ["Only the other's cognition itself has become the support of the <s>yogin</s>'s mind."] ॥ 20 ॥

body.text: kāyarūpasaṁyamāttadgrāhyaśaktistambhe cakṣuṣprakāśāsaṁprayoge'ntardhānam ॥ 21 ॥
body.translated_text: From <s>saṁyama</s> on the form of the body, upon the suspension of its power of being grasped, when there is no contact with the light of the eye, invisibility [arises]. ॥ 21 ॥

body.text: kāyasya rūpe saṁyamādrūpasya yā grāhyā śaktistāṁ pratiṣṭabhrāti। grāhyaśaktistambhe sati cakṣuṣprakāśāsaṁprayoge'ntardhānamutpadyate yoginaḥ। etena śabdādyantardhānamuktaṁ veditavyam ॥ 21 ॥
body.translated_text: From <s>saṁyama</s> on the form of the body, one arrests the graspable power of that form. When the graspable power is suspended, and there is no contact with the light of the eye, invisibility arises for the <s>yogin</s>. By this, the disappearance of sound and other [sense objects] should also be understood. ॥ 21 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[kāyarūpasaṁyamāttadgrāhyaśaktistambhe cakṣuḥ prakāśāsamprayoge antadhānam ।] yāgina ātmīyasya [kāyasya rūpaṁ kāyarūpam । tasmin rūpe saṁyamāt] tasya [rūpasya yā paracakṣugrahmā śaktiḥ tāṁ pratibadhnāti] niruṇaddhi । tataḥ pareṣāṁ [cakṣuḥprakāśo] yogikāyarūpeṇa na [samprayujyate ।] tataśca [antardhānam । etena śabdādyantardhānamuktam ।] yogiśabdasya yā grāhyaśaktiḥ tasyāṁ saṁyame sati yā śabdasya grāhyaśaktiḥ sā pratiṣṭabhyate । tena yogiśandaṁnaparaḥ śṛṇoti । tathāsparśādiṣvapi draṣṭavyam ॥ 21 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
["From <s>saṁyama</s> on the form of the body, upon the suspension of its power of being grasped, when there is no contact with the light of the eye, invisibility."] The form of the <s>yogin</s>'s own ["body is the body-form. From <s>saṁyama</s> on that form,"] one ["arrests"] — obstructs — ["the graspable power of that form"] by others' eyes. Then ["the light of others' eyes"] does not ["come into contact"] with the form of the <s>yogin</s>'s body. And from that, ["invisibility."] ["By this, the disappearance of sound and other [sense objects] is stated."] When there is <s>saṁyama</s> on the graspable power of the <s>yogin</s>'s sound, the graspable power of that sound is arrested. Thereby, another does not hear the <s>yogin</s>'s sound. The same should be understood with regard to touch and the other [sense objects]. ॥ 21 ॥

body.text: sopakramaṁ nirupakramaṁ ca karma tatsaṁyamādaparāntajñānamariṣṭebhyo vā ॥ 22 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> (action) is of two kinds — <s>sopakrama</s> (actively fruiting) and <s>nirupakrama</s> (dormantly fruiting). From <s>saṁyama</s> on that, knowledge of death (<s>aparānta</s>) [arises], or from portents (<s>ariṣṭa</s>). ॥ 22 ॥

body.text: āyurvipākaṁ karma dvividhaṁ sopakramaṁ nirupakramaṁ ca। tatra yathā''rdraṁ vastraṁ vitānitaṁ laghīyasā kālena śuṣyettathā sopakramam। yathā ca tadeva saṁpiṇḍitaṁ cireṇa saṁśuṣyedevaṁ nirupakramam। yathā vā'gniḥ śuṣke kakṣe mukto vātena samantato yuktaḥ kṣepīyasā kālena dahettathā sopakramam। yathā vā sa evāgnistṛṇarāśau kramaśo'vayaveṣu nyastaścireṇa dahettathā nirupakramam। tadaikabhavikamāyuṣkaraṁ karma dvividhaṁ sopakramaṁ nirupakramaṁ ca। tatsaṁyamādaparāntasya prāyaṇasya jñānam।
body.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> whose fruition is lifespan is of two kinds: <s>sopakrama</s> (actively fruiting) and <s>nirupakrama</s> (dormantly fruiting). Among these — just as a wet cloth spread out dries in a shorter time, so is <s>sopakrama</s> [karma]. And just as that same cloth, when bunched together, takes a long time to dry, so is <s>nirupakrama</s> [karma]. Or, just as a fire set loose in dry undergrowth, fanned by wind from all sides, burns in a very short time, so is <s>sopakrama</s>. And just as that very same fire, placed gradually in portions of a heap of grass, burns over a long time, so is <s>nirupakrama</s>. Thus, <s>karma</s> that produces the lifespan of a single existence is of two kinds — <s>sopakrama</s> and <s>nirupakrama</s>. From <s>saṁyama</s> on that comes knowledge of death (<s>aparānta</s>), that is, of the time of passing.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[sopakramaṁ nirupakramaṁ ca karma tatsaṁyamādaparāntajñānamāriṣṭebhyo vā । āyurvipākaṁ karma dvidhā ।] katham? tvaritaṁ nimittamādāya phalapradaṁ [sopakramam] ucyate । yattu mandaprasaraṁ cireṇa phalaṁ dāsyati tat [nirupakramam ॥]
[yathā ārdraṁ vastraṁ vitānitaṁ] vistāritaṁ [kṣepīyasā] kṣiprateraṇa [kālena śuṣyet, tathā sopakramaṁ karma] kṣipramāyurvipākaṁ kṛtvā kṣīyate ॥
[tadeva vastraṁ sampiṇḍitam] avitānitaṁ [cireṇa śuṣyedevaṁ nirupakramaṁ] cireṇa āyuḥ karoti ॥
[yathā vā agniḥ śuṣke kakṣe yuktavāte] anukūlamātariśvani [samantato niyuktaḥ kṣepīyasā kālena dahet, tathā sopakramaṁ] karmakṣepīyasā kālena āyurdhakṣyati ॥
[sa evāgniḥ tṛṇarāśau krameṇa nyastaścireṇa dahet, tathā nirupakrarmakarma ॥]
tadetat [dvividham aikabhavikamāyuṣkaraṁ karma ।] tatsaṁyamādaparāntajñānam । [aparāntasya prāyaṇasya] ātmīyasya [jñānam ।] tathā parakīyadvividhakarmasaṁyamātparaprāyaṇajñānamapi bhavati । prāyaṇajñāne ca prayojanaṁ puruṣakartavyatāṁ prati samīhanam ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
["<s>Karma</s> is <s>sopakrama</s> and <s>nirupakrama</s>; from <s>saṁyama</s> on that, knowledge of death, or from portents. <s>Karma</s> whose fruition is lifespan is of two kinds."] How? That which quickly seizes a proximate cause and yields its fruit ["is called <s>sopakrama</s>."] But that which proceeds slowly and will yield its fruit after a long time ["is <s>nirupakrama</s>."]
["Just as a wet cloth spread out"] — spread open — ["dries in a shorter"] — from the comparative of 'quickly' — ["time, so <s>sopakrama</s> karma"] quickly effects its lifespan-fruition and is exhausted.
["That very cloth, bunched together"] — not spread out — ["takes a long time to dry; so <s>nirupakrama</s>"] produces its lifespan over a long duration.
["Or, just as a fire in dry undergrowth, with favorable wind,"] with a favorable breeze, ["set in all directions, burns in a very short time, so <s>sopakrama</s>"] karma will consume the lifespan in a very short time.
["That very fire, placed gradually in a heap of grass, burns over a long time; so <s>nirupakrama</s> karma."]
Thus, this ["twofold karma produces the lifespan of a single existence. From <s>saṁyama</s> on that, knowledge of death."] ["Of death, of the time of passing"] — one's own. Likewise, from <s>saṁyama</s> on the twofold karma of another, knowledge of the other's time of death also arises. And the purpose of knowledge of death is the effort towards what a person must do.

body.text: ariṣṭebhyo veti। trividhamariṣṭamādhyātmikamādhibhautikamādhidaivikaṁ ceti। tatrā''dhyātmikaṁ ghoṣaṁ svadehe pihitakarṇo na śṛṇoti, jyotirvā netre'vaṣṭabdhe na paśyati। tathā''dhibhautikaṁ yamapuruṣānpaśyati, pitṝnatītānakasmātpaśyati। tathā''dhidaivikaṁ svargamakasmātsiddhānvā paśyati। viparītaṁ vā sarvamiti। anena vā jānātyaparāntamupasthitamiti ॥ 22 ॥
body.translated_text: 'Or from portents' — portents (<s>ariṣṭa</s>) are of three kinds: <s>ādhyātmika</s> (pertaining to the self), <s>ādhibhautika</s> (pertaining to material beings), and <s>ādhidaivika</s> (pertaining to divine forces). Among these, the <s>ādhyātmika</s>: when one blocks one's ears and does not hear the inner sound in one's own body, or when one presses upon the eyes and does not see the inner light. The <s>ādhibhautika</s>: one sees the messengers of <s>Yama</s> (Death), or one suddenly sees departed ancestors. The <s>ādhidaivika</s>: one suddenly sees heaven or the <s>Siddhas</s> (perfected beings). Or everything appears reversed. By these signs too, one knows that death is imminent. ॥ 22 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[ariṣṭebhyo vā] prāyaṇajñānam । [trividhamariṣṭamādhyātmikamādhibhautikamādhidaivikaṁ ca ।] tatrādhyātmikasyodāharaṇam– [ghoṣaṁ svadehe pihitakarṇau na śṛṇoti । jyotirvā netre'vaṣṭabdhena paśyati ॥]
[tathā ādhibhautikaṁ–yamapuruṣānpaśyati । pitṝnatītānāgatānakasmādvetti । adhidaivikam—akasmādeva siddhādīnpaśyati । viparītaṁ vā sarvaṁ] paśyati karoti ca । tatrāriṣṭamiti laukikī vācāyutiḥ । evaṁ hyāha--viparītadarśanaṁ mamāsīdariṣṭāṁmati ॥ 23 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
["Or from portents"] — knowledge of death [arises]. ["Portents are of three kinds: <s>ādhyātmika</s>, <s>ādhibhautika</s>, and <s>ādhidaivika</s>."] Of these, an example of the <s>ādhyātmika</s> — ["when one blocks one's ears and does not hear the inner sound in one's own body; or when one presses upon the eyes and does not see [the inner light]."]
["The <s>ādhibhautika</s> — one sees the messengers of <s>Yama</s>; one suddenly knows departed and future ancestors. The <s>ādhidaivika</s> — one suddenly sees the <s>Siddhas</s> and the like. Or one sees and does everything reversed."] Therein, '<s>ariṣṭa</s>' is a conventional worldly expression. For thus one says — 'I had a reversed vision — it is a portent of ill.' ॥ 23 ॥

body.text: maitryādiṣu balāni ॥ 23 ॥
body.translated_text: From [<s>saṁyama</s> on] friendliness (<s>maitrī</s>) and the like, [come] powers. ॥ 23 ॥

body.text: maitrī karuṇā muditeti tisro bhāvanāstatra bhūteṣu sukhiteṣu maitrīṁ bhāvayitvā maitrībalaṁ labhate। duḥkhiteṣu karuṇāṁ bhāvayitvā karuṇābalaṁ labhate। puṇyaśīleṣu muditāṁ bhāvayitvā muditābalaṁ labhate। bhāvanātaḥ samādhiryaḥ sa saṁyamastato balānyavandhyavīryāṇi jāyante। pāpaśīleṣūpekṣā na tu bhāvanā। tataśca tasyāṁ nāsti samādhirityato na balamupekṣātastatra saṁyamābhāvāditi ॥ 23 ॥
body.translated_text: Friendliness (<s>maitrī</s>), compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), and sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>) — these are three <s>bhāvanās</s> (cultivations). Among them, by cultivating friendliness towards beings who are happy, one obtains the power of friendliness. By cultivating compassion towards those who are suffering, one obtains the power of compassion. By cultivating sympathetic joy towards those who are virtuous, one obtains the power of joy. The <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) that arises from this cultivation is the <s>saṁyama</s>, and from it arise powers of unfailing potency. Towards those who are sinful, there is equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>), but not cultivation. Therefore, in that case there is no <s>samādhi</s>, and hence no power from equanimity, since there is no <s>saṁyama</s> in that regard. ॥ 23 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[maitryādiṣu balāni । maitrīkaruṇāmuditeti tisro bhāvanāḥ । tatra bhūteṣu sukhiteṣu maitrīṁ bhāvayitvā maitrībalaṁ labhate । du:khiteṣu karuṇāṁ bhāvayitvā karuṇābalaṁ labhate । puṇyaśīleṣu muditāṁ bhāvayitvā muditābalaṁ labhate ॥]
[bhāvanātaḥ] maitryādibhāvanātaḥ [samādhiryaḥ] saṁjāyate [sa] , [saṁyamaḥ] maitryādibhāvanāsthairyanimittaḥ । [tataḥ] saṁyamāt maitryādigatāt [yogino balānyavandhyavaryāṇi jāyante ॥]
[pāpaśīleṣu tu asya upekṣā, na tu bhāvanā ॥ tataśca] bhāvanāyā abhāvāt [tasyām] upekṣāyāṁ [nāsti samādhirityato na balamupekṣātaḥ । tatra saṁyamābhāvāditi ॥ 23 ॥]
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
['From friendliness and so forth, strengths arise. Friendliness (maitrī), compassion (karuṇā), and gladness (muditā) — these are the three cultivations (bhāvanā). Among these, by cultivating friendliness toward beings who are happy, one obtains the strength of friendliness. By cultivating compassion toward those who suffer, one obtains the strength of compassion. By cultivating gladness toward the virtuous, one obtains the strength of gladness.']
[From cultivation] — from the cultivation of friendliness and so forth — [the samādhi that] arises, [that] is [the saṁyama] caused by the stability of cultivating friendliness and so forth. [From that] saṁyama directed toward friendliness and so forth, [the yogin's strengths, unfailing and supreme, arise.]
['But toward the sinful, there is equanimity (upekṣā), not cultivation. And therefore,] due to the absence of cultivation, [in that] equanimity, [there is no samādhi, hence no strength from equanimity. Because there is no saṁyama therein.' || 23 ||]

body.text: baleṣu hastibalādīni ॥ 24 ॥
body.translated_text: By [saṁyama] on strengths, [one gains] the strength of an elephant and so forth. || 24 ||

body.text: hastibale saṁyamāddhastibalo bhavati। vainateyabale saṁyamādvainateyabalo bhavati। vāyubale saṁyamādvāyubalo bhavatītyevamādi ॥ 24 ॥
body.translated_text: By <s>saṁyama</s> on the strength of an elephant, one becomes as strong as an elephant. By <s>saṁyama</s> on the strength of <s>Vainateya</s> (Garuḍa), one becomes as strong as <s>Vainateya</s>. By <s>saṁyama</s> on the strength of the wind, one becomes as strong as the wind — and so on. || 24 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[baleṣu hastibalādīni ।] etairmaitryādinimittairbalairbalavānyogīhastyādīnabaleṣu saṁyamaṁkṛtvāhastyādibalo bhavati ॥ 24 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['By saṁyama on strengths, one gains the strength of an elephant and so forth.'] The <s>yogin</s>, empowered by the strengths arising from friendliness and so forth, by performing <s>saṁyama</s> on the strengths of elephants and others, gains the strength of elephants and so forth. || 24 ||

body.text: pravṛttyālokanyāsātsūkṣmavyavahitaviprakṛṣṭajñānam ॥ 25 ॥
body.translated_text: From directing the light of higher perception (<s>pravṛtti</s>), knowledge of the subtle, concealed, and distant arises. || 25 ||

body.text: jyotiṣmatī pravṛttiruktā manasastasyā ya ālokastaṁ yogī sūkṣme vā vyavahite vā viprakṛṣṭe vā'rthe vinyasya tamarthamadhigacchati ॥ 25 ॥
body.translated_text: The luminous (<s>jyotiṣmatī</s>) higher perception (<s>pravṛtti</s>) has been described as belonging to the mind. The <s>yogin</s>, by directing its light upon a subtle, concealed, or distant object, comprehends that object. || 25 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[pravṛttyālokanyāsāt sūkṣmavyavahitaviprakṛṣṭajñānam ।] yā asau [jyotiṣmatī pravṛttiruktā,] tasyāṁ prakāśaḥ [ālokaḥ] taṁ prakāśaṁ [yogī sūkṣme vā vyavahite vā viprakṛṣṭe vā arthe vinyasya] sthāpayatvā [tamadhigacchati ॥ 25 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['From directing the light of higher perception, knowledge of the subtle, concealed, and distant arises.'] That which was called ['the luminous higher perception'] — its radiance is the ['light']. ['The yogin, by directing'] that radiance ['upon a subtle, concealed, or distant object,'] having placed it there, ['comprehends that.' || 25 ||]

body.text: bhuvanajñānaṁ sūrye saṁyamāt ॥ 26 ॥
body.translated_text: Knowledge of the worlds arises from <s>saṁyama</s> on the sun. || 26 ||

body.text: tatprastāraḥ sapta lokāḥ। tatrāvīceḥ prabhṛti merupṛṣṭhaṁ yāvadityevaṁ bhūrlokaḥ। merupṛṣṭhādārabhya ādhruvādgrahanakṣatratārāvicitro'ntarikṣalokaḥ। tataḥ paraḥ svarlokaḥ pañcavidho māhendrastṛtīyo lokaḥ। caturthaḥ prājāpatyo maharlokaḥ। trividho brāhmaḥ। tadyathā – janalokastapolokaḥ satyaloka iti। brāhmastribhūmiko lokaḥ prājāpatyastato mahān। māhendraśca svarityukto divi tārā bhuvi prajāḥ ॥ iti saṁgrahaślokaḥ।
body.translated_text: The layout of that [cosmology]: there are seven worlds. From <s>Avīci</s> (the lowest hell) upward to the summit of <s>Meru</s> — this is <s>Bhūrloka</s> (the earthly world). From the summit of <s>Meru</s> extending to the Pole Star, adorned with planets, constellations, and stars — this is <s>Antarikṣaloka</s> (the intermediate world). Beyond that is <s>Svarloka</s> (the celestial world), which is fivefold. The third world is <s>Māhendra</s>. The fourth is <s>Prājāpatya</s>, the great world (<s>Maharloka</s>). The <s>Brāhma</s> world is threefold: namely, <s>Janaloka</s>, <s>Tapoloka</s>, and <s>Satyaloka</s>. The summary verse: 'The <s>Brāhma</s> world has three levels; <s>Prājāpatya</s> is greater than that; <s>Māhendra</s> is called <s>Svar</s>; in heaven are the stars, on earth are the creatures.'

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[bhuvanajñānaṁ sūrye saṁyamāt ।] sūrye saṁyamaṁ kṛtvā samastaṁ bhuvanaprastāraṁ pratyakṣākurvīta । bhāṣyaṁ tu gatārthaṁ, sarvapurāṇaprasiddhatvāta ॥ 26 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['Knowledge of the worlds from saṁyama on the sun.'] Having performed <s>saṁyama</s> on the sun, one would make the entire layout of the worlds directly perceptible. The <s>bhāṣya</s>, however, has a well-known meaning, being established in all the <s>Purāṇas</s>. || 26 ||

body.text: tatrāvīceruparyupari niviṣṭāḥ ṣaṇmahānarakabhūmayo ghanasalilānalānilākāśatamaḥpratiṣṭhā mahākālāmbarīṣarauravamahārauravamahārauravakālasūtrāndhatāmisrāḥ। yatra svakarmopārjitaduḥkhavedanāḥ prāṇinaḥ kaṣṭamāyurdīrghamākṣipya jāyante। tato mahātalarasātalātalasutalavitalatalātalapātālākhyāni sapta pātālāni। bhūmiriyamaṣṭamī saptadvīpā vasumatī, yasyāḥ sumerurmadhye parvatarājaḥ kāñcanaḥ। tasya rājatavaidūryasphaṭikahemamaṇimayāni śṛṅgāṇi। tatra vaidūryaprabhānurāgānnīlotpalapatraśyāmo nabhaso dakṣiṇo bhāgaḥ, śvetaḥ pūrvaḥ, svacchaḥ paścimaḥ, kuraṇṭakābha uttaraḥ। dakṣiṇapārśve cāsya jambūryato'yaṁ jambūdvīpaḥ। tasya sūryapracārādrātriṁ divaṁ lagnamiva vartate। tasya nīlaśvetaśṛṅgavanta udīcīnāstrayaḥ parvatā dvisāhasrāyāmāḥ। tadantareṣu trīṇi varṣāṇi nava nava yojanasāhasrāṇi ramaṇakaṁ hiraṇmayamuttarāḥ kurava iti। niṣadhahemakūṭahimaśailā dakṣiṇato dvisāhasrāyāmāḥ। tadantareṣu trīṇi varṣāṇi nava nava yojanasāhasrāṇi harivarṣa kiṁpuruṣaṁ bhāratamiti। sumeroḥ prācīnā bhadrāśvamālyavatsīmānaḥ pratīcīnāḥ ketumālā gandhamādanasīmānaḥ। madhye varṣamilāvṛtam। tadetadyojanaśatasāhasraṁ sumerordiśi diśi tadardhena vyūḍham।
body.translated_text: Above <s>Avīci</s>, situated one above another, are the six great hellish realms — <s>Ghanaḥ</s>, <s>Salilam</s>, <s>Analam</s>, <s>Anilam</s>, <s>Ākāśam</s>, and <s>Tamaḥ</s>-pratiṣṭhā</s> — [also called] <s>Mahākāla</s>, <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, and <s>Andhatāmisra</s>. There, beings experiencing suffering earned by their own actions are born, dragging out a painfully long lifespan. Below that are the seven netherworlds called <s>Mahātala</s>, <s>Rasātala</s>, <s>Atala</s>, <s>Sutala</s>, <s>Vitala</s>, <s>Talātala</s>, and <s>Pātāla</s>. This earth is the eighth, the seven-island <s>Vasumatī</s>, in whose center is <s>Sumeru</s>, the king of mountains, made of gold. Its peaks are made of silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, gold, and gems. There, due to the glow of lapis lazuli, the southern portion of the sky appears dark like blue lotus petals; the eastern portion is white, the western is clear, and the northern is ruddy like <s>kurantaka</s> flowers. On its southern side is <s>Jambū</s> (the rose-apple tree), from which this is called <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>. Due to the course of the sun, night and day seem to follow it continuously. To its north are three mountains — <s>Nīla</s>, <s>Śveta</s>, and <s>Śṛṅgavān</s> — each two thousand <s>yojanas</s> in extent. Between them are three regions of nine thousand <s>yojanas</s> each: <s>Ramaṇaka</s>, <s>Hiraṇmaya</s>, and <s>Uttarāḥ Kuravaḥ</s>. To the south, <s>Niṣadha</s>, <s>Hemakūṭa</s>, and <s>Himālaya</s> are each two thousand <s>yojanas</s> in extent. Between them are three regions of nine thousand <s>yojanas</s> each: <s>Harivarṣa</s>, <s>Kiṁpuruṣa</s>, and <s>Bhārata</s>. East of <s>Sumeru</s>, <s>Bhadrāśva</s> extends to the boundary of <s>Mālyavān</s>; to the west, <s>Ketumālā</s> extends to the boundary of <s>Gandhamādana</s>. In the center is the region of <s>Ilāvṛta</s>. This all extends one hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>, spread out half that distance in each direction from <s>Sumeru</s>.

body.text: sa khalvayaṁ śatasāhasrāyāmo jambūdvīpastato dviguṇena lavaṇodadhinā valayākṛtinā veṣṭitaḥ। tataśca dviguṇā dviguṇāḥ śākakuśakrauñcaśālmalagomedha(plakṣa)puṣkaradvīpāḥ, samudrāśca sarṣaparāśikalpāḥ savicitraśailāvataṁsā ikṣurasasurāsarpirdadhimaṇḍakṣīrasvādūdakāḥ। sapta samudrapariveṣṭitā valayākṛtayo lokālokaparvataparivārāḥ pañcāśadyojanakoṭiparisaṁkhyātāḥ। tadetatsarvaṁ supratiṣṭhitasaṁsthānamaṇḍamadhye vyūḍham। aṇḍaṁ ca pradhānasyāṇurayavayavo yathā''kāśe khadyota iti।
body.translated_text: This <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> is one hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s> in extent, encircled ring-like by the salt ocean (<s>Lavaṇodadhi</s>) which is twice as large. Beyond that, each twice as large as the preceding, are the islands of <s>Śāka</s>, <s>Kuśa</s>, <s>Krauñca</s>, <s>Śālmala</s>, <s>Gomeda</s> (<s>Plakṣa</s>), and <s>Puṣkara</s>, and the oceans — comparable in proportion to a mustard seed — adorned with various mountains, filled with sugarcane juice, wine, ghee, buttermilk, milk, and sweet water respectively. These seven [dvīpas], each encircled by an ocean, ring-shaped, surrounded by the <s>Lokāloka</s> mountain, are enumerated as totaling fifty <s>koṭi yojanas</s>. All of this is arranged within a well-established cosmic egg (<s>aṇḍa</s>). And the egg is but an atom, a tiny fraction of <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) — like a firefly in space.

body.text: tatra pātāle jaladhau parvateṣveteṣu devanikāyā asuragandharvakinnarakiṁpuruṣayakṣarākṣasabhūtapreta-piśācāpasmārakāpsarobrahmarākṣasakūṣmāṇḍavināyakāḥ prativasanti। sarveṣu dvīpeṣu puṇyātmāno devamanuṣyāḥ।
body.translated_text: In those netherworlds, in the ocean, and on those mountains, the hosts of divine beings dwell: <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Kiṁpuruṣas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Bhūtas</s>, <s>Pretas</s>, <s>Piśācas</s>, <s>Apasmāras</s>, <s>Apsarases</s>, <s>Brahmarākṣasas</s>, <s>Kūṣmāṇḍas</s>, and <s>Vināyakas</s>. On all the islands dwell meritorious divine humans (<s>devamanuṣyas</s>).

body.text: sumerustridaśānāmudyānabhūmiḥ। tatra miśravanaṁ nandanaṁ caitrarathaṁ sumānasamityudyānāni। sudharmā devasabhā। sudarśanaṁ puram। vaijayantaḥ prāsādaḥ। grahanakṣatratārakāstu dhruve nibaddhā vāyuvikṣepaniyamenopalakṣitapracārāḥ sumeroruparyupari sanniviṣṭā divi viparivartante।
body.translated_text: <s>Sumeru</s> is the pleasure-ground of the gods. There are the gardens: <s>Miśravana</s>, <s>Nandana</s>, <s>Caitrarata</s>, and <s>Sumānasa</s>. <s>Sudharmā</s> is the divine assembly hall. <s>Sudarśana</s> is the city. <s>Vaijayanta</s> is the palace. The planets, constellations, and stars, fastened to the Pole Star (<s>Dhruva</s>), their courses governed by the impelling of the wind, are arranged above <s>Sumeru</s> and revolve in the sky.

body.text: māhendranivāsinaḥ ṣaḍdevanikāyāḥ - tridaśā agniṣvāttā yāmyāstuṣitā aparinirmitavaśavartinaḥ parinirmitavaśavartinaśceti। sarve saṁkalpasiddhā aṇimādyaiśvaryopapannāḥ kalpāyuṣo vṛndārakāḥ kāmabhogina aupapādikadehā uttamānukūlābhirapsarobhiḥ kṛtaparicārāḥ।
body.translated_text: The six classes of divine beings dwelling in <s>Māhendra</s> (the Indra-realm) are: <s>Tridaśas</s>, <s>Agniṣvāttas</s>, <s>Yāmyas</s>, <s>Tuṣitas</s>, <s>Aparinirmitavaśavartins</s>, and <s>Parinirmitavaśavartins</s>. All of them have their desires fulfilled by mere intention, endowed with the supernatural powers beginning with <s>aṇimā</s>, having lifespans of a <s>kalpa</s>, eternal youths (<s>vṛndārakas</s>), enjoyers of desires, with spontaneously-born bodies, attended upon by the most excellent and agreeable <s>Apsarases</s>.

body.text: mahati loke prājāpatye pañcavidho devanikāyaḥ – kumudā ṛbhavaḥ pratardanā añjanābhāḥ pracitābhā iti। ete mahābhūtavaśino dhyānāhārāḥ kalpasahasrāyuṣaḥ। prathame brahmaṇo janaloke caturvidho devanikāyo brahmapurohitā brahmakāyikā brahmamahākāyikā amarā iti। te bhūtendriyavaśino dviguṇadviguṇottarāyuṣaḥ।
body.translated_text: In the great <s>Prājāpatya</s> world (<s>Maharloka</s>), there are five classes of divine beings: <s>Kumudas</s>, <s>Ṛbhavas</s>, <s>Pratardanas</s>, <s>Añjanābhas</s>, and <s>Pracitābhas</s>. These have mastery over the great elements, subsist on <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and have lifespans of a thousand <s>kalpas</s>. In the first <s>Brahma</s> world, <s>Janaloka</s>, there are four classes of divine beings: <s>Brahmapurohitas</s>, <s>Brahmakāyikas</s>, <s>Brahmamahākāyikas</s>, and <s>Amaras</s>. These have mastery over elements and senses, with lifespans each double that of the preceding.

body.text: dvitīye tapasi loke trividho devanikāyaḥ – ābhāsvarā mahābhāsvarāḥ satyamahābhāsvarā iti। te bhūtendriyaprakṛtivaśino dviguṇadviguṇottarāyuṣaḥ sarve dhyānāhārā ūrdhvaretasa ūrdhvamapratihatajñānā adharabhūmiṣvanāvṛtajñānaviṣayāḥ। tṛtīye brahmaṇaḥ satyaloke catvāro devanikāyā akṛtabhavananyāsāḥ svapratiṣṭhā uparyuparisthitāḥ pradhānavaśino yāvatsargāyuṣaḥ।
body.translated_text: In the second [Brahma world], <s>Tapoloka</s>, there are three classes of divine beings: <s>Ābhāsvaras</s>, <s>Mahābhāsvaras</s>, and <s>Satyamahābhāsvaras</s>. These have mastery over elements, senses, and <s>prakṛti</s>, with lifespans each double that of the preceding, all subsisting on <s>dhyāna</s>, with upward-flowing seed (<s>ūrdhvaretas</s>), with unobstructed knowledge directed upward, with the domains of their knowledge uncovered in the lower realms. In the third <s>Brahma</s> world, <s>Satyaloka</s>, there are four classes of divine beings, dwelling without fixed abodes, self-established, situated one above another, having mastery over <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter), with lifespans lasting as long as creation.

body.text: tatrācyutāḥ savitarkadhyānasukhāḥ, śuddhanivāsāḥ savicāradhyānasukhāḥ, satyābhā ānandamātradhyānasukhāḥ, saṁjñāsaṁjñinaścāsmitāmātradhyānasukhāḥ। te'pi trailākyamadhye pratitiṣṭhanti। ta ete sapta lokāḥ sarva eva brahmalokāḥ। videhaprakṛtilayāstu mokṣapade vartanta iti na lokamadhye nyastā iti। etadyoginā sākṣātkaraṇīyaṁ sūryadvāre saṁyamaṁ kṛtvā, tato'nyatrāpi evaṁ tāvadabhyasedyāvadidaṁ sarva dṛṣṭamiti ॥ 26 ॥
body.translated_text: Among those, the <s>Acyutas</s> have the bliss of meditation with deliberation (<s>savitarka</s>); the <s>Śuddhanivāsas</s> have the bliss of meditation with reflection (<s>savicāra</s>); the <s>Satyābhas</s> have the bliss of meditation that is pure bliss alone; and the <s>Saṁjñāsaṁjñins</s> have the bliss of meditation that is pure I-am-ness (<s>asmitā-mātra</s>). They too abide within the triple world. These are the seven worlds, all of which are <s>Brahma</s> worlds. But the <s>Videhas</s> and <s>Prakṛtilayas</s> are situated in the state of liberation, and thus are not placed within the [seven] worlds. This is to be directly realized by the <s>yogin</s> by performing <s>saṁyama</s> through the gateway of the sun; then one should practice likewise elsewhere, until all of this is seen. || 26 ||

body.text: candre tārāvyūhajñānam ॥ 27 ॥
body.translated_text: From [<s>saṁyama</s>] on the moon, knowledge of the arrangement of stars. || 27 ||

body.text: candre saṁyamaṁ kṛtvā tārāṇāṁ vyūhaṁ vijānīyāt ॥ 27 ॥
body.translated_text: Having performed <s>saṁyama</s> on the moon, one should know the arrangement of the stars. || 27 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[candre tārāvyūhajñānam।] sūrye saṁyamanādbhuvanaprastāraṁ viditvā, tadanantaraṁ [candre saṁyamaṁ kṛtvā tārāṇāṁ vyūhaṁ vijānīyāt ।] sūryaseyamādbhuvanaprastāramātraṁ prajñātam—evaṁ prastīrṇāḥ lokānadyaḥ samudrāgirayaśceti । na tu tārā itthaṁ vyūhatā anena sambaddhā iti । candrasaṁyamāttu tārāvyūhaprakārāvagatiriti ॥ 27 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['From saṁyama on the moon, knowledge of the arrangement of stars.'] Having known the layout of the worlds through <s>saṁyama</s> on the sun, then ['having performed saṁyama on the moon, one should know the arrangement of the stars.'] Through the <s>saṁyama</s> on the sun, only the layout of the worlds was known — that the worlds, rivers, oceans, and mountains are spread out in this manner. But the specific arrangement of the stars and their connections was not known. Through <s>saṁyama</s> on the moon, however, the manner of star-arrangement is comprehended. || 27 ||

body.text: dhruve tadgatijñānam ॥ 28 ॥
body.translated_text: From [<s>saṁyama</s>] on the Pole Star (<s>Dhruva</s>), knowledge of their movement. || 28 ||

body.text: tato dhruve saṁyamaṁ kṛtvā tārāṇāṁ gatiṁ vijānīyāt। ūrdhvaṁ vimāneṣu kṛtasaṁyamastāni vijānīyāt ॥ 28 ॥
body.translated_text: Then, having performed <s>saṁyama</s> on the Pole Star, one should know the movement of the stars. Having performed <s>saṁyama</s> on the celestial vehicles (<s>vimānas</s>) above, one should know them. || 28 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[dhruve tadgatijñānam ।] tataśca samanantaraṁ [dhruve saṁyamaṁ kṛtvā tārāṇāṁ gatiṁ vijānīyāt] -anena prakoraṇa sañcaramāṇā anena viśiṣṭā iti । asminkāle'nena graheṇa ayaṁ graho virudhyate, itthamastamayaḥ । itthamudayaḥ, taddvāreṇaprāṇabhṛtāṁ śubhamaśubhe cetyādivi jānīyāt ॥
evamanyeṣu [cordhvaṁ vimāneṣu saṁyamaṁ kṛtvā tāni] vimānānītthaṁprakārāṇyevaṁgatānātyevamādisarvaṁ [vijānīyāt ॥ 28 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['From saṁyama on the Pole Star, knowledge of their movement.'] Then, immediately after, ['having performed saṁyama on the Pole Star, one should know the movement of the stars'] — through which orbit they move, with what distinctive qualities. At this time, this planet is in opposition with that planet, in this manner is its setting, in this manner its rising — and through that, one should know the auspicious and inauspicious [fates] of living beings, and so forth.
Likewise, regarding the others — ['having performed saṁyama on the celestial vehicles above, one should know those'] vehicles — of what kind they are, how they move, and everything else of that nature. || 28 ||

body.text: nābhicakre kāyavyūhajñānam ॥ 29 ॥
body.translated_text: From [<s>saṁyama</s>] on the navel center (<s>nābhi-cakra</s>), knowledge of the arrangement of the body. || 29 ||

body.text: nābhicakre saṁyamaṁ kṛtvā kāyavyūhaṁ vijānīyāt। vātapitta śleṣmāṇastrayo doṣāḥ। dhātavaḥ sapta tvaglohitamāṁsasnāyvasthimajjāśukrāṇi। pūrvaṁ pūrvameṣāṁ bāhyamityeṣa vinyāsaḥ ॥ 29 ॥
body.translated_text: Having performed <s>saṁyama</s> on the navel center, one should know the arrangement of the body. The three <s>doṣas</s> (humors) are <s>vāta</s> (wind), <s>pitta</s> (bile), and <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm). The seven <s>dhātus</s> (bodily constituents) are: skin, blood, flesh, sinew, bone, marrow, and semen. Of these, each preceding one is more external — this is the arrangement. || 29 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[nābhicakre kāyavyūhajñānam । nābhicakre saṁyamaṁ kṛtvā kāyavyūhaṁ vijānīyāt । vātapittaśleṣmāṇastrayo doṣāḥ] etāvatpramāṇā etatpratiṣṭhā ityādi jñeyam ॥
tathā [dhātavaḥ sapta] bāhyābhyantarabhāvenāvasthitāḥ । ( [rasaḥ] ) tvagbāhyā sarveṣām । tato'bhyantaraṁ [lohitaṁ] , tato [māṁsaṁ] , tato ['sthi,] tato [medaḥ] , tato [majjā] , tataḥ [śuklaṁ] sarvābhyantaramityevaṁ [pūrvaṁ pūrvameṣāṁ bāhyam ityeṣa vinyāsaḥ] । tathā nāḍīnāṁ cavyūhavijānīyāt ॥ 29 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['From saṁyama on the navel center, knowledge of the arrangement of the body. Having performed saṁyama on the navel center, one should know the arrangement of the body. The three doṣas are vāta, pitta, and śleṣma'] — their extent, their foundation, and so forth should be known.
Likewise, ['the seven dhātus,'] situated in an outer-to-inner arrangement: (rasa) skin is the outermost of all. Then inward is ['blood,'] then ['flesh,'] then ['bone,'] then ['fat,'] then ['marrow,'] then ['semen'] is the innermost — thus ['each preceding one is more external — this is the arrangement.'] Likewise, one should know the arrangement of the <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels). || 29 ||

body.text: kaṇṭhakūpe kṣutpipāsānivṛttiḥ ॥ 30 ॥
body.translated_text: From [<s>saṁyama</s>] on the pit of the throat (<s>kaṇṭha-kūpa</s>), cessation of hunger and thirst. || 30 ||

body.text: jihvāyā adhastāttantustantoradhastātkaṇṭhastato'dhastātkūpastatra saṁyamātkṣutpipāse na bādhete ॥ 30 ॥
body.translated_text: Below the tongue is a tendon; below the tendon is the throat; below that is the pit (<s>kūpa</s>). Through <s>saṁyama</s> on that, hunger and thirst no longer afflict [the yogin]. || 30 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[kaṇṭhakūpe kṣutpipāsānivṛttiḥ । jihvāyā adhastāttantuḥ] unnāmikāyāṁ jihvāyāṁ dṛśyate । [tantoradhastāt kaṇṭhaḥ । tato'dhastāt kūpaḥ । tatra saṁyamāt kṣutpipāse na pratibādhete ॥ 30 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['From saṁyama on the pit of the throat, cessation of hunger and thirst. Below the tongue is the tendon'] — it is visible when the tongue is lifted upward. ['Below the tendon is the throat. Below that is the pit. Through saṁyama on that, hunger and thirst no longer afflict.' || 30 ||]

body.text: kūrmanāḍyāṁ sthairyam ॥ 31 ॥
body.translated_text: From [<s>saṁyama</s>] on the <s>kūrma-nāḍī</s> (tortoise-channel), steadiness. || 31 ||

body.text: kūpādadha urasi kūrmākārā nāḍī, tasyāṁ kṛtasaṁyamaḥ sthirapadaṁ labhate। yathā sarpo godhā veti ॥ 31 ॥
body.translated_text: Below the pit, in the chest, is a channel shaped like a tortoise. One who performs <s>saṁyama</s> on it attains a steady position — just as a serpent or a monitor lizard [becomes still]. || 31 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
kūpasyādhastādurasi kūrmā nāma nāḍī । tasyāṁ kṛtasaṁyamaḥ sthirapadaṁ labhate cittasthairyaṁ labhate । yathā sarpo godhā vā dhāraṇādurasā atyantaṁ sthirībhavati ॥ 31 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
Below the pit, in the chest, is a channel called <s>kūrma</s> (tortoise). One who performs <s>saṁyama</s> on it attains a steady position — attains steadiness of mind. Just as a serpent or a monitor lizard, through holding [still], becomes extremely steady in the chest. || 31 ||

body.text: mūrdhajyotiṣi siddhadarśanam ॥ 32 ॥
body.translated_text: From [<s>saṁyama</s>] on the light at the crown of the head (<s>mūrdha-jyotis</s>), vision of the <s>Siddhas</s> (perfected beings). || 32 ||

body.text: śiraḥkapāle'ntaśchidraṁ prabhāsvaraṁ jyotistatra saṁyamaṁ kṛtvā siddhānāṁ dyāvāpṛthivyorantarālacāriṇāṁ darśanam ॥ 32 ॥
body.translated_text: Inside the skull there is an opening filled with radiant light. By performing <s>saṁyama</s> on that, one gains vision of the <s>Siddhas</s>, who move in the space between heaven and earth. || 32 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
śiraḥkapāle'ntaśchidraṁ prabhāsvaratvāt jyotiḥ ityucyate , tatra saṁyamāt siddhānāṁ dyāvāpṛthivyorantarālacāriṇāṁ darśanaṁ bhavati ॥ 32 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
Inside the skull, due to its radiant nature, there is what is called 'light' (<s>jyotis</s>). Through <s>saṁyama</s> on that, vision of the <s>Siddhas</s>, who move in the space between heaven and earth, arises. || 32 ||

body.text: prātibhādvā sarvam ॥ 33 ॥
body.translated_text: Or, from <s>prātibha</s> (intuitive knowledge), [one knows] everything. || 33 ||

body.text: prātibhaṁ nāma tārakaṁ tadvivekajasya jñānasya pūrvarūpam। yathodaye prabhā bhāskarasya। tena vā sarvameva jānāti yogī prātibhasya jñānasyotpattāviti ॥ 33 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>Prātibha</s> is called <s>tāraka</s> (transcendent knowledge); it is the precursor of knowledge born of discrimination (<s>vivekaja-jñāna</s>). Just as the dawn-glow precedes the rising sun. By that, or by the arising of <s>prātibha</s> knowledge, the <s>yogin</s> knows everything. || 33 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
ātmani saṁyamaṁ kurvataḥ, īśvaraṁ vā atyantaṁ praṇidadhānasya yoginaḥ prātibhaṁ tārakaṁ svayamutthitaṁ mānasaṁ jñānam, tat vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇasya vivekajasya jñānasya pūrvarūpam । yathā udaye prabhā auṣasī kiñcidunmīlantī lohitāyamānā bhāskarasya ujjigamiṣataḥ pūrvarūpam । tasmādā sarvaṁ vijānanti yoginaḥ prātibhasya jñānasya utpādāditi ॥ 33 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
For a <s>yogin</s> who performs <s>saṁyama</s> on the self, or who intensely devotes himself to <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), <s>prātibha</s> is the spontaneously-arisen mental knowledge called <s>tāraka</s> (transcendent). It is the precursor of the knowledge born of discrimination (<s>vivekaja-jñāna</s>) whose characteristics will be described later. Just as the dawn glow — slightly opening, becoming reddish — is the precursor of the sun about to rise. Therefore, <s>yogins</s> know everything from the arising of <s>prātibha</s> knowledge. || 33 ||

body.text: hadaye cittasaṁvit ॥ 34 ॥
body.translated_text: From [<s>saṁyama</s>] on the heart, understanding of <s>citta</s> (mind). || 34 ||

body.text: yadidamasminbrahmapure daharaṁ puṇḍarīkaṁ veśma tatra vijñānaṁ tasminsaṁyamāccittasaṁvit ॥ 34 ॥
body.translated_text: In this city of <s>Brahman</s> (the body), there is a small lotus-dwelling (<s>dahara puṇḍarīka veśma</s>); therein is consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>). Through <s>saṁyama</s> on that, understanding of <s>citta</s> [arises]. || 34 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[hṛdaye cittasaṁvit । yadidamasmin brahmapure] śarīre [daharam] alpaṁ [puṇḍarīkaṁ] puṇḍarīkākāromāṁ sa piṇḍo'dhomukhaḥ, veśmavadane kanāḍīsuṣirayogāt [veśma । tatra vijñānaṁ cittaṁ, tasmin] urassaro vilagnanāleprāṇaveśmanipuṇḍarīke [saṁyamāccitte] sattve [saṁvit] bhavati [॥ 34 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['From saṁyama on the heart, understanding of citta. In this city of Brahman'] — the body — ['the small'] — tiny — ['lotus'] — a lump of flesh in the shape of a lotus, facing downward, ['dwelling'] — like a house, due to the openings of the <s>nāḍī</s> (channels). ['Therein is consciousness'] — the <s>citta</s>. ['Through saṁyama on that'] lotus of the heart-lake, connected by a stalk to the chest, the dwelling of <s>prāṇa</s>, ['understanding of citta'] — of <s>sattva</s> — ['arises.' || 34 ||]

body.text: sattvapuruṣayoratyantāsaṁkīrṇayoḥ pratyayāviśeṣo bhogaḥ parārthātsvārthasaṁyamātpuruṣajñānam ॥ 35 ॥
body.translated_text: Experience (<s>bhoga</s>) is a cognition that does not distinguish between <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, which are absolutely distinct. From <s>saṁyama</s> on self-purpose (<s>svārtha</s>), as distinct from other-purpose (<s>parārtha</s>), knowledge of <s>Puruṣa</s> [arises]. || 35 ||

body.text: buddhisattvaṁ prakhyāśīlaṁ samānasattvopanibandhane rajastamasī vaśīkṛtya sattvapuruṣānyatāpratyayena pariṇatam। tasmācca sattvātpariṇāmino'tyantavidharmā viśuddho'nyaścitimātrarūpaḥ puruṣaḥ। tayoratyantāsaṁkīrṇayoḥ pratyayāviśeṣo bhogaḥ puruṣasya darśitaviṣayatvāt। sa bhogapratyayaḥ sattvasya parārthatvāddṛśyaḥ।
body.translated_text: The <s>sattva</s> of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), whose nature is luminosity (<s>prakhyā</s>), having subjugated <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> — which have their basis in a common <s>sattva</s> — is transformed through the cognition of the distinction between <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>. And from that <s>sattva</s>, which is subject to transformation, <s>Puruṣa</s> is completely different — pure, other, of the nature of mere consciousness (<s>citimātra</s>). The non-distinction of cognition between these two, which are completely unmixed, is experience (<s>bhoga</s>), because <s>Puruṣa</s> has objects shown to it. That experiential cognition, because <s>sattva</s> exists for another's purpose, is the seen (<s>dṛśya</s>).

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[sattvapuruṣayoratyantāsaṁkīrṇayoḥ pratyayāviśeṣo bhogaḥ parārthātsvārthasaṁyamātpuruṣajñānam । sattvaṁ] cittaṁ, [puruṣo] bhoktā, tayoḥ [atyantāsaṅkīrṇayoḥ] atyantavilakṣaṇayoratīvapṛthagbhūtayoḥ vṛttisārūpyaṁ [pratyayāviśeṣaḥ] , sa [bhogaḥ] puruṣasya । [parārthāt] sattvāt puruṣapratyayena saṅgīṇībhāsādvivicya [svārthe] citimātrasvarūpe [saṁyamāt puruṣajñānaṁ bhavati ॥]
kīdṛśaṁ tatparārthaṁ cittasattvam? yato vivicya svārthe puruṣe saṁyamaḥ kriyata iti । [buddhisattvaṁ prakhyāśīlaṁ] samānaṁ sattvaṁ vastukāryaṁ puruṣārthakartavyatayā samavasthānam upanibandhanaṁ yayoste [samānasatvopanibandhane rajastamasī vaśīkṛtya] nyagbhāvamāpādya [sattvapuruṣānyatāpratyayena] yoginaḥ [pariṇatam ॥]
[tasmācca sattvāt pariṇāminaḥ] triguṇādanityādaśuddhāt parārthādacetanāt [atyantavidharmā viśuddho'nyaḥ] apariṇāmī svārtho nityaḥ [cinmātrarūpaḥ puruṣaḥ ॥]
[tayoratyantāsaṅkīrṇayoḥ pratyayāviśeṣobhogaḥ puruṣasya darśitaviṣayatvāt । sa bhogapratyayaḥ ।] nāpariṇāmitve sati darśitaviṣayatvādanyo bhogaḥ sambhavati । [sattvasya parārthatvāt] aviśiṣṭhībhogapratyayo dṛśyaḥ puruṣeṇa ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['The non-distinction of cognition between <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, which are completely unmixed, is experience; from <s>saṁyama</s> on one's own purpose as distinct from that which serves another's purpose, knowledge of <s>Puruṣa</s> arises. <s>Sattva</s>'] is <s>citta</s> (mind), ['<s>Puruṣa</s>'] is the experiencer (<s>bhoktā</s>). Of these two, ['completely unmixed'] — completely distinct, extremely separate — the similarity with mental modification is ['the non-distinction of cognition']; that is ['experience'] of <s>Puruṣa</s>. ['From that which serves another's purpose'] — discriminating <s>sattva</s> from the appearance of being mixed with <s>Puruṣa</s>'s cognition, ['from <s>saṁyama</s> on one's own purpose'] — on the nature of mere consciousness — ['knowledge of <s>Puruṣa</s> arises.']
What kind is that <s>citta-sattva</s> which serves another's purpose? Because discriminating from it, <s>saṁyama</s> is performed on <s>Puruṣa</s> as one's own purpose. ['The <s>sattva</s> of <s>buddhi</s>, whose nature is luminosity'] — the common <s>sattva</s>, the functional effect, the established state for the purpose of accomplishing <s>Puruṣa</s>'s ends — this is the basis of those two; ['having subjugated <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, which have their basis in common <s>sattva</s>'] — having brought them to a subordinate state — ['it is transformed through the cognition of the distinction between <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>'] by the <s>yogin</s>.
['And from that <s>sattva</s>, which is subject to transformation'] — which is of the three <s>guṇas</s>, impermanent, impure, serving another's purpose, and insentient — ['completely different, pure, other'] — non-transforming, self-purposive, eternal — ['of the nature of mere consciousness (<s>citimātra</s>) is <s>Puruṣa</s>.']
['The non-distinction of cognition between these two, which are completely unmixed, is experience, because <s>Puruṣa</s> has objects shown to it. That is the experiential cognition.'] No other experience is possible when there is non-transformation, through having objects shown to it. ['Because <s>sattva</s> exists for another's purpose,'] the non-differentiated experiential cognition is seen (<s>dṛśya</s>) by <s>Puruṣa</s>.

body.text: yastu tasmādviśiṣṭaścitimātrarūpo'nyaḥ pauruṣeyaḥ pratyayastatra saṁyamātpuruṣaviṣayā prajñā jāyate। na ca puruṣapratyayena buddhisattvātmanā puruṣo dṛśyate। puruṣa eva taṁ pratyayaṁ svātmāvalambanaṁ paśyati। tathā hyuktam - vijñātāramare kena vijānīyāt iti ॥ 35 ॥
body.translated_text: But the cognition that is distinct from that, of the nature of mere consciousness (<s>citimātra</s>), different, belonging to <s>Puruṣa</s> — from <s>saṁyama</s> on that, knowledge (<s>prajñā</s>) having <s>Puruṣa</s> as its object arises. And <s>Puruṣa</s> is not seen through the cognition of <s>Puruṣa</s> that has the nature of <s>buddhi-sattva</s>. <s>Puruṣa</s> himself sees that cognition which has his own self as its support. As it has been stated — 'By what, O dear one, would one know the knower?' ॥ 35 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[yastu tasmāt] gauṇapratyayāt pratyayinaśca [viśiṣṭaścitimātrarūpo'nyaḥ pauruṣeyaḥ pratyayaḥ] , svārthaḥ puruṣa eva pariṇāmānupapatteḥ pratyayaḥ । [tatra saṁyamāt puruṣaviṣayāprajñā jāyate ॥]
nanu ca yadi puruṣaḥ pratyayasya viṣayīkriyate, tena cetpuruṣo gṛhyate, parārthaḥ puruṣaḥ prāpnoti । naiṣa doṣaḥ । [na ca puruṣapratyayena] puruṣaviṣayeṇa pratyayena [buddhisattvātmanā] buddhisattvadharmeṇa [puruṣo dṛśyate] buddheracetanatvāt ॥
[puruṣa eva taṁ pratyayaṁ svālambanaṁ] puruṣābhāsaṁ [paśyati] puruṣābhāsatvameva pratyayasya puruṣālambanatvam । na pratyayasya puruṣālambanatvam । yathā mukhasannidhau darpaṇo mukhākareṇa pariṇamate, tathā cittaṁ puruṣākāreṇa pariṇataṁ puruṣābhāsaṁ puruṣeṇa gṛhyate ॥
[tathā coktaṁ – ‘vijñātāramarekena vijānīyāt'] iti । na kasyacitpuruṣaḥ karmatāṁ pratipadyata ityarthaḥ ॥
nanu cakṣurādarśatalapratihataṁ pratinivṛtya yathā mukhasya grāhakam, evaṁ puruṣo'pi cittasattvapratihataḥ pratinivṛtya svātmānaṁ gṛhṇīyāt – na – pariṇāmānupapatteḥ puruṣasya । nahyapariṇāminaścittaṁ prati pravṛttiḥ pratinivṛttirvīsādhimānamupānuvīta ॥
na cāpi cakṣuḥ pratinivṛtya mukhaṁ grāhayati । mukhasya darpaṇamaṇḍalādhikaraṇatvena anubhūyamānatvāt । na hi svamukhaṁ darpaṇādhikaraṇastham । kiṁca, ādarśānuvidhānāca । yathā svaḍge dīrdhamukhe dṛśyate । na svamukhaṁ dīrdham । pratihatena cedupalamyeta cakṣuṣā nijamukhaṁ, tatra ādarśānuvidhānamayuktam ॥ 35 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['But that which'] is distinct from that secondary cognition and from the cognizable object, ['of the nature of mere consciousness, different, the cognition belonging to <s>Puruṣa</s>'] — being self-purposive, it is <s>Puruṣa</s>'s own cognition, since transformation is impossible for him. ['From <s>saṁyama</s> on that, knowledge having <s>Puruṣa</s> as its object arises.']
Now, if <s>Puruṣa</s> is made the object of a cognition, and if through that <s>Puruṣa</s> is grasped, then <s>Puruṣa</s> would exist for another's purpose. This is no fault. ['And <s>Puruṣa</s> is not seen through the cognition of <s>Puruṣa</s>'] — through a cognition having <s>Puruṣa</s> as its object — ['which has the nature of <s>buddhi-sattva</s>'] — which has the property of <s>buddhi-sattva</s> — ['<s>Puruṣa</s> is not seen,'] because <s>buddhi</s> is insentient.
['<s>Puruṣa</s> himself sees that cognition which has his own self as its support'] — the reflection of <s>Puruṣa</s> — ['he sees it.'] The fact of the cognition being a reflection of <s>Puruṣa</s> is itself what constitutes it having <s>Puruṣa</s> as its support. It is not that the cognition truly has <s>Puruṣa</s> as its object. Just as a mirror transforms into the form of a face when near a face, so the mind (<s>citta</s>), transformed into the form of <s>Puruṣa</s>, is grasped by <s>Puruṣa</s> as a reflection of <s>Puruṣa</s>.
['And thus it has been stated — "By what, O dear one, would one know the knower?"'] The meaning is that <s>Puruṣa</s> never assumes the status of being an object for anyone.
Now, just as the eye, reflected back from the surface of a mirror, becomes the grasper of the face — similarly, might not <s>Puruṣa</s> too, reflected back from <s>citta-sattva</s>, grasp his own self? No — because transformation is impossible for <s>Puruṣa</s>. For there is no going forth or turning back for one who does not undergo transformation with respect to the mind.
Nor does the eye, by turning back, cause the face to be grasped. Because the face is experienced as located in the domain of the mirror surface. For one's own face is not located in the mirror. Moreover, because of conformity to the mirror — just as in a long mirror, the face appears long. One's own face is not long. And if the face were perceived by the reflected eye, then conformity to the mirror would be unjustified. ॥ 35 ॥

body.text: tataḥ prātibhaśrāvaṇavedanādarśāsvādavārtā jāyante ॥ 36 ॥
body.translated_text: From that arise <s>prātibha</s> (intuitive), <s>śrāvaṇa</s> (auditory), <s>vedanā</s> (tactile), <s>ādarśa</s> (visual), <s>āsvāda</s> (gustatory), and <s>vārtā</s> (olfactory) [perceptions]. ॥ 36 ॥

body.text: prātibhātsūkṣmavyavahitaviprakṛṣṭātītānāgatajñānam। śrāvaṇāddivyaśabdaśravaṇam। vedanāddivya-sparśādhigamaḥ। ādarśāddivyarūpasaṁvit। āsvādāddivyarasasaṁvit। vārtāto divyagandhavijñānamityetāni nityaṁ jāyante ॥ 36 ॥
body.translated_text: From <s>prātibha</s> (intuitive knowledge) arises knowledge of subtle, hidden, distant, past, and future things. From <s>śrāvaṇa</s> arises the hearing of divine sounds. From <s>vedanā</s> arises the attainment of divine touch. From <s>ādarśa</s> arises perception of divine forms. From <s>āsvāda</s> arises perception of divine tastes. From <s>vārtā</s> arises knowledge of divine smells — these arise constantly. ॥ 36 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tataḥ prātibhāśrāvaṇavedanādarśasvādavārtā jāyante । tataḥ] svārthe samādhānāt, [prātibhāt] ātmasaṁyamajanitātā mānasāt jñānāt, [sūkṣmavyavahitaviprakṛṣṭātītānāgatajñānaṁ] sampadyate । [śrāvaṇāt divyaśabdānāṁ śravaṇam । vedanāt] sparśajñānāt [siddhādīnāṁ sparśaṁ jānāti । ādarśāt] cākṣuṣāt jñānāt divyaṁ rūpam avagacchati । [āsvādāt] rasanendriyajñānāt [divavyarasasaṁvedanaṁ] bhavati । vṛttau bhavaṁ [vārtaṁ] lokasaṁvyavahārajñānaṁ, tasmādeṣa [saṁvyavahārataruvarūpaṁ yathāvadadhigacchati ॥ 36 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['From that arise <s>prātibha</s>, <s>śrāvaṇa</s>, <s>vedanā</s>, <s>ādarśa</s>, <s>āsvāda</s>, and <s>vārtā</s> perceptions. From that'] — from <s>samādhi</s> focused on one's own purpose, ['from <s>prātibha</s>'] — from mental knowledge born of <s>saṁyama</s> on the self — ['knowledge of subtle, hidden, distant, past, and future things'] is attained. ['From <s>śrāvaṇa</s>, hearing of divine sounds. From <s>vedanā</s>'] — from tactile knowledge — ['one knows the touch of <s>siddhas</s> (perfected beings) and others. From <s>ādarśa</s>'] — from visual knowledge — one perceives divine form. ['From <s>āsvāda</s>'] — from knowledge of the taste sense — ['perception of divine tastes'] arises. That which arises in activity is ['<s>vārta</s>'] — knowledge of worldly dealings; from that, ['one comprehends the form of worldly dealings as they truly are.' ॥ 36 ॥]

body.text: te samādhāvupasargā vyutthāne siddhayaḥ ॥ 37 ॥
body.translated_text: These are obstacles (<s>upasarga</s>) in <s>samādhi</s>, but accomplishments (<s>siddhi</s>) in the outward-turned state (<s>vyutthāna</s>). ॥ 37 ॥

body.text: te prātibhādayaḥ samāhitacittasyotpadyamānā upasargāstaddarśanapratyanīkatvāt। vyutthitacittasyotpadyamānāḥ siddhayaḥ ॥ 37 ॥
body.translated_text: These <s>prātibha</s> and other [perceptions], when arising for one whose mind is concentrated (<s>samāhita-citta</s>), are obstacles — because they are contrary to that vision (of <s>Puruṣa</s>). When arising for one whose mind is in the outward-turned state, they are accomplishments (<s>siddhis</s>). ॥ 37 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[te samādhāvupasargāvyutthāne siddhayaḥ । te prātibhādayaḥ] puruṣe [samāhitacittasya u(syasamu)tpadyamānā upasargāḥ puruṣadarśanapratyanīkatvāt । vyutthitacittasyotpadyamānāḥ siddhayaḥ ।] yadyapi puruṣe saṁyamādutpadyante, tathāpi na viraktasya samāhitacittasya jāyante ॥ 37 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['These are obstacles in <s>samādhi</s>, but accomplishments in the outward-turned state. These <s>prātibha</s> and other perceptions,'] regarding <s>Puruṣa</s>, ['when arising for one whose mind is concentrated, are obstacles — because they are contrary to the vision of <s>Puruṣa</s>. When arising for one whose mind is in the outward-turned state, they are accomplishments.'] Although they arise from <s>saṁyama</s> on <s>Puruṣa</s>, they do not arise for the dispassionate one whose mind is concentrated. ॥ 37 ॥

body.text: bandhakāraṇaśaithilyātpracārasaṁvedanācca cittasya paraśarīrāveśaḥ ॥ 38 ॥
body.translated_text: From the loosening of the cause of bondage and from the knowledge of the mind's pathways of movement, [there arises] entry into another body (<s>paraśarīrāveśa</s>). ॥ 38 ॥

body.text: lolībhūtasya manaso'pratiṣṭhasya śarīre karmāśayavaśādbandhaḥ pratiṣṭhetyarthaḥ। tasya karmaṇo bandhakāraṇasya śaithilyaṁ samādhibalādbhavati। pracārasaṁvedanaṁ ca cittasya samādhijameva। karmabandhakṣayātsvacittasya pracārasaṁvedanācca yogī cittaṁ svaśarīrānniṣkṛṣya śarīrāntareṣu nikṣipati। nikṣiptaṁ cittaṁ cendriyāṇyanupatanti। yathā madhukararājānaṁ makṣikā utpatantamanūtpatanti niviśamānamanuniviśante tathendriyāṇi paraśarīrāveśe cittamanuvidhīyanta iti ॥ 38 ॥
body.translated_text: The mind, having become unstable (<s>lolībhūta</s>), without firm footing in the body — its bondage, meaning its establishment, occurs due to the force of <s>karmāśaya</s> (latent impressions of actions). The loosening of that <s>karma</s>, the cause of bondage, occurs through the power of <s>samādhi</s>. And the knowledge of the mind's pathways of movement is also born of <s>samādhi</s> alone. Through the weakening of the bondage of <s>karma</s> and through knowledge of the pathways of one's own mind, the <s>yogin</s> withdraws the mind from his own body and deposits it in other bodies. When the mind is deposited, the senses follow it — just as bees follow the queen bee: when she flies up, they fly up; when she alights, they alight — so too the senses conform to the mind when entering another body. ॥ 38 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[bandhakāraṇaśaithilyāt pracārasaṁvedanācca cittasya paraśarīrāveśaḥ । lolībhūtasya] ghaṇṭābhighātatulyasya dedīpyamānāṅgārarāśidyuticañcalasya [manaso'pratiṣṭhasya śarīre karmāśayādbandhaḥ pratiṣṭhetyarthaḥ ।] śarīramātrasaṁkocāvasthānam ॥
tasya [bandhasya karma] kāraṇam । [kāraṇaśaithilyaṁ,] karmāśayaśithilatvaṁ [samādhibalādbhavati । pracārasaṁvedanaṁ ca cittasya samādhijameva । karmabandhakṣayāt svacittapracārasaṁvedanācca] ‘asminnimitte hṛṣyati muhyati lubhyati cānena kāraṇena' ityevamādisvacittasañcaraṇasatattvavedanācca [yogī cittaṁ svaśarīrānniṣkṛṣya śarīrāntareṣu nikṣipati ॥]
[cittam] asya utpatat indriyāṇi [anutpatanti ।] tasmādindriyavṛttilābhātparaśarīreṣu prāṇādivṛttaya utpadyante । [yathā madhukararājaṁ makṣikā utpatantamanutpatanti, niviśamānamanuniviśante, tathendriyāṇi paraśarīrāveśe cittamanu vidhīyante ॥ 38 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['From the loosening of the cause of bondage and from the knowledge of the mind's pathways of movement, entry into another body. The mind, having become unstable'] — like the vibration produced by striking a bell, flickering like the radiance of a blazing mass of embers — ['without firm footing in the body, its bondage, its establishment, occurs due to the force of <s>karmāśaya</s>' (latent impressions of actions).] This means confinement to the body alone.
Of that ['bondage, <s>karma</s>'] is the cause. ['The loosening of the cause'] — the weakening of the <s>karmāśaya</s> — ['occurs through the power of <s>samādhi</s>. And the knowledge of the mind's pathways of movement is also born of <s>samādhi</s> alone. Through the weakening of the bondage of <s>karma</s> and through knowledge of the pathways of one's own mind'] — 'on this occasion it rejoices, on that it is deluded, on that it craves, and for this reason' — through such true understanding of the movements of one's own mind — ['the <s>yogin</s> withdraws the mind from his own body and deposits it in other bodies.']
['The mind'] of this one rises up, and the senses ['follow it.'] Therefore, from the attainment of sensory function in other bodies, vital activities such as <s>prāṇa</s> and the like arise. ['Just as bees follow the queen bee: when she flies up, they fly up; when she alights, they alight — so too the senses conform to the mind when entering another body.' ॥ 38 ॥]

body.text: udānajayājjalapaṅkakaṇṭakādiṣvasaṅga utkrāntiśca ॥ 39 ॥
body.translated_text: From mastery of <s>udāna</s>, [there arises] non-contact with water, mud, thorns, and the like, and ascension [at the time of death]. ॥ 39 ॥

body.text: samastendriyavṛttiḥ prāṇādilakṣaṇā jīvanaṁ, tasya kriyā pañcatayī prāṇo mukhanāsikāgatirāhṛdayavṛttiḥ। samaṁ nayanātsamānaścā''nābhivṛttiḥ। apanayanādapāna āpādatalavṛttiḥ। unnayanādudāna āśirovṛttiḥ। vyāpī vyāna iti। eṣāṁ pradhānaṁ prāṇaḥ। udānajayājjalapaṅkakaṇṭakādiṣvasaṅga utkrāntiśca prāyaṇakāle bhavati। tāṁ vaśitvena pratipadyate ॥ 39 ॥
body.translated_text: The function of all the senses collectively, characterized by <s>prāṇa</s> and the other [vital airs], is life (<s>jīvana</s>). Its activity is fivefold: <s>prāṇa</s> is the movement through the mouth and nose, functioning in the region of the heart. <s>Samāna</s>, from equalizing, functions in the navel region. <s>Apāna</s>, from carrying downward, functions from the soles of the feet [upward]. <s>Udāna</s>, from carrying upward, functions up to the head. <s>Vyāna</s> is all-pervading. Among these, <s>prāṇa</s> is the chief. From mastery of <s>udāna</s>, non-contact with water, mud, thorns, and the like [arises], and ascension (<s>utkrānti</s>) occurs at the time of death. One attains it through mastery. ॥ 39 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[udānajayājjalapaṅkakaṇṭakādiṣvasaṅga utkrāntiśca । samastendriyavṛttiḥ jīvanaṁ] sarveṣāmekādaśānāmindriyāṇāṁ vartanaṁ jīvanam । yathā pañjaragataśakunisañcalanena pañjaracalanam, evam aśeṣakaraṇānamekena saṁmūrchitena vyāpāreṇa yena śarīraṁ dhriyate tajjīvanam । [tasya] jīvanasya puruṣārthakartavyatāniyamāt [pañcatayī kriyā] prāṇāpānavyānodānasaṁmānabhedena prastīryate ॥
[tatra prāṇo mukhanāsikāgātirāhṛdayavṛttiḥ । samaṁ nayanātsamāna: ānābhivṛttiḥ] ānābhideśaṁ vartate । mūtrapurīṣādīnām [apanayanādapānaḥ,] sa ca nābhiprabhṛti [āpādatalaṁ vartate । ūrdhvaṁ] śarīrasya [nayanādudānaḥ,] sa ca pādatalādārabhya [āmastakavṛttiḥ ।] samastaśarīra [vyāpī vyāna iti ॥]
[eteṣāṁ pradhānaḥ prāṇaḥ ।] tajjayācca sarveṣāmapānādīnāṁ tu jayo bhavati । teṣāṁ tu jayopāye vistareṇa hairaṇyagarbhe vyākhyātaḥ । iha tu manojayānujitatvājjayopāyona pṛthagabhihitaḥ । prāṇāyāmajayāttu jīyanta eva । napṛthageṣāṁ jayopāyapratipādanamādṛṣyamiti phalamātramudānajiterucyate–
[udānajayāt jalapaṅkakaṇṭakādiṣu,] ādinā kṛpāṇadhārādiṣu asaṅgaḥ । kiṁca, [utkrāntiśca prāyaṇakāle bhavati । tāṁ] prāyaṇakāle bhavantīmutkrāntimudānajayāt [vaśīkṛtya] svatantratayā [pratipadyate ॥ 39 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['From mastery of <s>udāna</s>, non-contact with water, mud, thorns, and the like, and ascension. The function of all the senses collectively is life (<s>jīvana</s>)'] — the functioning of all eleven senses is life. Just as the movement of a bird in a cage causes the cage to move, so by the single, unified operation of all the instruments, by which the body is sustained — that is life. ['Its'] — of life — because of the restriction to accomplishing <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose, ['the fivefold activity'] is extended through the divisions of <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, <s>vyāna</s>, <s>udāna</s>, and <s>samāna</s>.
['Among these, <s>prāṇa</s> is the movement through the mouth and nose, functioning in the region of the heart. <s>Samāna</s>, from equalizing, functions in the navel region'] — it operates in the region of the navel. ['<s>Apāna</s>, from carrying downward'] — of urine, feces, and the like — it ['operates from the navel down to the soles of the feet. <s>Udāna</s>, from carrying upward'] the body, it ['operates from the soles of the feet up to the crown of the head. <s>Vyāna</s> pervades'] the entire body.]
['Among these, <s>prāṇa</s> is the chief.'] And from its mastery, the mastery of all the others — <s>apāna</s> and so forth — also comes about. The method for mastering them has been explained in detail in the <s>Hairaṇyagarbha</s> [system]. Here, however, because they are subdued following the subduing of the mind, the method of mastery is not stated separately. But through mastery of <s>prāṇāyāma</s> they are indeed subdued. Since the separate exposition of their method of mastery is not considered necessary, only the result of mastery over <s>udāna</s> is stated —
['From mastery of <s>udāna</s>, non-contact with water, mud, thorns, and the like'] — by the word 'and the like,' also with the edges of swords and such. Moreover, ['ascension occurs at the time of death. That'] ascension which occurs at the time of death, ['through mastery of <s>udāna</s>,'] one ['attains'] it with independence. [॥ 39 ॥]

body.text: samānajayājjvalanam ॥ 40 ॥
body.translated_text: From mastery of <s>samāna</s>, [there arises] effulgence (<s>jvalana</s>). ॥ 40 ॥

body.text: jitasamānastejasa upadhmānaṁ kṛtvā jvalayati ॥ 40 ॥
body.translated_text: One who has mastered <s>samāna</s>, having fanned the fire (<s>tejas</s>), blazes forth. ॥ 40 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[samānajayāt jvalanam ।] jitasamānaḥ [tejasa upadhmānaṁ kṛtvā] samānavāyvāśrayatvāt udānatejasoḥ tadupadhmānarmakārakastāvadyegī । jāṭharaṁ jvalayati [॥ 40 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['From mastery of <s>samāna</s>, effulgence.'] One who has mastered <s>samāna</s>, ['having fanned the fire'] — because <s>udāna</s> and <s>tejas</s> (fire) depend on <s>samāna-vāyu</s> (the equalizing breath), the <s>yogin</s> becomes the agent of fanning it. He causes the digestive fire (<s>jāṭhara</s>) to blaze. [॥ 40 ॥]

body.text: śrotrākāśayoḥ saṁbandhasaṁyamāddivyaṁ śrotram ॥ 41 ॥
body.translated_text: From <s>saṁyama</s> on the relation between the ear and space (<s>ākāśa</s>), [there arises] divine hearing (<s>divya śrotra</s>). ॥ 41 ॥

body.text: sarvaśrotrāṇāmākāśaṁ pratiṣṭhā sarvaśabdānāṁ ca। yathoktam – tulyadeśaśravaṇānāmekadeśaśrutitvaṁ sarveṣāṁ bhavatīti। taccaitadākāśasya liṅgam।
body.translated_text: Space (<s>ākāśa</s>) is the foundation of all ears, and of all sounds. As it has been stated — 'For those whose organs of hearing are in the same location, the hearing is singular for all.' And this is the characteristic mark of space (<s>ākāśa</s>).

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[śrotrākāśayoḥ saṁbandhasaṁyamāddivyaṁ śrotram ।] kaḥ punarasau saṁbandho yatra saṁyama ityāha– [sarvaśrotrāṇāmākāśaṁ pratiṣṭhā । śabdānāṁ] cākāśaguṇatvādākāśameva pratiṣṭhā । grāhyaṁ śabdaṁ pratiśrotrasya vyavadhānābhāvaḥ śrotrākāśayoḥ sambandhaḥ ॥
[tathācoktam - tulyadeśaśravaṇānām ।] śrūyate'neneti śravaṇam । tulyadeśāni śravaṇāni yeṣāṁ te tulyadeśaśravaṇāḥ । teṣām [ekaśrutitvaṁ sarveṣāṁ bhavati ।] tadekasminnavakāśadāyininirāvaraṇātmake vastuni sati yujyate । [taccaitadākāśasya] sattve [liṅgam ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['From <s>saṁyama</s> on the relation between the ear and space, divine hearing.'] What then is that relation on which <s>saṁyama</s> is performed? He says — ['Space is the foundation of all ears.'] And ['of sounds'] — because sound is a quality of space (<s>ākāśa-guṇa</s>), space alone is the foundation. The relation between the ear and space is the absence of obstruction between the ear and the sound that is to be grasped.
['And thus it has been stated — "For those whose organs of hearing are in the same location."] That by which one hears is the organ of hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>). Those whose organs of hearing are in the same location are called 'of the same location of hearing.' ['The hearing is singular for all of them.'] That is justified only when there exists a single entity that provides space, that is unobstructed in nature. ['And this is the characteristic mark'] — the evidence for ['the existence of space.']

body.text: anāvaraṇaṁ coktam। tathā'mūrtasyānāvaraṇadarśanādvibhutvamapi prakhyātamākāśasya। śabdagrahaṇānumitaṁ śrotram। badhirābadhirayorekaḥ śabdaṁ gṛhṇātyaparo na gṛhṇātīti। tasmācchrotrameva śabdaviṣayam। śrotrākāśayoḥ saṁbandhe kṛtasaṁyamasya yogino divyaṁ śrotraṁ pravartate ॥ 41 ॥
body.translated_text: And its unobstructed nature has been stated. Likewise, from the observation that the formless is unobstructed, the all-pervasiveness of space (<s>ākāśa</s>) has also become well known. The ear is inferred from the grasping of sound — of two persons, one deaf and one not deaf, one grasps the sound and the other does not. Therefore, it is the ear alone that has sound as its object. For the <s>yogin</s> who has performed <s>saṁyama</s> on the relation between the ear and space, divine hearing (<s>divya śrotra</s>) manifests. ॥ 41 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
tathā [anāvaraṇātmakaṁ coktam ।] (kutaḥ) [tathā mūrtasyānyatrākāśāt] ākāśavilakṣaṇasya ghaṭādeḥ [āvaraṇadarśanāt ।] ato yasya maṇivajrādimadhyeṣvapyāvaraṇaṁ nāsti, tadākāśam । ata eva [vibhutvamapi prakhyātamākāśasya ॥]
śrotrasya liṅgamāha – [śabdagrahaṇānumitaṁ tu śrotram ।] yasmāt [badhirābadhirayorekaḥ śabdaṁ gṛhṇāti aparo na gṛhṇāti ।] yannimittamabadhirasya śabdagrahaṇamitarasya cāgrahaṇaṁ tacchrotram । [tasmācchrotrameva śabdaviṣayam ।] badhireṇāśravaṇāt । [śrotrākāśayoḥ saṁbandhe kṛtasaṁyamasya yoginaḥ divyaṁ śrotraṁ pravartate ॥ 41 ॥]
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
Likewise, ['it is also said to be of the nature of non-obstruction.'] (Why?) ['Because obstruction is observed in material objects (mūrta) other than space'] — in things distinct from space, such as a pot. Therefore, that which has no obstruction even in the midst of gems, diamonds, and the like — that is space (ākāśa). For this very reason, ['the all-pervasiveness of space is also well-known.']
He states the mark of the organ of hearing — ['The organ of hearing is inferred from the apprehension of sound.'] Because ['of a deaf and a non-deaf person, one apprehends sound and the other does not.'] That on account of which the non-deaf person apprehends sound while the other does not — that is the organ of hearing (śrotra). ['Therefore, the organ of hearing alone has sound as its object.'] Because the deaf person does not hear. ['For the yogin who performs saṁyama on the connection between the organ of hearing and space, the divine ear arises.' || 41 ||]

body.text: kāyākāśayoḥ saṁbandhasaṁyamāllaghutūlasamāpatteścā''kāśagamanam ॥ 42 ॥
body.translated_text: From <s>saṁyama</s> on the connection between the body and space (<s>ākāśa</s>), and from <s>samāpatti</s> (attainment) on light objects like cotton, traversal of space [arises]. || 42 ||

body.text: yatra kāyastatrā''kāśaṁ tasyāvakāśadānātkāyasya tena saṁbandhaḥ prāptistatra kṛtasaṁyamo jitvā tatsaṁbandhaṁ laghuṣu vā tūlādiṣvā paramāṇubhyaḥ samāpattiṁ labdhvā jitasaṁbandho laghurbhavati। laghutvācca jale pādābhyāṁ viharati। tatastūrṇanābhitantumātre vihṛtya raśmiṣu viharati। tato yatheṣṭamākāśagatirasya bhavatīti ॥ 42 ॥
body.translated_text: Wherever the body is, there is space. Because it provides room for the body, the body has a connection with it — an attainment. Having performed <s>saṁyama</s> on that and having conquered that connection, or having attained <s>samāpatti</s> on light things like cotton down to atoms, one who has conquered the connection becomes light. Due to that lightness, one walks upon water with one's feet. Then, having moved upon something as fine as a spider's thread, one moves upon rays of light. Then one's movement through space becomes as one desires. || 42 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[kāyākāśayoḥ sambandhasaṁyamālladhutūlasamāpatteśca akāśagamanam । yatra kāyaḥ tatra ākāśam । tasya avakāśadānāt kāyasya] avinābhāvalakṣaṇaḥ [sambandhaḥ tena] ākāśena । [tatra] kāyākāśayoḥ itaretarāvinābhāvaprāptilakṣaṇasambandhe [kṛtasaṁyamo] yogī [jitvā tatsambandhaṁ] tato [laghuṣu tūlādiṣu ā paramāṇubhyaḥ samāpatteḥ jitasambandhaḥ] tūlādivallāghavaṁ pratipadyate ॥
jitakāyākāśasambandhaḥ samāpanna: tulāditulyalāghavaśīlanārthaṁ [jale pādābhyāṁ viharati । tataḥ] ūrdhvam [ūrṇanābhitantumātre] viharati । tatra sañjātakokilatantusamānalādhavaḥ [punaḥ raśmiṣu viharati ।] tato mātariśvani । tato [yatheṣṭam ākāśe gatirasya bhavati ॥ 42 ॥]
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
['From saṁyama on the connection between body and space, and from samāpatti on light cotton, traversal of space. Wherever the body is, there is space. Because it provides room for the body,'] the [connection] characterized by invariable concomitance [with] space. ['The yogin who performs saṁyama on that'] connection between body and space, characterized by their mutual invariable concomitance, ['having conquered that connection,'] then ['from samāpatti on light things like cotton down to atoms, having conquered the connection,'] attains lightness like cotton and such.
Having conquered the body-space connection and attained [samāpatti], in order to practice lightness equal to cotton and such, ['one walks upon water with one's feet. Then'] upward, ['one moves upon something as fine as a spider's thread.'] There, having acquired lightness equal to a spider's thread, ['one then moves upon rays of light.'] Then upon the wind. Then ['one's movement through space becomes as one desires.' || 42 ||]

body.text: bahirakalpitā vṛttirmahāvidehā tataḥ prakāśāvaraṇakṣayaḥ ॥ 43 ॥
body.translated_text: The external, non-imagined mental operation is the great bodiless state (<s>mahāvidehā</s>). From that, the destruction of the covering over luminosity [arises]. || 43 ||
