body.text: śarīrādbahimarnaso vṛttilābho videhā nāma dhāraṇā। sā yadi śarīrapratiṣṭhasya manaso bahirvṛttimātreṇa bhavati sā kalpitetyucyate। yā tu śarīranirapekṣā vahirbhūtasyaiva manaso bahirvṛttiḥ sā khalvakalpitā। tatra kalpitayā sādhayantyakalpitā mahāvidehāmiti। yayā paraśarīrāṇyāviśanti yoginaḥ। tataśca dhāraṇātaḥ prakāśātmano buddhisattvasya yadāvaraṇaṁ kleśakarma vipākatrayaṁ rajastamośūlaṁ tasya ca kṣayo bhavati ॥ 43 ॥
body.translated_text: The attainment of a mental operation outside the body is a concentration (<s>dhāraṇā</s>) called 'bodiless' (<s>videhā</s>). If that occurs merely through the outward operation of the mind while it is still established in the body, it is called 'imagined' (<s>kalpitā</s>). But when the outward operation belongs to the mind that has actually gone outside, independent of the body, that is indeed 'non-imagined' (<s>akalpitā</s>). Of these, through the imagined, one accomplishes the non-imagined — the <s>mahāvidehā</s> (great bodiless state) — by which <s>yogins</s> enter other bodies. And from that <s>dhāraṇā</s>, the covering over the luminous <s>buddhi-sattva</s> — the triad of <s>kleśa</s> (affliction), <s>karma</s> (action), and <s>vipāka</s> (fruition), rooted in <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> — is destroyed. || 43 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[bahirakalpitā vṛttirmahāvidehā tataḥ prakāśāvaraṇakṣayaḥ । śarīrāt bahiḥ] deśāntare viṣayaviśeṣe svayameva samādhibalāt upajāyate yā [manaso vṛttiḥ sā mahāvidehā nāma dhāraṇā । sā yadi śarīrapratiṣṭhasyaiva manaso vṛttimātreṇa bahiḥ viṣaye bhavati,] tadānīṁ [kalpitā ucyate ।] śarīrasthamanassaṅkalpapūrvakatvāt । [yā] tu samādhibalanimittāt śarīre bandhakāraṇaśaithilyāt [śarīranirapekṣā bahirbhūtasyaiva manaso bahirvṛttiḥ, sā khalu akalpitā] ityucyate । yathaiva kalpitāyāṁ śarīrāvadhika eva bahirvṛttilābhaḥ, evaṁ nākālpatāyāṁ śarīrādhiṣṭhānāvadhisamīkṣā ॥
sā cobhayyapividehaiva bahirupakalpitatvāt । tatra yā iya [makalpitā] mahāvideheti samākhyāyate । [tatra kalpitayā sādhayantyakalpitāṁ] mahāvidehām । kalpanāsaṁśīlanasādhyatvādakalpitāyāḥ kalpitayā ca saṁsādhayanti । [yayā] mahāvidehayā [paraśarīrāṇyāviśanti yoginaḥ । tataśca dhāraṇātaḥ] mahāvidehātaḥ [prakāśātmano buddhisattvasya yadāvaraṇaṁ kleśakarmavipākatrayaṁ rajastamomūlaṁ tasya ca kṣayaṁ bhavati ॥ 43 ॥]
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
['The external, non-imagined mental operation is the great bodiless state; from that, destruction of the covering over luminosity. Outside the body,'] in another location, upon a particular object, through the power of samādhi alone, there arises ['a mental operation — that is the dhāraṇā called mahāvidehā. If it occurs merely through the outward operation of the mind that is still established in the body,'] then ['it is called imagined.'] Because it is preceded by the intention of the mind dwelling in the body. ['But'] when, due to the loosening of the cause of bondage in the body through the power of samādhi, ['the outward operation of the mind that has actually gone outside, independent of the body, that is called non-imagined.'] Just as in the imagined state the outward mental operation extends only as far as the body, so too in the non-imagined state there is no such limitation to the body's foundation.
Both of these are indeed bodiless (videhā), since both operate externally. Of these, ['the non-imagined'] one is designated as mahāvidehā. ['Through the imagined, one accomplishes the non-imagined'] mahāvidehā. Because the non-imagined is accomplished through the practice of imagining, they accomplish it through the imagined. ['By which'] mahāvidehā, ['yogins enter other bodies. And from that dhāraṇā'] — from the mahāvidehā — ['the covering over the luminous buddhi-sattva — the triad of kleśa, karma, and vipāka, rooted in rajas and tamas — is destroyed.' || 43 ||]

body.text: sthūlasvarūpasūkṣmānvayārthavattvasaṁyamādbhūtajayaḥ ॥ 44 ॥
body.translated_text: From <s>saṁyama</s> on the gross, essential nature, subtle, inherent connection, and purposefulness [of the elements], mastery over the elements (<s>bhūtajaya</s>) [arises]. || 44 ||

body.text: tatra pārthivādyāḥ śabdādayo viśeṣāḥ sahā''kārādibhirdharmaiḥ sthūlaśabdena paribhāṣitāḥ। etadbhūtānāṁ prathamaṁ rūpam। dvitīyaṁ rūpaṁ svasāmānyaṁ mūrtirbhūmiḥ sneho jalaṁ vahniruṣṇatā vāyuḥ praṇāmī sarvatogatirākāśa ityetatsvarūpaśabdenocyate।
body.translated_text: Therein, the particularities (<s>viśeṣas</s>) such as sound and the rest, belonging to earth and the other [elements], together with properties (<s>dharmas</s>) beginning with form (<s>ākāra</s>), are designated by the term 'gross' (<s>sthūla</s>). This is the first aspect of the elements. The second aspect is their essential nature (<s>svarūpa</s>), their own universals: solidity is earth, fluidity is water, heat is fire, motility is wind, all-pervasiveness is space — this is expressed by the term 'svarūpa.'

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[sthūlasvarūpasūkṣmānvayārthavattvasaṁyamāt bhūtajayaḥ ।] sthūlaṁ ca svarūpaṁ ca sūkṣmaṁ cānvayaścārthavattvaṁ cetyevamekaikaṁ bhūtaṁ pañcātmakam । [tatra pārthivāḥ śabdādayaḥ] śabdasparśarūparasagandhāḥ [viśeṣāḥ] pañcalakṣaṇatanmātrārabdhatvātpṛthivyāḥ । [saha akārādamiḥ ।] pṛthivyāstāvadākārādayaḥ---
[ākāro gauravaṁ raukṣyaṁ ceraṇaṁ sthairyameva ca ।]
[sthitirbhedaḥ kṣamākārṣṇyaṁ kāṭhinyaṁ sarvabhogyatā ॥] iti ॥
tathā - snehahaprabhāsaikṣmyamārdavagauravarakṣāpavitratvasandhānādaya audakā guṇāḥ ॥
tathā – taijasāḥ ūrdhvabhāktvapāvanatādagdhṛtvapācakatvalāghavabhāsvaratvādayaḥ ॥
tathā – vāyavīyāḥ tiryagyānapavitratvākṣepabalanodanatvādayaḥ ॥
tathā – nābhasāḥ sarvagatyavyūhaviṣṭambhāḥ ॥
tadetaiḥ [ākārādibhiḥ sahaśabdādayo viśeṣāḥ sthūlabdena] saṁvyavahārārthaṁ śākhe [paribhāṣitāḥ ।] evamāpyāścatvāro rasādayo viśeṣāḥ saikṣmyādibhiḥ । saha, evaṁ taijasārūpādayasvayo viśeṣā ūrdhvabhāktvādibhiḥ sahasthūlā ucyante । tathā vāyavīyāḥ śabdasparśatiryakpātādayaḥ sthūlāviśeṣāḥ । evamākāśasyasarvagatatvādayaḥrathūlāviśeṣāḥ । tat [etat bhūtānāṁ prathamaṁ sthūlaṁ rūpaṁ uktam ॥]
[dvitīyam] adhunā [svarūpam] ucyate । tacca [sāmānyaṁ] pārthiveṣu bhinneṣvabhinnamanugataṁ [mūrtire] va bhūmiḥ iti । tathā rasādiṣvāpyeṣvanugataṁ sāmānyaṁ [sneha eva jalam] iti । tathaivāgneyeṣu rūpādiṣvanugataṁ sāmānyaṁ [vahniruṣṇatvame] va । tathā sparśatiryaikpātādiṣvanugataṁ sāmānyaṁ [praṇāmitvameva vāyuḥ] । tathā śabdādiṣvanugatam sāmānyaṁ [sarvatogatire] va [ākāśaḥ] , [ityetat svarūpaśabdenoktaṁ] dvitīyaṁ rūpam ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
['From saṁyama on the gross, essential nature, subtle, inherent connection, and purposefulness, mastery over the elements.'] Gross, essential nature, subtle, connection, and purposefulness — thus each element has five aspects. ['Therein, the particularities of earth are sound and the rest'] — sound, touch, form, taste, and smell — ['because earth is constituted of five tanmātras (subtle elements). Together with'] properties beginning with form. The properties of earth beginning with form are:
['Form, heaviness, roughness, motility, steadiness,'] ['stability, cleavability, patience, darkness, and hardness — being the object of all enjoyment.'] Thus.
Likewise, the qualities of water: fluidity, brightness, subtlety, softness, heaviness, purification, purity, cohesion, and so forth.
Likewise, the qualities of fire: upward-burning, purifying, consuming, cooking, lightness, luminosity, and so forth.
Likewise, the qualities of wind: lateral movement, purification, propelling, strength, impelling, and so forth.
Likewise, the qualities of space: all-pervasiveness, non-arrangement, and resistance.
With these ['properties beginning with form, the particularities such as sound are designated by the term "gross"'] — for the purpose of conventional usage, in the treatise. Similarly, the four particularities of water beginning with taste, together with subtlety and the rest; likewise the particularities of fire such as form, together with upward-burning; likewise the particularities of wind — sound, touch, lateral movement, and so forth — are called gross particularities. Likewise, the all-pervasiveness and other [properties] of space are gross particularities. ['This first gross aspect of the elements has been stated.']
['The second'] is now stated — ['essential nature.'] And that ['universal'] — the undifferentiated [nature] that pervades the differentiated earthy things — is ['solidity'] itself, earth.

body.text: asya sāmānyasya śabdādayo viśeṣāḥ। tathā coktam – ekajātisamanvitānāmeṣāṁ dharmamātravyāvṛttiriti।
body.translated_text: The particularities of this universal are sound and the rest. As it has been said: 'Of those endowed with a single class, the differentiation is through properties alone.'

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tasya sāmānyasya] rūpasya [śabdādayo viśeṣāḥ । tathā coktam] - [ekajātisamanvitānāṁ] sattvadiguṇasamanugatānām [eṣāṁ] bhūtānāṁ pṛthivyādīnasāmānyānāṁ śabdādidharmamātraṁ vyāvartate ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
['The particularities of that universal'] form ['are sound and the rest. As it has been said:'] ['Of those endowed with a single class'] — possessed of the quality of sattva and the like — ['of these'] elements such as earth, which share a common universal, only the properties beginning with sound are differentiated.

body.text: sāmānyaviśeṣasamudāyo'tra dravyam। dviṣṭho hi samūhaḥ pratyastamitabhedāvayavānugataḥ śarīraṁ vṛkṣo yūthaṁ vanamiti।
body.translated_text: The aggregate of universal and particular is here called substance (<s>dravya</s>). For a collection that is two-fold, with the distinctions of its parts subsumed, is [called] a body, a tree, a herd, or a forest.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[sāmānyaviśeṣasamudāyo dravyam ।] kasmāt? [dviṣṭho hi samūhaḥ] dvābhyāṁ prakārābhyāṁ sthito [dviṣṭhaḥ pratyastamitabhedāvayavaḥ] vyāvṛttapratyayaśūnya ityarthaḥ । yathā [śarīraṁ vṛkṣo yūthaṁ vanamiti ॥]
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
['The aggregate of universal and particular is substance.'] Why? ['For a collection established in two modes'] — situated in two aspects — ['two-fold, with the distinctions of its parts subsumed'] — meaning devoid of awareness of distinction. As in ['a body, a tree, a herd, or a forest.']

body.text: śabdenopāttabhedāvayavānugataḥ samūha ubhaye devamanuṣyāḥ। samūhasya devā eko bhāgo manuṣyā dvitīyo bhāgastābhyāmevābhidhīyate samūhaḥ।
body.translated_text: A collection in which the distinctions of parts are apprehended through the word [is illustrated by] 'both gods and humans' (<s>ubhaye devamanuṣyāḥ</s>). Gods are one part of the collection, humans are the second part — the collection is denoted by means of these two.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[upātabhedāvayavānugataḥ] āgṛhītabhedāvayavānugataḥ [samūhaḥ] ubhayaśabdenepādīyata । [ubhaye devamanuṣyā] iti । tadyathā – [samūhasya devā ekobhāgaḥ, manuṣyā ekobhāgaḥ । tābhyāmeva] bhāgābhyāmāgṛhītayathāsvabhedānugatābhyām । [abhidhīyate samūhaḥ] ubhaye iti ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
['A collection in which the distinctions of parts are apprehended'] — in which the distinctions of parts are grasped — ['is indicated by the word "ubhaye" (both).'] ['Both gods and humans.'] For example: ['Gods are one part of the collection, humans are one part. By these two'] parts — each accompanied by its respective grasped distinctions — ['the collection is denoted'] as 'both.'

body.text: sa ca bhedābhedavivakṣitaḥ। āmrāṇāṁ vanaṁ brāhmaṇānāṁ saṁgha āmravaṇaṁ brāhmaṇasaṁgha iti।
body.translated_text: And that [collection] is expressed with [both] difference and non-difference. 'A forest of mango trees,' 'an assembly of brāhmaṇas' — '<s>āmravanam</s>' (mango-forest), '<s>brāhmaṇasaṅgha</s>' (brāhmaṇa-assembly).

body.text:
vivaraṇam
tayoḥ [bhedābhedo vivakṣitaḥ āmrāṇāṁ vanam] iti । āmrāṇāmiti bhedena vivakṣā । vanamitybhedena । tābhyāṁ dvābhyāṁ bhadābhedābhyām । āmrāṇāṁ vanamiti ṣaṣṭhīprathamā । taddvayorvivakṣitaekaḥ samūha iti ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
Of those two, ['difference and non-difference are expressed:'] 'of mango trees' — expression through difference; 'forest' — through non-difference. By those two — by both difference and non-difference — 'of mango trees, the forest' — a genitive and nominative compound. The intended meaning is that one collection is expressed by both.

body.text: sa punardvividho yutasiddhāvayavo'yutasiddhāvayavaśca। yutasiddhāvayavaḥ samūho vanaṁ saṁgha iti। ayutasiddhāvayavaḥ saṁghātaḥ śarīraṁ vṛkṣaḥ paramāṇuriti। ayutasiddhāvayavabhedānugataḥ samūho dravyamiti patañjaliḥ। etatsvarūpamityuktam।
body.translated_text: That [aggregate] is again of two kinds: one whose parts are separately established (<s>yutasiddha</s>) and one whose parts are not separately established (<s>ayutasiddha</s>). A collection with separately established parts is a forest or an assembly. A composite with non-separately established parts is a body, a tree, or an atom. <s>Patañjali</s> [holds that] substance (<s>dravya</s>) is a collection whose non-separately-established parts are accompanied by distinctions. This is what is meant by 'essential nature' (<s>svarūpa</s>).

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[sa punardvividhaḥ] samūhaḥ - [yutasiddhāvayavo'yutasiddhāvayavaśca । yutasiddhāvayavaḥ] pṛthaksiddhāvayavaḥ [samūho vanaṁ saṅgha iti । ayutasiddhāvayavaḥ] apṛthaksiddhāvayavaḥ [saṅghātaḥ śarīraṁ vṛkṣaḥ paramāṇuriti ॥]
paramāṇūnāmapi sāvayavatvaṁ sattvādikāryatvānmūrtatvācca ghaṭādivadeva । [ayutasiddhāvayavabhedānugataḥ samūho dravyamiti patañjaliḥ । etatsvarūpamityuktaṁ] sāmānyaviśaṣātmakam ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
['That is again of two kinds'] — the collection — ['one whose parts are separately established and one whose parts are not separately established. One with separately established parts'] — parts that exist independently — ['a collection such as a forest or assembly. One with non-separately established parts'] — parts that do not exist independently — ['a composite such as a body, tree, or atom.']
Even atoms have parts, because they are effects of sattva and the like, and because they have material form — just like a pot and such. ['A collection whose non-separately-established parts are accompanied by distinctions is substance, according to Patañjali. This is what is meant by "essential nature"'] — consisting of universal and particular.

body.text: atha kimeṣāṁ sūkṣmarūpaṁ, tanmātraṁ bhūtakāraṇaṁ, tasyaiko'vayavaḥ paramāṇuḥ sāmānyaviśeṣātmā'yutasiddhāvayavabhedānugataḥ samudāya ityevaṁ sarvatanmātrāṇyetattṛtīyam। atha bhūtānāṁ caturthaṁ rūpaṁ khyātikriyāsthitiśīlā guṇāḥ kāryasvabhāvānupātino'nvaya śabdenoktāḥ। athaiṣāṁ paścamaṁ rūpamarthavattvaṁ, bhogāpavargārthatā guṇeṣvevānvayinī, guṇāstanmātrabhūtabhautikeṣviti sarvamarthavat। teṣvidānīṁ bhūteṣu pañcasu pañcarūpeṣu saṁyamāttasya tasya rūpasya darśanaṁ jayaśca prādurbhavati। tatra pañca bhūtasvarūpāṇi jitvā bhūtajayī bhavati। tajjayādvatsānusāriṇya iva gāvo'sya saṁkalpānuvidhāyinyo bhūtaprakṛtayo bhavanti ॥ 44 ॥
body.translated_text: Now, what is the subtle aspect of these? The <s>tanmātra</s> (subtle element) is the cause of the [gross] elements. Its single constituent part is the atom (<s>paramāṇu</s>) — an aggregate consisting of universal and particular, accompanied by the distinctions of non-separately-established parts — thus all the <s>tanmātras</s> constitute this third [aspect]. Now the fourth aspect of the elements: the <s>guṇas</s> (constituents), whose nature is luminosity (<s>khyāti</s>), activity (<s>kriyā</s>), and stability (<s>sthiti</s>), conforming to the nature of effects, are expressed by the term 'connection' (<s>anvaya</s>). Now their fifth aspect is purposefulness (<s>arthavattva</s>) — serving the purposes of experience (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>), which is inherent in the <s>guṇas</s> themselves; the <s>guṇas</s> [pervade] the <s>tanmātras</s>, elements, and their products — thus everything is purposeful. Now, from <s>saṁyama</s> on these five elements in their five aspects, the vision and mastery of each respective aspect arises. Having mastered the five essential natures of the elements, one becomes a conqueror of the elements. From that mastery, like cows following their calves, the elemental natures become obedient to his will. || 44 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[atha kimeṣāṁ sūkṣmaṁ rūpam iti । tanmātraṁ bhūtakāraṇam ।] anekaparamāṇuprārabdhatvāt [tasya] tanmātrasya [eko'vayavaḥ paramāṇuḥ] । so'pi [sāmānyaviśeṣātmā ayutasiddhāvayavabhedānugataḥ samudāya iti । evaṁ sarvatanmātrāṇi ।] tataśca tanmātrāṇi viśeṣavinirmuktāni tadavayavāśca paramāṇava iti [etat bhūtānāṁ tṛtīyaṁ] sūkṣmākhyaṁ rūpaṁ saṁyamasya viṣaya iti । tanmātrārabdhatvācca sāvayavamākāśamanityaṁ ca । na ca śabdavyatirekeṇa ākāśaṁ nāmadravyam upalabdhuṁ śakyam । dharmadharmiṇorabhedāt ॥
nanu ca keśādīnāṁ kṛṣṇimā'pyupaiti, śuklimāsamupajāyate । tathā ca apāyopajanadharmāṇaḥ kṛṣṇimādayaḥ te guṇāḥ । yattu na kṛṣṇimānamanuvinaśyati, śuklimānamanveti, taddravyam । evam ākāśādīnāmapiguṇavyatirekeṇa sadbhāvaḥ, śabdapratyayādibhedāt iti ॥
na--dṛṣṭāntābhāvāt । te eva kṛṣṇāḥ śuklāśca keśāḥ kṛṣṇaśuklatvādidharmai: pariṇamante । sarvaṁ hi sarvātmakamityuktam । na khalu kvacidapi kūṭasthe āśraye guṇāḥ śuklatvādayaḥ apāyopajanavanta upalabhyante । na ca kṛṣṇatvādivyapanayanena dravyasvarūpam । yadyapi – darśanasparśanābhyāṁ yadupalabhyate taddravyam iti, tadapyayutasiddharūpasparśasamudāyatvādubhābhyāṁ darśanasparśanābhyāṁ gṛhyata ityadoṣaḥ ॥
nanu ca na rūpaṁ sparśanena gṛhyate, nāpi darśanena sparśaḥ, yadubhābhyāṁ gṛhyate ‘yatpaśyāmitadevaspṛśāmī’ti taddravyam । yattu cakṣuṣaiva gṛhyate sparśanenaiva ca gṛhyate sa guṇa iti ॥
na – māṣatilayavādibhikṣajātivimiśrarāśāvanaikantikatvāt । gṛhyate ca darśanasparśanābhyāṁ rāśiḥ । kiṁca – darśanasparśane guṇasyaiva grāhake, bāhyendriyatvāt, śrotravat । na hi jātirapi guṇavyatiriktā vidyate bhede jāgrahaṇāt ॥ kiṁca, ghaṭādādāvapi parasparādhyāsena darśanasparśanābhyāṁ rūpasparśayoreva grahaṇam । yathedaṁrūpaṁ durgandhi surabhigandhi ceti । tasmādākāśamapi tanmātrārabdhaṁ śabdavyatirekeṇāśakyaṁ pratipattumiti sāvayavamanityaṁ ca ॥
[atha bhūtānāṁ caturthaṁ rūpam । khyātikriyāsthitiśīlāguṇāḥ kāryasvarūpānupātinaḥ] kāryadharmānuyāyinaḥ [anvayaśabdenoktāḥ ।] anugamāt । tadetadbhūtānāṁ caturthaṁ rūpaṁ saṁyamasya guṇānvayākhyo viṣayaḥ ॥
[athaiṣāṁ pañcamaṁ rūpamarthavatvam ।] asya vyākhyānaṁ [bhogāpavargārthatā ।] sā ca [guṇeṣvanvayinī ।] tatra yā guṇeṣvanuvṛttā bhogāpavargārthatātadidaṁ bhūtānāṁ pañcamaṁ rūpaṁ saṁyamasyārthavattvākhyo viṣayaḥ ॥
[guṇāstanmātreṣu bhūteṣu bhūtavikāreṣu] cānvayinaḥ । evaṁ tanmātraṁ sūkṣmarūpaṁ bhūtabhūtavikāreṣvanugatam । bhūtasvarūpaṁ ca sthūleṣu bhūtavikāreṣvanugatamiti [sarvamarthavat ।] guṇānāṁ bhogāpavargārthavatvātteṣāṁ ca sarvānvayitvāttadarthavattvena sarvaṁ bhūtāvikārādikam arthavat ॥
[teṣvidānīṁ bhūteṣu pañcasu pañcarūpeṣu] sthūlādipañcarūpeṣu yathākramaṁ [saṁyamāt] pūrvaṁ sthūlena saṁyamaṁ kṛtvā tajjayasākṣātkaraṇānantaraṁ svarūpasaṁyamaṁ kurvīta । pūnaḥ sūkṣme, punaścānvaye, punaścārthavatve ityevaṁ yathākramaṁ [saṁyamāttasya tasya] sthūlādikasya [darśanaṁ jayaśca] yathāvat [prādurbhavati । tatra bhūtasvarūpāṇi jitvā] yogī [bhūtajayī bhavati । tajjayāt vatsānusāriṇya iva gāvaḥ] (yathā prakṛtibhūtagāvaḥ) [asya saṁkalpānuvidhāyinyo bhūtaprakṛtayo bhavanti ॥ 44 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
["Now, what is the subtle form of these? The <s>tanmātra</s> (subtle element) is the cause of the gross elements."] Since it is composed of multiple atoms, ["one part of that"] <s>tanmātra</s> ["is the atom (<s>paramāṇu</s>)."] That too ["is of the nature of the universal and the particular, a composite pervaded by the distinction of inseparably established parts. Thus all <s>tanmātras</s>."] Therefore, the <s>tanmātras</s>, freed from particularities, and their parts, the atoms — ["this is the third"] form of the elements, called 'subtle,' which is the object of <s>saṁyama</s>. And since <s>ākāśa</s> (space) is composed from the sound-<s>tanmātra</s>, it has parts and is non-eternal. Nor can a substance called '<s>ākāśa</s>' be apprehended apart from sound, because there is no difference between property and property-bearer.
But surely — blackness departs from hair and the like, and whiteness arises. Thus, blackness and such, having the character of departing and arising, are qualities. But that which does not perish with blackness nor come into being with whiteness — that is the substance. Similarly, even for <s>ākāśa</s> and the like, there is existence apart from their qualities, because of the distinction between sound, cognition, and so forth.
No — because there is no valid example. Those very hairs, whether black or white, undergo transformation through properties such as blackness and whiteness. For it has been said that everything has the nature of everything. Nowhere indeed are qualities such as whiteness observed as departing from and arising in an immutable substratum. Nor is the essential nature of substance [revealed] by the removal of blackness and the like. Even though it is said that 'substance is that which is apprehended by sight and touch,' this too is unproblematic, since it is a composite of inseparably established form and touch, and is grasped by both sight and touch.
But surely — form is not grasped by touch, nor touch by sight; that which is grasped by both — 'what I see is what I touch' — that is substance. But what is grasped by the eye alone or by touch alone — that is a quality.
No — because this is not invariable, as in a mixed heap of beans, sesame, barley, and other grain varieties. For a heap too is grasped by both sight and touch. Moreover — sight and touch grasp only qualities, being external sense organs, like the ear. Nor does a universal (<s>jāti</s>) exist apart from qualities, since universals are not apprehended in distinct [substances]. Furthermore, even in a pot and the like, through mutual superimposition, what is grasped by sight and touch is only form and touch — just as [one says] 'this form is foul-smelling' or 'fragrant.' Therefore, <s>ākāśa</s> too is composed from the <s>tanmātra</s>, cannot be apprehended apart from sound, and thus has parts and is non-eternal.
["Now, the fourth form of the elements. The <s>guṇas</s> (constituents), whose nature is illumination, activity, and stability, follow the essential nature of their effects"] — they conform to the properties of their effects — ["are expressed by the word 'connection' (<s>anvaya</s>)."] Because of their pervasion. This is the fourth form of the elements, the object of <s>saṁyama</s> called <s>guṇa</s>-connection.
["Now their fifth form is purposefulness (<s>arthavattva</s>)."] Its explanation is ["serving the purpose of experience (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>)."] And that ["is inherent in the <s>guṇas</s>."] The purposefulness of experience and liberation that pervades the <s>guṇas</s> — this is the fifth form of the elements, the object of <s>saṁyama</s> called purposefulness.
["The <s>guṇas</s> are inherent in the <s>tanmātras</s>, the elements, and the modifications of the elements."] Thus the <s>tanmātra</s>, the subtle form, pervades the elements and their modifications. And the essential form of the elements pervades the gross modifications of the elements. Thus ["everything is purposeful,"] because the <s>guṇas</s> serve the purposes of experience and liberation, and because they pervade everything, everything — elements, modifications, and the like — is purposeful through that purposefulness.
["Now, from sequential <s>saṁyama</s> on these five forms of the elements"] — on the five forms beginning with the gross — one should first perform <s>saṁyama</s> on the gross, and after achieving mastery and direct realization of that, perform <s>saṁyama</s> on the essential form; then on the subtle, then on the connection, then on the purposefulness — thus sequentially. ["From <s>saṁyama</s> on each of those"] gross and other [forms], ["perception and mastery"] of each ["arise properly. Having mastered the essential forms of the elements,"] the <s>yogin</s> ["becomes a conqueror of the elements. From that mastery, like cows following their calves,"] (just as cows by their nature) ["the elemental natures become obedient to his will."] ॥ 44 ॥

body.text: tato'ṇimādiprādurbhāvaḥ kāyasaṁpattaddharmānabhighātaśca ॥ 45 ॥
body.translated_text: From that arise the manifestation of <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness) and the other [powers], perfection of the body, and non-obstruction by the properties [of the elements]. ॥ 45 ॥

body.text: tatrāṇimā bhavatyaṇuḥ। laghimā laghurbhavati। mahimā mahābhavati। prāptiraṅgulyagreṇāpi spṛśati candramasam। prākāmyamicchānabhighātaḥ। bhūmāvunmajjati nimajjati yathodake। vaśitvaṁ bhūtabhautikeṣu vaśī bhavatyavaśyaścānyeṣām। īśitṛtvaṁ teṣāṁ prabhavāpyayavyūhānāmīṣṭe। yatra kāmāvasāyitvaṁ satyasaṁkalpatā yathā saṁkalpastathā bhūtaprakṛtīnāmavasthānam। na ca śakto'pi padārthaviparyāsaṁ karoti। kasmāt। anyasya yatra kāmāvasāyinaḥ pūrvasiddhasya tathā bhūteṣu saṁkalpāditi। etānyaṣṭāvaiśvaryāṇi।
body.translated_text: Of these, <s>aṇimā</s> — one becomes minute. <s>Laghimā</s> — one becomes light. <s>Mahimā</s> — one becomes great. <s>Prāpti</s> (reach) — one touches the moon even with the tip of one's finger. <s>Prākāmya</s> (irresistible will) — non-obstruction of desire; one emerges from and submerges into the earth as if in water. <s>Vaśitva</s> (mastery) — one becomes master over the elements and their products, and is not subject to others. <s>Īśitṛtva</s> (lordship) — one commands their origination, dissolution, and arrangement. <s>Yatrakāmāvasāyitva</s> (fulfillment of resolve wherever desired) — one's resolve is unfailingly true; as one wills, so the elemental natures are disposed. Yet even though capable, one does not bring about a reversal of the natural order of things. Why? Because of the will of another who possesses <s>yatrakāmāvasāyitva</s> and who is established before [him] — [namely, the Supreme Lord] — such is His resolve regarding the elements. These are the eight sovereign powers (<s>aiśvarya</s>).

body.text:
vivaraṇam
(sva)saṁyamaphalamidānīmāha – [tato'ṇimādiprādurbhāvaḥ kāyasampattaddharmānabhighātaśca] । [tatrāṇimā ko bhavati] ityāha – [aṇuḥ] iti । sūkṣmādapi sūkṣmataro bhavatīcchātaḥ । tenāṇimnā sarvamanupraviśativajramapi । tathā sarvasyādṛśyo bhavati ।
[laghimā] – [laghuḥ] laghubhyaḥ tūlādibhyo'pilaghutaraḥ bhavati । tena nirālambanaḥ sarvato gantuṁ paryāmoti । [mahimā] - [mahānbhavati ।] ākāśamapi vyāpnoti । [prāptiḥ] – ihastha eva [aṅgulyagreṇāpi spṛśati candramasam । prākāmyaṁ –] pracurakāmeyatheṣṭakāmo bhavati [icchānabhidhātaḥ । bhūmāvunmajjati nimajjati ca ।] yathākāmatvāt [yathodake ॥]
[vaśitvam –] sarvalokavaśitvam । asya vyākhyānaṁ [bhūtabhautikavaśī bhavati avaśyañcānyeṣām । īśitvam – teṣāṁ] bhūtānāṁ [prabhavavyūhāpyayānām] utpattisthitipralayānām [īṣṭe । yatra kāmāvasāyitvam] – yarimankāmastatraiva tadavasānaṁ tadantaṁ gacchati । [satyasaṁkalpāddhetoḥ yathā saṁkalpaḥ tathā bhūtaprakṛtīnāmavasthānaṁ] bhavati ॥
[śakto'pi] sa yogī [na padārthaviparyāsaṁ karoti ।] nāgniṁ śītīkareti । kasmāt? [anyasya yatra kāmāvasāyinaḥ pūrvasiddhasya] parameśvarasya [tathā teṣu] padārtheṣu viparyāsena [saṁkalpāt ।] na hi padārtha viparyāsaṁ cikīrṣamāṇasya pūrvasiddhaṁ prativinādveṣeṇa tadviparyāso bhavati । tadaśuddhyabhāvādeva na padārthaviparyāsaṁ karoti । kalyāṇatarācaraṇo hi sa iti । [etānyaṣṭau] aṇimādyai [śvaryāṇi] bhūtajayādbhavanti ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
Now he states the fruit of [elemental] <s>saṁyama</s> — ["From that arise the manifestation of <s>aṇimā</s> and the other powers, perfection of the body, and non-obstruction by their properties."] ["What is <s>aṇimā</s>?"] He says — ["minute."] One becomes subtler even than the subtle, at will. By that minuteness, one penetrates everything, even diamond. Likewise, one becomes invisible to all.
["<s>Laghimā</s>"] — ["light;"] one becomes lighter even than light things like cotton. By that, unsupported, one is able to travel everywhere. ["<s>Mahimā</s>"] — ["one becomes great;"] one pervades even space. ["<s>Prāpti</s>"] — remaining right here, ["one touches the moon even with the tip of one's finger. <s>Prākāmya</s>"] — one whose desires are abundant becomes one whose desires are fulfilled as wished — ["non-obstruction of desire; one emerges from and submerges into the earth,"] because of having [the power of doing] as one wishes, ["as if in water."]
["<s>Vaśitva</s>"] — mastery over all worlds. Its explanation: ["one becomes master over elements and their products, and is not subject to others. <s>Īśitva</s> — one commands"] the elements' ["origination, arrangement, and dissolution"] — creation, maintenance, and destruction. ["<s>Yatrakāmāvasāyitva</s>"] — wherever one's desire is directed, there its conclusion, its fulfillment, goes. ["Through the cause of unfailing resolve, as one wills, so the elemental natures are disposed."]
["Yet even though capable,"] that <s>yogin</s> ["does not bring about a reversal of the natural order."] He does not make fire cold. Why? ["Because of the will of another who possesses <s>yatrakāmāvasāyitva</s>, who is established before"] — the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>) — ["whose resolve regarding those"] objects is contrary [to reversal]. For one who wishes to reverse the natural order cannot accomplish that reversal except by overcoming the one established before. Because there is no such impurity [in the yogin], he does not reverse the natural order. For he is one whose conduct is supremely virtuous. ["These eight"] powers beginning with <s>aṇimā</s> ["are the sovereign powers"] that arise from mastery of the elements.

body.text: kāyasaṁpadvakṣyamāṇā। taddharmānabhighātaśca pṛthivī mūrtyā na niruṇaddhi yoginaḥ śarīrādikriyāṁ, śilāmapyanuviśatīti। nā''paḥ snigdhāḥ kledayanti। nāgnirūṣṇo dahati। na vāyuḥ praṇāmī vahati। anāvaraṇātmake'pyākāśe bhavatyāvṛtakāyaḥ siddhānāmapyadṛśyo bhavati ॥ 45 ॥
body.translated_text: Perfection of the body will be described [in the next sūtra]. And non-obstruction by their properties: earth with its solidity does not obstruct the bodily activities of the <s>yogin</s> — he enters even into rock. Water with its moisture does not wet him. Fire with its heat does not burn him. Wind with its movement does not carry him away. Even in space (<s>ākāśa</s>), whose nature is non-obstruction, his body becomes concealed — he becomes invisible even to the <s>Siddhas</s> (perfected beings). ॥ 45 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[kāyasampadvakṣyamāṇā । taddharmānabhidhātaḥ] teṣāṁ bhūtānāṁ dharmaiḥ na yogino'bhighāto bhavati । [pṛthivī] svena dharmeṇa [mūrtyā na viruṇaddhi yoginaḥ śarīrādikriyām ।] katham ? [śilāmapyanupraviśati] । [nāpaḥ snigdhā yoginaṁ kledayanti] varṣasahasramapyudake tiṣṭhantam । [nāgniruṣṇo dahati । na vāyuḥ praṇāmī vahati । anāvaraṇātmake'pi] prakaṭarūpe'pi [bhavatyāvṛtaḥ] prakaṭo na bhavati । [siddhānāmapyadṛśyo bhavati ॥ 45 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
["Perfection of the body will be described. Non-obstruction by their properties"] — the <s>yogin</s> is not harmed by the properties of the elements. ["Earth, by its own property,"] ["solidity, does not obstruct the bodily activities of the <s>yogin</s>."] How? ["He enters even into rock."] ["Water with its moisture does not wet the <s>yogin</s>,"] even if he stands in water for a thousand years. ["Fire with its heat does not burn him. Wind with its movement does not carry him away. Even in space, whose nature is non-obstruction"] — even in that which is of manifest form — ["he becomes concealed"] — he does not become manifest. ["He becomes invisible even to the <s>Siddhas</s>."] ॥ 45 ॥

body.text: rūpalāvaṇyabalavajrasaṁhananatvāni kāyasaṁpat ॥ 46 ॥
body.translated_text: Beauty, grace, strength, and adamantine firmness constitute perfection of the body. ॥ 46 ॥

body.text: darśanīyaḥ kāntimānatiśayabalo vajrasaṁhananaśceti ॥ 46 ॥
body.translated_text: One becomes beautiful, radiant, of surpassing strength, and of adamantine firmness. ॥ 46 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[rūpalāvaṇyabalavajrasaṁhananatvāni kāyasampat ।] rūpavān [darśanīyaḥ ।] lāvaṇyavān [kāntimānatiśayabalo vajrasaṁhananaśca] bhavati ॥ 46 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
["Beauty, grace, strength, and adamantine firmness constitute perfection of the body."] One who possesses beauty is ["good-looking;"] one who possesses grace ["is radiant, of surpassing strength, and of adamantine firmness."] ॥ 46 ॥

body.text: grahaṇasvarūpāsmi​tānvayārthavattva​saṁyamādindriyajayaḥ ॥ 47 ॥
body.translated_text: From <s>saṁyama</s> on grasping, essential form, <s>asmitā</s> (I-am-ness), connection, and purposefulness, [arises] mastery of the sense organs. ॥ 47 ॥

body.text: sāmānyaviśeṣātmā śabdādirgrāhyaḥ। teṣvindriyāṇāṁ vṛttirgrahaṇam। na ca tatsāmānyamātragrahaṇākāraṁ kathamanālocitaḥ sa viṣayaviśeṣa indriyeṇa manasā'nuvyavasīyeteti। svarūpaṁ punaḥ prakāśātmano buddhisattvasya sāmānyaviśeṣayorayutasiddhāvayavabhedānugataḥ samūho dravyamindriyam। teṣāṁ tṛtīyaṁ rūpamasmitālakṣaṇo'haṁkāraḥ। tasya sāmānyasyendriyāṇi viśeṣāḥ। caturthaṁ rūpaṁ vyayavasāyātmakāḥ prakāśakriyāsthitiśīlā guṇā yeṣāmindriyāṇi sāhaṁkārāṇi pariṇāmaḥ। pañcamaṁ rūpaṁ guṇeṣu yadanugataṁ puruṣārthavattvamiti। pañcasveteṣvindriyarūpeṣu yathākramaṁ saṁyamastatra tatra jayaṁ kṛtvā pañcarūpajayādindriyajayaḥ prādurbhavati yoginaḥ ॥ 47 ॥
body.translated_text: The graspable object, such as sound, is of the nature of the universal and the particular. The operation of the sense organs upon these is grasping. And that is not merely a grasping of the universal aspect — how could a particular object, not examined by the sense organ, be determined by the mind? The essential form, moreover: of <s>buddhi-sattva</s> (the luminous essence of intellect), whose nature is illumination — the sense organ is a substance that is a composite pervaded by the distinction of inseparably established parts of the universal and the particular. Their third form is <s>ahaṁkāra</s> (ego-sense), characterized by <s>asmitā</s> (I-am-ness). The sense organs are the particulars of that universal [ego-sense]. The fourth form: the <s>guṇas</s>, whose nature is determination, whose character is illumination, activity, and stability — of which the sense organs together with the ego-sense are a transformation. The fifth form: the purposefulness (<s>puruṣārthavatva</s>) that pervades the <s>guṇas</s>. From sequential <s>saṁyama</s> on these five forms of the sense organs, having achieved mastery over each successively, mastery of the senses arises for the <s>yogin</s> through conquest of the five forms. ॥ 47 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[grahaṇasvarūpāsmitānvayārthavatvasaṁyamādindriyajayaḥ । sarva] metadgatasūtreṇa tulyavyākhyānam । asmitāmātraṁ tu viśeṣo bhūtānāmiva tanmātrāṇi । [sāmānyaviśeṣātmā śabdādirviṣayaḥ । teṣvindriyāṇāṁ] yā [vṛttiḥ] viṣayaviśeṣāvalokanātmikā tat [grahaṇam । na ca tatsāmānyamātre] śabdādisāmānyābhāsanamātre manasi [grahaṇākāraḥ] upapadyate । katham? [anālocitaḥ svaviṣayaviśeṣa indriyeṇa] anigṛhīto nijo viṣayaviśeṣe [manasā kathaṁ] nu nāma [anuvyavasīyeta ।] na kathañcidanuvyavasīyeta taimirikā taimirikayā'nuvyavasāyānanuvyavasāyābhyām । tasmānnendriyeṇānālocitaviṣaye manasā । anuvyavasāyaḥ । tatrāsyāṁ viśeṣātmikāyāṁ vṛttau prathamaṁ saṁyamaḥ kartavyaḥ ॥
[atha svarūpaṁ punaḥ] indriyāṇāṁ dvitīyaṁ rūpam । [prakāśātmanoḥ sāmānyaviśeṣayoḥ] viṣayaviśeṣālocanamindriyāṇāṁ viśeṣaḥ । yathā pradīpasya ghaṭādiviśeṣākārālokoviśeṣaḥ । prakāśamātraṁ sāmānyam । ataḥ sāmānyaviśeṣātmakam [ayutasiddhāvayavabhedānugataṁ dravyamindriyaṁ] pradīpavat । yathāsāmānyamūrtidharmaḥ sthūlādiṣvanupravartate, tathendriyaṁ prakāśātmakaṁ dravyaviśeṣātmikāyāṁ grahaṇavṛttāvanupravartate । tadetasmindvitīye indriyāṇāṁ svarūpe saṁyamaḥ kriyata ॥
[teṣām] indriyāṇāṁ [tṛtīyaṁ rūpamasmitālakṣaṇo'haṅkāraḥ । tasya] ahaṅkārasya [sāmānyasyendriyāṇi] ayutasiddhāvayavabhedānugatāni grahaṇarūpānvayīni [viśeṣāḥ ।] tatra asmitāyāṁ saṁyamaḥ karaṇīyaḥ ॥
[caturthaṁ rūpaṁ vyavasāyātmakāḥ prakāśakriyāsthitiśīlāguṇāḥ । yeṣāmindriyāṇi sāhaṅkārāṇi pariṇāmaḥ ।] tatra guṇānugame saṁyamaḥ kartavyaḥ ॥
[pañcamaṁ rūpaṁ guṇeṣu yadanugataṁ puruṣārthavattvam ।] ataḥ sarveṣāmarthavatvamanugamaśca pūrvavat ॥
evaṁ [eṣu pañcasvindriyarūpeṣu yathākramaṁ] kramānatikrameṇa [saṁyamaḥ । tatra] pratyekaṁ pañcasu [jayaṁ kṛtvā] pañcasvarūpajayaṁ labhate । tasmāt [pañcasvarūpajayādindriya(yādi)jayo] vakṣyamāṇaphalāya [prādurbhavati yoginaḥ ।] yattu [tataḥ paramāvaśyatendriyāṇām’] iti, tadviṣayagrahaṇavṛttirveśitvamātraṁ viṣayāpratipattirūpam ॥ 47 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
["From <s>saṁyama</s> on grasping, essential form, <s>asmitā</s>, connection, and purposefulness, mastery of the sense organs. All"] this has the same explanation as the preceding <s>sūtra</s> [on elements]. <s>Asmitā</s> alone is the distinctive [feature here], just as the <s>tanmātras</s> were for the elements. ["The graspable object such as sound is of the nature of the universal and the particular. The operation of the sense organs upon these"] — which consists in examining the particular object — is ["grasping. And in the mere universal"] — in the mere appearance of the universal of sound and the like in the mind — ["the character of grasping"] is not tenable. How? ["A particular object not examined by the sense organ"] — one's own particular object, unrestricted in its particularity — ["how could it be determined by the mind?"] It could not be determined in any way — as shown by the cases of a person with impaired vision, regarding determination and non-determination. Therefore, where the object has not been examined by the sense organ, the mind cannot make a determination. In this particular-natured operation, <s>saṁyama</s> should first be performed.
["Now the essential form,"] the second form of the sense organs. ["Of the universal and particular,"] whose nature is illumination — the examining of particular objects is the specific [function] of the sense organs, just as the illumination of specific forms of pots and the like is the specific [function] of a lamp. Mere illumination is the universal. Therefore, the sense organ, being of the nature of universal and particular, ["is a substance, a composite pervaded by the distinction of inseparably established parts,"] like a lamp. Just as the universal property of material form pervades gross things and the like, so the sense organ, whose nature is illumination, pervades the grasping operation that is of the nature of particular substance. Thus, <s>saṁyama</s> is performed on this second form, the essential form of the sense organs.
["Their"] — the sense organs' — ["third form is <s>ahaṁkāra</s>, characterized by <s>asmitā</s>. The sense organs,"] pervaded by the distinction of inseparably established parts, following the form of grasping, ["are the particulars of that"] universal [<s>ahaṁkāra</s>]. Therein, <s>saṁyama</s> should be performed on <s>asmitā</s>.
["The fourth form: the <s>guṇas</s>, whose nature is determination, whose character is illumination, activity, and stability; of which the sense organs together with the ego-sense are a transformation."] Therein, <s>saṁyama</s> should be performed on the <s>guṇa</s>-connection.
["The fifth form: the purposefulness that pervades the <s>guṇas</s>."] Therefore, the purposefulness and connection of all are as before.
Thus, ["from sequential <s>saṁyama</s> on these five forms of the sense organs,"] without transgressing the order, ["having achieved mastery"] over each of the five individually, one obtains conquest of the five forms. From that, ["mastery of the senses arises for the <s>yogin</s>"] for the sake of the results to be described. As for the statement ["'thence comes supreme swiftness of the senses,'"] that is merely the capacity of the sense organs' grasping operation to function independently [of the body], in the form of non-apprehension of objects [at will]. ॥ 47 ॥

body.text: tato manojavitvaṁ vikaraṇabhāvaḥ pradhānajayaśca ॥ 48 ॥
body.translated_text: From that [arise] swiftness of mind, the state of being independent of instruments, and mastery over <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial nature). ॥ 48 ॥

body.text: kāyasyānuttamo gatilābho manojavitvam। videhānāmindriyāṇāmabhipretadeśakālaviṣayāpekṣo vṛttilābho vikaraṇabhāvaḥ। sarvaprakṛtivikāravaśitvaṁ pradhānajaya ityetāstisraḥ siddhayo madhupratīkā ucyante। etāśca karaṇapañcarūpajayādadhigamyante ॥ 48 ॥
body.translated_text: The unsurpassed attainment of speed for the body is swiftness of mind (<s>manojavitva</s>). The attainment by the sense organs, when freed from the body, of the ability to function with regard to desired place, time, and object is the state of being independent of instruments (<s>vikaraṇabhāva</s>). Mastery over all modifications of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) is mastery over <s>pradhāna</s> (<s>pradhānajaya</s>). These three <s>siddhis</s> (attainments) are called <s>madhu-pratīkā</s> ('honey-faced'). And these are attained through conquest of the five forms of the sense organs. ॥ 48 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tato manojavatvaṁ vikaraṇabhāvaḥ pradhānajayaśca] । [tata] indriyajayāt [kāyasyānuttamaḥ na] vidyate'smāduttama ityanuttamaḥ [gatilābho manojavatvam । videhānāṁ] śarīranirapekṣāṇām [indriyāṇām abhipretadeśāpekṣo'bhipretakālāpekṣo'bhipretaśabdādiviṣayāpekṣaśca vṛttilābho vikaraṇabhāvaḥ । sarvaprakṛtivikāravāśatvam] aṣṭānāṁ prakṛtīnāṁ tadvikārāṇāṁ ca vaśitvaṁ [pradhānajaya ityetāstisraḥ siddhayo madhupratīkāḥ] iti [ucyante । tāśca pañcasvarūpajayādadhigamyante ॥ 48 ॥]
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
['From that, speed of mind, the state of being without instruments, and mastery over pradhāna.'] ['From that'] — from mastery over the senses — ['the body attains unsurpassed'] — there is none superior to this, hence 'unsurpassed' — ['acquisition of movement, which is speed of mind. Of the bodiless'] — independent of the body — ['senses, the acquisition of functioning with respect to desired location, desired time, and desired objects such as sound, is the state of being without instruments (vikaraṇabhāva). Mastery over all modifications of prakṛti'] — control over the eight prakṛtis and their modifications — ['is mastery over pradhāna (primordial matter). These three accomplishments are called "honey-faced" (madhupratīkā).'] They ['are attained from mastery over the five essential natures.' || 48 ||]

body.text: sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātimātrasya sarvabhāvādhiṣṭhātṛtvaṁ sarvajñātṛtvaṁ ca ॥ 49 ॥
body.translated_text: For one who has merely the discernment of the otherness of <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, there is sovereignty over all states of existence and omniscience. || 49 ||

body.text: nirdhūtarajastamomalasya buddhisattvasya pare vaiśāradye parasyāṁ vaśīkārasaṁjñāyāṁ vartamānasya sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātimātrarūpapratiṣṭhasya sarvabhāvādhiṣṭhātṛtvam। sarvātmāno guṇā vyavasāyavyavaseyātmakāḥ svāminaṁ kṣetrajñaṁ pratyaśeṣadṛśyātmatvenopasthitā ityarthaḥ। sarvajñātṛtvaṁ sarvātmanāṁ guṇānāṁ śāntoditāvyapadeśyadharmatvena vyavasthitānāmakramopārūḍhaṁ vivekajaṁ jñānamityarthaḥ। ityeṣā viśokā nāma siddhiryāṁ prāpya yogī sarvajñaḥ kṣīṇakleśabandhano vaśī viharati ॥ 49 ॥
body.translated_text: For one whose <s>buddhi-sattva</s> has shaken off the impurities of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, who abides in the supreme clarity (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), in the supreme state called mastery (<s>vaśīkāra-saṁjñā</s>), and who is established in the mere form of discerning the otherness of <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> — for such a one there is sovereignty over all states of existence. The meaning is: the <s>guṇas</s>, in all their forms, consisting of determination and the determinable, present themselves to their master, the knower of the field (<s>kṣetrajña</s>), entirely as the seen (<s>dṛśya</s>). Omniscience means: knowledge born of discrimination (<s>vivekaja-jñāna</s>), simultaneously comprehending without sequence all the <s>guṇas</s> in all their forms, established as properties that are quiescent, arisen, and indeterminable. This is the accomplishment called '<s>viśokā</s>' (sorrowless). Having attained it, the <s>yogin</s>, omniscient, with the bonds of affliction destroyed, moves about as a master. || 49 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātimātrasya sarvabhāvādhiṣṭhātṛtve sarvajñātṛtvaṁ ca ।] sarvaprakāreṇa sarvasādhanena [nirdhūtarajastamomalasya sattvasya pare vaiśāradye] svacche sthitipravāhe pare [vartamānasya parasyāṁ vaśīkārasaṁjñāyāṁ] jñānaprasādamātre niratiśaye [vartamānasya sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātimātrarūpapratiṣṭhasya sarvabhāvādhiṣṭhātṛtvam ।] sarvasya vastujātasyeṣṭe ॥
[sarvātmanā] sakalaprakṛtivikārātmanā [guṇādhyavasāyātmakāḥ] buddhyādikāraṇabhāvapariṇatā'dhyavasāyātmakāḥ śāntoditāvyapadeśyadharmānuprasarpiṇaḥ [svāminaṁ kṣetrajñaṁ] dṛśimātram [aśeṣaguṇāḥ dṛśyatvena] bhogyatvena [avasthitāḥ] labhyante [ityarthaḥ ॥]
[sarvajñātṛtvaṁ sarvātmakānāṁ śāntoditāvyapadaśyadharmatvenāvasthitānāṁ guṇānām akramopārūḍham] ekakālabhāvi [vivekajaṁ jñānamityarthaḥ । ityeṣā] sarvavaśitvasarvajñātṛtvalakṣaṇā [viśokā nāma siddhiḥ । yāṁ prāpya yogī sarvajñaḥ kṣīṇakleśabandhano viharati vaśī ॥ 49 ॥]
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
['For one who has merely the discernment of the otherness of sattva and Puruṣa, sovereignty over all states of existence and omniscience.'] Through every means and every instrument, ['for one whose sattva has shaken off the impurities of rajas and tamas, who abides in the supreme clarity'] — in the transparent flow of stability — ['in the supreme state called mastery'] — in the mere serenity of knowledge, unsurpassed — ['established in the mere form of discerning the otherness of sattva and Puruṣa, there is sovereignty over all states of existence.'] Lordship over the entire range of existent things is desired.
['The guṇas, in all their forms'] — transformed into the nature of causes such as buddhi and the rest, consisting of determination — ['pervaded by the properties that are quiescent, arisen, and indeterminable, present themselves to their master, the knower of the field (kṣetrajña)'] — to pure seeing alone — ['all the guṇas as the seen'] — as the enjoyable — ['are obtained.' This is the meaning.]
['Omniscience means: knowledge born of discrimination (vivekaja-jñāna), arising simultaneously without sequence,'] occurring at a single moment, ['of the guṇas in all their forms, established as properties that are quiescent, arisen, and indeterminable. This is the meaning. This is the accomplishment called viśokā (sorrowless). Having attained it, the yogin, omniscient, with the bonds of affliction destroyed, moves about as a master.' || 49 ||]

body.text: tadvairāgyādapi doṣabījakṣaye kaivalyam ॥ 50 ॥
body.translated_text: From dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) even toward that, upon the destruction of the seeds of deficiency, <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute isolation) [arises]. || 50 ||

body.text: yadā'syaivaṁ bhavā kleśakarmakṣaye sattvasyāyaṁ vivekapratyayo dharmaḥ sattvaṁ ca heyapakṣe nyastaṁ puruṣaścāpariṇāmī śuddho'nyaḥ sattvāditi। evamasya tato virajyamānasya yāni kleśabījāni dagdhaśālibījakalpānyaprasavasamarthāni tāni saha manasā pratyastaṁ gacchanti। teṣu pralīneṣu puruṣaḥ punaridaṁ tāpatrayaṁ na bhuṅkte। tadeteṣāṁ guṇānāṁ manasi karmakleśavipākasvarūpeṇābhivyaktānāṁ caritārthānāṁ pratiprasave puruṣasyā''tyantiko guṇaviyogaḥ kaivalyaṁ, tadā svarūpapratiṣṭhā citiśaktireva puruṣa iti ॥ 50 ॥
body.translated_text: When this [understanding] arises for him — upon the destruction of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and <s>karma</s>, this discriminative cognition is a property of <s>sattva</s>, and <s>sattva</s> is placed on the side of what is to be abandoned, while <s>Puruṣa</s> is non-transforming, pure, and other than <s>sattva</s> — thus, as he becomes dispassionate even toward that, the seeds of affliction, like roasted rice seeds incapable of sprouting, along with the mind, dissolve away. When those have dissolved, <s>Puruṣa</s> no longer experiences this threefold suffering. Then, in the counter-involution (<s>pratiprasava</s>) of these <s>guṇas</s> — which had manifested in the mind in the form of affliction, action, and fruition, and which have fulfilled their purpose — there is the absolute separation of <s>Puruṣa</s> from the <s>guṇas</s>, which is <s>kaivalya</s>. Then the power of awareness (<s>citi-śakti</s>), established in its own nature, is <s>Puruṣa</s>. || 50 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tadvairāgyādapi doṣabījakṣaye kaivalyam । yadā asyaivaṁ bhavati] savaijñasya sarvabhāvānadhitiṣṭhataḥ [kleśakarmakṣaye vivekī sattvasya pratyayaḥ ।] kīdṛśa ityāha – [sattvaṁ ca heyapakṣe nyastaṁ] pariṇāmitvāśuddhatvatriguṇatvādibhiḥ । [puruṣaśca] satyavidharmā [apariṇāmī śuddho'ntaḥ sattvāt] ityanena prakāreṇa ॥
[tataḥ] api sarvajñasarvabhāvādhyakṣatvāt [virajyamānasya yāni kleśabījāni] avidyāvāsanārūpāṇi [dagdhaśālibījakalpāni prasavāsamarthāni tāni] caritārthena pralīyamānena [saha] āśrayeṇa [manasā prayastaṁ gacchanti । teṣu pralīneṣu puruṣaḥ punaridaṁ tāpatrayam] ādhyātmikādilakṣaṇaṁ [na bhuṅke ॥]
[tadeṣāṁ guṇānāṁ manasi kleśakarmavipākasvarūpeṇābhivyaktānāṁ caritārthānāṁ pratiprasave] pralaye [puruṣasyātyantiko guṇaviyogaḥ kaivalyam । tadā svarūpapratiṣṭhā citiśaktireva puruṣaḥ ।] tatra [tadvairāgyādapi] ityapiśabdādaprāptayogaiśvaryasyāpi samyagdarśanātkaivalyamiti ॥ 50 ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
['From dispassion even toward that, upon the destruction of the seeds of deficiency, kaivalya.'] ['When this arises'] for the omniscient one, presiding over all states of existence, ['upon the destruction of kleśas and karma, the discriminative cognition is a property of sattva.'] What kind? He says: ['Sattva is placed on the side of what is to be abandoned'] — due to its being transforming, impure, consisting of three guṇas, and so forth. ['And Puruṣa,'] having contrary qualities, ['is non-transforming, pure, other than sattva'] — in this manner.
['Then'] even from omniscience and sovereignty over all states, ['as he becomes dispassionate, the seeds of affliction'] — in the form of the latent impressions of ignorance (avidyā-vāsanā) — ['like roasted rice seeds, incapable of sprouting, those,'] together with the mind as their support, which is dissolving having fulfilled its purpose, ['dissolve away. When those have dissolved, Puruṣa no longer experiences this threefold suffering'] characterized as subjective (ādhyātmika) and the rest.
['Then, in the counter-involution (pratiprasava) of these guṇas, manifested in the mind in the form of affliction, action, and fruition, which have fulfilled their purpose — in their dissolution — there is the absolute separation of Puruṣa from the guṇas, which is kaivalya. Then the power of awareness (citi-śakti), established in its own nature, is Puruṣa.'] Therein, ['from dispassion even toward that'] — from the word 'even' (api), it follows that even for one who has not attained yogic sovereignty, kaivalya comes from right vision (samyag-darśana). || 50 ||

body.text: sthānyupanimantraṇe saṅgasmayākaraṇaṁ punaraniṣṭaprasaṅgāt ॥ 51 ॥
body.translated_text: Upon invitation by the celestial beings (<s>sthānins</s>), one should not yield to attachment or pride, for there would again be the occurrence of the undesirable. || 51 ||

body.text: catvāraḥ khalvamī yoginaḥ prāthamakalpiko madhubhūmikaḥ prajñājyotiratikrāntabhāvanīyaśceti। tatrābhyāsī pravṛttamātrajyotiḥ prathamaḥ। ṛtaṁbharaprajño dvitīyaḥ। bhūtendriyajayī tṛtīyaḥ sarveṣu bhāviteṣu bhāvanīyeṣu kṛtarakṣābandhaḥ kartavyasādhanādimān। caturtho yastvatikrāntabhāvanīyastasya cittapratisarga eko'rthaḥ। saptavidhā'sya prāntabhūmiprajñā।
body.translated_text: There are indeed four [types of] <s>yogins</s>: the beginner (<s>prāthamakalpika</s>), one at the honey-level (<s>madhubhūmika</s>), the light-of-wisdom (<s>prajñājyoti</s>), and one who has transcended what is to be cultivated (<s>atikrāntabhāvanīya</s>). Among these, the first is the practitioner whose light has just begun to manifest (<s>pravṛttajyoti</s>). The second has wisdom full of truth (<s>ṛtaṁbhara-prajñā</s>). The third has conquered the elements and senses, has established protective measures over all that has been cultivated, and possesses the means for what remains to be accomplished. The fourth, who has transcended what is to be cultivated, has only one purpose remaining — the dissolution of the mind (<s>citta-pratisarga</s>). His wisdom is sevenfold, at its final stage.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[sthānyupamantraṇe saṅgasmayākaraṇaṁ punaraniṣṭaprasaṅgāt । sthānaṁ] svargādikaṁ yeṣānte [sthānino] devā indrādayaḥ । [tai: upamantraṇaṁ bho bho ihoṣyatām] ityādi । tasmin satyātmano hīnatvaṁ smarataḥ prāpnutaḥ [saṅgasmayau] (arthāditi) tau ca na kartavyau । saṅgasmayakaraṇe'niṣṭaṁ prasajyeta ॥
[catvāraḥ khalvamī yoginaḥ – prāthamakalpiko madhubhūmikaḥ prajñājyetiḥ atikrāntabhāvanīyaśva ।] tānkrameṇa vyācaṣṭe – [tatrābhyāsī] abhyasanaśīla: [pravṛttajyotiḥ] jyotiṣmatyādīnāmanyatamāpravṛttiḥ pravṛttā yasya sa [pravṛttajyotiḥ prathamaḥ ॥]
[ṛtambharaprajño dvitīyaḥ । bhūtendriyajayī tṛtīyaḥ ।] sa tu [sarveṣu bhāviteṣu bhāvanīyeṣu] sākṣātkṛteṣu jiteṣu ca [kṛtarakṣābandhaḥ,] upāttasya hi rakṣāvidhānīyā, [bhāvanīyeṣu] sākṣātkaraṇīyeṣu [kartavyatāsādhanavāṁśca ।] kartavyatāyāḥ sādhanāni kartavyatāsādhanāni abhyāsavairāgyādīni yasya saḥ [kartavyatāsādhanavān ॥]
[yastvatikrāntabhāvanīyaścaturthaḥ tasya cittapratisarga eva] cittapralaya eva [eko'rthaḥ] pariśiṣṭaḥ । [saptavidhā । tasya prāntabhūmiprajñā ।]
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
['Upon invitation by the celestial beings, one should not yield to attachment or pride, for there would again be the occurrence of the undesirable.'] ['The beings of station'] — the gods such as <s>Indra</s> and others — are those who possess stations such as heaven. ['Their invitation:'] 'Come, sit here,' and so forth. When this happens, for one who remembers and recognizes the inferiority [of such a state], ['attachment and pride'] should not be indulged. If attachment and pride are indulged, the undesirable would result.
['There are indeed four yogins: the beginner, one at the honey-level, the light-of-wisdom, and one who has transcended what is to be cultivated.'] He explains them in order: ['Among these, the practitioner'] — one inclined to practice — ['whose light has emerged'] — for whom one or another of the higher perceptions such as jyotiṣmatī has emerged — ['is the first.']
['One with wisdom full of truth is the second. The conqueror of elements and senses is the third.'] But he, ['having directly realized and conquered all that was to be cultivated, has established protective measures,'] for what has been attained must be guarded. ['Possessing the means for what is to be accomplished'] — the means of accomplishment, such as practice and dispassion.
['The fourth, who has transcended what is to be cultivated, has only'] the dissolution of the mind — ['the dissolution of citta as his one remaining purpose. His wisdom is sevenfold, at its final stage.']

body.text: tatra madhumatīṁ bhūmiṁ sākṣātkurvato brāhmaṇasya sthānino devāḥ sattvaviśuddhimanupaśyantaḥ sthānairupanimantrayante bho ihā''syatāmiha ramyatāṁ kamanīyo'yaṁ bhogaḥ kamanīyeyaṁ kanyā rasāyanamidaṁ jarāmṛtyuṁ bādhate vaihāyasavidaṁ yānamamī kalpadrumāḥ puṇyā mandākinī siddhā maharṣaya uttamā anukūlā apsaraso divye śrotracakṣuṣī vajropamaḥ kāyaḥ svaguṇaiḥ sarvamidamupārjitamāyuṣmatā pratipadyatāmidamakṣayamajaramamarasthānaṁ devānāṁ priyamiti। evamabhidhīyamānaḥ saṅgadoṣānbhāvayedghoreṣu saṁsārāṅgāreṣu pacyamānena mayā jananamaraṇāndhakāre viparivartamānena kathaṁcidāsāditaḥ kleśatimiravināśī yogapradīpastasya caite tṛṣṇāyonayo viṣavavāyavaḥ pratipakṣāḥ। sa khalvahaṁ labdhālokaḥ kathamanayā viṣayamṛgatṛṣṇayā vañcitastasyaiva punaḥ pradīptasya saṁsārāgnerātmānamindhanī kuryāmiti। svasti vaḥ svapnopamebhyaḥ kṛpaṇajanaprārthanīyebhyo viṣayebhya ityevaṁ niścitamatiḥ samādhiṁ bhāvayet।
body.translated_text: There, for the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (spiritual aspirant) who is directly realizing the honey-stage (<s>madhumatī bhūmi</s>), the gods who possess stations, observing the purity of his <s>sattva</s>, invite him with their stations: 'Come, sit here, enjoy here — this pleasure is delightful, this maiden is charming, this elixir wards off old age and death, this is a vehicle that moves through the sky, these are wish-fulfilling trees, the holy <s>Mandākinī</s> river, accomplished great sages, excellent and agreeable <s>Apsarases</s>, divine hearing and sight, a body hard as diamond — all this has been earned by the fortunate one's own merits. Accept this imperishable, ageless, deathless station, beloved of the gods.' Being thus addressed, one should contemplate the faults of attachment: 'While being roasted on the terrible embers of <s>saṁsāra</s>, revolving in the darkness of birth and death, I have with great difficulty obtained the lamp of <s>yoga</s> that destroys the darkness of affliction. These [temptations] are counter-winds arising from craving — opponents of that lamp. Having obtained illumination, how could I, deceived by this mirage of sense-objects, make myself fuel for that very fire of <s>saṁsāra</s> which blazes once more?' Farewell to you, sense-pleasures — dreamlike things craved by the wretched! With such firm resolve, one should cultivate <s>samādhi</s>.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tatra maghumatīṁ bhūmiṁ] dvitīyāmṛtambharaprajñābhūmiṁ [sākṣātkurvato brāhmaṇasya sthānino devāḥ satvaviśuddhimanupaśyantaḥ sthānairupamntryante ।] bhoḥ ityādi prasiddhārthaṁ bhāṣyam [॥ 51 ॥]
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
['There, for the one directly realizing the honey-stage'] — the second stage of wisdom full of truth (ṛtaṁbhara-prajñā) — ['the gods who possess stations, observing the purity of sattva, invite him with their stations.'] 'Come,' and so forth — the bhāṣya has a well-known meaning. || 51 ||

body.text: saṅgamakṛtvā smayamapi na kuryādevamahaṁ devānāmapi prārthanīya iti। smayādayaṁ susthitaṁmanyatayā mṛtyunā keśeṣu gṛhītamivā''tmānaṁ na bhāvayiṣyati। tathā cāsya cchidrāntaraprekṣī nityaṁ yatnopacaryaḥ pramādo labdhavivaraḥ kleśānuttambhayiṣyati tataḥ punaraniṣṭaprasaṅgaḥ। evamasya saṅgasmayāvakurvato bhāvito'rtho dṛḍhī bhaviṣyati। bhāvanīyaścārtho'bhimukhī bhaviṣyatīti ॥ 51 ॥
body.translated_text: Having not yielded to attachment, one should also not indulge in pride, thinking 'I am sought even by the gods.' Through pride, one who considers oneself well-established will not contemplate oneself as if seized by the hair by death. And thus, heedlessness, always watching for an opening, if it finds a gap despite constant effort, will prop up the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). Then again the undesirable would result. Thus, for one who does not indulge in attachment and pride, the purpose that has been cultivated will become firm, and the purpose yet to be cultivated will become accessible. || 51 ||

body.text: kṣaṇatatkramayoḥ saṁyamādvivekajaṁ jñānam ॥ 52 ॥
body.translated_text: From <s>saṁyama</s> on the moment (<s>kṣaṇa</s>) and its succession (<s>krama</s>), knowledge born of discrimination (<s>vivekaja-jñāna</s>) [arises]. || 52 ||

body.text: yathā'pakarṣaparyantaṁ dravyaṁ paramāṇurevaṁ paramāpakarṣaparyantaḥ kālaḥ kṣaṇo yāvatā vā samayena calitaḥ paramāṇuḥ pūrvadeśaṁ jahyāduttaradeśamupasaṁpadyeta sa kālaḥ kṣaṇaḥ। tatpravāhāvicchedastu kramaḥ। kṣaṇatatkramayornāsti vastusamāhāra iti buddhisamāhāro muhūrtāhorātrādayaḥ। sa khalvayaṁ kālo vastuśūnyo'pi buddhinirmāṇaḥ śabdajñānānupātī laukikānāṁ vyutthitadarśanānāṁ vastusvarūpa ivāvabhāsate।
body.translated_text: Just as the ultimate limit of the reduction of matter is the atom (<s>paramāṇu</s>), so the ultimate limit of the reduction of time is the moment (<s>kṣaṇa</s>) — the time in which a moving atom would leave one position and arrive at the next — that time is a moment. The uninterrupted flow of those [moments] is succession (<s>krama</s>). In the moment and its succession, there is no real aggregate — [aggregates such as] hours, days and nights, and so forth are mental constructs (<s>buddhi-samāhāra</s>). This time, though devoid of real substance, being a mental fabrication that follows words and concepts, appears to those of ordinary worldly vision as if it were the very nature of a real thing.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[kṣaṇatatkramayoḥ saṁyamādvivekajaṁ jñānam ।] kṣaṇaṁ kramaṁ ca svayameva vistareṇācaṣṭe–tatra [apakarṣaparyantaṁ] yataḥ paramapakarṣo na śakyeta kartuṁ taddravyaṁ [paramāṇuḥ ।] evaṁ lekabuddhivikalpatādahorātralakṣaṇādapakṛṣyamāṇātkālādalpīyaḥ parijighṛkṣayāyataḥ param apakraṣṭuṁ na śakyate saḥ [apakarṣaparyantaḥ kālaḥ kṣaṇaḥ] vastubhūtaḥ ॥
[yadvā, yāvatā samayena vicalitaḥ paramāṇuḥ pūrvaṁ deśaṁ jahyādutaramābhasaṁpadyeta sakālaḥ kṣaṇaḥ ।] sarvathā'pyasti (sūkṣma)kṣaṇa ityarthaḥ ॥
[tasya pravāhāvicchedabhāvinaḥ] tasya kṣaṇasya pravāhaḥ prabandhaḥ avicchedenairantarthaṁ tathā bhavituṁ śīlaṁ yasya kṣaṇasya pravāhāvicchedabhāvinaḥ kṣaṇasya yat ānantaryaṁ saḥ kṣaṇasya [kramaḥ ।] tayośca [kṣaṇatatkramayornāsti vastusamāhāraḥ] kṣaṇakramasyāvastutvātkṣaṇasya caikatvānnāsti tayoḥ samāhāraḥ samūhaḥ ॥
nanu cāsati kṣaṇatatkramasamāhare kathaṁ māsasaṁvatsarādayaḥ pravarteranniti, tadarthamāha– [buddhisamāhārāt] buddhiparikalpitāt kṣaṇatatkramayoḥ samāhārādādityādideśāntarasaṁbandhāvabandhabuddhisamudbhavitāt [muhūrtāhorātrādayaḥ ।] tataścabuddhisthita eṣabhedaḥ ॥
yo hi prasannasamānapratyayapravāhimānasaḥ ekāgrabhūmipratiṣṭhicittasatvaḥ, tasya satyapi kālānubhavekṣaṇayugasahasrayostulyatā । naivaṁ vyutthitacittasya । tathā svapne'pi ghaṭikāmātreṇa buddhiparikalpitaṁ yo janasahasranamanekaṁ saṁvatsareṇaiva [gantavyaṁ] gacchati । tasmādbuddhivaicitryānirmita eva kālasamāhāraḥ ।
yasya tu kriyāvyatiriktaḥ kālaḥ nityo vibhuḥ, tasya cirakṣipratvādyapi kriyāmātreparyavasitatvātpṛthakkālāstitvena liṅge ghaṭate । niyataparimāṇā hi kriyā anavagataparimāṇāyāḥ kriyāyā lakṣaṇam । yathā āgodohanaṁ svapati । āodanapākamadhīte iti । sa eva ca kālaḥ । na hi nityasya vibhoḥ tasya kūṭasthasya asambandhatvātvastvantaraparicchedakatvaṁ prasthādivadupapadyate ॥
kriyāvānkālaḥ paricchedakaḥ prasthādivaditi cet, tasyāpi kriyāvatvātkriyāvataśca paricchedanīyatvadanyena kriyāvatā paricchedakena kālena bhāvitavyam । tasyāpyanyenatyanavasthāprasaṅgaḥ kriyāvattvācānityatvamapi prasajyeta ॥
atha svavyāpāreṇaiva kāla: paricchedanīyakaṁ yāyāditi cet, anye'pi svavyāpāreṇaiva paricchedyā itikālapṛthaktvakalpanānirarthikā । tathā ca kriyai vāstukālaḥ ॥
athāpi sadbhāvamātreṇa kālaḥ paricchedaka iti, sarveṣāmapi sadbhāvāviśaṣādeva prasaktam ॥
kriyākālapakṣe'pyeṣa vikalpaḥ prāpta iti cet – na, kriyāyāḥ sarvaprasiddhatvāt । paricchedakatvasya ca āgodohamāste ityādiṣu siddhatvātkriyaiva paraicchedikā labhyate, nāparaḥ kāla: paricchedaka iti । ciraṁ kṣipramiti ca prayatnamandimapāṭavakṛtaḥ pratyayonavyatiriktakālanibandhana ityāha– [sa khalvayaṁ kālaḥ] saṁvatsarādirūpo [vastuśūnyo budvinirmāṇaḥ] buddhyā nirmāpiṣyate ॥
[śabdadharmānupātī] truṭinimeṣāhorātrādiśabdavikalpānupravartī । [laukikānāṁ vyutthitadarśanānāṁ vastusvarūpa ivābhāsate ।]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['From <s>saṁyama</s> on the moment (<s>kṣaṇa</s>) and its sequence (<s>krama</s>), knowledge born of discrimination (<s>vivekaja jñāna</s>) arises.'] He himself explains the moment and the sequence in detail — there, ['the ultimate limit of reduction'] — that substance which cannot be reduced further — is the ['atom (<s>paramāṇu</s>).'] Similarly, from time characterized by day and night, which is a mere conceptual construction of ordinary cognition, when one desires to grasp something smaller by progressively reducing — that which cannot be further reduced is ['the ultimate limit of reduction of time, the moment (<s>kṣaṇa</s>),'] which is a real entity.
['Alternatively, the time in which a moving atom would leave its former position and arrive at the next — that time is a moment (<s>kṣaṇa</s>).'] In either case, the subtle moment exists — this is the meaning.
['Of that which has the nature of an unbroken flow'] — of that moment, the flow is the continuity; the unbroken, continuous nature of that moment whose character is to exist as an unbroken flow — the immediate succession of that moment is the ['sequence (<s>krama</s>) of the moment.'] And of these two, ['there is no real aggregate of the moment and its sequence,'] because the sequence of moments has no substantial reality and because the moment is singular, there is no aggregate or collection of these two.
Now, if there is no aggregate of moment and its sequence, how would months, years, and so on operate? To address this he says — ['From a mental aggregate'] — from an aggregate that is mentally constructed from the moment and its sequence, arising from the cognition of the connection of the sun and other bodies with different locations — ['periods (<s>muhūrta</s>), days and nights, and so on arise.'] And therefore this distinction exists only in the mind.
For one whose mind has a flow of clear, uniform cognitions, whose <s>citta-sattva</s> is established in the one-pointed stage — for him, even while experiencing time, a moment and a thousand ages are equal. Not so for one whose mind is in the outward-turned state. Likewise, in a dream too, one traverses in a mere moment what is mentally constructed as a journey of many thousands of people that would take many years. Therefore, the aggregate of time is indeed fabricated by the diversity of the mind.
But for one who holds that time is eternal, all-pervading, and distinct from action — even for him, since the notions of long and short duration ultimately rest in action alone, there is no valid evidence for the separate existence of time. For an action of determined measure is the defining mark of an action whose measure has not been ascertained — as in 'he sleeps for the duration of milking a cow,' or 'he studies for the duration of cooking rice.' And that itself is time. For an eternal, all-pervading, immutable entity, because of its non-relation, cannot serve as a delimiter of other things, as a measure like <s>prastha</s> can.
If it be said that time, possessing action, is a delimiter like a <s>prastha</s> measure — even that would possess action, and what possesses action requires another time possessing action to delimit it, and of that too another — leading to an infinite regress. And because of possessing action, impermanence would also follow.
If it be said that time would serve as a delimiter through its own operation alone — then others too could be delimited through their own operations alone, making the postulation of a separate time purposeless. And thus, action itself is the real time.
Even if one holds that time delimits merely by its existence — since there is no distinction in the mere existence of all things, the same absurd consequence follows.
If it be said that this difficulty arises also in the view that time consists of action — no, because action is universally well-known. And because the delimiting capacity is established in expressions like 'he sits for the duration of milking a cow,' action itself is obtained as the delimiter, and no separate time is needed as a delimiter. And the notions of 'long' and 'short' are produced by effort, slowness, and skill — not based on a separate time. Thus he says — ['This time indeed,'] in the form of years and so on, ['is devoid of substance, a mental construction'] — it is fabricated by the mind.
['It follows the conventions of language'] — it operates in conformity with verbal concepts such as <s>truṭi</s>, <s>nimeṣa</s>, day, night, and so on. ['For those of ordinary vision who are in the outward-turned state, it appears as if it were a substantial reality.']

body.text: kṣaṇastu vastupatitaḥ kramāvalambī। kramaśca kṣaṇānantaryātmā taṁ kālavidaḥ kāla ityācakṣate yoginaḥ। naca dvau kṣaṇau saha bhavataḥ। kramaśca na dvayoḥ sahabhuvorasaṁbhavāt। pūrvasmāduttarabhāvino yadānantaryaṁ kṣaṇasya sa kramaḥ। tasmādvartamāna evaikaḥ kṣaṇo na pūrvottarakṣaṇāḥ santīti। tasmānnāsti tatsamāhāraḥ। ye tu bhūtabhāvinaḥ kṣaṇāste pariṇāmānvitā vyākhyeyāḥ। tenaikena kṣaṇena kṛtsno lokaḥ pariṇāmamanubhavati। tatkṣaṇopārūḍhāḥ khalvamī sarve dharmāḥ। tayoḥ kṣaṇatatkramayoḥ saṁyamāttayoḥ sākṣātkaraṇam। tataśca vivekajaṁ jñānaṁ prādurbhavati ॥ 52 ॥
body.translated_text: But the moment (<s>kṣaṇa</s>) is grounded in reality and depends on sequence (<s>krama</s>). And sequence, whose nature is the immediate succession of moments — the knowers of time, the <s>yogins</s>, call that time. And two moments do not exist simultaneously. And sequence does not belong to two [simultaneous moments], because two simultaneous moments are impossible. The immediate succession of a moment that comes into being after a prior one — that is sequence. Therefore, only one present moment exists; past and future moments do not exist. Therefore, there is no aggregate of those. But those moments that have been and will be — they should be explained in terms of transformations. By that one moment, the entire world undergoes transformation. Indeed, all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) are mounted upon that moment. From <s>saṁyama</s> on those two — the moment and its sequence — comes their direct realization. And from that, knowledge born of discrimination (<s>vivekaja jñāna</s>) arises. ॥ 52 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[kṣaṇastu vasturūpaḥ] vāstavikaḥtaddravyānyathātvenānumīyamānaḥ [kramāvalambī । kramaśca kṣaṇānantaryātmā] kṣaṇapravāhavicchedabuddhinimittaḥ ॥
[taṁ kṣaṇaṁ kālāvidaḥ kāla ityācakṣate yoginaḥ । na ca dvau kṣaṇau saha bhavataḥ,] yayoḥ samāhāraḥ kalpyeta । ekasmindharmiṇisa ahajanmanoḥ kṣaṇayorasaṁbhavāt । jāyamāno hi caitra ekasminkṣaṇe jāyate । [na tatra dvau kṣaṇau saha bhavataḥ । kramaśca na dvayoḥ ।] kasmāt? [dvayoḥ] kṣaṇayoḥ [sahabhuvorasambhavāt ॥]
[pūrvasmāduttarasya bhāvino yadānantaryaṁ kṣaṇasya sa kramaḥ ।] yathā piṇḍāduttarabhāvino ghaṭasya yadā naṁntaryaṁ sa kramaḥ । na hi cakrāntarasthasya mṛtpiṇḍasya cakrāntarasthamṛtpiṇḍajanito ghaṭaḥ krame vartate । [tasmādvartamāna evaikaḥ kṣaṇaḥ ।] na pūrvottarāvatītānāgatau staḥ pūrvottarayordharmisvarūpamātratvāt । dharmī ca vartamānakṣaṇārūḍha eva । [tasmānnāsti tatsamāhāraḥ] kṣaṇatatkramasamāhāraḥ ॥
[ye tu bhūtabhavinaḥ] atītabhaviṣyantaḥ [kṣaṇāḥ te dharmiṇaḥ pūriṇmāstitayā] dharmipāraṁṇāmāpekṣayā vyākhyeyā: । [tenaikena kṣaṇena kṛtsno loka: pariṇāmamanubhavati । tatkṣaṇopārūḍhāḥ] vartamānakṣaṇopārūḍhāḥ [khalvamī sarve dharmāḥ] sarvapadārthāḥ ॥
yaduktamatītakṣaṇasya nāstikrama iti, tasyaitatprayojanaṁ, tatkramakramapratiṣedhaḥ । kṣaṇakramakrame hi sati kṣaṇakramasya vastutvaṁ prasajyeta । vastuno hi krama iti । tataśca krapatatkṣaṇayoḥ saṁyamāditinopakalpeta । tasmāt [etayoḥ kṣaṇa] [tat] [kramayoḥ seyamāttayoḥ sākṣātkaraṇam । tataśca vivekajaṁ jñānam ।] kṣaṇatatkramāṅkitā eva hi sarve padārthā iti tānaśeṣānvivicya vijānāti [॥ 52 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['But the moment is grounded in reality'] — it is actual, being inferred through the otherwise-ness of substances. ['It depends on sequence. And sequence, whose nature is the immediate succession of moments'] — it is occasioned by the cognition of the interruption of the flow of moments.
['The knowers of time call that moment "time." And two moments do not exist simultaneously,'] such that an aggregate of them could be postulated. Because in one substance-bearer, two moments of simultaneous birth are impossible. For <s>Caitra</s>, being born, is born in one moment. ['Two moments do not exist simultaneously there. And sequence does not belong to two.'] Why? ['Because two'] moments ['existing simultaneously is impossible.']
['The immediate succession of a later moment that comes into being after a prior one — that is sequence.'] Just as the immediate succession of a pot that comes into being after a lump of clay — that is sequence. For the pot produced from a lump of clay on the potter's wheel does not exist in sequence while the clay lump is still on the wheel. ['Therefore, only one present moment exists.'] The prior and the later — the past and the future — do not exist, because the prior and the later are merely the substance-bearer's own nature. And the substance-bearer is mounted only upon the present moment. ['Therefore, there is no aggregate of those'] — no aggregate of moment and its sequence.
['But those moments that have been and will be'] — past and future — ['those should be explained with reference to the substance-bearer's prior existence'] — in relation to the transformation of the substance-bearer. ['By that one moment, the entire world undergoes transformation. All <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) are mounted upon that moment'] — mounted upon the present moment — ['indeed all these <s>dharmas</s>'] — all entities.
What was stated — that a past moment has no sequence — the purpose of that is the negation of the sequence of that sequence. For if there were a sequence of the sequence of moments, then the sequence of moments would have substantial reality, since sequence belongs to what is substantial. And then it would not be possible to perform <s>saṁyama</s> 'on these two — the moment and its sequence.' Therefore, ['from <s>saṁyama</s> on these two — the moment'] ['and its'] ['sequence — comes their direct realization. And from that, knowledge born of discrimination arises.'] For indeed all entities are marked by the moment and its sequence, and thus one discriminates and knows them in their entirety. [॥ 52 ॥]

body.text: tasya viṣayaviśeṣa upakṣipyate –
body.translated_text: The specific object of that [knowledge] is indicated —

body.text: jātilakṣaṇadeśairanyatānavacchedāttulyayostataḥ pratipattiḥ ॥ 53 ॥
body.translated_text: From that (discriminative knowledge) comes the recognition of two [things that are] similar, when their difference (<s>anyatā</s>) is not delimited by class (<s>jāti</s>), mark (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), or location (<s>deśa</s>). ॥ 53 ॥

body.text: tulyayordeśalakṣaṇasārūpye jātibhedo'nyatāyā hetuḥ, gauriyaṁ vaḍaveyamiti। tulyadeśajātīyatve lakṣaṇamanyatvakaraṁ kālākṣī gauḥ svastimatī gauriti। dvayorāmalakayorjātilakṣaṇasārūpyāddeśabhedo'nyatvakara idaṁ pūrvamidamuttaramiti। yadā tu pūrvamāmalakamanyavyagrasya jñāturuttaradeśa upāvartyate tadā tulyadeśatve pūrvametaduttarametaditipravibhāgānupapattiḥ। asaṁdigdhena ca tattvajñānena bhavitavyamityata idamuktaṁ tataḥ pratipattirvivekajajñānāditi।
body.translated_text: When two things are similar in location and mark, the difference of class is the cause of their distinction — 'this is a cow, this is a mare.' When they are of the same class and location, a distinguishing mark differentiates them — 'this is the dark-eyed cow, this is the auspicious-marked cow.' When two <s>āmalaka</s> fruits are similar in class and mark, difference of location causes their distinction — 'this is the one in front, this is the one behind.' But when the front <s>āmalaka</s> fruit is moved to the location of the rear one for a perceiver whose attention is elsewhere, then when the locations are the same, the distinction 'this is the front one, this is the rear one' becomes impossible. And yet there must be certain knowledge of the truth — hence it is said: 'from that comes recognition,' meaning from knowledge born of discrimination.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
tasya vivekajñasya jñānasya kīdṛśaṁ jñeyamiti [tasya viṣayaviśeṣaḥ upakṣipyate – jātilakṣaṇadeśairanyatānavacchedāt tulyayostataḥ pratipattiḥ । [tulyayordeśalakṣaṇasārūpye] jātibhedaḥ] padārthānām [anyatāyāḥ] anyatvāvacchedasya [hetuḥ ।] yathā - [gairiyaṁ baḍaveyamiti ॥]
yatra jātibhedo nāstyekaiva jātiḥ, tatra [tulyajātitve lakṣaṇaṁ] liṅgam [anyatvāvacchedakaram - kālākṣī gauḥ, svastimatī gauriti ॥]
yatra na jātibhedo nāpi lakṣaṇabhedastatra deśabhedo'nyatvāvacchedahetuḥ । yathā- [dvayorāmalakayorjātilakṣaṇasārūpye deśabhedo'nyatvakaraḥ idaṁ pūrvam] āmalakam [idamuttaramiti ॥]
[yadā tu pūrvamāmalakam anyavyagrasya] samākulitacittasya [jñāturuttaradeśa upāvartate] pūrvadeśe cottaraṁ, [tadā tulyadeśatve pūrvametaduttarametaditi] tulyayoḥ [pravibhāgānupapattiḥ । asandigdhena tattvajñānena bhavitavyaṁ,] jñeyasya vidyamānatvādekarūpasya [ityata idamuktaṁ tataḥ prātipattirvivekajñānāditi ।] kṣaṇatatkramasaṁyamāpāditavivekajanmano jñānāt pratipattiriti ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
What kind of object does the knowledge of one who possesses discriminative knowledge have? ['The specific object of that is indicated — From that comes the recognition of two similar things when their difference is not delimited by class, mark, or location. When two things are similar in location and mark, the difference of class'] of objects ['is the cause of'] the delimitation of ['their distinction.'] As in — ['this is a cow, this is a mare.']
Where there is no class difference — where the class is one and the same — there, ['when the class is the same, a mark'] — a distinguishing sign — ['causes the delimitation of distinction — "this is the dark-eyed cow, this is the auspicious-marked cow."']
Where there is neither class difference nor mark difference, there difference of location is the cause of delimiting distinction. As — ['when two <s>āmalaka</s> fruits are similar in class and mark, difference of location causes distinction — "this is the front'] <s>āmalaka</s>, ['this is the rear one."']
['But when the front <s>āmalaka</s> fruit is moved to the rear location for a perceiver'] whose mind is distracted, ['then when the locations are the same, the distinction "this is the front one, this is the rear one"'] between the two similar ones ['becomes impossible. And yet there must be certain knowledge of the truth,'] because the knowable object exists in a single form, ['hence it is said: from that comes recognition, from knowledge born of discrimination.'] From knowledge whose birth is discrimination attained through <s>saṁyama</s> on the moment and its sequence comes recognition.

body.text: kathaṁ, pūrvāmalakasahakṣaṇo deśa uttarāmalakasahakṣaṇāddeśādbhinnaḥ। te cā''malake svadeśakṣaṇānubhavabhinne। anyadeśakṣaṇānubhavastu tayoranyatve heturiti। etena dṛṣṭāntena paramāṇostulyajātilakṣaṇadeśasya pūrvaparamāṇudeśasahakṣaṇasākṣātkaraṇāduttarasya paramāṇostaddeśā-nupapattāvuttarasya taddeśānubhavo bhinnaḥ sahakṣaṇabhedāttayorīśvarasya yogino'nyatvapratyayo bhavatīti।
body.translated_text: How? The location that coexists with the moment of the front <s>āmalaka</s> is different from the location that coexists with the moment of the rear <s>āmalaka</s>. And those two <s>āmalaka</s> fruits are differentiated by the experience of their respective location-moments. But the experience of a different location-moment is the cause of their distinction. By this example, for an atom that is similar in class, mark, and location — through the direct realization of the moment coexisting with the location of the prior atom, when the location of the subsequent atom cannot be the same — the experience of that location for the subsequent atom is different due to the difference of coexisting moments. From the difference of moments, the Lord, the <s>yogin</s>, has the cognition of their distinction.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tat katham? pūrvāmalakasaha(la)kṣaṇo deśaḥ] pūrvāmalakasahacaro deśaḥ [uttarāmalakasaha(la)kṣaṇāt] uttarāmalakasahacarāt deśāt miśraḥ । [te cāmalake] pūrvottara(la)kṣaṇasahacarite [svadeśa(la)kṣaṇānubhavabhinne] svadeśacihnabhūte yaḥ kṣaṇaḥ tadanubhavaminne svedeśa(la)kṣaṇānubhavacihnite [anyadeśa(la)kṣaṇānubhavastayoranyatve heturiti ॥]
[anena dṛṣṭāntena paramāṇoratulyajātilakṣaṇameda(deśa)sya pūrvaparamāṇudeśasaha(la)kṣaṇasākṣātkaraṇāt] pūrvaparamāṇudeśana sahabhūtasya (la)kṣaṇasya sākṣātkaraṇāt [uttaraparamāṇostaddeśāpavṛtau] pūrvadeśagatāvapi [uttarasya taddeśānubhavabhinnaḥ kṣaṇaḥ । kṣaṇabhedāttayorīśvarasya yogino'nya(thā)tvapratyayaḥ] bhedāvacechado [bhavati ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['How then?
