The location that coexists with the moment of the front <s>āmalaka</s>'] — the location that accompanies the front <s>āmalaka</s> — ['is different from the location that coexists with the moment of the rear <s>āmalaka</s>'] — from the location that accompanies the rear <s>āmalaka</s>. ['And those two <s>āmalaka</s> fruits,'] characterized by the prior and the later, ['are differentiated by the experience of their respective location-moments'] — by the moment that serves as the mark of their respective locations — ['the experience of a different location-moment is the cause of their distinction.']
['By this example, for an atom that is similar in class, mark, and location — through the direct realization of the moment coexisting with the location of the prior atom'] — through the direct realization of the mark (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) coexisting with the location of the prior atom — ['when the subsequent atom arrives at that location'] — even when it reaches the prior location — ['the moment of that location-experience for the subsequent atom is different. From the difference of moments, the Lord, the <s>yogin</s>, has the cognition of distinction'] — the delimitation of difference — ['arises.']

body.text: apare tu varṇayanti – ye'ntyā viśeṣāste'nyatāpratyayaṁ kurvantīti। tatrāpi deśalakṣaṇabhedo mūrtivyavadhijātibhedaścānyatve hetuḥ। kṣaṇabhedastu yogibuddhigamya eveti। ata uktaṁ mūrtivyavadhijātibhedābhāvānnāsti mūlapṛthaktvamiti vārṣagaṇyaḥ ॥ 53 ॥
body.translated_text: Others, however, explain it thus — the ultimate specific differences (<s>antyā viśeṣāḥ</s>) produce the cognition of distinction. Even there, difference of location and mark, and difference of class through physical form and spatial separation, are the causes of distinction. But the difference of moments is comprehensible only to the <s>yogin</s>'s intellect. Hence it has been stated — 'Because of the absence of difference in physical form, spatial separation, and class, there is no fundamental separateness' — this is the view of <s>Vārṣagaṇya</s>. ॥ 53 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[atrāpare varṇayanti--ye antyā viśeṣāḥ] paramāṇugatā nityāḥ, [te eva anyatāpratyayaṁ kurvantīti] kiṁ tatkṣaṇatatkramasaṁyamena । yathā ghaṭādigatā viśeṣā anyatāpratyayaṁ kurvanti, tathā paramāṇugatā ye viśeṣāḥ ta eva tadbhāvapratyayaṁ svasadbhāvapratyayaṁ ca kurvīran । āśrayabhedapralyayamapi kurvanti ॥
atrocyate - [deśalakṣaṇabhedo mūrtivyavadhijātibhedaścānyatve hetuḥ] ukta eva sthūleṣu (na tu) nanu paramāṇuṣu pratikṣaṇapariṇāmitvāt । avasthiteṣu hi viśeṣeṣvantyeṣu syādanyathā'vadhāraṇam । na cānavaratapariṇāmeṣu ghaṭate ॥
yadā pūrvaḥ paramāṇuruttaraparamāṇurūpeṇa pariṇamate, pūrvaparamāṇurūpeṇa cottaraḥ, tatrāvasthitāntyaviśeṣābhāvādvivekapratipaktiranupapannā । tatrāvaśyaṁ kṣaṇatatkramasaṁyamajanitavivekajñānādeva saṁpratipattiḥ । anityāśca paramāṇava iti hyuktam । tasmāt [kṣaṇabhedastu yogibuddhigamya eva ॥]
tathā cānityatvasya paramāṇūnāmācāryāntaramatapratipādanadvāreṇa prasiddhiṁ darśayati-- [ata uktam] - [mūrtivyavadhijātibhedābhāvāt nāsti mūla] (jāti) [pṛthaktvamiti vārṣagaṇyaḥ ।] yathā pratikṣetrajñaṁ pradhānabuhutvaṁ nyāyaviruddhaṁ mūrtivyavadhijātibhedābhāvāt pradhānānāṁ pṛthaktvam ekapuruṣārthadṛśyavat anupapannam, evaṁ paramāṇūnāmapi mūlatve pṛthaktvaṁ nopakalpate । tataśca ekaṁ mūlamiti prāptam । na paramāṇubhedo hi nityo yuktaḥ । paramāṇūnāṁ ca mūrtatvāt rūpādimattvācca anilyatvaṁ ghaṭādivadeveti ॥ 53 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
["Here others explain — the ultimate particularities"] residing in atoms, being eternal, ["are what produce the cognition of difference."] What then is the need for <s>saṁyama</s> on the moment and its sequence? Just as particularities residing in pots and the like produce the cognition of difference, so too the particularities residing in atoms would produce the cognition of their existence and their own being. They also produce the cognition of difference of substratum.
To this it is replied — ["Difference of place and characteristic, difference of solidity, boundary, and class are the causes of otherness"] — this has already been stated for gross objects, but not for atoms, because of their constant transformation at every moment. If the ultimate particularities were stable, then a determination of otherness would be possible. But it is not feasible in things that are ceaselessly transforming.
When a prior atom transforms into the form of a subsequent atom, and the subsequent into the form of the prior, since there are no stable ultimate particularities therein, discrimination-based understanding is untenable. Therefore, understanding must necessarily come from discrimination-knowledge born of <s>saṁyama</s> on the moment and its sequence alone. And it has been stated that atoms are non-eternal. Therefore, ["the distinction of moments is accessible only to the <s>yogin</s>'s intellect."]
Accordingly, he demonstrates the well-known non-eternality of atoms by presenting the view of another teacher — ["Therefore it has been said"] — ["because of the absence of differences of solidity, boundary, and class, there is no fundamental separateness — so says <s>Vārṣagaṇya</s>."] Just as the plurality of <s>pradhāna</s> for each individual <s>puruṣa</s> is logically untenable — because, in the absence of differences of solidity, boundary, and class, the separateness of <s>pradhānas</s> is untenable, being like [everything being] visible to a single <s>puruṣa</s> — similarly, even the separateness of atoms as fundamental [entities] cannot be maintained. And thus the conclusion is that there is a single root [cause]. For the eternal distinction of atoms is not logically tenable. And since atoms are material, possessing form and the like, their non-eternality follows, just like pots and the like. ॥ 53 ॥

body.text: tārakaṁ sarvaviṣayaṁ sarvathāviṣayamakramaṁ ceti vivekajaṁ jñānam ॥ 54 ॥
body.translated_text: Transcendent (<s>tāraka</s>), having all things as its object, having all modes as its object, and non-sequential — such is the knowledge born of discrimination (<s>vivekaja jñāna</s>). ॥ 54 ॥

body.text: tārakamitisvapratibhotthamanaupadeśikamityarthaḥ। sarvaviṣayaṁ nāsya kiṁcidaviṣayībhūtamityarthaḥ। sarvathāviṣayamatītānāgatapratyutpannaṁ sarvaṁ paryāyaiḥ sarvathā jānātītyarthaḥ। akramamityekakṣaṇopārūḍhaṁ sarvaṁ sarvathā gṛhṇātītyarthaḥ। etadvivekajaṁ jñānaṁ paripūrṇam। asyaivāṁśo yogapradīpo madhumatīṁ bhūmimupādāya yāvadasya parisamāptiriti ॥ 54 ॥
body.translated_text: 'Transcendent' (<s>tāraka</s>) means arising from one's own intuitive insight (<s>pratibhā</s>), not from instruction — this is the meaning. 'Having all things as its object' means nothing remains outside its scope — this is the meaning. 'Having all modes as its object' means it knows everything — past, future, and present — in all its aspects, through all its modes — this is the meaning. 'Non-sequential' means it grasps everything in all its modes, mounted upon a single moment — this is the meaning. This discrimination-born knowledge is complete. A portion of this very [knowledge] is the 'lamp of yoga' (<s>yoga-pradīpa</s>), from the 'honey-like stage' (<s>madhumatī bhūmi</s>) up to its full consummation. ॥ 54 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tārakaṁ sarvaviṣayaṁ sarvathāviṣayam akramaṁ ceti vivekajaṁ jñānam ।] kāṣṭhāprāpta jñānaṁ devarṣigandharvādīnām । [tārakamiti ।] vivekajāmidamucyate [svapratibhotthamanaupadeśikamityarthaḥ ।] nānyenopadeṣṭuṁ śakyaṁ, nāpyupadeśena yathāvat grahītuṁ śakyate । yasmāt tat [sarvavastuviṣayam । nāsya kiṁcidaviṣayībhūtam ।]
[sarvathāviṣayaṁ ca] sarvam [atītānāgatapratyutpatraṁ sarvaparyāyaiḥ] sarvaviśeṣaṇaiḥ [sarvathā] sarveṇa prakāreṇa [jānāti । akramam ekakṣaṇopārūḍha़m ।] ekasmin kṣaṇe [sarvaṁ sarvathā gṛhṇāti ।] nāsmadādivat krameṇa ॥
tat [etadvivekajaṁ jñānaṁ paripūrṇam, asyaivāṁśo yogapradīpaḥ ।] sa eva jñānāṁśo yogaśca pradīpaśca । yogasya vā pradīpo yogapradīpaḥ । [madhumatīṁ bhūmimupādāya] ārabhya [yāvadasya] vivekajasya jñānasya [parisamāptiḥ] tāvat । vivekajajñānaparisamāptiparyantāni jñānāni manojavaktvādiyuktāni asyaivāṁśaḥ ॥ 54 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
["Transcendent, having all things as its object, having all modes as its object, and non-sequential — such is the knowledge born of discrimination."] This is the knowledge that has reached its culmination — belonging to divine sages (<s>devarṣi</s>), <s>Gandharvas</s>, and the like. ["Transcendent."] This is called discrimination-born, ["arising from one's own intuitive insight, not from instruction — this is the meaning."] It cannot be taught by another, nor can it be properly grasped through instruction. Because that [knowledge] ["has all things as its object. Nothing remains outside its scope."]
["Having all modes as its object"] — ["everything — past, future, and present — through all its modes"] — it knows simultaneously, in a single moment. This knowledge ["mounted upon a single moment, grasps everything in all its modes — this is the meaning."] This is the most complete of all knowledges born of discrimination. A portion of it is the 'lamp of yoga,' beginning from the 'honey-like stage' — this is as before. ॥ 54 ॥

body.text: prāptavivekajajñānasyāprāptavivekajajñānasya vā –
body.translated_text: For one who has attained discrimination-born knowledge, or for one who has not attained discrimination-born knowledge —

body.text: sattvapuruṣayoḥ śuddhisāmye kaivalyamiti ॥ 55 ॥
body.translated_text: When there is equality of purity between <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, [there is] <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation). ॥ 55 ॥

body.text: yadā nirdhūtarajastamomalaṁ buddhisattvaṁ puruṣasyānyatāpratītimātrādhikāraṁ dagdhakleśabījaṁ bhavati tadā puruṣasya śuddhisārūpyamivā''pannaṁ bhavati, tadā puruṣasyopacaritabhogābhāvaḥ śuddhiḥ। etasyāmavasthāyāṁ kaivalyaṁ bhavatīśvarasyānīśvarasya vā vivekajajñānabhāgina itarasya vā। nahi dagdhakleśabījasya jñāne punarapekṣā kācidasti। sattvaśuddhidvāreṇaitatsamādhijamaiśvaryaṁ jñānaṁ copakrāntam। paramārthatastu jñānādadarśanaṁ nivartate tasminnivṛtte na santyuttare kleśāḥ। kleśābhāvātkarmavipākābhāvaḥ। caritādhikārāścaittasyāmavasthāyāṁ guṇā na puruṣasya punardṛśyatvenopatiṣṭhante। tatpuruṣasya kaivalyaṁ, tadā puruṣaḥ svarūpamātrajyotiramalaḥ kevalī bhavati ॥ 55 ॥
body.translated_text: When <s>buddhi-sattva</s> (the luminous essence of intellect), having shaken off the impurity of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, has its function reduced to merely the cognition of the otherness of <s>Puruṣa</s>, and has its seeds of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) burnt — then it has attained, as it were, a likeness to the purity of <s>Puruṣa</s>. Then the absence of figurative experience for <s>Puruṣa</s> is purity. In this state, <s>kaivalya</s> occurs — whether for the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) or for one who is not the Lord, whether for one who possesses discrimination-born knowledge or for another. For one whose seeds of affliction have been burnt, there is no further need of anything with regard to knowledge. Through the gateway of the purity of <s>sattva</s>, this <s>samādhi</s>-born sovereignty and knowledge have been undertaken. But in the ultimate sense, from [right] knowledge, false seeing (<s>adarśana</s>) ceases; when that ceases, there are no further <s>kleśas</s>. From the absence of <s>kleśas</s>, there is absence of the fruition of <s>karma</s>. In this state, the <s>guṇas</s>, having fulfilled their function, no longer present themselves to <s>Puruṣa</s> as the seen. That is <s>kaivalya</s> for <s>Puruṣa</s>. Then <s>Puruṣa</s>, being the light of its own essential form alone, immaculate, becomes liberated (<s>kevalin</s>). ॥ 55 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
yogaje jñānaiścarya atikrānte parisamāpite ca । nātaḥ paraṁ yogajñānamaiśvaryaṁ ca । tada(du)pakramaṇācca prāptajñānaiśvaryasyaiva tadvairāgyānantaraṁ kaivalyamiti prāptamata āha- [prāptavivekajñānasya [aprāptavivekajñānasya vā]] bāhyadarśananivṛtau kaivalyam । kathamiti ? [sattvapuruṣayoḥ śuddhisāmye kaivalyāniti ॥]
[yadā nirdhūtarajastamomalaṁ purūṣānyatāpratyayamātram] anyatāmātrapratyayavaibhavayuktaṁ [dagdhakleśabījaṁ] vinivṛttāvidyāpratyayavāsanārūpaṁ [buddhisatvaṁ bhavati, tadā puruṣasya śuddhisārūpyamivāpannam ॥]
yadyapi triguṇaṁ puruṣavilakṣaṇaṁ, puruṣaśca tadvilakṣaṇaḥ, tathā'pi puruṣānyatāpratyayapariṇāmitvāt [śuddhisārūpyamivāpannam] ityucyate । [etasyāmavasthāyāṁ kaivalyaṁ bhavatīścarasyānīścarasya vā, vivekajñānabhāginaḥ itarasya vā ।] yasmādubhayoravidyānivṛtireva kāraṇaṁ tasmāt । [nahi dagdhaleśabījasya jñāne kācidapekṣā ।] yataḥ samyagdarśī sarvaṁ triguṇamiti manyate, triguṇaśca pratyayo heya iti, madhumatyādijñāne tasya na kadācidapyapekṣā ॥
yattu yogajñānamaiśvaryaṁ coktaṁ, tat samyagdarśanārthanukrāntasattvaśuddhipadamārgeṇa prakrāntamānuṣaṅgikam । [paramārthatastu jñānādadarśanaṁ vinivartate । tasmin vinivṛtte na santyuktakleśāḥ] asmitādayaḥ । teṣāmavidyākṣetratvāt । [kleśābhāvācca karmavipākābhāvaḥ “kleśamūlaḥ karmāśayaḥ” “sati mūle tadvipākaḥ”] iti hi pratipāditam ॥
tasmāt samyagdarśanārthamevedaṁ śāstram, na jñānaiśvaryavibhūtiprayojanam । [caritādhikārācaitasyāmavasthāyāṁ guṇāḥ । na puruṣasya punarddaśyatvenātiṣṭhante । tat puruṣasya kaivalyam । tadā puruṣaḥ svarūpamātrajyotiḥ iti amalaḥ kevalībhavati] iti । [iti] śabdaḥ samāptyarthaḥ ॥ 55 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
When the yoga-born knowledge and sovereignty have been transcended and brought to consummation — there is no yoga-born knowledge or sovereignty beyond this. And since this has been undertaken, it is only for one who has attained knowledge and sovereignty that <s>kaivalya</s> follows immediately upon dispassion towards those — thus it is established. Therefore he says — ["For one who has attained discrimination-born knowledge, or for one who has not attained it"] — upon the cessation of outward-directed seeing, there is <s>kaivalya</s>. How? ["When there is equality of purity between <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, there is <s>kaivalya</s>."]
["When <s>buddhi-sattva</s>, having shaken off the impurity of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, has been reduced to merely the cognition of the otherness of <s>Puruṣa</s>,"] endowed with the power of cognizing merely the otherness [of <s>Puruṣa</s>], ["with its seeds of affliction burnt"] — its latent dispositions in the form of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) having ceased — ["then <s>buddhi-sattva</s> has attained, as it were, a likeness to the purity of <s>Puruṣa</s>."]
Although it is constituted of the three <s>guṇas</s> and is different from <s>Puruṣa</s>, and <s>Puruṣa</s> is different from it, nevertheless, because it has transformed into merely the cognition of the otherness of <s>Puruṣa</s>, ["it is said to have attained, as it were, a likeness to purity."] ["In this state, <s>kaivalya</s> occurs — whether for the Lord or for one who is not the Lord, whether for one who possesses discrimination-born knowledge or for another."] Because for both, the cessation of <s>avidyā</s> alone is the cause. ["For one whose seeds of affliction have been burnt, there is no further need of anything with regard to knowledge."] Since one who sees rightly considers everything as constituted of the three <s>guṇas</s>, and a cognition constituted of the three <s>guṇas</s> is to be abandoned — in knowledge such as the 'honey-like' and so forth, he has no need whatsoever.
As for the yoga-born knowledge and sovereignty that have been stated, they arise incidentally through the path of the stage of purity of <s>sattva</s> that accompanies [the pursuit of] right vision. ["But in the ultimate sense, from knowledge, false seeing ceases. When that ceases, there are no further <s>kleśas</s>"] — <s>asmitā</s> (I-am-ness) and the rest — because <s>avidyā</s> is their field. ["And from the absence of <s>kleśas</s>, there is absence of the fruition of <s>karma</s>"] — for it has been established that ["'the <s>kleśas</s> are the root of the store of <s>karma</s>'"] and ["'when the root exists, there is its fruition.'"] 
Therefore, this <s>śāstra</s> (teaching) is only for the purpose of right vision, not for the purpose of knowledge-sovereignty-powers. ["Having fulfilled their function, in this state the <s>guṇas</s> no longer present themselves to <s>Puruṣa</s> as the seen. That is <s>kaivalya</s> for <s>Puruṣa</s>. Then <s>Puruṣa</s>, being the light of its own essential form alone,"] immaculate, ["becomes liberated."] The word '<s>iti</s>' denotes conclusion. ॥ 55 ॥

body.text: kaivalyapādaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Kaivalya-pāda</s> (Chapter on Liberation)

body.text: janmauṣadhimantratapaḥsamādhijāḥ siddhayaḥ ॥ 1 ॥
body.translated_text: The <s>siddhis</s> (attainments) arise from birth, herbs, <s>mantras</s>, austerity (<s>tapas</s>), and <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption). ॥ 1 ॥

body.text: dehāntaritā janmanā siddhiḥ। oṣīdhibhirasurabhavaneṣu rasāyanenetyevamādiḥ। mantrairākāśagamanāṇimādilābhaḥ। tapasā saṁkalpasiddhiḥ, kāmarūpī yatra tatra kāmaga ityevamādi। samādhijāḥ siddhayo vyākhyātāḥ ॥ 1 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>Siddhi</s> arising from birth is [acquired] through a different body. From herbs — in the abodes of the <s>Asuras</s>, through elixirs (<s>rasāyana</s>), and so forth. From <s>mantras</s> — attainment of traversing the sky, <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness), and the like. From <s>tapas</s> (austerity) — fulfillment of resolve: becoming one who assumes any form at will, going wherever one wishes, and so forth. The <s>siddhis</s> arising from <s>samādhi</s> have [already] been explained. ॥ 1 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
prathame pāde samādhiḥ prādhānyena nirdiṣṭaḥ । dvitīye tatsādhanāni vyākhyātāni । tṛtīye tu samyagdarśanārthayogāṅgānuṣṭhānānuṣaṅgajajñānaiśvaryānukramaṇaṁ kṛtam । tacca sarva du:khasyeti jaigīṣavyākhyānena pratipāditam । du:khahānaṁ cātyantikaguṇoparama ityuktam । tathaiva [‘tadvairāgyādapi' doṣabījakṣaye kaivalyam । ”prāptavivekajñānasyāprāptavivekajñānasya vā “sattvapuruṣayoḥ śuddhisāmye kaivalyam] ' ityanantaramuktam । tacca kaivalyaṁ pratipakṣanivartanena pratipādanīyamitīdaṁ kaivalyapādānukramaṇaṁ kriyate ॥
tathā anekajanmāntaropārjitavāsanocchedaprakārāśca kaivalyārthameva pradarśanīyāḥ । tathā kaivalyopayogisamādhisiddhistutyarthaṁ pūrvatrānuktaṁ siddhyantaraṁ prakriyate । tulyajātīyānāmanyatamānindanenānyatamastutirbhavati ॥ [“tatra dhyānajamanāśayam’ 'karmāśuklākṛṣṇaṁ yoginastrividhamitareṣām”] iti vakṣyamāṇena stutyarthatā āviṣkariṣyate ॥
[janmauṣadhimantratapassamādhijāḥ siddhayaḥ । dehāntaritā] yathā yogādinā dehāntareṣu svargādiṣu janmasiddhiḥ । [oṣadhibhirasurabhavaneṣu rasāyanena] somāmalakādibhakṣaṇena pūrvadehānapanayenaiva । [mantraiḥ] upajapyamānaiḥ [ā.ākāśagamanādi । tapasā saṁkalpasiddhiḥ kāmarūpī yatra kāmagamana ityevamādiḥ । samādhijāḥ siddhayaḥ] pūrvameva [vyākhyātāḥ ॥ 1 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
In the first chapter, <s>samādhi</s> was primarily set forth. In the second, its means were explained. In the third, the sequential exposition of knowledge and sovereignty arising incidentally from the practice of the limbs of yoga for the purpose of right vision was carried out. And that [the goal] is the cessation of all suffering was demonstrated through the narrative of <s>Jaigīṣavya</s>. And it was stated that the cessation of suffering is the absolute cessation of the <s>guṇas</s>. Likewise, ['from dispassion towards even that,'] upon the destruction of the seeds of defects, there is <s>kaivalya</s>. "For one who has attained discrimination-born knowledge or for one who has not" — "when there is equality of purity between <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, there is <s>kaivalya</s>" — this was stated immediately after. And that <s>kaivalya</s> is to be established through the removal of its opposite — for this purpose the sequential exposition of the <s>Kaivalya-pāda</s> is undertaken.
Also, the methods for uprooting latent impressions (<s>vāsanās</s>) accumulated across many births are to be demonstrated for the sake of <s>kaivalya</s> itself. Likewise, for the purpose of praising the <s>samādhi</s>-attainment conducive to <s>kaivalya</s>, other <s>siddhis</s> not mentioned earlier are presented. By censuring one among things of the same class, another is praised.
["'Therein, the meditation-born is without residual deposit,' 'the <s>yogin</s>'s <s>karma</s> is neither white nor black; for others it is threefold'"] — by what is to be stated thus, the purpose of praise will be made clear.
["The <s>siddhis</s> arise from birth, herbs, <s>mantras</s>, austerity, and <s>samādhi</s>. Through a different body"] — just as through yoga and the like, there is <s>siddhi</s> through birth in other [realms] such as heaven. ["From herbs, in the abodes of the <s>Asuras</s>, through elixirs"] — through consumption of <s>Soma</s>, <s>āmalaka</s> (gooseberry), and the like, without abandoning the previous body itself. ["From <s>mantras</s>,"] when recited — ["traversing the sky and the like. From austerity, fulfillment of resolve: becoming one who assumes any form at will, going wherever one wishes, and so forth. The <s>siddhis</s> arising from <s>samādhi</s>"] have ["already been explained."] ॥ 1 ॥

body.text: tatra kāyendriyāṇāmanyajātīyapariṇatānām –
body.translated_text: Therein, when the body and sense organs have been transformed into another class —

body.text: jātyantarapariṇāmaḥ prakṛtyāpūrāt ॥ 2 ॥
body.translated_text: The transformation into another class of being arises from the flowing in of <s>Prakṛti</s> (nature). ॥ 2 ॥

body.text: pūrvapariṇāmāpāya uttarapariṇāmopajanasteṣāmapūrvāvayavānupraveśādbhavati। kāyendriyaprakṛtayaśca svaṁ svaṁ vikāramanugṛhṇantyāpūreṇa dharmādinimittamapekṣamāṇā iti ॥ 2 ॥
body.translated_text: The cessation of the prior transformation and the arising of the subsequent transformation occur through the entry of new elements into them. And the material natures (<s>prakṛtis</s>) of body and sense organs support their respective modifications through the flowing in [of new elements], depending on <s>dharma</s> (merit) and other causes. ॥ 2 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
tatra siddhiḥ kāryakaraṇānāmutkarṣaḥ । jarnmasiddhau tu patitapūrvopārjitakāryakaraṇasya śarīrāntaramupādāyiṣyata iti nāsti tatra saṁśayaḥ । apatitaśarīrasya tu jāyantarapariṇāme kiṁ tadeva kāryakaraṇamupādānamutānyadapīti – [tatra kāyendriyāṇāmanyajātipariṇatānāṁ – jātyantarapariṇāmaḥ prakṛtyāpūrāt ॥]
[pūrvapariṇāmāpāye] samavasthitānameva pūrvakāryakaraṇānām [uttarapariṇāmopajanaḥ apūrvavayavānupraveśena bhavati ।] kasmāt ? alpaparimāṇasyopādānasya mahāparimāṇakāryānupapatteḥ । na hi daśapalāttapanīyapiṇḍādaśītipalā patrī janiṣyate ?
[kāyendriyaprakṛtayaḥ svaṁ svaṁ vikāraṁ] kāyamindriyaṁ vā [anugṛhṇantyāpūreṇa dharmādinimittam] ādigrahaṇādavakmamari nimittam [apekṣamāṇāḥ] ॥ 2 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
Therein, <s>siddhi</s> is the enhancement of the body-and-instrument complex. In the case of <s>siddhi</s> through birth, there is no doubt — one whose previously acquired body-and-instrument complex has fallen will take up a different body. But for one whose body has not fallen, in the case of transformation into another class: does one take up the very same body-and-instrument complex, or does one take up another as well? — ["Therein, when the body and sense organs have been transformed into another class — the transformation into another class of being arises from the flowing in of <s>Prakṛti</s>."]
["Upon the cessation of the prior transformation,"] for the body-and-instrument complex that remains in its established state, ["the arising of the subsequent transformation occurs through the entry of new elements."] Why? Because an effect of great magnitude cannot arise from a material cause of small magnitude. For surely a plate weighing eighty <s>palas</s> will not be produced from a gold lump of ten <s>palas</s>?
["The material natures of body and sense organs support their respective modifications"] — body or sense organ — ["through the flowing in, depending on <s>dharma</s> and other causes"] — the word 'and other' includes non-meritorious causes — ["as instrumental conditions."] ॥ 2 ॥

body.text: nimittamaprayojakaṁ prakṛtīnāṁ varaṇabhedastu tataḥ kṣetrikavat ॥ 3 ॥
body.translated_text: The instrumental cause does not set the material natures (<s>prakṛtis</s>) in motion; rather, from it [comes] the removal of the obstacle — like a farmer. ॥ 3 ॥

body.text: na hi dharmādi nimittaṁ tatprayojakaṁ prakṛtīnāṁ bhavati। na kāryeṇa kāraṇaṁ pravartyata iti। kathaṁ tarhi, varaṇabhedastu tataḥ kṣetrikavat। yathā kṣetrikaḥ kedārādapāṁ pūrṇātkedārāntaraṁ piplāvayiṣuḥ samaṁ nimnaṁ nimnataraṁ vā nāpaḥ pāṇinā'pakarṣatyāvaraṇaṁ tvāsāṁ bhinatti tasminbhinne svayamevā''paḥ kedārāntaramāplāvayanti tathā dharmaḥ prakṛtīnāmāvaraṇamadharmaṁ bhinatti tasminbhinne svayameva prakṛtayaḥ svaṁ svaṁ vikāramāplāvayanti। yathā vā sa eva kṣetrikastasminneva kedāre na prabhavatyaudakānbhaumānvā rasāndhānyamūlānyanupraveśayituṁ, kiṁ tarhi mudgagavedhukaśyāmākādīṁstato'pakarṣati। apakṛṣṭeṣu teṣu svayameva rasā dhānyamūlānyanupraviśanti, tathā dharmo nivṛttimātre kāraṇamadharmasya, śuddhyaśuddhyoratyantavirodhāt, na tu prakṛtipravṛttau dharmo heturbhavatīti। atra nandīśvarādaya udāhāryāḥ। viparyayeṇāpyadharmo dharmaṁ bādhate। tataścāśuddhipariṇāma iti। tatrāpi nahuṣājagarādaya udāhāryāḥ ॥ 3 ॥
body.translated_text: For <s>dharma</s> (merit) and other instrumental causes do not set the material natures in motion. An effect does not activate a cause. How then? Rather, from it comes the removal of the obstacle — like a farmer. Just as a farmer, wishing to flood another field from a field full of water — whether level, low, or lower — does not drag the water with his hand, but breaks the barrier; and when it is broken, the water itself floods the other field — so too <s>dharma</s> breaks the obstacle of <s>adharma</s> (demerit) [blocking] the material natures; when that is broken, the material natures themselves flood into their respective modifications. Or, just as that same farmer cannot cause aqueous or terrestrial nutrients to enter the grain-roots in that very field; rather, he removes the mung beans, millet, barnyard grass, and the like; and when those are removed, the nutrients themselves enter the grain-roots — so too <s>dharma</s> is merely the cause of the cessation of <s>adharma</s>, because of the absolute opposition between purity and impurity; but <s>dharma</s> is not the cause of the activity of the material natures. Here <s>Nandīśvara</s> and others may be cited as examples. Conversely, <s>adharma</s> also obstructs <s>dharma</s>, and from that comes the transformation into impurity. Therein too, <s>Nahuṣa</s>, [who became] a serpent, and others may be cited as examples. ॥ 3 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[dharmādinimittamapekṣamāṇāḥ svaṁ svaṁ vikāramanugṛhṇanti] ityuktam । tatra kiṁ dharmodinimittaṁ prakṛtīnāṁ prayojakaṁ, kiṁ vā neti, tadāha – [nimittamaprayojakaṁ prakṛtīnāṁ varaṇabhedastu tataḥ kṣetrikavat । na hi dharmādinimittaṁ prayojakaṁ prakṛtīnām ।] kasmāt ? na hi kāryeṇa dharmadinā nimittena [kāraṇaṁ] kāryakaraṇaprāptarūpaṁ [pravartyate ॥]
[kathaṁ tarhi? varaṇabhedastu tataḥ] dharmādinimittāt bhavati । [kṣetrikavat । yathā kṣetrikaḥ kedārādapāṁ pūrṇāt kedārāntaraṁ piplāvayiṣuḥ nāpaḥ pāṇinā apakarṣati । āvaraṇaṁ tu tāsāṁ bhinatti । tasmit minne svayamevā''paḥ kedārāntaramāplāvayanti ॥]
[tathā dharmaḥ prakṛtīnāmāvaraṇamadharmaṁ bhinatti ।] dharmamadharmo'pi bhinattyāvaraṇam । [tasmin bhinne svayameva prakṛtayaḥ svaṁ svaṁ vikāramāplāvayanti] pūrayanti ॥
[yathā vā sa eva kṣetrikastasminneva kedāre na prabhavatyaudakān bhaumān vā rasān dhānyamūlānyanupraveśayitum । kiṁ tu mudbhatindukagavīthukaśyāmākādīn] tasmāt dhānyamūlāt [apakarṣati । apakṛṣṭeṣu teṣu svayameva rasā dhānyamūlānyanupraviśanti ॥]
[tathā dharmo nivṛttimātre kāraṇamadharmasya ।] adharmo'pi dharmasya । [śuddhyaśuddhyoratyantavirodhāt । na tu prakṛtipravṛttau dharmo heturbhavatīti ॥]
[atra nandīśvaraprabhṛtaya udāhāryāḥ । viparyayeṇā[pya]dharmo dharmaṁ bādhate । tataśdhāśudvipariṇāma iti । atrāpi nahuṣādaya udāhāryāḥ ॥ 3 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇa</s> (Sub-commentary):
It was stated that "[<s>dharma</s> (merit) and other causes, being dependent on conditions, facilitate their respective transformations]." Now the question is whether <s>dharma</s> and other causes are the impellers of the <s>prakṛtis</s> (primordial natures) or not. To this he says: "[The cause is not the impeller of the <s>prakṛtis</s>; rather, the breaking of the barrier is from that, like a farmer. For <s>dharma</s> and other causes do not impel the <s>prakṛtis</s>.]" Why? Because an effect, namely <s>dharma</s> and other causes, does not set in motion a cause that has already attained the form capable of producing effects.
"[How then? The breaking of the barrier is from that]" — from <s>dharma</s> and other causes. "[Like a farmer. Just as a farmer wishing to flood another field from a field full of water does not drag the water with his hands, but rather breaks the barrier of those waters. When that is broken, the waters themselves flood the other field.]"
"[Likewise, <s>dharma</s> breaks the barrier of <s>adharma</s> (demerit), which is the obstruction of the <s>prakṛtis</s>.]" And <s>adharma</s> also breaks the barrier that is <s>dharma</s>. "[When that is broken, the <s>prakṛtis</s> themselves flood — that is, fill — their respective transformations.]"
"[Or, just as that same farmer in that same field cannot make the watery or earthy essences enter the grain-roots, but rather he removes the weeds such as <s>mudbhatin</s>, <s>induka</s>, <s>gavīthuka</s>, and <s>śyāmāka</s>] from those grain-roots. [When those are removed, the essences themselves enter the grain-roots.]"
"[Likewise, <s>dharma</s> is the cause only of the cessation of <s>adharma</s>.]" And <s>adharma</s> likewise of <s>dharma</s>. "[Because purity and impurity are absolutely opposed to each other. But <s>dharma</s> is not the cause of the activity of <s>prakṛti</s>.]"
"[Here <s>Nandīśvara</s> and others are to be cited as examples. Conversely, <s>adharma</s> also obstructs <s>dharma</s>. From that comes the transformation of impurity. Here too, <s>Nahuṣa</s> and others are to be cited as examples.] (3)"

body.text: yadā tu yogī bahūnkāyānnirmimīte tadā kimekamanaskāste bhavantyathānekamanaskā iti –
body.translated_text: Now, when a <s>yogī</s> creates many bodies, do those have one mind or many minds?

body.text: nirmāṇacittānyasmitāmātrāt ॥ 4 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>Nirmāṇa-cittāni asmitā-mātrāt</s> — The created minds arise from the sense of pure I-am-ness alone. (4)

body.text: asmitāmātraṁ cittakāraṇamupādāya nirmāṇacittāni karoti, tataḥ sacittāni bhavantīti ॥ 4 ॥
body.translated_text: Taking <s>asmitā-mātra</s> (the mere sense of I-am-ness), which is the cause of <s>citta</s> (mind), as the basis, he creates the <s>nirmāṇa-cittāni</s> (manufactured minds); from that, they become endowed with minds. (4)

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[yadā tu yogī bahūn kāyānnirmimīte, tadā kimekamanaskāste bhavanti, athānekamanaskā iti] samādhisiddhe kaścidanukto viśeṣa ucyate - [nirmāṇacittānyasmitāmātrāt ।] so'haṁkāraṁ [cittakāraṇamupādāya nirmāṇacittāni] nirmitāni cintāni aprākṛtānīśvaracitāni navāni [karoti] yogī । cittagrahaṇamudāharaṇamātram । indriyāṇyapyasmitāmātrādeva । [tataḥ] te [sacittāḥ] sakāraṇāṁśca [bhavanti ॥]
cittendriyābhāve ca mṛtadeśīyaḥ kāyo nirarthakaḥ syāt । ekacittatve tu guṇapradhānabhāvaḥ pravṛttibhadeśca nopakalpate । tatra vibhutvādekakṣatrajñatve'pi bahukāyārāmbhatvamupapadyate । guṇapradhānānekapravṛttibhedārthaṁ tu karaṇabheda eṣitavyaḥ ॥
kecitu kṣetrajñā apyanye pratikāyabhedaṁ bhavantīti manvate । kecidatra codayanti akṛtābhyāgamam । anye tu tadanurūpopārjitakarmāṇaḥ kṣetrajñā bhavantīti parihāramāhuḥ ॥ 4 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇa</s> (Sub-commentary):
"[When a <s>yogī</s> creates many bodies, do they have one mind or many minds?]" — A specific point not previously stated regarding the accomplishments of <s>samādhi</s> is now stated: "[The created minds arise from <s>asmitā-mātra</s> alone.]" Taking <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-sense), [which is] the cause of <s>citta</s>, as the basis, the <s>yogī</s> creates the <s>nirmāṇa-cittāni</s> (manufactured minds) — minds that are newly created, not born of <s>Prakṛti</s>, fashioned by the Lord's will. The mention of <s>citta</s> is merely illustrative; the <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs) too arise from <s>asmitā-mātra</s> alone. "[From that]" they "[become endowed with minds]" and with causes.
The body, which serves as the basis for <s>citta</s> and <s>indriyas</s>, is also created from that very cause — this is established by reason.
But how do the created [bodies] become endowed with minds? The single <s>asmitā-mātra</s> is the cause for the <s>yogī</s>; from that, each individual <s>nirmāṇa-citta</s> (created mind) is produced; and through each of those, the <s>nirmāṇa-indriyas</s> (created sense organs) too possess [their respective functions] — this is the meaning.
Now, that which is the "[created mind]," its "[cause]" — which is a synonym for the transformation of the <s>sattva-dharma</s> (quality of pure being) of the <s>yogī</s> who creates — "[that is <s>asmitā-mātra</s>]," one and the same for all created [minds]. Thus it does not pertain to its own domain with differentiated functions caused by different <s>adṛṣṭas</s> (unseen karmic forces), but rather is a particular transformation of the <s>yogī</s>'s mind that serves as the cause of all <s>nirmāṇa-cittāni</s>.
And at all times the root-mind of the <s>yogī</s> governs all the <s>nirmāṇa-cittāni</s>, but the <s>nirmāṇa-cittāni</s> do not always govern the root-mind — with this intention he says: (4)

body.text: pravṛttibhede prayojakaṁ cittamekamanekeṣām ॥ 5 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>Pravṛtti-bhede prayojakaṁ cittam ekam anekeṣām</s> — When there is diversity of activity, the one mind is the director of the many. (5)

body.text: bahūnāṁ cittānāṁ kathamekacittābhiprāyapuraḥsarā pravṛttiriti sarvacittānāṁ prayojakaṁ cittamekaṁ nirmimīte, tataḥ pravṛttibhedaḥ ॥ 5 ॥
body.translated_text: How is the activity of many minds preceded by the intention of one mind? He creates one mind that is the director of all minds; from that arises the diversity of activity. (5)

body.text:
vivaraṇam
yadyevaṁ [kathaṁ bahūnāṁ cittānām ekacitābhiprāyapurassarā pravṛtiriti ।] tatrocyate - [pravṛttibheda prayojakaṁ cittamekamanekeṣām । pravṛttibhede satyapi sarvacittānāṁ prayojakaṁ cittamekaṁ] phalādhikṛtadeśīyaṁ śarīrāntare [nirmimīte ॥]
tacca yogibuddhimanuvartate । anyāni ca nirmāṇacittāni bhinnānekapravṛttīni । tannāyakacittānuvartīni bhavanti । tataśca teṣāṁ pravṛttiḥ 'nivṛttiḥ upekṣā ityevamadipravṛtibhedaḥ upapadyate । rājaprakṛtipravṛtibhedavat । evamekacittābhiprāyapuraḥsarā ca pravṛttiravakalpate ॥ 5 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇa</s> (Sub-commentary):
If so, "[how is the activity of many minds preceded by the intention of one mind?]" To that it is said: "[When there is diversity of activity, the one mind is the director of the many. Even when there is diversity of activity, the one mind that is the director of all minds]" creates [it] in another body located in the region governed by the fruit of [<s>karma</s>]."
And that [directing mind] follows the <s>yogī</s>'s <s>buddhi</s> (intellect). The other <s>nirmāṇa-cittāni</s> (created minds) have diverse and multiple activities. They follow the leader-mind. Thus their activity, cessation, or indifference occurs through the grace of the <s>yogī</s>'s intellect — this is the meaning.
What is the difference between the created and root minds? To this he says: The root-mind has its own latent impressions (<s>āśaya</s>), whereas the created minds are without latent impressions.

body.text: tatra dhyānajamanāśayam ॥ 6 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>Tatra dhyānajam anāśayam</s> — Among those, the one born of meditation is without latent impressions. (6)

body.text: pañcavidhaṁ nirmāṇacittaṁ janmauṣadhimantratapaḥsamādhijāḥ siddhaya iti। tatra yadeva dhyānajaṁ cittaṁ tadevānāśayaṁ tasyaiva nāstyāśayo rāgādipravṛttirnātaḥ puṇyapāpābhisaṁbandhaḥ kṣīṇakleśatvādyogina iti। itareṣāṁ tu vidyate karmāśayaḥ ॥ 6 ॥
body.translated_text: The <s>nirmāṇa-citta</s> (created mind) is of five kinds, since <s>siddhis</s> (attainments) arise from birth, herbs, <s>mantras</s>, <s>tapas</s> (austerity), and <s>samādhi</s>. Among those, only the mind born of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is without latent impressions (<s>anāśaya</s>); it alone has no <s>āśaya</s> — no tendency toward <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and other [afflictions] — and therefore has no connection with merit or demerit, because the <s>yogī</s>'s <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) are destroyed. But for the others, <s>karmāśaya</s> (the latent deposit of <s>karma</s>) exists. (6)

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tatra dhyānajamanāśayam । pañcavidhaṁ nirmāṇacittaṁ] janmauṣadhimantratapassamādhisāmarthyanirmitam । [tatra] teṣu [yadeva dhyānajaṁ cittaṁ tadeva anāśayaṁ] kleśakarmāśayāpavarjitam । [tasyaiva nāstyāśayaḥ rāgādipravṛttiḥ, ato na puṇyapāpābhisaṁbandhaḥ kṣīṇaṅkeśatvādyoginaḥ ॥ ‘kleśamūlo hi karmāśayaḥ’] ityuktam । tadabhāvācca karmāśayānupapattiḥ । apareṣāṁ tu janmādisiddhānāṁ [karmāśayaḥ] akṣīṇakleśavādvidyate eva ॥ 6 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇa</s> (Sub-commentary):
"[Among those, the one born of meditation is without latent impressions. The <s>nirmāṇa-citta</s> is of five kinds]" — created through the power of birth, herbs, <s>mantras</s>, <s>tapas</s>, and <s>samādhi</s>. "[Among]" those, "[only the mind born of <s>dhyāna</s> is without latent impressions]" — free from the deposit of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and <s>karma</s>. "[It alone has no <s>āśaya</s>, no tendency toward <s>rāga</s> and other afflictions; therefore there is no connection with merit or demerit, because the <s>yogī</s>'s <s>kleśas</s> are destroyed.]" It has been stated that "[the deposit of <s>karma</s> is indeed rooted in <s>kleśas</s>]." And due to the absence of those [<s>kleśas</s>], <s>karmāśaya</s> is impossible. But for the others — those who have attained <s>siddhis</s> through birth and so forth — "[<s>karmāśaya</s> exists]," because [their attainments] are caused by <s>rāga</s> and other [afflictions]. (6)

body.text: yataḥ –
body.translated_text: Because —

body.text: karmāśuklākṛṣṇaṁ yoginastrividhamitareṣām ॥ 7 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>Karma aśukla-akṛṣṇaṁ yoginas trividham itareṣām</s> — The <s>karma</s> of a <s>yogī</s> is neither white nor black; for others it is threefold. (7)

body.text: catuṣpadī khalviyaṁ karmajātiḥ। kṛṣṇā śuklakṛṣṇā śuklā'śuklākṛṣṇā ceti। tatra kṛṣṇā durātmanām। śuklakṛṣṇā bahiḥsādhanasādhyā। tatra parapīḍānugrahadvāreṇaiva karmāśayapracayaḥ। śuklā tapaḥsvādhyāyadhyānavatām। sā hi kevale manasyāyattatvādabahiḥsādhanādhīnā na parānpīḍayitvā bhavati। aśuklākṛṣṇā saṁnyāsināṁ kṣīṇakleśānāṁ caramadehānāmiti। tatrāśuklaṁ yogina eva phalasaṁnyāsādakṛṣṇaṁ cānupādānāt। itareṣāṁ tu bhūtānāṁ pūrvameva trividhamiti ॥ 7 ॥
body.translated_text: This classification of <s>karma</s> is indeed fourfold: black, white-and-black, white, and neither-white-nor-black. Among these, the black belongs to the wicked. The white-and-black is accomplished through external means; in that case, the accumulation of <s>karmāśaya</s> (karmic deposit) occurs only through the door of harming or helping others. The white belongs to those devoted to <s>tapas</s> (austerity), <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study), and <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation); for it depends solely on the mind and thus does not depend on external means, nor does it arise from causing harm to others. The neither-white-nor-black belongs to <s>saṁnyāsins</s> (renouncers) whose <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) are destroyed and who are in their final body. Of these, it is neither-white for the <s>yogī</s> alone, due to the renunciation of fruits, and neither-black due to the non-appropriation [of <s>karma</s>].

body.text:
vivaraṇam
kuta etayogina eva na karmāśayaḥ ? itareṣāṁ tvastīti । [yataḥ karmāśuklakṛṣṇaṁ yoginastrividhamitareṣām ।] siddhāsiddhasāmānyāviṣayamidaṁ sūtram ॥
nanu ca pūrvasūtrarmāpa sāmānyaviṣayameva । na । samādhisiddhistulyarthatvāt । sāmānyaviṣayatve tu samādhisiddhistutiranupapannā syāt । siddhiparisaṁkhyānena tu viśeṣaviṣayatve, tulyajātīyajanmādisiddhicatuṣṭayasāvadyatvasaṁkīrtanāt samādhisiddheḥ stutirupapadyate ॥
kiṁ ca, janmādisiddhisādhanānāṁ kaivalyārthatāpratiṣedhaścārthāditi viśiṣṭaviṣayameva pūrvasūtram । idaṁ tu sāmānyaviṣayameva pūrvasūtrahetutvenopādānāt ॥
[catuṣpadī khalviyaṁ karmajātiḥ । kṛṣṇā durātmanāṁ] śāstramārgatirvārtaduṣṭacetasāmaśuddhatarā । yā tu [bahissādhanasādhyā] jāyāputrapaśuyājakādiniṣpādyā sā śuklakṛṣṇā । ko'sau ? [yatra [para]pīḍā'nugrahadvāreṇa karmāśayapracayaḥ,] sā kleśabāhulakaniṣpādanīyatvāt kṛṣṇā ca śuklā ca ॥
nanu jyotiṣṭemādikarmaśāstrasamadhigatatvānna kṛṣṇaṁ, śuklameva tu tat । atrocyate – na - kāgyairanaikāntikatvāt । tānyeva cārthānarthobhayakāraṇāni । atha tatphalasya svargīderābhimatatvādarthatvameveti cenna - paradārābhimarśanasyāpi vāñchitatvādarthetvaprasaṅgāt ॥
atha paradārābhisaraṇādāvabhyugradoṣasampātāt, pratiṣiddhatvāśca rāgādiniyogapravṛteśvāsamānamiti cenna - tatrāpi samānatvāt । kāmātmatāniṣedhādaniṣṭayogaśca । janmamaraṇayorabhyugradoṣabhūtayoravaśyaṁbhāvitvādiṣṭāniṣṭadvayahetutvameva । sa cāniṣṭayogaḥ parapīḍāderityavasīyate । tatpratiṣedhopapatteḥ ॥
avaśyaṁ hi janmamaraṇadvayena vinā svargādiphalamupabhoktuṁ na śakyam । taścedasti tasya duḥkharūpavādāyātaṁ tarhi jyotiṣṭomādīnāmubhayātmakatvam । atha karmāntaromeva pratiṣiddhaṁ janmamaraṇārambhakāraṇamiti cenna - tadbhāvabhāvitvāt । tasmin hi sati janmamaraṇabhāvāt ॥
atha tu bhavatpakṣe nityameva kurvīta, na janmamaraṇe pravarteyātām । kurvata eva te bhavato nākurvataḥ । tasmānnimittatvamavagamyate । kiṁ ca - yena janmamaraṇamārapsyate tvargādau tat karma yadi janmāntaragataṁ, tatrānirmokṣaprasaṅgaḥ । kāmyapratiṣiddhākriyāyāmapi pūrvajanmakṛtaphalasyāvaśyaprāparṇīyatvāt ॥
atha prāktanajanmakarmakṣayārthāni nityānīti cet – tanna - niyamānupapateḥ । aniṣṭaphalānyevārabdhakāryāṇi pūrvakarmāṇi, na tviṣṭaphalānīti [ni]-niyantuṁ śakyate । adṛṣṭaphaleṣu hi satsu nityānyeva kurvato'pi mokṣānupapattirjanmārambhitvaṁ ca ॥
tata iṣṭānāmapyubhayahetutvaṁ siddham । bāhyasādhanānāṁ karmaṇāṁ pīḍānugraharūpatvāt । na vai khalvapi nityena pūrvakṛtakarmaṇāmiṣṭānāṁ jyetiṣṭomādīnāṁ nivṛttirupakalpate । virodhābhāvāt । avirodhaścobhayeṣāṁ śuddhirūpatvāt । tantrasiddheśca ॥
athāpi brūyāde[dane]kajanmārabdhāni karmaṇi janmai(kai)kamārabhante, nānārabdhakāryamavaśiṣyata iti । tathā'pi pūrvajanmakarmaṇa idānīntanajanmaphaladānena kṣayaṅgatatvādadhunātanajanmaniṣpāditānāmabhinavānāmeva kāmyānāṁ svargaphalajanmamaraṇaduḥkhārambhitvāmiti śuklakṛṣṇarūpāpattiḥ ॥
tataśca janmamaraṇaduḥkhasya svargābhidhānāyāḥ prīteśca darśanāt tatkāraṇasya dvirūpatvamanumāsyāmahe । tathā ca siddhe pratiṣiddhabhūtahiṁsācaraṇaṁ kratvarthamapyagrīṣemīyādau pravartamānaṁ kṛṣṇarūpāmityanumāsyāmahe । kravarthapi satī hiṁsā aniṣṭabhūtaiva tadarthatāṁ pratipadyate ॥
yaduktam - aviśeṣeṇa yacchāstraṁ śirovadita cottarīmita, tatra śirevadityevaṁjātīyakadṛṣṭantāsiddhatvam । aviśeṣeṇa yacchāstramiti tu homasvarūpasya virodhādvādhyabādhakatvamupapadyate । hiṁsāyāstu virodhābhāvādubhayorhetutvaṁ bhojanasyeva sukhaśarīrasthitidvayahetutvam । yathā ca tīrthasnānasya hlādādṛṣṭārthatvaṁ tathā hiṁsā'pyaniṣṭaphalatvamaparityajantī mahāphalaṁ kratuṁ naiva nābhinirvartayati ॥
atha bāhyasādhanasādhyamapi nilyaṁ kevalaṁ kāmasaṁyogābhāvācchuknumeveti cedevamucyate – na - doṣavatvena nityakāmyānāmaviśeṣāt । yathā kāminaḥ kāmyānīti kāmasaṁyogena kāmyānāṁ doṣavatvamevaṁ kāmādihetubhūtavidyādoṣavatvamaviśiṣṭamiti nityānāmapyubhayātmakatvameva । avidyāvatvaṁ ca nityeṣu pravṛttasya prāyaścittanimittotpateravaśyaṁbhāvitvāt ॥
api cāviduṣa eva sarvaṁ karma । viduṣaḥ karmānutpatteḥ । vidvān hi puruṣaḥ svarūpāvasthānavyatirekeṇa phalaṁ nābhimanyate । svarūpamātrāvasthānaṁ ca samastavyāpāravirāmeṇa pravartate । na caivaṁ viduṣaḥ kriyā'nuṣṭhānaṁ ghaṭate । na hi sthalapathenābhipratiṣṭhāsamāno jalamārgābhiprasthānasādhanaṁ nāvādikamanutiṣṭhati ॥
nanu (na ca) nityakāmyayerevaṁ satyaviśeṣaḥ syāt । atrocyate -kāmitaphala(tanmātraṁ ni)karmamātranivṛtiprayojanatvānityānāmadoṣaḥ । yo hi kāmyādvinivṛttastasya bahulaṁ karmaṇāṁ kāmarahitena śuddhena kartrā kṛtatvādatiśuddhaphalatvaṁ śuklatvabahutvāñca saṁskārārthatvam । api ca kāmanivṛttireva mahat phalam ॥
kiṁ ca, nityaṁ kurvataḥ kimarthaṁ karomi, kiṁ vā'sya phalaṁ, ke vāsyānuṣṭhāne doṣāḥ, iti samyamdarśanarūpaḥ parāmarśo jāyata iti nityasyāsti viśeṣaḥ । śuklakṛṣṇātmakatvaṁ tvaviśiṣṭamubhayeṣāmapi karmaṇām । bāhyasādhanasādhanīyatvena parapīḍopapatteḥ । [iti] tasmāducyate ॥
[śuklā] karmajātiḥ [tapassvādhyāyadhyānavatām । sā hi kevale manasyāyattatvādabahissādhanā] bāhyasādhānānapekṣā [na parān pīḍayitvā bhavati ॥]
[aśuklakṛṣṇā saṁnyāsināṁ kṣīṇakleśānāṁ caramadehānām ।] eṣām ārabdhaikaśarīrāṇām । [aśuklā sanyāsāt akṛṣṇā ca anupādānāt] akaraṇāt । nāpi śuklakṛṣṇavimiśrā, bāhyasenyāsānupādānābhyāṁ hetubhyām । tathā coktam –
aniṣṭābhiṣṭaṁ miśraṁ ca trividhaṁ karmaṇaḥ phalam ॥
bhavatya[tyatyagināṁ]yogināṁ pretya na tu saṁnyāsināṁ kaścittū ॥ iti ॥
[itareṣāṁ tu bhūtānāṁ] janmauṣadhimantratapassiddhānāmanyeṣāṁ ca [trividhaṁ] śuklaṁ kṛṣṇaṁ miśraṁ ca [pūrvamiva] yathā dvitīye pāde ['kleśamūlaḥ’] ityādau [॥ 7 ॥]
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
Why is it that for the yogin alone there is no karmic deposit (karmāśaya), while for others there is? ['Because karma is neither white nor black for the yogin, and threefold for others.'] This sūtra applies commonly to both the accomplished and the unaccomplished.
But was not the previous sūtra also of general application? No — because the accomplishment through samādhi would be of equal status [with other means]. If it were of general application, the praise of the accomplishment through samādhi would be unjustified. But when there is a specific application through the enumeration of accomplishments, the praise of samādhi-accomplishment is justified, because the four similar accomplishments arising from birth and the rest are declared to be defective.
Moreover, the negation of the purpose-of-kaivalya for the means of accomplishments such as birth and the rest is implied — thus the previous sūtra had a specific application. This sūtra, however, has general application, being adduced as the reason for the previous sūtra.
['This class of karma is indeed fourfold. Black is that of the wicked'] — of those whose minds are corrupted by transgressing the path of scripture, the most impure. ['That which is accomplished through external means'] — accomplished through wife, sons, animals, sacrificial priests, and the like — that is white-and-black. What is that? ['Where there is accumulation of karmic deposit through the channel of causing pain and benefit to others'] — that is both black and white, because it must be accomplished through an abundance of afflictions.
But objection: since rites like the Jyotiṣṭoma are prescribed by scripture, they are not black but purely white. The answer: No — because the bodily acts involved are inconclusive. Those very acts are causes of both benefit and harm. If one argues that because the fruit — heaven and such — is desirable, it is therefore beneficial: No — for then even approaching another's wife, being desired, would absurdly have to be considered beneficial.
If one argues that approaching another's wife involves manifestly grave faults and is prohibited, while acts impelled by desire and such in prescribed rites are different: No — because even there it is the same. Because desire-nature is prohibited, and there is conjunction with the undesirable. Since birth and death — which are manifestly grave faults — are inevitable, they are causes of both the desired and the undesired. And that conjunction with the undesirable is determined to arise from causing pain to others and the like. Because the prohibition of that is justified.
For indeed, without the pair of birth and death, the fruit of heaven and such cannot be enjoyed. And if these exist and are admitted to be of the nature of suffering, then the Jyotiṣṭoma and such have a dual nature. If one argues that some other karma, which is prohibited, is the cause of birth and death: No — because [birth and death] occur due to the existence of that [prescribed karma]. For when that exists, birth and death occur.
But in your view, one who constantly performs [the rites] should never undergo birth and death. They occur for one who performs, not for one who does not. Therefore, their causal relation is established. Moreover —

body.text: tatastadvipākānuguṇānāmevābhivyaktirvāsanānām ॥ 8 ॥
body.translated_text: From that, only those <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions) that correspond to the fruition of that [karma] manifest. || 8 ||

body.text: tata iti trividhātkarmaṇaḥ, tadvipākānuguṇānāmeveti yajjātīyasya karmaṇo yo vipākastasyānuguṇā yā vāsanāḥ karmavipākamanuśerate tāsāmevābhivyaktiḥ। na hi daivaṁ karma vipacyamānaṁ nārakatiryaṅmanuṣyavāsanābhivyaktinimittaṁ saṁbhavati। kiṁtu daivānuguṇā evāsya vāsanā vyajyante। nārakatiryaṅmanuṣyeṣu caivaṁ samānaścarcaḥ ॥ 8 ॥
body.translated_text: 'From that' means from the threefold karma. 'Only those that correspond to the fruition of that' means: whatever class of karma has a certain fruition, the <s>vāsanās</s> that correspond to it — that follow the fruition of that karma — only those manifest. For a divine karma that is ripening cannot possibly be the cause of the manifestation of hellish, animal, or human <s>vāsanās</s>. Rather, only <s>vāsanās</s> corresponding to the divine manifest for that [being]. The same discussion applies equally to the hellish, animal, and human [destinies]. || 8 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
kaivalyasya prastutatvāt tasya ca pratibandhahetayaḥ kleśāḥ, karmāṇi, vāsānāśca, [vyākhyātavyāḥ] । kleśānāṁ tu vyāpāraḥ, pratipakṣaḥ, nivṛttiśca teṣāṁ, vistareṇa vyākhyātāḥ । evaṁ karmaṇāmapi vāsanānāṁ tulyavyāpārāvasthānapratipakṣanivṛttayo nirvarṇanīyā ityata uttarāṇi sūtrāṇyārabhyante-yatastānnivṛttau kaivalyamupapadyate nānyathā । [tatastadvipākānuguṇānāmevābhivyatirvāsanānām ॥]
tataḥ tasmāt [trividhāt] uktalakṣaṇāt kṛṣṇaśuklavimiśrarūpāt [karmaṇaḥ] pravipacyamānāddhetubhūtāt [tadvipākānuguṇānāṁ tasyaiva] karmaṇo [vipākaḥ] phalaṁ [tadanuguṇānāṁ] tadanurūpāṇāṁ tādṛśīnām [eva vāsanānāmabhivyaktiḥ ॥]
etaduktaṁ bhavati - devatiryaṅmanuṣyāvipākahetuṣu karmasu madhye [yajjātīyasya karmaṇo yādṛśo vipākaḥ tasya] vipākasya [anuguṇā vāsanāḥ] tat [karmavipākamanuśarete] anutpadyante, [tāsāmevābhivyaktiḥ ।] tatsadṛśena karmavipākena saṁskṛtatvāt । yathā mātṛsadṛśī pravilokya vatso'nudhāvati । nānyāsāmatadanuguṇānāmabhivyaktiḥ ॥
[na hi daivaṁ karma vipacyamānaṁ] phalābhimukhībhāvamāpadyamānaṁ [nārakatiryeṅmanunuṣavāsanābhivyaktinimittaṁ[saṁ]bhavati ।] nimittanaimittikayoḥ pratiniyatānuguṇatvāt । [kiṁ tu daivānuguṇā evāsyābhivyajyante । nārakatiryaṅmānuṣeṣvevaṁ samānaścarcaḥ] samādhiḥ ॥
nārake karmaṇi vipaśyamāne tatkarmānuguṇā vāsanāḥ prādurbhavanti । tathā tairyagyonakarmaṇi vipacyamāne tadvipākānurūpā vāsanā vyajyante । tathā mānuṣe'pi samāno nyāyaḥ । na hi svavipākasadṛśīranupādāya vāsanāstasya tasya karmaṇe vipākaḥ saṁbhavati । nāpi vāsanānāmātmaniṣpādakavipākārābhikarmatulyarūpāṇi karmāntarāṇi vipākābhimukhānyantareṇābhivyaktiḥ । evaṁ karmaṇāṁ vāsanānāṁ ca parasparahetuhetumadbhāvo'nādibhūtaḥ ॥ 8 ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
Since kaivalya is the subject under discussion, and the obstacles to it are kleśas (afflictions), karmas (actions), and vāsanās (latent impressions), [these] are to be explained. The functioning of the kleśas, their antidote, and their cessation have been explained in detail. Likewise, the functioning, subsistence, antidote, and cessation of karmas and vāsanās are to be examined — therefore the following sūtras are commenced, because kaivalya is attained when these cease, and not otherwise. ['From that, only those vāsanās that correspond to the fruition of that karma manifest.']
'From that' — from that ['threefold'] karma having the described characteristics of black, white, and mixed, ['from karma'] that is ripening and serving as a cause, ['only those vāsanās corresponding to the fruition of that'] very ['karma, the fruition'] being the fruit, ['corresponding to that'] — resembling it, of such a kind — ['only those vāsanās manifest.']
What is being said is this: among the karmas that serve as causes for the fruitions of divine, animal, and human [births], ['whatever class of karma has whatever kind of fruition, the vāsanās that correspond to'] that fruition — ['that follow the fruition of that karma'] — arise accordingly. ['Only those manifest.'] Because they have been conditioned by a similar karmic fruition. Just as a calf, seeing one who resembles its mother, runs after it. The vāsanās that do not correspond to that are not manifested.
['For a divine karma that is ripening'] — approaching the state of bearing fruit — ['cannot possibly be the cause of the manifestation of hellish, animal, or human vāsanās.'] Because of the fixed correspondence between cause and effect. ['Rather, only those corresponding to the divine manifest. The same discussion applies equally to the hellish, animal, and human destinies'] — the same reasoning.

body.text: jātideśakālavyavahitānāmapyānantaryaṁ smṛtisaṁskārayorekarūpatvāt ॥ 9 ॥
body.translated_text: Even for those [<s>vāsanās</s>] separated by birth, place, and time, there is uninterrupted continuity, because memory (<s>smṛti</s>) and latent impressions (<s>saṁskāra</s>) are of one form. || 9 ||

body.text: vṛṣadaṁśavipākodayaḥ svavyañjakāñjanābhivyaktaḥ। sa yadi jātiśatena vā dūradeśatayā vā kalpaśatena vā vyavahitaḥ punaśca svavyañjakāñjana evodiyāddrāgityevaṁ pūrvānubhūtavṛṣadaṁśavipākābhisaṁskṛtā vāsanā upādāya vyajyeta। kasmāt। yato vyavahitānāmapyāsāṁ sadṛśaṁ karmābhivyañjakaṁ nimittībhūtamityānantaryameva। kutaśca, smṛtisaṁskārayorekarūpatvāt। yathā'nubhavāstathā saṁskārāḥ। te ca karmavāsanānurūpāḥ। yathā ca vāsanāstathā smṛtiriti jātideśakālavyavahitebhyaḥ saṁskārebhyaḥ smṛtiḥ। smṛteśca punaḥ saṁskārā ityevamete smṛtisaṁskārāḥ karmāśayavṛttilābhavaśādvyajyante। ataśca vyavahitānāmapi nimittanaimittikabhāvānucchedādānantaryameva siddhamiti ॥ 9 ॥
body.translated_text: The fruition-arising of a bull-fly [bite experience]: it is manifested by its own revealing cause. If it is separated by a hundred births, or by great distance of place, or by a hundred kalpas, and if its own revealing cause again arises, then swiftly the vāsanā conditioned by the previously experienced bull-fly fruition would be manifested. Why? Because even for those separated [by birth, place, and time], the similar karma that is their revealing cause has become the occasion — hence there is indeed uninterrupted continuity. And why else? Because memory and latent impressions are of one form. As the experiences are, so are the impressions (saṁskāras). And these correspond to the karmic vāsanās. And as the vāsanās are, so is the memory — thus from impressions separated by birth, place, and time, memory [arises]. And from memory, again impressions — thus these memories and impressions are manifested through the operation of the karmic deposit. Therefore, even for those separated [in time and space], since the causal relation between cause and effect is unbroken, uninterrupted continuity is indeed established. || 9 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
tatra vāsanānāmanekajātikāladeśavyavadhānena davīyasīnāmānantaryaṁ vipacyamānena karmaṇā saha nāsti । yathā davīyasāṁ mitrasvajanādīnām । yathaiva · ca nedīyasī vāsanā paṭīyasī, na tathā davīyasī paṭīyamānamāsīdati । tasmānnāsti davīyasīnāmānantaryaṁ vāsanānām ॥
tadabhāve cāyaṁ doṣaḥ prāpnoti – yathā kalpaśatāntaritaḥ vṛṣadaṁśavipākaḥ bhaviṣyataḥ vṛṣadaṁśavipākasvānantarātīto daivavipākaḥ । tatra nedīyasī daivavāsanā viruddhatvāt vṛṣadaṁśavipākābhivyaktihetutāṁ na pratipadyate । kalpaśatavyavahitānāmapi vṛṣadaṁśavāsanānāṁ viprakarṣādanupādāne vṛṣadaṁśavipākahetoḥ karmaṇo vipāko nāvakalpeta । tataśca karmaṇāṁ vāsanānāṁ cānarthakyaṁ prasajyateti ॥
atrocyate – [jātideśakālavyavahitānāmapyānantaryaṁ smṛtisaṁskārayorekarūpatvāt । vṛṣadaṁśavipākādayaḥ svakarmavyañjakāñjanāḥ] vyañjakena svena karmaṇā vyajyamānāḥ [yadi jātiśatena vā dūradeśatayā vā kalpasahasreṇa vā] vyavahitāḥ ॥
tathā coktam [“grāhyoparaktaḥ pratyayo grāhyagrahaṇobhayākāranirbhāsaḥ”] ityādi । [jātideśakālavyavahitebhyaḥ saṁskārebhyaḥ smṛtayaḥ । smṛtibhyaśca punaḥ saṁskārā ityevamete smṛtisaṁskārāḥ karmāśayavṛttilābhavaśāveśādabhivyajyante ।] karmāśayasyāpi vṛttilābho deśādinimittāpekṣayeti pratipāditam ॥
[ataśca vyavahitānāmapi nimittanaimittikabhāvānucchedādānantaryameva ।] yādṛśaḥ saṁskārastādṛśī, smṛtiḥ । pratiniyatavyañjakatvācca tayorna viprakarṣaḥ kāraṇam । yataḥ kalpaśatavyavahitādapi saṁskārādeva tulyajātīyā smṛtiriti, [ānantaryameva siddham ॥ 9 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s>:
In this regard, <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions) that are remote — separated by many births, times, and places — do not have immediate succession with the <s>karma</s> that is ripening. Just as with distant friends and relatives. And just as a proximate <s>vāsanā</s> is more potent, so a remote one does not attain such potency. Therefore there is no immediate succession of remote <s>vāsanās</s>.
In the absence of that [succession], this defect would follow: suppose a bull-fly <s>vipāka</s> (fruition) is separated by a hundred <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), and a divine <s>vipāka</s> has passed immediately before the future bull-fly fruition. There, the proximate divine <s>vāsanā</s>, being of contrary nature, does not serve as the cause for the manifestation of the bull-fly fruition. And if the bull-fly <s>vāsanās</s>, separated by a hundred <s>kalpas</s>, are not taken up due to their remoteness, then the fruition of the <s>karma</s> that is the cause of the bull-fly result would not be possible. Consequently, the purposelessness of both <s>karmas</s> and <s>vāsanās</s> would follow.
To this it is said: [Even for those separated by birth, place, and time, there is immediate succession, because memory and <s>saṁskāra</s> (mental impression) are of one form. The bull-fly fruitions and so forth] are manifested by their own <s>karma</s> which serves as the revealer — [whether] separated [by a hundred births, or by great distance of place, or by a thousand <s>kalpas</s>].
And thus it has been stated: ["The cognition colored by the object appears in the form of both the grasped and the grasper"] and so forth. [From <s>saṁskāras</s> separated by birth, place, and time arise memories. And from memories again arise <s>saṁskāras</s> — thus these memories and <s>saṁskāras</s> are manifested through the <s>karmāśaya</s> (repository of actions) gaining activity.] It has been established that the <s>karmāśaya</s> too gains activity depending on conditions such as place and so forth.
[Therefore, even for those that are separated, because the relation of cause and effect is not severed, there is indeed immediate succession.] The memory is of the same kind as the <s>saṁskāra</s>. And because each has its own specific revealer, remoteness is not a [hindering] cause for them. Since even from a <s>saṁskāra</s> separated by a hundred <s>kalpas</s>, a memory of the same class arises, [immediate succession is indeed established. || 9 ||]

body.text: tāsāmanāditvaṁ cā''śiṣo nityatvāt ॥ 10 ॥
body.translated_text: And the beginninglessness of these [<s>vāsanās</s>] is due to the eternality of the will to live (<s>āśis</s>). || 10 ||

body.text: tāsāṁ vāsanānāmāśiṣo nityatvādanāditvam। yeyamātmāśīrmā na bhūvaṁ bhūyāsamiti sarvasya dṛśyate sā na svābhāvikī। kasmāt। jātamātrasya jantorananubhūtamaraṇadharmakasya dveṣaduḥkhānusmṛtinimitto maraṇatrāsaḥ kathaṁ bhavet। na ca svābhāvikaṁ vastu nimittamupādatte। tasmādanādivāsanānuviddhamidaṁ cittaṁ nimittavaśātkāścideva vāsanāḥ pratilabhya puruṣasya bhogāyopāvartata iti।
body.translated_text: The beginninglessness of those <s>vāsanās</s> is due to the eternality of the will to live (<s>āśis</s>). This self-directed wish that is seen in everyone — "May I not cease to be, may I continue to exist" — is not innate. Why? How could the terror of death, which is caused by the recollection of aversion and suffering, arise in a being just born, who has not experienced the nature of death? And an innate thing does not depend on a cause. Therefore, this <s>citta</s> (mind), pervaded by beginningless <s>vāsanās</s>, obtains certain <s>vāsanās</s> through the force of conditions and turns toward providing experience (<s>bhoga</s>) for <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Self).

body.text:
vivaraṇam
idānīṁ vāsanānāmanāditvena vipākanirvartakatvamamidarśayati – saṁskārasya cānāditvomakaikasya cāsaṁṅkhyayayonigamanaṁ vairāgyapratipattyarthaṁ pratipādayati – [tāsāmanāditvaṁ cā''śiṣo nityatvāt । tāsāṁ vāsanānāmāśiṣo nityatvādanāditvam । yeyamātmāśīḥ ‘maraṇaṁ mā nu bhūt’] iti, evamāśīrvā [‘bhūyāsam' iti sarvasya dṛśyate । sa na svābhāvikī] svarasapravṛttā'pi nirūḍhā'pi ॥
[kasmāt? jātamātrasya ananubhūtajananamaraṇadharmakasya dveṣānusmṛtinimitto duḥkhānusmṛtihetuko vā maraṇatrāsaḥ kathaṁ bhavet ?] na hi kathañcana du:khasmaraṇādinimittopādāna svābhāvikasyopapadyate । [na ca svābhāvikaṁ vastu nimittamupādatte ।] na hi jvalanasyoṣṇatvaṁ svābhāvikaṁ sadātmīyakārye nimittamīkṣeta ॥
na cānanubhūte viṣaye smṛtiriṣṭe'niṣṭe vā kasyacidupaploṣyate । anubhūtapriyānanusmaraṇe, na ca tadviṣayavāñchā । tathā anubhūtāpriyānanusmaraṇe, na tadviṣayo dveṣastrāsaśca loke paridṛśyate । tathā ca yo yo jātastasya tasyeha janmanyananubhūtajanmamaraṇasya janmānantaramevātmāśīrabhidṛśyate । tasmāt tadāśīrnityatvāt pūrvajanmamaraṇānubhavo'numīyate । tataḥ pūrvastato'pi pūrva iti, smṛtisaṁskārāṇāṁ tatkāraṇānāṁ ca janmamaraṇānubhavānāmanāditvamanumimīmahe ॥
tathaiva ekaikasya prāṇabhṛto'nekayonigamanāsāddhiḥ । evametā vāsanā duravahanā avihānīyāḥ । kuta evam ? [yasmādanādivāsanānuviddhaṁ cittamidaṁ nimittavaśāt] karmanimittavaśāt [kāścideva vāsanāḥ] pravipacyamānakarmatulyajātīyakriyāvipākābhi(nna)niṣpāditāḥ [pratilabhya puruṣasya bhogāyopāvartate] yāvadavasitādhikāramiti ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s>:
Now he demonstrates that through their beginninglessness, <s>vāsanās</s> have the capacity to bring about fruition — and he teaches the beginninglessness of each <s>saṁskāra</s> and the passage through innumerable wombs of each [being], for the purpose of establishing <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion): [The beginninglessness of these is due to the eternality of the will to live. The beginninglessness of those <s>vāsanās</s> is due to the eternality of <s>āśis</s>. This self-directed wish, "May death not come"] — such a wish, or ["May I continue to exist," is seen in everyone. It is not innate] — even though it arises spontaneously, even though it is deeply rooted.
[Why? How could the terror of death — caused by the recollection of aversion, or caused by the recollection of suffering — arise in one just born, who has not experienced the nature of birth and death?] For in no way is it possible for something innate to depend on a cause such as the memory of suffering. [And an innate thing does not depend on a cause.] For the heat of fire, being innate, does not look for a cause in producing its own effect.
Nor does memory of an unexperienced object — whether pleasant or unpleasant — arise for anyone. Without remembering a previously experienced pleasure, there is no desire for that object. Likewise, without remembering a previously experienced pain, no aversion or terror regarding that object is observed in the world. And thus, for every being that is born, though birth and death have not been experienced in this life, the will to live is seen immediately after birth. Therefore, from the eternality of that wish, experience of death in a previous birth is inferred. From that [birth], an even earlier one — thus we infer the beginninglessness of memories, <s>saṁskāras</s>, their causes, and the experiences of birth and death.
Likewise, the passage of each single living being through innumerable wombs is established. Thus these <s>vāsanās</s> are unbearable and indestructible. Why so? [Because this <s>citta</s>, pervaded by beginningless <s>vāsanās</s>, through the force of conditions] — through the force of <s>karmic</s> conditions — [obtaining certain <s>vāsanās</s>] produced as fruitions of actions of the same class as the <s>karma</s> now ripening, [turns toward providing experience for <s>Puruṣa</s>] until its task is completed.

body.text: ghaṭaprāsādapradīpakalpaṁ saṁkocavikāsi cittaṁ śarīraparimāṇākāramātramityapare pratipannāḥ। tathā cāntarābhāvaḥ saṁsāraśca yukta iti। vṛttirevāsya vibhunaścittasya saṁkocavikāsinītyācāryaḥ।
body.translated_text: Others have maintained that the <s>citta</s> (mind) contracts and expands like a pot, a palace, or a lamp, and is merely of the size and shape of the body. And thus, they say, the intermediate state (<s>antarābhāva</s>) and <s>saṁsāra</s> (transmigration) are logically accounted for. But the <s>Ācārya</s> (Teacher) holds that it is only the <s>vṛtti</s> (modification) of the all-pervading <s>citta</s> that contracts and expands.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
tadeta [ccittaṁ ghaṭaprāsādapradīpakalpaṁ saṁkocavikāsi] hastimaśakādi [śarīraparimāṇākaraṁ] yathā dīpo ghaṭaprāsādādiṣu । tadevam [apare pratipannāḥ ।] tatra ca yuktimāha- [tathā ceti । tathā ca] saṁkocavikasitve ca [antarābhāvaḥ] maraṇāduttarakālaṁ janmanaśca prāgetasmin antarāle bhavatītyantarābhāvaḥ [saṁsaraṇaṁ] sañcaraṇaṁ yena sañcarati tadapi śarīramātivāhikaṁ cittasyāvibhutve [yuktamiti] bruvanti । [vṛttirevāsya vibhunaścittasya saṅgocavikāsinītyācāryāḥ ।] ācāryagrahaṇam upapattimatvāt pūjārtham । cittasya sthitirgataśca pariṇāmitvādvibhutve'pīndriyāṇāṁ copapadyate yogināṁ ca vikaraṇabhāvaḥ sarvajñatvaṁ vibhutve ghaṭate ॥
na copabhogaśūnyasyātivāhikaśarīrasya kalpanāyāmasti pramāṇam । śaśaviṣāṇavadanupalabhyamānatvāt ॥ “na ha vai saśarīrasya sataḥ priyāpriyayorapahatirasti” iti śruteḥ । tathā “atha yo haitānanantānupāste ” iti śrutiḥ karaṇavyāpitvaṁ khyāpayati ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s>:
This [<s>citta</s> is said to be] like a pot, a palace, or a lamp — [contracting and expanding] like an elephant or a mosquito and so forth — [of the size and shape of the body,] just as a lamp [adapts to] a pot or a palace. Thus [others have maintained.] And regarding that, he states the reasoning: ["And thus" — and thus,] given contraction and expansion, [the intermediate state] — that which exists in the interval after death and before the next birth is the <s>antarābhāva</s> (intermediate existence) — [and transmigration,] the journeying by which one transmigrates, that too requires an <s>ātivāhika</s> (subtle transmigrating) body; [they say this is] logical [if] the <s>citta</s> is not all-pervading. [But the <s>Ācāryas</s> (Teachers) hold that it is only the <s>vṛtti</s> of the all-pervading <s>citta</s> that contracts and expands.] The use of the word <s>Ācārya</s> is out of reverence, because this view is supported by reasoning. The abiding and movement of <s>citta</s>, even when all-pervading, is possible due to its transformative nature, and the functioning of the sense organs is also accounted for; and for <s>yogins</s>, the state of operating without instruments (<s>vikaraṇa-bhāva</s>) and omniscience (<s>sarvajñatva</s>) are compatible with all-pervasiveness.
Moreover, there is no valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) for postulating a subtle transmigrating body devoid of experience — because it is unperceived, like the horn of a hare. As the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) says: "For one who is embodied, there is no escape from pleasure and pain." And the <s>śruti</s> "Now, he who meditates on these infinite [qualities]" proclaims the pervasion of the instruments [of cognition].

body.text: tacca dharmādinimittāpekṣam। nimittaṁ ca dvividham – bāhyamādhyātmikaṁ ca। śarīrādisādhanāpekṣaṁ bāhyaṁ stutidānābhivādanādi, cittamātrādhīnaṁ śraddhādyādhyātmikam। tathā coktam – ye caite maitryādayo dhyāyināṁ vihārāste bāhyasādhananiranugrahātmānaḥ prakṛṣṭaṁ dharmamabhinirvartayanti। tayormānasaṁ balīyaḥ। kathaṁ, jñānavairāgye kenātiśayyete, daṇḍakāraṇyaṁ ca cittabalavyatirekeṇa śārīreṇa karmaṇā śūnyaṁ kaḥ kartumutsaheta samudramagastyavadvā pibet ॥ 10 ॥
body.translated_text: And that [expansion and contraction of <s>vṛtti</s>] depends on conditions such as <s>dharma</s> (merit) and the like. The conditions are of two kinds: external and internal. The external, which depends on instruments such as the body, includes praise, gifts, salutations, and so forth. The internal depends solely on the mind, such as faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) and the like. And thus it has been said: Those states of abiding of meditators such as <s>maitrī</s> (friendliness) and others, being independent of external instruments, produce supreme <s>dharma</s>. Of the two, the mental is more powerful. How so? By what can knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) and dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) be surpassed? And who, without the power of mind, could render the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest empty through mere bodily action, or drink the ocean like <s>Agastya</s>? || 10 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
tacca saṁkocavikāsitvaṁ vṛtteḥ dharmādinimittāpekṣam । [nimittaṁ] ca dvidhā [bāhyamādhyātmikaṁ ca । śarīrādisādhanāpekṣaṁ bāhyaṁ stutyabhivādanādi] karma । kiṁ punarādhyātmikam? āha - [kevalacittamātrādhīnaṁ śraddhādi ॥]
[tathā coktam - ye caite maitryādayo dhyāyināṁ vihārā: cittavyāpārāḥ] ceṣṭitāni [te bāhyasādhananiranugrahāḥ] bāhyasādhananirapekṣāḥ kevalacittamātranirvṛttāḥ [prakṛṣṭaṁ dharmamābhinirvartayanti ॥]
[tayoḥ] bāhyādhyātmikayornimittayoḥ [mānasam] ādhyātmikaṁ maitryādicittābhiniṣpannaṁ nimittaṁ [balīyaḥ । katham] iti? [jñānavairāgye kenātiśayyete ?] na kenāpītyarthaḥ । yatastṛtīyapādānukrāntāvibhūtajātaṁ jñānavairāgyasādhyam । [daṇḍakāraṇyaṁ cittabalavyatirekeṇa kaḥ kartuṁ śaknoti । kaśca pibet samudramagastyavat] iti । ato mānasabalameva balam । na śārīram । [“tasmāt mānasaṁ paramaṁ vadanti”] iti śruteḥ । tathā ca bhagavānābabhāṣe-
[“śreyān dravyamayādyajñājjñānayajñaḥ parantapa । “]
[“sarvaṁ karmākhilaṁ pārtha jñāne parisamāpyate“] iti ॥ 10 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s>:
And that contraction and expansion of <s>vṛtti</s> depends on conditions such as <s>dharma</s> and the like. [The conditions] are of two kinds: [external and internal. The external, depending on instruments such as the body, includes] actions such as [praise, salutations] and the like. What then is the internal? He says: [That which depends solely on the mind alone, such as <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) and the like.]
[And thus it has been said: Those states of abiding of meditators such as <s>maitrī</s> (friendliness) and others — mental activities,] exertions — [being independent of external instruments,] not requiring external instruments, accomplished by the mind alone, [produce supreme <s>dharma</s>.]
[Of the two] — external and internal conditions — [the mental] internal condition, accomplished through mental states such as <s>maitrī</s> and others, [is more powerful. How so?] [By what can knowledge and dispassion be surpassed?] By nothing — that is the meaning. Since the entire range of <s>vibhūtis</s> (supernatural powers) described in the third <s>pāda</s> (chapter) is attainable through knowledge and dispassion. [Who, without the power of mind, could render the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest [desolate]? And who could drink the ocean like <s>Agastya</s>?] Therefore, mental strength alone is true strength, not physical. As the <s>śruti</s> says: ["Therefore they declare the mental to be supreme."]
And the Blessed Lord has declared:
["The sacrifice of knowledge is superior to the sacrifice of material offerings, O <s>Parantapa</s> (Scorcher of Foes)."]
["All action in its entirety, O <s>Pārtha</s>, culminates in knowledge."] || 10 ||

body.text: hetuphalāśrayālambanaiḥ saṁgṛhītatvādeṣāmabhāve tadabhāvaḥ ॥ 11 ॥
body.translated_text: Because these [<s>vāsanās</s>] are held together by cause (<s>hetu</s>), fruit (<s>phala</s>), substratum (<s>āśraya</s>), and object (<s>ālambana</s>), in the absence of these, there is the absence of those [<s>vāsanās</s>]. || 11 ||

body.text: heturdharmātsukhamadharmādduḥkhaṁ, sukhādrāgo duḥkhāddveṣastataśca prayatnastena manasā vācā kāyena vā parispandamānaḥ paramanugṛhṇātyupahanti vā tataḥ punardharmādharmau sukhaduḥkhe rāgadveṣāviti pravṛttamidaṁ ṣaḍaraṁ saṁsāracakram। asya ca pratikṣaṇamāvartamānasyāvidyā netrī mūlaṁ sarvakleśānāmityeṣa hetuḥ। phalaṁ tu yamāśritya yasya pratyutpannatā dharmādeḥ, na hyapūrvopajanaḥ। manastu sādhikāramāśrayo vāsanānām। na hyavasitādhikāre manasi nirāśrayā vāsanāḥ sthātumutsahante। yadabhimukhībhūtaṁ vastu yāṁ vāsanāṁ vyanakti tasyāstadālambanam। evaṁ hetuphalāśrayālambanairetaiḥ saṁgṛhītāḥ sarvā vāsanāḥ। eṣāmabhāve tatsaṁśrayāṇāmapi vāsanānāmabhāvaḥ ॥ 11 ॥
body.translated_text: The cause (<s>hetu</s>): from <s>dharma</s> (merit) comes pleasure, from <s>adharma</s> (demerit) comes pain; from pleasure arises attachment (<s>rāga</s>), from pain arises aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>); from these comes effort (<s>prayatna</s>); through that effort, acting with mind, speech, or body, one either benefits or harms others; from that again arise <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, pleasure and pain, attachment and aversion — thus this six-spoked wheel of <s>saṁsāra</s> (cyclic existence) is set in motion. And <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is the driver of this [wheel] as it revolves at every moment — it is the root of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). This is the cause. The fruit (<s>phala</s>) is that upon which the present existence of <s>dharma</s> and the rest depends; for there is no origination from what is entirely new. The mind (<s>manas</s>), as long as it has a function to fulfill, is the substratum (<s>āśraya</s>) of <s>vāsanās</s>; for when the mind has completed its purpose, <s>vāsanās</s> without a substratum cannot persist. Whatever object, when encountered, manifests a particular <s>vāsanā</s> — that is its <s>ālambana</s> (supporting object). Thus, all <s>vāsanās</s> are held together by these — cause, fruit, substratum, and object. In the absence of these, there is the absence of the <s>vāsanās</s> dependent on them. || 11 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
kathaṁ punastāsāṁ vāsanānāṁ nivṛttiḥ । anādirūḍhatvāt na nivṛttirāsāṁ ghaṭāmāḍhaukate । na ca tannivṛttimantareṇa kaivalyopapattirityata ucyate - [hetuphalāśrayālambanaiḥ saṁgṛhītatvādeṣāmabhāve tadabhāvaḥ ।] hetuśca phalaṁ cāśrayaścālambanaṁ ca hetuphalāśrayālambanāni । taiḥ saṁgṛhītatvādupagrathitatvādeṣāṁ hetvādīnāmabhāve tadabhāve vāsanānāmabhāvaḥ । tasmādupapadyate vāsanānāṁ nivṛtiḥ ॥
ko'sau hetuḥ? ityāha-dharmastāvadavidyāvinamitacetasām । tato [dharmāt sukham । sukhānuśayī rāgaḥ ।] evamavidyāta eva niṣiddhācaraṇāt [adharmaḥ । tato du:kham । duḥkhānuśayī dveṣaḥ । tataḥ] sukhopārjane du:khaparihāre ca pūrvavedava [prayatnaḥ । tena] prayatnena [vācā kāyena parispandamānaḥ paramanugṛhṇātyupahanti ca । punaśca tataḥ] parānugrahaparapīḍanāmyāṁ [dharmādharmau ।] tābhyāṁ [sukhaduḥkhe ।] tābhyāṁ ca [rāgadveṣau] pūrvavadeva । tataḥ prayatnaḥ ॥
ityevamanavarataprārabdhaparibhramaṇaṁ [pravṛttamidaṁ ṣaḍaraṁ saṁsāracakram । asya ca pratikṣaṇamāvartamānasyāvidyā netrī] rathacakrasya turaṅgayuvatiriva ॥
[sā mūlaṁ sarvakleśānāmiti] yadetadavidyānetṛkaṁ ṣaḍaraṁ cakram eṣa [hetuḥ] vāsanānām । etaccakrāvṛttikṛtā hi tāḥ । avidyāyāstvabhāve viśīrṇanābhibandhanamiva cakraṁ, dharmādihetucakramapi viśīryate । tadviśaraṇe ca cakrāvṛttikṛtajanmanāṁ vāsanānāmakāryakṣamatvam ॥
[phalaṁ tu] yam artham āśritya [yasya pratyutpannatā] tat tasya phalam । tadapi vāsanānāṁ saṁgrāhakam । tadabhāve vāsanābhivyaktyabhāvāt । sukhādiphalasya vāsanādhāyitvāt । [na hyapūrvopajanaḥ ।] nātyantamasadutpadyate ॥
[manaḥ sādhikāraṁ] kartavyatāvat na puruṣārthaśūnyam । kṛtapuruṣārthasvarūpajñānaṁ vinivṛttāvidyākamiti [sādhikāramāśrayo vāsanānām ।] tadāśritya hi hetucakraparibhramaṇam । [na hyavasitādhikāre] karaṇīyapuruṣārthaśūnye [manasi nirāśrāyā vāsanāḥ sthātumutsahante ।]
[yadabhimukhībhūtaṁ vastu yāṁ vāsanāṁ vyanakti tasyāstadālambanam । evaṁ hetuphalāśrayālambanairetaiḥ saṁgṛhītāḥ sarvā vāsanāḥ । teṣāṁ] hetvādīnām [abhāve tatsaṁśrayāṇāmapi vāsanānāmabhāvaḥ] chatrābhāve chāyānivṛttivat ॥
eṣāṁ cābhāvopāyo dvitīyapāde vyākhyātaḥ । tasmāt na vāsanā samyagdarśane sati kaivatyapratibandhinī । bhavatyevāvidyānivṛttau kaivatyamiti ॥ 11 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s>:
But how is the cessation of those <s>vāsanās</s> possible? Since they are beginninglessly established, their cessation does not seem feasible. And without their cessation, <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation) cannot be established — therefore it is said: [Because these are held together by cause, fruit, substratum, and object, in the absence of these, there is the absence of those.] Cause, fruit, substratum, and object — these are the <s>hetu-phala-āśraya-ālambanas</s>. Because they are held together — bound up — by these, in the absence of these causes and the rest, there is the absence of <s>vāsanās</s>. Therefore the cessation of <s>vāsanās</s> is established.
What is that cause? He says: First, <s>dharma</s> [arises] for those whose minds are bent by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). Then [from <s>dharma</s> comes pleasure. The latent tendency of pleasure is attachment (<s>rāga</s>).] Likewise, from <s>avidyā</s> itself, through prohibited conduct, [comes <s>adharma</s>. From that, pain. The latent tendency of pain is aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>). Then,] for acquiring pleasure and avoiding pain, as before, [comes effort. Through that] effort, [acting with speech or body, one benefits or harms others. And again from that,] through helping and harming others, [arise <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>.] From those two, [pleasure and pain.] From those two, [attachment and aversion,] just as before. Then effort.
Thus this [is the] six-spoked wheel of <s>saṁsāra</s>, [set in motion with] unceasing, perpetual revolution. [And <s>avidyā</s> is the driver of this, as it revolves at every moment] — like a mare yoked to a chariot wheel.
[It is the root of all <s>kleśas</s>] — this six-spoked wheel driven by <s>avidyā</s> is the [cause] of <s>vāsanās</s>. For they are produced by the revolution of this wheel. But when <s>avidyā</s> ceases, like a wheel whose hub-binding is destroyed, the wheel of causes beginning with <s>dharma</s> also disintegrates. And with its disintegration, the <s>vāsanās</s> born from the wheel's revolution become incapable of producing effects.
[The fruit] — that purpose depending on which [something] has its present existence — that is its fruit. That too is a holder of <s>vāsanās</s>. In its absence, there is no manifestation of <s>vāsanās</s>. Because fruit such as pleasure and the rest implants <s>vāsanās</s>. [For there is no origination from what is entirely new.] What is absolutely non-existent does not come into being.
[The mind, as long as it has a function to fulfill] — having something yet to accomplish, not devoid of purpose for <s>Puruṣa</s>. When the knowledge of <s>Puruṣa's</s> true nature has been accomplished and <s>avidyā</s> has ceased, then [it has a function to fulfill and is] the substratum of <s>vāsanās</s>. For it is depending on that [mind] that the wheel of causes revolves. [When the mind has completed its purpose] — devoid of any <s>Puruṣa</s>-purpose yet to be accomplished — [<s>vāsanās</s> without a substratum cannot persist.]
[Whatever object, when encountered, manifests a particular <s>vāsanā</s> — that is its supporting object. Thus, all <s>vāsanās</s> are held together by these — cause, fruit, substratum, and object. In] the absence of the causes and the rest, [there is the absence of the <s>vāsanās</s> dependent on them] — like the cessation of shade when the umbrella is removed.
