nanu cāhaṁpratyayena cittaṁ pratyayi gṛhyata iti viṣayaviṣāyitvamekasyaiva । naiṣa doṣaḥ । triguṇatvāccittasya । yattatra tamaḥpradhānaṁ cittaṁ tadanyayā satvātmikayā vṛttyā samālambyeta, hasteneva śarīraṁ kaṇḍūyamānam । tatrāpyupalabdhā viṣayī bhinna eva puruṣaḥ । etena jātyantaragrāhyagrāhakatvena niravayavatvena puruṣaśca svayameva grāhyaḥ grāhakaścetyetat pratyavocāma ॥
[kiṁ ca-svābhāsaṁ cittamiti] ucyamāne ca [agrāhyameva cittaṁ syāditi । evaṁ śabdārthaḥ ।] svābhāsamiti hyukte anyena nāvabhāsyate na gṛhyata ityarthaḥ । na tu svayamātmānaṁ gṛhṇātītyucyate । evamādiśabdaprayogeṣu śabdasya viparītārthatvam ॥
[tadyathā-svātmapratiṣṭhamākāśam, apratiṣṭhamiti] śabdārthaḥ । tathā svastho devadatta iti, nīroga ityarthaḥ, na tu svātmani sthita iti । tatra dṛśyatvāditi hetorasiddhimācakṣāṇasya pratyakṣavirodho lokavirodho vyavahāravilopaścetyāha - [svabuddhipracārapratisaṁvedanāt sattvānāṁ] prāṇināṁ [pravṛttirdṛśyate ॥]
[kruddho'haṁ bhīto'hamamutra me rāgo'mutra me krodha iti] svāṁ svāṁ buddhimevaṁ carantīṁ pratisaṁvedya dṛṣṭvā krodhalobhādiparihārāya vivekavatāṁ pravṛttirupalabhyate । tathā prasannaṁ me cittaṁ kaळ.uṣitaṁ mūḍhamiti ca । tat [etat svabuddheragrahaṇe, na yuktamiti ।] na hi niśāmya parispandinīṁ buddhiradṛyeti yuktaṁ vaktum ॥ 19 ॥
body.translated_text: Commentary: To this it is replied — it is impossible to refute the <s>Ātman</s> (Self), who ascends the path universally acknowledged by all people, by relying on such a flawed analogy. Why? [Fire is not a valid analogy here. For fire does not illuminate its own nature as though it were previously unmanifest.] If fire, being non-luminous, were to be illuminated by itself just like a pot and the rest, then the analogy would hold. But this is not so. For fire does not illuminate its own nature as though it were non-luminous; rather, being always luminous by nature, it illuminates other things. However, the operation of a means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) regarding its own luminous nature is valid. For this very reason, [this illumination is observed in the conjunction of the illuminated and the illuminator.] Since that is so, [there is no conjunction with respect to one's own nature alone.] [Moreover, if <s>citta</s> is said to be self-luminous (<s>svābhāsa</s>),] the [meaning of this term is that it would not be graspable by anything.] For just as some explain the word <s>svābhāsa</s> by an alternative expression 'self-established' (<s>svapratiṣṭha</s>), [just as] <s>ākāśa</s> (space) [is 'self-established, not established through another'] — self-established <s>ākāśa</s> is not dependent on another as a pot depends on a substrate — [that is the meaning.] Thus, if by the word <s>svābhāsa</s> one means 'self-established,' then it would follow that <s>citta</s>, being self-luminous, would be ungraspable — if this is the objection, then to this he states our established doctrine: [The awareness of the activity of one's own <s>buddhi</s> is established through direct perception by all living beings.] The activity (<s>pracāra</s>) of <s>buddhi</s> is its modification (<s>vṛtti</s>); its awareness (<s>pratisaṁvedana</s>) is accomplished by <s>Puruṣa</s>, who is denoted by the word 'one's own' (<s>sva</s>). Thus the established doctrine is that the awareness of the modification of <s>buddhi</s>, though established through direct perception by all living beings, belongs to <s>Puruṣa</s> himself, not to <s>buddhi</s>. || 19 ||

body.text: ekasamaye cobhayānavadhāraṇam ॥ 20 ॥
body.translated_text: And at a single moment, it is impossible to ascertain both [subject and object simultaneously]. || 20 ||

body.text: na caikasminkṣaṇe svapararūpāvadhāraṇaṁ yuktaṁ, kṣaṇikavādino yadbhavanaṁ saiva kriyā tadeva ca kārakamityabhyupagamaḥ ॥ 20 ॥
body.translated_text: It is not proper that at a single instant there be ascertainment of both one's own form and another's form. For one who holds the doctrine of momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikavāda</s>), the accepted position is that the arising itself is the action, and that alone is also the agent. || 20 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
abhyupagamya vādo'yam-yadyapi svābhāsaṁ viṣayābhāsaṁ ca mano bhavatu । tatra dūṣaṇam [ekasamaye cobhayānavadhāraṇam ।] viṣayaparicchedakatve, nānākṣaṇatvādātmaparicchedo na yujyate । atha punarātmānamavadhārayati, na tadā viṣayābhimukhaṁ, svātmaparicchedakatve nānākṣaṇatvāt ॥
athobhayaparicchittirekaiveti cenna, niravayavatvāt paricchitteḥ । na hi niravayavāyāścittavṛtteḥ pradīpavadanekāvabhāsakatve yuktam । avayavabhadāttu pradīpasyānekaprakāśakatvaṁ saṁbhavati । na tu jñānasya sāvayavatvaṁ parairabhyupeyate ॥
kiṁ ca, jñānamekamekasmin kṣaṇe ubhayamavadhārayatīti cābhyupagame kriyākārakabhedaprasaṅgaḥ । yadubhayāvadhāraṇaṁ sā kriyā । yadavadhārayati tat kārakam । [na caikasmin kṣaṇe svaparo bhayāvadhāraṇaṁ kṣaṇavādino yuktam ।] kasmāt ? uktaṁ hi kṣaṇikatvasiddhaye [yadbhavanam] utpattiḥ [saiva kriyā tadeva ca kārakamityabhyupagamaḥ ।] kriyākārakabhede ca kṣaṇabhaṅgabhaṅgaḥ syāt । kārakeṇa hi kriyākṣaṇamavasthānīyam ॥ 20 ॥
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
This is an argument by way of concession — even if the mind be granted to illuminate both itself and the object, therein is the refutation: ["And the impossibility of ascertaining both at a single moment."] If [the mind] is what delimits the object, then self-delimitation is not tenable, because of the many-momentariness [involved]. If, on the other hand, it delimits itself, then at that time it is not directed toward the object, because of the many-momentariness [involved] in self-delimitation.
If [one argues that] the delimitation of both is a single [act] — no, because delimitation is without parts. For it is not tenable that a mental modification without parts should illuminate multiple things, like a lamp. A lamp can illuminate multiple things because of the differentiation of its parts. But the opponents do not accept that cognition has parts.
Moreover, if one accepts that a single cognition ascertains both in a single moment, there follows the unwanted consequence of a distinction between action and agent. That which ascertains both — that is the action. That which ascertains — that is the agent. ["And the ascertainment of both self and other in a single moment is not tenable for the proponent of momentariness."] Why? For it has been stated, in order to establish momentariness, ["that the coming-into-being"] — the origination — ["is itself the action, and that very thing is the agent — this is the accepted position."] But if there were a distinction of action and agent, there would be a breakdown of the doctrine of momentary destruction. For the agent would have to endure through the moment of action. ॥ 20 ॥

body.text: syānmatiḥ svarasaniruddhaṁ cittaṁ cittāntareṇa samanantareṇa gṛhyata iti –
body.translated_text: One might think that the mind, which has naturally ceased, is grasped by another immediately subsequent mind —

body.text: cittāntaradṛśye buddhibuddheratiprasaṅgaḥ smṛtisaṁkaraśca ॥ 21 ॥
body.translated_text: If [the mind] were to be seen by another mind, there would be an infinite regress of cognition of cognition, and a confusion of memories. ॥ 21 ॥

body.text: atha cittaṁ ceccittāntareṇa gṛhyeta buddhibuddhiḥ kena gṛhyate, sā'pyanyayā sā'pyanyayetyatiprasaṅgaḥ। smṛtisaṁkaraśca, yāvanto buddhibuddhīnāmanubhavāstāvatyaḥ smṛtayaḥ prāpnuvanti। tatsaṁkarāccaikasmṛtyanavadhāraṇaṁ ca syādityevaṁ buddhipratisaṁvedinaṁ puruṣamapalapadbhirvaināśikaiḥ sarvamevā''kulīkṛtam। te tu bhoktṛsvarūpaṁ yatra kvacana kalpayanto na nyāyena saṁgacchante। kecittu sattvamātramapi parikalpyāsti sa sattvo ya etānpañca skandhānnikṣipyānyāṁśca pratisaṁdadhātītyuktvā tata eva punastrasyanti। tathā skandhānāṁ mahannirvedāya virāgāyānutpādāya praśāntaye gurorantike brahmacaryaṁ cariṣyāmītyuktvā sattvasya punaḥ sattvamevāpahnuvate। sāṁkhyayogādayastu pravādāḥ svaśabdena puruṣameva svāminaṁ cittasya bhoktāramupayantīti ॥ 21 ॥
body.translated_text: If the mind were grasped by another mind, then by what would the cognition of that cognition be grasped? By yet another, and that by yet another — thus an infinite regress. And there would be a confusion of memories: as many experiences of cognition-of-cognitions as there are, that many memories would result. From their confusion, there would be the inability to determine any single memory. Thus, the <s>Vaināśikas</s> (Buddhist proponents of destruction), who deny <s>Puruṣa</s> as the experiencer of cognition, have thrown everything into confusion. They, positing the nature of the experiencer in one place or another, do not accord with reason. Some, even positing mere <s>sattva</s> (existence/being) [as the experiencer], having said 'there exists that being who, depositing these five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), takes up others in rebirth' — are then frightened by that very [admission]. Similarly, having said 'I will practice celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>) in the presence of the teacher for the sake of great weariness toward the <s>skandhas</s>, dispassion, non-arising, and peace' — they then deny the very being of that being [who practices]. But the doctrines of <s>Sāṅkhya</s>, <s>Yoga</s>, and others, by their own terminology, accept <s>Puruṣa</s> alone as the owner of the mind and the experiencer. ॥ 21 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[syānmatiḥ] kasyāpi- [svarasasanniruddhaṁ cittaṁ cittānteraṇa gṛhyate] iti bhāvena vinaṣṭaṁ bhaṅgurataraṁ cittaṁ [cittāntareṇa samanantareṇa] saṁjāyamānena [gṛhyata] iti, athāpi nityāvasthitapuruṣaparikalpanā nirarthikaiva । atrocyate— [cittāntaradṛśye buddhibuddheratiprasaṅgaḥ smṛtisaṅkaraśca ॥]
[yadi cittaṁ cittāntareṇa] svarasaniruddhaṁ paurastyaṁ pāścātyena jāyamānena samanantareṇa gṛheta, [buddhibuddhiḥ] ghaṭaviṣayā buddhiḥ buddhirucyate, tadviṣayā tu buddhibuddhiḥ, sā kena [gṛhyate] vyavasthitagrāhakābhāvāt । [sā'pyanyayā] grahītavyā [sā'pyanyathetyatiprasaṅgaḥ ॥]
na cāgṛhītāsu buddhibuddhiṣu saṁvyavahāro ghaṭate smṛtisaṁskārānupapatteḥ । tatraikajātīyānāmeva ghaṭabuddhibuddhīnāṁ dāśatayī mālā syādanavasthitā, na ghaṭabuddhiḥ । parisamāptau ca ghaṭabuddhibuddhīnāṁ asatyāṁ kathaṁ ghaṭadibuddhirupatiṣṭheta ॥
ayaṁ cāparo doṣaḥ [smṛtisaṁkaraśca] iti । buddhibuddhīnāṁ tatsaṁskārāṇāṁ caikarūpatvāt [smṛtisaṁkaraḥ] prāpnoti । [yāvanto buddhibuddhīnāmanubhavāstāvatyaḥ smṛtayaḥ] saṁkīrṇāḥ [prāpnuvanti । tatsaṅkarāt] smṛtisaṅkarāt [smṛtyanavadhāraṇe] iyamasyā buddheḥ smṛtirityanavadhārayantaḥ kathaṁ vyavaharemahi । tathā ca sarūpatvāt smṛtisaṁkaraḥ prāpnoti ॥
yāvanto buddhibuddhīnāṁ vidānāḥ svabuddhismṛtipūrvavyavahārāsambhavāt sarve saṁmohena saṅgacchemahi । yadi cānavasthāparijihāsayā kvacit buddhyantare samavatiṣṭhemahi, tameva [buddhipratisaṁvedinaṁ] buddhipratisaṁvedanaliṅgena spaṣṭataramapi [puruṣamapalapadbhirvaināśikairākulīkṛtaṁ jagaditi ॥]
nanu cālayavijñānakalpanayā'navasthādoṣaṁ pariharemahi । tathā cātmakalpanāmapalapemahītyevaṁ [te bhoktṛsvarūpaṁ yatra kvacana kalpayanto na nyāyena saṅgacchante ।] tasyāpyālayavijñānasya grāhyatvādanavasthitatvācābhihitasakaladoṣānuṣaṅgaḥ ॥
[kecit] vaināśikaviśeṣāḥ [sattvamātramapi] śabdāntereṇa [sattvamātraṁ] bhoktṛsvarūpaṁ [parikalpya asti sa sattvo ya etān pañca skandhān] rūpavedanāsaṁjñāsaṁskāravijñānalakṣaṇān [nikṣipya] parityajya [anyāṁśca] skandhān [pratisandadhāti] gṛhṇāti [ityuktvā tata eva] bhūtānāgataskandhapratisandhātrekasattvaparikalpanātaḥ [trasyanti ॥]
[tathā] teṣāmanyā viruddhakalpanā- [skandhānāṁ mahānirvedāya virāgāyānutpādāya praśāntaye gurorantike brahmacaryaṁ carāmī] tyuktvā [puna] stamevābhyugataṁ [satvasya sattva] (sādhyasādhanasambandha) [mapahnuvate ।] vijñānamātraṁ kṣaṇikaṁ śūnyaṁ ceti ātmānamapalapanti । (namabhisandadhīmahi । tadevaṁ) [sāṅkhyayogādayastu pravādāḥ । svaśabdena puruṣameva svāminaṁ cittasya bhoktāramabhyupayanti iti ॥ 21 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
["One might think"] — someone might — ["that the mind, which has naturally ceased, is grasped by another mind"] — the mind that has perished in its very being, that is utterly perishable, ["is grasped by another mind that is immediately subsequent"] — that arises [right after]. Thus the postulation of an eternally established <s>Puruṣa</s> would be pointless. To this it is replied — ["If the mind were to be seen by another mind, there would be an infinite regress of cognition of cognition, and a confusion of memories."]
["If the mind were"] grasped ["by another mind"] — the prior by the posterior that arises as immediately subsequent — then the ["cognition of cognition"] — the cognition whose object is the pot is called 'cognition,' and the cognition whose object is that [cognition] is 'cognition of cognition' — by what ["is that grasped?"] — since there is no established grasper. ["That too must be grasped by another, and that by yet another — thus an infinite regress."]
And without the cognitions-of-cognitions being grasped, practical activity is not possible, because of the impossibility of memory-impressions. In that case, there would be an endless chain of ten [or more] cognitions-of-pot-cognitions of one and the same type, not [just] the pot-cognition. And without the series of cognitions-of-pot-cognitions reaching completion, how would a cognition of pot and the like arise?
Here is another fault — ["and a confusion of memories."] Because the cognitions-of-cognitions and their impressions are of a single form, ["a confusion of memories"] results. ["As many experiences of cognitions-of-cognitions as there are, that many memories"] become confused ["and result. From that confusion"] — from the confusion of memories — ["there would be the inability to determine"] — those who cannot determine 'this memory belongs to this cognition' — how would they carry on practical activity? And thus, because of sameness of form, a confusion of memories results.
All the modes of cognitions-of-cognitions — because of the impossibility of practical activity involving one's own cognition-memory — all of us would be engulfed in delusion. And if, out of the desire to avoid the infinite regress, we were to halt at some particular cognition, [we would thereby accept] that very ["experiencer who cognizes cognition"] — <s>Puruṣa</s> — who is made all the more evident by the mark of cognition-experiencing — ["by the <s>Vaināśikas</s> who deny him, the world has been thrown into confusion."]
But [the Buddhist might say], by the postulation of an <s>ālaya-vijñāna</s> (store-consciousness), we could avoid the fault of infinite regress. And thus we could deny the postulation of a self. To this — ["they, positing the nature of the experiencer in one place or another, do not accord with reason."] Because that <s>ālaya-vijñāna</s> too would be an object of grasping and would be non-enduring, all the faults already stated would attach to it.
["Some"] particular <s>Vaināśikas</s>, ["even positing"] by another term ["mere <s>sattva</s>"] — the nature of the experiencer — ["having said 'there exists that being who deposits these five <s>skandhas</s>"] — characterized as form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — ["and takes up others'"] in rebirth, ["are then frightened"] by that very postulation of a single being who effects the connection with past and future aggregates.
["Similarly,"] there is another contradictory postulation of theirs — having said ["'I will practice celibacy in the presence of the teacher for the sake of great weariness toward the <s>skandhas</s>, dispassion, non-arising, and peace,'"] they ["then"] deny that very accepted being — ["the being of that being"] — (the relation of end and means) — saying it is merely momentary consciousness, empty, and thus they deny the self. ["But the doctrines of <s>Sāṅkhya</s>, <s>Yoga</s>, and others, by their own terminology, accept <s>Puruṣa</s> alone as the owner of the mind and the experiencer."] ॥ 21 ॥

body.text: katham –
body.translated_text: How —

body.text: citerapratisaṁkramāyāstadākārāpattau svabuddhisaṁvedanam ॥ 22 ॥
body.translated_text: When <s>Citi</s> (pure awareness), which does not migrate, assumes the form of that [mind], there is self-cognition of one's own intellect. ॥ 22 ॥

body.text: apariṇāminī hi bhoktṛśaktirapratisaṁkramā ca pariṇāminyarthe pratisaṁkrānteva tadvṛttimanupatati। tasyāśca prāptacaitanyopagrahasvarūpāyā buddhivṛtteranukārimātratayā vuddhivṛttyaviśiṣṭā hi jñānavṛttirākhyāyate। tathā coktam – na pātālaṁ na ca vivaraṁ girīṇāṁ naivāndhakāraṁ kukṣayo nodadhīnām। guhā yasyāṁ nihitaṁ brahma śāśvataṁ buddhivṛttimaviśiṣṭāṁ kavayo vedayante ॥ iti ॥ 22 ॥
body.translated_text: The power of the experiencer (<s>bhoktṛ-śakti</s>) is indeed unchanging and does not migrate; yet, as though migrated into the changing object [i.e., the mind], it follows its modifications. And the cognitive modification (<s>jñāna-vṛtti</s>) — of that <s>buddhi</s>-modification which has attained the form of being grasped by consciousness — by virtue of merely imitating [the <s>buddhi</s>-modification], is described as indistinguishable from the <s>buddhi</s>-modification. And thus it has been said: 'Not in the netherworld, not in the caverns of mountains, not in darkness, nor in the bellies of oceans — the cave in which the eternal <s>Brahman</s> is deposited, the wise know to be the <s>buddhi</s>-modification itself, indistinguishable [from awareness].' ॥ 22 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[kathaṁ] bhoktāraṁ svaśabdenaivābhyupayanti ? yataḥ [citerapratisaṁkramāyāstadākārāpattau] satyāṁ [svabuddhisaṁvedanaṁ] bhavati । [citiḥ] caitanyaṁ puruṣa ityarthaḥ । sā cāpariṇāmitvāt [apratisaṁkramā] । tasyāḥ [apratisaṁkramāyāḥ] api satyāściteḥ [tadākārāpattiḥ ।] taditi prakṛtaṁ cittaṁ pratyāmnāyate tasyākārāpattistadākārāpattiḥ । tasyāścite [stadākārāpattau] satyāṁ [svabuddhisaṁvedanaṁ] bhavati । svasya bauddhasya pratyayasyopalabdhirbhavati । tadarthameva hi sā buddhiḥ śabdādipratyayarūpeṇa pariṇamate ॥
tadetat pratipādayati(pratītya)- [apariṇāminī hi bhoktṛśaktiḥ] dṛkśaktiḥ yathāvyākhyātā । [apratisaṁkramā ca] satī [pariṇāminyarthe] bauddhapratyaye [pratisaṁkrānteva] pratyayiviṣayatvāt [tadvṛttimanupatantīvānupatantī] draṣṭṛtvādupalabhamānā । bauddhaḥ pratyayo jāyamāna eva tasyāḥ karmatāmāpadyate । taṁ bauddhaṁ pratyayaṁ vṛttimanupatantyupalabhamānā bhoktṛśaktiḥ ॥
[tasyāśca prāptacaitanyopagraha[sva]rūpāyāḥ] prāptaṁ caitanyopagraharūpaṁ puruṣopagraharūpaṁ yayā buddhivṛtyā samāsāditapāvakopagraharūpataptalohapiṇḍavat dṛśikarmatvādeva [anukāramātratayā,] buddhivṛttisārūpyamātratayā । [buddhivṛtyaviśiṣṭā jñavṛttiriti ।] jña evopalabdhireva vṛttiriti [ākhyāyate । ‘vṛttisārūpyamitaratra’] iti hi vyākhyātam । tathā [“pratyayāviśeṣo bhogaḥ”] iti prakhyāpitam ॥
bhoktṛbhogyabhede ca sati cittākārāpattirūpapadyate । na cāsati vyatirikte bhoktari cittasyaiva dṛṣṭṛdṛśyobhayābhāsatvamakasmādupakalpate । tasmāt suṣṭhūcyate- [‘sāṅkhyayogādaya eva puruṣaṁ svaśabdenābhyupayanti’] iti । anye tu śabdāntareṇopayanto'pi tata eva bibhyati ॥
[tathā cottam] -buddhivṛtyanukāramātratayā buddhāveva jñavṛttirupalabhyate, nānyatreti । [na pātālaṁ no vivaraṁ girīṇāṁ naivāndhakāraḥ kukṣayo nodadhīnām ,] evamādīni [na guhā । yasyāṁ] guhāyāṁ [nihitaṁ brahma śāścataṁ sā guhā,] na pātāळ.ādīni । kasyāṁ punarguhāyāṁ nihitamityāha-buddhāveva guhāyāṁ [vṛttim] ātmākhyāṁ brahmākhyām [aviśiṣṭām] apṛthagbhūtāṁ buddhivṛtyaviśiṣṭāṁ [vedayante] vivekinaḥ [॥ 22 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
["How"] do they accept <s>Puruṣa</s> as the experiencer by their own terminology? Because ["when <s>Citi</s>, which does not migrate, assumes the form of that [mind],"] there is ["self-cognition of one's own intellect."] ["<s>Citi</s>"] means consciousness, <s>Puruṣa</s> — this is the meaning. And that [<s>Citi</s>], being unchanging, ["does not migrate."] Of that [<s>Citi</s>], ["which does not migrate,"] even though it exists, there is ["the assumption of its form."] 'That' refers to the <s>citta</s> (mind) under discussion — the assumption of its form is 'the assumption of that form.' When there is ["the assumption of that form"] by <s>Citi</s>, ["self-cognition of one's own intellect"] occurs. There is apprehension of one's own mental cognition. For that <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) transforms into the form of cognitions of sound and the like for that very purpose.
He explains this — ["the power of the experiencer"] is the power of seeing (<s>dṛk-śakti</s>), as previously explained. ["Not migrating,"] yet ["as though migrated into the changing object"] — the mental cognition — because of being the object of the cognizer, ["following its modifications as though following them"] — apprehending them by virtue of being the seer. The mental cognition, at the very moment of arising, becomes the object of that [<s>Citi</s>]. The power of the experiencer apprehends that mental cognition — the modification — by following it.
["Of that <s>buddhi</s>-modification which has attained the form of being grasped by consciousness"] — that <s>buddhi</s>-modification which has acquired the form of being grasped by <s>Puruṣa</s>, like a ball of iron that has acquired the form of being grasped by a nearby fire — ["by virtue of merely imitating,"] by virtue of merely having the likeness of the <s>buddhi</s>-modification — ["the cognitive modification (<s>jña-vṛtti</s>) is described as indistinguishable from the <s>buddhi</s>-modification."] [That is,] the modification that is the knower himself — apprehension itself — ["is described"] [as such]. For it has been explained — ['there is identification with the modification in other states.'] And it has been proclaimed — ["'experience is the non-distinction of cognition.'"]
When there is a distinction between experiencer and experienced, the assumption of the form of the mind [by <s>Citi</s>] is tenable. But without a seer distinct [from the mind], the mind's appearing as both seer and seen would arise without cause. Therefore, it is well said — ["'the doctrines of <s>Sāṅkhya</s>, <s>Yoga</s>, and others accept <s>Puruṣa</s> by their own terminology.'"] Others, though approaching [the truth] under a different name, are frightened by that very [implication].
["And thus it has been said"] — by virtue of merely imitating the <s>buddhi</s>-modification, the cognitive modification is apprehended in the <s>buddhi</s> itself, and nowhere else. ["Not in the netherworld, not in the caverns of mountains, not in darkness, nor in the bellies of oceans"] — none of these ["is the cave. In which"] cave ["the eternal <s>Brahman</s> is deposited — that cave"] is not the netherworld and the like. In which cave, then, is it deposited? He says — in the <s>buddhi</s> itself, the cave — ["the modification"] known as the self, known as <s>Brahman</s>, ["indistinguishable"] — not separate — indistinguishable from the <s>buddhi</s>-modification — ["the discriminating ones know."] ॥ 22 ॥

body.text: ataścaitadabhyupagamyate –
body.translated_text: And therefore this is accepted —

body.text: draṣṭṛdṛśyoparaktaṁ cittaṁ sarvārtham ॥ 23 ॥
body.translated_text: The mind, colored by the seer and the seen, is [capable of apprehending] all objects. ॥ 23 ॥

body.text: mano hi mantavyenārthenoparaktaṁ, tatsvayaṁ ca viṣayatvādviṣayiṇā puruṣeṇā''tmīyayā vṛttyā'bhisaṁbaddhaṁ, tadetaccittameva draṣṭṛdṛśyoparaktaṁ viṣayaviṣayinirbhāsaṁ cetanācetanasvarūpāpannaṁ viṣayātmakamapyaviṣayātmakamivācetanaṁ cetanamiva sphaṭikamaṇikalpaṁ sarvārthamityucyate।
body.translated_text: For the mind is colored by the object that is to be thought about; and it itself, being also an object, is connected with the subject, <s>Puruṣa</s>, through its own modification. Thus this very mind, colored by the seer and the seen, reflecting both object and subject, having assumed both the conscious and unconscious natures — though of the nature of the object, appearing as though not of the nature of the object; though unconscious, appearing as though conscious — like a crystal gem, is said to be [capable of apprehending] all objects.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
kāmāt punaḥ kāraṇāt puruṣasya cettākārāpattiḥ । tasyāṁ vā satyāṁ svabuddhisaṁvedanam । kuto vaināśikānāṁ cittameva grāhyaṁ grāhakaṁ ceti bhrāntirityāha - [draṣṭṛdṛśyoparaktaṁ cittu sarvārtham । draṣṭā] puruṣo [dṛśyaṁ] śabdādi tābhyām [uparaktaṁ cittaṁ sarvārthaṁ] puruṣasya bhogāpavargārthaṁ bhavati । [mano'bhimantavyenārthena] ayaskāntamaṇideśīyena viṣayeṇa [uparaktaṁ svayaṁ ca viṣayatvāt puruṣasya viṣayiṇā puruṣeṇa] sannihitena [ātmīyayā vṛttyā] mānasena pratyayena viṣayatayā [abhisambaddham ॥]
[tadetaccittam] ātmavṛttidvāreṇa puruṣeṇa sambandhāddraṣṭuḥ svarūpoparaktaṁ śabdādinā ca mantavyenoparaktamiti [draṣṭṛdṛśyoparaktaṁ cittameva] na puruṣaḥ । [draṣṭṛdṛśyoparaktam] ityasya vyākhyānaṁ karoti- [viṣayaviṣayinirbhāsaṁ cetanācetanasvarūpāpannam ॥]
kathaṁ punaḥ svayamacetanaṁ sacetanasvarūpāpannamiti ? naiṣa doṣaḥ--puruṣeṇa nityasannidhānācetanamiva । tadevāvivekibhiścetanamityucyate । na tathā viṣayāḥ । nityamacetanātmakā hi te । svatastu cittamacetanameveti [cetanācetanasvarūpāpannaṁ] ityucyate ॥
[viṣayātmakamiva] śabdādisvarūpamātramiva cetyartha: । [acetanaṁ cetanāmiva] puruṣasvarūpāpannamiva cetyarthaḥ । [sphaṭikamāṇikalpaṁ] yathā sphaṭikamaṇiralaktakādisannidhau tadākāratāṁ bibharti, tathaiva tat [sarvārthaṁ] cittam [ucyate ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
For what reason, then, does <s>Citi</s> assume the form of the mind? And when it does, how does self-cognition of one's own intellect [occur]? From what source arises the <s>Vaināśikas</s>' error that the mind itself is both grasped and grasper? To this he says — ["The mind, colored by the seer and the seen, is capable of all objects. The seer"] is <s>Puruṣa</s>; ["the seen"] is sound and the like. ["Colored"] by both of these, ["the mind is capable of all objects"] — it serves the purposes of experience and liberation for <s>Puruṣa</s>. ["The mind, colored by the object to be thought about"] — by the object which is like a lodestone — ["and itself, being also an object of <s>Puruṣa</s>, by <s>Puruṣa</s> the subject"] who is in proximity, ["through its own modification"] — the mental cognition — is ["connected"] as an object.
["Thus this very mind,"] through the connection with <s>Puruṣa</s> via its own modification, colored by the essential form of the seer, and colored by the object such as sound which is to be thought about — ["colored by the seer and the seen — it is the mind itself,"] not <s>Puruṣa</s>. He explains the meaning of ["colored by the seer and the seen"] — ["reflecting both object and subject, having assumed the nature of both conscious and unconscious."]
But how can what is itself unconscious assume the nature of the conscious? This is not a fault — because of the eternal proximity of <s>Puruṣa</s>, [it appears] as though conscious. And it is said to be [as though] conscious by those who lack discrimination. Not so the objects [of the senses] — for they are eternally of unconscious nature. But in itself, the mind is indeed unconscious — thus it is said to have ["assumed both the conscious and unconscious natures."]
["As though of the nature of the object"] — as though of the nature of mere sound and the like — this is the meaning. ["Though unconscious, as though conscious"] — as though having assumed the nature of <s>Puruṣa</s> — this is the meaning. ["Like a crystal gem"] — just as a crystal gem, in the proximity of lac and the like, assumes their form — even so that mind ["is said to be capable of all objects."]

body.text: tadanena cittasārūpyeṇa bhrāntāḥ kecittadeva cetanamityāhuḥ। apare cittamātramevedaṁ sarvaṁ nāsti khalvayaṁ gavādirghaṭādiśca sakāraṇo loka iti। anukampanīyāste। kasmāt, asti hi teṣāṁ bhrāntibījaṁ sarvarūpākāranirbhāsaṁ cittamiti। samādhiprajñāyāṁ prajñeyo'rthaḥ pratibimbībhūtastasyā''lambanībhūtatvādanyaḥ। sa cedarthaścittamātraṁ syātkathaṁ prajñayaiva prajñārūpamavadhāryeta। tasmātpratibimbībhūto'rthaḥ prajñāyāṁ yenāvadhāryate sa puruṣa iti। evaṁ grahītṛgrahaṇagrāhyasvarūpacittabhedāttrayamapyetajjātitaḥ pravibhajante te samyagdarśinastairadhigataḥ puruṣaḥ ॥ 23 ॥
body.translated_text: By this likeness to the mind, some, deluded, declare that [the mind] itself is conscious. Others [say] that all this is merely mind — that this world with its cows, pots, and their causes does not truly exist. They are to be pitied. Why? Because the seed of their error is the mind that reflects all forms and appearances. In the wisdom of <s>samādhi</s>, the object to be known appears as a reflection, and since it has become the support [of that wisdom], it is something other [than the mind]. If that object were merely mind, how would one ascertain the very form of wisdom by means of wisdom itself? Therefore, the object that appears as a reflection in wisdom — that by which it is ascertained — that is <s>Puruṣa</s>. Thus, from the distinction of the mind into the forms of grasper, grasping, and graspable, those who see rightly distinguish all three by class — and by them <s>Puruṣa</s> has been realized. ॥ 23 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
tasmāt [anena cittasārūpyeṇa bhrāntāḥ kecit ।] etattu cittasārūpyaṁ vaiśeṣikāṇāṁ pramohakāraṇam । vaiśeṣikādayastu cittasārūpyamāhendrajālavyāmohitacetasaḥ [tadeva] cittaṁ [cetanamityāhuḥ ।] katham ? yasmānmanaḥpuruṣasaṁyogajaṁ caitanye guṇaḥ ucchedanīya iti manyante । vaināśikebhyastvayaṁ viśeṣaḥ-sthiramekaṁ dharmiṇamicchantīti ॥
[apare] bauddhāḥ [cittamātramevedaṁ sarvam , nāsti gavādirghaṭādiśca svākāreṇa] viśiṣṭaḥ sarveṣāṁ pratyayasya sādhāraṇo [lokaḥ] iti svānubhavamapyapalapanti । [te] evaṁ bhrāntāḥ sukumāratarabuddhayo vaināśikā [anukampanīyāḥ ॥]
[kasmāt ? asti hi teṣāṁ bhrāntibījaṁ sarvarūpākāranirbhāsaṁ cittamiti ।] sanimittā hi teṣāṁ bhrāntiḥ na lokāyatikānāṁ śūnyavādināmiva nirbījā । kevalajagadvañcanārthapravṛttatvāttu naiteṣvanukampā kartavyā । tasmādyuktamuktaṁ teṣāṁ varākāṇāṁ sabījabhrāntacetasāmanukampanīyamiti ॥
ke punarabhrāntā ityāha- [samādhiprajñāyāmiti ।] samādhiprajñāgrahaṇamabhrāntacittagrahaṇārtham । vikṣiptacetaso hi bhrāntāḥ । [samādhiprajñāyām] abhrāntāyāṁ viśuddhāyāṁ vivekavatyāṁ prasannagambhīratarāyāṁ [prajñeyo'rthaḥ pratibimbībhūtaḥ] nirmaladarpaṇamaṇḍala iva [tasyāṁ] samādhiprajñāyāṁ karaṇabhūtāyām [alambanībhūtatvādanyaḥ] prajñātaḥ sakāśājjātisvarūpakriyādibhiranyaḥ ॥
[sa cet] anyaḥ [cittamāttraṁ syāt kathaṁ prajñayaiva prajñārūpamavadhāryeta ।] svātmani kriyāvirodhāt na hi kathañcidavadhāryeta । [tasmāt] prajñāyāḥ anyo'sāvarthaḥ saḥ, yasyāṁ [prajñāyāṁ pratibimbībhūto'rtho yenāvadhāryete] saḥ tasyāḥ prajñāyā ālambanībhūtācārthadanyaḥ kartṛkārakabhūtaḥ । [sa puruṣaḥ ॥]
[ityevaṁ ye grahītṛgrahaṇagrāhyasvarūpabhedāt] kartṛkaraṇakarmabhedopapatteḥ, nahi niravayavamekamevaikāsmin kṣaṇe vastu kartṛ ca karma ca bhavati, tato ye [trayamapyetat jātitaḥ pravibhajante, te samyagdarśinaḥ tairadhigataḥ puruṣaḥ,] prāpta ityarthaḥ । sāmarthyāttu jñāta iti gamyate [॥ 23 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
Therefore, ['some are deluded by this similarity with <s>citta</s> (mind).'] This similarity with <s>citta</s> is the cause of delusion for the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>. The <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> and others, their minds deluded by the magic-like similarity with <s>citta</s>, ['say that very'] <s>citta</s> ['is conscious.'] How? Because they think that consciousness is a quality born from the conjunction of <s>manas</s> (mind) and <s>Puruṣa</s>, which must be eliminated. Their distinction from the <s>Vaināśikas</s> (Buddhists) is that they accept a stable, unitary substance-bearer.
['Others'] — the Buddhists — ['say that all this is mind alone; neither a cow nor a pot exists in its own form,'] distinguished as a world common to all cognitions — thus they deny even their own experience. ['They,'] thus deluded, being of exceedingly tender intellect, the <s>Vaināśikas</s> ['are to be pitied.']
['Why? Because the seed of their delusion exists — namely, that <s>citta</s> manifests all forms and appearances.'] For their delusion has a cause, unlike the baseless delusion of the <s>Lokāyatikas</s> (materialists) and the <s>Śūnyavādins</s> (voidists). But since the latter are engaged solely in deceiving the world, no sympathy need be shown to them. Therefore, it is rightly said that those pitiable ones, whose minds are deluded though with a seed [of reason], are to be pitied.
Who then are the undeluded? He says — ['In the wisdom of <s>samādhi</s>.'] The mention of <s>samādhi</s>-wisdom is for the purpose of indicating the undeluded mind. For those whose minds are distracted are deluded. ['In the wisdom of <s>samādhi</s>'] — which is undeluded, purified, possessed of discrimination, exceedingly clear and profound — ['the knowable object, having become a reflection'] — as in a spotless mirror surface — ['in that'] <s>samādhi</s>-wisdom, which serves as the instrument, ['because of being the support, is other'] — other from the cognition in terms of class, essential nature, activity, and so on.
['If that'] other ['were merely mind, how could the form of cognition be ascertained by cognition itself?'] Because of the contradiction of action upon oneself, it could not be ascertained in any way. ['Therefore,'] that object is other than cognition; he ['in whose cognition the object has become a reflection, by whom it is ascertained'] — he is other than both the object which has become the support and the cognition; he has the role of agent and instrument. ['He is <s>Puruṣa</s>.']
['Thus, those who, from the distinction in the essential nature of the grasper, the grasping, and the grasped'] — because of the applicability of the distinction of agent, instrument, and object of action — for indeed one single, partless entity cannot in one moment be both agent and object — therefore those who ['distinguish all three of these by class, they are the right seers; by them <s>Puruṣa</s> has been attained'] — realized, this is the meaning. By implication, it is understood that he has been known. [॥ 23 ॥]

body.text: kutaśca –
body.translated_text: And furthermore —

body.text: tadasaṁkhyeyavāsanābhiścitramapi parārthaṁ saṁhatyakāritvāt ॥ 24 ॥
body.translated_text: That [mind], though variegated by innumerable <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions), exists for another's purpose, because it acts in conjunction (<s>saṁhatyakāritva</s>). ॥ 24 ॥

body.text: tadetaccittamasaṁkhyeyābhirvāsanābhireva citrīkṛtamapi parārthaṁ parasya bhogāpavargārthaṁ na svārthaṁ saṁhatyakāritvādgṛhavat। saṁhatyakāriṇā cittena na svārthena bhavitavyaṁ, na sukhacittaṁ sukhārthaṁ na jñānaṁ jñānārthamubhayamapyetatparārtham। yaśca bhogenāpavargeṇa cārthenārthavānpuruṣaḥ sa eva paro na paraḥ sāmānyamātram। yattu kiṁcitparaṁ sāmānyamātraṁ svarūpeṇodāharedvaināśikastatsarvaṁ saṁhatyakāritvātparārthameva syāt। yastvasau paro viśeṣaḥ sa na saṁhatyakārī puruṣa iti ॥ 24 ॥
body.translated_text: That mind, though diversified by innumerable <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions), exists for another's purpose — for the purpose of another's experience and liberation — not for its own purpose, because it acts in conjunction, like a house. The mind, which acts in conjunction, cannot exist for its own purpose. The mind of pleasure is not for the purpose of pleasure; knowledge is not for the purpose of knowledge — both of these are for another's purpose. And he who has purpose through the ends of experience (<s>bhoga</s>) and liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) — that is <s>Puruṣa</s>; he alone is the 'other,' not [merely] the 'other' in a general sense. Whatever general 'other' the <s>Vaināśika</s> (Buddhist) might cite by its own nature — all that, because of acting in conjunction, would itself serve another's purpose. But that specific 'other' who does not act in conjunction — that is <s>Puruṣa</s>. ॥ 24 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[kutaśca] asti puruṣaścittavyatiriktaḥ ? pūrvaṁ cittasya dṛśyatvena vyatiriktapuruṣasiddhirāpāditā । tasyaiva tu cittasya saṁhatyakāritvenādhunā svāmisiddhyarthamāha – [tadasaṅkhyeyavāsanācitramapi parārtha saṁhatyakāritvāt ॥]
yadyapi [tadeva cittamasaṁkhyeyābhirvāsanābhiḥ] anādisamayābhiḥ [citrīkṛtaṁ] bhrāntikāraṇamuktaṁ, tathāpi [parārthaṁ parasya bhogārthameveti] pratijñāyate । [saṁhatyakāritvāt] kāryakaraṇaviṣayādivyāpārāpekṣamarthasādhakatvāt saṁhatyakāritvam, ataḥ [saṁhatyakāritvāt gṛhādivat] iti pārārthyaṁ cittasya । na hi kiṁcana loke saṁhatyakāri dṛṣṭaṁ svārtham ॥
tasmāt [saṁhatyakāriṇā, citena na svārthena bhāvitavyam । na hi sukhacittaṁ, sukhārthaṁ] sukhacittārthaṁ vā । [nāpi jñānacittaṁ jñānārthaṁ] vā jñānacittārthaṁ vā । kiṁ tarhi ? sukhacittaṁ jñānacittamapi etadubhayaṁ [parārtham ॥]
yaśca [bhogena] sukhācittena jñānacittena ca [apavargeṇārthenārthavān puruṣaḥ sa eva paraḥ । na parasāmānyamātraṁ] śarīramindriyāṇi viṣayā vā । nahi vaināśikaḥ sukhacittaṁ śarīrendriyaviṣayārthamicchati । tathā cecchannabhyupagataṁ virundhīta । vijñānasyaiva hi sukhāpavargābhyāmarthitvamabhimanyate । tasmāt ya eva śarīrendriyaviṣayavyatiriktaḥ puruṣo bhogāpavargābhyāmarthavānanyo vijñānādabhyupagamanīyaḥ ॥
yadi [yatkiñcic parasāmānyamātram udāharedvaināśikaḥ,] yadi tu vaināśikaḥ saṁhatyakāriṇāṁ gṛhādīnāṁ devadattādisaṁhataparārthatvamiti vyāmohādabhimanyamānaḥ kaṁcana viśiṣṭaṁ na paramicchet, evaṁ cenmanvīta, sa idaṁ vaktavyaḥ--yaḥ paraḥ śarīrendriyaviṣayatyayānāṁ sāmānyam, uta sarve eveti, kimeṣāmanyatamaḥ, kiṁ vā kaśvidevaitebhyo bhinnajātīya iti ॥
na tāvatsāmānyam । na hi bhogāpavargarthinārtha sāmānyavastuvaidrāśiko'bhyupaiti, svasamayavirodhāt । nāpi śarīrādīni samastāni bhogāpavargībhyāmarthīnīti vāñchati । vijñānasantatereva bhogāpavargārthitvābhimānāt ॥
na cāpi jñānasantatirityekaṁ vastu(santateḥ kṣaṇikatvam । ) na cāpi santānasyāvastutayā śaśaviṣāṇakalpasya bhogāpavargībhyāmarthitvam । nāpi śarīrendriyādīnāmanyatamatvamicchati । vijñānavyatiritānām ā.ātmayasamaye bhogāpavargārthitvānabhyupagamāt ॥
nāpi śarīrendriyāṇāṁ saṅghāto nāma vastuto bhavato vidyate, yena cittaṁ saṁhataparārthaṁ prārthayethāḥ । avastuno hi kathamarthitvam । nāpi śarirendriyādibhyo'nyaṁ saṁhatabhinnajātīyaṁ pratijānīṣe । yadi bhinnajātīrya bhogāpavargābhyāmarthavantamadṛṣṭaṁ parikalpayethāḥ, sa evāsmābhiruktaḥ para iti । tasya ca saṁhṛtatve paratvaṁ dṛṣṭānātmavajropakalpate । pariśeṣāttu asaṁhato bhogāpavargābhyāmarthī para iti ॥
kiṁ cānyat-saṁhataparārthaṁ cittamiti sādhayato'rthinaḥ saṁhatasyānyasyānupapatteḥ svārthameva cittamityuktaṁ bhavati । tathā ca sati bhavato dṛṣṭāntābhāvo'bhyupagamavirodhaśca । tathā manvānasyānyadvāce hṛdaye cānyadaniśamyakāritrva cāpatati । yena cakṣurādiparārthavasādhanena viruddhatādoṣaḥ pralyākhyāyi । teṣa vijñānaparārthatvamita cedvijñānasyāpi saṁhatatvāt parārthavaṁ prasādhitam । atha vijñānasyāpi kṣaṇikatvādarsahatatvamita cet । na-tattya vyatiriktadṛśyatvātū dharmamātrānabhyupagamācca kṣaṇikatvānabhyupagamācetyetadapi pratyavocāma ॥
tasmāducyate--- [yatkiṁcit parasāmānyamātraṁ svarūpeṇe.odāharedvaināśikaḥ sa sarvaḥ saṁhatyakāritvāt parārtha eva syāt ।] na devadattārdisaṁhatārthatvam । ubhābhyāmāvābhyāmanabhyupagamāt । tvamapi vijñānavyatirekeṇa nānyamabhyupaiṣi । vayamapi puruṣavyatirekeṇa nānyārthatvamabhivāñchāmaḥ । vijñānamātratvaṁ ca nopapadyata ityuktam । ato [yastvasau paro viśeṣaḥ sa na saṁhatyakārī puruṣaḥ] svārtha iti siddhaḥ । tasmādasti bhoktā tasya svārthasya svena dṛśyena parārthena yannimittaḥ saṁyogaḥ । tadviyogāt kaivalyamupakalpate [॥ 24 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
['And furthermore,'] does <s>Puruṣa</s> exist distinct from <s>citta</s>? Previously, the existence of <s>Puruṣa</s> distinct [from <s>citta</s>] was established through the seen-ness (<s>dṛśyatva</s>) of <s>citta</s>. But now, through the conjunctive activity (<s>saṁhatyakāritva</s>) of that very <s>citta</s>, he states [the argument] for the purpose of establishing the owner (<s>svāmin</s>) — ['That mind, though variegated by innumerable <s>vāsanās</s>, exists for another's purpose, because it acts in conjunction.']
Although ['that very mind, diversified by innumerable <s>vāsanās</s>'] — from beginningless time — ['has been stated as the cause of delusion,'] nevertheless ['it exists for another's purpose — for the purpose of another's experience alone'] — this is the proposition. ['Because it acts in conjunction'] — because it accomplishes its purpose depending on the operation of body, instruments, objects, and so on — this is conjunctive activity. Therefore, ['because it acts in conjunction, like a house and the like,'] the mind exists for another's purpose. For nothing in the world that acts in conjunction is observed to exist for its own purpose.
Therefore, ['the mind, which acts in conjunction, cannot exist for its own purpose. For the mind of pleasure is not for the purpose of pleasure,'] nor for the purpose of the pleasure-mind. ['Nor is the mind of knowledge for the purpose of knowledge,'] nor for the purpose of the knowledge-mind. What then? The mind of pleasure and the mind of knowledge — both of these are ['for another's purpose.']
And ['he who has purpose through the ends of experience'] — through the pleasure-mind — and through the knowledge-mind — ['and liberation — that <s>Puruṣa</s> is the "other." Not a mere general "other"'] — not the body, sense organs, or objects. For the <s>Vaināśika</s> (Buddhist) does not accept that the pleasure-mind exists for the purpose of the body, sense organs, and objects. And if he did accept that, it would contradict his own established position. For it is consciousness alone that is considered to desire pleasure and liberation. Therefore, he who is distinct from body, sense organs, and objects, who has purpose through experience and liberation — that <s>Puruṣa</s>, other than consciousness, must be accepted.
If ['the <s>Vaināśika</s> were to cite some mere general "other,"'] if the <s>Vaināśika</s>, out of delusion thinking that the other-purposiveness of conjunctive entities like houses is for the sake of a conjunctive other like <s>Devadatta</s>, were not to accept any specific 'other' — if he were to think thus, he should be asked: is the 'other' for whom body, sense organs, objects, and cognitions serve a generality of these, or all of them, or one among them, or someone of a different class from these?
Not a generality, first of all. For the <s>Vaināśika</s> does not accept a general entity as desiring experience and liberation, because it contradicts his own doctrine. Nor does he wish that the body and sense organs collectively desire experience and liberation — because it is the stream of consciousness alone that is considered to desire experience and liberation.
Nor is the stream of consciousness one thing, because the stream is momentary. Nor, since the continuum has no substantial reality and is like a hare's horn, can it desire experience and liberation. Nor does he accept that it is any one among the body, sense organs, and so on — because in his own doctrine, things other than consciousness are not accepted as desiring experience and liberation.
Nor does an aggregate of body and sense organs truly exist as a real entity, so that you could claim the mind serves that aggregate's purpose. For how can what is unreal have desire? Nor do you assert another of a different class from body, sense organs, and the rest that is conjunctive. If you were to postulate an unseen entity of a different class that has purpose through experience and liberation — that is exactly what we call the 'other.' And for that entity, if it were conjunctive, its other-purposiveness would be established, like a diamond-thunderbolt, contradicting the example. But by elimination, the non-conjunctive one who desires experience and liberation is the 'other.'
Moreover — for one who seeks to prove that the mind serves another's purpose through conjunction, since a conjunctive 'other' is impossible, it would be said that the mind exists for its own purpose. And that being so, you would have no example [to support your thesis] and a contradiction with your own position. For one who thinks thus, saying one thing while having another in the heart, the fault of inconsistency would follow constantly. The fault of contradiction, which was refuted by [the argument from] the other-purposiveness of the eye and other [sense organs] — if through that the other-purposiveness of consciousness [is established], then because consciousness too acts in conjunction, its other-purposiveness has been proven. If it be said that consciousness, being momentary, is non-conjunctive — no, because [we have already] responded: because of the seen-ness of what is distinct from it, and because the momentariness [of consciousness] is not accepted, since only <s>dharmas</s> alone are not accepted.
Therefore it is said — ['Whatever mere general "other" the <s>Vaināśika</s> might cite by its own nature — all that, because of acting in conjunction, would itself serve another's purpose.'] Not other-purposiveness for a conjunctive entity like <s>Devadatta</s> — because neither of us accepts that. You too do not accept another apart from consciousness. We too do not wish for other-purposiveness except for <s>Puruṣa</s>. And that it cannot be consciousness alone has been stated. Therefore, ['that specific "other" who does not act in conjunction — that is <s>Puruṣa</s>,'] existing for his own purpose — this is established. Therefore, there is an experiencer, and because of the conjunction caused by the seen (which is for another's purpose) with his own purpose — from the separation from that, <s>kaivalya</s> is established. [॥ 24 ॥]

body.text: viśeṣadarśina ātmabhāvabhāvanānivṛttiḥ ॥ 25 ॥
body.translated_text: For the seer of the distinction (<s>viśeṣa</s>), the contemplation of self-identity (<s>ātmabhāvabhāvanā</s>) ceases. ॥ 25 ॥

body.text: yathā prāvṛṣi tṛṇāṅkurasyodbhedena tadbījasattā'numīyate tathā mokṣamārgaśravaṇena yasya romaharṣāśrupātau dṛśyete tatrāpyasti viśeṣadarśanabījamapavargabhāgīyaṁ karmābhinirvartitamityanumīyate। tasyā''tmabhāvabhāvanā svābhāvikī pravartate। yasyābhāvādidamuktaṁ svabhāvaṁ muktvā doṣādyeṣāṁ pūrvapakṣe rucirbhavatyaruciśca nirṇaye bhavati। tatrā''tmabhāvabhāvanā ko'hamāsaṁ kathamahamāsaṁ kiṁsvididaṁ kathaṁsvididaṁ ke bhaviṣyāmaḥ kathaṁ vā bhaviṣyāma iti। sā tu viśeṣadarśino nivartate। kutaḥ। cittasyaivaiṣa vicitraḥ pariṇāmaḥ, puruṣastvasatyāmavidyāyāṁ śuddhaścittadharmairaparāmṛṣṭa iti। tato'syā''tmabhāvabhāvanā kuśalasya nivartata iti ॥ 25 ॥
body.translated_text: Just as in the rainy season, from the sprouting of a blade of grass, the existence of its seed is inferred, so too, when upon hearing the path to liberation one experiences horripilation and tears, it is inferred that there exists in that person the seed of discriminative seeing — <s>karma</s> (action) conducive to liberation that has been brought about. For such a person, the contemplation of self-identity (<s>ātmabhāvabhāvanā</s>) naturally operates. In the absence of which, this has been said: due to the fault of one's nature, some have a liking for the opponent's position and a dislike for the correct conclusion. Now, the contemplation of self-identity consists of: 'Who was I? How was I? What is this? How is this? What shall we become? How shall we become?' But this ceases for the seer of the distinction. Why? Because this variegated transformation belongs to <s>citta</s> alone, while <s>Puruṣa</s>, when <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is absent, is pure and untouched by the properties of <s>citta</s>. Therefore, for the accomplished one, this contemplation of self-identity ceases. ॥ 25 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
guṇapuruṣayogāsyāvidyā nimittamuttam । sā ca viśeṣadarśina ātmānaṁ vijijñāsamānasya vinivartate । tannivṛttai ca liṅgamāha- [viśeṣadarśina ātmabhāvabhāvanānivṛttiḥ ।] vyaktāvyaktasāmānyādviśiṣṭaḥ puruṣaḥ asādhāraṇe.o [viśeṣaḥ ।] taṁ viśeṣaṁ vyaktāvyaktasāmānyāt pravivicya draṣṭuṁ śīlaṁ yasya sa [viśeṣadarśī ।] tasya [ātmabhāvabhāvanā nivartate ।] sā ca samyagdarśanābhimukhā kaivalyaprāpikarmanimittā ॥
kathaṁ punarātmabhāvabhāvanā asyāstīti vijñāyata ityāha - [yathā prāvṛṣi tṛṇasyāṅkurodbhedena] liṅgena [tadbījasaddhāvo'numīya(gamya)te, tathā mokṣamārgaśravaṇena yasya romaharṣāśrupāto dṛśyate, tatrāpyasti viśeṣadarśanabījamapavargabhāgīyaṁ karmābhinirvartitamiti] romaharṣāśrupātādīleṅgena [anumīyate ॥]
[tasya] viśeṣadarśina: [ātmabhāvabhāvanā] kaivalyabhāgīyakarmanimittā [svābhāvikī] janmāntarakarmanimittā ihajanmāparigrahasthairyakāraṇā vā । sā hyācāryopadeśānapekṣā [svābhāvikī pravartate । tasya] karmaṇastādṛśasya [abhāvāt idamuktam - svabhāvadoṣāt] aśuddhakarmayogāt [eṣāṁ pūrvapakṣe] samyagdarśanatadupāyaviparyaye [rucirbhavati, aruciśva nirṇaye] samyagdarśane ॥
[tatrātmabhāvabhāvanā] kā punarityāha--- [ko'hamāsaṁ, kathamahamāsaṁ, kiṁsvi.ādada, kathaṁsvididaṁ, ke bhaviṣyāma:, kathaṁ bhaviṣyāmaḥ,] iti । [sā tu viśeṣadarśino nivartate ।] yadviṣayā hi jijñāsā, tasminnadhigate tadviṣayā jijñāsā vinivartate । kutaḥ etadavam ? yataḥ [cittasyaivaiṣaḥ] ke bhaviṣyāma ityādiḥ [citraḥ pariṇāmaḥ] na puruṣasya । [puruṣastvasatyāmavidyāyāṁ śuddhaścittadharmairaparāmṛṣṭa iti ।] yasmādevamata evaṁ viśeṣadarśinaḥ [tasyātmabhāvabhāvanā kuśalasya nivataite ॥ 25 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
<s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance) has been stated as the cause of the conjunction of <s>guṇas</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>. And that ceases for the seer of the distinction who wishes to know the self. And the sign of its cessation he states — ['For the seer of the distinction, the contemplation of self-identity ceases.'] <s>Puruṣa</s>, distinguished from the general category of the manifest and the unmanifest, having an uncommon ['distinction (<s>viśeṣa</s>)'] — he whose habit is to see that distinction by discriminating it from the general category of the manifest and unmanifest is the ['seer of the distinction.'] For him, ['the contemplation of self-identity ceases.'] And that is directed toward right vision, occasioned by <s>karma</s> leading to the attainment of <s>kaivalya</s>.
How then is it known that this contemplation of self-identity exists for him? He says — ['Just as in the rainy season, from the sprouting of a blade of grass'] — by this sign — ['the existence of its seed is inferred, so too, when upon hearing the path to liberation, one in whom horripilation and tears are seen — it is inferred that there too exists the seed of discriminative seeing, <s>karma</s> conducive to liberation that has been brought about'] — by the sign of horripilation and tears — ['it is inferred.']
['For such a person,'] the seer of the distinction, ['the contemplation of self-identity'] — occasioned by <s>karma</s> conducive to <s>kaivalya</s> — ['naturally'] — occasioned by <s>karma</s> from a previous birth, or caused by the firmness of renunciation in this birth — that indeed, not depending on a teacher's instruction, ['naturally operates. In the absence of'] such ['<s>karma</s>, this has been said — due to the fault of one's nature'] — due to the conjunction with impure <s>karma</s> — ['some have a liking for the opponent's position'] — for the opposite of right vision and its means — ['and a dislike for the correct conclusion'] — for right vision.
['Now, the contemplation of self-identity'] — what is it? He says — ['"Who was I? How was I? What is this? How is this? What shall we become? How shall we become?"'] ['But this ceases for the seer of the distinction.'] For the inquiry directed toward a particular subject ceases when that subject has been understood. How do we know this? Because ['this'] 'what shall we become?' and so on — ['variegated transformation belongs to <s>citta</s> alone,'] not to <s>Puruṣa</s>. ['But <s>Puruṣa</s>, when <s>avidyā</s> is absent, is pure and untouched by the properties of <s>citta</s>.'] Because this is so, for this reason, ['for that'] seer of the distinction, ['the contemplation of self-identity ceases for the accomplished one.' ॥ 25 ॥]

body.text: tadā vivekanimnaṁ kaivalyaprāgbhāraṁ cittam ॥ 26 ॥
body.translated_text: Then the mind inclines toward discrimination and gravitates toward <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute freedom). ॥ 26 ॥

body.text: tadānīṁ yadasya cittaṁ viṣayaprāgbhāramajñānanimnamāsīttadasyānyathā bhavati kaivalyaprāgbhāraṁ vivekajajñānanimnamiti ॥ 26 ॥
body.translated_text: At that time, this mind which had previously been gravitating toward objects and inclining toward ignorance — it becomes otherwise: gravitating toward <s>kaivalya</s> and inclining toward knowledge born of discrimination. ॥ 26 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
yadā ca viśeṣadarśanamudapādi, [tadā vivekanimnaṁ kaivalyaprāgbhāraṁ cittam । yadasya cittaṁ viṣayanimnaṁ] viṣayapravaṇam [ajñānaprāgbhāram] ajñānaniṣṭhaṁ saṁsārābhimukham [āsīt , tadasya] viśeṣadarśinaḥ [tadānīmanyathā bhavati, kaivalyaprāgbhāraṁ vivekanimnam] iti pratisrotovṛttijñāyate [॥ 26 ॥]
body.translated_text:
<s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Elucidation)
And when discriminative seeing has arisen, ['then the mind inclines toward discrimination and gravitates toward <s>kaivalya</s>. This mind of his which had been inclining toward objects'] — prone toward objects — ['gravitating toward ignorance'] — established in ignorance, facing toward <s>saṁsāra</s> (cycle of rebirth) — ['that mind of this'] seer of the distinction ['then becomes otherwise — gravitating toward <s>kaivalya</s>, inclining toward discrimination.'] This is known as the counter-current flow (<s>pratisroto-vṛtti</s>). [॥ 26 ॥]

body.text: tacchidreṣu pratyayāntarāṇi saṁskārebhyaḥ ॥ 27 ॥
body.translated_text: In the intervals of that, other cognitions [arise] from <s>saṁskāras</s> (latent impressions). ॥ 27 ॥

body.text: pratyayavivekanimnasya sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātimātrapravāhiṇaścittasya tacchidreṣu pratyayāntarāṇyasmīti vā mameti vā jānāmīti vā na jānāmīti vā। kutaḥ, kṣīyamāṇabījebhyaḥ pūrvasaṁskārebhya iti ॥ 27 ॥
body.translated_text: For the mind whose cognition inclines toward discrimination, whose flow consists solely of the discernment of the difference between <s>sattva</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> — in the intervals of that, other cognitions arise: 'I am,' 'mine,' 'I know,' 'I do not know.' From where? From previous <s>saṁskāras</s> (latent impressions) whose seeds are being attenuated. ॥ 27 ॥

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tacchidreṣu pratyayāntarāṇi saṁskārebhyaḥ । vivekanimnasya] uttarottaravivekapravaṇacetasaḥ [puruṣasya] jñāninaḥ [anyatākhyātipravāhādhirohiṇaḥ] sattvapuruṣānyatāsrotaḥplāvinaḥ [cittasya tacchidreṣu] vivekapratyayapravāhāntarāleṣu [pratyayāntarāṇi] viparyayalakṣaṇāni [asmīti vā mameti vā । kutaḥ] tāni bhavantītyāha-- [kṣīyamāṇakleśādibījasya] cittasya [pūrvepacitaviparītasaṁskārebhyaḥ] pratyayāntarāṇi jāyante ॥ 27 ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
['In those gaps, other cognitions arise from saṁskāras (impressions). For the Puruṣa inclined toward discrimination'] — whose mind is progressively inclined toward higher discrimination — ['the knower,'] ['who is ascending the stream of discernment of otherness'] — who is immersed in the stream of the otherness of sattva and Puruṣa — ['in those gaps of his mind'] — in the intervals within the stream of discriminative cognition — ['other cognitions'] characterized by error — ['"I am" or "mine" arise. From where?'] — he explains whence they arise: ['From the saṁskāras previously accumulated, belonging to the opposite direction,'] of the mind ['whose seeds of kleśa (affliction) and the like are being destroyed,'] other cognitions arise. || 27 ||

body.text: hānameṣāṁ kleśavaduktam ॥ 28 ॥
body.translated_text: The removal of these is described as [being] like [the removal of] the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). || 28 ||

body.text: yathā kleśā dagdhabījabhāvā na prarohasamarthā bhavanti tathā jñānāgninā dagdhabījabhāvaḥ pūrvasaṁskāro na pratyayaprasūrbhavati। jñānasaṁskārāstu cittādhikārasamāptimanuśerata iti na cintyante ॥ 28 ॥
body.translated_text: Just as the <s>kleśas</s>, with their seeds burnt, are no longer capable of sprouting, so too the prior <s>saṁskāra</s> (impression), with its seed burnt by the fire of knowledge, no longer gives rise to cognitions. But the <s>saṁskāras</s> of knowledge follow the completion of the mind's function and are therefore not of concern. || 28 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[hānameṣāṁ kleśavaduktam । yathā kleśā dagdhabījabhāvā na prarohasamarthā bhavanti] iti [te pratiprasavaheyāḥ sūkṣmāḥ] ityatroktam, [evaṁ jñānāgnidagdhabījabhāvā:] asmi mametyādipratyayasaṁskārā na prarohasamarthā bhavanti । dagdhaśālibījavat [pūrvasaṁskāro na pratyayaprasūrbhavatītyarthaḥ ॥]
jñānasaṁskārāstu kathamapratipakṣāḥ santaścittamadhikāre na(vija)yojayiṣyantīti ? te tu [samyagdarśanasaṁskārāścitādhikāraparisamāptimanuśerate ।] sahaivāśrayeṇāvasitaprayojanena cittena pralīyante । na punaścittamadhikārapravaṇaṁ kurvanti । adhikārahetoravidyāyāḥ pratipakṣatvājjñānasya । tatra niṣphalatvāt [na cintyante ।] na hi svayaṁ patataḥ patanaheturanveṣaṇīyaḥ ॥ 28 ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
['The removal of these is described as being like that of the kleśas. Just as the kleśas, with their seeds burnt, are no longer capable of sprouting'] — as stated in ['those subtle ones are to be removed by counter-involution (pratiprasava)'] — ['likewise, with their seeds burnt by the fire of knowledge,'] the saṁskāras of cognitions such as 'I am' and 'mine' are no longer capable of sprouting. Like roasted rice seeds, ['the prior saṁskāra no longer gives rise to cognitions — this is the meaning.']
But how will the saṁskāras of knowledge, having no antidote, not engage the mind in [further] function? They ['the saṁskāras of right vision follow the completion of the mind's function.'] They dissolve along with their support — the mind whose purpose has been fulfilled. They do not again make the mind inclined toward function — because knowledge is the antidote of ignorance, which is the cause of [the mind's] function. Since they are fruitless therein, ['they are not of concern.'] For one need not search for the cause of falling for something that falls of its own accord. || 28 ||

body.text: prasaṁkhyāne'pyakusīdasya sarvathā vivekakhyāterdharmameghaḥ samādhiḥ ॥ 29 ॥
body.translated_text: For one who has no interest even in the highest meditation (<s>prasaṁkhyāna</s>), from the discrimination (<s>vivekakhyāti</s>) in every respect, there is the <s>dharma-megha</s> (cloud of dharma) <s>samādhi</s>. || 29 ||

body.text: yadā'yaṁ brāhmaṇaḥ prasaṁkhyāne'pyakusīdastato'pi na kiṁcitprārthayate। tatrāpi viraktasya sarvathā vivekakhyātireva bhavatīti saṁskārabījakṣayānnāspa pratyayāntarāṇyutpadyante। tadā'sya dharmamegho nāma samādhirbhavati ॥ 29 ॥
body.translated_text: When this <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (spiritual aspirant) has no interest even in <s>prasaṁkhyāna</s> (the highest discriminative meditation), desiring nothing even from that — when, being dispassionate even toward that, there is only discriminative discernment in every respect — then, from the destruction of the seeds of <s>saṁskāras</s>, no other cognitions arise for him. Then for him there comes the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>dharma-megha</s> (cloud of dharma). || 29 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
vivekakhyātipravaṇāntaḥkaraṇasya brāhmaṇasya prasaṁkhyāne'pyakusīdasya [sarvathāvivekakhyāterdharmameghaḥ samādhiḥ ।] sa yadā ayaṁ brāhmaṇaḥ prasaṁkhyāne vivekadarśanaśīlate'pyakusīdaḥ avṛddhiko bhavati, [tato'pi] prasaṁkhyānaprasādaviśeṣādadhikaṁ na [kiṁcit prārthayate ।] apiśabdāṁt prasaṁkhyāne'pi na prārthanā । tatrāpi prasaṁkhyāne [viraktaḥ । sarvathā] sarveṇa prakāreṇa vivekakhyātiryasya sa [sarvathāvivekakhyātireva bhavati ॥]
[kleśasaṁskārabījakṣayāt nāsya] śarīrādau śūnyaveśmanīva asmi mameti vā jñānaprasādamātraikāyatanasya [pratyayāntarāṇyutpadyante । tadā'sya] brāhmaṇasya [sarvathāvivekakhyāte: dharmamegho nāma samādhirbhavati ।] kaivalyākhyaṁ paraṁ dharmaṁ varṣatīti [dharmameghaḥ] iti saṁjñā [॥ 29 ॥]
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
For the brāhmaṇa whose inner instrument is inclined toward discriminative discernment, who has no interest even in prasaṁkhyāna, ['from discrimination in every respect, the dharma-megha samādhi.'] When this brāhmaṇa, though inclined to the practice of discriminative vision in prasaṁkhyāna, becomes without interest — without gain-seeking — ['desiring nothing even more'] than the special serenity of prasaṁkhyāna. The word 'even' (api) indicates that there is no desire even in prasaṁkhyāna. ['Being dispassionate even toward that'] — toward prasaṁkhyāna. ['In every respect'] — in every manner — ['he becomes one for whom there is discriminative discernment in every respect.']
['From the destruction of the seeds of kleśa-saṁskāras, no other'] cognitions such as 'I am' or 'mine' arise for this one ['whose sole abode is the mere serenity of knowledge,'] as in an empty house regarding body and the like. ['Then for this'] brāhmaṇa, ['from discrimination in every respect, there comes the samādhi called dharma-megha.'] It ['rains the supreme dharma called kaivalya'] — hence the designation ['dharma-megha' (cloud of dharma). || 29 ||]

body.text: tataḥ kleśakarmanivṛttiḥ ॥ 30 ॥
body.translated_text: From that, the cessation of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and <s>karma</s> (actions). || 30 ||

body.text: tallābhādavidyādayaḥ kleśāḥ samūlakāṣaṁ kaṣitā bhavanti। kuśalākuśalāśca karmāśayāḥ samūlaghātaṁ hatā bhavanti।kleśakarmanivṛttau jīvanneva vidvānvimukto bhavati। kasmāt, yasmādviparyayo bhavasya kāraṇam। na hi kṣīṇaviparyayaḥ kaścitkenacitkvacijjāto dṛśyata iti ॥ 30 ॥
body.translated_text: From the attainment of that [dharma-megha samādhi], the <s>kleśas</s> beginning with <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) are uprooted with their roots. And the <s>karmāśayas</s> (karmic deposits), whether wholesome or unwholesome, are destroyed root and all. Upon the cessation of <s>kleśas</s> and <s>karma</s>, the wise one becomes liberated even while living (<s>jīvanmukta</s>). Why? Because erroneous cognition (<s>viparyaya</s>) is the cause of worldly existence (<s>bhava</s>). For no one whose erroneous cognition has been destroyed is ever seen to be born anywhere. || 30 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tataḥ kleśakarmanivṛttiḥ । tasya] dharmameghanāmnaḥ samādheḥ samyagdarśanapākābhirūpasya [ [lābhāt] ] bhāvāt [avidyādayaḥ kleśāḥ samūlakāṣaṁ kaṣitāḥ] vāsanābhiḥ saha samastāḥ pralīnāḥ [bhavanti] । [kuśalākuśalāśca karmāśayāḥ samūlaghātaṁ hatā bhavanti ।] mūlaiḥ kleśaiḥ sahocchinnā bhavanti ॥
[kleśakarmanivṛtauṁ jīvanneva vidvān mukto bhavati । kasmāt] evama ? yato [viparyayaḥ] mithyājñānaṁ [bhavasya] janmanaḥ [kāraṇam । na hi kṣīṇaviparyayaḥ kaścit kacijjāto dṛśyate ॥ 30 ॥]
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
['From that, the cessation of kleśas and karma.'] ['From the attainment'] — the arising — of that samādhi called dharma-megha, which has the nature of the ripening of right vision, ['the kleśas beginning with avidyā are uprooted'] — dissolved entirely, along with their vāsanās (latent impressions). ['And the karmāśayas, whether wholesome or unwholesome, are destroyed root and all.'] They are cut off together with their roots, the kleśas.
['Upon the cessation of kleśas and karma, the wise one becomes liberated even while living. Why'] is this so? Because ['erroneous cognition (viparyaya) is the cause of worldly existence (bhava). For no one whose erroneous cognition has been destroyed is ever seen to be born anywhere.' || 30 ||]

body.text: tadā sarvāvaraṇamalāpetasya jñānasyā''nantyājjñeyamalpam ॥ 31 ॥
body.translated_text: Then, with all the covering impurities of knowledge removed, due to the infinity of knowledge, what remains to be known is little. || 31 ||

body.text: sarvaiḥ kleśakarmāvaraṇairvimuktasya jñānasyā''nantyaṁ bhavati। āvarakeṇa tamasā'bhibhūtamāvṛtamanantaṁ jñānasattvaṁ kvacideva rajasā pravartitamuddhāṭitaṁ grahaṇasamarthaṁ bhavati। tatra yadā sarvairāvaraṇamalairapagataṁ bhavati tadā bhavatyasyā''nantyam। jñānasyā''nantyājjñeyamalpaṁ saṁpadyate। yathā''kāśe khadyotaḥ। yatredayuktam – andho maṇimavidhyattamanaṅgulirāvayat। agrīvastaṁ pratyamuñcattamajihvo'bhyapūjayat ॥ iti ॥ 31 ॥
body.translated_text: For knowledge freed from all the coverings of <s>kleśas</s> and <s>karma</s>, there arises infinitude. The infinite knowledge-<s>sattva</s>, overwhelmed by the covering <s>tamas</s>, is only here and there, when set in motion and uncovered by <s>rajas</s>, capable of apprehension. When it becomes free from all covering impurities, its infinitude becomes manifest. Due to the infinitude of knowledge, what remains to be known becomes small — like a firefly in space. As it has been said: 'The blind man pierced the jewel; the fingerless one strung it on a thread; the neckless one wore it; the tongueless one praised it.' || 31 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[tadā sarvāvaraṇamalāpetasya jñānasyā''nantyāt jñeyamalpam ।] tadā dharmameghasamādhisamaye, [sarvaiḥ kleśakarmāvaraṇaiḥ] rajastamojanmabhiḥ [vimuktasya, jñānasya] sattvapuruṣānyatākhyātimātrasya bhavatyā [nantyam ।] tat kathamiti ? [tamasā(na)'bhibhūtamanantaṁ jñānasattvaṁ,] tasya tiraskṛtarajomalasyānantasya nistaraṅgamahodadhideśīyasya nirahitasyāvikriyasya kathaṁ tadgrahaṇasāmarthyamityāha- [kvacidrajasā pravartitaṁ] cittasattvam [udghāṭitaṁ] vāyuneva mahāpayodamaṇḍalamāhataṁ sūcitaṁ [grahaṇasamarthaṁ bhavati ।] svataḥ sattvasyāpravartanāt rajaso hi pravṛttisāmarthyamiti ॥
[tadā'sya] cittasya [bhavatyānantyam,] aśeṣajñeyaviṣayatvamambaratalamadhyavartino jaladharānarodhanirgatasya raveriva । tasya [jñānasyānanyāt] aśeṣaviṣayatvāt [jñeyamalpaṁ sampadyate । yathā ākāśe khadyota:] iti । yathā ākāśāpekṣayā khadyoto na kiṁcidevametajjñānābhisamīkṣayā jñeya na kiṁciditi ॥
paramātmajñānāvasthāyāmaśeṣaviparyayatirodhāne sarvapuruṣārthaśūnyatā cetyetatpradaraśanārthamudāharaṇamāha - yatredamuktam - andho maṇimavindat (dhyat) tamanaṅgulirāvayat । agrīvaḥ (taṁ) pratyamuñcat tamajihve'bhyapūjayat iti । yathā andhādīnāṁ maṇīvedhādikamasambhavadapi viparyayeṇāndho maṇimavidhyaditi vyavahriyate, tathā jñānajñeyasaṁvyavahāro'pi viparyayāvasthāyāmeva । viparyayābhāve tu sarvapuruṣārthaśūnyā eva guṇāḥ sampadyanta iti ॥ 31 ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
['Then, with all the covering impurities of knowledge removed, due to the infinity of knowledge, what remains to be known is little.'] Then, at the time of dharma-megha samādhi, ['freed from all the coverings of kleśa and karma'] born of rajas and tamas, ['knowledge'] — the mere discernment of the otherness of sattva and Puruṣa — ['becomes infinite.'] How is that? The ['infinite knowledge-sattva, overwhelmed by tamas'] — with its rajas-impurity concealed, infinite like a waveless great ocean, undisturbed, unchanging — how does it acquire the capacity for apprehension? He says: ['When here and there, set in motion by rajas,'] the citta-sattva, ['uncovered'] — struck open like a great mass of clouds by the wind, revealed — ['becomes capable of apprehension.'] Because sattva by itself does not move — for rajas has the power of activity.
['Then its'] — the mind's — ['infinitude becomes manifest,'] its being the object of all that is knowable, like the sun emerging from the obstruction of clouds while dwelling in mid-sky. Due to ['the infinitude of that knowledge'] — its having all things as objects — ['what remains to be known becomes little. Like a firefly in space.'] Just as a firefly is nothing compared to space, so what is knowable is nothing in comparison with this knowledge.
In order to illustrate the emptiness of all purposes of puruṣa in the state of knowledge of the supreme self, and the concealment of all erroneous cognition, he cites the example —

body.text: tataḥ kṛtārthānāṁ pariṇāmakramasamāptirguṇānām ॥ 32 ॥
body.translated_text: From that, the completion of the sequence of transformations of the <s>guṇas</s>, which have fulfilled their purpose. || 32 ||

body.text: tasya dharmameghasyodayātkṛtārthānāṁ guṇānāṁ pariṇāmakramaḥ parisamāpyate। na hi kṛtabhogāpavargāḥ parisamāptakramāḥ kṣaṇamapyavasthātumutsahante ॥ 32 ॥
body.translated_text: From the arising of that <s>dharma-megha</s> [samādhi], the sequence of transformations of the <s>guṇas</s>, which have fulfilled their purpose, comes to completion. For [the guṇas] whose experience and liberation have been accomplished, whose sequence is completed, cannot endure even for a moment. || 32 ||

body.text:
vivaraṇam
tataḥ dharmameghasamādhisamudayāt kṛtārthāścittaguṇāssampadyante । cittādhīnatvācca kāryakaraṇārambhiṇo'pi sattvādayaḥ kṛtārthā bhavanti । samastasya puruṣārthasya kṛtatvāt । eṣāṁ kṛtārthānāṁ guṇānāṁ janmamaraṇapra(bhāva)vāharūpaḥ pariṇāmakramaḥ parisamāpyate । na hi kṛtabhogāpavargārthāḥ kṣaṇamapi prayojanābhāvāt avasthātumutsahante ॥ 32 ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
From the arising of dharma-megha samādhi, the guṇas of the mind become fulfilled in their purpose. And since sattva and the others, which initiate the [activity of] effects and instruments, also depend on the mind, they too become fulfilled in their purpose — because the entire purpose of Puruṣa has been accomplished. The sequence of transformations of these guṇas that have fulfilled their purpose — in the form of the flow of birth and death — comes to completion. For [the guṇas] whose purposes of experience and liberation have been accomplished cannot endure even for a moment, due to the absence of purpose. || 32 ||

body.text: atha ko'yaṁ kramo nāmeti –
body.translated_text: Now, what is this 'sequence' (<s>krama</s>)?

body.text: kṣaṇapratiyogī pariṇāmāparāntanirgrāhyaḥ kramaḥ ॥ 33 ॥
body.translated_text: Sequence (<s>krama</s>) is the correlate of the moment (<s>kṣaṇa</s>), apprehended at the final end of transformation. || 33 ||

body.text: kṣaṇānantaryātmā pariṇāmasyāparāntenāvasānena gṛhyate kramaḥ। na hyananubhūtakramakṣaṇā purāṇatā vastrasyānte bhavati। nityeṣu ca kramo dṛṣṭaḥ।
body.translated_text: Sequence, whose essence is the unbroken succession of moments, is apprehended at the final end (<s>aparānta</s>) — the conclusion — of transformation. For the aging of a cloth, without having experienced [its] moment-by-moment sequence, does not occur at the end. And sequence is observed even in eternal things.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
pariṇāmakramaparisāmāptirityuktam । atha ko'yaṁ guṇakramo nāma yasya parisamāptirupavarṇitā? tasyāyamadhigamopāya ucyate - kṣaṇapratiyogī pariṇāmāparāntanigrārhyaḥ kramaḥ । kṣaṇaṁ prati yujyata iti kṣaṇāpratiyogī ।
[kṣaṇānantaryātmā] kṣaṇasyānantaratā kṣaṇānantaryaṁ tadātmā tatsvabhāvaḥ । kṣaṇānantaryameva [‘kṣaṇatatkramayoḥ’] iti vyākhyātam ॥
kiṁ punarasya grahaṇe liṅgamityāha— [pariṇāmasyāparāntena] vināśāvasthārūpaṇa [avasānena] liṅgena [nigṛhyate saḥ kramaḥ ।] kathamaparāntena nirgrahaṇamiti ? ucyate-- [na hyānanubhūtakramā] kramamanavalambamānā kṣaṇe [kṣaṇe purāṇatā vastrasyānte] vināśakāle bhavati iti । na hi kadācidbhūtamātrasyaiva vastrasya purāṇatā dṛśyate । tasmāt purāṇatābhivyaktiliṅgenābhyūhyate--yeneyaṁ purāṇatā vasrasyābhivyaktimupasaṁprāpitā sa kramaḥ ॥
tatra yadi labdhāvasānatvamalabdhāvasānatvaṁ ca kramasya syāt, tato yuktaṁ [kṛtārthānāṁ pariṇāmakramaparisamāsiguṇānāmū] iti vaktum । taca labdhalabdhāva sānatvaṁ kramasya niṣyānityatve ghaṭate । tatrānityeṣu vastrādiṣu krame dṛṣṭra:, na tu nityeṣu । tataśca guṇānāṁ nityānāṁ pariṇāmakramaparisamāptirayuktā syādityāśaṅkamāna āha- [niyeṣu ca kramo dṛṣṭaḥ ।]
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
It was said: 'the completion of the sequence of transformations.' Now what is this sequence of the guṇas whose completion has been described? The means of understanding it is stated: 'Sequence is the correlate of the moment, apprehended at the final end of transformation.' It is correlated with the moment — hence 'the correlate of the moment.'
['Whose essence is the unbroken succession of moments'] — the uninterruptedness of moments is the succession of moments; that is its essence, its nature. The succession of moments has been explained in ['on the moment and its succession.']
What then is the mark by which it is apprehended? He says: ['By the final end of transformation'] — by the form of the state of destruction — ['by the conclusion'] — by that mark — ['that sequence is apprehended.'] How is it apprehended by the final end? It is said: ['For the aging that has not experienced its sequence'] — not depending on the sequence — ['moment by moment, does not occur at the end'] — at the time of destruction — of the cloth. For the aging of a cloth that has just come into being is not observed. Therefore, by the inferential mark of the manifestation of aging, one infers: that which has brought the aging of the cloth to manifestation is the sequence.
If the sequence had both attained termination and unattained termination, then it would be proper to say ['the completion of the sequence of transformations of the guṇas that have fulfilled their purpose.'] And such attained-and-unattained termination of the sequence is possible given both eternality and non-eternality. Sequence is observed in non-eternal things like cloth, but not in eternal things. Therefore, the completion of the sequence of transformations for the eternal guṇas would be unjustified — anticipating this objection, he says: ['And sequence is observed even in eternal things.']

body.text: dvayī ceyaṁ nityatā kūṭasthanityatā pariṇāminityatā ca। tatra kūṭasthanityatā puruṣasya। pariṇāminityatā guṇānām। yasminpariṇamyamāne tattvaṁ na vihanyate tannityam। ubhayasya ca tattvānabhighātānnityatvam। tatra guṇadharmeṣu buddhyādiṣu pariṇāmāparāntanirgrāhyaḥ kramo labdhaparyavasāno nityeṣu dharmiṣu guṇeṣvalabdhaparyavasānaḥ। kūṭasthanityeṣu svarūpamātrapratiṣṭheṣu muktapuruṣeṣu svarūpāstitā krameṇaivānubhūyata iti tatrāpyalabdhaparyavasānaḥ śabdapṛṣṭhenāstikriyāmupādāya kalpita iti।
body.translated_text: This eternality is of two kinds: immutable eternality (<s>kūṭastha-nityatā</s>) and transforming eternality (<s>pariṇāmi-nityatā</s>). Among these, immutable eternality belongs to <s>Puruṣa</s>; transforming eternality belongs to the <s>guṇas</s>. That in which, though undergoing transformation, the essential nature (<s>tattva</s>) is not destroyed — that is eternal. And the eternality of both is due to the non-destruction of their essential nature. Among the properties of the <s>guṇas</s> — <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) and the rest — the sequence apprehended at the final end of transformation has attained termination. But in the eternal <s>guṇas</s> as property-bearers (<s>dharmins</s>), [the sequence] has not attained termination. In the immutably eternal liberated <s>Puruṣas</s>, established solely in their own nature, the existence of their own nature is experienced only through sequence — and so there too [the sequence] has not attained termination. It is merely conceptualized by relying on the verb 'exists' at the surface level of language.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
kiṁ sarvatra ? netyāha- [dvivigheyaṁ nityatā, pariṇāmanityatā guṇānāṁ, kūṭasthānityatā puruṣasyeti ॥]
nanu pariṇāmināṁ guṇānāṁ kathaṁ nityatā syāditi bravīti--- [yasmin pariṇamamāne tattvaṁ na vihanyate ।] yasya yadrūpaṁ pramāṇenopalabdhaṁ, tasya tat tattvam । tadyasmin na vihanyate na vyabhicarati, tadapi nityam । guṇānāmapi sukhadu:khamohātmatā prakāśakriyāsthitiśīlatā ca tatvaṁ na vihanyate । tasmādete'pa pariṇāmanityāḥ । ubhayatra ca guṇapuruṣeṣu [tattvasyāvighātānnityatvam ।] tato guṇeṣvapi nityeṣu pariṇāmo dṛṣṭa iti labdhālabdhaparyavasāntvaṁ sthitam ॥
[tatra guṇadharmeṣu mahadādiṣu pariṇāmāparāntanirgrāhyaḥ kramo labdhaparyavasānaḥ] śarīrādiṣviva । [nityeṣu tu] guṇeṣu dharmiṣvalabdhaparyavasānaḥ nityatvādeṣām । [kūṭasthanileṣu svarūpamātrapratiṣṭheṣu muktapuruṣeṣu svarūpāstitā krameṇaivānubhūyate ।] tena muktapuruṣeṣvasannapyanubhavadvāreṇa, [śabdapṛṣṭhenāstikriyāmupādāya vikalpitaḥ] iti alabdhaparyavasāna eva । paramārthataḥ । puruṣaṣvapāraṇāmitvānnāsti krama ityarthaḥ ॥
body.translated_text:
Vivaraṇam (Elucidation)
Is [sequence observed] everywhere? No, he says: ['This eternality is of two kinds: transforming eternality of the guṇas, and immutable eternality of Puruṣa.']
But how can there be eternality for the guṇas, which undergo transformation? He explains: ['That in which, though undergoing transformation, the essential nature is not destroyed.'] The essential nature (tattva) of something is that form which is apprehended through a valid means of knowledge. That in which it is not destroyed, does not deviate — that too is eternal. The essential nature of the guṇas — being of the nature of pleasure, pain, and delusion, and being characterized by luminosity, activity, and stability — is not destroyed. Therefore, these too are eternal through transformation. And in both — guṇas and Puruṣas — ['due to the non-destruction of essential nature, there is eternality.'] Therefore, since transformation is observed even in the guṇas that are eternal, the attained-and-unattained termination [of sequence] is established.
['Among the properties of the guṇas — mahat (the great principle) and the rest — the sequence apprehended at the final end of transformation has attained termination,'] like bodies and such. ['But in the eternal'] guṇas as property-bearers, [the sequence] has not attained termination, due to their eternality. ['In the immutably eternal liberated Puruṣas, established solely in their own nature, the existence of their own nature is experienced only through sequence.'] Therefore, in the liberated Puruṣas, though the sequence does not really exist, through the channel of experience, ['it is conceptualized by relying on the verb "exists" at the surface level of language'] — so it has indeed not attained termination. In ultimate reality, in Puruṣas, due to their non-transforming nature, there is no sequence — this is the meaning.

body.text: athāsya saṁsārasya sthityā gatyā ca guṇeṣu vartamānasyāsti kramasamāptirna veti। avacanīyametat। katham। asti praśna ekāntavacanīyaḥ sarvo jāto mariṣyatīti। oṁ bho iti।
body.translated_text: Now, for this [being in] <s>saṁsāra</s>, abiding and moving within the <s>guṇas</s> — is there a completion of sequence or not? This is unanswerable. How? There is a question that can be answered categorically: 'Everyone who is born will die.' 'Yes indeed!'

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[athāsya sasārasya sthityā] pradhānarūpeṇa, gatyā vikārātmanā, dvaya ca guṇātmakamiti [guṇeṣu ca vartamānasya asti kramaparisamāptiḥ na veti ? avacanīyametat ।] astyevetyavadhāraṇaṁ na śakyaṁ kartum । nāpi nāstyeveti । kiṁ tu vibhajya, kasyacidasti kasyāpi nāstīti vacanīyameva ॥
[katham ? asti praśna ekāntavacanīyaḥ] apravibhajyāpi । yathā [sarvo jāto mariṣyati] ajñānī [iti ।] nanu jñānavānapi mariṣyatyeva । ucyate – ajñasya hi maraṇamityabhimānaḥ, na jñāninaḥ । tathā coktam – [mithyaitadāhurmriyatīti mūḍhāḥ] iti ॥
body.translated_text: <s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Sub-commentary): [Now, of this <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of existence), by its abiding] in the form of <s>pradhāna</s> (primal matter), [by its activity] in the form of modifications, and both being of the nature of the <s>guṇas</s> (constituents) — [is there a completion of the sequence (<s>kramaparisamāpti</s>) for the <s>guṇas</s> in which one is engaged, or not? This is unanswerable.] It cannot be determined with certainty that it definitely exists, nor that it definitely does not exist. Rather, it must be stated by making a distinction: for some it exists, and for some it does not. [How so? There are questions that are answerable with a definitive statement] even without making a distinction. For example: [Everyone born will die] — the ignorant person [thus.] But does not even the wise person die? It is said — for the ignorant there is the notion of death, but not for the knower. And thus it has been declared: [The deluded say 'he dies' — this is false.]

body.text: atha sarvo mṛtvā janiṣyata iti। vibhajyavacanīyametat। pratyuditakhyātiḥ kṣīṇatṛṣṇaḥ kuśalo na janiṣyata itarastu janiṣyate। tathā manuṣyajātiḥ śreyasī na vā śreyasītyevaṁ paripṛṣṭe vibhajya vacanīyaḥ praśnaḥ paśūnadhikṛtya śreyasī devānṛṣīṁścādhikṛtya neti। ayaṁ tvavacanīyaḥ praśnaḥ saṁsāro'yamantavānathānanta iti। kuśalasyāsti saṁsārakramasamāptirnetarasyeti anyatarāvadhāraṇe doṣaḥ।tasmādvyākarīya evāyaṁ praśna iti ॥ 33 ॥
