body.translated_text: Now, will everyone, having died, be reborn? This must be answered by making a distinction. One who has attained discriminative knowledge (<s>pratyuditakhyāti</s>), whose thirst (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) is exhausted, who is skilled — such a one will not be reborn; the other, however, will be reborn. Similarly, when asked whether the human birth is the most excellent or not, the question must be answered by making a distinction: in relation to animals it is the most excellent, but in relation to gods and sages it is not. But this is an unanswerable question when posed in general terms: whether this <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of existence) is finite or infinite. There is a fault in affirming either alternative exclusively — that the completion of the sequence of <s>saṃsāra</s> exists for the skilled one but not for the other. Therefore, this question must indeed be answered by making a distinction.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[atha sarvo mṛtvā janiṣyata iti ? vibhajya vacanīyametat] ekāntānupapatteḥ । katham ? [pratyuditakhyātiḥ kṣīṇatṛṣṇaḥ kuśalo na janiṣyate, itaraḥ] ajñaḥ [janiṣyate ॥]
[tathā manuṣyajātiḥ śreyasī] eva [naiva vetyavacanīyaḥ praśnaḥ ।] pravibhajya tu vacanīya eva । katham ? [paśūnuddiśya śreyasī] bhavati । [devānṛṣīṁścādhikṛtya na] śreyasī bhavati ॥
[ayaṁ tvavacanaya eva] apravibhajya sāmānyena [praśnaḥ] --yathā [saṁsāro'yamantavāneveti ananta eveti vā ।] bandhamokṣānupapatteḥ । pravibhajya tu vacanīya eva । yathā kuśalasyāsti [saṁsāracakraparisamāptirnetarasyeti ॥]
[anyatarāvadhāraṇe doṣaḥ ।] saṁsāro'ntavānevānanta eveti vānyatarāvadhāraṇe doṣaḥ । [tasmādavyākaraṇīya evāyaṁ] sāmānyenāpravibhajya [praśnaḥ] , yathā – [sarvo mṛtvā janiṣyate] iti, evaṁ [manuṣyajātiḥ śreyasyeveti] ca । tasmāt suṣṭhūktaṁ [kṛtārthānāṁ pariṇāmakramaparisamāsiguṁṇānāmiti] viśeṣaṇam [॥ 33 ॥]
body.translated_text: <s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Sub-commentary): [Now, will everyone, having died, be reborn? This must be answered by making a distinction,] since a one-sided answer is untenable. How so? [One who has attained discriminative knowledge, whose thirst is exhausted, who is skilled — will not be reborn; the other,] the ignorant one, [will be reborn.] [Similarly, whether the human birth is the most excellent] indeed [or not — this is an unanswerable question] without distinction. But when distinguished, it is indeed answerable. How? [In relation to animals, it is the most excellent.] [In relation to gods and sages, it is not] the most excellent. [But this indeed is unanswerable] without distinction, as a general [question] — such as [whether this <s>saṃsāra</s> is definitely finite or definitely infinite,] since both bondage and liberation would be untenable. But when distinguished, it is indeed answerable. As: for the skilled one there is [completion of the cycle of <s>saṃsāra</s>, but not for the other.] [There is a fault in affirming either alternative exclusively] — the fault lies in exclusively affirming either that <s>saṃsāra</s> is definitely finite or definitely infinite. [Therefore, this] question, in general terms without distinction, [is unanswerable] — just as [everyone having died will be reborn], and likewise [the human birth is the most excellent]. Therefore, the qualifying phrase ["of the <s>guṇas</s> whose sequence of transformation has reached completion for those who have fulfilled their purpose"] is well stated.

body.text: guṇādhikārakramasamāptau kaivalyamuktaṁ tatsvarūpamavadhāryate –
body.translated_text: Having stated <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation) upon the completion of the sequence of the <s>guṇas</s>' operation, its essential nature is now determined —

body.text: puruṣārthaśūnyānāṁ guṇānāṁ pratiprasavaḥ kaivalyaṁ svarūpapratiṣṭhā vā citiśaktiriti ॥ 34 ॥
body.translated_text: The <s>pratiprasava</s> (involution) of the <s>guṇas</s> (constituents), which are devoid of purpose for <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Self), is <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation); or it is the <s>svarūpa-pratiṣṭhā</s> (establishment in its own nature) of <s>citiśakti</s> (the power of consciousness).

body.text: kṛtabhogāpavargāṇāṁ puruṣārthaśūnyānāṁ yaḥ pratiprasavaḥ kāryakāraṇātmakānāṁ guṇānāṁ tatkaivalyaṁ, svarūpapratiṣṭhā punarbuddhisattvānabhisaṁbandhātpuruṣasya citiśaktireva kevalā, tasyāḥ sadā tathaivāvasthānaṁ kaivalyamiti ॥ 34 ॥
body.translated_text: When experience and liberation have been accomplished, the <s>guṇas</s> (constituents) — which are of the nature of both effect and cause — become devoid of purpose for <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Self); their <s>pratiprasava</s> (involution back to their source) is <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation). <s>Svarūpa-pratiṣṭhā</s> (establishment in own nature) means that, due to the absence of connection with the <s>sattva</s> (purity) of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>Puruṣa</s>'s <s>citiśakti</s> (power of consciousness) alone remains in its pure state — its abiding thus forever is <s>kaivalya</s>.

body.text:
vivaraṇam
[guṇādhikāraparisamāptau kaivalyamuktam । tatsvarūpamavadhāryate ।] kaivalyaṁ prati vipratipatteḥ । keṣāñcidvijñānasantānasyātyantopaśamaḥ kaivalyam । keṣāñcittu navānāmātmaguṇānāṁ buddhīcchādveṣaprayatnasukhaduḥkhadharmādharmasaṁskārāṇāmucchedenācetanasya dravyamātrasya puruṣasyāvasthānam । keṣāñcidīśvarasyāyujyam । keṣāñcit sarvajñatvādīśvaratulyadharmatvaprāptiḥ kaivalyamiti bhinnā matiḥ ॥
ihāpi vipratipattipraṇodāya kaivalyasvarūpamavadhāryate – [puruṣārthaśūnyānāṁ guṇānāṁ yaḥ pratiprasavaḥ] pratisaṁsargaḥ svakāraṇe pratyastamaya ityarthaḥ, [kāryakaraṇātmakatayā pariṇatānām] , tat [kaivalyaṁ] puruṣasya kevalatvaṁ guṇairamiśrībhāva ityarthaḥ ॥
[svarūpapratiṣṭhā vā citiśakti] riti । [buddhisattvānabhisaṁbandhinī yā puruṣasya citiśaktiḥ] amiśrā [kevalā tasyāḥ sadā tathaiva avasthānaṁ kevalāyāḥ] bhāvaḥ kaivalyam ॥
nanu kaivalyasyaikatve kathaṁ vikalpaḥ? kriyāyāṁ hi vikalpo na tu vastuni । vastusvarūpasya bhedānupapatteḥ । kaivalyamapi vastu, kathaṁ tadvikalpyata iti । naiṣa doṣaḥ । nimittanaimittikayoḥ prabhedopapatteḥ । nimittanaimittikabhede.opacarito'pi vikalpe na vastusvarūpabhedakṛtaḥ । yā tu guṇānāṁ pariṇāmitā puruṣasya vimiśratā vṛttisarūpatā, sā kāryakaraṇātmakānāṁ puruṣārthaśūnyānāṁ guṇānāṁ pratisaṁsargānnimittādapagacchatīti nimittageva pratiprasavākhyaṁ kaivalyaśabdenopacaritaṁ pūrvam ॥
dvitīyaṁ tu guṇapratiprasavanimittabhāvi yat svarūpāvasthānaṁ puruṣasya guṇairamiśritatayā, tat kaivalyamiti viśeṣaḥ । guṇapuruṣāntarasvarūpatattvanirdhāraṇena tantrāntarīyatatvasvarūpanirākaraṇena ca kaivalyāntarāṇi niveditavyāni ॥
tatroṅkāro maṅgalārthaḥ prayuktaḥ paraṁmaśvaranāmāṅkitamastakatayā tantrapracayārthaṁ śāntyarthaṁ vā vedāraṇyakavaditi om iti ॥
oṅkāro yasya vaktā samacarata phalaiḥ karma yasmādaśeṣaṁ niṣkarmakळ.eśapāko ghaṭayati sakalaṁ yaḥ phalena kriyāṇām । īśānāmīśvaro yaḥ sthitibhavanidhanaprakriyāṇāṁ vidhātā dhyāyannaḥ śuklimānaṁ vyapanudatu tarāṁ kṛṣṇimānaṁ sa kṛṣṇaḥ ॥
yātrākṛtastrijagatāṁ yadacintyaśakti- leśān daśāhureha mīnamukhāvatārān । kleśodbhavatrividhatāpaparamparārtā: taṁ nāganāthaśāyanaṁ śaraṇaṁ vrajāmaḥ ॥
phaṇarataughavadyoti [ pṛthivī ] dyunabhodiśe । yogīndrāya phaṇīndrāya tatpatañjalaye namaḥ ॥
yogena cittasya padena vācāṁ malaṁ śarīrasya tu vaidyakena । yo'pākarottaṁ pravaraṁ munīnāṁ patanaliṁ prāñjalirānato'smi ॥
sa jayati patañjalimuniḥ yena śreyo'rthisārthasasyānām । vihito harṣastāpatritayahṛtā dharmamedhena ॥
yastatāna bhavamārgalaṅghināṁ kleśakarmamayadharmanuttaye । dharmameghamukhayogatoyadam [rta patañjalimṛrṣiṁ praṇato'smi] ॥
vadanāhitapūrṇacandrakaṁ gurumīśānamabhūtibhūṣaṇam । praṇamāmbhujaṅgasaṅgrahaṁ bhagavatpādamapūrvaśaṅkaram ॥ 34 ॥
body.translated_text: <s>Vivaraṇam</s> (Sub-commentary): [Having stated <s>kaivalya</s> upon the completion of the <s>guṇas</s>' operation, its essential nature is now determined,] since there are conflicting views regarding <s>kaivalya</s>. For some, <s>kaivalya</s> is the absolute cessation of the stream of consciousness (<s>vijñānasantāna</s>). For others, it is said to be the state of <s>Puruṣa</s> as mere insentient substance, upon the destruction of nine qualities of the self — cognition, desire, aversion, effort, pleasure, pain, merit, demerit, and latent impressions — and to show the defect in that view: [The <s>pratiprasava</s> (involution) of the <s>guṇas</s>, devoid of purpose for <s>Puruṣa</s>, is <s>kaivalya</s>; or it is the <s>svarūpa-pratiṣṭhā</s> (establishment in own nature) of <s>citiśakti</s> (the power of consciousness).] [When experience and liberation have been accomplished] — when both enjoyment and release have been fulfilled and completed — then [the <s>guṇas</s>], devoid of any purpose for <s>Puruṣa</s>, undergo [<s>pratiprasava</s>], dissolution into their cause — [that is <s>kaivalya</s>.] Alternatively, [<s>svarūpa-pratiṣṭhā</s>] means establishment in one's own nature, abiding in one's own form — [<s>citiśakti</s> alone in its pure state], the power of consciousness abiding in its own essence alone, being pure — [its remaining thus forever is <s>kaivalya</s>.] It is presented in both ways. The pure <s>citiśakti</s> is never in a state other than its own nature; rather, since it always abides thus, <s>kaivalya</s> is as before, through the absence of the limiting adjunct of <s>pradhāna</s> (primal matter). The <s>pratiprasava</s> of the <s>guṇas</s> is the second definition of <s>kaivalya</s>. <s>Pratiprasava</s> means dissolution beginning with <s>pradhāna</s> — each into its own cause: <s>mahat</s> (the great principle) into <s>pradhāna</s>, <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-principle) into <s>mahat</s>, the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) which originate from it into <s>ahaṃkāra</s> itself, the gross elements from those, and the sense organs dissolve into <s>ahaṃkāra</s> as their own cause — thus the dissolution of all modifications into <s>pradhāna</s> is <s>pratiprasava</s>, which is <s>kaivalya</s>. Both have been stated regarding <s>kaivalya</s> — that it is abiding in one's own nature and that it is <s>pratiprasava</s>. In this regard, [indeed, the purport of this system, having completely set aside everything in every way, is that <s>kaivalya</s> is nothing but the essential nature of <s>citiśakti</s>, not the <s>pratiprasava</s> of the <s>guṇas</s>]. Although the <s>pratiprasava</s> of the <s>guṇas</s> has been called <s>kaivalya</s>, nevertheless the abiding of <s>citiśakti</s> in its own nature is the primary meaning of <s>kaivalya</s>; the <s>pratiprasava</s> of the <s>guṇas</s> is merely incidental — this is the true doctrine. Thus concludes the sub-commentary composed by the revered <s>Śaṅkara</s> <s>Bhagavatpūjyapāda</s>.
